In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
The earth was empty and dark. Water covered everything, and God's Spirit moved over the water.
God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
God saw that the light was good, so He separated the light from the darkness.
God called the light "day" and the darkness "night." There was evening, and there was morning. That was the first day.
God said, "Let there be a sky in the middle of the waters to separate water from water."
So God made the sky and separated the water below it from the water above it. And it happened just as He said.
God called the sky "heavens." There was evening, and there was morning. That was the second day.
God said, "Let the water under the sky gather in one place so dry land can appear." And it happened.
God called the dry land "earth" and the gathered water "seas." God saw that it was good.
Then God said, "Let the earth grow plants. Let them make seeds, and let fruit trees make fruit with seeds in it, each kind matching its own kind." And it happened.
The earth grew plants and trees. Each kind made seeds or fruit with seeds, just as God had said. God saw that it was good.
There was evening, and there was morning. That was the third day.
God said, "Let there be lights in the sky to separate day from night. Let them be signs for seasons, days, and years.
Let them shine on the earth." And it happened.
God made two great lights. The bigger one rules the day, and the smaller one rules the night. He also made the stars.
God placed them in the sky to shine on the earth.
They rule over day and night, and they separate light from darkness. God saw that it was good.
There was evening, and there was morning. That was the fourth day.
God said, "Let the water be full of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the sky."
So God created the great sea animals and every living thing that moves in the water. He made them by their kinds. He also made every kind of bird. God saw that it was good.
God blessed them and said, "Have many children. Fill the seas, and let the birds grow in number on the earth."
There was evening, and there was morning. That was the fifth day.
God said, "Let the earth bring out living animals. Let there be farm animals, crawling things, and wild animals, each by its kind." And it happened.
God made the wild animals, the farm animals, and everything that crawls on the ground, each by its kind. God saw that it was good.
Then God said, "Let Us make people in Our image, like Us. Let them rule over the fish, the birds, the farm animals, and all the earth and every crawling thing."
So God created people in His image. He created them male and female.
God blessed them and said, "Have many children. Fill the earth and take charge of it. Rule over the fish, the birds, and every living thing that moves on the earth."
God said, "Look, I have given you every plant that makes seed and every tree with fruit that has seed. They are for you to eat.
I have given every green plant to the animals, the birds, and everything that crawls on the earth—everything with life in it—for food." And it happened.
God looked at everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening, and there was morning. That was the sixth day.
So the heavens and the earth were finished, along with everything in them.
By the seventh day, God had finished the work He had been doing. On that day He rested from all His work.
God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because He rested on it from all the work He had done in creating.
This is the story of the heavens and the earth when they were created. When the LORD God made the earth and the heavens,
no bush of the field had yet grown on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet come up. the LORD God had not sent rain on the earth, and there was no one to work the ground.
But water came up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
Then the LORD God formed the man from the dust of the ground. He breathed the breath of life into his nose, and the man became a living being.
Now the LORD God had planted a garden in the east, in Eden. He put the man He had formed there.
The LORD God made every tree that is pleasing to look at and good for food grow from the ground. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden. From there it split into four rivers.
The first river is called the Pishon. It winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
The gold of that land is good. Resin and onyx stone are also found there.
The second river is called the Gihon. It winds through the whole land of Cush.
The third river is called the Tigris. It runs east of Ashur. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
The LORD God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
The LORD God commanded the man, "You are free to eat from any tree in the garden.
But you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, because the day you eat from it, you will surely die."
The LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper who is right for him."

The LORD God had formed every wild animal and every bird of the sky from the ground. He brought them to the man to see what he would name them. Whatever the man called each living creature became its name.
So the man gave names to all the livestock, the birds of the sky, and all the wild animals. But no helper was found who was right for Adam.
So the LORD God made the man fall into a deep sleep. While he slept, God took one of the man's ribs and closed the place with flesh.
Then the LORD God made the rib He had taken from the man into a woman. He brought her to the man.
The man said, "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She will be called 'woman,' because she was taken out of man."
That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife, and the two become one flesh.
The man and his wife were both naked, but they felt no shame.
Now the snake was more cunning than any wild animal the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, "Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?"
The woman said to the snake, "We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden.
But God said, 'You must not eat fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden, and you must not touch it, or you will die.'"
The snake said, "You will not surely die.
For God knows that when you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil."

When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, beautiful to look at, and desirable for gaining wisdom, she took some of its fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it.
Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
Then the man and his wife heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid from the LORD God among the trees.
The LORD God called to the man, "Where are you?"
He answered, "I heard Your voice in the garden, and I was afraid because I am naked. So I hid."
The LORD God said, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?"
The man said, "The woman You gave to be with me—she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate."
Then the LORD God said to the woman, "What is this you have done?" The woman said, "The snake tricked me, and I ate."
So the LORD God said to the snake, "Because you have done this, you are cursed more than all livestock and all wild animals. You will crawl on your belly and eat dust all the days of your life.
I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will crush your head, and you will crush His heel."
To the woman He said, "I will greatly increase your pain in childbirth. With pain you will give birth to children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you."

To Adam He said, "Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree about which I commanded you, 'You must not eat from it,' the ground is cursed because of you. Through painful toil you will eat food from it all the days of your life.
It will produce thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your brow you will eat your food until you return to the ground, since from it you were taken. For dust you are, and to dust you will return."
Adam named his wife Eve, because she would become the mother of all the living.
The LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.
And the LORD God said, "The man has now become like one of Us, knowing good and evil. He must not be allowed to reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life and eat, and live forever."
So the LORD God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.
After He drove the man out, He placed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a flaming sword flashing back and forth to guard the way to the tree of life.
Adam knew his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, "With the LORD's help, I have brought forth a man."
Later she gave birth to Cain's brother Abel. Abel took care of sheep, and Cain worked the soil.
In time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the LORD.
Abel also brought the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions. The LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering,
but He did not look with favor on Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and he looked upset.
Then the LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why do you look so upset?"
"If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door. It wants to control you, but you must rule over it."
Cain said to his brother Abel. While they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
Then the LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" Cain replied, "I don't know. Am I responsible for my brother?"
The LORD said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the ground.
Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
When you work the ground, it will no longer yield its crops for you. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth."
Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is greater than I can bear.
Today You have driven me away from the land, and I will be hidden from Your presence. I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."
The LORD said to him, "Not so! If anyone kills Cain, he will suffer vengeance seven times over." Then the LORD put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him.
So Cain went out from the LORD's presence and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
Cain slept with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.
Enoch fathered Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock.
His brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.
Zillah also gave birth to Tubal-cain, who forged all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-cain's sister was Naamah.
Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to me; wives of Lamech, hear my words: I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for injuring me.
If Cain is avenged seven times, then Lamech seventy-seven times."
Adam again slept with his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, "God has granted me another child in place of Abel, since Cain killed him."
Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. At that time people began to call on the name of the LORD.
This is the book of Adam's family line. In the day God created man, He made him in His own likeness.
Male and female He created them, and He blessed them. He called them "Mankind" on the day they were created.
Adam lived 130 years, and he had a son in his own likeness, after his image. He named him Seth.
After Seth was born, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
Adam lived 930 years in all, and then he died.
Seth lived 105 years, and he had a son named Enosh.
After Enosh was born, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
Seth lived 912 years in all, and then he died.
Enosh lived 90 years, and he had a son named Kenan.
After Kenan was born, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.
Enosh lived 905 years in all, and then he died.
Kenan lived 70 years, and he had a son named Mahalalel.
After Mahalalel was born, Kenan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.
Kenan lived 910 years in all, and then he died.
Mahalalel lived 65 years, and he had a son named Jared.
After Jared was born, Mahalalel lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.
Mahalalel lived 895 years in all, and then he died.
Jared lived 162 years, and he had a son named Enoch.
After Enoch was born, Jared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
Jared lived 962 years in all, and then he died.
Enoch lived 65 years, and he had a son named Methuselah.
After Methuselah was born, Enoch walked with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
Enoch walked with God, and then he was gone, because God took him.
Methuselah lived 187 years, and he had a son named Lamech.
After Lamech was born, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
Methuselah lived 969 years in all, and then he died.
Lamech lived 182 years, and he had a son.
He named him Noah and said, "This one will bring us comfort in our work and in the toil of our hands, because of the ground the LORD has cursed."
After Noah was born, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
Lamech lived 777 years in all, and then he died.
Noah was 500 years old when he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
When people began to increase in number on the earth, and daughters were born to them,
the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they married any of them they chose.
Then the LORD said, "My Spirit will not always struggle with people, because they are only human. They will live 120 years."
The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and later too—when the sons of God came to the daughters of men and had children with them. These children became the mighty heroes of old, famous men.
The LORD saw that people's wickedness was great on the earth, and that every plan their hearts made was only evil all the time.
The LORD was sorry that He had made people on the earth, and His heart was filled with pain.
So the LORD said, "I will wipe mankind off the earth—people, animals, creatures that crawl, and birds of the sky—for I am sorry that I made them."
But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
This is the story of Noah's family. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked with God.
Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Now the earth was corrupt in God's sight, and it was full of violence.
God looked at the earth and saw that it was ruined, because everyone had corrupted their way of life on the earth.
God said to Noah, "I have decided to put an end to all living creatures, because the earth is full of violence because of them. I am going to destroy them along with the earth.
Make an ark of gopher wood. Build rooms in it, and cover it inside and outside with pitch.
This is how you will build it: The ark is to be three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
Make a roof for the ark, and finish the walls to within a cubit of the top. Put a door in the side of the ark, and make lower, middle, and upper decks. "
I am going to bring a flood of water on the earth to destroy all life under the sky—everything that has the breath of life. Everything on earth will die.
But I will make My covenant with you. You will go into the ark—you, your sons, your wife, and your sons' wives.
Bring into the ark two of every living creature, male and female, to keep them alive with you.
Two of every kind of bird, animal, and creature that moves along the ground will come to you, so they can stay alive.
Take every kind of food that can be eaten, store it away, and it will be food for you and for them."
Noah did everything just as God commanded him.
The LORD said to Noah, “Come into the ark, you and all your family, because I have seen that you are right with Me in this generation.
Take with you seven of every clean animal, a male and its mate, and two of every unclean animal, a male and its mate.
Also take seven of every bird, males and females, so life can continue on the earth.
In seven days I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will wipe out every living thing I have made.”
Noah did everything the LORD commanded him.
Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came on the earth.
Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives went into the ark to escape the floodwaters.
Clean animals and unclean animals, birds, and everything that crawls on the ground
came to Noah in pairs, male and female, just as God had commanded Noah.
After seven days, the floodwaters came on the earth.
In Noah’s six hundredth year, in the second month, on the seventeenth day, the springs of the great deep burst open, and the windows of heaven opened.
Rain fell on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that very day, Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Noah’s wife, and the three wives of his sons went into the ark with them.
Every kind of wild animal, livestock, crawling creature, and bird—each after its kind—went with them.
They came to Noah in pairs, two by two, from all living things that had breath.
The males and females of all flesh entered, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.
The flood lasted forty days on the earth. The waters rose and lifted the ark, and it floated high above the ground.
The waters grew stronger and rose greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the waters.
The waters rose even more and covered all the high mountains under the whole sky.
The waters rose fifteen cubits above the mountains, and the mountains were covered.
Every living thing that moved on the earth died—birds, livestock, wild animals, every creature that swarms on the earth, and all people.
Everything on dry land that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.
God wiped out every living thing on the ground—people, livestock, crawling creatures, and birds. They were wiped out from the earth. Only Noah and those with him in the ark were left.
The waters stayed strong on the earth for one hundred fifty days.
God remembered Noah and every wild animal and farm animal that was with him in the ark. God sent a wind over the earth, and the water went down.
He closed the springs deep under the earth and the windows of the sky. He stopped the rain from the sky.
The water slowly went back from the earth. After 150 days, the water had gone down a lot.
On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
The water kept going down until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains could be seen.
Forty days later, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark.
He sent out a raven. It flew back and forth until the water dried up from the earth.
Then he sent out a dove to see if the water had gone down from the ground.

But the dove could not find a place to rest. So it came back to him in the ark, because water still covered the whole earth. Noah reached out his hand, caught the dove, and brought it back into the ark.
He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again.
In the evening the dove came back. It had a fresh olive leaf in its beak. Then Noah knew the water had gone down from the earth.
He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again, but it did not come back.
In Noah's six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the water had dried up from the earth. Noah took off the cover of the ark and looked out. He saw that the ground was dry.
By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was dry.
He said, "Go out of the ark. Take your wife, your sons, and your sons' wives with you.
Bring out with you every living thing that is with you—every bird, animal, and creature that moves on the ground—so they can spread across the earth, have many young, and fill the earth."
So Noah went out with his wife, his sons, and his sons' wives.
Every animal, every creature that moves, and every bird—everything that moves on the ground—left the ark by families.
Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took one of every clean animal and clean bird and burned them on the altar.

The LORD smelled the pleasing smell. Then the LORD said in His heart, "I will never again curse the ground because of people, because people's hearts are set on evil from the time they are young. I will never again destroy every living thing, as I have done.
As long as the earth lasts, planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night will not stop."
God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.
Every animal on earth will fear and dread you. Every bird of the sky, every creature that moves on the ground, and every fish in the sea are given into your hands.
Everything that lives and moves will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.
"But you must not eat meat that still has its lifeblood in it.
I will surely hold every animal and every person responsible for taking a human life. I will hold each person responsible for the life of his brother.
Whoever sheds human blood will have his blood shed by man, for God made man in His image.
And as for you, be fruitful and multiply. Spread out over the earth and multiply on it."
Then God said to Noah and his sons with him,
"I am now making My covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
and with every living creature that is with you—the birds, the livestock, and all the wild animals, every creature that came out of the ark.
I promise that never again will all life be cut off by floodwaters. Never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.
This is the sign of the covenant I am making between Me and you and every living creature with you, for all generations to come:
"I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.
Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,
I will remember My covenant between Me and you and all living creatures. The waters will never again become a flood to destroy all life.
The rainbow will be in the clouds, and I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh on the earth.
This is the sign of the covenant I have made between Me and all life on the earth."
The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were Noah's sons, and from them the whole earth was populated.
Noah, a man of the soil, began by planting a vineyard.
He drank some of the wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered in his tent.
Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside.
Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it across their shoulders, and walked backward to cover their father's nakedness. Their faces were turned away, so they did not see their father's nakedness.
When Noah woke from his wine, he learned what his youngest son had done to him.
He said, "Cursed be Canaan! He will be the lowest servant to his brothers."
He also said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be their servant.
May God enlarge Japheth, and may he live in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be their servant."
After the flood, Noah lived 350 more years.
Noah lived a total of 950 years, and then he died.
These are the family lines of Noah. His sons were Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and sons were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
From these people the coastlands of the nations spread out in their lands. Each group had its own language, clan, and nation.
The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty man on the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before the the LORD. That is why people say, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the the LORD."
The first cities of his kingdom were Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar.
From that land he went to Assyria and built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, and Calah.
He also built Resen between Nineveh and Calah, which is the great city.
Mizraim was the father of the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim.
He was also the father of the Pathrusim, Casluhim (from whom the Philistines came), and Caphtorim.
Canaan was the father of Sidon his firstborn, and of Heth.
He was also the father of the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites,
Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites. Later the clans of the Canaanites spread out.
The territory of the Canaanites stretched from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Lasha.
These were the sons of Ham, grouped by their clans, languages, lands, and nations.
Sons were also born to Shem. He was the forefather of all the descendants of Eber, and he was Japheth's brother.
The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arpachshad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.
Two sons were born to Eber. One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided. His brother was named Joktan.
Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
Their home was in the hill country of the east, from Mesha toward Sephar.
These were the sons of Shem, grouped by their clans, languages, lands, and nations.
These were the clans of Noah, listed by their generations and nations. From them the nations spread out over the earth after the flood.
At that time, everyone in the world spoke the same language and used the same words.
As people moved east, they found a flat plain in Shinar and settled there.
They said to one another, "Come, let's make bricks and bake them hard." They used brick instead of stone, and tar for mortar.
Then they said, "Come, let's build a city for ourselves, with a tower that reaches the sky. We want to make a name for ourselves so we won't be scattered all over the earth."
But the LORD came down to see the city and the tower the people were building.
The LORD said, "They are one people, and they all speak the same language. This is just the beginning of what they will do. Soon nothing they plan will be too hard for them.
Come, let's go down and mix up their language so they won't understand each other."
So the LORD scattered them from there over the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.
That is why it was called Babel—because there the LORD mixed up the language of the whole world. From there the LORD scattered them over the whole earth.
These are the family records of Shem. Shem was 100 years old when he became the father of Arphaxad, two years after the flood.
After Arphaxad was born, Shem lived 500 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Arphaxad was 35 years old when he became the father of Shelah.
After Shelah was born, Arphaxad lived 403 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Shelah was 30 years old when he became the father of Eber.
After Eber was born, Shelah lived 403 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Eber was 34 years old when he became the father of Peleg.
After Peleg was born, Eber lived 430 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Peleg was 30 years old when he became the father of Reu.
After Reu was born, Peleg lived 209 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Reu was 32 years old when he became the father of Serug.
After Serug was born, Reu lived 207 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Serug was 30 years old when he became the father of Nahor.
After Nahor was born, Serug lived 200 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Nahor was 29 years old when he became the father of Terah.
After Terah was born, Nahor lived 119 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Terah was 70 years old when he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
These are the family records of Terah: Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Haran became the father of Lot.
Haran died while his father Terah was still alive, in the land where he was born, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
Abram and Nahor married. Abram's wife was named Sarai, and Nahor's wife was named Milcah. Milcah was the daughter of Haran, who was the father of both Milcah and Iscah.
Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot (Haran's son), and his daughter-in-law Sarai (Abram's wife), and they left Ur of the Chaldeans to go to Canaan. When they reached Haran, they settled there.
Terah lived 205 years and died in Haran.
The LORD said to Abram, "Go from your country, your people, and your father's house to the land that I will show you.
I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you. I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing.
I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse those who curse you. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you."
So Abram went, as the LORD had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions they had gathered, along with the servants they had acquired in Haran. They set out for the land of Canaan and arrived there.
Abram traveled through the land as far as the place of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.
The LORD appeared to Abram and said, "To your descendants I will give this land." So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
From there he moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.
Then Abram set out and traveled toward the south.
Now there was a famine in the land, so Abram went down to Egypt to stay there for a while, because the famine was severe.
As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, "I know that you are a beautiful woman.
When the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife,' and they will kill me but let you live.
Please say you are my sister, so that I will be treated well for your sake and my life will be spared because of you."
When Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
When Pharaoh's officials saw her, they praised her to Pharaoh, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's palace.
He treated Abram well for her sake, and Abram acquired sheep, cattle, male donkeys, female donkeys, male servants, female servants, and camels.
But the LORD struck Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
So Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me she was your wife?
Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her as my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go."
Then Pharaoh gave orders concerning him, and they sent him away, along with his wife and everything he had.
Abram went up from Egypt to the Negev. He took his wife, everything he owned, and Lot with him.
Abram was very rich. He had livestock, silver, and gold.
He traveled from the Negev, moving from place to place, until he reached Bethel. He camped between Bethel and Ai, where his tent had been before.
He went back to the place where he had built an altar the first time. There Abram called on the name of the LORD.
Lot, who traveled with Abram, also had flocks, herds, and tents.
The land could not support both of them living together. They had too much, so they could not stay together.
Quarrels broke out between Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen. The Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land at that time.
Abram said to Lot, “Let's not have any arguing between you and me, or between our herdsmen. We are brothers.
The whole land is open before you. Please separate from me. If you go to the left, I'll go to the right. If you go to the right, I'll go to the left.”

Lot looked up and saw the whole Jordan Valley. It was well watered everywhere, before the the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. It looked like the garden of the the LORD and like the land of Egypt toward Zoar.
So Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley and traveled east. The two men separated.
Abram stayed in the land of Canaan, while Lot settled in the cities of the valley and camped near Sodom.
The men of Sodom were very wicked sinners against the the LORD.
After Lot left, the the LORD spoke to Abram. He said, “Look up from where you are. Look north, south, east, and west.
I will give you and your descendants all the land you see, forever.
I will make your descendants as many as the dust of the earth. If anyone can count the dust of the earth, then your descendants can be counted too.
Get up and walk through the land, from one end to the other. I am giving it to you.”
So Abram moved his tent and settled near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron. There he built an altar to the the LORD.
In the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
these kings made war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
All of them joined together in the Valley of Siddim, which is the Salt Sea.
They had served Chedorlaomer for twelve years, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings with him came and defeated the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
and the Horites in their hill country of Seir, all the way to El-paran near the desert.
Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat, which is Kadesh, and defeated all the country of the Amalekites and also the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
The king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar, went out and lined up for battle against them in the Valley of Siddim.
They fought four kings against five.
The Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell into them, while the rest fled to the hills.
The invaders took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food and left.
They also took Lot, Abram's nephew, and his possessions, because he was living in Sodom, and they left.

Then a man who had escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew. Abram was living near the oak trees of Mamre the Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and the brother of Aner. These men had made an agreement with Abram.
When Abram heard that his relative had been captured, he led out his trained men, born in his house—318 of them—and chased the enemy as far as Dan.
He split his forces against them at night, he and his servants, and defeated them. He chased them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
He brought back all the goods. He also brought back his relative Lot and his goods, and the women and the people.
After Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, which is the King's Valley.
Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High.
He blessed Abram and said, "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth;
and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand." Then Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people, but you may keep the goods."
Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I have sworn to the LORD, God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth,
that I will not take a thread or a sandal strap from anything that is yours, so that you cannot say, 'I made Abram rich.'
I will take nothing except what the young men have eaten, and the share for the men who went with me—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their share."
After these things, the word of the the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying, "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, and your reward will be very great."
Abram said, "O Lord the LORD, what will You give me? I still have no children, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus.
Look, You have given me no children, so a servant born in my house will inherit everything I own."
Then the word of the the LORD came to him, saying, "This man will not be your heir, but a son from your own body will be your heir."
He took him outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars, if you can count them." Then He said, "Your descendants will be that many."
Abram believed the the LORD, and the the LORD counted it to him as righteousness.
He also said to him, "I am the the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to own."
But Abram said, "O Lord the LORD, how can I know that I will inherit it?"
He said to him, "Bring Me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."
Abram brought all these animals to Him, cut them in half, and placed each half opposite the other. But he did not cut the birds in half.
Birds of prey came down on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a thick, terrifying darkness came over him.
Then the the LORD said to Abram, "Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs. They will be enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years.
But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will leave with great wealth.
You, however, will go to your ancestors in peace and be buried at a good old age.
In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure."
When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, a smoking firepot and a blazing torch passed between the pieces.
On that day the the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, "To your descendants I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates—
the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, and Kadmonites;
and the Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites."
Now Sarai, Abram's wife, had not had any children. She had an Egyptian servant named Hagar.
So Sarai said to Abram, "The LORD has kept me from having children. Please sleep with my servant. Maybe I can have a family through her." Abram listened to Sarai.
After Abram had lived ten years in Canaan, Sarai took her Egyptian servant Hagar and gave her to Abram as his wife.
Abram slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When she saw she was pregnant, she looked down on her mistress.
Then Sarai said to Abram, "You are to blame for this wrong against me. I gave my servant to you, and now that she is pregnant, she looks down on me. May the LORD decide between you and me."
Abram said, "Your servant is in your hands. Do what you think is best." Then Sarai treated her badly, and Hagar ran away.
The angel of the LORD found her by a spring in the desert, on the road to Shur.
He said, "Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" She answered, "I am running away from my mistress Sarai."
The angel of the LORD said to her, "Go back to your mistress and obey her."
The angel of the LORD also said, "I will increase your family so much that no one can count them."

The angel of the LORD continued, "You are pregnant, and you will have a son. Name him Ishmael, because the the LORD has heard your suffering. He will be like a wild donkey. He will fight with everyone, and everyone will fight with him. He will live in conflict with all his brothers."
She called the the LORD who spoke to her, "You are the God who sees me," because she said, "Have I really seen the One who sees me?"
So the well was called Beer-lahai-roi. It is between Kadesh and Bered.
Hagar had a son for Abram, and Abram named his son Ishmael.
Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar had Ishmael.
When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless.
I will make My covenant between Me and you, and I will make you very fruitful."
Abram fell facedown, and God spoke with him.
"As for Me, this is My covenant with you: You will be the father of many nations.
No longer will you be called Abram; your name will be Abraham, because I have made you the father of many nations.
I will make you very fruitful. I will make nations come from you, and kings will come from you."
"I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you for the generations to come. I will be your God and the God of your descendants after you.
I will give to you and your descendants after you the land where you are living now—all the land of Canaan—as an everlasting possession. I will be their God.
God said to Abraham, "As for you, you must keep My covenant, you and your descendants after you for the generations to come."
"This is My covenant with you and your descendants after you, which you are to keep: Every male among you must be circumcised.
You must circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and this will be the sign of the covenant between Me and you.
Throughout your generations, every male among you who is eight days old must be circumcised, including those born in your household or bought with money from any foreigner who is not your descendant.
Whether born in your household or bought with money, they must be circumcised. My covenant will be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
Any uncircumcised male who has not been circumcised in the flesh will be cut off from his people, because he has broken My covenant."
God said to Abraham, "As for your wife Sarai, do not call her Sarai; her name will be Sarah.
I will bless her and give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations; kings of nations will come from her."
Abraham fell facedown and laughed. He said to himself, "Can a child be born to a man who is one hundred years old? Can Sarah, who is ninety, have a child?"
Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live under Your blessing!"
God said, "No, but your wife Sarah will bear you a son, and you will name him Isaac. I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
As for Ishmael, I have heard you. I will bless him and make him very fruitful. I will multiply him greatly. He will be the father of twelve princes, and I will make him into a great nation.
But I will establish My covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year."
When He had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.
On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and every male in his household, whether born there or bought with money, and circumcised them, just as God had told him.
Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised,
and his son Ishmael was thirteen.
Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on the same day.
Every male in Abraham's household, whether born there or bought with money from a foreigner, was circumcised with him.
The LORD appeared to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day.
He looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the tent door to meet them and bowed low to the ground.
He said, "My lord, if I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass by your servant.
Please let a little water be brought so you can wash your feet and rest under the tree.
I will bring a piece of bread so you may refresh yourselves. Then you can go on, since you have come to your servant." "Do as you have said."
Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah and said, "Quickly! Prepare three measures of fine flour, knead it, and make cakes."
Abraham ran to the herd, took a tender, good calf, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.
He took curds and milk and the calf he had prepared, and set it before them. He stood by them under the tree while they ate.
They said to him, "Where is Sarah your wife?" He said, "She is in the tent."
He said, "I will surely return to you at this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son." Sarah was listening at the tent door behind him.
Now Abraham and Sarah were old, advanced in years, and Sarah was past childbearing age.
Sarah laughed to herself and said, "After I am worn out, and my lord is old, will I really have pleasure?"
The LORD said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say that she would really bear a child now that she is old?
Is anything too hard for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you, at this time next year, and Sarah will have a son."
Sarah denied it and said, "I did not laugh," because she was afraid. But He said, "No, you did laugh."
The men rose up from there and looked toward Sodom, and Abraham walked with them to send them on their way.
The LORD said, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do,
since Abraham will surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed through him?

For I have known him, so that he may command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing righteousness and justice, so that the LORD may bring to Abraham what He has spoken about him."
The LORD said, "The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and their sin is very grave.
I will go down now and see if they have really done all the evil that people are crying out about; and if not, I will know."
The men turned away from there and went toward Sodom, but Abraham still stood before the LORD.
Abraham came near and said, "Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
Suppose there are fifty righteous within the city. Will You then sweep away the place and not spare it for the fifty righteous who are in it?

It would be wrong for You to do such a thing, to put the righteous to death with the wicked, so that the righteous are treated like the wicked! It would be wrong for You! Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?"
The LORD said, "If I find fifty righteous in Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake."
Abraham answered and said, "Look, I have undertaken to speak to the Lord, I who am but dust and ashes.
Suppose five of the fifty righteous are lacking. Will You destroy the whole city for lack of five?" He said, "I will not destroy it if I find forty-five."
He spoke to Him again and said, "Suppose forty are found there." He said, "I will not do it for the sake of forty."
Then he said, "Please don't let the Lord be angry, and I will speak. Suppose thirty are found there." He said, "I will not do it if I find thirty."
He said, "Look, I have undertaken to speak to the Lord. Suppose twenty are found there." He said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty."
Then he said, "Please don't let the Lord be angry, and I will speak just once more. Suppose ten are found there." He said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of ten."
When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He went away, and Abraham returned to his place.
Two angels came to Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom. When Lot saw them, he got up to meet them and bowed with his face to the ground.
He said, "Please, my lords, turn aside to your servant's house. Wash your feet and stay the night. Then you can get up early and go on your way." "No," they said, "we will stay in the street."
But he urged them strongly, so they turned aside to him and entered his house. He made a feast for them and baked bread without yeast, and they ate.
Before they lay down, the men of the city—the men of Sodom, both young and old, all the people from every part of the city—surrounded the house.
They called to Lot and said to him, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so we can have sex with them."
Lot went out to them at the door and shut the door behind him.
He said, "Please, my brothers, do not do such a wicked thing.

Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you can do to them what seems good to you. Only do nothing to these men, because they are staying in my home."

They said, "Get out of the way! This fellow came to live here, and now he wants to play judge! Now we will do worse to you than to them." Then they pushed hard against Lot and came near to break the door.
The men reached out their hands, brought Lot into the house, and shut the door.
They struck all the men at the door, young and old, with blindness, so that they could not find the door no matter how hard they tried.
The men said to Lot, "Do you still have anyone here—sons-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone else in the city? Bring them out of this place.
For we are about to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has become so great before the LORD that the LORD has sent us to destroy it."

Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law who were to marry his daughters. He said, "Get up and get out of this place, because the LORD is about to destroy the city." But to his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking.
When dawn came, the angels urged Lot, saying, "Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away in the punishment of the city."
He hesitated, but the men seized his hand, his wife's hand, and his two daughters' hands. The LORD was merciful to him, and they brought him out and set him outside the city.
When they brought them out, one said, "Run for your life! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere in the valley. Run to the hills, or you will be swept away."
Lot said to them, "Oh no, my lord!
Your servant has found favor in your sight, and you have shown great kindness by saving my life. But I cannot run to the hills. Disaster might catch me, and I would die.
Look, this town is near enough to run to, and it is small. Please let me escape there—it is only a little place—so my life may be saved."
He said to him, "All right, I have granted your request about this matter too; I will not destroy the town you spoke of.
Hurry and escape there, because I cannot do anything until you get there." So the town was called Zoar.
The sun had risen over the earth when Lot came to Zoar.
Then the LORD rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah—from the LORD out of heaven.
He overthrew those cities and the whole valley, and all the people who lived in the cities, and also the plants of the ground.
But Lot's wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
Abraham got up early in the morning and went to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and toward all the land of the valley, and he saw smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.
When God destroyed the cities of the valley, God remembered Abraham and rescued Lot from the destruction. When He overthrew the cities where Lot had lived, He spared Lot.
Lot went up from Zoar with his two daughters and lived in the hills, because he was afraid to live in Zoar. He and his two daughters lived in a cave.
The older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is no man on earth left to marry us.
Come, let us get our father drunk with wine, and we will lie with him, so our family line can continue."
That night they got their father drunk with wine. The older daughter went in and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day the older daughter said to the younger, "Look, I lay with my father last night. Let us get him drunk with wine again tonight, and you go in and lie with him, so our family line can continue."
So that night they got their father drunk with wine again. The younger daughter went in and lay with him, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter gave birth to a son and named him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites to this day.
The younger daughter gave birth to a son and named him Ben-ammi. He is the father of the Ammonites to this day.
Abraham left there and traveled to the Negev. He settled between Kadesh and Shur and lived in Gerar.
Abraham said about his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." So Abimelech, king of Gerar, sent for Sarah and took her.
But that night God came to Abimelech in a dream and said, "You are about to die because of the woman you took. She is already married."
Abimelech had not gone near her. He said, "Lord, will You destroy a nation that has done nothing wrong?
Didn't he say to me, 'She is my sister'? And didn't she say, 'He is my brother'? I did this honestly and in good faith."
God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know you did this honestly. I also kept you from sinning against Me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
Now return the man's wife. He is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not return her, know for sure that you and all who belong to you will die."
Early the next morning, Abimelech called all his servants and told them everything. They were very afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abraham and said, "What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you brought such a great sin on me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not be done.
What were you thinking when you did this?"
Abraham answered, "I thought, 'People here do not respect God, and they will kill me because of my wife.'
She is indeed my sister. She is my father's daughter, but not my mother's daughter. She became my wife.
When God led me away from my father's house, I said to her, 'Please do me this favor: Everywhere we go, say about me, "He is my brother."'"
Then Abimelech took sheep, cattle, male and female servants, and gave them to Abraham. He also returned his wife Sarah to him.
Abimelech said, "Look, my land is open to you. Live wherever you like."
To Sarah he said, "I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. This is to show everyone with you that you are innocent. You are cleared of all blame."
Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, so they could have children again.
For the LORD had kept all the women in Abimelech's household from having children because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
The LORD visited Sarah, just as He had promised, and the LORD did for her what He had said.
So Sarah became pregnant and had a son for Abraham in his old age. It happened at the exact time God had promised.
When Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, just as God had commanded him.
Abraham was one hundred years old when Isaac was born.
Sarah said, "God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."
She also said, "Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have had a son for him in his old age."
The child grew and was weaned. On the day Isaac was weaned, Abraham held a great feast.
But Sarah saw that the son Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking.
So she said to Abraham, "Send away this servant woman and her son, because the son of this servant woman will not share the inheritance with my son Isaac."
This matter deeply troubled Abraham because it concerned his son.
But God said to Abraham, "Do not be upset about the boy and your servant woman. Listen to everything Sarah tells you, because your descendants will come through Isaac.
I will also make the son of the servant woman into a nation, because he is your offspring."

Early the next morning Abraham took some food and a leather bag of water and gave them to Hagar. He placed them on her shoulders, along with the boy, and sent her away. She left and wandered in the Desert of Beersheba.
When the water in the bag was gone, she put the boy under a bush.
Then she went and sat down a good distance away, about as far as a bow can shoot, because she thought, "I cannot watch the boy die." As she sat there, she began to cry.
God heard the boy crying, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, because God has heard the boy's cry where he is.
Get up, lift the boy, and hold him by the hand, because I will make him into a great nation."
Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the bag with water and gave the boy a drink.
God was with the boy as he grew. He lived in the desert and became an archer.
While he lived in the Desert of Paran, his mother chose a wife for him from Egypt.
At that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do.

Now swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me or my children or my descendants. Show the same kindness to me and to the land where you are living as a foreigner that I have shown to you."
Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized.
Abimelech said, "I did not know who did this. You did not tell me, and I heard about it only today."
So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a treaty.
Abraham set apart seven female lambs from the flock.
Abimelech asked Abraham, "What is the meaning of these seven female lambs you have set apart?"
He replied, "Accept these seven lambs from my hand as proof that I dug this well."
So that place was called Beersheba, because the two of them swore an oath there.
After they made the treaty at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, returned to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.
Abraham stayed in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
After these things, God tested Abraham. He said to him, "Abraham!" Abraham answered, "Here I am."
God said, "Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains I will tell you about."

Early the next morning, Abraham got up and saddled his donkey. He took two of his young men and his son Isaac with him. He cut wood for the burnt offering. Then he set out for the place God had told him about.
On the third day, Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
Abraham said to his young men, "Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there and worship, and then we will come back to you."
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and put it on his son Isaac. He carried the fire and the knife in his hand. The two of them walked on together.
Isaac spoke to his father Abraham. He said, "My father!" Abraham said, "Here I am, my son." Isaac said, "We have the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?"
Abraham said, "God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son." So the two of them walked on together.
When they reached the place God had told him about, Abraham built an altar there. He arranged the wood on it. He tied up his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to kill his son.
But the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven. He said, "Abraham! Abraham!" Abraham answered, "Here I am."
The angel said, "Do not raise your hand against the boy. Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God, because you have not kept your son, your only son, from Me."
Abraham looked up and saw a ram behind him. Its horns were caught in a bush. Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering instead of his son.
Abraham named that place The LORD Will Provide. People still say today, "On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided."
The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time.
He said, "I swear by Myself, says the LORD, that because you have done this and have not kept your son, your only son, from Me,
I will surely bless you. I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will defeat their enemies.
All the nations on earth will be blessed through your descendants, because you obeyed My voice."
Then Abraham went back to his young men. They got up and traveled together to Beersheba. Abraham settled there.
After these things, someone told Abraham, "Milcah has also had children for your brother Nahor.
They are Uz, his firstborn, Buz, his brother, Kemuel, the father of Aram,
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel."
Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight children Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
Nahor's concubine, Reumah, also had children: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
Sarah lived to be one hundred twenty-seven years old.
She died in Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
Then Abraham got up from beside his dead wife and spoke to the Hittites. He said,
"I am a foreigner and a stranger among you. Sell me a burial place here so I can bury my dead."
"Listen to us, my lord. You are a great leader among us. Bury your dead in the best of our tombs. None of us will keep you from burying your dead."
Then Abraham stood up and bowed down to the people of the land, the Hittites.
He said to them, "If you are willing to let me bury my dead, listen to me and speak to Ephron son of Zohar for me.
Ask him to sell me the cave of Machpelah at the end of his field. I will pay the full price for it as a burial place among you."
Ephron the Hittite was sitting among the people. He answered Abraham in front of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city.
"No, my lord," he said. "Listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave in it. I give it to you in front of my people. Bury your dead."
Again Abraham bowed down to the people of the land.
He said to Ephron in their hearing, "Listen to me, if you will. I will pay for the field. Take the money from me so I can bury my dead there."
"Listen to me, my lord. The land is worth four hundred shekels of silver. But what is that between you and me? Bury your dead."
Abraham agreed to Ephron's price. He weighed out four hundred shekels of silver for him in front of the Hittites, using the standard weight for merchants.
So Ephron's field in Machpelah near Mamre was made Abraham's property. The field, the cave in it, and all the trees inside its borders became his.
This happened in front of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of the city.
After that, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave in the field of Machpelah near Mamre, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan.
So the field and the cave in it were given to Abraham by the Hittites as a burial place.
Abraham was old and had lived a long life. The LORD had blessed him in everything.
Abraham said to his oldest servant, the one in charge of everything he owned, "Put your hand under my thigh.
Swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I live.
Instead, go to my country and my family, and get a wife for my son Isaac."
The servant asked him, "What if the woman does not want to follow me to this land? Should I take your son back to the land you came from?"
Abraham said, "Make sure you do not take my son back there.

The LORD, the God of heaven, who took me from my father's house and my homeland, spoke to me and promised me with an oath that He would give this land to my descendants. He will send His angel ahead of you, and you will bring back a wife for my son from there.
If the woman is not willing to follow you, then you are free from this oath. Only do not take my son back there."
So the servant put his hand under Abraham's thigh and swore to him about this matter.
The servant took ten of his master's camels and left, carrying all kinds of good things from his master. He set out for the city of Nahor in Mesopotamia.
He had the camels kneel down by the well outside the city. It was evening, the time when women come out to draw water.
He said, "the LORD, God of my master Abraham, please give me success today and show kindness to my master Abraham.
See, I am standing by the spring, and the daughters of the men of this city are coming out to draw water.

Let the young woman to whom I say, 'Please lower your jar so I can drink,' and who answers, 'Drink, and I will water your camels too,' be the one You have chosen for Your servant Isaac. By this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master."
Before he finished speaking, Rebekah came out. She was born to Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor. She carried a jar on her shoulder.
The young woman was very beautiful, a virgin, and no man had been with her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came back up.
The servant ran to meet her and said, "Please let me have a little water from your jar."
"Drink, my lord," she said. She quickly lowered her jar onto her hand and gave him a drink.
When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, "I will draw water for your camels too, until they have had enough to drink."
She quickly emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well to draw more water, and drew enough for all his camels.
The man watched her quietly to learn whether the LORD had made his journey successful or not.
When the camels had finished drinking, the man took a gold nose ring weighing a beka and two gold bracelets weighing ten shekels, and put them on her wrists.
He asked, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?"
"I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor," she answered.
She also said to him, "We have plenty of straw and feed, and room for you to spend the night."
Then the man bowed down and worshiped the LORD.

He said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not stopped showing kindness and truth to my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the right road to the house of my master's relatives."
The young woman ran and told her mother's household about these things.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban. He ran out to the man at the spring.

When he saw the nose ring and the bracelets on his sister's wrists, and when he heard Rebekah say what the man had told her, he went out to the man. There he was, standing by the camels at the spring.
Laban said, "Come in, you who are blessed by the LORD. Why are you standing outside? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels."
So the man went into the house. He unloaded the camels and gave them straw and feed. He also brought water to wash his feet and the feet of the men with him.
Food was set before him, but he said, "I will not eat until I have said what I need to say." "Speak," they said.
"The the LORD has greatly blessed my master, and he has become very rich. He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female servants, camels and donkeys.
My master's wife Sarah bore a son to him in her old age, and my master has given him everything he owns.
"My master made me swear, 'You must not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, where I live.
Instead, go to my father's house and my family, and get a wife for my son.'
I asked my master, 'What if the woman will not follow me?'
He answered, 'The the LORD, before whom I have walked, will send His angel with you and make your journey successful, so you can get a wife for my son from my family and my father's house.'
You will be free from my oath if you go to my family and they refuse to give her to you. Then you will be free from my oath.'
"Today I came to the spring and said, 'The the LORD, God of my master Abraham, if You are going to make my journey successful, please help me.'
See, I am standing by the spring. When the young woman comes out to draw water, I will say to her, 'Please give me a little water from your jar.'
She will answer, 'Drink, and I will draw water for your camels too.' Let that woman be the one the LORD has chosen for my master's son.
"Before I finished speaking in my heart, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water. I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'
She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, 'Drink, and I will water your camels too.' So I drank, and she watered the camels.
I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' She said, 'I am the daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.' Then I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists.
Then I bowed down and worshiped the LORD. I praised the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who led me on the right road to get the daughter of my master's brother for his son.
"Now, if you are going to show kindness and truth to my master, tell me. If not, tell me, so I will know which way to turn."
Laban and Bethuel answered, "This matter comes from the LORD. We cannot say anything to you, either good or bad."
"Rebekah is here in front of you. Take her and go, and let her be the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has spoken."
When Abraham's servant heard their words, he bowed to the ground before the LORD.
Then the servant brought out silver and gold jewelry and clothes and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave costly gifts to her brother and her mother.
He and the men with him ate and drank, and they spent the night there. When they got up in the morning, he said, "Send me back to my master."
Her brother and her mother said, "Let the young woman stay with us for ten days or so. After that, she can go."
But he said, "Do not delay me. The LORD has made my journey successful. Send me on my way so I can go to my master."
They said, "Let us call the young woman and ask her."
They called Rebekah and asked her, "Will you go with this man?" She said, "I will go."
So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse and Abraham's servant and his men.
They blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your descendants take over the cities of their enemies."
Then Rebekah and her young women got up, rode on the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.
Now Isaac had come from Beer-lahai-roi and was living in the Negev.
In the evening Isaac went out to the field to pray. He looked up and saw camels coming.
Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac. She got down from her camel.
She asked the servant, "Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?" The servant said, "He is my master." So she took her veil and covered herself.
Then the servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah. He married Rebekah, and she became his wife. He loved her, and she comforted him after his mother's death.
Abraham took another wife, named Keturah.
She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan. Dedan's sons were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were sons of Keturah.
Abraham gave everything he owned to Isaac.
While he was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from his son Isaac, eastward to the east country.
He breathed his last and died at a good old age, old and full of years. Then he was gathered to his people.
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, east of Mamre.
Abraham had bought that field from the Hittites. There he buried his wife Sarah.
After Abraham's death, God blessed his son Isaac. Isaac was living near Beer-lahai-roi.
These are the family lines of Abraham's son Ishmael, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's slave, bore to Abraham.
These are the names of Ishmael's sons, listed in the order of their birth: Nebaioth, the firstborn, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These were Ishmael's sons, and these are their names by their villages and camps. They were twelve leaders of their tribes.
Ishmael lived 137 years. He breathed his last and died, and he was gathered to his people.
His descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt, as you travel toward Assyria. He died among all his relatives.
This is the family history of Isaac, Abraham's son. Abraham was Isaac's father.
Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram and sister of Laban the Aramean.
Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife, because she could not have children. The LORD answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.
The babies struggled inside her. She said, "If this is so, why did I get pregnant?" So she went to ask the LORD.
The LORD said to her, "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from your body. One people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger."
When the time came for her to give birth, there were twins in her womb.
The first came out red and hairy all over, like a garment. They named him Esau.
After that, his brother came out with his hand holding Esau's heel. They named him Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when they were born.
The boys grew up. Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the open country. Jacob was a quiet man who stayed among the tents.
Isaac loved Esau because he brought him game. Rebekah loved Jacob.
Once Jacob was cooking stew. Esau came in from the field, and he was exhausted.
Esau said to Jacob, "Let me eat some of that red stew, because I am exhausted!" That is why he was called Edom.
Jacob said, "Sell me your birthright today."
Esau said, "Look, I am about to die. What good is the birthright to me?"
Jacob said, "Swear to me today." So Esau swore and sold his birthright to Jacob.
Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. Esau ate and drank, got up, and went away. So Esau treated his birthright as if it meant nothing.
There was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that happened in Abraham's days. Isaac went to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, in Gerar.
The LORD appeared to him and said, "Do not go down to Egypt. Live in the land I will show you.
Stay in this land, and I will be with you and bless you. I will give all these lands to you and your descendants, and I will keep the promise I made to your father Abraham. "
I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky. I will give your descendants all these lands, and all nations on earth will be blessed through your descendants.
I will do this because Abraham obeyed Me and kept My rules, My commands, My laws, and My teachings."

The men of that place asked about his wife. Isaac said, "She is my sister," because he was afraid to say, "She is my wife." He thought, "The men of this place might kill me because of Rebekah, because she is beautiful."
After Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech, king of the Philistines, looked out through a window. He saw Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.
Abimelech called Isaac and said, "Look, she is your wife! Why did you say, 'She is my sister'?" Isaac said to him, "I said it because I thought I might die because of her."
Abimelech said, "What have you done to us? One of the people could have slept with your wife, and you would have made us guilty."
Abimelech ordered all the people, "Anyone who harms this man or his wife will be put to death."
Isaac planted crops in that land. That same year he gathered a hundred times as much, because the LORD blessed him.
Isaac became very rich and kept growing richer.
He had large flocks and herds and many servants, so the Philistines became jealous of him.
They filled with dirt all the wells his father's servants had dug in Abraham's time.
Abimelech said to Isaac, "Leave us. You are much stronger than we are."
Isaac left and camped in the Gerar Valley, where he stayed.
Isaac dug again the wells that had been dug in Abraham's time. The Philistines had filled them in after Abraham died. Isaac gave them the same names his father had given them.
Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found a well of fresh water.
The herdsmen of Gerar argued with Isaac's herdsmen. They said, "This water is ours." So Isaac named the well Esek, because they quarreled with him.
They dug another well, and they argued over that one too. Isaac named it Sitnah.
He moved on and dug another well. No one argued over it. He named it Rehoboth and said, "Now the LORD has made room for us, and we will grow in this land."
From there Isaac went up to Beersheba.

The LORD appeared to him that night and said, "I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, because I am with you. I will bless you and give you many descendants because of My servant Abraham."
Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the LORD. He set up his tent there, and his servants dug a well.
Abimelech came from Gerar with Ahuzzath, his friend, and Phicol, the commander of his army.
Isaac asked them, "Why have you come to me? You hate me and sent me away."
They said, "We see clearly that the LORD has been with you. So we said, 'Let there be a sworn promise between us and you. Let us make an agreement with you, that you will not harm us.
Just as we did not hurt you and did only good to you, and sent you away in peace, you are now blessed by the LORD.'"
Isaac made a feast for them, and they ate and drank.
They got up early the next morning and swore an oath to each other. Isaac sent them away, and they left in peace.
That same day, Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had dug. They said, "We found water."
Isaac named the well Shibah. That is why the city is called Beersheba to this day.
When Esau was forty years old, he married Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite.
These wives made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah.
When Isaac was old, his eyes were so weak that he could not see well. He called his older son Esau and said, "My son." Esau answered, "Here I am."
Isaac said, "I am old now, and I do not know when I will die.
So take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field to hunt some wild game for me.
Then make the kind of tasty food I love, bring it to me, and I will eat it. After that, I will bless you before I die."
Rebekah was listening while Isaac spoke to his son Esau. When Esau went out to the field to hunt game and bring it back,
Rebekah said to her son Jacob, "I heard your father tell your brother Esau,
