All the people saw the thunder and lightning, heard the trumpet, and saw the mountain smoking. They were afraid and shook, and they stood far away.
They said to Moses, "You speak to us, and we will listen. But do not let God speak to us, or we will die."
Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid, because God has come to test you. He wants you to respect Him so that you will not sin."
The people stood far away, while Moses went near the thick darkness where God was.
The LORD said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites, 'You have seen for yourselves that I spoke to you from heaven.
You must not make gods of silver to stand beside Me, and you must not make gods of gold for yourselves.

Make an altar of earth for Me, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle. Wherever I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
If you make an altar of stone for Me, do not build it with cut stones, because using a tool on it would make it unclean.
Do not go up to My altar by steps, so that your nakedness is not exposed on it.'"
These are the rules you must set before them.
If you buy a Hebrew servant, he must serve six years. In the seventh year, he goes free without paying anything.
If he came alone, he leaves alone. If he has a wife, she leaves with him.
If his master gives him a wife and she has sons or daughters for him, the wife and her children belong to the master. The man leaves alone.
But if the servant says, “I love my master, my wife, and my children. I will not go free,”
then his master must take him to God. He must take him to the door or the doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then the servant will serve his master for life.
If a man sells his daughter as a servant, she does not go free the way male servants do.
If she does not please the master who chose her for himself, he must let her be bought back. He may not sell her to foreigners, because he broke his promise to her.
If he chooses her for his son, he must treat her like a daughter.
If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the first wife’s food, clothing, or rights as a wife.
If he does not do these three things for her, she goes free without paying money.
Anyone who hits a person and kills him must be put to death.
But if he did not plan it, and God let it happen, I will give you a place where he can run.
But if someone plans to kill his neighbor on purpose, you must take him from My altar so he can be put to death.
Anyone who hits his father or mother must be put to death.
Anyone who kidnaps a person and sells him, or is caught with him, must be put to death.
Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.
If men quarrel and one hits the other with a stone or his fist, and the man does not die but stays in bed,
and later gets up and walks outside with a cane, the one who hit him is not guilty. He only has to pay for the time the man could not work and pay for his healing.
If a man beats his male or female servant with a rod and the servant dies from it, the man must be punished.
But if the servant lives for a day or two, the owner is not punished, because the servant is his property.

If men fight and hit a pregnant woman, causing her baby to be born too early, but no serious harm comes to her or the baby, the man who hit her must pay a fine. The husband sets the amount, and he pays what the judges decide.
But if there is serious harm, you must take a life for a life.
Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
Burn for burn, wound for wound, and bruise for bruise.
If a man hits his male or female servant and ruins the servant’s eye, he must set the servant free because of the eye.
If he knocks out the servant’s tooth, he must set the servant free because of the tooth.
If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must be stoned, and no one may eat its meat. The owner is not guilty.
But if the ox has gored before and the owner was warned but did not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, the ox must be stoned and the owner must also be put to death.
If a payment is set to save his life, he must pay whatever amount is set.
This same rule applies if the ox gores a son or a daughter.
If the ox gores a male or female servant, the owner must pay the servant’s master thirty silver coins, and the ox must be stoned.
If a man uncovers a pit or digs one and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls into it,
the owner of the pit must pay. He must give money to the animal’s owner, and he keeps the dead animal.
If one man’s ox kills another man’s ox, they must sell the living ox and divide the money. They must also divide the dead ox.
But if it was known that the ox had gored before and the owner did not restrain it, the owner must pay one ox for the other, and he keeps the dead ox.
If a man steals an ox or a sheep and kills it or sells it, he must pay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
If a thief is caught breaking in and is struck and killed, no one is guilty of his death.
But if the sun has risen, killing him is a crime. The thief must pay in full; if he has nothing, he must be sold to pay for his theft.
If the stolen animal is found alive in his possession, whether it is an ox, a donkey, or a sheep, he must pay double.
If a man lets his animal loose so it grazes in someone else's field or vineyard, he must pay with the best of his own field and vineyard.
If a fire breaks out and spreads to thorn bushes, burning up stacked grain, standing grain, or a field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.
If someone gives a neighbor money or goods to keep, and they are stolen from the neighbor's house, the thief, if caught, must pay double.
If the thief is not found, the homeowner must go before God to show whether he took his neighbor's property.
In any dispute about an ox, donkey, sheep, clothing, or lost item, if one person says, "This is mine," both must go before God. The one God finds guilty must pay double to his neighbor.
If a man gives a neighbor a donkey, ox, sheep, or any animal to watch, and it dies, is injured, or is stolen with no one watching,
the two men must swear an oath before the LORD that the watcher did not take the animal. The owner must accept it, and the watcher will not have to pay.
But if the animal was stolen from him, he must pay the owner.
If it was torn by a wild animal, he must bring the remains as proof; he will not have to pay for the torn animal.
If a man borrows an animal from a neighbor and it is injured or dies while the owner is not present, he must pay full compensation.
If the owner was present, no payment is required. If the animal was hired, its loss is covered by the rental price.
If a man seduces a young woman who is not engaged and sleeps with her, he must pay the bride-price and marry her.
If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, the man must still pay the same amount as the bride-price for a virgin.
You must not allow a sorceress to live.
Anyone who has sexual relations with an animal must be put to death.
Anyone who sacrifices to any god except the LORD alone must be destroyed.
Do not mistreat or oppress a foreigner, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
Do not mistreat any widow or orphan.
If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to Me, I will surely hear their cry.
My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword; your wives will become widows, and your children will become orphans.
If you lend money to My people, to the poor among you, do not treat him like a moneylender; do not charge him interest.
If you take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, return it to him by sunset.
For that cloak is his only covering; it is his garment for his body. What else will he sleep in? If he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am gracious.
You must not blaspheme God or curse a ruler of your people.
Do not delay your offerings or your firstfruits. Give Me the firstborn of your sons.
Do the same with your oxen and your sheep. Let them stay with their mother for seven days, but give them to Me on the eighth day.
You are to be My holy people. Do not eat meat torn by wild animals in the field; throw it to the dogs.
You must not spread false rumors. Don't team up with evil people to give a false witness.
Don't follow the crowd to do wrong. When you speak in a case, don't twist justice by siding with the crowd.
Don't show special favor to a poor person in court.
If you meet your enemy's ox or donkey wandering away, you must bring it back to him.
If you see the donkey of someone who hates you fallen under its load, don't leave it there. Help him get it up.
Don't deny justice to a poor person in his lawsuit.
Stay far from a false charge. Don't kill innocent or honest people, because I won't let the guilty go free.
Don't take a bribe, because a bribe blinds people who can see and twists the words of honest people.
Don't mistreat a foreigner. You know how it feels to be a foreigner, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
Plant your land for six years and gather its crops.
But in the seventh year, let it rest and leave it alone. Then the poor among your people can eat from it, and wild animals can eat what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove.
Work for six days, but rest on the seventh day. That way your ox and your donkey can rest, and your servant's son and the foreigner can rest too.
Be careful to do everything I have told you. Don't call on the names of other gods, and don't let those names be heard from your lips.
Three times a year, celebrate a feast to Me.

Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, just as I commanded you. Eat unleavened bread for seven days at the set time in the month of Abib, because you came out of Egypt in that month. No one should come to Me empty-handed.
Keep the Feast of Harvest with the first crops from your fields, and the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you bring in your crops from the field.
Three times a year, all your men must come before the Lord the LORD.
Don't offer the blood of My sacrifice with bread that has yeast in it, and don't let the fat from My feast stay until morning.
Bring the best of the first crops from your soil to the house of the LORD your God. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Look, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and bring you to the place I have prepared.
Pay attention to him and listen to his voice. Don't rebel against him, because he won't forgive your sins, since My name is in him.
But if you listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.
My angel will go before you and bring you to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
Don't bow down to their gods or serve them. Don't follow their ways. Instead, tear down their idols and smash their sacred stones.
Serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. I will take sickness away from you.
No woman in your land will miscarry or be unable to have children. I will give you a full life.
I will send My terror ahead of you, and I will throw into confusion every nation you meet. I will make all your enemies turn and run.
I will send hornets ahead of you to drive out the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites before you.
I won't drive them out in one year, or the land would become empty and wild animals would multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out before you, until you grow in number and take over the land.

I will set your borders from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates River. I will hand the people who live in the land over to you, and you will drive them out.
Don't make a treaty with them or with their gods.
They must not live in your land, or they will cause you to sin against Me. If you serve their gods, it will surely become a trap for you.
Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel. You are to worship at a distance,
but Moses alone may approach the LORD. The others must not come near, and the people may not come up with him.”
When Moses went and told the people all the LORD's words and laws, they answered with one voice, “All the words the LORD has spoken, we will do.”

Moses then wrote down everything the LORD had said. He got up early the next morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain. He also set up twelve stone pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
Then he sent young Israelite men, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as fellowship offerings to the LORD.
Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls. The other half he sprinkled on the altar.
Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it aloud to the people. They said, “We will do everything the LORD has said, and we will obey.”
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people. He said, “This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in keeping with all these words.”
Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and the seventy elders of Israel went up
and saw the God of Israel. Under His feet was something like a pavement made of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.
But God did not raise His hand against the leaders of the Israelites. They saw God, and they ate and drank.
The LORD said to Moses, “Come up to Me on the mountain and stay there, and I will give you the stone tablets with the law and the commands I have written to teach them.”
Then Moses set out with his assistant, Joshua, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
He said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are with you, and anyone who has a dispute can go to them.”
When Moses went up the mountain, the cloud covered it.
The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered the mountain for six days. On the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from inside the cloud.
To the Israelites, the glory of the LORD looked like a consuming fire on top of the mountain.
Moses entered the cloud as he went farther up the mountain, and he stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the people of Israel, that they take for Me a contribution. From every man whose heart moves him you shall receive My contribution.
This is the contribution that you shall receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goat hair;
ram skins dyed red and fine leather; acacia wood;
oil for the lamps; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and other gems for the ephod and the breastpiece.
And let them make a sanctuary for Me, that I may dwell among them.
You shall make the tabernacle and all its furnishings exactly like the pattern that I show you.
They are to make an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
You shall overlay it with pure gold, inside and out, and you shall make a molding of gold around it.
You shall cast four gold rings for it and put them on its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.
You shall make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
You shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, so that the ark may be carried by them.
The poles shall remain in the rings of the ark; they must not be removed.
You shall put into the ark the Testimony, which I will give you.
You shall make a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
You shall make two cherubim of hammered gold at the two ends of the mercy seat.
You shall make one cherub at one end and the other cherub at the other end. You shall make the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat, at its two ends.
The cherubim shall spread their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, and they shall face one another. Their faces shall be toward the mercy seat.
You shall put the mercy seat on top of the ark, and you shall put in the ark the Testimony that I will give you.

There I will meet with you, and I will speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim that are on the ark of the Testimony, about all that I command you concerning the people of Israel.
You shall make a table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
You shall overlay it with pure gold and make a molding of gold around it.
You shall make a rim around it a handbreadth wide, and you shall make a molding of gold around the rim.
You shall make four gold rings for it and fasten them to the four corners at its four feet.
The rings shall be close to the rim, as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
You shall make the poles of acacia wood, overlay them with gold, and carry the table with them.
You shall make its plates, dishes, pitchers, and bowls for pouring drink offerings, and you shall make them of pure gold.
You shall put the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times.
You shall make a lampstand of pure gold. The lampstand and its base and shaft shall be made of hammered work; its cups, buds, and blossoms shall be of one piece with it.
Six branches shall extend from its sides, three on one side and three on the other.
There shall be three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the first branch, each with bud and petals, and three on the second branch, and so for the six branches that extend from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself there shall be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and petals.
A bud shall be under the first pair of branches, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair, for the six branches that extend from the lampstand.
The buds and branches shall be one piece with it, all hammered out of pure gold.
You shall make seven lamps for it and set them up so that they light the area in front of it.
Its tongs and trays shall be of pure gold.
It shall be made, with all these utensils, from a talent of pure gold.
See that you make them according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain."
You are to make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine linen. Weave blue, purple, and scarlet yarn into them, and work cherubim into them with skill.
Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains are to be the same size.
Join five curtains together into one set, and join the other five together into another set.
Make loops of blue yarn along the edge of the last curtain in the first set. Do the same along the edge of the last curtain in the second set.
Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, so the loops face each other.
Make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains with them, so the tabernacle becomes one piece.
You are to make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle. Make eleven curtains in all.
Each of the eleven curtains is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.
Join five curtains into one set and the other six into another set. Then fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the matching curtain in the second set.
Make fifty bronze clasps and put them in the loops to join the tent into one piece.
The extra part of the tent curtains, the half curtain left over, is to hang down over the back of the tabernacle.
The tent curtains will be one cubit longer on each side. The extra part is to hang over the sides of the tabernacle to cover it.
Make a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
You are to make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame is to be ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Put two pegs on each frame to join them together. Make all the frames of the tabernacle this way.
Make twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle.
Make forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames—two bases for each frame, one under each peg.
For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames.
Make forty silver bases—two bases under each frame.
Make six frames for the rear of the tabernacle, the west side.
Make two frames for the two back corners of the tabernacle.
Join them from bottom to top and fit them into a single ring. Make both corners the same way.
So there are to be eight frames and sixteen silver bases—two bases under each frame.
You are to make five crossbars of acacia wood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle.
Make five for the other side, and five for the rear side of the tabernacle, to the west.
The middle crossbar is to run from end to end, halfway up the frames.
Overlay the frames with gold and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Also overlay the crossbars with gold.
you are to set up the tabernacle according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.
You are to make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen, with cherubim worked into it.
Hang it with gold hooks on four posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold, standing on four silver bases.
Hang the veil under the clasps and bring the ark of the Testimony in there behind the veil. The veil will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
Put the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy Place.
Place the table outside the veil on the north side of the tabernacle, and put the lampstand opposite the table on the south side.
For the entrance to the tent, make a curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen, the work of an embroiderer.
Make five posts of acacia wood for the curtain, overlay them with gold, and make gold hooks for them. Cast five bronze bases for them.
You should make the altar out of acacia wood. It should be square, five cubits long and five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
You should make horns on its four corners. The horns should be one piece with the altar, and you should cover the altar with bronze.
You should make bronze tools for it: pots for ashes, shovels, bowls, forks, and fire pans. All of its tools should be bronze.
You should make a bronze grate for it, like a net. You should make four bronze rings on its four corners.
You should put the grate under the rim of the altar, so it hangs halfway down the altar.
You should make poles for the altar out of acacia wood, and cover them with bronze.
The poles should be put through the rings, so they rest on two sides of the altar when it is carried.
You should make it hollow, with boards. Make it just as it was shown to you on the mountain.
You should make the courtyard around the tabernacle. On the south side, hang fine twisted linen curtains that are one hundred cubits long.
It will have twenty bronze pillars with twenty bronze bases. The hooks and bands on the pillars should be silver.
Do the same on the north side: hangings one hundred cubits long, twenty bronze pillars with bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands.
On the west side, the courtyard should be fifty cubits wide, with hangings, ten pillars, and ten bases.
The east side should also be fifty cubits wide.
On one side of the entrance, hang curtains fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
On the other side, hang curtains fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
For the courtyard entrance, make a screen twenty cubits long from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, with skillful needlework. It needs four pillars and four bases.
All pillars around the courtyard should be joined with silver bands. Their hooks should be silver, and their bases bronze.
The courtyard should be one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains five cubits high made of fine twisted linen. The bases should be bronze.
All tools used in the tabernacle and all its tent pegs, along with the pegs for the courtyard, should be bronze.
You should command the Israelites to bring you pure olive oil, pressed for the lamp, so it can burn steadily.

In the tent of meeting, outside the curtain that is before the Testimony, Aaron and his sons should keep the lamp burning before the LORD from evening to morning. This is a lasting rule for the Israelites for all generations.
“Bring your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar near to you from among the Israelites, so they can serve Me as priests.
Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, for glory and splendor.
You are to speak to all the skilled craftsmen, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, so they may make Aaron's garments to set him apart for serving Me as priest.

These are the garments they are to make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are to make holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so they may serve Me as priests.
They are to use gold, along with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
“They are to make the ephod of finely spun linen, embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
It must have two shoulder pieces attached at two of its corners, so it can be fastened.
The woven waistband of the ephod must be one piece with it, made the same way, of finely spun linen embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
“Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
six names on one stone and the remaining six on the other, in the order of their birth.
Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. Then mount the stones in gold settings.
Fasten both stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron must carry their names on his two shoulders before the LORD as a memorial.
and two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and attach the chains to the settings.
“You are to make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skilled craftsman. Make it like the ephod—of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.
It must be square when folded over, a span long and a span wide.
Mount on it a setting of four rows of stones: The first row must be a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald.
The second row must be a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond.
The third row must be a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
The fourth row must be a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount them in gold settings.
The stones must match the names of the sons of Israel, twelve stones, one for each name, engraved like a seal for each of the twelve tribes.
“For the breastpiece, make braided chains of pure gold, like cords.
You are to make two gold rings for the breastpiece and fasten them to its two upper corners.
Then attach the two gold chains to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece.
Fasten the other ends of the chains to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
Make two more gold rings and attach them to the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
Make two more gold rings and attach them to the lower part of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the front, near the seam just above the woven waistband.
Tie the rings of the breastpiece to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so the breastpiece stays above the waistband of the ephod and does not swing loose.
“Whenever Aaron enters the Holy Place, he must carry the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece of judgment, as a continual memorial before the LORD.

Place the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece of judgment, so they will be over Aaron's heart whenever he enters the presence of the LORD. In this way Aaron will always carry the judgment of the Israelites over his heart before the LORD.
“You are to make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth.
It must have an opening for the head in the center. Around the opening, make a woven collar like the opening of a garment, so it will not tear.
Make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn around the lower hem, with gold bells between them.
The gold bells and pomegranates must alternate around the lower hem of the robe.
Aaron must wear it when he serves, and the sound of the bells must be heard when he enters or leaves the Holy Place before the LORD, so he will not die.
“You are to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it as on a seal: HOLY TO the LORD.
Fasten a blue cord to it to attach it to the turban; it is to be on the front of the turban.

It will be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron will carry the guilt of the holy things that the Israelites set apart with all their holy gifts. It will always be on his forehead, so they may be accepted before the LORD.
“You are to weave the tunic of fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and make the sash the work of an embroiderer.
Make tunics, sashes, and headbands for Aaron's sons, to give them glory and splendor.
Put these garments on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint them, ordain them, and set them apart, so they may serve Me as priests.
“Make linen undergarments to cover their nakedness, reaching from waist to thigh.

Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to serve in the Holy Place, so they will not bring guilt on themselves and die. This will be a lasting rule for Aaron and his descendants.”
"Now this is what you are to do to set them apart to serve Me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams that have no defects.
Use fine wheat flour to make unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil.
Put them in a basket and bring them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
"Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
Take the special clothes and dress Aaron in the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece. Fasten the ephod on him with its woven belt.
Put the turban on his head and place the holy crown on the turban.
Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
"Bring his sons and dress them in tunics.
Tie sashes around them and put head coverings on them. The priesthood will belong to them forever as a law for all time. In this way you will ordain Aaron and his sons.
"Bring the bull to the front of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron and his sons must lay their hands on the bull's head.
Slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
Take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger. Pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
Take all the fat that covers the inner parts, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
But burn the bull's meat, its hide, and its waste outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
"Take one of the rams. Aaron and his sons must lay their hands on its head.
Slaughter the ram and take its blood and sprinkle it all around the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces. Wash its inner parts and legs, and place them with its head and the other pieces.
Burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing smell, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
"Take the second ram. Aaron and his sons must lay their hands on its head.

Slaughter the ram. Take some of its blood and put it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Sprinkle the rest of the blood on all sides of the altar.

Take some of the blood from the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle them on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. Then he and his clothes will be set apart, and his sons and their clothes will be set apart too.
"Take the fat from the ram, the fat tail, the fat that covers the inner parts, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh, because this is a ram for ordination.
Take one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.
Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar on top of the burnt offering. It is a pleasing smell before the LORD, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
"Take the breast of the ram used for ordination and wave it before the LORD as a wave offering. It will be your portion.
Set apart for Aaron and his sons the breast of the wave offering that is waved and the thigh of the offering that is lifted up from the ram used for ordination.
It will belong to Aaron and his sons forever as a law from the Israelites. It is their offering that is lifted up to the LORD from their peace offerings.
"The holy clothes that belong to Aaron will belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them.
The son who takes his place as priest and enters the Tent of Meeting to serve in the Holy Place must wear them for seven days.
"Take the ram used for ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
At the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons must eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.
They must eat the things used to make atonement for their ordination and set them apart. No one outside may eat them, because they are holy.
If any of the meat used for ordination or any bread is left until morning, burn up what is left. It must not be eaten, because it is holy.

Sacrifice a bull as a sin offering each day to make atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to set it apart.
For seven days make atonement for the altar and set it apart. Then the altar will be most holy, and whatever touches the altar will become holy.

Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.
With the first lamb offer one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil from pressed olives, and a drink offering of one-fourth of a hin of wine.
Offer the second lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a pleasing smell, an offering made by fire to the LORD.

There I will meet with the Israelites, and the place will be set apart by My glory.
So I will set apart the Tent of Meeting and the altar. I will also set apart Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
Then I will live among the Israelites and be their God.
They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might live among them. I am the LORD their God."

Use it to anoint the tent of meeting, the ark of the covenant,
the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, and the incense altar.
Anoint the burnt offering altar and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
You must set them apart so they will be most holy; whatever touches them will become holy.
Anoint Aaron and his sons and set them apart to serve Me as priests.
"Say to the Israelites, 'This is to be My holy anointing oil for all your generations.
Do not pour it on the body of an ordinary man, and do not make any other oil like it with the same formula. It is holy, and it must be holy to you.
Anyone who mixes a similar perfume or puts some of it on an outsider must be cut off from his people.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "Take spices: gum resin, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, with each spice in equal amount.
Make incense from them, a perfume blended by a perfumer. It must be seasoned with salt, pure, and holy.
"Grind some of it into a very fine powder and put it in front of the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It is to be most holy to you.
Do not make any incense like it for yourselves using the same formula. It is holy to the LORD.
Anyone who makes something like it to enjoy its fragrance must be cut off from his people."
“See, I have chosen Bezalel by name. He is the son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with the Spirit of God, giving him wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and skill in all kinds of work.
He can plan beautiful designs and work in gold, silver, and bronze.
He can cut and set stones, work with wood, and do all kinds of skilled work.
I have also appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to help him. I have given skill to all the craftsmen, so they can make everything I have commanded you:
the tent of meeting, the ark of the Testimony, the atonement cover on it, and all the furnishings for the tent;
the table and its utensils; the pure gold lampstand and all its accessories; and the altar of incense;
the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils; and the basin with its stand;
the woven garments—both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests;
and the anointing oil and fragrant incense for the Holy Place. They must make them just as I have commanded you.”
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“Tell the Israelites, ‘You must observe My Sabbaths, for this will be a sign between Me and you for the generations to come, so you may know that I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
Keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Anyone who treats it as ordinary must be put to death. Whoever does work on that day must be removed from his people.
For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day must be put to death.
The Israelites must observe the Sabbath, celebrating it as a lasting agreement for the generations to come.
It is a sign between Me and the Israelites forever, because in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, but on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.’”
When the LORD had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him the two tablets of the Testimony—stone tablets written by the finger of God.

When the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, "Come, make us gods who will go before us. We do not know what has happened to this Moses, the man who brought us up out of Egypt."
Aaron said to them, "Take off the gold earrings from your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me."
So all the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
He took the gold from their hands and shaped it with a tool. He made it into a metal calf. Then they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt."
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, "Tomorrow will be a feast to the LORD."
The next day the people got up early and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then they sat down to eat and drink, and they got up to dance and play.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go down, because your people, whom you brought up out of Egypt, have ruined themselves.
They have quickly turned away from the way I commanded them. They made a metal calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt.'
I have seen these people, and they are stubborn.
Now leave Me alone so My anger can burn against them and destroy them. Then I will make you into a great nation."
But Moses begged the LORD his God and said, "the LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of Egypt with great power and a strong hand?

Why should the Egyptians say, 'He brought them out to harm them, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the earth'? Turn from Your fierce anger. Relent and do not bring disaster on Your people.

Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. You swore to them by Yourself and said, 'I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky and give them all this land I promised. They will inherit it forever.'
So the LORD relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring on His people.
Moses turned and went down the mountain. He had the two tablets of the covenant in his hands, and they were written on both sides.
The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was God's writing, engraved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, "There is a sound of war in the camp."
Moses replied, "That is not the sound of victory or the sound of defeat. It is the sound of singing that I hear."
As he came near the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing. Moses became very angry. He threw the tablets from his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain.
Then he took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses asked Aaron, "What did these people do to you that you brought such a great sin on them?"
Aaron said, "Do not let my lord's anger burn. You know these people are set on evil.
They said to me, 'Make us gods who will go before us. We do not know what has happened to this Moses, the man who brought us up out of Egypt.'
So I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, take it off.' They gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf."
Moses saw that the people were out of control, because Aaron had let them get out of control and become a joke to their enemies.
Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said, "Whoever is for the LORD, come to me!" All the Levites gathered around him.

He said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Put your swords on your thighs. Go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate. Kill your brother, your friend, and your neighbor.'"
The Levites did as Moses said. That day about three thousand men died.
Moses said, "Today you have set yourselves apart for the LORD, because each of you stood against his son and brother. So He may bless you today."
The next day Moses said to the people, "You have sinned a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD. Perhaps I can make atonement for your sin."
So Moses went back to the LORD and said, "Oh, these people have sinned a great sin. They made gods of gold for themselves.
But now, if You will forgive their sin—but if not, please blot me out of Your book that You have written."
The LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book.
Now go and lead the people to the place I told you about. My angel will go before you. But when I punish them, I will punish them for their sin."
Then the LORD struck the people because of what they did with the calf Aaron had made.

The LORD spoke to Moses, "Leave this place, you and the people you led out of Egypt. Go up to the land I promised with an oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.'
I will send an angel before you and drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up among you, because you are a stubborn people. Otherwise, I might destroy you on the way."
When the people heard this bad news, they mourned. No one put on his jewelry.

The LORD said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites, 'You are a stubborn people. If I went with you even for a moment, I would destroy you. Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.'"
So the Israelites took off their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.

Moses used to take the tent and set it up outside the camp, far away from the camp. He called it the tent of meeting. Anyone who wanted to seek the the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people rose and stood at the entrances to their tents, watching Moses until he entered the tent.
As Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance, while the the LORD spoke with Moses.
Whenever the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they all stood and worshiped, each at the entrance to his tent.
The the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as one person speaks to a friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young aide Joshua son of Nun did not leave the tent.
Moses said to the the LORD, "You tell me to lead these people, but You have not told me whom You will send with me. You have said, 'I know you by name, and you have found favor with Me.'
Now, if I have found favor in Your sight, please show me Your ways so I can know You and keep finding favor with You. Remember, too, that this nation is Your people."
The the LORD replied, "My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest."
Then Moses said to Him, "If Your Presence does not go with us, do not send us up from here.
How will anyone know that You are pleased with me and Your people unless You go with us? What else will make us different from all the other people on the earth?"
The the LORD said to Moses, "I will do the very thing you have asked, because you have found favor with Me and I know you by name."
Then Moses said, "Please show me Your glory."

The the LORD said, "I will let all My goodness pass in front of you, and I will proclaim My name, the LORD, before you. I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.
But He said, "You cannot see My face, because no one can see Me and live.
There is a place near Me where you can stand on a rock.
When My glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft in the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take away My hand, and you will see My back. But My face will not be seen."
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Chisel out two stone tablets like the first ones. I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, the ones you broke.
Be ready in the morning, and come up on Mount Sinai. Present yourself to Me there on top of the mountain.
No one may come up with you. No one may be seen anywhere on the mountain, and no flocks or herds may graze in front of it."
So Moses chiseled out two stone tablets like the first ones. He got up early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him. He carried the two stone tablets in his hands.
Then the LORD came down in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed His name, the LORD.
Then the LORD passed in front of him and proclaimed: "The LORD, the LORD, the compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, full of faithful love and truth,

keeping faithful love for thousands, forgiving wrongdoing, rebellion, and sin. But He will not leave the guilty unpunished. He will bring the fathers' sin on the children and grandchildren, even to the third and fourth generations."
Moses quickly bowed to the ground and worshiped.
"O Lord, if I have found favor in Your sight," he said, "please go with us. Even though this is a stubborn people, forgive our wrongdoing and sin, and take us as Your own."

Then the LORD said, "I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will do wonders that have never been done in any nation in all the earth. Everyone among whom you live will see the LORD's work, for it is an awesome thing that I am doing with you.
"Observe what I command you today. I will drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Be careful not to make a covenant with the people who live in the land you are entering. If you do, they may become a trap among you.
Instead, tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and cut down their Asherah poles.
You must not worship any other god, because the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God."
"Be careful not to make a treaty with the people of that land. When they worship their gods and sacrifice to them, they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.
If you take some of their daughters as wives for your sons, those daughters will worship their gods and lead your sons to do the same."
"You must not make any metal gods for yourselves."
"Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For seven days eat bread without yeast, as I commanded you, at the set time in the month of Abib, because in Abib you came out of Egypt.
Every firstborn male is Mine, including the firstborn of all your livestock, whether ox or sheep.

You must redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb. If you do not redeem it, break its neck. You must redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one may come before Me without bringing an offering."
"Work six days, but rest on the seventh day. Even during plowing and harvest, you must rest.
Celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the first grain from your wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year."
"Three times a year all your males must appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your territory, so no one will want your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God."
"Do not offer the blood of My sacrifice with anything that has yeast. Do not let the Passover sacrifice remain until morning.
Bring the best of the firstfruits from your soil to the house of the LORD your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk."
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write down these words, because by these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. The LORD wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant—the Ten Commandments.
When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the covenant in his hands, he did not know that his face was shining because he had spoken with the LORD.
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, they saw that his face was shining. They were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them, so Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and Moses spoke to them.
Afterward all the Israelites came near, and Moses commanded them to do everything the LORD had told him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
Whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with Him, he took off the veil until he came out. When he came out, he told the Israelites what he had been commanded.
The Israelites would see that Moses' face was glowing. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the LORD.
Moses gathered the whole community of Israelites and said, “These are the things the LORD has commanded you to do.
For six days, work may be done, but the seventh day must be holy to you. It is a Sabbath of rest to the LORD. Anyone who does work on that day must be put to death.
Do not light a fire in any of your homes on the Sabbath day.”
Moses said to the whole community of Israelites, “This is what the LORD has commanded:
Take from among you an offering for the LORD. Everyone who is willing may bring the LORD’s offering: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen; goat hair;
ram skins dyed red; fine leather; and acacia wood;
olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense;
and onyx stones and other stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece.
“Let every skilled person among you come and make all that the LORD has commanded:
the tabernacle, its tent and covering, its clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
the ark with its poles, the atonement cover, and the curtain;
the table with its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand for the light with its utensils and lamps, and the oil for the light;
the incense altar with its poles; the anointing oil and the fragrant incense; the curtain for the entrance to the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, poles, and utensils; the basin and its stand;
the hangings of the courtyard, its posts and bases, and the screen for the courtyard gate;
the tent pegs for the tabernacle and courtyard, and their ropes;
and the woven garments for serving in the holy place, the sacred garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.”
Then the whole community of Israelites left Moses.
Everyone whose heart moved them and whose spirit was willing came and brought an offering to the LORD for the work on the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the sacred garments.
Men and women came and brought brooches, earrings, rings, and ornaments, all kinds of gold jewelry. Everyone who waved a gold offering to the LORD brought it.
Everyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goat hair, ram skins dyed red, or fine leather brought them.
Everyone who could give silver or bronze brought it as an offering to the LORD. Everyone who had acacia wood brought it for all the work.
All the skilled women spun with their hands and brought what they had spun: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts moved them spun the goat hair.
The leaders brought onyx stones and stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece.
They also brought spices and olive oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
So all the Israelite men and women whose hearts moved them brought freewill offerings for all the work the LORD had commanded through Moses.
Moses said, “See, the LORD has chosen Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, and with all kinds of skill—
to make artistic designs for work in gold, silver, and bronze;
to cut and set stones; to carve wood; and to do all kinds of skilled work.
He has also given him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others.

He has filled them with skill to do all kinds of work: engraving, designing, and embroidering with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and weaving. They will do all kinds of work and carry out every design.”

Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled worker whose heart the LORD had filled with wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work for the holy place did everything just as the LORD had commanded. The LORD had given them that wisdom and understanding.
Moses called Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled worker whose heart the LORD had filled with wisdom and whose heart moved him to come and do the work.
They received from Moses all the offering the Israelites had brought for the work of serving in the holy place. The people kept bringing more freewill offerings every morning.
All the skilled workers who were doing the work for the holy place came, each from his own task.
They said to Moses, "The people are bringing much more than enough for the work the LORD commanded us to do."
Moses gave a command, and they sent word through the camp: "No man or woman should make anything more as an offering for the holy place." So the people stopped bringing gifts.
The materials were enough for all the work, with some left over.
All the skilled workers made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim skillfully worked into them.
Each curtain was 28 cubits long and 4 cubits wide. All the curtains were the same size.
They joined five curtains together, and the other five curtains together.
They made loops of blue yarn on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and did the same on the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
They made fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set, with the loops opposite each other.
They made fifty gold clasps and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, so the tabernacle became one piece.
They made curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle. They made eleven curtains.
Each curtain was 30 cubits long and 4 cubits wide. All eleven curtains were the same size.
They joined five curtains together and six curtains together.
They made fifty loops on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops on the edge of the matching curtain in the second set.
They made fifty bronze clasps to join the tent together into one piece.
They made a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
They made upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame was 10 cubits long and 1.5 cubits wide.
Each frame had two tenons joined together. They made all the frames of the tabernacle this way.
They made twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle.
They made forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames—two bases under each frame for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, they made twenty frames.
Their forty silver bases were two bases under each frame.
For the west side of the tabernacle, they made six frames.
They made two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the back.
These corner frames were joined at the bottom and joined at the top to one ring. They made both corners this way.
So there were eight frames with sixteen silver bases—two bases under each frame.
They made five crossbars of acacia wood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle.
They made five crossbars for the frames on the other side, and five crossbars for the frames at the back of the tabernacle, on the west.
They made the middle crossbar to run from end to end through the middle of the frames.
They overlaid the frames with gold and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. They also overlaid the crossbars with gold.
They made the inner curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.
They made four pillars of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold. They also made gold hooks for them and cast four silver bases for them.
For the entrance to the tent, they made a screen of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, embroidered with needlework.
They made five pillars with hooks for them. They overlaid the tops of the pillars and their bands with gold, and their five bases were bronze.
Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. It was two and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one and a half cubits high.
He covered it with pure gold inside and out, and he made a gold molding around it.
He cast four gold rings for it and fastened them to its four corners. He put two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
He made poles of acacia wood and covered them with gold.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark so it could be carried.
He made the mercy seat of pure gold. It was two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
He made two cherubim of hammered gold at the two ends of the mercy seat.
One cherub was at one end and the other at the other end. He made them as one piece with the mercy seat.
The cherubim had wings spread upward, and their wings covered the mercy seat. Their faces looked toward each other, toward the mercy seat.
He made the table of acacia wood. It was two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and a half cubits high.
He covered it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it.
He made a frame around it one handbreadth wide, and he made a gold molding around the frame.
He cast four gold rings for it and attached them to the four corners by its four legs.
The rings were close to the frame. They held the poles used to carry the table.
He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with gold.
He made the table's pieces of pure gold: its plates, dishes, bowls, and jars used for pouring drink offerings.
He made the lampstand of pure gold. He hammered it out so its base, stem, branches, cups, buds, and flowers were all one piece.
Six branches came out from its sides: three from one side and three from the other.
Each branch had three cups shaped like almond flowers, with a bud and a flower. This was true for all six branches coming out of the lampstand.
The lampstand itself had four cups shaped like almond flowers, with buds and flowers.
A bud was under the first two branches that came out of it, a bud was under the next two branches, and a bud was under the last two branches. This was for all six branches.
The buds and branches were one piece with it. The whole lampstand was one piece of hammered pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, its wick trimmers, and its trays of pure gold.
He used one talent of pure gold for the lampstand and all its tools.
He made the altar of incense from acacia wood. It was square, one cubit long, one cubit wide, and two cubits high. Its horns were made as one piece with it.
He covered its top, sides, and horns with pure gold. He made a gold molding around it.
He made two gold rings under the molding on two opposite sides. They held the poles used to carry it.
He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with gold.
He made the holy anointing oil and the pure, sweet-smelling incense. A skilled perfumer made them.
He made the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood. It was square, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
He made horns on its four corners. The horns were one piece with the altar, and he covered it with bronze.
He made all the altar's utensils of bronze: the pots, shovels, basins, forks, and firepans.
He made a bronze grating, a net under the altar's rim, halfway up.
He cast four bronze rings for the four corners of the grating, to hold the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with bronze.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar to carry it. He made the altar hollow, with boards.
He made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
He made the courtyard. On the south side, it was a hundred cubits long, with curtains of finely twisted linen.
There were twenty posts with twenty bronze bases. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver.
The north side was also a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver.
The west side was fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver.
The east side was fifty cubits wide.
On one side of the entrance, the curtains were fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
On the other side of the entrance to the courtyard, the curtains were also fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
All the curtains around the courtyard were of finely twisted linen.
The bases for the posts were bronze. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver, and their tops were covered with silver. All the posts around the courtyard had silver bands.

The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard was embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen. It was twenty cubits long and five cubits high, matching the courtyard curtains.
It had four posts with four bronze bases. Their hooks were silver, and their tops and bands were covered with silver.
All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and the courtyard were bronze.
These are the accounts of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the Testimony. They were recorded at Moses' command. This was the work of the Levites under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, made everything the LORD commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. He was a craftsman, designer, and embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
All the gold used for the work, in all the work of the sanctuary, was 29 talents and 730 shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
The silver from the people counted in the community was 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
This was a beka, or half a shekel, per person, by the sanctuary shekel, for everyone twenty years old or older who was counted: 603,550 men.
From the 100 talents of silver, they cast the bases for the sanctuary and the bases for the veil: 100 bases from 100 talents, one talent for each base.
From the 1,775 shekels, he made hooks for the posts, covered their tops, and connected them.
The bronze from the offering was 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance to the tent of meeting, the bronze altar and its bronze grating, and all the altar's utensils.
He also made the bases for the courtyard all around, the bases for the courtyard gate, and all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and the courtyard.
From the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, they made woven garments for serving in the holy place. They also made the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the ephod from gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
They hammered the gold into thin sheets and cut them into threads. Then they worked the gold into the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and into the fine linen. The work was done by a skilled worker.
They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, joined together at its two ends.

The waistband of the ephod was made from the same material and was attached to the ephod. It was made of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They mounted the onyx stones in gold settings. They were engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
They fastened them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the breastpiece like the ephod: a skilled worker's work, of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
It was square and folded double. It was a span long and a span wide.
They set four rows of stones in it. The first row had carnelian, chrysolite, and emerald.
The second row had turquoise, sapphire, and diamond.
The third row had jacinth, agate, and amethyst.
The fourth row had beryl, onyx, and jasper. They were set in gold settings.
The stones matched the names of the sons of Israel, twelve in all. Each stone was engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
They made braided chains of pure gold for the breastpiece.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings, and they fastened the two rings to the two upper corners of the breastpiece.
They attached the two gold chains to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece.
They fastened the other ends of the two chains to the two settings and attached them to the front shoulder pieces of the ephod.
They made two gold rings and fastened them to the two lower corners of the breastpiece, on the inner edge toward the ephod.
They made two more gold rings and attached them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the front, near the seam above the waistband.

They tied the rings of the breastpiece to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so the breastpiece would rest on the waistband of the ephod and not come loose. This was as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue yarn, the work of a weaver.
It had an opening in the center for the head, with a woven collar around the opening so it would not tear.
They made pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen around the hem of the robe.
They made bells of pure gold and put them between the pomegranates around the hem of the robe.
There were bells and pomegranates all around the hem of the robe, for serving, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made tunics of fine linen for Aaron and his sons, woven work.
They made the turban of fine linen, the ornate headbands of fine linen, the linen undergarments of finely twisted linen,
and the sash of finely twisted linen with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, embroidered work, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the holy plate, the pure gold crown. They engraved on it, in seal-like letters, "Holy to the LORD."
They fastened a blue cord to it to attach it to the turban above, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So all the work on the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was finished. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, the inner curtain;
the ark of the Testimony with its poles and the atonement cover;
the table with all its utensils and the bread of the Presence;
the pure gold lampstand with its lamps, the lamps in a row, and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grate, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases; the curtain for the courtyard gate; its ropes and tent pegs; and all the utensils for the service of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting;
the woven garments for serving in the holy place; the holy garments for Aaron the priest; and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses saw all the work, and indeed they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“On the first day of the first month, you are to set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.
Put the ark of the Testimony inside it, and cover the ark with the veil.
Bring in the table and set out its bread; bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
Place the gold altar of incense in front of the ark of the Testimony, and hang the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
Place the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.
Place the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Set up the courtyard all around, and hang the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard.
“Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it. Consecrate it and all its furnishings, and it will be holy.
Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils. Consecrate the altar, and it will be most holy.
Anoint the basin and its stand, and consecrate them.
“Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
Put the holy garments on Aaron, anoint him, and consecrate him, so that he may serve Me as priest.
Bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics.
Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so that they may serve Me as priests. Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.”
So Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
In the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was set up.
Moses set up the tabernacle. He placed its bases, set up its frames, inserted its crossbars, and set up its posts.
Then he spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering over the tent, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses took the Testimony and placed it in the ark. He attached the poles to the ark and set the mercy seat on top of the ark.
Then he brought the ark into the tabernacle, put up the veil as a screen, and covered the ark of the Testimony, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses placed the table in the Tent of Meeting on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
He arranged the bread on it before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He placed the lampstand in the Tent of Meeting opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle.
He set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses placed the gold altar in the Tent of Meeting in front of the veil.
He burned fragrant incense on it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he put up the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
He placed the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He placed the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing.
Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet there.
They washed whenever they entered the Tent of Meeting or approached the altar, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So Moses finished the work. Then he set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and he hung the curtain for the gateway of the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Moses could not enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out on all their journeys.
But if the cloud was not taken up, they would not set out until the day it was taken up.
For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel in all their journeys.
The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting. He said,
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them, ‘When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you shall bring your offering from the livestock, either from the herd or from the flock.
“‘If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall offer a male without defect. He shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting so that he may be accepted before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted for him to make atonement for him.
“‘He shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD. Aaron's sons, the priests, shall bring the blood and sprinkle it all around on the altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
“‘He shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
“‘Then Aaron's sons, the priests, shall arrange the pieces, the head, and the fat, on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
He shall wash the inner parts and the legs with water. Then the priest shall burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
“‘If his offering is a burnt offering from the flock, from the sheep or the goats, he shall offer a male without defect.
“‘He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD. Aaron's sons, the priests, shall sprinkle its blood all around on the altar.
“‘He shall cut it into pieces. The priest shall arrange them, along with the head and the fat, on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.

“‘He shall wash the inner parts and the legs with water. Then the priest shall bring all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
“‘If his offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he shall bring his offering of turtledoves or young pigeons.
“‘The priest shall bring it to the altar, twist off its head, and burn it on the altar. Its blood shall be drained against the side of the altar.
“‘He shall remove its crop with its feathers and throw it on the east side of the altar, in the place for ashes.

“‘He shall tear it open by the wings without dividing it completely. Then the priest shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.’”
When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering must be fine flour. He must pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.

He must bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. The priest will take a handful of the fine flour and oil, along with all the frankincense, and burn the memorial portion on the altar. It is an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy part of the offerings made by fire to the LORD.
If you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it must be fine flour. It can be unleavened cakes mixed with oil or unleavened wafers coated with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering cooked on a griddle, it must be fine flour mixed with oil, without yeast.
Break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it must be made of fine flour with oil.
When you bring to the LORD a grain offering made in any of these ways, it must be given to the priest. He will bring it to the altar.
The priest will take the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar. It is an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy part of the offerings made by fire to the LORD.
No grain offering that you bring to the LORD may contain yeast, because you must not burn any yeast or honey as an offering made by fire to the LORD.
You may bring them as an offering of firstfruits to the LORD, but they must not go up in smoke on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
Season all your grain offerings with salt. Do not leave out the salt of the covenant of your God from your grain offering. Add salt to all your offerings.
If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you must bring crushed new grain roasted with fire. It is a grain offering from your firstfruits.
You must put oil on it and add frankincense. It is a grain offering.
The priest will burn the memorial portion—taken from the crushed grain and the oil—along with all the frankincense. It is an offering made by fire to the LORD.
If someone brings a peace offering from the cattle, whether male or female, he must offer an animal without a flaw before the LORD.
He must lay his hand on the head of his offering and kill it at the entrance to the tent of meeting. Then Aaron's sons, the priests, must throw the blood against the altar on all sides.
From the peace offering, he must bring an offering made by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the inner parts and all the fat on them.
He must remove the two kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, along with the lobe above the liver, and keep them with the kidneys.
Aaron's sons must burn this on the altar on top of the burnt offering that is on the wood and fire. It is an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If someone's offering for a peace offering to the LORD is from the flock, whether male or female, he must offer it without a flaw.
If he brings a lamb as his offering, he must present it before the LORD.
He must lay his hand on the head of his offering and kill it before the tent of meeting. Then Aaron's sons, the priests, must throw its blood against the altar on all sides.
From the peace offering, he must bring an offering made by fire to the LORD: its fat, the whole fat tail cut close to the backbone, the fat that covers the inner parts, and all the fat on them.
He must remove the two kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, along with the lobe above the liver, and keep them with the kidneys.
The priest must burn these on the altar. This is food, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
If someone's offering is a goat, he must present it before the LORD.
He must lay his hand on its head and kill it before the tent of meeting. Then Aaron's sons, the priests, must throw its blood against the altar on all sides.
He must present from it, as his offering made by fire to the LORD, the fat that covers the inner parts and all the fat on them.
He must remove the two kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, along with the lobe above the liver, and keep them with the kidneys.
