The priest must burn them on the altar. This is food, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma. All fat belongs to the LORD.
This is a lasting rule for all your generations, in all the places where you live: you must not eat any fat or any blood.
“Speak to the Israelites and say: If someone sins without meaning to and breaks one of the LORD’s commands by doing something that should not be done, he is still guilty.
If the anointed priest sins and brings guilt on the people, he must bring a young bull without any flaw to the LORD as a sin offering for the sin he committed.
He must bring the bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, in front of the LORD. He must lay his hand on the bull’s head and kill the bull in front of the LORD.
The anointed priest must take some of the bull’s blood and bring it into the Tent of Meeting.
He must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times in front of the LORD, in front of the curtain of the holy place.

The priest must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is in front of the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. He must pour out the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
He must remove all the fat from the bull for the sin offering: the fat that covers the inner parts and all the fat around them.
He must also remove the two kidneys with the fat on them near the hips, and the long part of the liver, which he removes with the kidneys.
He must do this just as the fat is removed from the bull in the peace offering. Then the priest must burn these parts on the altar of burnt offering.
But he must take the bull’s skin, all its meat, its head, its legs, its inner parts, and its dung.
He must carry the whole bull outside the camp to a clean place, the ash heap. He must burn it there on wood. It must be burned on the ash heap.
If all the Israelites sin without knowing it and do something the LORD has commanded them not to do, they are guilty.
When they learn about the sin they committed, the community must bring a young bull as a sin offering and bring it in front of the Tent of Meeting.
The elders of the community must lay their hands on the bull’s head in front of the LORD, and someone must kill the bull in front of the LORD.
Then the anointed priest must bring some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting.
He must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in front of the LORD, in front of the curtain.

He must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is in front of the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. He must pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
He must take all the fat from the bull and burn it on the altar.
He must do with this bull just as he did with the bull for the sin offering. In this way the priest makes atonement for them, and they are forgiven.
Then he must carry the bull outside the camp and burn it, just as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the community.
When a leader sins without meaning to and does something the LORD his God has commanded people not to do, he is guilty.
When he learns about his sin, he must bring a male goat without any flaw as his offering.
He must lay his hand on the goat’s head and kill it where they kill the burnt offering, in front of the LORD. It is a sin offering.

The priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
He must burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat from the peace offering. In this way the priest makes atonement for the leader’s sin, and he is forgiven.
If one of the common people sins without meaning to and does something the LORD has commanded people not to do, he is guilty.
When he learns about his sin, he must bring a female goat without any flaw as his offering for the sin he committed.
He must lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and kill it where they kill the burnt offering.
The priest must take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

He must remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the peace offering, and burn it on the altar. It gives a pleasing smell to the LORD. In this way the priest makes atonement for the person, and he is forgiven.
If he brings a lamb as his sin offering, he must bring a female without any flaw.
He must lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and kill it for a sin offering where they kill the burnt offering.
The priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

He must remove all its fat, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the peace offering, and burn the fat on the altar as a fire offering to the LORD. In this way the priest makes atonement for the person’s sin, and he is forgiven.
If someone sins by not speaking up when he is called to testify in public, even though he saw or knows about it, he will be guilty.
Or if someone touches anything unclean, such as the dead body of an unclean wild animal, farm animal, or small crawling creature, without knowing it, he is unclean and guilty.
Or if he touches human uncleanness—any kind of uncleanness that makes a person unclean—and he does not know it, when he finds out, he is guilty.
Or if someone makes a careless oath with his lips, to do good or harm—whatever a person might say in an oath—and he does not know it, when he learns of it, he is guilty of one of these things.
When he is guilty of any of these, he must confess the sin he has done.
He must bring his guilt offering to the the LORD for the sin he committed: a female lamb or goat from the flock, as a sin offering. Then the priest will make atonement for him for that sin.
If he cannot afford a lamb, he must bring to the the LORD two turtledoves or two young pigeons as his guilt offering for the sin he committed—one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
He must bring them to the priest, who will first offer the one for the sin offering. He will twist its head from its neck but not pull it off.
Then he must sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar. The rest of the blood must be poured out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
The second bird he must prepare as a burnt offering, following the proper rule. So the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he committed, and he will be forgiven.

But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he may bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not put oil or frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
He must bring it to the priest. The priest will take a handful of it as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar on top of the offerings made by fire to the the LORD. It is a sin offering.
In this way the priest will make atonement for him for any of these sins he has committed, and he will be forgiven. The rest will belong to the priest, as with the grain offering.
Then the the LORD said to Moses,

"If someone sins without meaning to and misuses one of the the LORD's holy things, he must bring his guilt offering to the the LORD: a ram from the flock without defect, worth the proper amount in silver shekels by the sanctuary standard. It is a guilt offering.

He must pay back for the holy thing he misused, adding one-fifth to its value, and give it to the priest. Then the priest will make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
"If someone sins and does something the the LORD has forbidden, even if he does not know it, he is still guilty and must carry his guilt.

He must bring to the priest a ram from the flock without defect, worth the proper amount, as a guilt offering. Then the priest will make atonement for him for the wrong he did without knowing it, and he will be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering; he was indeed guilty before the the LORD."
"If a person sins and is unfaithful to the LORD by lying to a neighbor about something left in his care, or about a pledge, or by robbery, or by cheating a neighbor,
or if he finds something lost and lies about it, and swears falsely about any of these sins a person may do,
then, when he sins and becomes guilty, he must return what he stole, or what he cheated someone out of, or the item left in his care, or the lost thing he found.
He must also pay back anything else he swore falsely about. He must pay it back in full and add one-fifth more. He must give it to the owner on the day he is found guilty.
He must bring his guilt offering to the LORD: a ram without defect from the flock, at the value you set, as a guilt offering.
The priest will make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for any of these things he did that made him guilty."
"Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law for the burnt offering. The burnt offering must stay on the altar all night until morning, and the fire must keep burning on the altar.
The priest must put on his linen robe and linen undergarments. Then he must remove the ashes left from the burnt offering and place them beside the altar.
Then he must take off those clothes, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
The fire on the altar must keep burning; it must not go out. Every morning the priest must add wood to it, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat of the peace offerings on it.
The fire must always burn on the altar; it must never go out.
"This is the law for the grain offering: Aaron's sons must bring it before the LORD, in front of the altar.
The priest must take a handful of the fine flour and oil, along with all the frankincense on the grain offering, and burn this memorial portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons may eat what is left of it. It must be eaten without yeast in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
It must not be baked with yeast. I have given it to them as their share of My offerings. It is Most Holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Every male among Aaron's sons may eat it. It is a lasting rule for your descendants from the LORD's food offerings. Anyone who touches them will become holy."

"This is the offering Aaron and his sons must bring to the LORD on the day he is anointed: one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
It must be prepared with oil on a griddle. Bring it well mixed, and offer it as baked pieces, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The priest from among Aaron's sons who is anointed to take his place must prepare it. It is a permanent rule to the LORD; it must be burned completely.
Every grain offering of a priest must be burned completely; it must not be eaten."
"Tell Aaron and his sons: This is the law for the sin offering. The sin offering must be killed in the same place as the burnt offering, before the LORD. It is Most Holy.
The priest who offers it for sin must eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
Anything that touches its meat will become holy, and if any of its blood is splashed on clothing, you must wash that clothing in a holy place.
The clay pot in which it is boiled must be broken. If it is boiled in a bronze pot, that pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
Every male among the priests may eat it. It is Most Holy.
But no sin offering may be eaten if its blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place. It must be burned with fire."
This is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.
The guilt offering must be killed in the same place where the burnt offering is killed, and its blood must be splashed all around the altar.
All of its fat must be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the inner parts,
the two kidneys with the fat on them near the lower back, and the long part of the liver. The priest must remove that with the kidneys.
The priest must burn them on the altar as an offering made by fire to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
The guilt offering follows the same rule as the sin offering. One law covers both. The priest who makes atonement with it gets to keep it.
When a priest offers a burnt offering for someone, the skin of that burnt offering belongs to that priest.
Every grain offering baked in an oven, and everything made in a pan or on a griddle, belongs to the priest who offers it.
Every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, must be shared equally among all of Aaron's sons.
This is the law of the peace offering that a person may bring to the LORD.
If he brings it as a thank offering, he must bring with it unleavened loaves mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and loaves of fine flour mixed well with oil.
Along with his peace offering for thanksgiving, he must also bring leavened bread with his offering.
He must bring one loaf from each kind as an offering lifted up to the LORD. That loaf belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offerings.
The meat of the thank offering must be eaten on the day it is offered. None of it may be left until morning.
If the sacrifice is a vow offering or a freewill offering, it may be eaten on the day he offers it, and whatever is left may be eaten the next day.
But any meat left from the sacrifice on the third day must be burned in the fire.

If any of the meat from his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not count for the person who offered it. It is unacceptable, and the person who eats it must bear the blame.
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten. It must be burned in the fire. As for other meat, anyone who is clean may eat it.
But if a person eats meat from the LORD's peace offering while he is unclean, that person must be removed from his people.

If a person touches anything unclean—whether human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean creature that crawls—and then eats meat from the LORD's peace offering, that person must be removed from his people.
"Speak to the Israelites and say: You must not eat any fat from an ox, a sheep, or a goat.
The fat of an animal that dies on its own or is torn by wild animals may be used for other things, but you must not eat it.
If anyone eats the fat of an animal from which an offering is made by fire to the LORD, that person must be removed from his people.
You must not eat the blood of any bird or animal in any of your homes.
Anyone who eats blood must be removed from his people."
"Speak to the Israelites and say: Anyone who brings a peace offering to the LORD must bring his offering to the LORD from that sacrifice.
He must bring it with his own hands as an offering made by fire to the LORD. He must bring the fat with the breast, so the breast can be waved as a wave offering before the LORD.
The priest must burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
You must give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your peace offerings.
The priest among Aaron's sons who offers the blood and fat of the peace offerings gets the right thigh as his share.

I have taken the waved breast and the contributed thigh from the Israelites, from their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons. This is a lasting rule for all generations."
This is the share of Aaron and his sons from the LORD's offerings made by fire. It began the day they were set apart to serve as priests to the LORD,
the day the LORD commanded the Israelites to give these things to them. This is a lasting rule for all generations.
This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering,
which the LORD commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day He commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.
"Take Aaron and his sons with you, and the garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
Bring the whole community together at the entrance to the tent of meeting."
Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the community gathered at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Moses said to the community, "This is what the LORD has commanded to be done."
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe, and put the ephod on him. He tied the woven band of the ephod around him and fastened it.
He put the breastpiece on him and placed the Urim and Thummim in it.
He set the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban he placed the gold plate, the holy crown, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and he made them holy.
He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and all its tools, the basin, and its stand, to make them holy.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him to make him holy.
Moses brought Aaron's sons forward, clothed them with tunics, tied sashes around them, and put caps on them, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then Moses brought the bull for the sin offering. Aaron and his sons placed their hands on the bull's head.

Moses killed it. He took the blood and, with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar all around. He purified the altar. He poured the rest of the blood at the base of the altar and made it holy, to purify it.
He took all the fat around the inner parts, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and burned them on the altar.
He burned the bull's hide, flesh, and dung outside the camp, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then Moses brought the ram for the burnt offering. Aaron and his sons placed their hands on its head.
Moses killed it and sprinkled the blood all around the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.

He washed the inner parts and the legs with water and burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then Moses brought the second ram, the ram used for ordination. Aaron and his sons placed their hands on its head.
Moses killed it. He took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

He brought Aaron's sons forward and put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses sprinkled the blood all around the altar.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat around the inner parts, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
From the basket of unleavened bread that was before the LORD, he took one unleavened cake, one loaf mixed with oil, and one wafer. He put them on the fat and on the right thigh.
He placed all of this in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and they waved it before the LORD as a wave offering.
Then Moses took it from their hands and burned it on the altar on top of the burnt offering. It was an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
Moses took the breast and waved it before the LORD as a wave offering. It was Moses' share from the ram of ordination, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron, his clothes, his sons, and their clothes. In this way he made Aaron, his clothes, his sons, and their clothes holy.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, "Boil the meat at the entrance to the tent of meeting and eat it there with the bread in the basket of ordination, as I commanded when I said, 'Aaron and his sons shall eat it.'
You shall burn whatever is left of the meat and the bread.
"You shall not leave the entrance to the tent of meeting for seven days, until your time of ordination is complete, because it takes seven days to ordain you.
The LORD has commanded this, as was done today, to make atonement for you.
"You shall stay at the entrance to the tent of meeting day and night for seven days, and keep the LORD's charge, so that you will not die, for this is what I was commanded."
Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel.
He said to Aaron, "Take for yourself a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. Both must have no flaw. Bring them before the LORD.
Then tell the Israelites, 'Take a male goat for a sin offering. Take a calf and a lamb, each one year old and without flaw, for a burnt offering.
Also bring a bull and a ram for peace offerings to sacrifice before the LORD. Bring a grain offering mixed with oil. Do this because today the LORD will appear to you.'"
They brought what Moses had commanded to the front of the tent of meeting. The whole community came near and stood before the LORD.
Moses said, "This is what the LORD commanded you to do, so the glory of the LORD may appear to you."

Moses said to Aaron, "Go to the altar. Offer your sin offering and your burnt offering. Make atonement for yourself and for the people. Offer the people's gift and make atonement for them, as the LORD has commanded."
Aaron went to the altar and killed the calf for his sin offering.
His sons brought the blood to him. He dipped his finger in it and put some on the horns of the altar. He poured the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
He burned the fat, the kidneys, and the covering of the liver from the sin offering on the altar. He did this as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He burned the meat and the skin outside the camp.
Then he killed the burnt offering. His sons brought him the blood, and he sprinkled it all around the altar.
They handed him the burnt offering, cut into pieces, along with the head. He burned all of it on the altar.
He washed the inner parts and the legs. Then he burned them on the altar with the burnt offering.
He brought the people's offering. He took the goat for the people's sin offering, killed it, and made it a sin offering like the first one.
He brought the burnt offering and offered it following the rules.
He brought the grain offering. He took a handful and burned it on the altar, besides the morning burnt offering.
He killed the bull and the ram for the people's peace offerings. His sons brought him the blood, and he sprinkled it all around the altar.
They took the fat from the bull and the ram: the fat tail, the covering fat, the kidneys, and the covering of the liver.
They put the fat on the breast pieces. Then he burned the fat on the altar.
Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh before the LORD as an offering. He did this as Moses had commanded.
Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them. Then he came down after offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
Fire came out from before the LORD. It burned up the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. All the people saw it. They shouted with joy and fell on their faces.
Now Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu each took his censer, put fire in it, and added incense. Then they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, which He had not commanded them.
Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
Then Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD said: 'I will show My holiness to those who come near Me, and I will be honored before all the people.'" And Aaron was silent.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel, and said to them, "Come here and carry your brothers' bodies outside the camp, away from the front of the sanctuary."
So they came and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, as Moses had ordered.

Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not let your hair hang loose or tear your clothes, or you will die and the LORD will be angry with the whole community. But your brothers, the whole house of Israel, may mourn for the fire the LORD has burned.
Do not go outside the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, or you will die, because the LORD's anointing oil is on you." So they did as Moses said.
Then the LORD said to Aaron,
"You and your sons are not to drink wine or strong drink when you go into the Tent of Meeting, or you will die. This is a permanent rule for your descendants.
You must distinguish between the holy and the common, between the unclean and the clean.
And teach the Israelites all the rules that the LORD has spoken to them through Moses."
Moses said to Aaron and his surviving sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Take the grain offering left from the food offerings to the LORD and eat it without yeast beside the altar, because it is most holy.
You are to eat it in a holy place, because it is your share and your sons' share of the food offerings to the LORD; for this is what I have been commanded.

And you and your sons and daughters may eat the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution in a clean place, because these are your portion and your children's portion from the peace offerings of the Israelites.

They are to bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering, along with the fat parts of the offerings, to be waved as a wave offering before the LORD. It will belong to you and your sons forever, as the LORD has commanded."
Then Moses asked about the goat of the sin offering, and saw that it had been burned. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's surviving sons, and asked,
"Why didn't you eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy. He gave it to you to take away the guilt of the community and to make atonement for them before the LORD.
Since its blood was not brought into the holy place, you should have eaten it there, as I commanded."

Aaron replied to Moses, "Look, today they presented their sin offering and burnt offering before the LORD. But such things as these have happened to me. Would it have been good in the LORD's sight if I had eaten the sin offering today?"
When Moses heard this, he was satisfied.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Of all the animals that live on the land,
you may eat any animal that has a split hoof and chews the cud.
But there are animals that chew the cud or have a split hoof, and you must not eat them. The camel chews the cud, but it does not have a split hoof, so it is unclean for you.
The rock badger chews the cud, but it does not have a split hoof, so it is unclean for you.
The rabbit chews the cud, but it does not have a split hoof, so it is unclean for you.
The pig has a split hoof, but it does not chew the cud, so it is unclean for you.
You must not eat their meat or touch their dead bodies. They are unclean for you.
"Of all the creatures that live in the water, whether in the seas or streams, you may eat any that have fins and scales.
But every creature in the seas or streams that does not have fins and scales, whether it swarms or not, is detestable to you.
They must stay detestable to you. Do not eat their meat, and detest their dead bodies.
Any creature in the water that does not have fins and scales is detestable to you.
"These are the birds you must detest and not eat, because they are detestable: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
the kite, any kind of falcon,
the horned owl, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
"All flying insects that walk on four legs are detestable to you.
But you may eat those that have jointed legs for hopping on the ground.
Of these you may eat any kind of locust, katydid, cricket, or grasshopper.
All other flying insects that have four legs are detestable to you.
"You will make yourselves unclean by these animals. Anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who picks up one of their dead bodies must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
Every animal that does not have a split hoof or does not chew the cud is unclean for you. Anyone who touches its dead body will be unclean.
Of all the animals that walk on four legs, those that walk on their paws are unclean for you. Anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who picks up their dead bodies must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
"Of the animals that move along the ground, these are unclean for you: the mole rat, the mouse, any kind of large lizard,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
Of all these that move along the ground, they are unclean for you. Anyone who touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.

When one of them dies and falls on something, that thing, whatever it is used for, becomes unclean. It may be made of wood, cloth, leather, or sackcloth. Put it in water, and it will be unclean until evening; then it will be clean.
If one of them falls into a clay pot, everything in the pot becomes unclean, and you must break the pot.
Any food that could be eaten but has water on it from such a pot is unclean, and any liquid in such a pot is unclean.
Anything that one of their dead bodies falls on becomes unclean. An oven or cooking pot must be broken. They are unclean, and you must treat them as unclean.
A spring, a cistern, or a collection of water stays clean, but anyone who touches one of their dead bodies is unclean.
If a dead body falls on any seeds that are to be planted, the seeds stay clean.
But if water has been put on the seed and a dead body falls on it, it is unclean for you.
"If an animal that you are allowed to eat dies, anyone who touches its dead body will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who eats some of its dead body must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening. Anyone who picks up its dead body must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
"Every creature that moves along the ground is detestable. It must not be eaten.
You must not eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it moves on its belly, walks on four legs, or has many feet. All such creatures are detestable.
Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these creatures. Do not make yourselves unclean by them, and do not let them make you unclean.
"I am the LORD your God. Set yourselves apart and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean by any of the swarming creatures that move along the ground.
I am the LORD, who brought you up out of Egypt to be your God. Be holy, because I am holy.
These are the rules for animals, birds, every living thing that moves in the water, and every creature that moves along the ground.
You must tell the difference between the unclean and the clean, between animals that may be eaten and animals that may not be eaten."
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the Israelites and say:
"When a woman becomes pregnant and has a baby boy, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period.
On the eighth day, the baby's foreskin must be circumcised.

Then she must wait thirty-three more days to be made clean from her bleeding. During that time, she must not touch anything holy, and she must not enter the sanctuary until her purification is complete.
"If she has a baby girl, she is unclean for two weeks, as she is during her period. Then she must wait sixty-six days to be made clean from her bleeding.

"When her days of purification are complete, whether for a son or a daughter, she must bring to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting a one-year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for a sin offering.
The priest will offer them before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she will be cleansed from her flow of blood. This is the law for a woman who gives birth, whether to a boy or a girl.
"If she cannot afford a lamb, she may take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean."
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
When a person has a swelling, rash, or bright spot on the skin, and it could be a skin disease, that person must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who are priests.
The priest must look at the sore on the skin. If the hair in the sore has turned white and the sore looks deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease. The priest must say the person is unclean.
If the spot is white but does not look deeper than the skin, and the hair has not turned white, the priest must keep the person apart for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest must look again. If the sore has not changed and has not spread, the priest must keep the person apart for another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest must look again. If the sore has faded and has not spread, the priest must say the person is clean. It is only a rash. The person must wash their clothes and will be clean.
But if the rash spreads after the person has been shown to the priest to be made clean, that person must come back to the priest.
The priest must look, and if the rash has spread, he must say the person is unclean. It is a skin disease.
When a person has a skin disease, that person must be brought to the priest.
The priest must look, and if there is a white swelling that has turned the hair white and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
it is a long-lasting skin disease. The priest must say the person is unclean. He must not keep the person apart, because the person is already unclean.
If the disease breaks out all over the skin and covers the person from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,
the priest must look. If the disease has covered the whole body, he must say the person is clean. Since all the skin has turned white, the person is clean.
But whenever raw flesh shows on the person, that person is unclean.
When the priest sees the raw flesh, he must say the person is unclean. The raw flesh is unclean. It is a skin disease.
If the raw flesh changes and turns white, the person must go to the priest.
The priest must look, and if the sore has turned white, the priest must say the person is clean. Then the person is clean.
When a person has a boil on the skin and it heals,
and a white swelling or reddish-white spot appears where the boil was, that person must show it to the priest.
The priest must look, and if it looks deeper than the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest must say the person is unclean. It is a skin disease that has broken out in the boil.
But if there is no white hair in it, and it is not deeper than the skin, and it has faded, the priest must keep the person apart for seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, the priest must say the person is unclean. It is a disease.
But if the spot stays the same and does not spread, it is only a scar from the boil. The priest must say the person is clean.
When a person has a burn on the skin, and a reddish-white or white spot appears in the raw flesh of the burn,

the priest must look at the spot. If the hair in it has turned white and it looks deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest must say the person is unclean. It is a skin disease.
But if there is no white hair in the spot, and it is not deeper than the skin, and it has faded, the priest must keep the person apart for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest must look, and if it has spread in the skin, the priest must say the person is unclean. It is a skin disease.
If the spot stays the same and has not spread, but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn. The priest must say the person is clean. It is only a scar from the burn.
If a man or woman has a sore on the head or chin,
the priest must look at the sore. If it looks deeper than the skin and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest must say the person is unclean. It is a skin disease on the head or chin.
But if the sore does not look deeper than the skin and there is no black hair in it, the priest must keep the person apart for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest must look at the sore. If it has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it and it does not look deeper than the skin,
the man or woman must shave, but not the sore. The priest must keep the person apart for another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest must look at the sore. If it has not spread in the skin and does not look deeper than the skin, the priest must say the person is clean. The person must wash their clothes and will be clean.
But if the sore spreads in the skin after the person has been made clean,
the priest must look. If the sore has spread, the priest does not need to look for yellow hair. The person is unclean.
If the sore stays the same and black hair grows in it, the sore has healed. The person is clean, and the priest must say so.
When a man or woman has white spots on the skin,
the priest must look. If the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash on the skin. The person is clean.
A man who has lost his hair and is bald is clean.
A man who has lost hair from the front of his head and has a bald forehead is clean.
But if he has a reddish-white sore on his bald head or forehead, it is a skin disease breaking out on his baldness.
The priest must look, and if the swollen sore on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white like a skin disease,
the man is unclean. The priest must say he is unclean. He has a skin disease on his head.
Anyone with such a disease must wear torn clothes. He must let his hair hang loose. He must cover his mouth and cry out, "Unclean! Unclean!"
As long as the person has the disease, that person stays unclean. The person must live alone, outside the camp.
When clothing is spoiled by a damaging mold—wool or linen clothing—
or woven or knitted material of linen or wool, or leather, or anything made of leather,
and the affected area is greenish or reddish, it is a spreading mold. That item must be shown to the priest.
The priest must look at the affected area and keep the item apart for seven days.
On the seventh day he must look again. If the mold has spread in the fabric, leather, woven or knitted material, or leather article, it is a lasting mold. The item is unclean.
The priest must burn the fabric, wool or linen clothing, or leather article that has the mold, because the mold is lasting. It must be burned.
But if the mold has not spread when the priest looks,
he must order the affected item to be washed. Then he must keep it apart for another seven days.
After the item has been washed, the priest must look again. If the mold has not changed its look and has not spread, it is unclean. Burn it, whether the mold has eaten into the fabric or the leather.
If the mold has faded after the item has been washed, the priest must tear the spoiled part out of the fabric, leather, woven or knitted material, or leather article.
But if it shows up again, it is a spreading mold. Burn the item.
Any fabric, woven or knitted material, or leather article that has been washed and is free of the mold must be washed again and will be clean.
These are the rules for mold in wool or linen clothing, woven or knitted material, or any leather article. They tell how to make such things clean or unclean.
Then the LORD said to Moses, “
This is the law for a person who has a skin disease when he is made clean: He must be brought to the priest. “
The priest must go outside the camp and look at him. If the skin disease has healed,
the priest will order that two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop be brought for the person being made clean. “
The priest will order that one of the birds be killed over fresh water in a clay pot.
He must take the live bird, along with the cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop, and dip them in the blood of the bird killed over the fresh water.
Seven times he must sprinkle the person being made clean from the skin disease. Then he must announce that the person is clean and let the live bird go free in the open field. “

The person being made clean must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water. Then he will be clean. After that he may come into the camp, but he must stay outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day he must shave off all his hair—his head, beard, eyebrows, and all the rest of his hair. He must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and then he will be clean. “
On the eighth day he must take two male lambs without flaws, a female lamb one year old without flaws, three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.
The priest who makes him clean must present the person and these offerings before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Then the priest must take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering, along with the log of oil. He must wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
He must kill the lamb in the holy place where the sin offering and burnt offering are killed. Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest. It is most holy. “
The priest must take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the right earlobe of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
Then the priest must take some of the log of oil and pour it into his left palm.
The priest must dip his right index finger into the oil in his left palm and sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before the LORD.

The priest must put some of the oil left over on the right earlobe of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
The priest must put the rest of the oil in his palm on the head of the person being made clean. This makes atonement for him before the LORD. “
Then the priest must offer the sin offering and make atonement for the person being made clean from his uncleanness. After that, the priest must kill the burnt offering.
He must offer the burnt offering on the altar, along with the grain offering, to make atonement for him, and he will be clean. “

If the person being made clean is poor and cannot afford these offerings, he must take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him. He must also take a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and a log of oil.
He must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford—one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he must bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD for his cleansing.
The priest must take the lamb for the guilt offering, along with the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.

Then he must kill the lamb for the guilt offering and take some of its blood and put it on the right earlobe of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot. “
Then the priest must pour some of the oil into his left palm
and sprinkle with his right index finger some of the oil in his left palm seven times before the LORD.

He must also put some of the oil on the right earlobe of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, in the same places as the blood of the guilt offering.
The priest must put the rest of the oil in his palm on the head of the person being made clean, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
Then he must offer one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford.
He must offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, along with the grain offering. In this way the priest will make atonement before the LORD for the person being made clean.
This is the law for someone who has a skin disease and cannot afford the cost of his cleansing.”
Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “
When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your own land, I will put mold in a house in the land you own.
The owner of the house must go and tell the priest, ‘Something like mold has appeared in my house.’
The priest must order that the house be emptied before he goes in to look at the mold, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. After this, the priest may enter to inspect the house. “
He must look at the mold. If it is greenish or reddish spots that seem to be deeper than the wall,
the priest must go out to the doorway of the house and close it up for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest must return and inspect it. If the mold has spread in the walls of the house, “
he must order that the stones with the mold be removed and thrown into an unclean place outside the city.
He must have the inside of the house scraped all around, and the scraped plaster must be dumped in an unclean place outside the city.
Then they must take other stones to replace the ones removed and take new mortar to replaster the house. “
If the mold comes back in the house after the stones have been removed and the house has been scraped and replastered,
the priest must come and inspect it. If the mold has spread in the house, it is a bad mold. The house is unclean.
It must be torn down—its stones, wood, and all the plaster—and taken outside the city to an unclean place. “
Anyone who enters the house during any of the days it is closed up will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sleeps in the house or eats in it must wash his clothes.
If, however, the priest comes and inspects it and the mold has not spread in the house after it was plastered, the priest must announce that the house is clean, because the mold is healed. “
To make the house clean, he must take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop.
He must kill one of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot.
Then he must take the cedar wood, hyssop, scarlet yarn, and live bird, dip them in the blood of the killed bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times. “
In this way he will cleanse the house with the blood of the bird, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet yarn.
Then he must let the live bird go free in the open field outside the city. In this way he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean. “
This is the law for any infectious skin disease, for a scaly outbreak,
for mold in clothing or in a house,
and for a swelling, rash, or bright spot,
to decide when something is clean or unclean. This is the law about skin diseases.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
He said to speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any man has a discharge from his body, that discharge makes him unclean.
This is how his discharge makes him unclean: whether his body lets the discharge flow or holds it back, it is his uncleanness.
Every bed he lies on is unclean, and everything he sits on is unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
Anyone who sits on something the man with the discharge sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches the body of the man with the discharge must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
Every saddle he rides on is unclean.
Anyone who touches anything under him is unclean until evening. Whoever carries those things must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
If the man with the discharge touches someone without first rinsing his hands in water, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
A clay pot he touches must be broken, and any wooden article must be rinsed with water.
When the man with the discharge is cleansed from it, he must count seven days for his cleansing. He must wash his clothes and bathe his body in running water; then he is clean.
On the eighth day he must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons. He must come before the the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and give them to the priest.
The priest must sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest makes atonement for him before the the LORD for his discharge.
When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body in water, and he is unclean until evening.
Any clothing or leather that has semen on it must be washed with water, and it is unclean until evening.
When a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both must bathe in water, and they are unclean until evening.
When a woman has a discharge of blood from her body, she is unclean for seven days. Anyone who touches her is unclean until evening.
Anything she lies on during her period is unclean, and anything she sits on is unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches anything she sits on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
If something is on the bed or on the thing she sits on, and someone touches it, he is unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her and her period comes on him, he is unclean for seven days, and every bed he lies on is unclean.
If a woman has a flow of blood for many days at a time other than her monthly period, or if it continues beyond her period, she is unclean all the days of her flow, just as she is during her period.
Any bed she lies on during the days of her flow is unclean, like her bed during her period. Anything she sits on is unclean, like the uncleanness of her period.
Anyone who touches them is unclean; he must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
When she is cleansed from her flow, she must count seven days, and then she is clean.
On the eighth day she must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest must sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest makes atonement for her before the the LORD for her unclean flow.
You must keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so they will not die in their uncleanness by making My tabernacle unclean, which is among them.
These are the rules for the man with a discharge, for anyone who has an emission of semen and becomes unclean by it,
for the woman in her period, and for anyone, male or female, who has a discharge. This also applies to a man who lies with an unclean woman.
The LORD spoke to Moses after two of Aaron's sons died. They had come near to the LORD, and they died.

The LORD said to Moses, “Tell your brother Aaron not to enter the Holy Place behind the curtain at just any time. He must not go in front of the mercy seat on the ark, or he will die, because I will appear in the cloud over the mercy seat.
“Aaron must enter the Holy Place with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

He must wear the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments against his body, a linen sash around him, and a linen turban on his head. These are holy clothes. He must wash his whole body with water before he puts them on.
He must take from the Israelite community two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
“Aaron must bring the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
He must take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Aaron must cast lots for the two goats. One lot is for the LORD, and the other lot is for Azazel.
Aaron must present the goat chosen by lot for the LORD and sacrifice it as a sin offering.
The goat chosen by lot for Azazel must be kept alive and presented before the LORD. Atonement must be made over it, and then it must be sent into the wilderness to Azazel.
“Aaron must bring the bull for his sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household. He must slaughter the bull.
He must take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and he must fill both hands with finely ground incense. He must bring them behind the curtain.
He must put the incense on the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense covers the mercy seat above the ark of the Testimony. Then he will not die.

He must take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the mercy seat on the east side. He must sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times in front of the mercy seat.

“Then he must slaughter the goat for the people's sin offering and bring its blood behind the curtain. He must do with its blood what he did with the bull's blood. He must sprinkle it on the mercy seat and in front of the mercy seat.

In this way he will make atonement for the Holy Place because of the uncleanness and rebellion of the Israelites, whatever their sins. He must do the same for the tent of meeting, which stays among them in the middle of their uncleanness.
No one may be in the tent of meeting when Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Holy Place until he comes out. He must make atonement for himself, his household, and the whole community of Israel.
“Then he must go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He must take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.
He must sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times. In this way he will cleanse it and set it apart from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
After he has finished making atonement for the Holy Place, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he must bring the live goat.

“Aaron must place both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the wickedness, rebellion, and sins of the Israelites. He must put them on the goat's head. Then he must send the goat into the wilderness with a man appointed for the task.
The goat will carry all their sins to a desolate place. The man must release the goat in the wilderness.
“Then Aaron must go into the tent of meeting and take off the linen clothes he wore when he entered the Holy Place. He must leave them there.

He must wash his body with water in a holy place and put on his own clothes. Then he must come out and offer his burnt offering and the people's burnt offering. He must make atonement for himself and for the people.
He must burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
“The man who released the goat for Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe his body with water. After that, he may come into the camp.

The bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp. Their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned in the fire.
The person who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe his body with water. After that, he may come into the camp.
“This will be a permanent rule for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month, you must deny yourselves and not do any work. This applies to the native-born and to the foreigner living among you.
Because on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you. Then you will be clean before the LORD from all your sins.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must deny yourselves. This is a permanent rule.
“The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve in his father's place must make atonement. He must wear the holy linen clothes.
He must make atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting, and the altar. He must make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the community.
This will be a permanent rule for you. Once a year, atonement must be made for the Israelites for all their sins.” He did as the LORD commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites. Tell them, 'This is what the LORD has commanded:
Any Israelite who slaughters an ox, a sheep, or a goat in the camp or outside it,
and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to offer it to the LORD before the LORD, is guilty of bloodshed. He has spilled blood and must be removed from his people.
This is so the Israelites will bring the sacrifices they now make in the open field to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and sacrifice them as peace offerings to the LORD.
The priest will sprinkle the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing smell to the LORD.
They must no longer sacrifice to goat demons, which they chase after. This will be a lasting law for them and their descendants.'
"Say to them, 'Any Israelite or foreigner living among you who offers a burnt offering or sacrifice
and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to make it to the LORD must be removed from his people.'
"Any Israelite or foreigner living among you who eats any blood, I will oppose that person who eats blood and remove him from his people.
For the life of the body is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for your lives on the altar. It is the blood that makes atonement because the life is in it.
Therefore I said to the Israelites, 'No person among you may eat blood, and no foreigner living among you may eat blood.'
"Any Israelite or foreigner living among you who hunts and catches a wild animal or a bird that may be eaten must pour out its blood and cover it with dirt.

For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I said to the Israelites, 'You must not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood. Anyone who eats it will be removed from his people.'

"Any person, whether a native Israelite or a foreigner, who eats an animal that died on its own or was torn by wild animals must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He will be unclean until evening, and then he will be clean.
But if he does not wash his clothes or bathe his body, he will carry his guilt."
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: I am the LORD your God.
You must not live like the people in Egypt, where you used to live, and you must not live like the people in Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not follow their customs.
You are to follow My laws and keep My rules, walking in them. I am the LORD your God.
Keep My rules and laws. A person who does these things will live by them. I am the LORD.
"No one may have sexual relations with a close relative. I am the LORD.
"You must not have sexual relations with your mother; she is your mother. You must not have sexual relations with her.
You must not have sexual relations with your father's wife; that would dishonor your father.
You must not have sexual relations with your sister, whether she is your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born at home or born somewhere else.
"You must not have sexual relations with your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, because they are your own flesh and blood.
You must not have sexual relations with the daughter of your father's wife who was born to your father; she is your sister.
You must not have sexual relations with your father's sister; she is your father's close relative.
You must not have sexual relations with your mother's sister, because she is your mother's close relative.
"You must not have sexual relations with your father's brother's wife; you must not go near her. She is your aunt.
You must not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law; she is your son's wife. You must not have sexual relations with her.
You must not have sexual relations with your brother's wife; that would dishonor your brother.
You must not have sexual relations with a woman and her daughter, and you must not take her granddaughter to have sexual relations with her. They are close relatives, and it is wicked.
"You must not take a woman's sister as a rival wife and have sexual relations with her while the first sister is still alive.
You must not have sexual relations with a woman during her monthly period.
You must not have sexual relations with your neighbor's wife and make yourself unclean with her.
You must not give any of your children to Molech, and you must not misuse the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You must not lie with a man as you would with a woman; that is detestable.
You must not have sexual relations with an animal and make yourself unclean with it. A woman must not offer herself to an animal. That is a perversion.
"You must not make yourselves unclean by any of these things, because the nations I am driving out before you became unclean by doing them.
The land became unclean, so I punished it for its sin, and the land vomited out its people.
You must keep My rules and laws, and you must not do any of these hateful things. This applies to the native-born and to the foreigner living among you.
The men who lived in the land before you did all these hateful things, and the land became unclean.
If you make the land unclean, it will vomit you out, just as it vomited out the nation before you.
"Anyone who does any of these hateful things must be cut off from his people.
You must keep My command not to practice any of these hateful customs that were practiced before you, and you must not make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God."
The LORD spoke to Moses and told him to tell all the people of Israel,
"Be holy, because I am the LORD your God, and I am holy."
Each person must respect his mother and father, and keep My Sabbath days. I am the LORD your God.
Do not turn to idols, and do not make metal gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
When you bring a fellowship offering to the LORD, offer it so He will accept it.
Eat it on the day you offer it and the next day. Burn any that is left on the third day.
If anyone eats it on the third day, it is spoiled and will not be accepted.
The person who eats it will be guilty, because he has treated something holy to the LORD as unholy. That person will be removed from his people.
When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap your field all the way to the edge, and do not gather the leftover grain.
Do not strip your vineyard bare, and do not pick up the fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
Do not steal. Do not be dishonest, and do not lie to each other.
Do not swear falsely by My name and dishonor the name of your God. I am the LORD.
Do not cheat your neighbor or rob him. Do not keep a worker's pay overnight.
Do not curse a deaf person, and do not put something in front of a blind person that makes him fall. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
Do not be unfair in court. Do not favor the poor, and do not show special respect to the rich. Judge your neighbor fairly.
Do not spread gossip among your people, and do not do anything that puts your neighbor's life in danger. I am the LORD.
Do not hate your brother in your heart. Correct your neighbor honestly, so you will not share his guilt.
Do not take revenge or hold a grudge against your people. Love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
Keep My laws. Do not breed your animals with a different kind. Do not plant two kinds of seed in your field. Do not wear clothing made of mixed fabrics.

If a man has sexual relations with a slave woman who is promised to another man, and she has not been bought back or set free, they must be punished. But they will not be put to death, because she was not free.
The man must bring a ram to the entrance of the tent of meeting as a guilt offering to the LORD.
The priest will offer the ram to make peace with the LORD for the sin the man committed, and the man will be forgiven.
When you come into the land and plant any tree for food, treat its fruit as forbidden to you for three years. Do not eat it.
In the fourth year, all its fruit will be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
In the fifth year, you may eat the fruit, so it will produce more for you. I am the LORD your God.
Do not eat meat that still has blood in it. Do not practice magic or fortune-telling.
Do not cut the hair at the sides of your head, and do not trim the edges of your beard.
Do not cut your body for the dead, and do not tattoo yourselves. I am the LORD.
Do not dishonor your daughter by making her a prostitute.
If you do, the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with evil. Keep My Sabbaths and respect My holy place. I am the LORD.
Do not turn to mediums or people who claim to speak with the dead. Do not seek them out, or you will become unclean. I am the LORD your God.
Stand up in the presence of the elderly, and show respect to older people. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
When a foreigner lives with you in your land, do not wrong him.
Treat the foreigner living among you as one of your own people. Love him as you love yourself, because you were foreigners in Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
Do not cheat in court, in measures of length, weight, or amount.
Use honest scales, honest weights, and honest measures. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt.
Keep all My laws and rules, and obey them. I am the LORD.
He said, "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: Any Israelite or foreigner living in Israel who gives one of his children to Molech must be put to death. The people of the land must stone him.
"I will turn My face against that man and cut him off from his people, because he gave his child to Molech. He made My holy place unclean and treated My holy name with disrespect.
"If the people of the land ignore him and do not put him to death when he gives his child to Molech,
I will turn My face against that man and his family. I will cut them off from their people. That includes him and everyone who follows him by worshiping Molech.
"I will turn My face against anyone who turns to people who talk to spirits and gives himself to them. I will cut that person off from his people.
"Set yourselves apart and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
Keep My rules and follow them. I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
"Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death. He cursed his father or mother, so his death is his own fault.
If a man sleeps with another man's wife, both of them must be put to death.
"If a man sleeps with his father's wife, he has dishonored his father. Both of them must be put to death. They are responsible for their own deaths.
If a man sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. What they did is a perversion. They are responsible for their own deaths.
If a man sleeps with a man as with a woman, both of them have done a hateful thing. They must be put to death. They are responsible for their own deaths.
"If a man marries a woman and her mother, it is wicked. He and the two women must be burned in fire, so that wickedness will not be among you.
If a man has sex with an animal, he must be put to death, and you must kill the animal.
If a woman goes near an animal to have sex with it, kill both the woman and the animal. They must be put to death. They are responsible for their own deaths.

"If a man marries his sister, the daughter of either his father or his mother, and they have sex, it is a disgrace. They must be removed from their people in front of everyone. He has dishonored his sister and will answer for it.
If a man has sex with a woman during her monthly period, he has exposed the source of her bleeding, and she has uncovered it too. Both of them must be cut off from their people.
"Do not have sex with your mother's sister or your father's sister. That would dishonor a close relative, and both people involved would be held responsible.
If a man has sex with his aunt, he dishonors his uncle. They will be held responsible and will die without children.
If a man marries his brother's wife, it is unclean. He has dishonored his brother. They will have no children.
"Keep all My rules and laws and follow them. Then the land I am bringing you to live in will not throw you out.
Do not follow the customs of the nations I am driving out before you. They did all these things, and I was disgusted by them.
"But I said to you, 'You will take their land. I will give it to you to own. It is a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God. I set you apart from the nations.'

"So you must tell the difference between clean and unclean animals and between unclean and clean birds. Do not make yourselves unclean by any animal or bird or anything that crawls on the ground. I have set those apart as unclean for you.
You are to be holy to Me, because I, the LORD, am holy. I have set you apart from the nations to be Mine.
"A man or woman among you who is a medium or spiritist must be put to death. You must stone them. They are responsible for their own deaths."
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron and his sons and tell them: No priest among his people may make himself unclean by touching a dead body,
except for his close relatives—his mother, father, son, daughter, and brother.
He may also make himself unclean for his virgin sister who is close to him and has never married.
He must not make himself unclean for those related to him by marriage, and so dishonor himself."
They must not shave their heads bald, trim the edges of their beards, or cut their bodies.
They must be holy to their God and not dishonor His name, because they present the LORD's food offerings, the bread of their God. So they must be holy.
They must not marry a woman who has been a prostitute or who has been divorced from her husband, because the priest is holy to his God.
You must set him apart as holy, because he offers the bread of your God. He must be holy to you, because I, the LORD, am holy—I am the One who makes you holy.
If a priest's daughter makes herself unclean by becoming a prostitute, she disgraces her father; she must be burned with fire.

The priest who is highest among his brothers—the one who has had the anointing oil poured on his head and who has been set apart to wear the holy clothes—must not let his hair hang loose or tear his clothes.
He must not go near any dead body or make himself unclean, even for his father or mother.
He must not leave the holy place or dishonor the holy place of his God, because the special oil that sets him apart to his God is on him. I am the LORD.
He must marry a woman who is still a virgin.
He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, a woman who has been defiled, or a prostitute. He may marry only a virgin from his own people,
so that he does not dishonor his children among his people. I am the LORD, who makes him holy.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to Aaron and say: In every generation, no man among your descendants who has a physical defect may come near to offer the bread of his God.
No man with a defect may come near: no blind man, no lame man, no man with a damaged face or a deformed limb,
no man with an injured foot or an injured hand,
no hunchback or dwarf, no man with an eye defect or a skin disease or scabs, and no man with crushed testicles.
No man from the family of Aaron the priest who has a defect may come near to present the LORD's food offerings. Because he has a defect, he must not come near to offer the bread of his God.
He may still eat the bread of his God, both from the most holy offerings and from the holy offerings.
But he must not go behind the curtain or come near the altar, because he has a defect. He must not dishonor My holy places, for I am the LORD, who makes them holy."
So Moses spoke to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to Aaron and his sons. Tell them to stay away from the holy things the Israelites set apart for Me, so they do not dishonor My holy name. I am the LORD. "

Say to them: Throughout your generations, any man among your descendants who comes near the holy things that the Israelites set apart for the LORD while he is unclean will be cut off from My presence. I am the LORD. "

Any man among Aaron's descendants who has a skin disease or a discharge must not eat the holy food until he is clean. Anyone who touches something made unclean by a dead body, or a man who has a flow of semen,
or anyone who touches a creature that makes him unclean, or a person who makes him unclean in any way,
will be unclean until evening. He must not eat the holy food unless he washes his body with water.
When the sun goes down, he will be clean, and after that he may eat the holy food, because it is his food.
He must not eat an animal that died on its own or was torn by wild animals, or he will become unclean by it. I am the LORD. "
The priests must guard My commands so they do not become guilty of sin and die for breaking them. I am the LORD, who makes them holy.
No one outside a priest's family may eat a holy offering. A guest of a priest or a hired worker may not eat a holy offering.
But if a priest buys a slave with his money, that slave may eat it. A child born in his house may also eat his food.
If a priest's daughter marries a man who is not a priest, she may not eat the holy offerings set apart for God.
But if she is a widow or divorced, has no children, and returns to her father's house as she did when she was young, she may eat her father's food. No outsider may eat it.
If a man eats a holy offering by mistake, he must add one-fifth more and give the holy offering to the priest.
The Israelites must not dishonor the holy things they offer to the LORD.
If they do, they will bring guilt on themselves when they eat those holy things, because I am the LORD, who makes them holy."
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,

"Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites. Say to them: When any man from the family of Israel or from the foreigners living in Israel brings his offering to the LORD, whether for a special promise or a gift he chooses to give, as a burnt offering to the LORD, "
you must bring a male animal without a flaw from the cattle, sheep, or goats so it will be accepted for you.
Do not bring an animal with a flaw, because it will not be accepted for you.
When a man brings a peace offering to the LORD to keep a promise or as a gift, from the herd or the flock, it must be perfect to be accepted. It must have no flaw.
Do not bring an animal that is blind, injured, maimed, or has a running sore, a scab, or a rash. Do not place any of these on the altar as a food offering to the LORD.
An ox or sheep that is deformed or stunted may be given as a freewill offering, but it will not be accepted to keep a promise.
Do not offer to the LORD an animal that is bruised, crushed, torn, or cut. Do not do this in your land.
Do not bring the food of your God from a foreigner's hand from any of these animals. Their defects are in them; they have a flaw, so they will not be accepted for you."
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"When an ox, sheep, or goat is born, it must stay with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be accepted as a food offering to the LORD.
Do not kill an ox or sheep and its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thanksgiving offering to the LORD, you must sacrifice it in a way that will be accepted for you.
It must be eaten on the same day. Do not leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD. "
Keep My commands and obey them. I am the LORD.
Do not dishonor My holy name. I will be treated as holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
I am the one who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: These are My appointed feasts, the feasts of the LORD that you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies.
"For six days you may work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a sacred assembly. You must not do any work; wherever you live, it is a Sabbath to the LORD.
"These are the LORD's appointed feasts, the sacred assemblies you are to proclaim at their appointed times.
"The Passover to the LORD begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month.
"On the fifteenth day of that same month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the LORD. For seven days you must eat unleavened bread.
"On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.
"For seven days you are to present an offering made by fire to the LORD. On the seventh day there is to be a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work."
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land I am giving you and reap its harvest, you are to bring to the priest a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest.
"The priest is to wave the sheaf before the LORD so it will be accepted on your behalf. He is to wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
"On the day you wave the sheaf, you are to offer a year-old male lamb without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD,
"along with a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil—an offering made by fire to the LORD, a pleasing smell—and a drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.
"You must not eat any bread or roasted grain or fresh grain until the very day you bring this offering to your God. This is to be a permanent rule for you and your descendants wherever you live.
"From the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering, you are to count seven full weeks.
"You are to count fifty days until the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then present an offering of new grain to the LORD.
"From your homes you are to bring two loaves of bread as a wave offering, made from two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked with yeast, as firstfruits to the LORD.

"Along with the bread, you are to present seven unblemished male lambs a year old, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the LORD, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings—an offering made by fire, a pleasing smell to the LORD.
"You are also to offer one male goat as a sin offering and two male lambs a year old as a peace offering.
"The priest is to wave them with the bread of the firstfruits as a wave offering before the LORD, along with the two lambs. They will be holy to the LORD for the priest.
"On that same day you are to proclaim a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work. This is to be a permanent rule for you and your descendants wherever you live.

"When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God."
