"Speak to the Israelites and say: On the first day of the seventh month you are to have a day of rest, a sacred assembly announced with trumpet blasts.
"You must not do any regular work, but you are to present an offering made by fire to the LORD."
"The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. You are to hold a sacred assembly and humble yourselves, and present an offering made by fire to the LORD.
"On this day you are not to do any work, for it is the Day of Atonement, when atonement is made for you before the LORD your God.
"If anyone does not humble himself on this day, he must be cut off from his people.
"I will destroy anyone among his people who does any work on this day.
"You are not to do any work at all. This is to be a permanent rule for you and your descendants wherever you live.
"It will be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you are to humble yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening, you are to keep your Sabbath."
"Speak to the Israelites and say: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the LORD's Feast of Tabernacles begins, and it lasts for seven days.
"On the first day there is to be a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.

"For seven days you are to present an offering made by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you are to hold a sacred assembly and present an offering made by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work.

"These are the LORD's appointed feasts, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies for presenting offerings made by fire to the LORD—burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings—each on its appointed day.
"These offerings are in addition to the LORD's Sabbaths, and in addition to your gifts, your vows, and your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.

"On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you have gathered the produce of the land, you are to celebrate the LORD's feast for seven days. The first day is a day of rest, and the eighth day also is a day of rest.
"On the first day you are to take the fruit of beautiful trees, palm branches, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook, and rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
"You are to celebrate this feast to the LORD for seven days each year. This is to be a permanent rule for you and your descendants; you are to celebrate it in the seventh month.
"You are to live in booths for seven days. All native-born Israelites must live in booths,
"so that your descendants may know that I made the Israelites live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."
So Moses told the Israelites the appointed feasts of the LORD.
Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil from pressed olives for the light, so the lamps can burn all the time.
Outside the curtain of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron must arrange it all the time, from evening to morning, before the LORD. This is a lasting rule for all your generations.
He must arrange the lamps on the pure lampstand before the LORD all the time. "
You must take fine flour and bake twelve loaves of bread. Each loaf should use two-tenths of an ephah of flour.
Put the loaves in two rows, six in each row, on the pure table before the LORD.
Put pure frankincense on each row. It will be a memorial portion for the bread, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
Every Sabbath day, arrange it before the LORD all the time. This is a lasting promise from the Israelites.
It belongs to Aaron and his sons. They must eat it in a holy place, because it is most holy to him from the offerings made by fire to the LORD. This is a lasting rule."
The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian father went out among the Israelites. He and an Israelite man got into a fight in the camp.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed. They brought him to Moses. His mother was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
They put him under guard until the LORD's will was made clear to them.
Bring out the one who cursed to outside the camp. Let all who heard him lay their hands on his head. Then let the whole congregation stone him.
Speak to the Israelites and say, 'Anyone who curses his God will bear his sin.

Whoever blasphemes the Name of the LORD must surely be put to death. The whole congregation must stone him. It does not matter whether he is a foreigner or a native-born Israelite; when he blasphemes the Name, he must be put to death.
Whoever takes a human life must surely be put to death.
Whoever kills an animal must pay for it, life for life.
If a man injures his neighbor, he must be treated the same way he treated the other person.
A broken bone for a broken bone, an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth. The injury he causes another person must be given back to him.
Whoever kills an animal must pay for it, but whoever kills a person must be put to death.
You must use the same law for the foreigner and the native-born, for I am the LORD your God.'"
Moses spoke to the Israelites. They brought the man who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him. The Israelites did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
He told Moses to speak to the Israelites and say that when you entered the land He was giving you, the land had to keep a Sabbath rest for the LORD.
For six years you may plant your field, prune your vineyard, and gather its crops.
But in the seventh year the land must have a full Sabbath rest, a Sabbath for the LORD. Do not plant your field or prune your vineyard.
Do not harvest what grows on its own, and do not pick grapes from vines you have not trimmed. That year is a complete rest for the land.

Whatever the land produces during its Sabbath may be food for you, your male and female servants, your hired workers, and the foreigners living with you. It may also feed your livestock and the wild animals in your land.
All its crops may be eaten.
You must count seven Sabbaths of years—seven times seven years, or forty-nine years.
On the tenth day of the seventh month, on the Day of Atonement, sound the trumpet all through your land.

Set apart the fiftieth year as holy, and proclaim freedom throughout the land for everyone who lives there. That year is a Jubilee for you. Each of you must return to his own property and to his family.
The fiftieth year is a Jubilee for you. Do not plant, do not harvest what grows on its own, and do not pick grapes from untrimmed vines.
You may eat what the field produces on its own.
In that Year of Jubilee, each of you must return to his own property.
If you sell land to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor, do not cheat each other.
Buy from your neighbor based on the number of years since the Jubilee, and he will sell to you based on the number of harvests.
If many years remain, the price will be higher; if few years remain, the price will be lower, because he is selling you a number of harvests.
Do not cheat one another. Respect your God, for I am the LORD your God.
Keep My laws and obey My rules. Then you will live safely in the land.
The land will give its fruit, you will eat until you are full, and you will live safely on it.
You may ask what you will eat in the seventh year if you do not plant or gather your crops.
But I will send My blessing for you in the sixth year, so the land will produce enough for three years.
You will plant in the eighth year and eat from the old crop until the ninth year's harvest comes in.
The land must not be sold for all time, because it is Mine. You are foreigners and temporary residents with Me.
In all the land you own, you must allow the land to be bought back.
If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his property, his nearest relative may buy it back for him.
If no one can buy it back for him but he can afford it himself, he must count the years since he sold it, pay back the extra money to the buyer, and return to his property.
If he cannot afford to buy it back, it stays with the buyer until the Year of Jubilee.
Then it is released, and he returns to his property.
If a man sells a house in a walled city, he may buy it back until one full year after the sale.
After a full year, the house in the walled city belongs permanently to the buyer and his descendants; it will not be released in the Jubilee.
Houses in villages without walls are treated like open fields. They may be bought back, and they are released in the Jubilee.
The Levites may always buy back the houses in their cities, and those houses are released in the Jubilee.
This is because the houses in the Levite cities are their permanent possession among the Israelites.
The fields around their cities may not be sold, because that is their permanent possession.
If your brother becomes poor and cannot support himself with you, help him as you would a foreigner or temporary resident, so he can live with you.
Do not charge him interest or make a profit from him, but respect your God, so your brother can live with you.
Do not lend him your money at interest or sell him your food for profit.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your brother becomes poor among you and sells himself to you, do not make him work like a slave.
Treat him as a hired worker or temporary resident. He is to work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
Then he and his children are to leave you and return to his family and to the property of his ancestors.
They are My servants, whom I brought out of Egypt. They must not be sold as slaves.
Do not rule over him harshly, but respect your God.
You may buy male and female slaves from the nations around you.
You may also buy them from the children of the foreigners living among you, and from their families born in your land. They may become your property.
You may leave them to your children as an inheritance and make them slaves for life. But you must not rule harshly over your brothers, the Israelites.
If a foreigner or temporary resident with you becomes rich and your brother becomes poor and sells himself to that foreigner or resident, or to a member of his family,
he keeps the right to be bought back after he is sold. One of his brothers may buy him back.
An uncle, a cousin, or another close relative may buy him back, or he may buy himself back if he can afford it.
He and his buyer must count the years from the year he was sold to the Year of Jubilee. His price is to be set like a hired worker's, based on the number of years left.
If many years remain, he must pay a larger part of his purchase price to be bought back.
If only a few years remain until the Jubilee, he is to be charged less.
He is to be treated as a hired worker from year to year, and his master must not rule over him harshly in your presence.
If he is not bought back in any of these ways, he and his children are released in the Year of Jubilee.
For the Israelites are My servants. I brought them out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
Do not make useless idols for yourselves. Do not set up a carved image or a sacred stone for yourselves. Do not put a carved stone in your land to bow down to it. I am the LORD your God.
Keep My Sabbaths and respect My sanctuary. I am the LORD.
If you walk in My laws and keep My commands and do them,
then I will give you rain at the right time. The land will give its crops, and the trees in the field will give their fruit.
Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will last until planting time. You will eat your bread until you are full, and you will live safely in your land.
I will give peace in the land. You will lie down, and no one will make you afraid. I will remove wild animals from the land, and no sword will pass through your land.
You will chase your enemies, and they will fall by the sword before you.
Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand. Your enemies will fall by the sword before you.
I will turn to you and make you fruitful and multiply you. I will keep My agreement with you.
You will eat old grain and clear out the old to make room for the new.
I will put My dwelling place among you, and I will not reject you.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt so you would not be slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and led you to walk proudly.
But if you will not listen to Me and do not obey all these commands,
and if you reject My laws and hate them in your hearts, so you do not obey all My commands, you break My agreement.
Then I will do this to you: I will bring sudden terror on you—wasting disease and fever that harm your eyes and drain your life. You will plant seed for nothing, because your enemies will eat it.
I will turn against you, and your enemies will defeat you. Those who hate you will rule over you. You will run even when no one is chasing you.
If after all this you still will not listen to Me, I will punish you seven times more for your sins.
I will break your stubborn pride. I will make your sky like iron and your ground like bronze.
Your strength will be used up for nothing. Your land will not give its crops, and the trees in the land will not give their fruit.
If you keep walking against Me and will not listen to Me, I will add seven more blows for your sins.
I will send wild animals against you. They will rob you of your children, kill your animals, and make your roads empty, so that few of you are left.
If even then you are not corrected by Me but keep walking against Me,
then I will also walk against you in anger. I will strike you seven times for your sins.
I will bring a sword against you that punishes you for breaking My agreement. You will gather in your cities, but I will send disease among you, and you will be handed over to your enemy.
When I cut off your bread supply, ten women will bake bread in one oven. They will weigh out your bread, and you will eat but not be full.
If after this you still will not listen to Me but keep walking against Me,
then I will walk against you in My burning anger. I will punish you seven times for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters.
I will destroy your hilltop shrines and cut down your sun idols. I will pile your dead bodies on the dead bodies of your idols, and I will reject you.
I will turn your cities into ruins and destroy your holy places. I will not accept your pleasing aroma.
I will destroy the land so much that your enemies who live there will be shocked by it.
I will scatter you among the nations and chase you with a sword. Your land will be empty, and your cities will be ruins.
Then the land will enjoy its Sabbath rest all the time it lies empty, while you are in your enemies' land. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
It will rest the whole time it is empty, the rest it did not get during your Sabbaths when you lived there.

Those of you who are left, I will make so afraid in your enemies' lands that the sound of a blowing leaf will chase them. They will run as if running from a sword and fall, even though no one is chasing them.
They will stumble over each other as if running from a sword, though no one is chasing them. You will have no strength to stand before your enemies.
You will be consumed in your enemies' land.
Those left among you will waste away in your enemies' lands because of their sins and their fathers' sins.
But if they confess their sin and the sin of their fathers—the unfaithfulness they showed against Me, and how they walked against Me—
then I will also walk against them in anger and bring them into their enemies' land. But if their stubborn hearts become humble and they accept the punishment for their sin,
then I will remember My agreement with Jacob, and I will remember My agreement with Isaac, and I will remember My agreement with Abraham. I will remember the land.

The land will be left by them and will enjoy its Sabbath rest while it lies empty without them. They will accept the punishment for their sin, because they rejected My laws and hated My rules in their hearts.
Yet even then, while they are in their enemies' land, I will not reject them or hate them so much that I destroy them and break My agreement with them. I am the LORD their God.
For their sake I will remember the first agreement I made when I brought them out of Egypt in front of the nations, to be their God. I am the LORD.
These are the laws, rules, and teachings that the LORD gave between Himself and the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If a man makes a special vow to the the LORD, the value of that person is set by these rules."
For a man from twenty to sixty years old, the value is fifty shekels of silver, using the holy shekel.
For a woman, the value is thirty shekels.
For a boy from five to twenty years old, the value is twenty shekels; for a girl, ten shekels.
For a child from one month to five years old, the value is five shekels for a boy and three shekels for a girl.
For a man sixty years or older, the value is fifteen shekels; for a woman, ten shekels.
If the person is too poor to pay the set value, he must stand before the priest. The priest will value him based on what the person who made the vow can afford.
If someone vows an animal that may be offered to the the LORD, it becomes holy. Anything from it that is given to the the LORD is holy.
Do not switch it for another animal, whether better or worse. If it is switched, both the original animal and its replacement become holy.
If the animal is unclean and cannot be offered, it must be brought before the priest.
The priest will value it, whether good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets is the price.
If the owner buys it back, he must add one-fifth to that value.
If a man sets apart his house as holy to the the LORD, the priest will value it, whether good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets will stand.
If the man who set it apart buys it back, he must add one-fifth to its value, and then it is his again.
If a man sets apart to the the LORD a field from his family land, the value is based on how much seed it takes. A field that takes a homer of barley seed is valued at fifty shekels of silver.
If he sets it apart in the Jubilee year, the value stands as given.
If he sets it apart after the Jubilee year, the priest will count the years left until the next Jubilee year and reduce the value.
If the man who set it apart buys it back, he must add one-fifth to its value, and then it is his again.
If he does not buy it back, or if he sells the field to someone else, it can no longer be bought back.
When the field is released in the Jubilee year, it becomes holy to the the LORD, like a field devoted to the the LORD. The priest receives it as his property.
If a man sets apart to the the LORD a field he bought, which is not part of his family land,
the priest will figure its value up to the Jubilee year. The man must give that amount as holy to the the LORD that day.
In the Jubilee year, the field goes back to the man it was bought from, the one who owns the land.
Every value is to be in the holy shekel, which has twenty gerahs.
No one may set apart the firstborn of an animal, whether ox or sheep, because the firstborn already belongs to the the LORD.
If it is an unclean animal, the owner may buy it back at its set value plus one-fifth. If it is not bought back, it must be sold at its set value.
But anything a person devotes to the the LORD from all he has—whether a person, an animal, or a field—must not be sold or bought back. It is most holy to the the LORD.
No person devoted to destruction may be ransomed. That person must be put to death.
A tenth of the land's produce, whether grain or fruit from trees, belongs to the the LORD and is holy to Him.
If a man buys back any part of his tithe, he must add one-fifth to it.
Every tenth animal from the herd or flock, counted as it passes under the shepherd's rod, is holy to the the LORD.
The owner must not sort out the good from the bad or swap one animal for another. If he does swap them, both animals become holy and cannot be bought back.
These are the commands the the LORD gave Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
On the first day of the second month, in the second year after the Israelites left Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Sinai Desert. He said:
"Take a census of all the Israelites. List them by their clans and families, and write down the name of every male, one by one.
"You and Aaron must count every man who is twenty years old or older and can serve in Israel's army. Count them by their groups.
"A man from each tribe will help you. Each one is the leader of his family.

"These are the names of the men who will help you: From Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur; from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai; from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab; from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar; from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon; from the sons of Joseph—from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur; from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni; from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai; from Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran; from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel; and from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan."
These men were chosen from the community. They were the leaders of their tribes and the heads of Israel's family groups.
So Moses and Aaron took these men, whose names had been given.
On the first day of the second month, they gathered the whole community and recorded each person's family line. They counted every man who was twenty years old or older, one by one.
They did this just as the LORD had commanded Moses, and he counted them in the Sinai Desert.
The descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn son, were counted by their clans and families. Every male twenty years old or older who could serve in the army was counted.
Simeon's descendants were counted the same way.
Gad's descendants were counted the same way.
Judah's descendants were counted the same way.
Issachar's descendants were counted the same way.
Zebulun's descendants were counted the same way.
The descendants of Joseph were counted through his sons Ephraim and Manasseh.
Manasseh's descendants were counted the same way.
Benjamin's descendants were counted the same way.
Dan's descendants were counted the same way.
Asher's descendants were counted the same way.
Naphtali's descendants were counted the same way.
These were the men Moses and Aaron counted, along with the twelve leaders of Israel. Each leader stood for his family.
All the Israelites who were twenty years old or older and could serve in Israel's army were counted by their families.
The Levites were not counted with the other tribes.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Do not count the tribe of Levi. Do not include them in the census of the Israelites.

"Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle that holds the covenant law and everything that belongs to it. They must carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings. They must serve it and camp around it.
"When the tabernacle is to move, the Levites must take it down. When it is to be set up, they must put it up. Anyone else who comes near it must be put to death.
"The Israelites must camp by their groups. Each man must stay in his own camp under his own banner.
"But the Levites must camp around the tabernacle that holds the covenant law. Then God's anger will not fall on the Israelite community. The Levites are in charge of caring for the tabernacle."
The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
"The Israelites are to camp around the Tent of Meeting, but not right beside it. Each man is to camp under his own banner, with the banners of his family group. They are to camp all around it.
"On the east side, toward the sunrise, the divisions of Judah are to camp under their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab is the leader of the people of Judah.
Next to him, the tribe of Issachar is to camp. Nethanel son of Zuar is the leader of the people of Issachar.
Then the tribe of Zebulun is to camp. Eliab son of Helon is the leader of the people of Zebulun.
The total for the camp of Judah is 186,400 men. They are to move out first.
"On the south side, the divisions of Reuben are to camp under their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur is the leader of the people of Reuben.
Next to him, the tribe of Simeon is to camp. Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai is the leader of the people of Simeon.
Then the tribe of Gad is to camp. Eliasaph son of Reuel is the leader of the people of Gad.
The total for the camp of Reuben is 151,450 men. They are to move out second.
Then the Tent of Meeting and the Levites' camp will set out in the middle of the camps. They will move in the same order they camp, each man in his place under his banner.
"On the west side, the divisions of Ephraim are to camp under their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud is the leader of the people of Ephraim.
Next to him, the tribe of Manasseh is to camp. Gamaliel son of Pedahzur is the leader of the people of Manasseh.
Then the tribe of Benjamin is to camp. Abidan son of Gideoni is the leader of the people of Benjamin.
The total for the camp of Ephraim is 108,100 men. They are to move out third.
"On the north side, the divisions of Dan are to camp under their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai is the leader of the people of Dan.
Next to him, the tribe of Asher is to camp. Pagiel son of Ocran is the leader of the people of Asher.
Then the tribe of Naphtali is to camp. Ahira son of Enan is the leader of the people of Naphtali.
The total for the camp of Dan is 157,600 men. They are to move out last, under their banners."
These are the Israelites counted by their families. The total of all the camps by their divisions is 603,550 men.
The Levites were not counted among the Israelites, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So the Israelites did everything the LORD commanded Moses. They camped under their banners, and they set out in the same order. Each man went with his family and his father's house.
These are the family lines of Aaron and Moses from the time the LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
Aaron's sons were Nadab, the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These were Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, who were set apart to serve as priests.

Nadab and Abihu died before the the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the the LORD in the Sinai wilderness. They had no sons, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests while their father Aaron was still alive.
"Bring the tribe of Levi and present them before Aaron the priest so they can serve him.
They must guard his duties and the duties of the whole community before the tent of meeting as they work on the tabernacle.
They must guard all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and do the work of the tabernacle for the Israelites.
Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They are given to him completely from among the Israelites.
Appoint Aaron and his sons, and they must take care of their priesthood. Anyone else who comes near must be put to death."
"See, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of all the firstborn Israelites. The Levites will be Mine.
For every firstborn is Mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in Egypt, I set apart for Myself every firstborn in Israel, both people and animals. They are Mine. I am the LORD."
The LORD said to Moses in the Sinai wilderness,
"Count the sons of Levi by their family groups and clans. Count every male who is one month old or more."
So Moses counted them as the LORD had commanded.
Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Gershon's sons, by their clans, were Libni and Shimei.
Kohath's sons, by their clans, were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Merari's sons, by their clans, were Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans by family group.
The Gershonite clans were Libni and Shimei.
All the males one month old or more were counted, and there were 7,500.
The Gershonite clans camped on the west side of the tabernacle.
Their leader was Eliasaph son of Lael.
The Gershonites were in charge of the tabernacle, the tent, its covering, the curtain at the entrance to the tent of meeting,
the curtains of the courtyard, the curtain at the courtyard entrance around the tabernacle and altar, and their ropes. They did all the work connected with these items.
The Kohathite clans were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
All the males one month old or more were counted, and there were 8,600. They were responsible for the duties of the sanctuary.
The Kohathite clans camped on the south side of the tabernacle.
Their leader was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
They were in charge of the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the sacred articles used with them, the curtain, and all the work connected with them.
Eleazar son of Aaron the priest was chief over the Levite leaders and had oversight of those responsible for the sanctuary duties.
The Merarite clans were Mahli and Mushi.
All the males one month old or more were counted, and there were 6,200.
Their leader was Zuriel son of Abihail, and they camped on the north side of the tabernacle.
They were assigned the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, pillars, bases, and all its equipment.
They also cared for the pillars of the courtyard all around, with their bases, tent pegs, and ropes.
Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons camped east of the tabernacle, in front of the tent of meeting. They guarded the sanctuary for the Israelites. Anyone else who came near was to be put to death.
The total number of Levites that Moses and Aaron counted by their clans, counting every male one month old or more, was 22,000.
"Count every firstborn male among the Israelites who is one month old or more, and record their names.
You are to take the Levites for Me in place of all the firstborn Israelites, and the Levites' livestock in place of all the firstborn livestock of the Israelites."
So Moses counted all the firstborn Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him.
The total number of firstborn males one month old or more, listed by name, was 22,273.
"Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn Israelites, and the Levites' livestock in place of their livestock. The Levites will be Mine; I am the LORD.
For the 273 firstborn Israelites who are more than the Levites,
you are to collect five shekels for each one, using the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs.
Give that money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the extra firstborn."
So Moses collected the redemption money from those who were more than the number redeemed by the Levites.
From the firstborn of the Israelites he collected 1,365 shekels, using the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Take a census of the Kohathite clans among the Levites. Count them by their families and their fathers' houses.
Count the men from thirty to fifty years old, everyone who can serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
"This is the work of the Kohathites at the Tent of Meeting: caring for the Most Holy Place.
When the camp moves, Aaron and his sons must go in and take down the curtain veil. They must cover the ark of the Testimony with it.
They must put a covering of fine leather over it, spread a solid blue cloth over that, and put its poles in place.
"They must spread a blue cloth over the table of the Presence. On it they must put the plates, dishes, bowls, and pitchers for the drink offering, along with the regular bread.
They must spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover them with fine leather, and put the poles in place.
They must take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand that gives light, along with its lamps, wick trimmers, trays, and all the oil containers used to care for it.
Then they must put it and all its tools inside a covering of fine leather and place it on the carrying frame.
"They must spread a blue cloth over the gold altar and cover it with fine leather. They must put its poles in place.
They must take all the tools used for serving in the holy place, put them in a blue cloth, cover them with fine leather, and place them on the carrying frame.
They must remove the ashes from the bronze altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

They must put on it all the tools used there: the firepans, meat forks, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. These are all the altar's tools. They must spread a covering of fine leather over it and put its poles in place.

"When Aaron and his sons finish covering the holy things and all their tools as the camp moves out, the Kohathites may come and carry them. But they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. This is how the Kohathites are to carry the things for the Tent of Meeting.

Eleazar son of Aaron the priest is to oversee the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil. He is in charge of the whole tabernacle and everything in it, including the holy things and their tools."
Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Do not let the Kohathite clans be cut off from the Levites.
So they may live and not die when they come near the Most Holy Place, do this for them: Aaron and his sons must go in and give each man his task and his load.
But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment, or they will die."
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Take a census of the Gershonites too, by their families and their fathers' houses.
Count the men from thirty to fifty years old, everyone who can serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
"This is the work of the Gershonite clans in carrying and moving things:
They are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering, the covering of fine leather over it, and the curtain at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

They are also to carry the curtains of the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard around the tabernacle and altar, their ropes, and all the equipment for their work. They will carry everything that needs to be done.
"All the work of the Gershonites, including all their carrying duties and other work, is to be done as Aaron and his sons direct. You are to assign them all their responsibilities.
This is the work of the Gershonite clans at the Tent of Meeting. Their duties are under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
"You are to count the Merarites by their clans and families.
Count the men from thirty to fifty years old, everyone who can serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
This is their duty for all their work at the Tent of Meeting: to carry the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, and bases.
They are also to carry the posts of the surrounding courtyard, their bases, tent pegs, ropes, and all their equipment and tools. You are to assign by name the items they are to carry.
This is the work of the Merarite clans in all their work at the Tent of Meeting. It is under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest."
So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the community counted the Kohathites by their clans and families.
They counted the men from thirty to fifty years old who could serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
The number counted by their clans was 2,750.
These were the counted men of the Kohathite clans, everyone who could serve at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
Then the Gershonites were counted by their clans and families.
They counted the men from thirty to fifty years old who could serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
The number counted by their clans was 2,630.
These were the counted men of the Gershonites, everyone who could serve at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them as the LORD had commanded.
Then the Merarites were counted by their clans and families.
They counted the men from thirty to fifty years old who could serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
The number counted by their clans was 3,200.
These were the counted men of the Merarite clans, everyone who could serve at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted all the Levites by their clans and families.
They counted the men from thirty to fifty years old who could do the work of serving and carrying loads in the Tent of Meeting.
At the LORD's command, Moses counted them. Each man was counted for his work and his load, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Command the Israelites to send out of the camp every person with a skin disease, everyone with a bodily discharge, and everyone who is unclean because of a dead body.
Send out both men and women. Send them outside the camp so they will not make their camp unclean, where I live among them."
The Israelites did this. They sent them outside the camp, just as the LORD had told Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Speak to the Israelites: When a man or woman sins against the LORD by doing something people often do wrong, that person is guilty.
They must confess the sin they committed. They must pay back in full for the wrong they did, and add one-fifth more. They must give it to the person they wronged.
If the person has no close relative to receive the payment, the payment for the wrong goes to the LORD for the priest. This is in addition to the ram used to make atonement for them.
Every holy gift the Israelites bring to the priest belongs to him.
Each person's holy things belong to that person, but whatever anyone gives to the priest belongs to the priest."
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Speak to the Israelites: If a man's wife is unfaithful to him,
and another man sleeps with her secretly, so her husband does not know, and she becomes unclean, but there is no witness against her and she was not caught,
and a jealous spirit comes over him, and he is jealous of his wife, whether she has been unclean or not,

then the man must bring his wife to the priest. He must bring an offering for her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He must not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering that brings her wrong to mind.
The priest must bring her near and set her before the LORD.
The priest must take holy water in a clay jar. He must take some dust from the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.

The priest must set the woman before the LORD and let her hair hang loose. He must put the grain offering of remembrance, which is the grain offering of jealousy, into her hands. The priest must hold the bitter water that brings a curse.

Then the priest must make her take an oath. He must say to the woman, 'If no man has slept with you, and if you have not been unfaithful to your husband, then you will be free from this bitter water that brings a curse.
But if you have been unfaithful to your husband, and you have made yourself unclean, and a man other than your husband has slept with you,
then may the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people. May the LORD make your thigh waste away and your belly swell.
May this cursed water go into your body and make your belly swell and your thigh waste away.' Then the woman must say, 'Amen, Amen.'
Then the priest must write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
He must make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and the water that brings a curse will enter her and become bitter.
The priest must take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman's hand and wave it before the LORD. Then he must bring it to the altar.
The priest must take a handful of the grain offering as a reminder and burn it on the altar. After that, he must make the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, if she has made herself unclean and been unfaithful to her husband, the cursed water will enter her and become bitter. Her belly will swell, and her thigh will waste away. The woman will become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not made herself unclean and is clean, she will be free and will have children.
This is the law for jealousy when a wife, while married to her husband, goes astray and makes herself unclean,
or when a jealous spirit comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife. Then he must set the woman before the LORD, and the priest must do to her all this law.
The man will be free from guilt, but the woman will carry her guilt."
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If a man or a woman makes a special vow, a Nazirite vow, to dedicate himself to the LORD,
he must not drink wine or other fermented drink. He must not drink vinegar made from wine or other fermented drink. He must not drink grape juice, and he must not eat fresh grapes or dried grapes.
As long as he is a Nazirite, he must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, from the seeds to the skins.
During all the days of his Nazirite vow, no razor may touch his head. He must be holy until the time is finished that he has dedicated himself to the LORD. He must let the hair on his head grow long.
During all the days he dedicates himself to the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.
He must not make himself unclean for his father, mother, brother, or sister when they die, because his dedication to God is on his head.
During all the days of his Nazirite vow, he is holy to the LORD.
"If someone dies suddenly near him and makes his head unclean, he must shave his head on the day he becomes clean—on the seventh day.
On the eighth day he must bring two doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

The priest must offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. He must make atonement for him because he sinned by being near the dead body. He must make his head holy again that same day.
He must dedicate himself to the LORD again. He must bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The earlier days do not count, because his Nazirite vow was defiled.
"This is the law for the Nazirite: When the days of his dedication are complete, he must be brought to the entrance to the tent of meeting.

He must present his offering to the LORD: one year-old male lamb without defect for a burnt offering, one year-old female lamb without defect for a sin offering, and one ram without defect for a peace offering.
He must also bring a basket of bread made without yeast—cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, and wafers coated with oil—plus their grain offering and drink offerings.
The priest must bring these before the LORD and sacrifice the sin offering and the burnt offering.
He must sacrifice the ram as a peace offering to the LORD, along with the basket of bread made without yeast. The priest must also offer the grain offering and the drink offering.
The Nazirite must shave off his dedicated hair at the entrance to the tent of meeting. He must take the hair from his head and put it on the fire under the peace offering.

The priest must take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one cake of bread made without yeast from the basket, and one wafer made without yeast. He must put them in the hands of the Nazirite after the Nazirite has shaved off his hair.

The priest must wave them before the LORD as a wave offering. They are holy and belong to the priest, along with the breast that was waved and the thigh that was lifted up. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the law for the Nazirite who makes a vow. He must bring to the LORD whatever he vowed for his dedication, in addition to what he can afford. He must do exactly what he vowed, following the law for his Nazirite vow.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Tell Aaron and his sons, 'This is how you must bless the Israelites. Say to them:'"
"The LORD bless you and keep you.
The LORD make His face shine on you and be gracious to you.
The LORD turn His face toward you and give you peace."
"So they will put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them."
On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and set it apart as holy. He did the same for all its furnishings, the altar, and all the altar’s tools.
The leaders of Israel brought offerings. They were the heads of the family groups and the leaders of the tribes who had helped count the people.
They brought their gifts to the LORD: six covered wagons and twelve oxen. There was one wagon for every two leaders and one ox for each leader. They presented them in front of the tabernacle.
“Take these gifts from them. They are to be used for the work of the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites. Give each man what fits his work.”
So Moses took the wagons and oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon for their work.
He gave four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari for their work. Ithamar son of Aaron the priest was in charge of them.
He gave none to the sons of Kohath, because they carried the holy things on their shoulders.
The leaders also brought gifts for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed. They presented them in front of the altar.
The LORD said to Moses, “Each leader is to bring his offering on his own day for the dedication of the altar.”
On the first day, Nahshon son of Amminadab, leader of Judah, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day, Nethanel son of Zuar, leader of Issachar, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day, Eliab son of Helon, leader of Zebulun, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day, Elizur son of Shedeur, leader of Reuben, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, leader of Simeon, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day, Eliasaph son of Deuel, leader of Gad, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.
On the seventh day, Elishama son of Ammihud, leader of Ephraim, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, leader of Manasseh, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
On the ninth day, Abidan son of Gideoni, leader of Benjamin, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.
On the tenth day, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, leader of Dan, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day, Pagiel son of Ocran, leader of Asher, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ocran.
On the twelfth day, Ahira son of Enan, leader of Naphtali, brought his offering.
He brought one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He brought one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense.
For the burnt offering he brought one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old.
He brought one male goat for a sin offering.
For the peace offering he brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
This was the dedication offering of the altar from the leaders of Israel when it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold dishes.
Each silver plate weighed 130 shekels, and each silver bowl weighed 70 shekels. All the silver vessels weighed 2,400 shekels by the sanctuary shekel.
The twelve gold dishes, full of incense, weighed 10 shekels each by the sanctuary shekel. All the gold of the dishes weighed 120 shekels.
All the animals for the burnt offering were twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male lambs a year old, along with their grain offering. There were also twelve male goats for a sin offering.
All the animals for the peace offering were twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication of the altar after it was anointed.
When Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with Him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat between the two cherubim on the ark of the Testimony. And He spoke to him.
"Speak to Aaron and tell him, 'When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps should shine in front of the lampstand.'"
Aaron did so. He set up the lamps in front of the lampstand, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The lampstand was hammered from gold. From its base to its flowers, it was hammered work. Aaron made it following the pattern the LORD had shown Moses.
"Take the Levites from among the people of Israel and cleanse them.
This is how you should make them clean: sprinkle the water of cleansing on them, have them shave their whole body, wash their clothes, and then they will be clean.
Then they should take a young bull from the herd, along with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil. You should also take a second young bull from the herd as a sin offering.
Bring the Levites before the tent of meeting and gather the whole community of Israel.
Bring the Levites before the LORD, and have the people of Israel lay their hands on them.
Aaron will wave the Levites as a wave offering before the LORD for the people of Israel, so they can serve the LORD.
The Levites will lay their hands on the heads of the bulls. You should offer one bull as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD to make atonement for the Levites.
Set the Levites before Aaron and his sons, and wave them as a wave offering to the LORD. "
Thus you shall separate the Levites from among the people of Israel, and the Levites shall be Mine.
After that the Levites shall go in to serve at the tent of meeting, when you have cleansed them and waved them as a wave offering.
For they are completely given to Me from among the people of Israel. In place of all the firstborn of the people of Israel, who open the womb, I have taken them for Myself.
For all the firstborn among the people of Israel are Mine, both people and animals. On the day I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set them apart for Myself.
I have taken the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the people of Israel.

I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the people of Israel, to serve the people of Israel at the tent of meeting and to make atonement for them, so that no plague may come on the people of Israel when they come near the sanctuary."
So Moses, Aaron, and all the community of Israel did for the Levites everything the LORD had commanded Moses about them.
The Levites purified themselves from sin and washed their clothes. Aaron waved them as a wave offering before the LORD, and he made atonement for them to cleanse them.
After that, the Levites began their service in the tent of meeting before Aaron and his sons, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
"This is the rule for the Levites: from twenty-five years old and up, they shall come to serve in the tent of meeting.
From the age of fifty, they shall retire from regular service and serve no more.
They may help their fellow Levites by keeping guard in the tent of meeting, but they shall do no regular service. Thus you shall deal with the Levites in their duties."
In the first month of the second year after the Israelites left Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai. He said,
“Command the Israelites to celebrate the Passover at its appointed time.
You must observe it at its appointed time, at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month. Follow all its rules and decisions.”
So Moses told the Israelites to celebrate the Passover,
and they did so in the Wilderness of Sinai at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
But some men were unclean because they had touched a dead body, so they could not celebrate the Passover that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that same day
and said to him, “We are unclean because of a dead body. Why should we be kept from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?”
Moses answered them, “Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands concerning you.”

Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites: ‘When any one of you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a journey, he may still celebrate the Passover to the LORD.
Such people are to observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month. They are to eat the lamb with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They must not leave any of it until morning or break any of its bones. They must observe the Passover according to all its rules.

But the man who is clean and is not on a journey, yet does not celebrate the Passover, must be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD’s offering at its appointed time. That man will be responsible for his sin.
If a foreigner living among you wants to celebrate the Passover to the LORD, he must follow the Passover rules and laws.
You must have the same rule for the foreigner and the native-born.’”
On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the Tent of the Testimony. From evening until morning, the cloud above the tabernacle looked like fire.
That is how it continued: The cloud covered it by day, and at night it looked like fire.
Whenever the cloud rose from above the Tent, the Israelites would set out. Wherever the cloud settled, the Israelites would camp.
At the LORD’s command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD’s command they camped. As long as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle, they stayed camped.
Even when the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites obeyed the LORD’s command and did not set out.
Sometimes the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for only a few days. They camped at the LORD’s command and set out at the LORD’s command.
Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening until morning. When it lifted in the morning, they set out. Whether by day or by night, when the cloud was taken up, they set out.
Whether the cloud stayed for two days, a month, or longer, the Israelites camped and did not set out as long as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle. But when it was lifted, they set out.
They camped at the LORD’s command and set out at the LORD’s command. They carried out the LORD’s command through Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Make two silver trumpets for yourself. Hammer them from one piece of silver. They will be for you to call the community together and to signal the camps to move.
When both trumpets sound, the whole community must gather at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
If only one trumpet sounds, the leaders, the heads of Israel's clans, must gather before you.
When you blow a loud blast, the camps on the east side must set out.
When you blow a second loud blast, the camps on the south side must set out. They must blow the blast as the signal for their journey.
To gather the assembly, blow the trumpets, but do not sound the alarm.
Aaron's sons, the priests, must blow the trumpets. This is a lasting rule for you and your descendants.
When you go to war in your land against an enemy who attacks you, sound the alarm on the trumpets. Then the LORD your God will remember you, and He will save you from your enemies.

On your joyful days, your appointed festivals, and the first days of your months, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. They will be a reminder for you before your God. I am the LORD your God."
On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle of the covenant.
Then the Israelites set out from the Desert of Sinai and traveled from place to place. The cloud came to rest in the Desert of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the LORD's command through Moses.
The divisions of the camp of Judah went first, under their standard. Nahshon son of Amminadab was in command.
Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of Issachar.
Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of Zebulun.
The tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and Merarites set out, carrying it.
The divisions of the camp of Reuben set out next, under their standard. Elizur son of Shedeur was in command.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of Simeon.
Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of Gad.
The Kohathites set out next, carrying the holy things. The tabernacle was to be set up before they arrived.
The divisions of the camp of Ephraim set out next, under their standard. Elishama son of Ammihud was in command.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of Manasseh.
Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of Benjamin.
Finally, the divisions of the camp of Dan set out last, under their standard. They were the rear guard for all the camps. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was in command.
Pagiel son of Okran was over the division of the tribe of Asher.
Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of Naphtali.
This was the order in which the Israelites set out, division by division.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We are setting out for the place the LORD promised to give us. Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things for Israel."
But Hobab said, "No, I will not go. I will return to my own country and my own people."
Moses said, "Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be our guide.
If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us."
So they set out from the mountain of the LORD and traveled for three days. The ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them for those three days to find a resting place for them.
The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses said, "Rise up, the LORD! May Your enemies be scattered, and may those who hate You flee before You."
When it came to rest, he said, "Return, the LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel."

Soon the people began to complain bitterly, and it sounded bad to the LORD. When the LORD heard them, His anger was aroused. Then fire from the LORD burned among them and consumed some of the outskirts of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
So that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
The mixed crowd among them had a strong craving, and the Israelites also wept again and said, "Who will give us meat to eat?"
"We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for free, and the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
But now we have no appetite; there is nothing to look at but this manna!"
The manna looked like coriander seed, and it appeared like bdellium.
The people went around and gathered it. They ground it on hand mills or crushed it in mortars, then boiled it in pots and made it into cakes. It tasted like cakes baked with olive oil.
When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna came down with it.
Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families, each at the entrance to his tent. The LORD was very angry, and Moses was also displeased.
So Moses said to the LORD, "Why have You brought trouble on Your servant? Why have I not found favor in Your sight, that You have laid the burden of all these people on me?
Did I conceive all these people? Did I give them birth, that You should tell me, 'Carry them in your arms like a nurse carries a baby,' to the land You swore to their fathers?
Where can I get meat to give to all these people? For they keep crying to me, 'Give us meat to eat!'
I can't carry all these people by myself; the burden is too heavy for me.
If this is how You are going to treat me, please go ahead and kill me—if I have found favor in Your sight—and don't let me see my own ruin."
The LORD said to Moses, "Bring Me seventy men from the elders of Israel, men you know to be elders and officers of the people. Have them stand with you at the Tent of Meeting.

I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them. They will help you carry the burden of the people, so that you will not have to carry it alone."

"Tell the people: 'Set yourselves apart for tomorrow, and you will eat meat. You cried out in the hearing of the LORD, saying, "Who will give us meat to eat? It was better for us in Egypt." So the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat it.
You will eat it not for one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days,
but for a whole month—until you are sick of it—because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have cried before Him, saying, "Why did we ever leave Egypt?"'"
Moses said, "Here I am among six hundred thousand men on foot, yet You say, 'I will give them meat, and they will eat for a whole month.'
Would flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, and would it be enough? Or would all the fish in the sea be gathered for them, and would it be enough?"
The LORD answered Moses, "Is the LORD not powerful enough? Now you will see whether My word will come true for you or not."
So Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent.

Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him; He took some of the Spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did not do so again.

Two men, however, had remained in the camp. One was named Eldad and the other Medad, and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those listed, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!"
Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' assistant since youth, spoke up and said, "Moses, my lord, stop them!"
But Moses said to him, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets and that the LORD would put His Spirit on all of them!"
Then Moses and the elders of Israel returned to the camp.
Now a wind went out from the LORD and drove quail in from the sea. It scattered them over the camp, about three feet deep for a day's walk in every direction around the camp.
All that day and night and all the next day the people stayed up and gathered the quail. No one gathered less than ten homers. They spread them out all around the camp.
But while the meat was still between their teeth, before they had even chewed it, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck them with a very severe plague.
So that place was called Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.
From Kibroth Hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they stayed.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had married a Cushite woman.
They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Hasn't He also spoken through us?" And the LORD heard this.
Now Moses was a very humble man, more humble than anyone else on earth.
At once the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, "All three of you come out to the tent of meeting." So the three of them went out.
Then the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud. He stood at the entrance to the tent and called Aaron and Miriam. The two of them came forward.
He said, "Listen to My words: When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, reveal Myself to them in visions. I speak to them in dreams.
But this is not true of My servant Moses. He is faithful in all My house.
I speak with him face to face—clearly, not in riddles. He sees the form of the LORD. Why weren't you afraid to speak against My servant Moses?"
The LORD's anger burned against them, and He left.
When the cloud lifted from above the tent, Miriam had leprosy, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw that she had leprosy.
Then Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not hold this sin against us. We acted foolishly, and we have sinned.
Please don't let her be like a dead baby whose body is half eaten away when it comes from its mother's womb."
So Moses cried out to the LORD, "Please, God, heal her!"
The LORD said to Moses, "If her father had spit in her face, wouldn't she be disgraced for seven days? Let her be shut out of the camp for seven days. After that, she can be brought back."
So Miriam was shut out of the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until she was brought back.
After that, the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the Wilderness of Paran.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
“Send out men for yourself to explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each tribe, send one man, and each man must be a leader among them.”
So, at the the LORD’s command, Moses sent them from the Wilderness of Paran. All the men were leaders of the Israelites.
These were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Manasseh, a tribe of Joseph, Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
and from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These are the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the new name Joshua.
When Moses sent them to explore Canaan, he said, “Go up through the Negev and into the hill country.
See what the land is like and whether its people are strong or weak, few or many.
Is the land where they live good or bad? Are their cities like open camps or strong forts?
Is the soil rich or poor? Are there trees there or not? Be brave, and bring back some of the fruit of the land.” It was the season for the first ripe grapes.
So they went up and explored the land from the Wilderness of Zin to Rehob, near Lebo Hamath.
They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived there. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
They came to the Valley of Eshcol and cut off a branch with one cluster of grapes. Two of them carried it on a pole between them. They also brought some pomegranates and figs.
That place was called the Valley of Eshcol because of the cluster the Israelites cut there.
After forty days, they returned from exploring the land.

They went back to Moses and Aaron and the whole community of Israel in the Wilderness of Paran at Kadesh. They gave a report to them and to the whole community, and they showed them the fruit of the land.
They told Moses, “We went to the land you sent us to. It is a rich and fertile land, and here is some of its fruit.
But the people who live there are powerful, and their cities are large and strongly built. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.
The Amalekites live in the Negev. The Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country. The Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.”
Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We should go up now and take the land, because we can certainly conquer it!”
But the men who had gone with him said, “We cannot go up against those people, because they are stronger than we are!”
So they gave the Israelites a bad report about the land they had explored. They said, “The land we traveled through destroys the people who live there, and all the people we saw were very tall.
We even saw the Nephilim there. They are the descendants of Anak who come from the Nephilim. We felt like tiny grasshoppers compared with them, and that is how we must have looked to them.”
Then the whole community raised their voices and cried out, and the people wept that night.
All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole community said to them, "If only we had died in Egypt! Or if only we had died in this wilderness!
Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and children will become loot. Wouldn't it be better for us to go back to Egypt?"
So they said to one another, "Let's appoint a leader and return to Egypt."
Then Moses and Aaron fell face down before the whole community of Israel.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among the men who scouted the land, tore their clothes
and said to the whole community of Israel, "The land we passed through and explored is very, very good.
If the LORD is pleased with us, He will bring us into this land, a land flowing with milk and honey, and He will give it to us.
Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land. They will be easy for us to defeat. Their protection is gone, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them!"
But the whole community threatened to stone them. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.
The LORD said to Moses, "How long will this people treat Me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in Me, even after all the signs I have done among them?
I will strike them with a plague and destroy them. Then I will make you into a nation greater and stronger than they are."
But Moses said to the LORD, "Then the Egyptians will hear about it. By Your strength You brought this people out from among them.

The people of this land will hear that You, the LORD, are among Your people. They know You, the LORD, are seen face to face, and that Your cloud stands over them. You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
If You kill all these people at once, the nations that have heard of Your fame will say,
'The LORD could not bring these people into the land He swore to give them, so He killed them in the wilderness.' "
So now, may the power of my Lord be great, just as You have said.

'The LORD is slow to get angry and full of faithful love. He forgives sin and rebellion. Yet He does not let the guilty go free. He punishes the children for the sins of their parents to the third and fourth generation.'
Please pardon the sin of this people, because Your faithful love is so great. You have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt."
Then the LORD said, "I have pardoned them, as you asked.
Yet as surely as I live, and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the LORD's glory,
not one of the men who have seen My glory and the signs I did in Egypt and in the wilderness—yet tested Me and disobeyed Me ten times—
not one of them will ever see the land I swore to give their ancestors. None of those who treated Me with contempt will see it.
But My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly. I will bring him into the land he entered, and his descendants will receive it.
Now the Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valleys. Turn back tomorrow and go into the wilderness toward the Red Sea."
Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"How long will this wicked community grumble against Me? I have heard the complaints the Israelites are making against Me.
So tell them: 'As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly as you have spoken in My hearing.
Your bodies will fall in this wilderness—all of you who were counted, everyone twenty years old or older who grumbled against Me.
Not one of you will enter the land I swore to bring you into, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
But I will bring your little ones, the ones you said would become loot, into the land you rejected. They will know the land you despised.
As for you, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.
Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years. They will suffer for your unfaithfulness until your bodies lie scattered in the wilderness.
For forty days you explored the land, and for forty years you will carry your guilt—one year for each day. Then you will know how I feel about you.
I, the LORD, have spoken. I will surely do this to the whole community that has joined together against Me. They will die in this wilderness.'"
The men Moses sent to scout the land returned and made the whole community grumble against him by giving a bad report about the land.
The men who spread the bad report about the land died of a plague before the LORD.
Of all the men who went to scout the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh survived.
When Moses told all the Israelites these words, the people mourned deeply.
Early the next morning they set out for the top of the hill country, saying, "Look, we have sinned! Now we are ready to go up to the place the LORD promised."
But Moses said, "Why are you now disobeying the LORD's command? This will not succeed.
Do not go up, or your enemies will strike you down, because the LORD is not with you.
The Amalekites and Canaanites are there ahead of you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you turned away from the LORD, He will not be with you."
But they boldly went up to the top of the hill country, even though the ark of the LORD's covenant and Moses did not leave the camp.
Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, attacked them, and chased them all the way to Hormah.
"Speak to the Israelites and say: When you enter the land I am giving you to settle in,

and you present a food offering to the LORD from your herds or flocks—to make an offering that pleases the LORD as a burnt offering or sacrifice, to keep a special promise or as a free gift, or at your appointed festivals—
