the one who brings the offering must also bring a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
With a burnt offering or sacrifice for each lamb, also bring a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering.
For a ram, bring a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil,
and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering. It is an offering that pleases the LORD.
When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice, to keep a special promise or as a peace offering to the LORD,
bring with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,
and half a hin of wine as a drink offering. It is an offering that pleases the LORD.
Do this for each bull, ram, lamb, or goat.
However many you offer, do this for each one.
Every native-born Israelite must do this when presenting a food offering, an offering that pleases the LORD.
For all your generations, if a foreigner living among you wants to present a food offering, an offering that pleases the LORD, he must do it the same way you do.
The whole community has one rule for you and for the foreigner living among you. It is a lasting rule for your generations. The foreigner is the same as you before the LORD.
There is one law and one rule for you and for the foreigner living among you."
"Speak to the Israelites and say: When you enter the land I am bringing you into,
and you eat food from that land, set aside a portion for the LORD.
Present a cake from the first of your dough as an offering. Offer it like the grain from your threshing floor.
For all your generations, give the LORD an offering from the first of your dough.
"If you fail to obey all these commands the LORD gave you through Moses—
all the LORD commanded you through Moses from the day He gave them and for your generations to come—

and if the whole community sins by mistake, and they do not realize it, the whole community must bring one young bull as a burnt offering, an offering that pleases the LORD, with its grain and drink offerings as required, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest will make atonement for the whole Israelite community. They will be forgiven, because it was a mistake, and they brought their offering to the LORD—a burnt offering—and their sin offering before the LORD for their mistake.
The whole community of Israelites and the foreigner living among them will be forgiven, because all the people sinned by mistake.
If one person sins by mistake, he must bring a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest will make atonement before the LORD for the person who sinned by mistake. When atonement is made for him, he will be forgiven.
One law applies to the native-born Israelite and to the foreigner living among you for sins done by mistake.
But anyone who sins on purpose, whether native-born or foreigner, speaks against the LORD. That person must be removed from his people.
Because he has rejected the LORD's word and broken His command, his guilt remains."
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community.
They kept him in custody because it was not clear what should be done with him.
The LORD said to Moses, "The man must be put to death. The whole community must stone him outside the camp."
So the community brought him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
"Speak to the Israelites and say: For all your generations, make tassels on the corners of your garments and put a blue cord on each tassel.
The tassels will remind you of all the LORD's commands, so you will obey them and not follow your own desires and eyes, which lead you away from God.
Then you will remember and obey all My commands and be holy to your God.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God."
Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, along with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took some men.
They stood against Moses with 250 Israelite men, leaders of the community, chosen men from the assembly, well-known men.

They gathered against Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You have gone too far! The whole community is holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them. Why do you put yourselves above the LORD's people?"
When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.

Then he said to Korah and all his followers, "Tomorrow morning the LORD will show who belongs to Him and who is holy, and He will bring that person near to Himself. The one He chooses, He will bring near to Himself.
Do this: Take censers for yourselves, Korah and all your followers,
and tomorrow put fire and incense in them before the LORD. Then the man the LORD chooses will be the holy one. You Levites have gone too far!"
Moses also said to Korah, "Now listen, you Levites!

Isn't it enough for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the community of Israel and brought you near to Himself to do the work at the LORD's tabernacle and to stand before the community to serve them?
He has brought you and all your fellow Levites near to Himself, but now you are seeking the priesthood as well!
Therefore, it is you and all your followers who have joined together against the LORD! As for Aaron, who is he that you grumble against him?"
Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, "We will not come!
Isn't it enough that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? Must you also make yourself ruler over us?
Besides, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us fields and vineyards to own. Do you think you can fool us? No, we will not come!"
Then Moses was very angry and said to the LORD, "Do not accept their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them, and I have not wronged any of them."
Moses said to Korah, "You and your whole community must appear before the LORD tomorrow—you, they, and Aaron.
Each man must take his censer, put incense in it, and bring it before the LORD—250 censers. You and Aaron must bring yours too."
So each man took his censer, put fire and incense in it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
When Korah had gathered the whole community against them at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole community.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Separate yourselves from this community so I can destroy them in a moment."
But Moses and Aaron fell facedown and said, "O God, God of the spirits of all people, if one man sins, will You pour out Your wrath on the whole community?"
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the community to move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram."
So Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
He warned the community, "Move away now from the tents of these wicked men. Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you may be swept away because of all their sins."
So they moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrances to their tents with their wives, sons, and little children.
Then Moses said, "By this you will know that the LORD sent me to do all these things, that I did not plan them myself.
If these men die a normal death like everyone else, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD does something new, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them, and they go down alive into the grave, then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt."
As soon as Moses finished speaking all these words, the ground under them split open.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, all Korah's men, and all their goods.
They went down alive into the grave, and the earth closed over them. They disappeared from the community.
At their cries, all the Israelites around them ran away, saying, "The earth may swallow us too!"
Then fire came out from the LORD and burned up the 250 men who were offering incense.
"Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to take the censers out of the fire and scatter the coals far away, because they are holy.

The censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives must be hammered into sheets to cover the altar, because they were offered before the LORD and are holy. In this way they will be a sign to the Israelites."
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers used by those who had been burned and had them hammered into a covering for the altar,

as a reminder to the Israelites that no one who is not a descendant of Aaron may come near to burn incense before the LORD, or he will be like Korah and his followers, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
The next day the whole community of Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron. They said, "You have killed the LORD's people!"
But when the community gathered against Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, they saw the cloud cover it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting.
"Get away from this community so I can destroy them in a moment." Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown.

Then Moses said to Aaron, "Take your censer, put fire from the altar in it, along with incense, and hurry to the community to make atonement for them. Wrath has come from the LORD; the plague has started."
So Aaron took the censer, just as Moses had said, and ran into the middle of the assembly. When he saw the plague had begun among the people, he put the incense on it and made atonement for them.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague stopped.
But 14,700 people died in the plague, besides those who died because of Korah.
Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and the plague stopped.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelites and get twelve staffs from them, one from the leader of each ancestral house. Write each man's name on his staff.
Write Aaron's name on the staff of Levi, because there is one staff for the head of each ancestral house.
Place them in the Tent of Meeting before the Testimony, where I meet with you.
The staff of the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid Myself of the Israelites' constant grumbling against you."
So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each of their leaders gave him a staff, one for each leader of their ancestral houses--twelve staffs in all. Aaron's staff was among them.
Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony.
The next day Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony and saw that Aaron's staff for the house of Levi had sprouted, budded, blossomed, and produced almonds.
Then Moses brought out all the staffs from the LORD's presence to all the Israelites. They looked at them, and each man took his own staff.
The LORD said to Moses, "Put Aaron's staff back in front of the Testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebellious, so that their grumbling against Me may stop and they will not die."
Moses did as the LORD commanded him.
Then the Israelites said to Moses, "Look, we are dying! We are lost--all of us are lost!
Anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD will die. Are we all going to die?"
The LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons, along with your father’s family, must carry the guilt for the holy place. You and your sons must carry the guilt for your priesthood.
Bring your brothers from Levi’s tribe, your father’s tribe, near to you. They will join you and help you and your sons in front of the Tent of the Testimony.
They must take care of your needs and the needs of the whole tent. But they must not go near the holy objects or the altar. If they do, both they and you will die.
They will join you and care for the Tent of Meeting, doing all the work of the tent. But no outsider may come near you.
You must take care of the holy place and the altar, so that God’s anger will not fall on the Israelites again.
Look, I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the Israelites. I give them to you as a gift. They are given to the LORD to do the work of the Tent of Meeting.

But you and your sons must take care of your priesthood for everything about the altar and behind the curtain. You will serve there. I am giving you the priesthood as a gift. Anyone who is not a priest who comes near must be put to death.”

Then the LORD said to Aaron, “Look, I have put you in charge of the offerings I set apart for Myself. I give all the holy things of the Israelites to you and your sons. This is your share, a lasting right.

The most holy part of the offerings kept back from the fire will be yours. From all the offerings they bring to Me as most holy—whether grain offerings, sin offerings, or guilt offerings—that part is most holy to you and your sons.
You must eat it in a most holy place. Every male may eat it. It is holy to you.

This also is yours: the special offering from their gifts, along with all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I have given them to you, your sons, and your daughters as a lasting right. Anyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
I give you the best of the fresh oil, the new wine, and the grain that the people give to the LORD as their first crops.
The first crops from everything in their land that they bring to the LORD will be yours. Anyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
Everything in Israel that is set apart for the LORD will be yours.
The firstborn of every womb, whether human or animal, that is offered to the LORD belongs to you. But you must redeem the firstborn son and the firstborn of an unclean animal.
You are to redeem them at one month old, at the set price of five shekels of silver, using the holy shekel, which is twenty gerahs.

But you must not redeem the firstborn of an ox, a sheep, or a goat. They are holy. You must sprinkle their blood on the altar and burn their fat as an offering made by fire, a pleasing smell to the LORD.
Their meat will be yours, like the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh. It is yours.

All the special offerings of holy things that the Israelites bring to the LORD, I have given to you, your sons, and your daughters as a lasting right. It is a lasting promise before the LORD for you and your children after you.”
Then the LORD said to Aaron, “You will not receive land in their country, and you will not have a share among them. I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.
Look, I have given the Levites all the tithes in Israel as their inheritance, in return for the work they do, the work of the Tent of Meeting.
From now on, the Israelites must not come near the Tent of Meeting, or they will be guilty and die.
The Levites will do the work of the Tent of Meeting, and they will carry their own guilt. This is a lasting rule for all generations: They will not receive land among the Israelites.
For I have given the Levites as their inheritance the tithes that the Israelites bring to the LORD as a special offering. That is why I said they will not receive land among the Israelites.”
“Speak to the Levites and tell them: When you receive from the Israelites the tithe I have given you as your inheritance, you must give a tenth of that tithe as an offering to the LORD.
Your offering will count for you as if it were grain from the threshing floor or juice from the winepress.
In this way you also must give an offering to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites. From that offering, you must give the LORD’s share to Aaron the priest.
You must give the best part of everything you receive as the LORD’s offering, the best part of it.
Say to them: When you have given the best part, it will count for you as if it were produce from the threshing floor or winepress.
You and your households may eat the rest anywhere, because it is your pay for your work in the Tent of Meeting.
By giving the best part, you will not be guilty. You will not treat the holy offerings of the Israelites as unclean, and you will not die.”
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"This is the rule of the law that the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer that has no defect or blemish and has never been under a yoke.
Give it to Eleazar the priest. He will take it outside the camp and slaughter it in front of him.
Eleazar the priest must take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.
Then the heifer must be burned while he watches. Its hide, meat, blood, and dung must be burned.
"The priest must take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet wool and throw them into the fire where the heifer is burning.
Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may enter the camp, but he will be unclean until evening.
The person who burns the heifer must also wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. He too will be unclean until evening.

A clean person must gather the ashes of the heifer and put them in a clean place outside the camp. They must be kept for the Israelite community to use in the water of purification. It is for purification from sin.
The man who gathers the ashes of the heifer must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. This is a permanent rule for the Israelites and for the foreigner living among them.
"Anyone who touches a dead body will be unclean for seven days.
He must make himself clean with the water on the third day and on the seventh day. Then he will be clean. But if he does not make himself clean on the third and seventh days, he will not be clean.

Anyone who touches a dead body, the body of a person who has died, and does not make himself clean, defiles the the LORD's tabernacle. That person must be removed from Israel, because the water of purification was not sprinkled on him. He is unclean, and his uncleanness stays with him.
"This is the law when a man dies in a tent: Everyone who enters the tent and everyone already in the tent will be unclean for seven days.
Any open container that has no lid fastened on it is unclean.
Anyone in the open field who touches someone killed by a sword, or any dead person, or a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
"For the unclean person, take some ashes from the burnt sin offering and put them in a container with fresh water.

Then a clean person must take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent and on all the furnishings and people who were there. He must also sprinkle it on anyone who touched a bone, a dead body, or a grave.

The clean person must sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. After the unclean person has made himself clean on the seventh day, he must wash his clothes and bathe in water. That evening he will be clean.

But if a person who is unclean does not make himself clean, he must be removed from the community, because he has defiled the the LORD's sanctuary. The water of purification was not sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
"This is a permanent rule for them. The person who sprinkles the water of purification must wash his clothes, and anyone who touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.
Anything the unclean person touches will be unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening."
In the first month, the whole Israelite community came to the Desert of Zin and stayed at Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.
There was no water for the community, so they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people argued with Moses and said, "If only we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!
Why did you bring the LORD's people into this desert to die here along with our animals?
Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to bring us to this awful place? It is not a place for grain, figs, vines, or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink."
Moses and Aaron left the assembly and went to the entrance of the tent of meeting. They fell facedown, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.

"Take the staff and gather the community, you and your brother Aaron. Speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water. You will bring water out of the rock for them and give the community and their animals a drink."
So Moses took the staff from before the LORD, as He had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, "Listen now, you rebels! Must we bring water out of this rock for you?"
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water gushed out, and the community and their animals drank.
But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not trust Me enough to honor Me as holy before the Israelites, you will not lead this community into the land I gave them."
These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and He showed His holiness among them.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: "This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship we have faced.
Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived there many years. The Egyptians mistreated us and our ancestors.
We cried out to the LORD, and He heard our voice. He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your territory.

Please let us pass through your land. We will not go through fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from your wells. We will stay on the king's road and not turn aside to the right or left until we have passed through your territory."
But Edom answered, "You may not pass through my land, or I will come out against you with the sword."
The Israelites said to him, "We will go up by the main road. If we or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We only want to pass through on foot—nothing else."
Edom said, "You shall not pass through." Then Edom came out against them with a large and powerful army.
So Edom refused to let Israel pass through his territory, and Israel turned away from him.
The whole Israelite community set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, near the border of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Aaron will die and join his ancestors, because he will not enter the land I gave the Israelites. You both rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.
Remove Aaron's garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will die there."
Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole community.
Moses removed Aaron's garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died there on top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down the mountain.
When the whole community saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel mourned for Aaron thirty days.
When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the way of Atharim, he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
Israel made a vow to the LORD and said, "If You will indeed give this people into my hand, then I will completely destroy their cities."
The LORD listened to Israel's request and gave the Canaanites into their hands. They completely destroyed the Canaanites and their cities, and the place was called Hormah.
They left Mount Hor by the road to the Red Sea to go around the land of Edom, but the people grew impatient along the way.
The people spoke against God and against Moses, saying, "Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no food and no water, and we are sick of this awful food."
Then the LORD sent poisonous snakes among the people, and they bit the people, so many Israelites died.
The people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned, because we have spoken against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD, that He take away the snakes from us." So Moses prayed for the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Make a snake and put it on a pole. Then everyone who is bitten can look at it and live."
So Moses made a bronze snake and put it on a pole. If a snake bit someone, he looked at the bronze snake and lived.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They left Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the wilderness east of Moab.
From there they moved on and camped in the Zered Valley.
From there they moved on and camped beyond the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that extends from the border of the Amorites. The Arnon is the border between Moab and the Amorites.
That is why the Book of the Wars of the LORD says, "Waheb in Suphah, and the valleys of the Arnon,
and the slopes of the valleys that stretch toward the town of Ar and lean on the border of Moab."
From there they went on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people together, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song: "Spring up, O well! Sing to it!
The well that the princes dug, that the nobles of the people dug with their scepters and staffs." Then they went from the wilderness to Mattanah,
from Mattanah to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
and from Bamoth to the valley in the region of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which overlooks the wasteland.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

"Let us pass through your land. We will not turn off into field or vineyard, and we will not drink water from a well. We will travel along the King's Highway until we have passed through your territory."
But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. He gathered all his people and went out to meet Israel in the wilderness. He came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Israel struck him down with the sword and took over his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the border of the Ammonites, because the border of the Ammonites was strong.
Israel took all these cities and settled in all the Amorite cities, including Heshbon and its surrounding villages.
Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites. He had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land from him as far as the Arnon.
That is why those who speak in proverbs say, "Come to Heshbon and rebuild it; let the city of Sihon be restored.
For fire came out from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon. It burned up Ar of Moab and swallowed the heights of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You are ruined, O people of Chemosh! He gave his sons as refugees and his daughters into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites.
But we have conquered them; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon. We have wiped out the land as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba."
So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer, and they captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
Then they turned and went up by the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out with all his people to fight them at Edrei.

The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have given him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. You will do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
So they struck him down, along with his sons and all his people, until no one was left. Then they took over his land.
The Israelites traveled and camped in the plains of Moab near the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was terrified of the people because there were so many of them. Moab dreaded the Israelites.
Moab said to the elders of Midian, "This crowd will eat up everything around us, like an ox eats grass in a field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, by the Euphrates, in the land of his people. He said, "Look, a people has come out of Egypt. They cover the whole land and are living right across from me."

"Please come and curse this people for me, because they are too strong for me. Maybe I can defeat them and drive them out of the land. I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed."
So the elders of Moab and Midian went with money for fortune-telling in their hands. They came to Balaam and gave him Balak's message.
Balaam said to them, "Stay here tonight, and I will bring back to you whatever the LORD says to me." So Moab's leaders stayed with Balaam.
That night God came to Balaam and asked, "Who are these men with you?"
Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent them to me.
He said, 'Look, a people has come out of Egypt and covers the whole land. Come now and curse them for me. Maybe I can fight them and drive them out.'"
God said to Balaam, "Do not go with them. You must not curse the people, because they are blessed."
In the morning Balaam got up and said to Balak's messengers, "Go back to your land, because the LORD has refused to let me go with you."
Moab's leaders got up, went to Balak, and said, "Balaam refused to come with us."
Balak sent more officials, and they were more numerous and more important than the first ones.
They came to Balaam and said, "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: 'Please do not refuse to come to me.
I will honor you greatly, and I will do whatever you say. Please come and curse this people for me.'"
Balaam answered Balak's servants, "Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD my God and do anything small or great.
Now stay here tonight too, so I can find out what more the LORD will say to me."
That night God came to Balaam and said, "If the men have come to call you, get up and go with them. But do only what I tell you."
In the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with Moab's leaders.
But God became angry because Balaam was going. The Angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
The donkey saw the Angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in His hand. She turned off the road and went into a field. So Balaam beat the donkey to guide her back onto the road.
Then the Angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on each side.
The donkey saw the Angel of the LORD and pressed against the wall, crushing Balaam's foot against it. So he beat her again.
Then the Angel of the LORD went ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn right or left.
The donkey saw the Angel of the LORD and lay down under Balaam. Balaam became angry and beat the donkey with his staff.
Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?"
Balaam said to the donkey, "Because you have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now."
The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your donkey, the one you have ridden all your life? Have I ever done this to you before?" "No," he said.
Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the Angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in His hand. So Balaam bowed low and fell facedown.
The Angel of the LORD said to him, "Why have you beaten your donkey three times? Look, I came out to oppose you because your way is wrong before Me.
The donkey saw Me and turned away from Me three times. If she had not turned away, I would have killed you by now, but I would have spared her."
Balaam said to the Angel of the LORD, "I have sinned. I did not know you were standing in the road to meet me. Now, if it is wrong in your eyes, I will go back."
The Angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but speak only the word I give you." So Balaam went with Balak's officials.
When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at a Moabite city on the Arnon border, at the edge of his territory.
Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send for you again and again? Why didn't you come to me? Am I really not able to reward you?"
Balaam said to Balak, "Look, I have come to you now. But can I say anything on my own? I must speak only the word God puts in my mouth."
Then Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and sent some to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth-baal. From there Balaam could see the edge of the Israelite camp.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here."
Balak did what Balaam said. They offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your offering while I go off. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me. Whatever He shows me, I will tell you." So Balaam went to a bare hill.
God met him there, and Balaam said, "I have set up seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on each one."
The LORD put a message in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak and say this."
So Balaam returned and found Balak standing beside his offering, with all the Moabite leaders.
Then Balaam spoke his message: "Balak brought me from Aram. The king of Moab brought me from the eastern mountains. He said, 'Come, curse Jacob for me. Come, speak against Israel.'
How can I curse those God has not cursed? How can I speak against those the LORD has not spoken against?
From the rocky peaks I see them. From the hills I look down on them. I see a people who live alone. They do not count themselves among the nations.
Who can count Jacob's dust? Who can number even a fourth of Israel? Let me die like good people die. Let my end be like theirs!"
Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, but you have blessed them!"
Balaam answered, "Must I not speak what the LORD puts in my mouth?"
Then Balak said to him, "Come with me to another place. From there you will see them, but you will see only part of them, not all of them. Curse them for me from there."
So Balak took him to the field of Zophim on top of Pisgah. There Balaam built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each one.
Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your offering while I meet with Him over there."
The LORD met with Balaam and put a message in his mouth. He said, "Go back to Balak and say this."
So Balaam went back and found Balak standing beside his offering, with the Moabite leaders. Balak asked him, "What did the LORD say?"
Then Balaam spoke his message: "Get up, Balak, and listen. Hear me, son of Zippor.
God is not a man, so He does not lie. He is not a human being, so He does not change His mind. Does He say something and not do it? Does He promise something and not keep it?
I have been told to bless. He has blessed, and I cannot take it back.
He sees no wrong in Jacob and no trouble in Israel. The LORD their God is with them. The shout of the King is among them.
God brought them out of Egypt. They are as strong as a wild ox.
No magic can hurt Jacob. No spell can harm Israel. Now people will say about Jacob and Israel, 'Look what God has done!'
The people rise like a lioness. They rouse themselves like a lion. They will not lie down until they eat their prey and drink the blood of those they have killed."
Then Balak said to Balaam, "Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all!"
Balaam answered, "Did I not tell you I must do whatever the LORD says?"
Then Balak said to Balaam, "Come, let me take you to another place. Maybe God will be pleased to let you curse them for me from there."
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, looking out over the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here."
Balak did what Balaam said and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not look for omens as he had before. Instead, he turned toward the wilderness.
Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel camped by their tribes. The Spirit of God came on him.
He spoke his message and said, "The message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes are open,
the message of one who hears God's words, who sees a vision from the Almighty, falling down with eyes open:
"How good are your tents, Jacob! How good are your homes, Israel!
They spread out like valleys, like gardens beside a river, like aloes the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
Water will flow from his buckets, and his children will be many. His king will be greater than Agag, and his kingdom will be lifted up.
God brings him out of Egypt; he has strength like a wild ox. He will defeat enemy nations and crush their bones; he will pierce them with arrows.
He crouches and lies down like a lion, like a lioness. Who will wake him? Blessed is everyone who blesses you, and cursed is everyone who curses you."
Balak was very angry with Balaam. He clapped his hands and said to Balaam, "I called you to curse my enemies, but look, you have blessed them three times!
Now go back to your place! I said I would honor you greatly, but look, the LORD has kept you from honor."
Balaam said to Balak, "Did I not tell your messengers whom you sent to me,
'If Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the LORD's command. I cannot do good or bad by my own choice. I will say only what the LORD tells me to say.'
Now I am going back to my people. Come, and I will tell you what these people will do to your people in the days to come."
He spoke his message and said, "The message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes are open,
the message of one who hears God's words and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, falling down with eyes open:
"I see him, but not now. I look at him, but he is not near. A star will come from Jacob, and a scepter will rise from Israel. He will crush Moab and break down all the descendants of Sheth.
Edom will become a possession, and Seir, his enemies, will become a possession, while Israel grows strong.
A ruler will come from Jacob and destroy those left in the city.
He looked at Amalek and spoke his message: "Amalek was first among the nations, but its end will be destruction.
He looked at the Kenite and spoke his message: "Your home is secure, and your nest is set in the rock.
But the Kenites will be destroyed, and Assyria will carry you away.
He spoke his message: "Alas! Who can live when God does this?
But ships will come from Kittim and trouble Assyria and Eber, and they too will be destroyed."
Then Balaam got up and went back to his place, and Balak also went on his way.
While Israel was staying in Shittim, the people began to be unfaithful with the women of Moab.
The Moabite women invited the people to sacrifices for their gods. The people ate the food and bowed down to those gods.
So Israel joined itself to Baal of Peor, and the LORD became very angry with Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and hang them in the sun before the LORD, so the LORD's fierce anger will turn away from Israel."
Moses told the judges of Israel, "Each judge must kill the men in his own group who joined themselves to Baal of Peor."
An Israelite man brought a Midianite woman to his relatives. He did this right in front of Moses and all the people of Israel while they were crying at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he got up from among the people and took a spear in his hand.
He followed the Israelite man into the tent and drove the spear through both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through her body. Then the plague among the Israelites stopped.
But twenty-four thousand people had already died in the plague.
"Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned My anger away from the Israelites. He was jealous for Me among them, so I did not destroy the Israelites in My jealousy.
So tell him this: I am giving him My covenant of peace.
It will be a lasting covenant for him and his descendants after him. It will give him the right to serve as priest forever, because he was jealous for his God and paid for the sin of the Israelites."
The name of the Israelite who was killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu. He was a leader of a family group among the Simeonites.
The woman's name was Cozbi daughter of Zur. She was the head of a family group in Midian.
"Attack the Midianites and strike them down.

They are your enemies. They tricked you with their plan about Peor and about Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader. She was their sister, and she was killed on the day of the plague because of Peor."
After the plague, the LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest,
"Take a census of the whole Israelite community by family groups. Count every man twenty years old or older who can serve in Israel's army."
So on the plains of Moab by the Jordan River, across from Jericho, Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke to the people and said,
"Count the men twenty years old or older, just as the LORD commanded Moses and the Israelites who came out of Egypt."
Reuben was Israel's firstborn. His sons and clans were Hanoch (clan of Hanoch) and Pallu (clan of Pallu).
Hezron (clan of Hezron) and Carmi (clan of Carmi) were also included.

Eliab's sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These Dathan and Abiram were leaders chosen by the community. They rebelled against Moses and Aaron with Korah's group when they rebelled against the LORD.
The ground opened and swallowed them and Korah. Fire killed the 250 men, and this became a warning.
But Korah's sons did not die.
Simeon's sons and clans were Nemuel (clan of Nemuel), Jamin (clan of Jamin), and Jachin (clan of Jachin).
Zerah (clan of Zerah) and Shaul (clan of Shaul) were also included.
Gad's sons and clans were Zephon (clan of Zephon), Haggi (clan of Haggi), and Shuni (clan of Shuni).
Ozni (clan of Ozni) and Eri (clan of Eri) were also included.
Arod (clan of Arod) and Areli (clan of Areli) were also included.
Judah's sons Er and Onan died in Canaan.
Judah's sons and clans were Shelah (clan of Shelah), Perez (clan of Perez), and Zerah (clan of Zerah).
Perez's sons were Hezron (clan of Hezron) and Hamul (clan of Hamul).
Issachar's sons and clans were Tola (clan of Tola) and Puah (clan of Puah).
Jashub (clan of Jashub) and Shimron (clan of Shimron) were also included.
Zebulun's sons and clans were Sered (clan of Sered), Elon (clan of Elon), and Jahleel (clan of Jahleel).
Joseph's sons by families were Manasseh and Ephraim.
Manasseh's sons were Machir (clan of Machir). Machir was the father of Gilead (clan of Gilead).
Gilead's sons were Iezer (clan of Iezer) and Helek (clan of Helek).
Asriel (clan of Asriel) and Shechem (clan of Shechem) were also included.
Shemida (clan of Shemida) and Hepher (clan of Hepher) were also included.
Hepher's son Zelophehad had no sons, only daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
Ephraim's sons and clans were Shuthelah (clan of Shuthelah), Becher (clan of Becher), and Tahan (clan of Tahan).
Shuthelah's son Eran (clan of Eran) was also included.
These Ephraimite clans totaled 32,500. These were Joseph's sons by families.
Benjamin's sons and clans were Bela (clan of Bela), Ashbel (clan of Ashbel), and Ahiram (clan of Ahiram).
Shupham (clan of Shupham) and Hupham (clan of Hupham) were also included.
Bela's sons were Ard (clan of Ard) and Naaman (clan of Naaman).
Dan's sons and clans were Shuham (clan of Shuham). These were the Danite clans by their families.
Asher's sons and clans were Imnah (clan of Imnah), Ishvi (clan of Ishvi), and Beriah (clan of Beriah).
Beriah's sons were Heber (clan of Heber) and Malchiel (clan of Malchiel).
Naphtali's sons and clans were Jahzeel (clan of Jahzeel) and Guni (clan of Guni).
Jezer (clan of Jezer) and Shillem (clan of Shillem) were also included.
The total number of Israelites counted was 601,730.
"Divide the land among these people as an inheritance, based on the number of names.
Give more land to a larger group and less to a smaller one. Each group's land should match its number of counted men.
But divide the land by lot among the tribes of their fathers' families.
Divide the inheritance between the larger and smaller groups by lot."
These were the counted Levites by families: Gershon (clan of Gershon), Kohath (clan of Kohath), and Merari (clan of Merari).
These were Levi's families: Libni (clan of Libni), Hebron (clan of Hebron), Mahli (clan of Mahli), Mushi (clan of Mushi), and Korah (clan of Korah). Kohath was the father of Amram.
Amram's wife was Jochebed, a daughter of Levi born to Levi in Egypt. She bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam to Amram.
Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when they brought unauthorized fire before the LORD.
The Levites counted were 23,000 males one month old or older. They were not counted among the Israelites because they received no inheritance among them.
These were the men Moses and Eleazar the priest counted among the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan River across from Jericho.
Among this group, none were from those Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai wilderness.
For the LORD had said they would die in the wilderness. None survived except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

The daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph, came forward. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, before the leaders, and before the whole community at the entrance to the tent of meeting and said,
"Our father died in the wilderness. He was not one of Korah's followers who gathered against the LORD, but he died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should our father's name disappear from his clan just because he had no son? Give us land among our father's brothers."
So Moses brought their case before the LORD.
The The LORD said to Moses,
"The daughters of Zelophehad are right. You must certainly give them an inheritance among their father's brothers and pass their father's share on to them.
Tell the Israelites: If a man dies and has no son, then you must transfer his inheritance to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father's brothers.

If his father has no brothers, then give his inheritance to the closest relative in his clan, and that relative will take possession of it. This will be a lasting rule for the Israelites, as the LORD has commanded Moses."
The The LORD said to Moses, "Go up into the Abarim mountains and look at the land I have given to the Israelites.
After you have seen it, you will be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron was gathered.
For in the wilderness of Zin, when the people argued with you at the waters of Meribah Kadesh, you rebelled against My command and did not honor Me as holy before their eyes."
"Let the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation.
He must go out before them and come in before them, lead them out and bring them in, so the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd."
The The LORD said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man who has the Spirit in him, and lay your hand on him.
Stand him before Eleazar the priest and before the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight.
Give him some of your authority, so the whole congregation of Israel will obey him.

He will stand before Eleazar the priest, who will seek the LORD's will for him through the Urim. At Joshua's command the people will go out, and at his command they will come in—he and all the Israelites with him, even the whole congregation."
Moses did as the LORD commanded. He took Joshua and stood him before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation.
He laid his hands on Joshua and commissioned him, just as the LORD had spoken through Moses.
"Command the Israelites and tell them, 'Be sure you bring Me the food for My fire offerings, a pleasing aroma, at the proper time. "'
This is the fire offering you must bring to the LORD: two perfect male lambs, one year old, each day, as a regular burnt offering.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.
Along with it, bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of olive oil as a grain offering. "'
This regular burnt offering began at Mount Sinai. It is a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to the LORD.
Its drink offering is a quarter hin of wine for each lamb. Pour out the drink offering to the LORD in the holy place.
Offer the second lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. "'
On the Sabbath day, present two perfect male lambs, one year old, with two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, along with its drink offering.
This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.'" "'
At the beginning of every month, you are to present to the LORD a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven perfect male lambs, one year old.
Along with them, bring three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each bull, and two-tenths of an ephah for the ram. "'
And bring a tenth of an ephah for each lamb. This is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to the LORD.
Their drink offerings are half a hin of wine for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter hin for each lamb. This is the burnt offering for each month throughout the year.
In addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering, offer one male goat to the LORD as a sin offering.'" "'
The Passover to the LORD is on the fourteenth day of the first month.
On the fifteenth day of that month there is to be a feast. For seven days eat unleavened bread.
On the first day there is to be a sacred assembly. You must not do any regular work. "'
Present to the LORD a fire offering, a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven perfect male lambs, one year old.
Along with them, bring grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and a tenth for each lamb.
Include one male goat as a sin offering to pay for your sins. "'
Offer these in addition to the regular morning burnt offering.
Offer the same food each day for seven days as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. It is to be offered with its drink offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering.
On the seventh day you are to hold a sacred assembly. You must not do any regular work.'" "'
On the day of firstfruits, when you present to the LORD an offering of new grain during your Feast of Weeks, you are to hold a sacred assembly. You must not do any regular work.
Present a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven perfect male lambs, one year old, as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. "'
Along with them, bring grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and a tenth for each lamb.
Include one male goat to pay for your sins.
Offer them with their drink offerings in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. They must be unblemished.'"
On the first day of the seventh month, you must hold a sacred gathering. You must not do any regular work. It is a day for you to sound the trumpets.
Offer a burnt offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain offering must be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.

These are in addition to the monthly burnt offering and its grain offering, and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings. They are a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
On the tenth day of this seventh month, you must hold a sacred gathering and humble yourselves. You must not do any work.
Offer a burnt offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain offering must be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering. This is besides the sin offering for atonement and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you must hold a sacred gathering. You must not do any regular work, and you must keep a feast to the LORD for seven days.
Offer a burnt offering, a food offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain offering must be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths for each of the two rams,
and one-tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering. This is besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the second day, offer twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain and drink offerings must match the number of animals, as required.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering. This is besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings.
On the third day, offer eleven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain and drink offerings must match the number of animals, as required.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering. This is besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the fourth day, offer ten young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain and drink offerings must match the number of animals, as required.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering. This is besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the fifth day, offer nine young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain and drink offerings must match the number of animals, as required.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering. This is besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the sixth day, offer eight young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain and drink offerings must match the number of animals, as required.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering. This is besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings.
On the seventh day, offer seven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain and drink offerings must match the number of animals, as required.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering. This is besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the eighth day, you must hold a solemn gathering. You must not do any regular work.
Offer a burnt offering, a food offering with a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs one year old, all without a flaw.
Their grain and drink offerings must match the number of animals, as required.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering. This is besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

You must offer these to the LORD at your appointed feasts. This is in addition to your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, for your burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings.
Moses told the people of Israel everything, just as the LORD had commanded him.
Moses spoke to the leaders of Israel’s tribes and said, “This is what the LORD has commanded:
If a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to bind himself, he must not break his word. He must do everything he promised.
If a woman makes a vow to the LORD or binds herself with a promise while she is young and living in her father’s house,
and her father hears about her vow or promise but says nothing, then all her vows and promises will stand.
But if her father forbids her on the day he hears about it, then none of her vows or promises will stand. The LORD will forgive her, because her father forbade her.
If a woman marries while she is under a vow or a thoughtless promise she made,
and her husband hears about it but says nothing, then her vows and promises will stand.
But if her husband forbids her when he hears about it, he cancels the vow or promise she made, and the LORD will forgive her.
Every vow or promise made by a widow or a divorced woman will stand against her.
If a woman in her husband’s house makes a vow or binds herself with an oath,
and her husband hears about it but says nothing and does not forbid her, then all her vows and promises will stand.
But if her husband cancels them on the day he hears about them, then nothing she vowed or promised will stand. Her husband has canceled them, and the LORD will forgive her.
Her husband can confirm or cancel any vow or oath she makes to deny herself.
But if her husband says nothing to her day after day, then he confirms all her vows and promises. He confirms them by saying nothing on the day he hears about them.
If he cancels them after he hears about them, then he will carry her guilt.
These are the rules the LORD commanded Moses about a man and his wife, and about a father and his young daughter who still lives in his house.
"Take revenge on the Midianites for the Israelites. After that, you will die and join your ancestors.
So Moses said to the people, "Arm some of your men to go to war against Midian. They will carry out the the LORD's revenge on them.
Send one thousand men from each tribe of Israel into battle."
So twelve thousand men armed for battle were supplied from Israel's clans—one thousand from each tribe.
Moses sent them into battle, one thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who took with him holy items and the trumpets used to sound the attack.
They fought against Midian, as the the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
Among those killed were the kings of Midian—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites captured the Midianite women and children and took all their herds, flocks, and goods as plunder.
They burned all the towns where the Midianites had lived, along with all their camps.
They took all the plunder and spoils, both people and animals.
They brought the captives, spoils, and plunder to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the Israelite community at the camp on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the community went out to meet them outside the camp.
But Moses was angry with the army officers—the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds—who had returned from the battle.
"Have you spared all the women?" he asked them.
"Look, these women led the Israelites, on Balaam's advice, to be unfaithful to the the LORD at Peor, and a plague broke out among the the LORD's people.
Now kill every male child, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But keep for yourselves every girl who has never slept with a man.
All of you who have killed anyone or touched a dead body must stay outside the camp for seven days. Purify yourselves and your captives on the third day and the seventh day.
Purify every garment, everything made of leather, everything made of goat hair, and every article of wood."
Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, "This is the rule of the law that the the LORD has commanded Moses.
Only things made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, or lead—

everything that can withstand fire—you must pass through the fire, and it will be clean. But it must also be purified with purifying water. Everything that cannot withstand fire you must pass through the water.
On the seventh day you must wash your clothes, and then you will be clean. After that you may enter the camp."
"You and Eleazar the priest and the family leaders of the community are to count the spoils that were taken—both the people and the animals.
Then divide the spoils between the soldiers who went out to battle and the rest of the community.
From the soldiers who fought, take one out of every five hundred, whether people, cattle, donkeys, or sheep, as a tribute to the the LORD.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the the LORD's contribution.
From the Israelites' half, take one out of every fifty, whether people, cattle, donkeys, or sheep, and give them to the Levites who guard the the LORD's tabernacle."
So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the the LORD had commanded Moses.
The plunder remaining from the spoils taken by the fighting men was 675,000 sheep,
and 32,000 women—all of whom had never slept with a man.
The half given to those who had gone out to war numbered 337,500 sheep,
and the the LORD's tribute from the sheep was 675.
There were 36,000 cattle, and their tribute to the the LORD was 72.
There were 30,500 donkeys, and their tribute to the the LORD was 61.
There were 16,000 people, and the the LORD's tribute was 32.
Moses gave the tribute to Eleazar the priest as a contribution to the the LORD, just as the the LORD had commanded Moses.
From the Israelites' half, which Moses had separated from that of the men who had gone to battle,
Moses took one out of every fifty from the Israelites' share and gave them to the Levites who maintained the the LORD's tabernacle, as the the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then the army officers—the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds—came to Moses
and said, "Your servants have counted the men under our command, and not one of us is missing.
So we have brought an offering to the the LORD from the gold articles each man found—armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces—to make atonement for ourselves before the the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all the articles made of gold.
The gold that the commanders of thousands and hundreds offered as a contribution to the the LORD weighed 16,750 shekels.
(Each soldier had taken plunder for himself.)
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold and brought it to the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the the LORD.
The Reubenites and Gadites had very many animals.
They saw the land of Jazer and Gilead, and they saw that it was good for animals. So the Gadites and Reubenites came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the people.
They said, "Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon—
the land the the LORD defeated for the people of Israel is land for animals, and we, your servants, have animals.
If we have found favor in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants to own. Do not make us cross the Jordan."
Moses said to the Gadites and Reubenites, "Will your brothers go to war while you sit here?
Why do you discourage the people of Israel from crossing into the land the the LORD has given them?
Your fathers did the same thing when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to look at the land.
They went up to the Valley of Eshcol, saw the land, and discouraged the people of Israel from entering the land the the LORD had given them.
The the LORD was angry that day, and He swore an oath:
'Surely none of the men who came up from Egypt, twenty years old or older, will see the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they did not follow Me fully—
except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, because they followed the the LORD fully.'
So the the LORD was angry with Israel and made them wander in the desert for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in the the LORD's sight was gone.
And now you have taken your fathers' place, a group of sinful people, ready to make the the LORD even angrier with Israel.
If you turn away from following Him, He will leave them in the desert again, and you will destroy all these people."
They came closer and said, "We will build sheep pens here for our animals and towns for our children.
But we will arm ourselves and go quickly ahead of the people of Israel until we bring them to their place. Our children will stay in the fortified towns, safe from the people who live in the land.
We will not go home until every person among the people of Israel has received his land.
We will not share in their land west of the Jordan, because our share of land has come to us east of the Jordan."
Moses said to them, "If you do this—if you arm yourselves before the the LORD for war,
and all your armed men cross the Jordan before the the LORD until He has driven out His enemies before Him,
and the land is brought under control before the the LORD—then afterward you may return, and you will be blameless before the the LORD and Israel, and this land will be your land before the the LORD.
But if you do not do this, you have sinned against the the LORD. Know that your sin will find you.
Build towns for your children and pens for your sheep, and do what you have promised."
The Gadites and Reubenites said to Moses, "Your servants will do as my lord commands.
Our children, wives, animals, and all our livestock will stay in the towns of Gilead.
But your servants will cross over, every man armed for war, before the the LORD to fight, as my lord says."
Moses commanded them to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families of the tribes of Israel.

Moses said to them, "If the Gadites and Reubenites cross the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the the LORD, and the land is brought under control before you, then you will give them the land of Gilead to own.
But if they do not cross armed with you, they will receive land among you in Canaan."
The Gadites and Reubenites answered, "We will do what the the LORD has said to your servants.
We will cross over armed before the the LORD into Canaan, and our share of land will stay with us east of the Jordan."

So Moses gave to the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan—the land with its cities and the land around them.
The Gadites built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer.
They also built Atroth-shophan, Jazer, and Jogbehah.
They built Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran as fortified cities, and they made sheep pens.
The Reubenites built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim.
They built Nebo, Baal-meon, and Sibmah, and they gave new names to the cities they built.
The sons of Makir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
Moses gave Gilead to Makir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages and called them Havvoth-jair.
Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages and named it Nobah after himself.
These are the stages of the Israelites' journey. They left Egypt in battle groups, led by Moses and Aaron.
At the the LORD's command, Moses wrote down where they started and where they traveled. These are their journeys, stage by stage.
On the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after Passover, the Israelites set out from Rameses. They marched out boldly while all the Egyptians watched.
The Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom the the LORD had struck among them. The the LORD had also brought judgment on their gods.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham and turned back toward Pi-hahiroth, east of Baal-zephon, and camped before Migdol.
They set out from Pi-hahiroth and passed through the sea into the wilderness. They traveled three days in the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Elim. At Elim there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin at Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
At the the LORD's command, Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor and died there. This was in the fortieth year after the Israelites left Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iye-abarim and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
They camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.
The The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho. He said, "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'When you cross the Jordan into Canaan,
drive out all the people living there before you. Destroy all their carved images and cast idols. Destroy all their high places.
Take possession of the land and live in it, because I have given it to you to possess.

Divide the land by lot among your families. Give more land to the larger tribe and less to the smaller. Wherever the lot falls for a person, that will be his place. Divide it among the tribes of your fathers.
But if you do not drive out the people living in the land, those you leave will be like thorns in your eyes and pricks in your sides. They will trouble you in the land where you live.
And I will do to you what I planned to do to them.'"
He said, "Command the Israelites and tell them that when they enter Canaan, this land will be their inheritance. It is the land of Canaan with these borders:
"The southern border will be the Wilderness of Zin along the border of Edom. It will start at the southern end of the Dead Sea.
It will cross south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, continue to Zin, and end south of Kadesh Barnea. Then it will go to Hazar Addar and pass on to Azmon.
There it will turn toward the Brook of Egypt and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
"The western border will be the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. This will be their border on the west.
"The northern border will be like this: Draw a line from the Mediterranean Sea to Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor draw a line to Lebo Hamath. Then the border will go to Zedad,
continue to Ziphron, and end at Hazar Enan. This will be their border on the north.
"The eastern border will be like this: Draw a line from Hazar Enan to Shepham.
Then the border will go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain. It will continue along the slopes east of the Sea of Galilee.
Then it will go down along the Jordan River and end at the Dead Sea. This will be their land, with borders on every side."
Moses commanded the Israelites, "This is the land you are to receive by lot as your inheritance. The the LORD has commanded that it be given to the nine and a half tribes.
The tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance.
These two and a half tribes received their inheritance east of the Jordan, across from Jericho, to the east."
He said, "These are the names of the men who will divide the land for you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
Appoint one leader from each tribe to help divide the land. "
These are their names: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
from the tribe of Dan, Bukki son of Jogli;
from the tribe of Manasseh, Hanniel son of Ephod;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach;
from the tribe of Issachar, Paltiel son of Azzan;
from the tribe of Asher, Ahihud son of Shelomi;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud. "
These are the men the the LORD commanded to give the Israelites their inheritance in the land of Canaan."
The LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho. He said,
"Command the Israelites to give the Levites cities to live in from the land they own, and you must also give the Levites pastureland around those cities.
The cities will be for the Levites to live in, and the pastureland will be for their cattle, their goods, and all their animals.
The pastureland around the cities that you give the Levites must reach a thousand cubits from the city wall all the way around.

You must measure two thousand cubits outside the city on the east, two thousand on the south, two thousand on the west, and two thousand on the north, with the city in the middle. This will be the pastureland for the cities.
Among the cities you give the Levites, six will be cities of refuge, where a person who has killed someone can run for safety. Besides these, you must give them forty-two more cities.
So all the cities you give the Levites will be forty-eight, along with their pastureland.

The cities you give the Levites from the Israelites' land must come from the larger tribes more and from the smaller tribes less. Each tribe must give cities to the Levites in proportion to the land it receives."
Then the LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them, 'When you cross the Jordan into Canaan,
you must choose cities to be your cities of refuge. A person who kills someone by accident can run there for safety.
These cities will protect him from the relative who seeks revenge, so the killer will not die until he stands trial before the people.
The cities you give will be six cities of refuge for you.
You must give three cities east of the Jordan and three in Canaan. They will be cities of refuge.
These six cities will be a safe place for Israelites, foreigners, and travelers living among them, so anyone who kills a person by accident can run there.'"
If a man hits someone with an iron tool and kills him, he is a murderer and must be put to death.
If he hits him with a stone that could kill and the man dies, he is a murderer and must be put to death.
If he hits him with a wooden tool that could kill and the man dies, he is a murderer and must be put to death.
The relative who seeks revenge must kill the murderer when he finds him.
If a man pushes someone out of hatred, or throws something at him on purpose to kill him,
or hits him in anger and kills him, the one who hit him must be put to death. He is a murderer, and the relative who seeks revenge must kill him when he finds him.
But if he pushes someone suddenly, without hatred, or throws something at him without meaning to kill him,
or without seeing drops a stone that could kill on him and he dies, and the man was not his enemy and did not mean to hurt him,
then the community must judge between the killer and the relative who seeks revenge, using these rules.

The community must rescue the killer from the relative who seeks revenge and send him back to his city of refuge, where he fled. He must live there until the high priest dies, the one who was anointed with holy oil.
But if the killer leaves his city of refuge,
and the relative who seeks revenge finds him outside the city, that relative may kill him without guilt.
The killer must stay in his city of refuge until the high priest dies. After the high priest dies, he may return to his own land.
These rules will be a law for you and your descendants in every place you live.
If anyone kills a person, the murderer must be put to death, but only if witnesses testify against him. One witness is not enough to put someone to death.
You must not accept money to spare the life of a murderer who deserves to die. He must be put to death.
You must not accept money to let someone who fled to a city of refuge return home before the high priest dies.
Do not make the land where you live unclean. Bloodshed makes the land unclean, and the land cannot be made clean except by the blood of the one who shed it.
Do not make unclean the land where you live, where I dwell among you. I am the LORD, and I dwell among the Israelites.

The family leaders from the clan of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, one of Joseph’s family groups, came to Moses and to the leaders of Israel. These leaders were the heads of the Israelite families.
“The LORD told my lord to give the land to the Israelites by lot as their inheritance. My lord was also told by the LORD to give our brother Zelophehad’s inheritance to his daughters.

But if they marry men from other Israelite tribes, their inheritance will be taken from our fathers’ inheritance and added to the inheritance of the tribe they join. Then part of our share of the land would be lost.
When the Jubilee year comes for the Israelites, their inheritance will be added to the tribe they join and taken from our fathers’ tribe.”
So, at the LORD’s command, Moses gave this order to the Israelites: “The tribe of Joseph’s descendants is right.
This is what the LORD has commanded about Zelophehad’s daughters: They may marry anyone they choose, as long as they marry within their father’s tribe.
No inheritance in Israel may pass from one tribe to another, because each Israelite must keep the land of his fathers’ tribe.
