Also, every daughter who inherits land in any Israelite tribe must marry within her father’s tribe, so each Israelite keeps the land passed down from his fathers.
No inheritance may move from one tribe to another, because each Israelite tribe must keep its own land.”
So Zelophehad’s daughters did what the LORD commanded through Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah married their cousins.
They married into the family of Manasseh son of Joseph, so their inheritance stayed with their father’s tribe.
These are the commands and rules the LORD gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River near Jericho.
These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel in the wilderness east of the Jordan, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It takes eleven days to travel from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by way of Mount Seir.
In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses told the Israelites everything the the LORD had commanded him to say to them.
This was after he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
East of the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this law. He said:
The The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb. He said, "You have stayed at this mountain long enough.

Resume your journey and go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, the hill country, the foothills, the Negev, and along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. Go to the land of the Canaanites and to Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
See, I have given the land ahead of you. Go in and take it, the land the the LORD promised to give to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and to their descendants after them."
At that time I said to you, "I cannot carry you by myself.
The The LORD your God has made you many, and today you are as many as the stars in the sky.
May the the LORD, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times more and bless you, as He has promised you.
How can I carry your troubles, your loads, and your arguments by myself?
Choose wise, understanding, and respected men from each of your tribes, and I will put them over you as leaders."
You answered me, "What you say is good."
So I took the leaders of your tribes—wise and respected men—and put them over you. I made them commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers for your tribes.
At that time I told your judges, "Listen to the cases between your brothers and judge fairly between a man and his brother or a foreigner living among you."
Do not show favoritism in judging. Hear the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, because judgment belongs to God. Bring me any case that is too hard for you, and I will hear it.
At that time I gave you all the commands you are to follow.
Then we set out from Horeb and traveled through all that great and frightening wilderness you saw, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.
I said to you, "You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the the LORD our God is giving us.
See, the the LORD your God has given you the land. Go up and take it, as the the LORD, the God of your fathers, told you. Do not be afraid or discouraged."
Then all of you came to me and said, "Let us send men ahead of us to explore the land for us and bring back a report about the way we should go and the cities we will enter."
The idea seemed good to me, so I chose twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.
They set out and went up into the hill country and came to the Valley of Eshcol and spied it out.
They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands, brought it down to us, and reported, "The land the the LORD our God is giving us is good."
But you were not willing to go up. You rebelled against the command of the the LORD your God.
You grumbled in your tents and said, "The The LORD hates us. That is why He brought us out of Egypt—to hand us over to the Amorites to be destroyed.
Where can we go? Our brothers have discouraged us. They say the people are stronger and taller than we are, the cities are large with walls up to the sky, and they saw the sons of Anak there."
Then I said to you, "Do not be terrified or afraid of them.
The The LORD your God, who goes before you, will fight for you, just as you saw Him do for you in Egypt
and in the wilderness, where the the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way you traveled until you reached this place."
But even so, you did not believe the the LORD your God,
who went before you on your journey to find a place for you to camp and to show you the way you should go, with fire by night and cloud by day.
When the the LORD heard your words, He was angry and swore an oath:
"Not one of the men of this evil generation will see the good land I swore to give your fathers,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and I will give him and his descendants the land he walked on, because he followed the the LORD wholeheartedly."
The The LORD was also angry with me because of you, and He said, "You will not enter it either.
But Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, will enter it. Encourage him, for he will lead Israel to take it.
And your little ones, whom you said would become plunder, and your children who do not yet know good from evil, will enter it. I will give it to them, and they will take it.
But as for you, turn around and set out for the wilderness by way of the Red Sea."

Then you replied, "We have sinned against the the LORD. We will go up and fight, as the the LORD our God commanded us." So each of you put on his weapons of war, and you were eager to go up into the hill country.
But the the LORD said to me, "Tell them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not with you. If you do, you will be defeated by your enemies."
So I spoke to you, but you did not listen. You rebelled against the the LORD's command and went up into the hill country anyway.
Then the Amorites who lived in the hill country came out against you and chased you like a swarm of bees. They crushed you in Seir all the way to Hormah.
You returned and wept before the the LORD, but the the LORD would not listen to your voice or pay attention to you.
And you stayed in Kadesh for many days—the same number of days you had stayed before.
Then we turned and set out for the wilderness by way of the Red Sea, as the the LORD had told me, and for many days we traveled around Mount Seir.
Then the the LORD spoke to me and said,
You have circled this mountain long enough; now turn north.
Command the people: 'You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be very afraid of you, so watch yourselves carefully.
Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land—not even a foot of ground—because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.
You may buy food from them with money so that you may eat, and you may buy water from them with money so that you may drink.'

For the the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this great wilderness. These forty years the the LORD your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing.

So we passed by our brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. We turned away from the Arabah road that comes from Elath and Ezion-geber, and we traveled along the road through the wilderness of Moab.

Then the the LORD said to me, "Do not trouble Moab or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as a possession."
The Emim used to live there—a people great, numerous, and tall, like the Anakim.
Like the Anakim, they were also regarded as Rephaim, but the Moabites called them Emim.

The Horites also lived in Seir formerly, but the descendants of Esau drove them out and destroyed them and settled in their place, just as Israel did to the land the the LORD gave them as their possession.
"Now get up and cross the Zered Valley." So we crossed the Zered Valley.

The time we spent traveling from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley was thirty-eight years, until the whole generation of fighting men had died off from the camp, as the the LORD had sworn to them.
Indeed, the hand of the the LORD was against them, to destroy them from the camp, until they were gone.
So when all the fighting men had finally died among the people,
the the LORD spoke to me and said,
"Today you are to pass by the territory of Moab at Ar.

When you come near the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them, for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites as a possession, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as a possession."
That too is regarded as a land of the Rephaim. The Rephaim formerly lived there, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim.
They were a people great, numerous, and tall, like the Anakim, but the the LORD destroyed them before the Ammonites, who drove them out and settled in their place.
He did the same for the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites before them. They drove them out and settled in their place, and they remain there to this day.
The Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorim, who came from Caphtor and settled in their place.
"Arise, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession of it and engage him in battle.
This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon all the peoples under the whole heaven, who will hear your report and tremble and be in anguish because of you."
So I sent messengers from the Wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,
"Let me pass through your land. I will stay on the main road; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Sell me food for money so that I may eat, and give me water for money so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land the the LORD our God is giving us."
But Sihon king of Heshbon refused to let us pass through, for the the LORD your God hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, that He might give him into your hand, as he is this day.
And the the LORD said to me, "See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession, that you may inherit his land."
Then Sihon and all his people came out to meet us in battle at Jahaz.
And the the LORD our God gave him over to us, and we struck him down, along with his sons and all his people.
At that time we captured all his cities and completely destroyed every city—its men, women, and children. We left no survivors.
We took only the livestock and the spoil of the cities we captured as plunder for ourselves.
From Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and from the city in the valley, even as far as Gilead, there was not a city too strong for us. The The LORD our God gave everything into our hands.
But we did not go near the land of the Ammonites, or anywhere along the Jabbok River, or the cities of the hill country, or anywhere the the LORD our God had forbidden us.
Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, came out to meet us with all his people to fight at Edrei.
The LORD said to me, “Do not be afraid of him, because I have given him, his people, and his land into your hand. Do to him what you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
So the LORD our God also gave Og, king of Bashan, and all his people into our hands, and we struck them down until no one was left.
At that time we captured all his cities. There was not a city we did not take from them—sixty cities in all—the whole region of Argob, which was Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
All these cities had high walls, gates, and bars. There were also many towns without walls.
We completely destroyed them, just as we had done to Sihon, king of Heshbon. We destroyed every city, along with the men, women, and children.
But we kept all the livestock and the plunder from the cities for ourselves.
At that time we took the land from the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon.
(The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)
We took all the cities of the plain, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities in Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
(Og, king of Bashan, was the last of the Rephaim. His iron bed was nine cubits long and four cubits wide, using the standard cubit.)
This is the land we took over at that time: from Aroer on the Arnon River, I gave half the hill country of Gilead and its cities to the Reubenites and Gadites.
I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, Og’s kingdom, to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (The whole region of Argob in Bashan used to be called the land of the Rephaim.)
Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. He named the villages after himself; they are called Havvoth Jair to this day.
To the Reubenites and Gadites I gave land from Gilead to the Arnon River—the middle of the river as the border—and as far as the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
The Jordan River and the Arabah also served as a border, from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea), below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
At that time I commanded you: “The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your fighting men must cross over, armed, ahead of your brothers, the Israelites.
But your wives, little ones, and livestock—I know you have much livestock—may stay in the cities I have given you.

... until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as He has to you, and they too possess the land the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the land I have given you.”
At that time I also charged Joshua: “You have seen with your own eyes all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to enter.
Do not be afraid of them, because the LORD your God Himself is the One who fights for you.”
At that time I pleaded with the LORD:
“O Lord, the LORD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand. What god is there in heaven or on earth who can do works and mighty acts like Yours?
Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan—that good hill country and Lebanon.”
But the LORD was angry with me because of you, and He would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, “That is enough; do not speak to Me about this matter again.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and look west, north, south, and east. Look with your own eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.
But commission Joshua, and encourage and strengthen him, because he will cross over ahead of this people and will give them the land you will see.”
So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth Peor.
"Now, Israel, listen to the laws and rules I am teaching you. Do them so you can live, go in, and take the land the the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
Do not add anything to what I command you, and do not take anything away from it. Keep the commands of the the LORD your God that I give you.
You saw with your own eyes what the the LORD did at Baal Peor. The the LORD your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed Baal of Peor.
But all of you who stayed close to the the LORD your God are alive today.
"See, I have taught you the laws and rules, just as the the LORD my God commanded me. Follow them in the land you are entering to take.

Keep them and do them. They will be your wisdom and understanding before the nations. When those nations hear all these laws, they will say, 'Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.'
What great nation has a god so near to it as the the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on Him?
What great nation has laws and rules as fair as all this law I am giving you today?

"Only be very careful. Guard your soul closely so you do not forget what your eyes have seen. Do not let these things leave your heart as long as you live. Teach them to your children and grandchildren.

Remember the day you stood before the the LORD your God at Horeb. The the LORD said to me, 'Bring the people to Me so I can let them hear My words. Then they will learn to fear Me all the days they live on the earth, and they will teach their children.'
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain burned with fire up to the sky. It was dark, with clouds and thick darkness.
Then the the LORD spoke to you from the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you saw no form. There was only a voice.
He told you His covenant, which He commanded you to keep: the Ten Commandments. He wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time the the LORD commanded me to teach you the laws and rules, so you could do them in the land you are crossing over to take.
"So guard yourselves very carefully. You saw no form on the day the the LORD spoke to you from the fire at Horeb.
Be careful not to ruin yourselves by making a carved idol. Do not make an image of any shape, male or female.
Do not make an image of any animal on earth, any bird that flies in the sky,
anything that crawls on the ground, or any fish in the water below.

Do not look up to the sky and be led astray. When you see the sun, moon, and stars, all the host of heaven, do not bow down to them or serve them. The the LORD your God has given them to all the nations under the whole sky.
But the the LORD took you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt. He made you His own people, as you are today.
"Furthermore, the the LORD was angry with me because of you. He swore that I would not cross the Jordan or enter the good land the the LORD your God is giving you as your own.
I will die in this land. I will not cross the Jordan. But you will cross over and take this good land.
Be careful not to forget the covenant of the the LORD your God that He made with you. Do not make a carved idol of any kind that the the LORD your God has forbidden.
The the LORD your God is a consuming fire. He is a jealous God.

"When you have children and grandchildren, and you have grown old in the land, do not ruin yourselves. Do not make a carved idol of any kind, and do not do evil in the sight of the the LORD your God, because that makes Him angry.

I call heaven and earth to witness against you today. You will quickly be destroyed and removed from the land you are crossing the Jordan to take. You will not live there long. You will be completely destroyed.
The the LORD will scatter you among the peoples. Only a few of you will survive among the nations where the the LORD drives you.
There you will serve gods of wood and stone, made by human hands. They cannot see, hear, eat, or smell.
"But from there you will seek the the LORD your God. You will find Him if you search for Him with all your heart and all your soul.
When you are in trouble and all these things happen to you in the last days, you will return to the the LORD your God and obey His voice.
The the LORD your God is merciful. He will not leave you or destroy you. He will not forget the covenant with your fathers, which He swore to them.
"Ask about the past, before your time, since the day God created man on the earth. Ask from one end of the sky to the other. Has anything this great ever happened before? Has anyone ever heard of it?
Has any nation ever heard the voice of a god speaking from the fire, as you have heard, and lived?

Has any god ever tried to take a nation for himself from another nation by tests, signs, wonders, war, a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and great terrors? That is what the the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes.
"You were shown this so you would know that the the LORD is God. There is no other besides Him.
From heaven He let you hear His voice to teach you. On earth He let you see His great fire, and you heard His words from the fire.
Because He loved your fathers, He chose their children after them. He brought you out of Egypt with His own presence and great power.
He drove out nations greater and stronger than you so He could bring you in and give you their land as your own, as it is today.
Know today, and take it to heart, that the the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below. There is no other.

Keep His laws and commands, which I give you today, so it will go well with you and your children after you. Then you will live a long time in the land the the LORD your God is giving you for all your days."
Then Moses set apart three cities east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
A person who killed someone by accident, without hating them before, could run to one of these cities and live.
Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
This is the law Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the rules, laws, and commands Moses spoke to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
This was east of the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites defeated him when they came out of Egypt.
They took his land and the land of Og king of Bashan. These were the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
Their land ran from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley to Mount Sirion, that is, Hermon.
It also included all the Arabah east of the Jordan, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.
Moses called all the people of Israel together and said to them, "Hear, O Israel, the rules and laws I am speaking to your ears today. Learn them and be careful to do them.
The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
The LORD did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us—with all of us who are alive here today.
The LORD spoke with you face to face on the mountain, out of the fire.
At that time I stood between the the LORD and you to tell you the word of the the LORD, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
'I am the the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall have no other gods before Me.
You shall not make for yourself a carved image—any likeness of anything in heaven above, on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.

You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the the LORD your God, am a jealous God, punishing the sin of the fathers on the children, on the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me.
But I show mercy to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments.
'You shall not take the name of the the LORD your God in vain, for the the LORD will not hold guiltless anyone who takes His name in vain.
Observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy, as the the LORD your God has commanded you.
Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the the LORD your God. You shall not do any work—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your ox, your donkey, or any of your livestock, nor the stranger within your gates—so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as well as you.

Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the the LORD your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore the the LORD your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
'Honor your father and your mother, as the the LORD your God has commanded you, so that your days may be long and things may go well with you in the land that the the LORD your God is giving you.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. You shall not covet your neighbor's house, his field, his male servant, his female servant, his ox, his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.'

"The LORD spoke these words to your whole assembly at the mountain out of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, with a loud voice. He added nothing more. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
"When you heard the voice out of the darkness while the mountain was burning with fire, all the heads of your tribes and your elders came to me.
'Look, the the LORD our God has shown us His glory and greatness, and we have heard His voice out of the fire. Today we have seen that a person can live even though God speaks with him.
But now, why should we die? This great fire will burn us up, and we will die if we hear the voice of the the LORD our God any longer.
What person of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the fire, as we have, and lived?
You go near and hear all that the the LORD our God says, and you tell us everything the the LORD our God tells you, and we will listen and do it.'
"The LORD heard your words when you spoke to me, and the the LORD said to me,
'I have heard the words this people spoke to you. They have done well in all they have said.
If only they had such a heart, to fear Me and keep all My commandments always, so that it might go well with them and with their children forever!
Go tell them to return to their tents.
But you, stand here by Me, and I will speak to you all the commandments, rules, and laws that you are to teach them, so they may do them in the land I am giving them to possess.'
"So be careful to do as the the LORD your God has commanded you; do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Walk in all the way that the the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live and it may go well with you, and that you may prolong your days in the land you will possess."
These are the commandments, statutes, and ordinances that the the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, so you can obey them in the land you are crossing over to possess,

so that you, your children, and your grandchildren may fear the the LORD your God all the days of your life and keep all His statutes and commands that I am giving you today, so that your days may be long.
Listen, Israel, and be careful to do them, so that things go well for you and you multiply greatly in a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the the LORD, the God of your fathers, promised you.
Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the the LORD is One.
You shall love the the LORD your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your strength.
These words that I command you today are to be on your heart.
Teach them carefully to your children. Talk about them when you sit in your house, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Tie them as a sign on your hand, and let them be reminders between your eyes.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
When the the LORD your God brings you into the land He swore to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—to give you, you will find large and good cities that you did not build,
along with houses full of good things you did not fill, wells you did not dig, and vineyards and olive groves you did not plant. Then you will eat and be full.
Be careful not to forget the the LORD, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.
Fear the the LORD your God and serve Him, and swear by His name.
Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you.
For the the LORD your God among you is a jealous God. If His anger burns against you, the the LORD your God will wipe you from the face of the earth.
Do not test the the LORD your God, as you tested Him at Massah.
Carefully obey the commandments of the the LORD your God, along with His testimonies and statutes that He commanded you.
Do what is right and good in the the LORD's sight, so that things go well for you and you take possession of the good land the the LORD promised to your fathers.
He will drive out all your enemies before you, just as the the LORD has said.
In the future, when your son asks you, "What do these testimonies, statutes, and ordinances mean that the the LORD our God commanded you?"
Tell him, "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, but the the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand. "
The The LORD showed great and terrible signs and wonders in Egypt against Pharaoh and all his household, right before our eyes.
He brought us out of there to bring us into this land and give it to us, the land He promised to our fathers. "
The The LORD commanded us to obey all these statutes and to fear the the LORD our God, so that things will always go well for us and we will live, as we do today.
If we are careful to obey all this command before the the LORD our God, as He commanded us, it will be our righteousness."

For the LORD your God will bring you into the land you are entering to possess, and He will drive out before you many nations—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—seven nations larger and stronger than you.
When the LORD your God delivers them over to you and you defeat them, then you must completely destroy them. Make no treaty with them and show them no mercy.
Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons,
because they will turn your sons away from following Me to serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will quickly destroy you.
Instead, this is what you are to do to them: Break down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images in the fire.
For you are a holy people belonging to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be His people, His treasured possession, out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
The LORD did not set His affection on you and choose you because you were more numerous than the other peoples, for you were the fewest of all peoples.
But because the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers, He brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Know therefore that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God who keeps His covenant of faithful love for a thousand generations of those who love Him and keep His commandments.
But He repays those who hate Him to their faces, bringing swift destruction; He will not hesitate to repay the one who hates Him.
So keep the commands, laws, and rules that I am giving you today, and follow them.
If you listen to these rules and keep and practice them, then the LORD your God will keep His covenant and faithful love to you, as He swore to your fathers.

He will love you and bless you and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the produce of your land—your grain, your new wine, and your oil, the young of your herds and the lambs of your flocks—in the land that He swore to your fathers to give you.
You will be blessed more than all peoples. None of your men or women will be barren, and none of your livestock will be barren.
The LORD will remove from you all sickness. He will not lay upon you any of the terrible diseases you knew in Egypt, but He will inflict them on all who hate you.
You must destroy all the peoples the LORD your God will deliver to you. Do not look on them with pity, and do not serve their gods, for that will be a trap for you.
You may say in your heart, “These nations are greater than I am. How can I drive them out?”
But do not be afraid of them. Be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt—

the great trials your eyes saw, the signs and wonders, the mighty hand and outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. The LORD your God will do the same to all the peoples you now fear.
Moreover, the LORD your God will send the hornet against them until even the survivors and those hiding from you have perished.
Do not be terrified of them, for the LORD your God, who is among you, is a great and awesome God.
The LORD your God will drive out these nations before you little by little. You will not be able to destroy them all at once, or the wild animals will multiply around you.
But the LORD your God will give them over to you and throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
He will hand their kings over to you, and you will wipe out their names from under heaven. No one will be able to stand against you; you will destroy them.

You must burn up the carved images of their gods. Do not covet the silver or gold that is on them, and do not take it for yourself, or you will be trapped by it, for it is detestable to the LORD your God.
Do not bring a detestable thing into your house, or you will be set apart for destruction like it. You must utterly detest and abhor it, for it is set apart for destruction.
Be careful to obey all the commands I am giving you today, so that you may live and grow in number, and go in and take over the land the the LORD promised to your ancestors.

Remember how the the LORD your God led you all the way through the wilderness for forty years. He did it to humble you and test you, to learn what was in your heart and whether you would keep His commands.

He let you go hungry, then fed you manna, a food that neither you nor your ancestors had ever known. He did this so you would understand that people do not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of the the LORD.
Your clothes did not wear out, and your feet did not swell during those forty years.
You should know in your heart that the the LORD your God corrects you just as a father corrects his son.
So obey the commands of the the LORD your God by walking in His ways and fearing Him.
The LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land with streams and pools of water, with springs flowing out in the valleys and hills.
It is a land of wheat and barley, vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey.
It is a land where you will eat bread without ever running short, where you will lack nothing. It is a land whose stones are iron and whose hills you can dig copper from.
When you have eaten and are full, praise the the LORD your God for the good land He has given you.
Be careful not to forget the the LORD your God by failing to keep His commands, laws, and rules that I am giving you today.
When you eat and are full, and build good houses and settle down,
and when your herds and flocks grow, and your silver and gold increase, and everything you own increases,
do not let your heart become proud and forget the the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.
He led you through the great and dangerous wilderness, with its poisonous snakes and scorpions, and its dry ground with no water. He brought water out of hard rock for you.
In the wilderness He fed you with manna, which your ancestors had never known, to humble you and test you so that things would go well for you in the end.
Do not say in your heart that your strength and your own power made you wealthy.
Remember the the LORD your God, because He is the One who gives you power to become wealthy. He does this to keep the promise He made to your ancestors, just as He does today.
But if you forget the the LORD your God and follow other gods and worship them, I warn you today that you will certainly be destroyed.
Like the nations the the LORD is destroying before you, you too will be destroyed, because you did not obey the voice of the the LORD your God.
Hear, Israel! Today you are crossing the Jordan to go in and take over nations greater and stronger than you—cities with walls reaching up to the sky.
The people there are tall and strong. They are the Anakites. You know about them, and you have heard people ask, "Who can stand up to the Anakites?"

But know today that the LORD your God goes ahead of you. He is like a fire that destroys. He will destroy them and put them under your power. You will drive them out and wipe them out quickly, just as the LORD has promised you.

After the LORD your God has driven them out ahead of you, do not say in your heart, "The LORD brought me in to take this land because I am right with Him." No, it is because of the evil of these nations that the LORD is driving them out ahead of you.

You are not going in to take their land because you are good or because your heart is right. The LORD your God is driving them out before you because of their evil, and to keep the promise the LORD made to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Know that the LORD your God is not giving you this good land to take over because you are good. You are a stubborn people.
Remember this, and do not forget: you made the LORD your God angry in the desert. From the day you left Egypt until you came to this place, you have rebelled against the LORD.
At Mount Horeb you made the LORD angry. He was so angry with you that He wanted to destroy you.
When I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets—the tablets of the covenant the LORD made with you—I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
The LORD gave me the two stone tablets written with the finger of God. On them were all the words the LORD spoke to you from the fire on the mountain on the day you gathered there.
At the end of the forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets of the covenant.

Then the LORD said to me, "Get up and go down quickly from here, because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have ruined themselves. They have quickly turned away from what I commanded them and made a metal idol for themselves."
The LORD also said, "I have seen these people, and they are stubborn."
"Leave Me alone so I can destroy them and wipe out their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a nation stronger and greater than they are."
So I turned and went down the mountain while it was on fire. I had the two tablets of the covenant in my hands.
I looked, and there you were—you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made a molded calf for yourselves. You had quickly turned away from the path the LORD had commanded you to follow.
So I took the two tablets and threw them from my hands, breaking them in front of you.

Then I fell down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights, just as I had done before. I ate no bread and drank no water. I did this because of all the sin you had committed by doing evil in the LORD's sight and making Him angry.
I was afraid of the LORD's anger and fury, because He was angry enough with you to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me that time too.
The LORD was very angry with Aaron and would have destroyed him, so I prayed for Aaron too at that time.
I took the sinful thing—the calf you had made—and burned it in the fire. I crushed it and ground it into powder, as fine as dust. Then I threw the dust into the stream that flowed down the mountain.
You also made the LORD angry at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth Hattaavah.
When the LORD sent you from Kadesh Barnea and said, "Go up and take the land I have given you," you rebelled against the LORD your God. You did not believe Him or listen to His voice.
You have been rebelling against the LORD ever since I have known you.
So I fell down before the LORD for the forty days and forty nights I had already fallen down, because the LORD said He would destroy you.
I prayed to the LORD and said, "O Lord the LORD, do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance, whom You redeemed by Your great power and brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look at how stubborn this people is, or at their evil and sin,
so that the land You brought us from will not say, "'The LORD was not able to bring them into the land He promised them, and because He hated them, He brought them out to die in the desert.'
Yet they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out with Your great power and Your strong arm."
At that time, the LORD said to me, "Carve out two stone tablets for yourself, like the first ones. Come up to me on the mountain, and make a wooden ark for yourself."
I will write on the tablets the same words that were on the first tablets, the ones you broke, and you must put them in the ark.
So I made an ark of acacia wood and carved two stone tablets like the first ones. Then I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
The LORD wrote on the tablets the same writing as before—the Ten Commandments, which the LORD spoke to you from the fire on the mountain on the day the people gathered. Then the LORD gave them to me.
I turned around and came down the mountain, and I put the tablets in the ark I had made. They are still there, just as the LORD commanded me.
The Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah. Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar took his place as priest.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the LORD's covenant, to stand before the LORD and serve Him, and to bless people in His name. They still do this today.
That is why Levi has no share of land with his brothers. The LORD Himself is his share, just as the LORD your God said to him.
I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, as I did the first time, and the LORD listened to me then too. The LORD did not want to destroy you.
Then the LORD said to me, "Get up and go on ahead of the people, so they can enter and take the land I promised their ancestors I would give them."

And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you? He asks you to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to love Him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
He asks you to keep the LORD's commands and rules, which I am giving you today for your own good.
Look, heaven and the highest heavens belong to the LORD your God, along with the earth and everything in it.
Yet the LORD delighted in your ancestors and loved them. He chose their descendants after them—you—out of all the nations, as He has done today.
So cut away the stubbornness in your hearts and stop being stubborn.
For the LORD your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords. He is great, powerful, and awesome. He does not show favoritism, and He does not take bribes.
He makes sure orphans and widows get justice, and He loves foreigners, giving them food and clothing.
So love foreigners, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
Fear the LORD your God and serve Him. Hold on to Him, and swear by His name.
He is the one you praise. He is your God, who did these great and terrifying things for you, which your own eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down to Egypt with only seventy people, but now the LORD your God has made you as many as the stars in the sky.
Love the LORD your God and keep His rules, laws, and commands every day.
Remember today that your children did not know and did not see the discipline of the LORD your God. They did not see His greatness, His mighty hand, or His outstretched arm.
They did not see His signs and the things He did in Egypt to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to all his land.
They did not see what He did to Egypt's army, horses, and chariots when He made the Red Sea cover them as they chased you. The LORD destroyed them, and they are gone to this day.
They did not see what He did for you in the desert until you arrived here.

They did not see what He did to Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab son of Reuben, when the ground opened its mouth and swallowed them, their houses, their tents, and everything that followed their feet, right in front of all Israel.
But your eyes have seen all the great things the LORD has done.
So keep all the command I give you today. Then you will be strong, and you will go in and take the land you are crossing over to possess.
Then you will live a long time in the land the LORD promised your fathers He would give to them and their children. It is a land flowing with milk and honey.
The land you are entering to possess is not like Egypt, where you planted seed and watered it by foot, like a vegetable garden.
But the land you are crossing into is a land of hills and valleys. It drinks rain from heaven.
It is a land the LORD your God cares for. The eyes of the LORD your God are always on it, from the beginning of the year to the end.
If you carefully listen to the commands I give you today, and love the LORD your God and serve Him with all your heart and soul,
then I will send rain on your land at the right time, both the fall and spring rains. Then you will gather your grain, new wine, and olive oil.
I will give grass in your fields for your animals, and you will eat and be full.
Be careful, or your heart will be tricked. Then you will turn away and worship other gods and bow down to them.

Then the LORD's anger will burn against you. He will close the sky so there is no rain, and the ground will not give its crops. You will soon be destroyed and removed from the good land the LORD is giving you.
Put these words of Mine in your hearts and minds. Tie them as a sign on your hands, and let them be on your foreheads.
Teach them to your children. Talk about them when you sit at home, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Write them on the doorframes of your house and on your gates.
Then your days and your children's days will be many in the land the LORD promised your fathers. They will be as many as the days the sky is above the earth.
If you carefully keep all these commands I am giving you, and love the LORD your God, walk in all His ways, and stay close to Him,
then the LORD will drive out all these nations ahead of you. You will take over nations bigger and stronger than you.
Every place where you set your foot will belong to you. Your land will stretch from the desert and Lebanon, from the Euphrates River to the western sea.
No one will be able to stand against you. The LORD your God will put fear and dread of you on the whole land you walk on, just as He promised you.
Look, today I am putting a blessing and a curse in front of you.
You will get the blessing if you obey the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today.
You will get the curse if you do not obey the commands of the LORD your God, but turn from the way I command you today, and follow other gods you have not known.
When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
These mountains are across the Jordan, west of the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah. They are opposite Gilgal, near the oaks of Moreh.
You are about to cross the Jordan to take the land the LORD your God is giving you. You will possess it and live in it.
Be careful to follow all the rules and laws I am putting in front of you today.
These are the rules and decisions you must follow. Follow them every day you live in the land the the LORD, the God of your fathers, gave you to own.
You must completely destroy every place where the nations you are driving out worship their gods. Destroy their places on high mountains, on hills, and under every green tree.
Tear down their altars. Smash their sacred stone pillars. Burn their Asherah poles. Cut down the carved images of their gods. Erase their names from those places.
You must not worship the the LORD your God in that way.
Instead, look for the place the the LORD your God will choose from among all your tribes. He will put His Name there as His home. Go to that place.

There you must bring your burnt offerings and sacrifices. Bring your tithes and special gifts. Bring the offerings you promised. Bring your voluntary offerings. Bring the firstborn of your herds and flocks.
There, in the presence of the the LORD your God, you and your families must eat and rejoice. Rejoice in everything you do, because the the LORD your God has blessed you.
You are not to do what we are doing here today. Here, each person does what seems right in his own eyes.
You have not yet reached the resting place. You have not yet reached the land the the LORD your God is giving you.

But when you cross the Jordan and live in the land the the LORD your God is giving you as your own, He will give you rest. He will give you rest from all your enemies around you. Then you will live in safety.

Then you must bring everything I command you to the place the the LORD your God will choose. He will make it a home for His Name. Bring your burnt offerings and sacrifices. Bring your tithes and contributions. Bring all the best vow offerings you promise to the the LORD.
You must rejoice before the the LORD your God. Rejoice—you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite who lives in your towns. He has no share of land among you.
Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings just anywhere you see.
Instead, offer them only in the place the the LORD will choose in one of your tribes. There you must do everything I command you.

But whenever you want, you may slaughter and eat meat in any of your towns. The LORD your God has blessed you. Both people who are ritually clean and those who are unclean may eat it. Eat it just like a gazelle or a deer.
But you must not eat the blood. Pour it on the ground like water.

In your towns you may not eat the tithe of your grain, new wine, or oil. You may not eat the firstborn of your herd or flock. You may not eat any offering you promised, your voluntary offerings, or your special gifts.

Instead, you must eat them in the presence of the the LORD your God. Eat them at the place the the LORD your God will choose. Eat with your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite in your towns. Rejoice before the the LORD your God in everything you do.
Be careful not to ignore the Levite. Do this as long as you live in your land.
When the the LORD your God gives you more land, as He promised, you may crave meat. You may say, "I want to eat meat." Then you may eat meat whenever you want.

If the place the the LORD your God chooses for His Name is too far from you, you may slaughter an animal. Take it from the herd or flock the the LORD has given you. Do this as I have commanded you. Then eat it in your towns, as much as you want.
You may eat it the way you would eat a gazelle or a deer. Both clean and unclean people may eat it.
But be sure you do not eat the blood. The blood is the life. You must not eat the life with the meat.
You must not eat the blood. Pour it on the ground like water.
Do not eat it. Then things will go well for you and your children after you. You will be doing what is right in the eyes of the the LORD.
But you must take your holy things and your promised offerings. Go to the place the the LORD will choose.
Offer the meat and blood of your burnt offerings on the altar of the the LORD your God. Pour the blood of your other sacrifices beside the altar of the the LORD your God. But you may eat the meat.

Be careful to obey all these things I am commanding you. Then it will go well with you and your children after you forever. Do this when you do what is good and right in the eyes of the the LORD your God.
When the the LORD your God removes the nations before you, you will drive them out. You will settle in their land.
Be careful not to be trapped by their ways after they have been destroyed before you. Do not ask about their gods. Do not say, "How do these nations serve their gods? I will do the same."
You must not do this to the the LORD your God. They do for their gods every disgusting thing the the LORD hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire for their gods.
See that you do everything I command you. Do not add to it. Do not take anything away from it.
If a prophet or dreamer of dreams rises among you and gives you a sign or wonder,
and the sign or wonder he spoke about comes true, and he says, “Let us go after other gods—gods you have not known—and let us worship them,”
do not listen to that prophet or dreamer. The LORD your God is testing you to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
Follow the LORD your God, fear Him, keep His commands, listen to His voice, serve Him, and hold fast to Him.

That prophet or dreamer must be put to death, because he preached rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt and redeemed you from slavery, and he tried to turn you from the path the LORD your God commanded you to follow. Remove the evil from among you.
If your brother, your son or daughter, the wife you love, or your close friend secretly says, “Let us go and worship other gods”—gods neither you nor your fathers have known,
gods of the peoples around you, whether near or far, from one end of the earth to the other—
do not yield to him or listen to him. Do not pity him; do not spare him; and do not protect him.
You must put him to death. Your hand must be the first to put him to death, and then the hands of all the people.
Stone him to death, because he tried to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.
Then all Israel will hear and be afraid, and no one among you will do such an evil thing again.
If you hear it said about one of the towns the LORD your God is giving you to live in,
that worthless men have gone out from among you and have led the people of their town astray, saying, “Let us go and worship other gods”—gods you have not known—
then you must inquire, probe, and investigate thoroughly. If it is true and confirmed that this detestable thing has been done among you,
you must put to the sword all who live in that town. Destroy the town and everything in it, including its livestock, completely by the sword.
Gather all its plunder into the middle of the public square and burn the town and all its plunder as a whole burnt offering to the LORD your God. It must remain a ruin forever, never to be rebuilt.
None of the devoted things shall stick to your hands, so that the LORD may turn from His fierce anger and show you mercy, have compassion on you, and increase you as He promised your fathers.
For you will be obeying the LORD your God by keeping all His commands that I am giving you today, and by doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
You are children of the LORD your God. Do not cut yourselves or shave the front of your heads to mourn for the dead.
For you are a holy people to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you to be His treasured possession out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
You must not eat anything detestable.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
You may eat any animal that has a split hoof divided in two and that chews the cud.

But of those that chew the cud or have a split hoof, you must not eat these: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger. Although they chew the cud, they do not have a split hoof, so they are unclean for you.
The pig is also unclean for you, because it has a split hoof but does not chew the cud. You must not eat its meat or touch its dead body.
Of all the creatures in the water, you may eat anything with fins and scales.
But you must not eat anything that does not have fins and scales; it is unclean for you.
You may eat any clean bird.
But these you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite, the falcon, any kind of kite,
the ostrich, the owl, the seagull, any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
the pelican, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
All flying insects that swarm are unclean for you; do not eat them.
You may eat any clean flying creature.

You must not eat anything you find dead. You may give it to the foreigner in your cities, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner. For you are a holy people to the LORD your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Be sure to set aside a tenth of all the grain your field produces each year.

You must eat the tenth of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the LORD your God at the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
But if the distance is too great for you to carry it, because the place the LORD your God will choose to put His Name is too far away, and the LORD your God has blessed you,
then you may exchange it for money. Take the money in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God will choose.
Then spend the money on whatever you want: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything else you desire. Eat there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household.
Do not neglect the Levite in your cities, because he has no portion or inheritance among you.
At the end of every three years, bring out the entire tenth of your produce for that year and store it in your cities.

Then the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance among you, along with the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow in your cities, may come and eat and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
At the end of every seven years, you must cancel debts.
This is how the release works: Every creditor must release what he has lent to his neighbor. He must not press his neighbor or brother for payment, because the the LORD's release has been announced.
You may collect from a foreigner, but your hand must release what belongs to your brother.
There should be no poor among you, because the the LORD your God will richly bless you in the land the the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
If you carefully obey the the LORD your God and are careful to follow all these commands I am giving you today,
then the the LORD your God will bless you, as He promised. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.

If there is a poor person among you—one of your brothers—in any of your towns in the land the the LORD your God is giving you, you must not harden your heart or close your hand against your poor brother.
Instead, you must open your hand wide to him and lend him enough to meet his need.

Be careful not to think this evil thought: "The seventh year, the year of release, is near," so that you are stingy toward your poor brother and give him nothing. Then he may cry out to the the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
You must surely give to him, and your heart must not be sad when you give, because the the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you do.
There will always be poor people in the land. That is why I command you to open your hand to your brother, to the needy and the poor in your land.
If a Hebrew man or woman is sold to you and serves you six years, in the seventh year you must let him go free.
When you send him away free, do not send him away empty-handed.
Give him generously from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. Give to him as the the LORD your God has blessed you.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and the the LORD your God redeemed you. That is why I give you this command today.
But if he says to you, "I do not want to leave you," because he loves you and your household and is well off with you,
then you must take an awl and push it through his ear into the door, and he will be your servant for life. Do the same for your female servant.
Do not be upset when you send him away free, because for six years he has served you twice as much as a hired worker would. The the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
Set apart to the the LORD your God every firstborn male from your herds and flocks. Do not work the firstborn of your ox, and do not shear the firstborn of your sheep.
You and your household must eat it each year before the the LORD your God in the place He chooses.
But if it has a defect—lame or blind or any serious flaw—do not sacrifice it to the the LORD your God.
You may eat it in your towns. The unclean and the clean may eat it alike, like gazelle or deer.
But do not eat its blood; pour it out on the ground like water.
Watch for the month of Abib, and celebrate the Passover for the LORD your God. In that month, the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt at night.
Sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God from your flock and herd. Do it at the place the LORD chooses for His name to live.

Do not eat bread with yeast in it with the Passover. For seven days eat flatbread, the bread of hardship, because you left Egypt in a hurry. This will help you remember the day you left Egypt for as long as you live.
For seven days, no yeast should be seen anywhere in your land. Also, none of the meat from the animal you sacrifice on the first evening may be left overnight until morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any town the LORD your God gives you.
Instead, sacrifice it at the place the LORD your God chooses for His name. Do it in the evening, when the sun goes down, at the time you left Egypt.
Cook it and eat it there, at the place the LORD your God chooses. Then in the morning, turn and go back to your tents.
Eat flatbread for six days. On the seventh day, hold a special meeting for the LORD your God. Do not do any work that day.
Count seven weeks. Start counting when the sickle is first put to the standing grain.
Then celebrate the Feast of Weeks for the LORD your God. Give a freewill offering from your hand, as much as the LORD your God blesses you.

Rejoice before the LORD your God at the place He chooses for His name. You, your sons, your daughters, your male and female servants, the Levite in your towns, and the stranger, the orphan, and the widow among you should all rejoice.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. Keep and follow these rules.
Celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days, after you gather grain from your threshing floor and wine from your winepress.
Rejoice in your feast. You, your sons, your daughters, your male and female servants, the Levite, and the stranger, the orphan, and the widow in your towns should all rejoice.
For seven days, celebrate this feast for the LORD your God at the place He chooses. The LORD your God will bless you in all your crops and in all the work of your hands. You will be very happy.

Three times a year, all your men must appear before the LORD your God at the place He chooses: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles. No one should appear before the LORD empty-handed.
Each person should give as much as he can, based on the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
Appoint judges and officers for your tribes in all the towns the LORD your God gives you. They must judge the people fairly.
Do not twist justice. Do not show favoritism. Do not take a bribe, because a bribe blinds the wise and twists the words of good people.
Follow justice and only justice, so that you may live and take the land the LORD your God gives you.
Do not plant an Asherah pole beside the altar of the LORD your God.
Do not set up a sacred stone, which the LORD your God hates.
Do not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has a defect or any flaw. That is an abomination to the LORD your God.
If a man or woman among you in one of your towns that the LORD your God gives you is found doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God by breaking His covenant,
and that person has gone and served other gods and worshiped them, or the sun or the moon or all the host of heaven, which I have not commanded,
and it has been told to you, and you have heard it and searched carefully, and behold, the thing is true and certain, that this abomination has been done in Israel,
then you shall bring out to your gates that man or woman who has done this evil thing, and you shall stone them with stones so that they die.
A person must be put to death only on the testimony of two or three witnesses. He must not be put to death on the testimony of just one witness.
The witnesses must be the first to put him to death, and then all the people. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.

If a case is too hard for you to judge—between one case of bloodshed and another, between one legal ruling and another, or between one injury and another—these disputed matters in your towns, then you shall arise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
You shall come to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office in those days, and you shall inquire of them, and they shall declare to you the sentence of judgment.
You shall act according to the decision they announce to you from that place the the LORD will choose. Be careful to do everything they instruct you.
According to the law they teach you and according to the judgment they tell you, you shall do. You must not turn aside from what they declare to you, to the right or to the left.
But the man who deliberately refuses to obey the priest who stands there to serve the LORD your God, or the judge, that man shall die. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.
Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and they will not act so arrogantly again.
When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, take possession of it and settle there, and then you say, "Let me set a king over me, like all the nations around me."
You must be sure to set over you a king whom the LORD your God chooses. You must appoint a king from among your brothers. You may not put a foreigner over you, someone who is not your brother.
He must not get many horses for himself, and he must not make the people return to Egypt to get more horses, for the LORD has said to you, "You must never return that way again."
He must not take many wives for himself, or his heart will turn away. He must not collect large amounts of silver and gold for himself.
When he sits on his royal throne, he is to write for himself a copy of this law on a scroll, from the copy kept by the Levitical priests.
He must keep it with him and read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God and carefully follow all the words of this law and these statutes.

Then his heart will not become proud and think he is better than his brothers, and he will not turn from this command to the right or to the left. Then he and his sons will rule for a long time over his kingdom in Israel.

The Levite priests—that is, the whole tribe of Levi—will have no share or land of their own among the Israelites. They will eat the offerings made by fire to the LORD, because that is their inheritance.
They will have no inheritance among their brothers. The LORD is their inheritance, just as He promised them.
This is what the priests are owed by the people who bring a sacrifice, whether a bull or a sheep: they must give the priest the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach.
You must give him the first share of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the first wool sheared from your flock.
For the LORD your God has chosen him and his sons from all your tribes to stand and serve in the LORD’s name for all time.
If a Levite moves from any of your towns in Israel where he lives and comes with all his heart to the place the LORD will choose,
he may serve in the name of the LORD his God, like all his fellow Levites who serve there before the LORD.
They will eat equal shares, except for what he receives from selling his family’s property.
When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn to follow the hateful practices of those nations.
Let no one be found among you who sacrifices his son or daughter in the fire, or who practices fortune-telling or sorcery, or reads omens, or does witchcraft.
No one among you should cast spells, or be a medium or someone who speaks with spirits, or ask the dead for answers.
Anyone who does these things is hateful to the LORD. Because of these hateful practices, the LORD your God is driving those nations out before you.
You must be blameless before the LORD your God.
The nations you are driving out listen to fortune-tellers, but as for you, the LORD your God has not allowed you to do so.
The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to him.

This is what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day the people gathered, when you said, "Let us not hear the voice of the LORD our God or see this great fire anymore, so that we will not die."
Then the LORD said to me, "They have spoken well.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put My words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
I will hold accountable anyone who does not listen to My words that the prophet speaks in My name.
But if a prophet speaks on his own authority in My name a word I did not command him to speak, or speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet must be put to death."
You may ask in your heart, "How can we know when a message has not been spoken by the LORD?"
When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the message does not happen or come true, that is a message the LORD has not spoken. The prophet spoke on his own authority. Do not be afraid of him.
When the LORD your God destroys the nations whose land the LORD your God gives you, and you take over their land and live in their cities and houses,
set apart three cities for yourself in the middle of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to own.
Build roads to them, and divide into three parts the land that the LORD your God gives you, so that anyone who kills someone can run to one of these cities and be safe.
This is the rule for the killer who runs there to stay alive: He killed his neighbor without meaning to, and he did not hate him before.

For example, if a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and as he swings his axe to cut down a tree, the iron head slips off the handle and hits his neighbor and kills him, that man may run to one of these cities and live.
Otherwise, the avenger of blood might chase him while angry, catch him because the road is long, and kill him, even though he does not deserve death because he did not hate his neighbor before.
That is why I command you: Set apart three cities for yourself.
If the LORD your God makes your land larger, as He swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land He promised your fathers,
and if you carefully keep all these commands I am giving you today—to love the LORD your God and walk in His ways all your life—then you must add three more cities to these three.
Do this so innocent blood will not be shed in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and so you will not be guilty of bloodshed.
But if a man hates his neighbor, hides and waits for him, attacks him and kills him, and then runs to one of these cities,
the elders of his city must send for him, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die.
Do not feel sorry for him. Remove the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, and it will go well with you.
Do not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, the one set by your ancestors, in the land you will inherit, which the LORD your God is giving you to own.
One witness is not enough to convict a person of any crime or sin. A matter must be settled by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
If a witness comes forward to accuse someone of wrongdoing,
both people in the dispute must stand before the LORD, before the priests and judges who are serving at that time.
The judges must investigate carefully. If the witness is lying and has given false testimony against his brother,
then do to him what he planned to do to his brother. Remove the evil from among you.
The rest will hear about it and be afraid, and they will not do such an evil thing among you again.
Do not feel sorry for him: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army bigger than you, don't be afraid of them. The LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt, is with you.
When you get close to the battle, the priest will come forward and speak to the people.
He will say to them, "Listen, Israel! Today you are getting close to fight your enemies. Don't let your courage fail. Don't be afraid, don't panic, and don't be terrified of them.
The LORD your God is He who goes with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you."

Then the officers will speak to the people. They will say, "Is there any man who has built a new house but hasn't dedicated it? He should go home so he won't die in battle and someone else dedicate it.
Is there any man who has planted a vineyard but hasn't enjoyed its fruit? He should go home so he won't die in battle and someone else enjoy its fruit.
Is there any man who has promised to marry a woman but hasn't married her? He should go home so he won't die in battle and someone else marry her."
The officers will also say, "Is there any man who is afraid and has a weak heart? He should go home so he won't make his brothers lose courage too."
When the officers finish speaking to the people, they will appoint commanders to lead the army.
When you get close to a city to fight it, first offer it peace.
If it answers you with peace and opens its gates to you, then all the people in it will be forced to work for you and serve you.
But if it doesn't make peace with you and fights against you, then lay siege to it.
When the the LORD your God hands it over to you, kill all the men in it with the sword.
But you may take the women, children, animals, and everything else in the city as plunder. You may eat the goods taken from your enemies, which the the LORD your God has given you.
Do this to all the cities that are very far from you and don't belong to these nations.
But in the cities of these peoples that the the LORD your God is giving you as your own land, don't let anything that breathes survive.
You must completely destroy them—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—just as the the LORD your God commanded you.
Do this so they won't teach you to copy all the terrible things they do for their gods, and so you won't sin against the the LORD your God.

When you surround a city for a long time to fight and capture it, don't destroy its trees by swinging an axe on them. You may eat from them, but don't cut them down. Are trees in the field human, that they should be besieged by you?
You may destroy and cut down only trees that you know aren't food trees. Use them to build siege works against the city that is fighting you until it falls.
If someone is found killed and lying in a field in the land the LORD your God is giving you to own, and no one knows who killed him,
your elders and judges must go out and measure the distance from the body to the cities around it.
The elders of the city closest to the body must take a young cow that has never been worked and never pulled a yoke.
They must bring it down to a valley with running water that has not been plowed or planted, and break the cow's neck there.
The priests, the sons of Levi, must come forward, because the LORD your God chose them to serve Him and to bless in the LORD's name, and by their decision every dispute and every assault is settled.
All the elders of that city closest to the body must wash their hands over the cow whose neck was broken in the valley.
They must say, “Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
Forgive, O LORD, Your people Israel whom You have redeemed, and do not hold the guilt of innocent blood against Your people Israel.” Then the bloodshed will be forgiven.
So you will remove the guilt of innocent blood from among you, because you are doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and the LORD your God hands them over to you, you will take captives.
If you see a beautiful woman among the captives and want her, you may take her as your wife.
Bring her into your home. She must shave her head and trim her nails.

She must take off the clothes she wore as a captive. Then she may live in your house and mourn her father and mother for a full month. After that, you may sleep with her and be her husband, and she will be your wife.
If you are not pleased with her, let her go wherever she wishes. But you must not sell her for money, and you must not treat her like a slave, because you have humiliated her.
If a man has two wives, one he loves and one he hates, and both have sons, and the firstborn son belongs to the wife he hates,
then on the day he divides his property among his sons, he may not treat the son of the loved wife as the firstborn instead of the firstborn son of the hated wife.

He must recognize the firstborn son of the hated wife by giving him a double share of everything he owns, because that son is the first sign of his strength. The right of the firstborn belongs to him.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his father or mother, and even when they correct him he will not listen,
his father and mother must take hold of him and bring him to the elders of his city, at the gate of his town.
They must say to the elders, “This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey us. He is a glutton and a drunkard.”
Then all the men of his city must stone him to death. You must remove the evil from among you, and all Israel will hear and be afraid.
If a man commits a sin worthy of death and is put to death, and you hang his body on a tree,

his body must not stay on the tree overnight. You must bury him that same day, because a person hung on a tree is under God's curse. Do not make your land unclean, which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
If you see your brother's ox or sheep wandering away, do not pretend you do not see them. Be sure to take them back to your brother.
If your brother is not nearby or you do not know him, bring the animal to your home and keep it with you until he comes looking for it. Then give it back to him.
Do the same for his donkey, his clothes, or anything else your brother loses and you find. Do not act like you did not see it.
If you see your brother's donkey or ox fall down on the road, do not ignore it. Help him get it back on its feet.
A woman must not wear men's clothing, and a man must not wear women's clothing. Anyone who does this is detestable to the LORD your God.
If you come across a bird's nest along the road, in a tree or on the ground, and the mother is sitting on the young or on the eggs, do not take the mother with the young.
You may take the young, but let the mother go free. Then things will go well for you, and you will live a long time.
When you build a new house, put a railing around your roof. Then you will not be guilty if someone falls from it.
Do not plant two kinds of seed in your vineyard. If you do, the whole crop will be unfit to use, both the seed you planted and the fruit of the vineyard.
