Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
Do not wear clothing made of wool and linen woven together.
Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
If a man marries a woman and later hates her,
and slanders her by saying, "I married this woman, but when I was with her I found she was not a virgin."
Then the young woman's father and mother must bring proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate.
The young woman's father must say to the elders, "I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, but he hates her.

Now he has accused her of shameful things and says, 'I found that your daughter was not a virgin.' But here is proof that my daughter was a virgin." Then they must spread the cloth before the elders of the city.
The elders of that city must take the man and punish him.

They must fine him one hundred shekels of silver and give the money to the young woman's father, because the man gave an Israelite virgin a bad name. She must remain his wife, and he may never divorce her.
But if the charge is true and the young woman was not a virgin,

they must bring her to the door of her father's house. The men of her city must stone her to death, because she did a disgraceful thing in Israel by being unfaithful while still in her father's house. You must remove the evil from among you.
If a man is caught sleeping with another man's wife, both the man and the woman must die. You must remove this evil from Israel.
If a man meets a young woman who is engaged to another man, and he sleeps with her in the city,

bring both of them to the gate of that city and stone them to death. Stone the young woman because she did not cry out for help in the city, and stone the man because he violated another man's wife. You must remove the evil from among you.
But if a man meets an engaged young woman in the countryside and forces her and sleeps with her, only the man who slept with her must die.
Do nothing to the young woman, because she has done nothing deserving death. This case is like a man attacking and murdering his neighbor.
The man found her in the countryside, and the engaged young woman cried out, but no one was there to save her.
If a man meets a young woman who is not engaged, and he seizes her and sleeps with her, and they are found out,
the man who slept with her must pay the young woman's father fifty shekels of silver. She must become his wife, because he violated her. He may never divorce her.
A man must not marry his father's wife or sleep with her.
No man whose private parts are crushed or cut off may enter the assembly of the LORD.
No one born from an unlawful union may enter the assembly of the LORD, and none of his descendants may enter, even to the tenth generation.
No Ammonite or Moabite may ever enter the assembly of the LORD, not even in the tenth generation.
This is because they did not meet you with food and water on your way out of Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram Naharaim to curse you.
Yet the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam. Instead, the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you.
Never seek their peace or prosperity as long as you live.
Do not hate an Edomite, because he is your brother. Do not hate an Egyptian, because you were a foreigner in his land.
The children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.
When you go out to fight your enemies, keep yourself from every evil thing.
If a man among you becomes unclean because of a discharge during the night, he must leave the camp and stay outside it.
In the evening he must wash with water, and when the sun goes down he may return to the camp.
You must have a place outside the camp where you can go to relieve yourself.
You must carry a digging tool with your gear. When you relieve yourself, dig a hole and cover up your waste.
For the LORD your God walks through your camp to protect you and hand your enemies over to you. Your camp must be holy, so that He does not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.
Do not hand over to his master a slave who has escaped to you.
He may live among you wherever he chooses, in any of your towns he likes. Do not mistreat him.
No Israelite man or woman may be a temple prostitute.
You must not bring a prostitute's earnings or the price of a dog into the house of the LORD your God to pay any vow, because both are disgusting to the LORD your God.
Do not charge interest to your brother on money, food, or anything else that can earn interest.
You may charge interest to a foreigner, but not to your brother, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything you do in the land you are entering to possess.
If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not delay in keeping it, because He will certainly require it from you, and it will be counted as sin against you.
But if you do not make a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
Be careful to do what you have promised, because you freely vowed to the LORD your God with your own mouth.
When you enter your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you want, but you must not put any in your container.
When you enter your neighbor's grainfield, you may pluck heads of grain with your hand, but you must not use a sickle on your neighbor's standing grain.
If a man marries a woman and she does not please him because he finds something shameful in her, he may write her a certificate of divorce, put it in her hand, and send her away from his house.
She leaves his house, goes away, and becomes another man's wife.
If her second husband hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her away from his house, or if that second husband dies,

then her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her back as his wife after she has been made unclean. That is detestable to the LORD. You must not bring sin on the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
When a man takes a new wife, he must not go out with the army or be given any other duty. For one year he is to stay home and make his wife happy.
Do not take a hand mill or an upper millstone as a pledge, because that would be taking a person's livelihood as a pledge.
If a man is found kidnapping one of his fellow Israelites and treats him as a slave or sells him, that thief must die. You must remove the evil from among you.
In cases of leprous disease, be very careful to do exactly all that the Levitical priests instruct you. Follow carefully what I commanded them.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out of Egypt.
When you make a loan of any kind to your neighbor, you must not go into his house to take his pledge.
You must stand outside, and the man to whom you lend must bring the pledge out to you.
If he is a poor man, you must not go to sleep while keeping his pledge.
You must surely return the pledge to him when the sun goes down, so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you. That will be counted as righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
You must not cheat a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or a foreigner living in your land in your towns.
You must pay him his wages the same day, before the sun goes down, because he is poor and needs the money to live. Otherwise he may cry out against you to the LORD, and you will be guilty of sin.
Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers. Each person must be put to death for his own sin.
You must not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and you must not take a widow's garment as a pledge.
You must remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.

When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a bundle of grain in the field, you must not go back to get it. It will belong to the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive tree, you must not go over the branches again. It will belong to the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
When you pick grapes from your vineyard, you must not go over it again. It will belong to the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
You must remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
If two men have a disagreement and go to court, the judges will decide who is right and who is wrong.
If the guilty man deserves a beating, the judge will order him to lie down and be beaten in front of him. The number of blows must match his crime.
He may receive up to forty blows, but no more. If you give more, your brother would be humiliated in front of you.
Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing grain.
If brothers live together and one of them dies without a son, his widow must not marry someone outside the family. Her husband's brother should marry her and do his duty as a brother-in-law.
The first son she has will carry the name of the dead brother, so his name will not disappear from Israel.

But if the man does not want to marry his brother's widow, she must go to the elders at the town gate and say, "My brother-in-law refuses to keep his brother's name alive in Israel. He will not do his duty for me."
The elders of his town will call for him and talk to him. If he stands firm and says, "I do not want to marry her,"

then his brother's widow will go up to him in front of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and say, "This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's family."
After that, his family in Israel will be called "the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off."
If two men are fighting and the wife of one steps in to save her husband from the man hitting him, and she grabs the attacker by his private parts,
cut off her hand. Do not show her any mercy.
Do not keep two different weights in your bag—one heavy and one light.
Do not keep two different measures in your house—one large and one small.
Keep a full and fair weight and a full and fair measure. Then you will live a long time in the land the the LORD your God gives you.
For everyone who does these things, everyone who acts unfairly, is detestable to the the LORD your God.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the road when you came out of Egypt.
He met you on the way when you were tired and worn out. He attacked everyone who was lagging behind you, and he did not fear God.

When the the LORD your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land the the LORD your God is giving you to own, you must wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget.
When you come into the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and live in it,

you shall take some of the firstfruits of all the produce of the ground from your land that the LORD your God gives you, and put it in a basket. Then you shall go to the place the LORD your God chooses to make His name dwell.
You shall go to the priest who is in office in those days and say, “I declare today to the LORD your God that I have come into the land the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.”
The priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it before the altar of the LORD your God.

Then you shall answer and say before the LORD your God, “My father was a wandering Aramean. He went down into Egypt with only a few people and lived there, and there he became a great nation, mighty and numerous.
The Egyptians treated us badly and oppressed us, and they put hard work on us.
We cried out to the LORD, the God of our fathers, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our suffering, our hard work, and our oppression.
The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, and with signs and wonders.
He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Now look, I have brought the firstfruits of the produce of the ground that the LORD gave me. I set it before the LORD your God and bow down before the LORD your God.”
You and the Levite and the foreigner among you shall rejoice in all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household.

When you have finished setting aside a tenth of all your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, you shall give it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so they can eat and be full in your towns.

Then you shall say before the LORD your God, “I have removed the holy portion from my house, and I have also given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, just as You commanded me. I have not broken Your commands or forgotten them.

I have not eaten any of it while mourning, and I have not removed any of it while unclean, and I have not given any of it for the dead. I have obeyed the voice of the LORD my God. I have done everything You commanded me.
Look down from Your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the land You gave us, as You promised our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.”
Today the LORD your God commands you to follow these statutes and judgments. Keep them and do them with all your heart and all your soul.
Today you have declared that the LORD is your God, and that you will walk in His ways, keep His statutes, His commands, and His judgments, and listen to His voice.
Today the LORD has declared that you are His people, His treasured possession, as He said, and that you are to keep all His commands.
He will make you higher than all the nations He has made, for praise, for a name, and for honor, and you will be a holy people to the LORD your God, as He said.
Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, “Keep every command I give you today.”
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land the LORD your God gives you, set up large stones for yourself and coat them with plaster.

Write on them all the words of this law when you cross over, so that you may enter the land the LORD your God gives you, a land rich with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, said to you.
When you cross the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I command you today, and coat them with plaster.
Build an altar there to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. Do not use iron tools on them.
Build the altar of the LORD your God with whole stones, and offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
Sacrifice peace offerings there, eat them, and rejoice before the LORD your God.
Write all the words of this law on the stones very clearly.
Moses and the priests, who are Levites, spoke to all Israel, saying, “Be quiet and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.
So obey the voice of the LORD your God and do His commands and rules that I give you today.”
That same day Moses commanded the people, saying,
“When you cross the Jordan, these tribes shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
These tribes shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.”
The Levites shall say in a loud voice to all the men of Israel:
“Cursed is the man who makes a carved image or a metal image, something the LORD hates, made by a craftsman's hands, and sets it up in secret.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who dishonors his father or his mother.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who moves his neighbor's boundary stone.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who misleads a blind person on the road.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who twists justice for a foreigner, an orphan, or a widow.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father's wife and shames his father.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with any animal.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his sister, whether she is his father's daughter or his mother's daughter.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his mother-in-law.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who attacks his neighbor in secret.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who does not keep the words of this law by doing them.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
If you fully obey the the LORD your God and carefully follow all His commands that I am giving you today, the the LORD your God will put you above all the nations on earth.
All these blessings will come to you and catch up with you, because you obey the the LORD your God.
You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country.
Your children, your crops, and your animals will be blessed.
Your basket and your kneading bowl will be blessed.
You will be blessed when you come in and when you go out.
The The LORD will defeat your enemies who attack you. They will come at you one way and run away seven ways.
The The LORD will command His blessing on your stores and on everything you do. The The LORD your God will bless you in the land He is giving you.
The The LORD will make you His holy people, as He promised, if you keep His commands and walk in His ways.
Then all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the the LORD's name, and they will fear you.
The The LORD will give you plenty of good things: children, animals, and crops in the land He promised your fathers.
He will open the skies to send rain on your land at the right time and bless all your work. You will lend to many nations, but you will not need to borrow.
The The LORD will make you the head, not the tail. You will be on top and not on the bottom, if you obey the commands of the the LORD your God that I am giving you today.
Do not turn aside to the right or left from any of the commands I am giving you today, and do not follow other gods to serve them.
But if you do not obey the the LORD your God and carefully follow all His commands and rules that I am giving you today, all these curses will come on you and catch up with you.
You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the country.
Your basket and your kneading bowl will be cursed.
Your children, your crops, your calves, and your lambs will be cursed.
You will be cursed when you come in and when you go out.
The The LORD will send curses, confusion, and trouble on everything you do, until you are destroyed and quickly lost because of your evil actions in leaving Him.
The The LORD will make disease stick to you until He removes you from the land you are entering to possess.
The The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever, inflammation, burning heat, sword, blight, and mildew. They will chase you until you die.
The sky above you will be like bronze, and the ground beneath you will be like iron.
The The LORD will turn the rain on your land into dust and powder. It will fall from the sky until you are destroyed.
The The LORD will let your enemies defeat you. You will march out against them one way and flee seven ways. You will become a warning to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your dead body will be food for birds and wild animals, and no one will scare them away.
The The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, rash, and itch that cannot be healed.
The The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion of heart.
At noon you will feel around like a blind person in the dark, and you will not succeed in anything. You will be robbed and cheated all your days, with no one to save you.
You will be engaged to a woman, but another man will sleep with her. You will build a house but not live in it. You will plant a vineyard but not enjoy its fruit.
Your ox will be killed before your eyes, but you will not eat it. Your donkey will be stolen from you and not returned. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and no one will save you.
Your sons and daughters will be given to another people. You will look for them all day with failing eyes, and you will have no power to help.
A people you do not know will eat the fruit of your land and all your hard work. You will be crushed and treated badly all your days.
The sights you see will drive you mad.
The The LORD will strike you with painful boils from the soles of your feet to the top of your head, boils that cannot be healed.
The The LORD will send you and your king to a nation neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will serve other gods made of wood and stone.
You will become a horror, an example, and a joke among all the peoples where the the LORD sends you.
You will plant much seed in the field, but harvest little, because locusts will eat it.
You will plant and care for vineyards, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them.
You will have olive trees everywhere in your land, but you will not use the oil, because your olives will drop off.
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not stay with you, because they will be taken captive.
Locusts will take over all your trees and crops.
The foreigner among you will rise higher and higher, while you sink lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.
All these curses will come on you, chase you, and catch you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the the LORD your God or keep His commands and rules.
They will be a sign and wonder against you and your children forever.
Because you did not serve the the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart, even though you had plenty of everything, you will serve your enemies whom the the LORD sends against you.
You will be hungry, thirsty, naked, and lacking everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until He destroys you.
The The LORD will bring a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, flying like an eagle. It will be a nation whose language you do not understand.
It will be a fierce nation that shows no respect for the old and no pity for the young.
It will eat the young of your animals and the fruit of your land until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine, or oil, no calves or lambs, until it has destroyed you.

It will surround you in all your cities and all your land, until your high, fortified walls that you trust in come down. It will besiege you in all your cities throughout the land the the LORD your God has given you.
In the terrible trouble of being surrounded by your enemy, you will eat your own children, the flesh of your sons and daughters whom the the LORD your God has given you.
The most gentle and kind man among you will have a hard heart toward his brother, his wife, and his remaining children.
He will not share with any of them the flesh of his children that he is eating, because he has nothing left in the terrible trouble your enemy brings on you in all your cities.
The most delicate and gentle woman among you, who would not even put her foot on the ground because she was so pampered, will look with evil eyes at her husband, her son, and her daughter.
She will secretly eat her afterbirth and the children she gives birth to, because she has nothing else in the terrible trouble your enemy brings on you in your cities.
If you are not careful to obey all the words of this law written in this book, and if you do not fear this glorious and awesome name, the the LORD your God,
then the the LORD will send terrible plagues on you and your children. They will be long-lasting and severe, sicknesses and diseases that last.
He will bring back on you all the diseases of Egypt that you feared, and they will cling to you.
The The LORD will also bring on you every sickness and plague not written in this Book of the Law, until you are destroyed.
You may have been as many as the stars in the sky, but only a few of you will be left, because you did not obey the the LORD your God.
Just as the the LORD was glad to do good to you and make you grow, so He will be glad to destroy you and wipe you out. You will be pulled out of the land you are entering to possess.
The The LORD will scatter you among all the peoples from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve other gods of wood and stone that neither you nor your fathers have known.
Among those nations you will find no rest, and your foot will have no resting place. The The LORD will give you an anxious heart, your failing eyes, and a sick soul.
Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will be afraid night and day and will not trust that you will live.
In the morning you will say, "If only it were evening!" and in the evening you will say, "If only it were morning!" because of the fear in your heart and the sights your eyes see.
The The LORD will send you back to Egypt by ship, by the way I told you that you would never see again. There you will try to sell yourselves to your enemies as slaves, but no one will buy you.
These are the words of the covenant the the LORD commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in Moab, besides the covenant He made with them at Horeb. “
Your eyes have seen all that the the LORD did in Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his officials, and to all his land.
With your own eyes you saw those great trials, those signs, and those great wonders.
But to this day the the LORD has not given you a mind to understand, or eyes to see, or ears to hear.
The The LORD has led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes have not worn out, and your sandals have not worn out on your feet.
You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink. I did this so you would know that I am the the LORD your God. “
When you reached this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to fight us, but we defeated them.
We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
So keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may succeed in everything you do. “
All of you are standing today before the the LORD your God—your leaders, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, every man in Israel.
along with your children and wives, and the foreigners in your camps, from those who cut your wood to those who carry your water.
You are standing here to enter into the covenant of the the LORD your God, the covenant the the LORD is making with you today, along with its curses.
He is doing this to make you His people today and to be your God, as He promised you and as He swore to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. “
I am making this covenant and this oath not only with you who are standing here with us today before the the LORD our God,
but also with those who are not here with us today. “
You know how we lived in Egypt and how we passed through the nations on the way.
You saw their disgusting things and their idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold. “
Make sure no man or woman, family or tribe among you today turns away from the the LORD your God to worship the gods of those nations. Make sure no root among you grows into bitter poison.

When someone like that hears the words of this curse, he will bless himself and say, ‘I will be safe, even though I keep going my own way.’ This will bring disaster on the watered land as well as the dry.

The The LORD will never be willing to forgive him. Instead, the the LORD’s anger and jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse written in this book will fall on him. The The LORD will erase his name from under heaven.
The The LORD will set him apart from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law. “
Your children who come after you, and foreigners from far away, will see the troubles that have hit this land and the sicknesses the the LORD has sent on it.

The whole land will be a wasteland of burning sulfur and salt, with nothing planted and nothing growing, not even grass. It will be like Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the the LORD destroyed in His fierce anger. “
All the nations will ask, ‘Why has the the LORD done this to this land? Why this fierce, burning anger?’
And people will answer, ‘It is because they abandoned the covenant of the the LORD, the God of their ancestors, the covenant He made with them when He brought them out of Egypt.’
They went and worshiped other gods and bowed down to them—gods they did not know and that the the LORD had not given them.
So the the LORD’s anger burned against this land, and He brought on it all the curses written in this book.
In His fierce anger and great wrath the the LORD uprooted them from their land and banished them to another land, as we see today. “
The secret things belong to the the LORD our God, but the things revealed belong to us and to our children forever, so that we may follow all the words of this law.”
When all these things happen to you—the blessing and the curse I placed before you—and you take them to heart among all the nations where the LORD your God has sent you,
and when you and your children return to the LORD your God and obey His voice with all your heart and all your soul, just as I am commanding you today,
then the LORD your God will bring back your fortunes, show you mercy, and gather you again from all the nations where He scattered you.
Even if you are thrown to the farthest edge of the sky, the LORD your God will gather you from there and bring you back.
The LORD your God will bring you to the land your fathers owned, and you will own it. He will make you more successful and more numerous than your fathers.
The LORD your God will change your heart and the hearts of your children, so you can love the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul, and so you can live.
The LORD your God will put all these curses on your enemies, on those who hate you, and on those who chased you.
Then you will obey the LORD again and keep all His commands that I am giving you today.

The LORD your God will help you succeed in everything you do—in the fruit of your womb, your animals, and your crops. The LORD will once again be happy with you and make you prosperous, just as He was happy with your fathers.
This will happen if you obey the LORD your God by keeping His commands and rules written in this Book of the Law, and if you turn to the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
This command I am giving you today is not too hard for you, and it is not out of your reach.
It is not up in heaven, so you would say, “Who will go up to heaven for us and get it and tell it to us, so we can obey it?”
It is not across the sea, so you would say, “Who will cross the sea for us and get it and tell it to us, so we can obey it?”
No, the word is very close to you. It is in your mouth and in your heart, so you can obey it.
Look, today I have set before you life and good, and death and evil.
If you love the LORD your God, walk in His ways, and keep His commands, rules, and laws, then you will live and grow. The LORD your God will bless you in the land you are going in to own.
But if your heart turns away, and you do not listen, and you are led away to bow down to other gods and serve them,
I tell you today that you will surely be destroyed. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to enter and own.
I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. So choose life, so that you and your descendants may live.

Love the LORD your God, obey His voice, and hold fast to Him, because He is your life and the length of your days. He will let you live in the land the LORD promised to give to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Then Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
He said, "I am now one hundred twenty years old. I can no longer go out and come in. the LORD has said to me, 'You shall not cross this Jordan.'
The LORD your God Himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will take their land. Joshua will also go ahead of you, as the LORD has spoken.
The LORD will do to them what He did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, whom He destroyed along with their land.
The LORD will hand them over to you, and you must do to them exactly as I have commanded you.
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified of them, because the LORD your God goes with you. He will never leave you or forsake you."

Then Moses called Joshua and said to him where all Israel could see, "Be strong and courageous, because you will go with this people into the land the LORD promised to give their fathers, and you will give it to them as their land.
The LORD Himself goes before you. He will be with you. He will never leave you or forsake you. Do not be afraid or discouraged."
So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant, and to all the elders of Israel.
Then Moses commanded them, "At the end of every seven years, at the set time in the year of release, during the Feast of Tabernacles,
when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God in the place He chooses, you must read this law out loud so all Israel can hear it.
Gather the people—men, women, children, and the foreigners living in your towns—so they may hear and learn to fear the LORD your God and carefully obey all the words of this law.
Then their children, who do not know it, will hear and learn to fear the LORD your God as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take."

Then the LORD said to Moses, "Look, the time for your death is near. Call Joshua and stand together at the Tent of Meeting, so I can give him his orders." So Moses and Joshua went and stood at the Tent of Meeting.
The LORD appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the cloud stood above the entrance.

The LORD said to Moses, "You are about to lie down with your fathers. These people will rise up and be unfaithful to Me by chasing the gods of the land they are entering. They will leave Me and break the covenant I made with them.

On that day My anger will burn against them. I will leave them and hide My face from them, and they will be destroyed. Many troubles and disasters will come on them. On that day they will say, 'Have not these disasters found us because our God is not with us?'
I will surely hide My face on that day because of all the evil they have done, for they will have turned to other gods.
"So now write down this song and teach it to the Israelites. Put it in their mouths, so this song will be a witness for Me against them.

When I bring them into the land I promised their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey, they will eat and be full and grow comfortable. Then they will turn to other gods and worship them. They will reject Me and break My covenant.

When many troubles and disasters come on them, this song will speak against them, because it will not be forgotten by their children. I know what they plan to do, even before I bring them into the land I promised to give them."
So that same day Moses wrote down this song and taught it to the Israelites.
Then the LORD gave Joshua son of Nun his orders and said, "Be strong and courageous, because you will bring the Israelites into the land I promised to give them, and I will be with you."
When Moses finished writing all the words of this law in a book, from beginning to end,
he commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant,
"Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, so it will stay there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebellion and your stubborn neck. Even while I am still alive with you, you have been rebelling against the LORD. How much more will you do so after I die!"
"Bring together for me all the elders of your tribes and your officers, so I can speak these words to them and call heaven and earth to witness against them.

For I know that after I die you will become completely corrupt and turn away from the path I commanded you to follow. In the days to come, disaster will come on you because you will do what is evil in the LORD's sight and make Him angry by the work of your hands."
Then Moses recited the words of this song from beginning to end while all Israel listened.
Listen, heavens, and I will speak. Let the earth hear the words from my mouth.
Let my teaching fall like rain. Let my words drop like dew, like gentle rain on new grass, like showers on plants.
I will announce the name of the LORD. Give glory to our God!
The Rock is perfect in His work, because all His ways are fair. He is a faithful God without evil. He is good and right.
They have ruined themselves before Him. They are not His children because of their faults. They are a crooked and twisted generation.
Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish and senseless people? Isn't He your Father who created you? He made you and set you firm.
Remember the old days. Think about the years of many generations. Ask your father, and he will show you. Ask your elders, and they will tell you.
When the Most High gave the nations their land, when He divided the people, He set the borders of the nations to match the number of Israel's people.
For the LORD's share is His people. Jacob is His chosen inheritance.
He found him in a desert land, in an empty and howling wilderness. He surrounded him and cared for him. He guarded him like His most precious treasure.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, He spread His wings and caught him. He carried him on His wings.
The LORD alone led him. No foreign god was with him.
He made him ride on the high places of the land. He ate the crops of the field. He nursed him with honey from the rock and oil from the hard rock.
He gave him curds from cows and milk from sheep, with fat from lambs and goats and rams from Bashan. He fed him with the best wheat and gave him wine from grapes to drink.
But Israel grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, heavy, and well-fed. Then he left the God who made him and turned away from the Rock who saved him.
They made Him jealous with strange gods. They angered Him with disgusting idols.
They sacrificed to demons, not to God. These were gods they did not know, new gods that came lately, which your fathers never feared.
You forgot the Rock who gave you life. You forgot the God who created you.
The LORD saw this and rejected them. He was angry with His sons and daughters.
He said, "I will hide My face from them. I will see what happens to them in the end. They are a twisted generation, children who cannot be trusted."
They made Me jealous with what is not a god. They angered Me with their useless idols. So I will make them jealous with a people who are not a nation. I will anger them with a foolish nation.
For a fire is burning in My anger. It burns down to the deepest grave. It eats up the earth and its crops. It sets fire to the foundations of the mountains.
I will bring many troubles on them. I will use up My arrows on them.
They will waste away from hunger and be eaten by disease and bitter sickness. I will send wild animals against them, along with the poison of snakes in the dust.
Outside, the sword will strike. Inside, there will be terror. It will strike young men and young women, nursing babies and old men.
I thought I would scatter them and erase their memory from mankind.
But I held back because I feared the enemy would brag. I feared their foes would misunderstand and say, "Our hand won this victory. The LORD did not do all this."
They are a nation without good sense, and they have no understanding.
If they were wise, they would understand this. They would think about what will happen to them in the end.
How could one person chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them and the LORD had given them up?
For their rock is not like our Rock. Even our enemies can see the difference.
Their vine comes from Sodom's vine. Their grapes come from Gomorrah's fields. Their grapes are bitter and poisonous.
Their wine is like snake venom, like deadly cobra poison.
"Isn't this stored up with Me, sealed in My treasuries?"
Vengeance belongs to Me. I will pay them back when their foot slips. Their day of trouble is near. What is coming for them will happen soon.
For the LORD will judge His people and have mercy on His servants. He will see that their strength is gone and no one is left, slave or free.
Then He will say, "Where are their gods, the rock they trusted?
Who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their offerings? Let them rise up and help you. Let them be your protection!"
See now that I am He, and there is no god besides Me. I bring death and I give life. I wound and I heal. No one can rescue anyone from My hand.
For I raise My hand to heaven and swear that, as I live forever,
if I sharpen My flashing sword and take hold of judgment, I will take vengeance on My enemies and repay those who hate Me.
My arrows will be soaked in blood, and My sword will devour flesh. It will shed the blood of the slain and the captives, even the enemy leaders.
Rejoice, nations, with His people! For He will avenge the blood of His servants. He will take vengeance on His enemies and show mercy to His land and His people.
Moses came with Joshua son of Nun and spoke all the words of this song to the people.
When Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, "Take to heart all the words I am using to warn you today. Command your children to obey carefully all the words of this law.
For these words are not empty for you. They are your very life. By these words you will live a long time in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."
That same day the LORD spoke to Moses,
"Go up into the Abarim Mountains, to Mount Nebo in the land of Moab, across from Jericho. Look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites as their own.
Die on the mountain you are climbing, and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.
This is because you and Aaron broke faith with Me among the Israelites at the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin. You did not honor Me as holy among the Israelites.
You may see the land from a distance, but you will not enter it, the land I am giving to the Israelites."
This is the blessing Moses, the man of God, spoke to the Israelites before he died.
He said, “The LORD came from Sinai. He rose over them from Seir. He shone from Mount Paran. He came with thousands of holy ones, and fire burned at His right hand.
Surely You love the people; all Your holy ones are in Your hand. They bow at Your feet and receive Your words.
Moses gave us the law, an inheritance for Jacob's people.
The LORD was king in Jeshurun when the leaders of the people gathered, the tribes of Israel together.”
“Let Reuben live and not die, and let his people be many.”
And this he said about Judah: “Hear, O the LORD, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. His hands are strong for him, and be his help against his foes.”

About Levi he said, “Your Thummim and Your Urim belong to Your faithful man, the one You tested at Massah and challenged at the waters of Meribah.” He said about his father and mother that he did not recognize them, and he did not know his brothers or acknowledge his own children. For they kept Your word and guarded Your covenant.
They will teach Your laws to Jacob and Your instructions to Israel. They will offer incense before You and whole burnt offerings on Your altar.
“Bless, O the LORD, his strength, and accept the work of his hands. Crush those who rise against him and those who hate him, so they cannot rise again.”
About Benjamin he said, “The LORD's loved one rests safely with Him. The LORD covers him all day and rests between his shoulders.”
About Joseph he said, “May the LORD bless his land with the best from heaven, with dew, and with water from the deep below,
with the best the sun can give and the best each month brings,
with the best from the ancient mountains and the best from the everlasting hills,

with the best the earth can give and all that fills it, and with the favor of the One who lived in the bush. May these blessings rest on Joseph's head, on the crown of the one set apart among his brothers.

His bull has great strength, and its horns are like a wild ox's horns. With them he will push the peoples to the ends of the earth. They are the thousands of Ephraim and the ten thousands of Manasseh.”
About Zebulun he said, “Rejoice, Zebulun, when you go out, and Issachar, in your tents.
They will call the peoples to the mountain and offer right sacrifices there. For they will feed on the wealth of the seas and on the treasures hidden in the sand.”
About Gad he said, “Blessed is the one who expands Gad's territory. Gad lives like a lion and tears off arm and head.
He chose the best land for himself, for a leader's portion was kept there. He came with the leaders of the people and carried out the LORD's justice and His laws for Israel.”
About Dan he said, “Dan is a lion cub that leaps from Bashan.”
About Naphtali he said, “Naphtali, full of favor and filled with the LORD's blessing, take the west and the south.”
About Asher he said, “Asher is blessed with children. Let him be favored by his brothers and dip his foot in oil.
Your sandals will be iron and bronze, and your strength will last as long as you live.”
There is no one like the God of Jeshurun, who rides through the heavens to help you and through the skies in His majesty.
The eternal God is your refuge, and underneath are His everlasting arms. He will drive the enemy out before you and destroy them.
Israel will live safely alone. Jacob's spring is in a land of grain and wine, and the heavens will drip with dew.

How happy you are, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is your shield and your help, and the sword that gives you honor. Your enemies will cringe before you, and you will walk on their high places.
Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. The LORD showed him all the land: Gilead as far as Dan,
all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea,
the Negev, the plain of the Valley of Jericho, the City of Palms, as far as Zoar.

And the LORD said to him, "This is the land I swore on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, 'I will give it to your descendants.' I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross over into it."
So Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD.
And He buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor, and no one knows where his grave is to this day.
Moses was 120 years old when he died. His eyes were not dim, and his strength had not faded.
The Israelites wept for Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days, until the days of mourning for Moses were over.
Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Since then, no prophet has arisen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.
He was the one the LORD sent to do all the signs and wonders in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh, all his officials, and all his land.
He also did all the mighty acts and all the great and terrible deeds that Moses did before the eyes of all Israel.
After Moses, the servant of the LORD, died, the LORD said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant:
"Moses My servant is dead. Now get up, you and all the people, and cross this Jordan River into the land I am giving to the Israelites.
I have given you every place you set foot, just as I promised Moses.
Your territory will run from the desert and Lebanon to the great Euphrates River. It will include all the land of the Hittites and reach west to the Great Sea.
No one will be able to stand against you as long as you live. I will be with you, just as I was with Moses. I will not leave you or abandon you."
"Be strong and brave, because you will lead these people to take the land I swore to their ancestors I would give them.
Only be very strong and brave. Obey all the law that Moses My servant commanded you. Do not turn away from it to the right or the left, so you will succeed wherever you go.
Keep this Book of the Law with you. Read it day and night so you can obey everything written in it. Then you will be successful and do well.
I have commanded you to be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or discouraged, because the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."
Then Joshua commanded the people's leaders:
"Go through the camp and tell the people, 'Get your food ready, because in three days you will cross this Jordan River. You will go in and take the land the LORD your God is giving you to own.'"
Then Joshua spoke to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh:
"Remember what Moses, the servant of the LORD, commanded you. He said that the LORD your God is giving you rest and will give you this land.
Your wives, children, and animals may stay in the land Moses gave you east of the Jordan. But all your fighting men must cross over, armed, ahead of your brothers. You must help them.

Keep helping them until the LORD gives your brothers rest, just as He gave you. They will take the land the LORD your God is giving them. Then you can return to your own land east of the Jordan and take it. That is the land Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you."
The people answered Joshua, "We will do everything you command us. We will go wherever you send us.
We obeyed Moses in everything, and we will obey you in the same way. May the LORD your God be with you, just as He was with Moses.
Anyone who rebels against your commands and does not obey everything you tell him will be put to death. Just be strong and brave."
Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shittim. He told them, "Go and look at the land, especially Jericho." So they went and stayed at the house of Rahab, a prostitute.
The king of Jericho was told, "Men from Israel have come here tonight to spy out the land."
The king sent this message to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, because they came to spy out the whole land."
But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I didn't know where they were from."
"They left at dark, just as the gate was about to close. I don't know where they went. Pursue them quickly. You may catch them."
But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under stalks of flax she had laid out there.
The pursuers chased them along the road toward the Jordan River crossings. As soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut.
Before the spies lay down for the night, Rahab went up to the roof to talk to them.
She said to the men, "I know the the LORD has given you this land. We are terrified of you, and everyone in the land has melted with fear of you.
We heard how the the LORD dried up the Red Sea in front of you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, whom you completely destroyed.
When we heard this, our hearts melted. Everyone lost courage because of you. For the the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on earth below.
Now please swear to me by the the LORD that, since I showed kindness to you, you will show kindness to my family. Give me a trustworthy sign
that you will spare my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them, and that you will save us from death."
"Our lives for yours!" the men said. "If you don't tell us about this mission of ours, we will show you kindness and faithfulness when the the LORD gives us the land."
Then she let them down by a rope through the window, because her house was built into the city wall.
She told them, "Go to the hills so the pursuers won't find you. Hide there for three days until they return. Then go on your way."
The men said to her, "We will keep our promise. We will be free from the oath you made us swear."
"When we enter the land, tie this scarlet cord in the window you used to lower us. Gather your father and mother, your brothers, and all your father's family into your house.
Anyone who goes out of your house into the street will be responsible for his own death, and we will be innocent. But if anyone with you in the house is harmed, we will take the blame.
But if you tell what we are doing, we won't be bound by the oath you made us swear."
"Agreed," she said. "As your say, so be it." Then she sent them away, and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
They went into the hills and stayed there three days, until the pursuers returned. The pursuers had searched all along the road but didn't find them.
Then the two men came down from the hills, crossed the river, and went to Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, "The LORD has surely given the whole land into our hands. Everyone there is terrified of us."
Early in the morning Joshua got up. He and all the Israelites left Shittim and went to the Jordan. They camped there before crossing.
After three days the officers went through the camp.
They gave this command to the people: "When you see the ark of the covenant of the the LORD your God being carried by the Levite priests, leave your place and follow it.
Keep about 3,000 feet between you and the ark. Do not go near it, so you will know which way to go, because you have never traveled this way before."
Joshua told the people, "Make yourselves holy, because tomorrow the the LORD will do amazing things among you.
Then Joshua said to the priests, "Pick up the ark of the covenant and go ahead of the people." So they picked up the ark and went ahead of them.
The the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel. They will know that I am with you just as I was with Moses.
Tell the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, 'When you reach the edge of the Jordan's water, stand still in the Jordan.'"
Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come here and listen to the words of the the LORD your God.
By this you will know that the living God is among you. He will certainly drive out before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.
Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is crossing over ahead of you into the Jordan.
Now choose for yourselves twelve men from Israel, one from each tribe.

As soon as the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, touch the water of the Jordan, the water flowing down from upstream will be cut off and stand up in one heap."
The people left their tents to cross the Jordan. The priests carrying the ark went ahead of them.
The Jordan was at flood stage, overflowing all its banks during harvest time. When the priests carrying the ark reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water's edge,

the water flowing from upstream stopped. It piled up in a heap far away at Adam, a town near Zarethan. The water flowing toward the Sea of the Arabah—the Salt Sea—was completely cut off. Then the people crossed over opposite Jericho.
The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the the LORD stood on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. All Israel crossed on dry ground until the whole nation had crossed the Jordan.
After the whole nation had crossed the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua, "Choose twelve men from the people, one from each tribe.
Tell them, 'Take twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests stood.
Carry them with you and set them down where you camp tonight.'"
So Joshua called the twelve men he had chosen from the Israelites, one from each tribe.
Joshua said to them, "Go ahead of the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan. Each man should lift a stone onto his shoulder, one for each tribe of the Israelites.
This will be a sign among you. In the future, your children will ask what these stones mean to you.
Tell them that the Jordan's water was cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD when it crossed the Jordan. These stones will remind the Israelites forever."
The Israelites did as Joshua commanded. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, one for each tribe, carried them to the camp, and set them there.
Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, where the priests who carried the ark had stood. They are still there today.
The priests carrying the ark stood in the Jordan until everything the LORD commanded Joshua to tell the people was finished, just as Moses had commanded Joshua. Then the people hurried across.
After everyone had crossed, the ark of the LORD and the priests crossed in front of the people.
The men of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over in front of the Israelites, ready for battle, as Moses had told them.
About forty thousand armed men crossed before the LORD to the plains of Jericho.
That day the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they respected him all his life, just as they had respected Moses.
Then the LORD said to Joshua,
"Command the priests carrying the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua commanded the priests, "Come up out of the Jordan."

As soon as the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up from the middle of the Jordan, their feet touched dry ground. Then the water of the Jordan returned to its place and overflowed all its banks, just as it had before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and camped at Gilgal on the east side of Jericho.
Joshua set up there the twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan.
He said to the Israelites, "In the future, your children will ask their fathers what these stones mean.
Tell them that Israel crossed this Jordan on dry ground.
For the LORD your God dried up the water of the Jordan before you until you crossed, just as the LORD your God did to the Red Sea when He dried it up before us until we crossed.
So all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the LORD is strong, and so you may fear the LORD your God forever."

When all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings along the coast heard that the LORD had dried up the Jordan River for the Israelites until they crossed over, their hearts melted. They lost all courage because of the Israelites.
At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make flint knives and circumcise the Israelites a second time."
So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at the Hill of Foreskins.
Joshua did this because all the men who had left Egypt, the soldiers, had died in the wilderness on the way after they left Egypt.
The people who left Egypt had been circumcised, but those born in the wilderness along the way had not.

The Israelites had traveled in the wilderness for forty years, until all the fighting men who left Egypt were gone. They had not obeyed the LORD. So the LORD swore they would not see the land He had promised their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.
So Joshua circumcised their sons, who took their place. They had not been circumcised on the journey, so they were still uncircumcised.
After the whole nation had been circumcised, they stayed in the camp until they healed.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have removed the disgrace of Egypt from you." So that place was named Gilgal, and it still has that name today.
The Israelites camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho. On the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, they kept the Passover.
The day after the Passover, they ate unleavened bread and roasted grain from the land.
The manna stopped the day after they ate food from the land. The Israelites no longer had manna. That year they ate from the crops of Canaan.
While Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went to him and asked, "Are you for us or for our enemies?"
"No," he said. "I am the commander of the LORD's army, and I have come now." Then Joshua fell with his face to the ground and worshiped. He said, "What does my Lord have to say to His servant?"
The commander of the LORD's army said to Joshua, "Take off your sandals, because the place where you are standing is holy." So Joshua did as he was told.
Jericho was shut tight because of the Israelites. No one went out, and no one came in.
Then the the LORD said to Joshua, “Look, I have handed Jericho over to your hand, along with its king and its strong warriors.
March around the city once with all your fighting men. Do this for six days.
Have seven priests carry seven rams’ horns in front of the ark. On the seventh day, march around the city seven times while the priests blow the trumpets.
When you hear the long blast of the ram’s horn, all the people must shout loudly. Then the city wall will fall, and everyone will charge straight ahead.”
Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said, “Take up the ark of the covenant. Let seven priests carry seven rams’ horns in front of the ark of the the LORD.”
He told the people, “Move out and march around the city. Let the armed men go ahead of the ark of the the LORD.”
As soon as Joshua spoke, the seven priests carrying the seven rams’ horns went forward before the the LORD, blowing their trumpets. The ark of the covenant of the the LORD followed them.
The armed men went ahead of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the ark. The priests kept blowing the trumpets as they marched.
Joshua ordered the people, “Do not shout or make a sound with your voices until I tell you to shout. Then you must shout.”
So the ark of the the LORD went around the city once. Then they returned to camp and stayed there for the night.
Joshua got up early the next morning, and the priests carried the ark of the the LORD.
The seven priests carrying the seven rams’ horns went ahead of the ark of the the LORD, blowing their trumpets. The armed men went before them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the the LORD.
On the second day, they marched around the city once and returned to camp. They did the same thing for six days.
On the seventh day, they got up at dawn and marched around the city seven times, just as before. That was the only day they marched around it seven times.
On the seventh time, after the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, “Shout! The the LORD has given you the city.
The city and everything in it must be completely destroyed for the the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute and everyone in her house will live, because she hid the messengers we sent.
“But be careful not to take anything that is set apart for destruction. If you take any of them, you will bring trouble on Israel’s camp.
All the silver, gold, bronze, and iron are holy to the the LORD. They must go into the the LORD’s treasury.”

So the people shouted, and the priests blew the trumpets. When the people heard the trumpet sound, they gave a loud shout, and the wall fell down. Then everyone charged straight into the city and captured it.
They destroyed everything in the city—men, women, young, old, cattle, sheep, and donkeys—by the sword.
Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house and bring out the woman and everyone with her, just as you promised her.”
The young spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father, mother, brothers, and all her relatives. They placed them outside Israel’s camp.
Then they burned the city and everything in it. They saved only the silver, gold, bronze, and iron and put them in the the LORD’s treasury.
Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute and her family because she hid the spies Joshua sent to Jericho. She still lives among the Israelites today.

At that time Joshua made the people promise before the the LORD: “Anyone who rebuilds this city of Jericho is cursed. He will lose his oldest son when he lays the foundation, and his youngest son when he sets up the gates.”
So the the LORD was with Joshua, and people all over the country heard about him.

The Israelites did not keep faith with the things set apart for the LORD. Achan son of Karmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took some of those things. So the LORD was very angry with Israel.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, a town near Beth Aven, east of Bethel. He said, "Go up and spy on the land." The men went up and spied on Ai.

When they came back to Joshua, they said, "Not all the people need to go up against Ai. Send about two or three thousand men to attack it. Do not make all the people tired, because Ai has only a few people."
So about three thousand men went up. But the men of Ai beat them and chased them away.
The men of Ai killed about thirty-six of them. They chased the Israelites from the city gate to the stone pits and struck them down on the slopes. Then the people lost all courage and were terrified.
Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown on the ground before the ark of the LORD. He stayed there until evening. The leaders of Israel did the same. They put dust on their heads.

Joshua said, "O Lord, the LORD, why did You bring these people across the Jordan? Was it to hand us over to the Amorites so they could destroy us? If only we had stayed on the other side of the Jordan!
Lord, what can I say now that Israel has turned and run from its enemies?
The Canaanites and everyone else in the land will hear about this. They will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. Then what will You do for Your great name?"
The LORD said to Joshua, "Get up! Why are you lying facedown?
Israel has sinned. They broke My covenant that I gave them. They took some of the things set apart for Me. They stole them, lied about them, and hid them with their own things.

That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They turn and run from them. They themselves are now set apart for destruction. I will not be with you anymore unless you destroy the devoted things among you."

The LORD said, "Get up and set the people apart for Me. Tell them, 'Set yourselves apart for tomorrow. This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There are devoted things among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove them.'

In the morning, bring your tribes forward. The tribe the LORD chooses will come forward by clans. The clan the LORD chooses will come forward by families. The family the LORD chooses will come forward man by man.
Whoever is caught with the devoted things will be burned. He and everything he owns will be destroyed, because he broke the LORD's covenant and did a shameful thing in Israel."
Early the next morning, Joshua brought Israel forward by tribes. The tribe of Judah was chosen.
He brought the clans of Judah forward, and the Zerahites were chosen. Then he brought the Zerahite clans forward by families, and the family of Zabdi was chosen.
Joshua brought Zabdi's family forward man by man, and Achan son of Karmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, was chosen.
Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory and praise to the LORD, the God of Israel. Tell me what you have done. Do not hide it from me."
Achan answered, "It is true. I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did:

I saw a beautiful robe from Babylon, about two hundred shekels of silver, and a gold bar weighing fifty shekels. I wanted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground in my tent, with the silver under them."
Joshua sent messengers. They ran to the tent, and there were the things, hidden in the tent, with the silver underneath.
They took the things out of the tent and brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites. They spread them out before the LORD.

Then Joshua and all Israel took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the gold bar, his sons and daughters, his oxen, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything he owned. They brought them to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, "Why have you brought trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you today." Then all Israel stoned Achan. Afterward, they burned him and all he owned.
They piled a large heap of stones over Achan. It is still there today. Then the LORD turned from His fierce anger. That is why the place is called the Valley of Achor to this day.

After Israel's defeat at Ai, the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid or discouraged. Take all the warriors with you, and go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
Do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king. But you may take its plunder and livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city."
So Joshua and all the fighting men got ready to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out at night.
He gave them this order: "Watch carefully. You are to hide in ambush behind the city. Do not go very far from it, and all of you must be ready.
I and all the people with me will move toward the city. When its men come out to fight us, as they did before, we will run from them.
They will chase us until we have drawn them away from the city, because they will say, 'They are running from us again, just as before.' Then we will run from them.
You must rise up from your hiding place and take the city. The LORD your God will give it into your hands.
When you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do what the LORD has commanded. See, I have given you this order."
So Joshua sent them off, and they went to the hiding place. They stayed between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. Joshua spent that night with the people.
Early the next morning, Joshua got up and gathered the people. He and the elders of Israel went up in front of the people toward Ai.
All the fighting men who were with him went up and came near the city. They camped north of Ai, with a valley between them and Ai.
Joshua took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
So the main camp was north of the city, and the rear guard was west of the city. Joshua spent that night in the valley.
When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his men hurried out early in the morning to meet Israel in battle at the place near the Arabah. He did not know that men were hiding behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel let themselves be pushed back by them and ran toward the wilderness.
All the men in the city were called out to chase them. They chased Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go after Israel. They left the city open and chased Israel.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Stretch out the spear in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand." Joshua stretched out the spear in his hand toward the city.
As soon as he did, the men in ambush rose quickly from their place and ran into the city. They captured it and quickly set it on fire.

The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from the city into the sky. They had no way to escape in either direction. The Israelites who had been running toward the wilderness turned back against their pursuers.
When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and saw the smoke, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.
The other Israelites came out of the city against them, so the men of Ai were caught in the middle. Israel struck them down until no survivor or escapee was left.
But they captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

When Israel had finished killing all the people of Ai in the open country and in the wilderness where they had chased them, and when all of them had fallen by the sword, all Israel went back to Ai and struck it down with the sword.
Twelve thousand men and women of Ai died that day.
Joshua did not draw back the hand that held the spear until he had completely destroyed all the people of Ai.
Israel took only the livestock and the plunder of that city for themselves, as the LORD had commanded Joshua.
So Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent heap of ruins, which it still is today.

He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset, Joshua gave the order, and they took his body down from the tree. They threw it at the entrance to the city gate and piled a large heap of stones over it. That heap is still there today.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal.

He did this just as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had commanded the Israelites. It is written in the Book of the Law of Moses: an altar of whole stones, on which no iron tool had been used. On it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings.
There, in front of the Israelites, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the Law of Moses, which Moses had written.

All Israel, including foreigners and native-born people, along with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD. Half of them faced Mount Gerizim, and half faced Mount Ebal, just as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had commanded at first, in order to bless the people of Israel.
After that, Joshua read all the words of the Law, including the blessings and the curses, exactly as written in the Book of the Law.
There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the children, and the foreigners living among them.

When all the kings west of the Jordan heard what had happened, they joined together. These kings were from the hill country, the western foothills, and the whole coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon. They were Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
They came together with one purpose: to fight Joshua and Israel.
The people of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
So they decided to trick him. They packed old sacks on their donkeys, took old wineskins that were cracked and tied up,
and wore old, patched sandals and old clothes. All their food was dry and moldy.
They went to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have come from a far country. Make a treaty with us."
The men of Israel said to the Hivite, "Maybe you live near us. How can we make a treaty with you?"
"We are your servants," they said to Joshua. Then Joshua asked them, "Who are you? Where do you come from?"
They answered him, "Your servants have come from a very far country because of the name of the the LORD your God. We have heard about Him and about everything He did in Egypt.
We also heard what He did to the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.
Our elders and all the people of our land told us, 'Take food for the journey and go meet them. Say to them, "We are your servants. Please make a treaty with us."'
This bread was warm when we packed it at home, but now it is dry and moldy.
These wineskins were new when we filled them, but now they are cracked. Our clothes and sandals are worn out from the long trip."
The men of Israel tasted some of their food, but they did not ask the the LORD what to do.
Joshua made a peace treaty with them and agreed to let them live. The leaders of the people also swore an oath to them.
Three days after they made the treaty, the Israelites heard that these people lived nearby.
So the Israelites set out and reached their cities on the third day. The cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim.
But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders had sworn to them by the the LORD, the God of Israel. The whole community complained against the leaders.
All the leaders answered the community, "We have sworn to them by the the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.
This is what we will do for them: We will let them live, so the the LORD's anger will not come on us because of the oath we swore to them.
They will live," the leaders told them, "but they will cut wood and carry water for the whole community."
Joshua called the Gibeonites together and said to them, "Why did you trick us? You said, 'We live very far from you,' but you live among us.
Now you are cursed. None of you will be freed from being slaves. You will cut wood and carry water for the house of my God."

They answered Joshua, "We were told that the the LORD your God commanded His servant Moses to give you all this land and to destroy all who live in it. We were very afraid for our lives, so we did this.
Now we are in your hands. Do to us what seems good and right to you."
So Joshua saved them from the Israelites, and they were not killed.
That day he made them cut wood and carry water for the community and for the altar of the the LORD at the place He would choose.

Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and destroyed it. He had done to Ai and its king what he had done to Jericho and its king. Adoni-Zedek also heard that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and now lived among them.
He was very afraid, because Gibeon was a large city, like one of the royal cities. It was larger than Ai, and all its men were warriors.
So Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, sent this message to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon:
"Come up to me and help me. Let us attack Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and the Israelites."
The five Amorite kings—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—joined forces. They marched up with all their armies, camped around Gibeon, and attacked it.

The men of Gibeon sent a message to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants. Come quickly and save us and help us, for all the Amorite kings who live in the hill country have gathered against us."
So Joshua and all his fighting men, including all the mighty warriors, marched up from Gilgal.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for I have given them into your hand. Not one of them will stand before you."
Joshua marched all night from Gilgal and came upon them suddenly.

The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel. Joshua struck them with a great defeat at Gibeon and chased them along the road to Beth Horon. He struck them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled from Israel down the slope of Beth Horon, the LORD hurled large hailstones from the sky on them all the way to Azekah. More died from the hailstones than from the swords of the Israelites.
On the day the LORD gave the Amorites over to Israel, Joshua spoke to the LORD while Israel watched. He said, "Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon."

The sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took revenge on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a full day.
