There has never been a day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to a man's voice, because the LORD fought for Israel.
Then Joshua and all Israel returned to the camp at Gilgal.
The five kings fled and hid in a cave at Makkedah.
Joshua was told, "The five kings have been found hiding in a cave at Makkedah."
Joshua said, "Roll large stones to the mouth of the cave and post men there to guard them."
"But do not stay there. Pursue your enemies and attack them from behind. Do not let them reach their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand."
After Joshua and the Israelites finished striking them down with a terrible defeat, the survivors fled to fortified cities.
The whole army returned safely to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah. Not one person spoke against the Israelites.
Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me."
They did so and brought out the five kings—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.

When they brought them out to Joshua, he called all the men of Israel and said to the commanders who had gone with him, "Come near and put your feet on the necks of these kings." They came near and put their feet on the kings' necks.
Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or discouraged. Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all your enemies that you fight."
Then Joshua struck them and killed them. He hung them on five trees, and they hung there until evening.
At sunset Joshua commanded that they be taken down from the trees and thrown into the cave where they had hidden. Large stones were placed at the mouth of the cave, and they are still there today.

That same day Joshua captured Makkedah. He struck it and its king with the sword and devoted to destruction every person in it. He left no survivor. He did to Makkedah's king what he had done to Jericho's king.
Joshua and all Israel moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against it.
The LORD gave it and its king into Israel's hand. Joshua struck it and everyone in it with the sword and left no survivor. He did to its king what he had done to Jericho's king.
Joshua and all Israel moved on from Libnah to Lachish, camped around it, and fought against it.
The LORD gave Lachish into Israel's hand on the second day. Joshua struck it and everyone in it with the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, but Joshua struck him and his people until no one was left.
Joshua and all Israel moved on from Lachish to Eglon, camped around it, and fought against it.
They captured it that day and struck it with the sword. Joshua devoted to destruction every person in it that day, just as he had done to Lachish.
Joshua and all Israel went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.
They captured it and struck its king, all its towns, and everyone in it with the sword. Joshua left no survivor, just as he had done at Eglon. He devoted the city and everyone in it to destruction.
Joshua and all Israel turned back to Debir and fought against it.

They captured it, its king, and all its towns. They struck them with the sword and devoted to destruction every person in it. Joshua left no survivor. He did to Debir and its king as he had done to Hebron, and he did the same to Libnah and its king.

So Joshua struck the whole land—the hill country, the Negev, the western foothills, and the slopes. He struck all its kings and left no survivor. He devoted to destruction everything that breathed, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua struck them from Kadesh Barnea to Gaza and all the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their land at one time, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Then Joshua and all Israel returned to the camp at Gilgal.
When Jabin, king of Hazor, heard about this, he sent messages to Jobab, king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph.
He also sent messages to the kings in the north who lived in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the western foothills, and in Naphoth-dor by the sea.
He sent to the Canaanites in the east and west, the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites below Mount Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
They came out with all their troops. Their army was very large, like the sand on the seashore, and they had many horses and chariots.
All these kings met and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, because by this time tomorrow I will hand all of them over to Israel, dead. You are to hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
So Joshua and all his fighting men came against them by the waters of Merom suddenly and attacked them.

The LORD gave them into the hand of Israel. They struck them down and chased them to Great Sidon, to Misrephoth-maim, and to the Valley of Mizpah in the east. They struck them down until no survivors were left.
Joshua did to them as the LORD had commanded. He hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and struck down its king with the sword. Hazor had been the head of all those kingdoms.
They put to the sword every person in it, destroying them completely. No one was left alive. Then they burned Hazor with fire.
Joshua captured all these cities and their kings. He struck them with the sword and destroyed them, just as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had commanded.
But Israel did not burn any of the cities that stood on their mounds, except Hazor, which Joshua burned.
The Israelites took for themselves all the plunder and livestock of these cities. But they put all the people to the sword until they destroyed them, leaving no one alive.
As the LORD had commanded His servant Moses, so Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua did it. He did not fail to do anything the LORD had commanded Moses.
So Joshua took all that land: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the western foothills, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel and its lowlands.
It went from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, struck them down, and put them to death.
Joshua waged war against all these kings for a long time.
No city made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites who lived in Gibeon. They took all the others in battle.
For it was the LORD who hardened their hearts to fight against Israel, so that they would be destroyed completely and receive no mercy, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua came and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, Debir, and Anab, from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel. Joshua destroyed them and their cities completely.
No Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites except in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
Joshua took all the land, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses. He gave it to Israel as an inheritance, divided among their tribes. Then the land rested from war.
These are the kings of the land the Israelites defeated. They took the land east of the Jordan, from the Arnon River to Mount Hermon, including all the eastern plain.

Sihon, king of the Amorites, lived in Heshbon. He ruled from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon River, through the middle of that valley, up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites, and over half of Gilead.
His land also included the eastern plain up to the Sea of Chinnereth and down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, east of Beth Jeshimoth, and south below the slopes of Pisgah.
Og, king of Bashan, was one of the last Rephaim. He lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
He ruled Mount Hermon, Salecah, and all of Bashan up to the borders of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and over half of Gilead up to the border of Sihon, king of Heshbon.
Moses, servant of the LORD, and the Israelites defeated them. Moses, servant of the LORD, gave their land to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the land Joshua and the Israelites defeated west of the Jordan. Their land ran from Baal Gad in the valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir. Joshua gave this land to the tribes of Israel as their share.
It included the hill country, the lowlands, the Arabah, the slopes, the wilderness, and the Negev. The people living there were Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
the king of Jericho and the king of Ai near Bethel;
the king of Jerusalem and the king of Hebron;
the king of Jarmuth and the king of Lachish;
the king of Eglon and the king of Gezer;
the king of Debir and the king of Geder;
the king of Hormah and the king of Arad;
the king of Libnah and the king of Adullam;
the king of Makkedah and the king of Bethel;
the king of Tappuah and the king of Hepher;
the king of Aphek and the king of Sharon;
the king of Madon and the king of Hazor;
the king of Shimron-meron and the king of Achshaph;
the king of Taanach and the king of Megiddo;
the king of Kedesh and the king of Jokneam in Carmel;
the king of Dor in Naphath-dor and the king of Goiim in Gilgal;
and the king of Tirzah. That made thirty-one kings in all.
When Joshua was old and well along in years, the LORD said to him, “You are old and well along in years, and a lot of land still needs to be taken.
This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines and all the Geshurites,

from the Shihor on the border of Egypt to the border of Ekron in the north. It counts as Canaanite land. The five Philistine rulers are those of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron, along with the Avvites.
From the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek and the border of the Amorites.
Also the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon to the east, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.

I will drive out all the people who live in the hill country, from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, and all the Sidonians, before the Israelites. But allot this land to Israel as an inheritance, just as I commanded you.
Now divide this land as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
The Reubenites and Gadites had already received their inheritance, which Moses gave them east of the Jordan, just as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had given them:
from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, including the city in the middle of the valley, and all the plain of Medeba as far as Dibon;
and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites;
and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was one of the last of the Rephaim. Moses struck them down and took the land.
Yet the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. Geshur and Maacah still live among Israel to this day.
Only the tribe of Levi did not receive an inheritance. The offerings made by fire to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as He had promised.
Moses gave an inheritance to the clans of the tribe of Reuben:
Their territory was from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, including the city in the middle of the valley, and all the plain near Medeba,
with Heshbon and all its cities on the plain: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,
Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth,

and all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. Moses struck him down along with the leaders of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the princes of Sihon who lived in the land.
The Israelites also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword among those they struck down.
The border of the Reubenites was the Jordan. This was the inheritance of the Reubenites by their clans, with their cities and villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to its clans:
Their territory was Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, which is east of Rabbah;
from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;
and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, with the Jordan as its border, eastward to the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth.
This was the inheritance of the Gadites by their clans, with their cities and villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh; it was for the clans of the half-tribe of the descendants of Manasseh:
Their territory was from Mahanaim through all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair in Bashan—sixty cities.
Half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan, went to the clans of Machir son of Manasseh, that is, to half the descendants of Machir.
These are the inheritances Moses gave on the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan, across from Jericho.
But to the tribe of Levi, Moses gave no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as He had promised them.
These are the portions of land the people of Israel received in Canaan. Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the Israelite tribes gave them out.
The land was given by casting lots to the nine and a half tribes, just as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
Moses had already given land to the two and a half tribes east of the Jordan. But he gave no land among them to the Levites.
The sons of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites did not get a share of the land, except cities to live in, with fields around them for their animals and other property.
So the Israelites did what the LORD had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
The sons of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb son of Jephunneh, the Kenizzite, said to him, “You know what the LORD said to Moses, the man of God, at Kadesh-barnea about you and me.
I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of the LORD, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land. I brought back an honest report. “
My brothers who went with me made the people afraid, but I followed the LORD my God with all my heart.
On that day Moses swore to me, ‘The land you walked on will be yours and your children’s forever, because you followed the LORD my God with all your heart.’ “
Now the LORD has kept me alive, just as He promised, for forty-five years since He spoke those words to Moses, while Israel traveled in the desert. Today I am eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out. I have the same strength now for war and for going out and coming in.

So give me this hill country that the LORD promised me that day. You heard then that the Anakim were there, with large, well-protected cities. Maybe the LORD will be with me, and I will drive them out, as the LORD has said.”
Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his share.
So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart.
Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba. Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. Then the land had rest from war.
The lot for the family groups of Judah's tribe went to the border of Edom, the Wilderness of Zin, and the far south.
Their southern border started at the bay of the Salt Sea, from the southern end of it.
It went south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, passed through Zin, went up south of Kadesh-barnea, crossed Hezron, went up to Addar, and turned at Karka.
It passed along to Azmon, went out by the Brook of Egypt, and ended at the sea. This was your southern border.
The eastern border was the Salt Sea up to the mouth of the Jordan. The northern border began at the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan.
The border went up to Beth-hoglah and passed north of Beth-arabah. Then it went up to the stone of Bohan, Reuben's son.
It went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, turned north toward Gilgal, across from the Ascent of Adummim south of the valley. It passed to the waters of En-shemesh and ended at En-rogel.

It went up by the Valley of Ben-hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusite city, Jerusalem. It went up to the top of the mountain west of the Valley of Hinnom, at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim.
From the top of the mountain, the border curved to the spring of Nephtoah and went out to the cities of Mount Ephron. Then it curved to Baalah, which is Kiriath-jearim.
It turned west from Baalah to Mount Seir, passed along the north slope of Mount Jearim, which is Chesalon, went down to Beth-shemesh, and passed through Timnah.
It went out to the north shoulder of Ekron, curved to Shikkeron, passed Mount Baalah, went out to Jabneel, and ended at the sea.
The western border was the Great Sea and its coast. This was the border all around the family groups of Judah's sons.
As the the LORD had said, Joshua gave Caleb son of Jephunneh a portion among Judah's sons. It was Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron. Arba was the father of Anak.
Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak from there: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.
He went up from there against the people of Debir. Debir used to be called Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, "Whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as a wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
When she came, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"
She said, "Give me a blessing. You have given me land in the Negev. Give me springs of water too." So he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This was the land given to the tribe of Judah's sons by their family groups.
The cities at the far south of Judah's tribe, toward Edom's border, were Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon—twenty-nine cities with their villages.
In the lowland were Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim—fourteen cities with their villages.
Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah—sixteen cities with their villages.
Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah—nine cities with their villages.
Ekron, with its daughters and villages,
and all the places from Ekron to the sea, beside Ashdod, with their villages,
Ashdod, with its daughters and villages, Gaza, with its daughters and villages, as far as the Brook of Egypt, and the Great Sea border.
In the hill country were Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
Goshen, Holon, and Giloh—eleven cities with their villages.
Humtah, Kiriath-arba (that is Hebron), and Zior—nine cities with their villages.
Cain, Gibeah, and Timnah—ten cities with their villages.
Maarath, Beth-anoth, Eltekon—six cities with their villages.
Kiriath-baal (that is Kiriath-jearim) and Rabbah—two cities with their villages.
In the wilderness were Beth-arabah, Middin, Secacah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En-gedi—six cities with their villages.
But Judah's sons could not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites live there with Judah's sons to this day.
The land given to Joseph's sons began at the Jordan near Jericho. It ran east to the waters of Jericho, through the desert, and up from Jericho into the hill country to Bethel.
From Bethel it went to Luz and passed along the border of the Arkites at Ataroth.
Then it went down west to the border of the Japhletites, as far as the border of Lower Beth Horon, then to Gezer, and ended at the sea.
So the people of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their land.
The border of Ephraim's people, by their families, was this: on the east it ran from Ataroth Addar to Upper Beth Horon.
From there it went out to the sea. On the north it reached Michmethath, then turned east to Taanath Shiloh and passed beyond it on the east to Janoah.
From Janoah it went down to Ataroth and Naarah, touched Jericho, and ended at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border went west to the Brook of Kanah and ended at the sea. This was the land given to the tribe of Ephraim, by their families.
Ephraim also had cities set apart for them inside the land of Manasseh's people. This included all those cities and their villages.
They did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. The Canaanites still live among Ephraim's people today, but they became forced laborers.
This was the land share for the tribe of Manasseh, because he was Joseph's firstborn. Makir, Manasseh's firstborn and father of Gilead, received Gilead and Bashan because he was a warrior.

Land was also given to the rest of Manasseh's family groups: the families of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, listed by their family groups.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They came to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders. They said, "The LORD told Moses to give us land among our brothers." So Joshua gave them land among their father's brothers, just as the LORD had commanded.
Besides Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan, Manasseh received ten shares of land.
Manasseh's daughters received land among his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of Manasseh's sons.
Manasseh's border started at Asher and went to Michmethath, east of Shechem. Then it turned south to the people who lived at En Tappuah.
The land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but the town of Tappuah on Manasseh's border belonged to Ephraim.

The border went down to the Kanah Valley. The towns south of the valley belonged to Ephraim, even though they were among Manasseh's towns. Manasseh's border was north of the valley and ended at the sea.
The land south of the border belonged to Ephraim, and the land north belonged to Manasseh. The sea was their western border. To the north they touched Asher, and to the east they touched Issachar.
In Issachar and Asher, Manasseh had Beth Shan, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo, along with their surrounding villages.
But Manasseh could not drive out the people of those cities. The Canaanites kept living in that land.
Later, when the Israelites grew strong, they made the Canaanites work for them, but they did not drive them out completely.
The descendants of Joseph spoke to Joshua. They said, "Why did you give us only one share of land? We are a large people, and the LORD has blessed us greatly."
Joshua said, "If you are a large people, go up into the forest and clear land for yourselves in the land of the Perizzites and Rephaites, because the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you."

"The hill country is not enough for us," the descendants of Joseph replied. "All the Canaanites in the lowlands have iron chariots. This is true in Beth Shan and its villages, and it is true in the Jezreel Valley."
Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are a large and powerful people. You will not have just one share of land.
The hill country will be yours. Clear it, and its farthest borders will be yours. You can drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and are strong."
The whole community of Israel gathered at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land had been brought under their control.
Seven tribes of Israel still had not received their share of the land.
Joshua said to the Israelites, “How long will you keep waiting to go and take the land that the the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?”
“Choose three men from each tribe. I will send them out to explore the land and write a description of it, based on the share each tribe should receive. Then they will come back to me.
They will divide the land into seven parts. Judah will keep its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph will keep its territory in the north.
You are to write a description of these seven parts of the land and bring it to me. Then I will cast lots for you here before the the LORD our God.”

“The Levites will have no share among you, because their inheritance is serving the the LORD. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received the inheritance that Moses, the servant of the the LORD, gave them east of the Jordan.”

So the men started out. Joshua commanded those who were going to map the land, “Go and walk through the land, write a description of it, and come back to me. I will cast lots for you here before the the LORD at Shiloh.”
The men went and traveled through the land. They wrote its description in a book, listing the cities in seven parts. Then they came back to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
There Joshua cast lots for them before the the LORD. In Shiloh, Joshua divided the land among the Israelites according to their tribal groups.
The lot came up for the tribe of Benjamin, by its families. The border of their inheritance lay between the people of Judah and the people of Joseph.
On the north side, its border began at the Jordan. It went up along the north side of Jericho, then west through the hill country, and ended in the wilderness of Beth Aven.
From there the border passed to Luz, on the south side of Luz (that is, Bethel). Then it went down to Ataroth Addar, on the mountain south of Lower Beth Horon.
The border turned and curved south from the mountain that faces Beth Horon on the south. It ended at Kiriath Baal, which is Kiriath Jearim, a city of the people of Judah. This was the west side.
The south side began at the edge of Kiriath Jearim. It went west and came out at the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

Then the border went down to the end of the mountain that faces the Valley of Ben Hinnom, in the Valley of Rephaim on the north. It went down the Valley of Hinnom, along the south side of the Jebusite city, and came down to En Rogel.
It turned north and went out to En Shemesh. Then it went out to Geliloth, opposite the ascent of Adummim. It went down to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
It passed along the north side, opposite the Arabah, and went down into the Arabah.
Then the border passed along the north side of Beth Hoglah. It ended at the northern tip of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Jordan. This was the south boundary.
The Jordan formed the eastern boundary. These were the borders around the inheritance of the people of Benjamin, by their families.
The cities of the tribe of Benjamin, by their families, were Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz,
Chephar Ammoni, Ophni, Geba—twelve cities with their villages.
Zela, Eleph, the Jebusite city (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeah, and Kiriath—fourteen cities with their villages. This was the inheritance of the people of Benjamin, by their families.
The second lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Simeon. Their inheritance was inside Judah's territory.
It included Beersheba, or Sheba, Moladah,
Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen—thirteen cities with their villages.
Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four cities with their villages.
It also included all the villages around these cities as far as Baalath-beer, that is, Ramath of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the clans of Simeon.
Simeon's inheritance came from Judah's territory, because Judah's share was too large. So Simeon received land inside Judah's share.
The third lot came up for the clans of Zebulun. The border of their land went to Sarid.
It went west to Maralah, touched Dabbesheth, and met the brook east of Jokneam.
From Sarid it turned east toward the sunrise, to the border of Kisloth-tabor. Then it went to Daberath and up to Japhia.
From there it passed east to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, then came out at Rimmon, which borders Neah.
The border then turned north to Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el.
It also included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—twelve cities with their villages.
These cities and villages were the inheritance of the clans of Zebulun.
The fourth lot came out for the clans of Issachar.
Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, and Shunem,
The border reached Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh, and ended at the Jordan—sixteen cities with their villages.
These cities and villages were the inheritance of the clans of Issachar.
The fifth lot came out for the clans of Asher.
Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph,
Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. On the west the border touched Carmel and Shihor-libnath.
Then it turned east to Beth-dagon, touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el, and went north to Beth-emek and Neiel, passing Cabul on the left.
It went on to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
The border then turned back toward Ramah and the fortified city of Tyre, turned toward Hosah, and ended at the Sea in the region of Achzib.
It also included Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob—twenty-two cities with their villages.
These cities and villages were the inheritance of the clans of Asher.
The sixth lot came out for the clans of Naphtali.
Their border went from Heleph and the oak of Zaanannim, past Adami-nekeb and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan.
Then the border turned west to Aznoth-tabor and went from there to Hukkok, touching Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.
The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth,
Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh—nineteen cities with their villages.
These cities and villages were the inheritance of the clans of Naphtali.
The seventh lot came out for the clans of Dan.
The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-shemesh,
Me-jarkon, and Rakkon, near the border facing Joppa.

But Dan's territory was too small for them. So the Danites went up, fought against Leshem, captured it, put it to the sword, and took possession of it. They settled there and renamed Leshem Dan, after their father Dan.
These cities and villages were the inheritance of the clans of Dan.
When they had finished dividing the land by its borders, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
as the the LORD had commanded. They gave him the city he asked for—Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He rebuilt the city and settled in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the tribes of Israel distributed by lot at Shiloh before the the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
Then the LORD said to Joshua,
“Tell the Israelites to set apart cities of refuge, just as I told you through Moses.
That way, anyone who kills a person by accident, without meaning to, can run there. Those cities will protect him from the one who wants revenge for the death.
“When someone runs to one of those cities, he must stand at the city gate and explain his case to the city elders. Then they must let him in and give him a place to live with them.
If the one who wants revenge follows him, the city must not hand over the killer. He killed his neighbor by accident, not on purpose, and he did not hate him before.
He must stay in that city until he has had a trial before the community and until the high priest who is serving then dies. After that, he may go home to the city he ran from.”
So the Israelites set apart Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim; and Kiriath-arba, also called Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.
East of the Jordan, near Jericho, they set apart Bezer in the wilderness plateau from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.

These cities were chosen for all the Israelites and for any foreigner living among them. Anyone who killed a person by accident could run there and not be killed by the one seeking revenge until he had stood trial before the community.
The heads of the Levite families came to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the Israelite tribal families.
They said to them at Shiloh in Canaan, “The LORD commanded through Moses to give us cities to live in and pasturelands for our livestock.”
So the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands from their own land, just as the LORD had commanded.
The lot gave the Kohathite clans thirteen cities from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. These Levites were descendants of Aaron the priest.
The lot gave the remaining Kohathites ten cities from the clans of Ephraim, Dan, and half of Manasseh.
The lot gave the Gershonites thirteen cities from the clans of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and half of Manasseh in Bashan.
The lot gave the Merarites twelve cities from the clans of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
So the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands by lot, just as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
From the tribes of Judah and Simeon they gave these named cities.
They went to Aaron’s descendants, the Kohathites, because the first lot was theirs.
They gave them Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, with its pasturelands around it. Arba was the father of Anak.
But the fields and villages of that city were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his own land.
To Aaron’s sons, the priests, they gave Hebron, a city of refuge for anyone who killed someone by accident, along with Libnah and its pasturelands.
They also gave Jattir and its pasturelands, and Eshtemoa and its pasturelands.
They gave Holon and its pasturelands, and Debir and its pasturelands.
They gave Ain and its pasturelands, Juttah and its pasturelands, and Beth Shemesh and its pasturelands. These nine cities came from the two tribes of Judah and Simeon.
From Benjamin they gave Gibeon and its pasturelands, Geba and its pasturelands,
Anathoth and its pasturelands, and Almon and its pasturelands—four cities in all.
So the priests, Aaron’s sons, received thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
The remaining Kohathite clans received their cities from Ephraim.
They gave them Shechem, a city of refuge in the hill country of Ephraim, with its pasturelands, and Gezer with its pasturelands.
Kibzaim and Beth Horon, with their pasturelands—four cities in all.
From Dan they gave Eltekeh and Gibbethon, with their pasturelands.
Aijalon and Gath Rimmon, with their pasturelands—four cities.
From half of Manasseh they gave Taanach and Gath Rimmon, with their pasturelands—two cities.
So the remaining Kohathite clans received ten cities with their pasturelands.
The Gershonite clans received cities from half of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan, a city of refuge, with its pasturelands, and Beeshterah with its pasturelands—two cities.
From Issachar they received Kishion and Daberath, with their pasturelands.
Jarmuth and En Gannim, with their pasturelands—four cities.
From Asher they received Mishal and Abdon, with their pasturelands.
Helkath and Rehob, with their pasturelands—four cities.
From Naphtali they received Kedesh in Galilee, a city of refuge, with its pasturelands, Hammoth Dor with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands—three cities.
So the Gershonite clans received thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
The Merarite clans received cities from Zebulun: Jokneam and Kartah, with their pasturelands.
Dimnah and Nahalal, with their pasturelands—four cities.
From Reuben they received Bezer and Jahaz, with their pasturelands.
Kedemoth and Mephaath, with their pasturelands—four cities.
From Gad they received Ramoth in Gilead, a city of refuge, with its pasturelands, and Mahanaim with its pasturelands.
Heshbon and Jazer, with their pasturelands—four cities.
So the remaining Merarite clans received twelve cities.
In all, the Levites received forty-eight cities with their pasturelands inside the land of Israel.
Each of these cities had pasturelands around it; this was true for all of them.
So the LORD gave Israel all the land He had promised to their fathers. They took it and settled there.
The LORD gave them rest on every side, just as He had sworn to their fathers. None of their enemies could stand against them, because the LORD handed all their enemies over to them.
Not one of the LORD’s good promises to the people of Israel failed; everything He said came true.
Then Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
He said to them, "You have kept all that Moses, the servant of the the LORD, commanded you. You have also obeyed my voice in everything I commanded you.
For many days you have not left your brothers. To this day you have kept the charge of the command of the the LORD your God.

Now the the LORD your God has given rest to your brothers, just as He promised them. So turn and go to your tents, to the land you own. Moses, the servant of the the LORD, gave it to you east of the Jordan.

Only be very careful to obey the command and the law that Moses, the servant of the the LORD, gave you. Love the the LORD your God. Walk in all His ways. Keep His commands. Hold fast to Him. Serve Him with all your heart and all your soul."
Then Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.

Moses had given land in Bashan to the half-tribe of Manasseh, and Joshua had given land west of the Jordan to the other half. Joshua also sent them to their tents among their brothers and blessed them.
He said to them, "Return to your tents with great wealth: with very much livestock, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and clothing. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers."

So the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the Israelites at Shiloh in Canaan. They went to Gilead, to the land they owned, which they had taken as the the LORD had said through Moses.
When they came to the region of the Jordan in Canaan, they built a large altar there by the Jordan. It was big and easy to see.
The Israelites heard that the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had built an altar on the border of Canaan, at Geliloth near the Jordan, on the Israelite side.
When the whole Israelite community heard this, they gathered at Shiloh to go to war against them.
Then the Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to Gilead, to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
With him went ten leaders, one from each ancestral house and one for each tribe of Israel. They were heads of their ancestral houses among the clans of Israel.
They came to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead and said to them,

"This is what the whole community of the the LORD says: What is this wrong you have done today against the God of Israel? You have turned away today from following the the LORD by building an altar for yourselves. Are you rebelling today against the the LORD?
Wasn't the sin at Peor bad enough for us? We still have not fully turned from it, and it brought a plague on the the LORD's people.
Yet you turn away today from following the the LORD? If you rebel today against the the LORD, tomorrow He will be angry with all Israel."

"If the land you own is unclean, cross over to the land the the LORD owns, where the the LORD's tabernacle stands, and take land among us. But do not rebel against the the LORD or against us by building an altar for yourselves besides the altar of the the LORD our God.
Didn't Achan son of Zerah break faith by taking devoted things? Wrath came on all Israel, and he was not the only one who died for his sin."
Then the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of the clans of Israel.
They said, "The the LORD, the God of gods! The the LORD, the God of gods! He knows, and Israel will know too. If we rebelled or broke faith against the the LORD, do not save us today.
If we built this altar to turn away from following the the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings on it, or to make peace offerings on it, may the the LORD Himself hold us accountable.
No, we did this because we were worried. We thought, 'Someday your children might say to our children, "What do you have to do with the the LORD, the God of Israel?"'"
"The the LORD made the Jordan a border between us and you, Reubenites and Gadites. You have no share in the the LORD. We feared your children would make our children stop fearing the the LORD.
So we said, 'Let us build an altar—not for burnt offerings or sacrifices—

but as a witness between us and you and between our generations after us. Then we can serve the the LORD before Him with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings. That way your children will not say to our children later, "You have no share in the the LORD."'"

"We also said, 'If they say this to us or to our generations later, we will say, "Look at the model of the the LORD's altar that our fathers made. It is not for burnt offerings or sacrifices. It is a witness between us and you."'

Far be it from us to rebel against the the LORD or turn away from following Him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices, besides the altar of the the LORD our God that stands before His tabernacle."
Phinehas the priest, the leaders of the community, and the heads of Israel's clans with him heard what the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the Manassehites said. They were pleased.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the Manassehites, "Today we know the the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this wrong against the the LORD. Now you have saved the Israelites from the the LORD's hand."
Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders left the Reubenites and Gadites in Gilead and returned to Canaan. They brought a report back to the Israelites.
The Israelites were pleased with the report. They blessed God and decided not to go to war against them to destroy the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived.
The Reubenites and Gadites named the altar Witness, because they said, "It is a witness between us that the the LORD is God."
Many days after the LORD had given Israel rest from all their enemies around them, Joshua was old and advanced in years.
Joshua called all Israel together—its elders, leaders, judges, and officers—and said to them, "I am old and advanced in years.
"You have seen everything the LORD your God did to these nations for you, because He is the LORD your God, and He fights for you.
See, I have given you these remaining nations as an inheritance for your tribes, along with all the nations I destroyed, from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west.
The LORD your God will push them out and drive them away before you. You will take their land, just as the LORD your God promised you.
"So be very strong. Keep and do everything written in the Book of the Law of Moses. Do not turn away from it to the right or to the left.
Do not mix with these remaining nations among you. Do not even speak the names of their gods. Do not swear by them, serve them, or bow down to them.
Instead, stay close to the LORD your God, as you have done up to now.
"The LORD has driven out great and strong nations before you. No one has been able to stand against you to this day.
One of you will chase a thousand, because the LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised you.
So guard yourselves very carefully, and love the LORD your God.
"If you turn back and join the rest of these nations still among you, if you intermarry with them,

then know for sure that the LORD your God will no longer drive them out before you. They will become a trap and a snare to you, a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you are destroyed and driven from this good land the LORD your God has given you.
"Look, I am about to die, the way all people do. You know with all your heart and your soul that not one of the good promises the LORD your God made to you has failed. Every one has come true.

But just as all the good things the LORD your God promised have come to you, so the LORD will bring on you all the harm He warned about, until He destroys you and drives you from this good land the LORD your God has given you.

If you break the covenant of the LORD your God that He commanded you, and go serve other gods and bow down to them, then the LORD's anger will burn against you, and you will quickly be wiped off the good land He has given you."
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He called for the elders, leaders, judges, and officers of Israel. They stood before God.
Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Long ago your ancestors lived beyond the river. Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor, served other gods.
But I took your father Abraham from the other side of the river. I led him through all the land of Canaan. I gave him many descendants, and I gave him Isaac.
To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Seir to own. Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
Then I sent Moses and Aaron. I brought terrible trouble on Egypt, just as I did among them. After that, I brought you out.
I brought your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians chased your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.

Your fathers cried out to the LORD. He put darkness between you and the Egyptians. Then He brought the sea over them and covered them. Your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. After that, you lived in the wilderness for a long time.
I brought you into the land of the Amorites, who lived east of the Jordan. They fought against you, but I gave them into your hands. You took their land, and I destroyed them before you.
Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, got ready to fight Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
But I would not listen to Balaam. Instead, he blessed you, and I saved you from his hand.

You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought against you, along with the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites. But I gave them into your hands.
I sent hornets ahead of you. They drove out the two Amorite kings before you. You did not win that land with your swords or bows.
I gave you a land you did not work for. You live in cities you did not build. You eat from vineyards and olive groves you did not plant.'"
"Now fear the LORD and serve Him with all your heart and with truth. Throw away the gods your ancestors served beyond the river and in Egypt. Serve the LORD.

If it seems wrong to you to serve the LORD, choose today whom you will serve. You may serve the gods your ancestors served beyond the river, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you live. But as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."
The people answered, "We would never leave the LORD to serve other gods!

For the LORD our God brought us and our ancestors up from Egypt, out of the land of slavery. He did great and wonderful signs before our eyes. He kept us safe on the whole journey and among all the nations we passed through.
The LORD drove out all the nations before us, including the Amorites who lived in the land. So we will serve the LORD, because He is our God."
Joshua said to the people, "You cannot serve the LORD. He is a holy God. He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your rebellion and your sins.
If you leave the LORD and serve foreign gods, He will turn against you. He will bring harm to you and destroy you, even after He has been good to you."
The people said to Joshua, "No! We will serve the LORD."
Joshua said, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the LORD to serve Him." They said, "We are witnesses."
Joshua said, "Now throw away the foreign gods among you. Turn your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel."
The people said to Joshua, "We will serve the LORD our God, and we will obey His voice."
That day Joshua made a covenant with the people at Shechem. He set up a rule and a law for them.
Joshua wrote these words in the Book of the Law of God. Then he took a large stone and set it up there under the oak tree near the sanctuary of the LORD.
Joshua said to all the people, "Look! This stone will be a witness against us. It has heard all the words the LORD spoke to us. It will be a witness against you, so you do not deny your God."
Then Joshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance.
After these things, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of one hundred ten.
They buried him in the border of his inheritance at Timnath Serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who lived after Joshua. They knew all the work the LORD had done for Israel.

The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem. They were buried in the piece of land Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, for one hundred pieces of silver. It became an inheritance for Joseph's children.
Eleazar son of Aaron died too. They buried him at Gibeah, which belonged to his son Phinehas, in the hill country of Ephraim.
After Joshua died, the people of Israel asked the LORD, "Which tribe should go first and fight the Canaanites for us?"
The LORD said, "Judah should go. I have given the land into his hand."

Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come with me into the land I have been given by lot, and we will fight the Canaanites. Then I will go with you into the land you have been given." So Simeon went with him.
Judah went up, and the LORD gave the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands. They struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.
There they found Adoni-Bezek and fought him, defeating the Canaanites and Perizzites.
Adoni-Bezek ran away, but they chased him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.
Adoni-Bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to gather scraps under my table. God has paid me back for what I did." They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
The men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put the people to the sword and set the city on fire.
After that, the men of Judah went down to fight the Canaanites living in the hill country, the Negev, and the western foothills.
They marched against the Canaanites living in Hebron, which used to be called Kiriath Arba, and defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there they went against the people living in Debir, which used to be called Kiriath Sepher.
Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Achsah in marriage to the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got off her donkey, and Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
She said to him, "Give me a blessing. You gave me land in the Negev, so give me springs of water too." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
The descendants of Moses' father-in-law, the Kenite, went up from the City of Palms with the men of Judah into the Negev of Arad. They went and lived among the people there.
Judah went with his brother Simeon and struck the Canaanites living in Zephath. They destroyed the city completely and called it Hormah.
Judah also captured Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron, along with their surrounding lands.
The LORD was with Judah, and they took the hill country. But they could not drive out the people living in the plains, because those people had iron chariots.
As Moses had said, Hebron was given to Caleb, and he drove out the three sons of Anak from there.
The Benjamites did not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites have lived with the Benjamites in Jerusalem to this day.
The house of Joseph also went up to attack Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
They sent spies to Bethel, a city that used to be called Luz.
The spies saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, "Please show us the way into the city, and we will treat you kindly."
He showed them the way in, and they put the city to the sword. But they let the man and all his family go.
The man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city. He called it Luz, and that is its name to this day.
Manasseh did not drive out the people of Beth Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, and Megiddo, or their surrounding towns. The Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
When Israel grew strong, they made the Canaanites do forced labor, but they did not drive them out completely.
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. The Canaanites stayed among them in Gezer.
Zebulun did not drive out the people of Kitron or Nahalol. The Canaanites stayed among them and were put to forced labor.
Asher did not drive out the people of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphek, or Rehob.
The Asherites lived among the Canaanites who lived in the land, because they did not drive them out.
Naphtali did not drive out the people of Beth Shemesh or Beth Anath. They lived among the Canaanites in the land, but the people of Beth Shemesh and Beth Anath were put to forced labor.
The Amorites pushed the Danites back into the hill country and did not let them come down into the plains.
The Amorites were determined to stay in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when the house of Joseph grew strong, they made the Amorites do forced labor.
The border of the Amorites ran from Scorpion Pass to Sela and beyond.
The angel of the the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, "I brought you up out of Egypt and led you into the land I promised your fathers. I said, 'I will never break My agreement with you,
and you must not make an agreement with the people of this land. You must tear down their altars.' But you did not listen to My voice. What have you done?
So now I say, 'I will not drive them out ahead of you. They will be a constant trouble to you, and their gods will trap you.'"
When the angel of the the LORD had spoken these words to all the Israelites, the people lifted up their voices and wept.
So they called that place Bochim, and they offered sacrifices there to the the LORD.
After Joshua sent the people away, the Israelites went to take possession of the land, each to his own inheritance.
The people served the the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who lived after Joshua, who had seen all the great work the the LORD had done for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the the LORD, died at the age of 110.
They buried him within the borders of his inheritance at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
After that whole generation had been gathered to their fathers, another generation grew up who did not know the the LORD or the work He had done for Israel.
Then the Israelites did evil in the sight of the the LORD and served the Baals.

They turned away from the the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of Egypt. They followed other gods, the gods of the peoples around them, and worshiped them. They angered the the LORD.
They left the the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.

Then the the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and He handed them over to raiders who robbed them. He sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, and they could no longer stand against their enemies.
Wherever Israel went, the the LORD was against them and brought disaster, just as He had sworn. They were in great distress.
Then the the LORD raised up judges, who saved them from the hands of their raiders.

Yet they would not listen to their judges. They were unfaithful to the the LORD and worshiped other gods. They quickly turned from the way their fathers had walked in obeying the the LORD's commands. They did not do as their fathers had done.

Whenever the the LORD raised up a judge for them, He was with that judge and saved them from their enemies during that judge's lifetime. The the LORD felt sorry for them because of their crying out under those who oppressed and crushed them.

But when the judge died, they turned back to ways even more corrupt than their fathers'. They followed other gods, serving and worshiping them. They refused to give up their evil practices and stubborn ways.
So the the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and He said, "Because this nation has broken My agreement that I commanded their fathers, and they have not obeyed My voice,
I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.
In this way I will test Israel to see whether they will keep the way of the the LORD by walking in it, as their fathers did."
So the the LORD left those nations in place. He did not drive them out all at once, and He did not let Joshua defeat them.
These are the nations the the LORD left to test Israel. They would test all the Israelites who had not fought in Canaan's wars.
He did this only to teach war to the later generations of Israelites, especially those who had not known war before.
The nations were the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the Lebanon mountains from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance to Hamath.
They were left to test Israel. The LORD wanted to know if the Israelites would obey the commands He had given their fathers through Moses.
So the Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
They married the daughters of those people and gave their own daughters to those sons. They also served those people's gods.
The Israelites did what was evil in the the LORD's sight. They forgot the the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
So the the LORD was very angry with Israel. He handed them over to Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram-naharaim. The Israelites served him for eight years.
But when the Israelites cried out to the the LORD, He raised up Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, as a rescuer to save them.
The Spirit of the the LORD came on Othniel. He judged Israel and went out to war. The LORD gave him victory over Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram. Othniel overpowered him.
So the land had peace for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died.
Again the Israelites did what was evil in the the LORD's sight. So the the LORD gave Eglon, king of Moab, power over Israel, because they had done what was evil in the the LORD's sight.
Eglon gathered the Ammonites and Amalekites to himself. He came and attacked Israel, and he took the City of Palms.
The Israelites served Eglon, king of Moab, for eighteen years.
When the Israelites cried out to the the LORD, He raised up Ehud son of Gera, a Benjamite, as a rescuer. Ehud was left-handed. The Israelites sent him with a tribute payment to Eglon, king of Moab.
Ehud made a sword with two sharp edges. It was about a foot and a half long. He strapped it to his right thigh under his clothes.
He brought the tribute to Eglon, king of Moab. Eglon was a very fat man.
After Ehud finished giving the tribute, he sent away the men who had carried it.
But Ehud himself turned back at the stone idols near Gilgal. He said, "I have a secret message for you, O king." The king said, "Be quiet!" Then everyone standing near him left.
Then Ehud came to him. Eglon was sitting alone in his cool upper room. Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you." The king stood up from his throne.
Ehud reached with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and drove it into Eglon's belly.
Even the handle went in after the blade. The fat closed over it, so Ehud could not pull the sword out of his belly. Then Eglon's bowels emptied.
Then Ehud went out through the porch. He closed and locked the doors of the upper room behind him.
After Ehud left, Eglon's servants came. They saw that the doors of the upper room were locked. They said, "He must be using the bathroom in the cool room."
They waited until they were embarrassed. But when he did not open the doors, they took the key and opened them. There was their master, fallen dead on the floor.
Ehud escaped while they waited. He passed by the stone idols and escaped to Seirah.
When he arrived, he blew the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim. The Israelites went down from the hills with him, and he led them.

He said to them, "Follow me, because the the LORD has handed your enemies, the Moabites, over to you." So they followed him down. They took control of the places where people crossed the Jordan River into Moab. They did not let anyone cross over.
At that time they killed about ten thousand Moabites. All were strong and brave men. Not one escaped.
So Moab was brought under Israel's control that day. The land had peace for eighty years.
After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath. He also saved Israel. He killed six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.
After Ehud died, the Israelites again did evil in the eyes of the LORD.
So the LORD handed them over to Jabin, king of Canaan, who ruled from Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth Haggoyim.
The Israelites cried out to the LORD because Jabin had nine hundred iron chariots and had oppressed them for twenty years.
At that time Deborah, a prophetess and the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel.
She held court under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came to her for decisions.

She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, "The LORD, the God of Israel, commands you: 'Go, take ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun with you, and lead them up to Mount Tabor.
I will bring Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, to you at the Kishon River, along with his chariots and troops, and I will hand him over to you.'"
Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I will go. But if you don't go with me, I won't go."
Deborah said, "I will certainly go with you. But because of the way you are going, you won't get the honor. The LORD will hand Sisera over to a woman." So Deborah went with Barak to Kedesh.
There Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali to come, and ten thousand men went up with him. Deborah went up with him too.
Now Heber the Kenite had moved away from the other Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law. He had pitched his tent by the great tree in Zaanannim near Kedesh.
When Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor,
he gathered all his chariots—nine hundred iron chariots—and all his men from Harosheth Haggoyim to the Kishon River.
Deborah said to Barak, "Get up! This is the day the LORD has handed Sisera over to you. Hasn't the LORD gone out ahead of you?" So Barak went down Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him.
At Barak's advance, the LORD threw Sisera and all his chariots and troops into panic, and they were defeated by the sword. Sisera got down from his chariot and ran away on foot.
Barak chased the chariots and army all the way to Harosheth Haggoyim. Every soldier of Sisera fell by the sword; not one was left.
Sisera ran on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and Heber's family.
Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Come in, my lord. Come in. Don't be afraid." So he went into her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
He said, "I'm thirsty. Please give me a little water." She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him up.
He told her, "Stand at the entrance to the tent. If someone comes and asks you, 'Is anyone here?' say, 'No.'"
But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and a hammer. She went quietly to Sisera while he was fast asleep and worn out. She drove the peg through the side of his head into the ground, and he died.

Just then Barak came by, chasing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said, "Come, I will show you the man you are looking for." So he went in with her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the tent peg through the side of his head.
On that day God defeated Jabin king of Canaan for the Israelites.
The Israelites kept getting stronger against Jabin king of Canaan until they destroyed him.
On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang:
"When the leaders in Israel take the lead, when the people willingly offer themselves, bless the the LORD!
"Hear, O kings! Give ear, O rulers! I will sing to the the LORD; I will sing praise to the the LORD, the God of Israel.
"The LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the land of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens poured down rain, and the clouds poured down water.
"The mountains flowed before the the LORD, yes, Sinai before the the LORD, the God of Israel.
"In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted, and travelers took the back roads.
"Village life stopped; it ended in Israel, until I, Deborah, rose up, a mother in Israel.
"When they chose new gods, then war came to the gates. Not a shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.
"My heart goes out to the commanders of Israel, to the volunteers among the people. Bless the the LORD!
"You who ride white donkeys, who sit on saddle blankets, and who walk along the road, think about this!

"The voice of the singers at the watering places. There they tell about the righteous acts of the the LORD, the righteous deeds of His warriors in Israel. Then the people of the the LORD went down to the gates.
"Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, Barak, and take your captives, O son of Abinoam!
"Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the the LORD came down to me against the mighty.
"From Ephraim came those rooted in Amalek; Benjamin followed you with your troops. From Machir the commanders descended, and from Zebulun those who carry the staff of command.
"The leaders of Issachar were with Deborah, and Issachar was with Barak, rushing into the valley at his heels. Among the clans of Reuben there was great hesitation.
"Why did you sit among the sheepfolds to hear the whistling of the flocks? Among the clans of Reuben there was great hesitation.
"Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan, and Dan, why did he linger by the ships? Asher sat still at the coast of the sea and stayed by his harbors.
"Zebulun was a people who risked their lives; Naphtali, too, on the heights of the field.
"Kings came; they fought. Then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, but they took no plunder of silver.
"From the heavens the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.
"The river Kishon swept them away, the ancient river, the river Kishon. March on, my soul, with strength!
"Then the hooves of horses thundered—the galloping, galloping of his stallions.
"'Curse Meroz,' says the angel of the the LORD, 'curse its people bitterly, for they did not come to help the the LORD, to help the the LORD against the mighty.'
"Most blessed of women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, of tent-dwelling women most blessed.
"He asked for water, and she gave him milk. In a bowl fit for nobles she brought him curdled milk.
"She reached for a tent peg with her right hand, and for the workman's hammer with her left. She struck Sisera and crushed his skull; she shattered and pierced his temple.
"He sank, he fell, he lay at her feet; he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell dead.
"Sisera's mother looked through the window and cried out through the lattice: 'Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why are the hoofbeats of his chariots delayed?'
"The wisest of her ladies answer; indeed, she says to herself:
"'Are they not finding and dividing the plunder—a girl or two for each soldier, dyed garments for Sisera, embroidered garments for the neck of the looter?'
"So may all Your enemies perish, O the LORD! But may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest." And the land had rest forty years.
The Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the the LORD, so The LORD handed them over to Midian for seven years.
Midian was too strong for Israel, so the Israelites made hiding places for themselves in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.
Whenever Israel planted crops, the Midianites, Amalekites, and people from the east would come up and attack them.
They camped against Israel and destroyed the land’s crops all the way to Gaza. They left Israel nothing to eat—no sheep, oxen, or donkeys.
They came with their livestock and tents like a swarm of locusts. They and their camels were too many to count, and they ruined the land.
Israel was brought very low by Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the the LORD.
When the Israelites cried out to the the LORD because of Midian,
the the LORD sent a prophet to them. He said, “This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought you up out of Egypt and brought you out of slavery.
I saved you from the Egyptians and from everyone who oppressed you. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
I said to you, ‘Do not fear the gods of the Amorites, whose land you are living in.’ But you have not listened to My voice.”
The Angel of the the LORD came and sat under the oak tree in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite. His son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites.
The Angel of the the LORD appeared to Gideon and said, “The The LORD is with you, mighty warrior.”

Gideon said to him, “Pardon me, my lord, but if the the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where are all His wonders that our fathers told us about? They said, ‘Did not the the LORD bring us up out of Egypt?’ But now the the LORD has abandoned us and handed us over to Midian.”
The the LORD turned to him and said, “Go with the strength you have and save Israel from Midian. Have I not sent you?”
Gideon said to Him, “Pardon me, my lord, but how can I save Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.”
The the LORD said to him, “I will be with you, and you will defeat all the Midianites at once.”
Gideon said to Him, “If I have found favor in Your eyes, give me a sign that it is You speaking with me.
Please do not go away from this place until I come back to You with my offering and set it before You.” The the LORD said, “I will stay until you return.”
Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened bread from an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, and brought them out to Him under the oak tree.
The Angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened bread and place them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” Gideon did so.

The Angel of the the LORD stretched out the tip of the staff in His hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread. Fire came up from the rock and consumed the meat and the bread, and the Angel of the the LORD disappeared from his sight.
When Gideon saw that it was the Angel of the the LORD, he said, “Alas, Lord GOD! I have seen the Angel of the the LORD face to face.”
The the LORD said to him, “Peace be with you. Do not be afraid. You will not die.”
So Gideon built an altar to the the LORD there and called it “The The LORD Is Peace.” It still stands in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
That night the the LORD said to him, “Take your father’s second bull, the one that is seven years old, and tear down your father’s altar to Baal. Cut down the Asherah pole beside it.

Then build an altar to the the LORD your God on top of this stronghold, using the wood of the Asherah you cut down. Take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah.”
Gideon took ten of his servants and did what the the LORD had told him. But because he was afraid of his family and the men of the town, he did it at night instead of during the day.
When the men of the town got up early the next morning, they saw that Baal’s altar was torn down, the Asherah beside it was cut down, and the second bull had been offered on the new altar.
They asked one another, “Who did this?” After they looked into it, they were told, “Gideon son of Joash did it.”
The men of the town said to Joash, “Bring out your son so he may die, because he tore down Baal’s altar and cut down the Asherah beside it.”

Joash said to all who stood against him, “Are you going to defend Baal? Will you save him? Anyone who defends him should be put to death by morning. If Baal is a god, let him defend himself, because someone tore down his altar.”
So that day they called Gideon “Jerub-Baal,” saying, “Let Baal contend with him, because he tore down Baal’s altar.”
All the Midianites, Amalekites, and people of the east gathered together. They crossed the Jordan and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.
The Spirit of the the LORD came upon Gideon, and he blew the trumpet. The Abiezrites rallied to him.
He sent messengers throughout Manasseh, and they were called to arms. He also sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came up to meet him.
Gideon said to God, “If You are going to save Israel by my hand, as You said,
then I will put a wool fleece on the threshing floor. If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, I will know that You will save Israel by my hand, as You said.”
That is what happened. When Gideon got up early the next morning and squeezed the fleece, he wrung enough dew from it to fill a bowl with water.
Gideon said to God, “Do not be angry with me. Let me speak once more. Let me test the fleece one more time. Let the fleece be dry, and let all the ground be covered with dew.”
That night God did so. Only the fleece was dry, and dew covered all the ground.
Early in the morning, Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) and all the people with him camped by the spring of Harod. The Midianite camp was north of them in the valley near the hill of Moreh.
The LORD said to Gideon, "The people with you are too many for Me to give Midian into their hands. Israel might brag against Me, saying, 'My own hand saved me.'"
Now announce to the people, "Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him go back and leave Mount Gilead." So 22,000 of the people went back, and 10,000 stayed.

The LORD said to Gideon, "There are still too many people. Take them down to the water, and I will test them for you there. Anyone I tell you, 'This one will go with you,' will go with you. Anyone I tell you, 'This one will not go,' will not go."
So he took the people down to the water. The LORD said to Gideon, "Set apart everyone who laps water with his tongue, the way a dog laps, and everyone who kneels down to drink."
The number of men who lapped water with their hands to their mouths was 300. All the rest of the people knelt down to drink.
The LORD said to Gideon, "With the 300 men who lapped I will save you, and I will give Midian into your hand. Let all the other people go home."
So the people took their food and their trumpets. Gideon sent all the Israelites to their tents, but he kept the 300 men. The Midianite camp was below him in the valley.
That night the LORD said to him, "Get up and go down to the camp, because I have given it into your hand."
"But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant."
"You will hear what they say, and then your hands will be strong, and you will go down to the camp." So Gideon and his servant Purah went down to the edge of the armed men in the camp.

The Midianites, Amalekites, and all the people of the east were lying in the valley. There were so many of them, like locusts. Their camels could not be counted; they were as many as the sand on the seashore.

When Gideon arrived, a man was telling his friend about a dream. He said, "I dreamed that a loaf of barley bread rolled into the Midianite camp. It came to a tent, struck it, and the tent fell. It turned the tent upside down, and the tent collapsed."
His friend answered, "This can only mean the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has given Midian and the whole camp into his hand."
When Gideon heard the dream and its meaning, he bowed in worship. Then he returned to the Israelite camp and said, "Get up, for the LORD has given the Midianite camp into your hands."
He divided the 300 men into three groups. He gave each man a trumpet and an empty jar with a torch inside it.
He said to them, "Watch me and do what I do. When I reach the edge of the camp, do as I do."
"I and all who are with me will blow our trumpets. Then you also blow your trumpets all around the camp and shout, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"
Gideon and the 100 men with him came to the edge of the camp at the start of the middle watch, just as the guards had been posted. They blew their trumpets and broke the jars in their hands.
The three groups blew their trumpets and broke their jars. They held torches in their left hands and trumpets in their right hands to blow them. They shouted, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
Each man stood in his place around the camp. The whole camp ran, cried out, and fled.

When the 300 trumpets sounded, the LORD caused every man to turn his sword against his companion throughout the camp. The army fled to Beth Shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel Meholah by Tabbath.
The men of Israel from Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh were called out, and they pursued the Midianites.

Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim. He said, "Come down to meet Midian, and take control of the waters of the Jordan before they reach Beth Barah." So all the men of Ephraim were called out. They took control of the waters of the Jordan as far as Beth Barah.

They captured Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. They pursued Midian and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the Jordan.
The men of Ephraim said to Gideon, "What have you done to us? Why didn't you call us when you went to fight Midian?" They argued with him fiercely.
Gideon answered, "What have I done compared with you? Aren't the leftovers of Ephraim better than the full grape harvest of Abiezer?
God gave Oreb and Zeeb, the Midianite leaders, into your hands. What could I have done compared with you?" After he said this, their anger against him died down.
Gideon and his three hundred men came to the Jordan River. They were tired, but they kept chasing the enemy.
Gideon said to the men of Succoth, "Please give some bread to the men with me. They are tired, and I am chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
The leaders of Succoth asked, "Are Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand? Why should we give bread to your army?"
Gideon said, "When the LORD gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your skin with thorns and briers from the desert."
From there he went up to Penuel and asked them the same thing. The men of Penuel answered him the same way the men of Succoth had.
So he said to the men of Penuel, "When I come back safely, I will tear down this tower."
Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their army. About fifteen thousand men were left from the armies of the eastern peoples. One hundred twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen.
Gideon went up by the road used by the people who live in tents east of Nobah and Jogbehah. He attacked the camp while it felt safe.
Zebah and Zalmunna ran away, but Gideon chased them and captured the two Midianite kings. He also scattered their whole army.
