Jehoiakim paid the silver and gold to Pharaoh Neco. To raise the money, he taxed the land and collected the silver and gold from the people of the land, each man paying his share.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother was Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah; she was from Rumah.
He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his fathers had done.
In Jehoiakim's days, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came up. Jehoiakim served him for three years, but then he turned and rebelled.
The LORD sent Babylonian, Aramean, Moabite, and Ammonite raiders against him. He sent them to destroy Judah, just as the LORD had said through His prophets.
This happened to Judah only because the LORD commanded it. He wanted to remove them from His sight because of Manasseh's sins and everything he had done.
Manasseh had also killed innocent people and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. The LORD would not forgive that.
The rest of Jehoiakim's acts and everything he did are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
Jehoiakim died and was buried with his ancestors. His son Jehoiachin became king in his place.
The king of Egypt did not march out of his land again, because the king of Babylon had taken everything from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River that had belonged to Egypt.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for three months. His mother's name was Nehushta. She was the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father had done.
At that time, the servants of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, went up to Jerusalem. The city was surrounded.
Nebuchadnezzar himself came to the city while his servants were besieging it.

Jehoiachin, king of Judah, went out to the king of Babylon. He took his mother, his servants, his officials, and his eunuchs with him. The king of Babylon captured him in the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign.

He carried out all the treasures from the LORD's house and from the king's house. He also cut up all the gold articles that Solomon, king of Israel, had made for the LORD's temple, just as the LORD had said.
He carried all Jerusalem into exile. He took all the officials, all the mighty warriors, all the craftsmen, and all the smiths—ten thousand captives. Only the poorest people in the land were left.
He sent Jehoiachin to Babylon. He also took the king's mother, the king's wives, his officials, and the leading men of the land from Jerusalem to Babylon.
The king of Babylon brought to Babylon all seven thousand soldiers, all one thousand craftsmen and smiths, and every strong, battle-ready man.
The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place. He changed his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother's name was Hamutal. She was the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
Because of the LORD's anger, this happened to Jerusalem and Judah until He drove them from His presence. Zedekiah also rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of King Zedekiah's rule, on the tenth day of the tenth month, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his whole army. They camped outside the city and built siege works all around it.
The city stayed under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah's rule.
By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city had become so bad that the people had no food.

Then the city wall was broken through. At night the whole army fled through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, even though the Babylonians were all around the city. They fled toward the Arabah, a dry desert valley.
But the Babylonian army chased the king and caught him on the plains of Jericho. All his soldiers scattered.
They captured him and took him to King Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where he was sentenced.
They killed Zedekiah's sons in front of him. Then they put out his eyes, tied him with bronze chains, and took him to Babylon.
On the seventh day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar's rule, Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard and an official of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He burned down the temple of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses in Jerusalem. He burned every important building.
The whole Babylonian army under the commander tore down the walls around Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan carried into exile the people still left in the city, along with the rest of the people and those who had gone over to the king of Babylon.
But he left behind some of the poorest people to work the vineyards and fields.
The Babylonians broke up the bronze pillars, the movable stands, and the great bronze basin called the Sea in the temple of the LORD. They carried all that bronze to Babylon.
They also took the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, dishes, and all the bronze tools used in the temple service.
The commander took the incense pans and the sprinkling bowls, both gold and silver.
The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea, and the movable stands that Solomon had made for the temple of the LORD was too heavy to weigh.
Each pillar was about 27 feet tall. The bronze top on one pillar was about 4.5 feet high and was decorated with a network and bronze pomegranates all around. The second pillar was the same.
The commander took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three gatekeepers.
From the people still in the city, he took the officer in charge of the soldiers, five of the king's close advisers, the secretary in charge of drafting people, and sixty men found in the city.
Nebuzaradan took them all to King Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah.
There, in the land of Hamath, the king had them put to death. So Judah was carried away from its land into captivity.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon put Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, in charge of the people left in Judah.

When the army officers and their men heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, they came to him at Mizpah. They were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from Netophah, Jaazaniah son of the Maakathite, and their men.
Gedaliah swore to them and their men, "Do not be afraid of the Babylonian officials. Settle down in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you."

But in the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, who was from the royal family, came with ten men. They attacked and killed Gedaliah and his men, both the Jews and the Babylonians who were with him at Mizpah.
Then all the people, no matter their status, along with the army officers, fled to Egypt because they were afraid of the Babylonians.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in his first year as king, released Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.
He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor above the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes and ate at the king's table for the rest of his life.
Day by day the king gave him a regular allowance as long as he lived.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites, and the Rodanites.
The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty warrior on the earth.
Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites,
Pathrusites, Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came), and Caphtorites.
Canaan was the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and of the Hittites,
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram; Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.
Two sons were born to Eber. One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided. His brother was named Joktan.
Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
These are their family lines: Nebaioth, Ishmael's firstborn, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were the sons of Ishmael.
The sons born to Keturah, Abraham's concubine: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were descendants of Keturah.
Abraham was the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam. Timna was Lotan's sister.
The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
The sons of Anah: Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These are the kings who ruled in the land of Edom before any king ruled over the Israelites: Bela son of Beor. His city was named Dinhabah.
When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah ruled in his place.
When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites ruled in his place.
When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad ruled in his place. He had defeated Midian in the country of Moab. His city was named Avith.
When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah ruled in his place.
When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the River ruled in his place.
When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Achbor ruled in his place.
When Baal-hanan died, Hadad ruled in his place. His city was named Pai. His wife's name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
When Hadad died, the chiefs of Edom were: Chief Timna, Chief Alvah, Chief Jetheth,
Chief Oholibamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinon,
Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mibzar,
Chief Magdiel, and Chief Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.
These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
The other sons were Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
Judah had three sons by Bath-shua the Canaanite: Er, Onan, and Shelah. Er was Judah's firstborn, and he was wicked in the sight of the LORD, so He put him to death.
Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. In all, Judah had five sons.
The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara—five in all.
The son of Carmi was Achar, who brought trouble on Israel by taking what was set apart for destruction.
The son of Ethan was Azariah.
The sons born to Hezron were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.
Ram was the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, the leader of the sons of Judah.
Nahshon was the father of Salmon, and Salmon was the father of Boaz.
Boaz was the father of Obed, and Obed was the father of Jesse.
Jesse was the father of Eliab his firstborn, Abinadab the second, and Shimea the third.
Nethanel was the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, and David the seventh.
Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah had three sons: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
Abigail was the mother of Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb son of Hezron had children by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth. Her sons were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.
Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri was the father of Bezalel.
Later, Hezron married the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead, when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub.
Segub was the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
But Geshur and Aram took Havvoth-jair from them, along with Kenath and its sixty villages. All these were descendants of Machir, the father of Gilead.
After Hezron died at Caleb-ephrathah, his wife Abijah bore him Ashhur, the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn, were Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah; she was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram, Jerahmeel's firstborn, were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai were Nadab and Abishur.
Abishur's wife was named Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
The sons of Nadab were Seled and Appaim. Seled died without children.
The son of Appaim was Ishi. The son of Ishi was Sheshan. The son of Sheshan was Ahlai.
The sons of Jada, Shammai's brother, were Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without children.
The sons of Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza. These were the descendants of Jerahmeel.
Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. He had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to his servant Jarha, and she bore him Attai.
Attai was the father of Nathan, and Nathan was the father of Zabad.
Zabad was the father of Ephlal, and Ephlal was the father of Obed.
Obed was the father of Jehu, and Jehu was the father of Azariah.
Azariah was the father of Helez, and Helez was the father of Eleasah.
Eleasah was the father of Sismai, and Sismai was the father of Shallum.
Shallum was the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah was the father of Elishama.
The sons of Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, were Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah, the father of Hebron.
The sons of Hebron were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema was the father of Raham, the father of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai.
The son of Shammai was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth-zur.
Caleb's concubine Ephah bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran was the father of Gazez.
The sons of Jahdai were Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Caleb's concubine Maacah bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
She also bore Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, and Sheva, the father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
These were the descendants of Caleb. The sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, were Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim,
Salma, the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph, the father of Beth-gader.
Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim, had sons: Haroeh, half of the Manahathites,
and the families of Kiriath-jearim: the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites. From these came the Zorathites and Eshtaolites.
The sons of Salma were Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, half of the Manahathites, and the Zorites.
The families of scribes who lived at Jabez were the Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites. These are the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
These were the sons of David born to him in Hebron: Amnon the firstborn, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite; Daniel the second, by Abigail the Carmelite;
Absalom the third, by Maachah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; Adonijah the fourth, by Haggith;
Shephatiah the fifth, by Abital; and Ithream the sixth, by his wife Eglah.
Six sons were born to him in Hebron. He ruled there seven years and six months, and he ruled in Jerusalem thirty-three years.
These were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon—four by Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel.
All these were sons of David, besides the sons of his concubines, and Tamar their sister.
Solomon; Rehoboam his son; Abijah his son; Asa his son; Jehoshaphat his son.
Joram his son; Ahaziah his son; Joash his son.
Amaziah his son; Azariah his son; Jotham his son.
Ahaz his son; Hezekiah his son; Manasseh his son.
Amon his son; Josiah his son.
The sons of Josiah were Johanan the firstborn, Jehoiakim the second, Zedekiah the third, and Shallum the fourth.
The sons of Jehoiakim were Jeconiah his son and Zedekiah his son.
The sons of Jeconiah the captive: Shealtiel his son.
Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. The son of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister.
Also Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed—five.
The sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah; the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, and the sons of Shecaniah.
The sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat—six.
The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam—three.
The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani—seven.
The sons of Judah were Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah, Shobal's son, was the father of Jahath, and Jahath was the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These were the families of the Zorathites.
These were Etam's sons: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. Their sister was named Hazzelelponi.
Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer was the father of Hushah. These were the sons of Hur, Ephrathah's firstborn and the father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah gave birth to Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were Naarah's sons.
Helah's sons were Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
Koz was the father of Anub and Zobebah, and of the families of Aharhel son of Harum.
Jabez was more honored than his brothers. His mother named him Jabez, saying, "I gave birth to him in pain."

Jabez called on the God of Israel. He said, "If You will truly bless me and enlarge my territory, and if Your hand is with me, and You keep me from harm, then I won't be in pain." And God granted his request.
Chelub, Shuhah's brother, was the father of Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.
Eshton was the father of Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, who was the father of Ir-nahash. These were the men of Recah.
Kenaz's sons were Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel's son was Hathath.
Meonothai was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, who was the father of Ge-harashim, because they were craftsmen.
Caleb son of Jephunneh had sons named Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah's son was Kenaz.
Jehallelel's sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
Ezrah's sons were Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered's wife gave birth to Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, who was the father of Eshtemoa.

His Judahite wife gave birth to Jered, who was the father of Gedor; Heber, who was the father of Soco; and Jekuthiel, who was the father of Zanoah. These were the sons of Pharaoh's daughter Bithiah, whom Mered had married.
The sons of Hodiah's wife, Naham's sister, were the fathers of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
Shimon's sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon. Ishi's sons were Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.
Shelah's sons, Judah's son, were Er, who was the father of Lecah, and Laadah, who was the father of Mareshah. The families of linen workers at Beth-ashbea also came from them.
There were also Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and Saraph, who ruled in Moab and Jashubi-lehem. These records are old.
They were potters who lived in Netaim and Gederah. They stayed there with the king and worked for him.
Simeon's sons were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
Shaul's son was Shallum. His son was Mibsam. His son was Mishma.
Mishma's son was Hammuel. His son was Zaccur. His son was Shimei.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters. His brothers didn't have many children, so their whole family didn't grow as much as Judah's children.
They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual,
Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri, and Shaaraim. These were their towns until David became king.
Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan—five towns in all.
They also had all the villages around these towns as far as Baal. These were their homes, and they kept their family records.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah son of Seraiah son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
Ziza son of Shiphi son of Allon son of Jedaiah son of Shimri son of Shemaiah.
These men, listed by name, were leaders in their families, and their fathers' houses grew greatly.
They went to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley, to find pasture for their flocks.
They found rich, good pasture. The land was wide, quiet, and peaceful, because the Hamites had lived there before.

These men, listed by name, came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. They attacked the tents and the Meunites found there. They destroyed them completely, and they have stayed there to this day, because there was pasture for their flocks.
Five hundred of these Simeonites went to Mount Seir. Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, led them.
They struck down the rest of the Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.

The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, were listed first because Reuben was the oldest. But his birthright was given to Joseph's sons, since Reuben had disgraced his father by sleeping with his father's concubine. So Reuben was not counted as the firstborn in the family records.
Judah became the strongest of his brothers, and the ruler came from him. Still, the birthright belonged to Joseph.
Reuben's sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Joel's sons were Shemaiah, then Gog, then Shimei.
Then came Micah, Reaiah, and Baal.
Beerah was carried away by Tilgath-pilneser, king of Assyria. He was a leader of the Reubenites.
Their relatives were listed by family groups and family lines. Jeiel was the chief, and Zechariah came next.
Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel, lived in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal Meon.
He settled eastward as far as the edge of the desert near the Euphrates River, because they had many animals in Gilead.
In Saul's days, they fought the Hagrites. They won and lived in the Hagrites' tents all across the east side of Gilead.
The Gadites lived across from them in Bashan, as far as Salcah.
Joel was chief, Shapham was second, then Jaanai and Shaphat in Bashan.
Their relatives, by family groups, were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber—seven in all.
These were sons of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.
Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, was chief of their family groups.
They lived in Gilead, Bashan, its towns, and all the pasturelands of Sharon, to their borders.
All of them were recorded in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.
The Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh had 44,760 soldiers. They were brave men who carried shields and swords, drew bows, and knew how to fight.
They fought the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
They cried to God in battle. He helped them, and the Hagrites and everyone with them were handed over to them, because they trusted in Him. God answered their prayers.
They took 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, and 100,000 captives.
Many of the enemy died, because the battle was God's. They lived in the enemy's place until the exile.
Half of Manasseh lived in the land from Bashan to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon. They were many.
Their family leaders were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were strong warriors, famous men, and heads of their families.
They were unfaithful to the God of their fathers. They worshiped the gods of the people of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.

So the God of Israel stirred up Pul king of Assyria and Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria. They carried away the Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh. They brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the Gozan River, where they are to this day.
The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Amram were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar was the father of Phinehas. Phinehas was the father of Abishua.
Abishua was the father of Bukki. Bukki was the father of Uzzi.
Uzzi was the father of Zerahiah. Zerahiah was the father of Meraioth.
Meraioth was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah. Azariah was the father of Johanan.
Johanan was the father of Azariah. This Azariah served as priest in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Shallum.
Shallum was the father of Hilkiah. Hilkiah was the father of Azariah.
Azariah was the father of Seraiah. Seraiah was the father of Jehozadak.
Jehozadak went into exile when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile under Nebuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi were Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of Gershom's sons: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These are the Levite clans by their families.
For Gershom: Libni was his son, Jahath was his son, Zimmah was his son,
Joah was his son, Iddo was his son, Zerah was his son, and Jeatherai was his son.
The sons of Kohath were Amminadab his son, Korah his son, and Assir his son.
Elkanah was his son, Ebiasaph was his son, and Assir was his son.
Tahath was his son, Uriel was his son, Uzziah was his son, and Shaul was his son.
The sons of Elkanah were Amasai and Ahimoth.
Elkanah was his son, Elkanah was his son, Zophai was his son, and Nahath was his son.
Eliab was his son, Jeroham was his son, and Elkanah was his son.
The sons of Samuel were Joel, the firstborn, and Abijah.
The sons of Merari were Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,
Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, and Asaiah his son.
These are the men David put in charge of music in the LORD's house after the ark came to rest.
They served as musicians before the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, until Solomon built the LORD's house in Jerusalem. They did their work as ordered.
These are the ones who served, with their sons: From the Kohathites came Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel,
son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,
son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,
son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,
son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,
son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.
Heman's brother Asaph stood at his right. Asaph was the son of Berechiah, son of Shimea,
son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah,
son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah,
son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,
son of Jahath, son of Gershom, son of Levi.
On the left stood their brothers, the sons of Merari: Ethan son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,
son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer,
son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
Their fellow Levites were given to all the service of the tabernacle, the house of God.

But Aaron and his sons did all the work of the Most Holy Place. They burned offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense, and they made atonement for Israel, as Moses the servant of God had commanded.
These are the descendants of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
Zadok his son, and Ahimaaz his son.
These are their settlements by their territory: for the sons of Aaron of the Kohathite clan, because the lot fell to them.
They were given Hebron in Judah, with its pasturelands around it.
But the fields and villages around the city were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
To the sons of Aaron they gave Hebron, a city of refuge, and Libnah with its pasturelands, Jattir, and Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
Hilen with its pasturelands, Debir with its pasturelands,
Ashan with its pasturelands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Benjamin they received Geba with its pasturelands, Alemeth with its pasturelands, and Anathoth with its pasturelands. In all, there were thirteen cities for their families.
The rest of the Kohathites received ten cities by lot from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The Gershomites received thirteen cities from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh in Bashan.
The Merarites received twelve cities by lot from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
So the Israelites gave these cities and their pasturelands to the Levites.
They assigned by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin the cities named above.
Some of the Kohathite families received cities from the tribe of Ephraim.
They were given Shechem, a city of refuge, in the hill country of Ephraim, with its pasturelands, Gezer with its pasturelands,
Jokmeam with its pasturelands, Beth-horon with its pasturelands,
Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh, the rest of the Kohathite families received Aner with its pasturelands and Bileam with its pasturelands.
The Gershomites received Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands and Ashtaroth with its pasturelands from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
From Issachar they received Kedesh with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands,
Ramoth with its pasturelands, and Anem with its pasturelands.
From Asher they received Mashal with its pasturelands, Abdon with its pasturelands,
Hukok with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands.
From Naphtali they received Kedesh in Galilee with its pasturelands, Hammon with its pasturelands, and Kiriathaim with its pasturelands.
The remaining Merarites received from Zebulun Rimmono with its pasturelands and Tabor with its pasturelands.
From Reuben, across the Jordan east of Jericho, they received Bezer in the wilderness with its pasturelands, Jahzah with its pasturelands,
Kedemoth with its pasturelands, and Mephaath with its pasturelands.
From Gad they received Ramoth in Gilead with its pasturelands, Mahanaim with its pasturelands,
Heshbon with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands.
The sons of Issachar were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron. That was four sons.
Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel. They were leaders of their families. In David's time, Tola's family line had 22,600 brave soldiers listed in their family records.
Uzzi's son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah's sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah. All five of them were family leaders.
Their family lines also had 36,000 soldiers ready for war. They had many wives and children.
All their relatives from every Issachar family were brave soldiers. In all, 87,000 men were listed in their family records.
Benjamin's sons were Bela, Beker, and Jediael. That was three sons.
Bela's sons were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. These five men were family leaders. They were strong fighters, and their family records listed 22,034 men.
Beker's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All of these were Beker's sons.
Their family records listed them as family leaders. There were 20,200 strong fighters.
Jediael's son was Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these men were Jediael's sons. They were family leaders and strong fighters. Their records listed 17,200 men who could go to war.
Shuppim and Huppim were sons of Ir. Hushim was the son of Aher.
Naphtali's sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They were the sons of Bilhah.
Manasseh's son was Asriel. His Aramean concubine gave birth to him. She also gave birth to Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife from the Huppites and Shuppites. His sister was named Maacah. Another descendant was named Zelophehad, and he had only daughters.
Machir's wife Maacah gave birth to a son. She named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh. Sheresh's sons were Ulam and Rakem.
Ulam's son was Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.
Machir's sister Hammoleketh gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
Shemida's sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
Ephraim's sons were Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, and Tahath his son.
Zabad was his son, and Shuthelah was his son. Ezer and Elead were killed by men from Gath who were born in that land. They had gone down to steal livestock.
Their father Ephraim mourned for many days. His relatives came to comfort him.
Then he slept with his wife. She became pregnant and gave birth to a son. He named him Beriah, because trouble had come to his house.
His daughter was Sheerah. She built Lower Beth-horon, Upper Beth-horon, and Uzzen-sheerah.
Her descendants included Rephah, Resheph, Telah, and Tahan.
Ladan was his son, Ammihud was his son, and Elishama was his son.
Nun was his son, and Joshua was his son.
Their land and towns included Bethel and its villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its villages to the west, and Shechem and its villages as far as Ayyah and its villages.

Along the border of Manasseh were Beth-shean and its villages, Taanach and its villages, Megiddo and its villages, and Dor and its villages. The descendants of Joseph, the son of Israel, lived in these towns.
Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.
Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel. Malchiel was the father of Birzaith.
Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.
Japhlet's sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were Japhlet's sons.
Shemer's sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
The sons of Helem, his brother, were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
Zophah's sons were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, and Imrah.
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera were also his sons.
Jether's sons were Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
Ulla's sons were Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
All these were Asher's descendants. They were family leaders, chosen strong fighters, and leaders among the princes. Their family records listed 26,000 men who could fight in war.
Benjamin had these sons: Bela, his firstborn; Ashbel, second; Aharah, third;
Bela had these sons: Addar, Gera, and Abihud;
These were Ehud's sons. They were family leaders of the people who lived in Geba, and they were moved to Manahath.
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera moved them, and Gera had Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim had children in the land of Moab after he sent away his wives, Hushim and Baara.
By his wife Hodesh, he had Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, and Malcam.
He also had Jeuz, Sakiah, and Mirmah. These were his sons and family leaders.
From Hushim, he had Abitub and Elpaal.
Elpaal's sons were Eber, Misham, and Shemed. Shemed built the towns of Ono and Lod and their villages.
Beriah and Shema were family leaders of the people who lived in Aijalon. They drove out the people of Gath.
Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were the sons of Beriah.
Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were the sons of Elpaal;
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were the sons of Shimei.
Iphdeiah and Penuel were the sons of Shashak.
Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were the sons of Jeroham.
These were family leaders and chiefs. By their family lines, they lived in Jerusalem.
Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife's name was Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon. Then came Zur, Kish, Baal, and Nadab.
He also had Gedor, Ahio, and Zechar.
Mikloth had Shimeah. They also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner had Kish. Kish had Saul. Saul had Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal had Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz had Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah had Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri had Moza.
Moza had Binea. Raphah was his son, Eleasah was his son, and Azel was his son.
Azel had six sons: Azrikam, his firstborn; Bocheru; Ishmael; Sheariah; Obadiah; and Hanan. All of these were Azel's sons.
Azel's brother, Eshek, had these sons: Ulam, his firstborn; Jeush, second; and Eliphelet, third.
Ulam's sons were mighty warriors and archers. They had many sons and grandsons, one hundred fifty in all. All of these were Benjaminites.
All Israel was listed by family history. These records were written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. Judah was taken to Babylon because they were not faithful to God.
The first people to live again in their own towns were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
Some people from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem.
Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, was from the family line of Perez son of Judah.
From the Shilonites came Asaiah the firstborn and his sons.
From the Zerahites came Jeuel and 690 of their relatives.
From the Benjamites came Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah.
Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah.
Their family records showed 956 relatives. All these men were leaders of their family groups.
From the priests came Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.
Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, was the chief official of God's house.
Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah, and Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer, were also there.
They and their relatives were 1,760 strong, capable men. They were leaders of their family groups and did the work of serving in God's house.
From the Levites came Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, from the Merarites.
Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph.
Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of Netophah.
The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives. Shallum was the leader.
They served at the king's east gate. They were gatekeepers for the Levite camps.

Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his relatives from his father's house, the Korahites, were in charge of guarding the entrances to the tent. Their ancestors had guarded the entrance to the camp of the the LORD.
Phinehas son of Eleazar had been their leader in the past, and the the LORD was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
All these chosen gatekeepers numbered 212. They were listed by family history in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had appointed them to their trusted positions.
They and their sons guarded the gates of the the LORD's house, the tent.
The gatekeepers stood on four sides: east, west, north, and south.
Their relatives in their villages came to serve with them for seven days at a time.
The four chief gatekeepers were Levites. They were trusted with the rooms and storerooms of God's house.
They stayed around God's house because they were in charge of guarding it. They opened it every morning.
Some of them were in charge of the utensils used in worship. They counted them when they were brought in and when they were taken out.
Others were put in charge of the furniture and all the holy utensils, as well as the fine flour, wine, oil, incense, and spices.
Some of the priests mixed the spices.
Mattithiah, a Levite and the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was trusted with baking the flat cakes.
Some of their relatives from the Kohathites were in charge of setting out the bread that was replaced every Sabbath.
The musicians were family leaders of the Levites. They stayed in the rooms and were free from other work, because they served day and night.
These were the family leaders of the Levites. They lived in Jerusalem.
Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife was named Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon. His other sons were Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Mikloth became the father of Shimeam. They also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-baal. Merib-baal became the father of Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea.
Ahaz became the father of Jarah. Jarah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri became the father of Moza.
Moza became the father of Binea. Rephaiah was his son, Eleasah was his son, and Azel was his son.
Azel had six sons. Their names were Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel's sons.
The Philistines fought against Israel. The Israelites ran away, and many fell dead on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines chased Saul and his sons and killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
The fighting grew hard around Saul. The archers found him, and he was badly wounded.

Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and kill me with it. I don't want these godless men to come and mistreat me." But the armor-bearer was very afraid and refused. So Saul took his own sword and killed himself with it.
When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on his sword and died.
So Saul, his three sons, and his whole family died together.
When the Israelites in the valley saw that their army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they left their cities and ran away. The Philistines moved in and lived there.
The next day, the Philistines came to strip the dead. They found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
They stripped Saul, took his head and armor, and sent word throughout Philistia to tell their idols and their people.
They put his armor in the temple of their gods and put his head on display in the temple of Dagon.
When the people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
all their brave men went and took the bodies of Saul and his sons. They brought them to Jabesh and buried their bones under the oak tree there. Then they fasted for seven days.
Saul died because he was unfaithful to the LORD. He did not keep the LORD's word, and he even asked a medium for advice.
He did not ask the LORD for help. So the LORD put him to death and gave his kingdom to David, the son of Jesse.
All Israel gathered around David at Hebron and said, "Look, we are your own people.
Even when Saul was king, you led Israel out and brought them back. The LORD your God said to you, 'You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over My people Israel.'"
So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron. David made a covenant with them there before the LORD, and they anointed David king over Israel, just as the LORD had promised through Samuel.
David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, which was Jebus, where the Jebusites lived.
The Jebusites said to David, "You will not come in here." But David captured the stronghold of Zion, which is the City of David.
David had said, "Whoever strikes the Jebusites first will become chief and commander." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, so he became chief.
David lived in the stronghold, so they called it the City of David.
He built up the city all around, from the Millo to the surrounding wall, and Joab rebuilt the rest of the city.
David became greater and greater, and the LORD of Hosts was with him.
These were the chiefs of David's mighty warriors who helped make him king over all Israel, as the LORD had promised.
This is the list of David's mighty warriors: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the Thirty, raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them at one time.
After him came Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men.
He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gathered for battle in a field full of barley. The people fled from the Philistines.
But they took their stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. The LORD saved them with a great victory.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down to David at the rock, to the cave of Adullam, while the Philistine army camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was in the stronghold then, and the Philistine camp was in Bethlehem.
David longed for water and said, "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem by the gate!"

So the three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well of Bethlehem by the gate, carried it back, and gave it to David. But David would not drink it. Instead, he poured it out to the LORD.

He said, "I would never do that, my God. I cannot drink water that cost these men their lives. They brought it at the risk of their lives." So he would not drink it. These were the deeds of the three mighty men.
Abishai, Joab's brother, was chief of the Three. He raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and he became famous among the Three.
He was more honored than the Thirty and became their commander, but he was not one of the Three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did many great things. He struck down two sons of Ariel of Moab. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

He struck down an Egyptian who was seven and a half feet tall. The Egyptian had a spear like a weaver's beam, but Benaiah went down to him with a club, snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.
These were the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he became famous among the three mighty men.
He was more honored than the Thirty, but he was not one of the Three. David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
The other mighty warriors were Asahel, Joab's brother; Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem;
Shammoth the Harorite; Helez the Pelonite;
Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; Abiezer the Anathothite;
Sibbecai the Hushathite; Ilai the Ahohite;
Maharai the Netophathite; Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite;
Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjamites; Benaiah the Pirathonite;
Hurai from the valleys of Gaash; Abiel the Arbathite;
Azmaveth the Baharumite; Eliahba the Shaalbonite;
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite; Jonathan son of Shageh the Hararite;
Ahiam son of Sacar the Hararite; Eliphal son of Ur;
Hepher the Mecherathite; Ahijah the Pelonite.
Hezro the Carmelite; Naarai son of Ezbai;
Joel brother of Nathan; Mibhar son of Hagri;
Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai the Beerothite, armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah;
Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
Uriah the Hittite; Zabad son of Ahlai;
Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, a leader among the Reubenites, with thirty men with him;
Hanan son of Maacah; Joshaphat the Mithnite;
Uzzia the Ashterathite; Shama and Jeiel, sons of Hotham the Aroerite;
Jediael son of Shimri; Joha his brother, the Tizite;
Eliel the Mahavite; Jeribai and Joshaviah, sons of Elnaam; Ithmah the Moabite;
Eliel; Obed; and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
These are the men who came to David at Ziklag while he was still kept from Saul son of Kish. They were among the mighty warriors who helped in war.
They were bowmen who could shoot with either hand, throwing stones or shooting arrows from a bow. They were from Saul's relatives in Benjamin.
Ahiezer was the leader, along with Joash, sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Berachah; and Jehu the Anathothite.
Ishmaiah the Gibeonite was a hero among the Thirty and their leader. Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite also came.
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite came.
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam the Korahites came.
Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham from Gedor, came.

Some Gadites joined David at his stronghold in the wilderness. They were brave soldiers, trained for war, who knew how to use shield and spear. Their faces were as fierce as lions, and they ran as fast as gazelles on the mountains.
Ezer was the leader, Obadiah was second, Eliab was third,
Mishmannah was fourth, Jeremiah was fifth,
Attai was sixth, Eliel was seventh,
Johanan was eighth, Elzabad was ninth,
Jeremiah was tenth, and Machbannai was eleventh.
These Gadites were army officers. The least led one hundred men, and the greatest led one thousand.
They crossed the Jordan in the first month, when the river overflowed its banks. They chased away everyone living in the valleys to the east and to the west.
Some men from Benjamin and Judah also came to David at the stronghold.

David went out to meet them and said, "If you have come to me in peace to help me, I will join with you wholeheartedly. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies, even though I have done no wrong, the God of our fathers will see it and judge."

Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the Thirty, and he said, "We belong to you, David, and we are with you, son of Jesse. Peace, peace to you, and peace to those who help you, for your God has helped you." David accepted them and made them leaders of his troops.

Some Manassites came over to David when he went with the Philistines to fight Saul. But they did not help the Philistines, because the Philistine rulers sent David away. They said, "He might turn against us and go back to his master Saul, and then we would lose our heads."
As David traveled to Ziklag, these Manassites joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, leaders of thousands from Manasseh.
They helped David fight raiders, because all of them were brave soldiers and army commanders.
Day after day men came to help David, until his army was as large as God's army.
These are the numbers of armed leaders who came to David at Hebron to turn Saul's kingdom over to him, as the LORD had said.
From Judah: 6,800 armed men ready for war, carrying shields and spears.
From Simeon: 7,100 brave soldiers ready for war.
Jehoiada, leader of Aaron's family, came with 3,700 men.
Zadok, a brave young warrior, came with 22 leaders from his father's family.
From Benjamin, Saul's own tribe, came 3,000 men. Until then, most of them had guarded Saul's family.
From Ephraim: 20,800 brave soldiers, famous men in their family groups.
From half the tribe of Manasseh: 18,000 men chosen by name to come and make David king.
From Issachar: 200 leaders who understood the times and knew what Israel should do. All their relatives followed their orders.
From Zebulun: 50,000 soldiers ready for war, armed with every kind of weapon and fully committed.
From Naphtali: 1,000 commanders, along with 37,000 men with shields and spears.
From Dan: 28,600 men ready for battle.
From Asher: 40,000 soldiers ready to fight.
From east of the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh: 120,000 men armed with every kind of weapon.
All these soldiers came to Hebron ready to fight. They came with one purpose: to make David king over all Israel. The rest of Israel also agreed with one heart to make David king.
They stayed there three days, eating and drinking with David, because their relatives had prepared food for them.

Their neighbors, as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. They brought flour, fig cakes, raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in large amounts, because there was joy in Israel.
David met with the commanders of thousands and hundreds and with all the other leaders.

David said to all the people of Israel, "If this seems good to you, and if it is from the LORD our God, let us send word to our brothers who are left in all the lands of Israel. Let the priests and Levites who live in their towns with pasturelands join them, and let them gather to us.
Let us bring back the ark of our God to us, because we did not ask about it during the days of Saul."
All the people agreed to do it, because they thought it was right.
David gathered all Israel from the Shihor in Egypt to Hamath to bring the ark of God from Kiriath Jearim.
David and all Israel went up to Baalah, which is Kiriath Jearim in Judah, to bring up the ark of God. It is the ark of the LORD, who sits between the cherubim—the ark that is called by His Name.
They carried the ark of God from Abinadab's house on a new cart. Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the cart.
David and all Israel were celebrating before God with all their might. They used songs, harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
When they came to the threshing floor at Kidon, Uzzah reached out his hand to hold the ark, because the oxen stumbled.
The LORD was angry with Uzzah and struck him down because he had put his hand on the ark. He died there before God.
David was angry because the LORD had punished Uzzah. So that place has been called Perez Uzzah to this day.
David was afraid of God that day. He said, "How can I bring the ark of God to me?"
So David did not take the ark to the City of David. Instead, he sent it to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
The ark of God stayed in Obed-Edom's house for three months. The LORD blessed Obed-Edom and all his household.
Hiram, king of Tyre, sent messengers to David. He also sent cedar wood, builders, and stone workers to build David a house.
David knew the the LORD had made him king over Israel. He also knew his kingdom was raised high for the sake of His people Israel.
David took more wives in Jerusalem, and he had more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children born to him there: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon;
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they came to look for him. David heard about it and went out to meet them.
The Philistines arrived and spread out across the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked God, "Should I go up against the Philistines? Will You give them to me?" The LORD answered him, "Go up, and I will give them into your hand."
David and his men went up to Baal Perazim. David defeated the Philistines there. He said, "God has broken through my enemies like a flood of water." So that place was called Baal Perazim.
The Philistines left their gods there. David ordered them burned, and they were burned in the fire.
The Philistines came again and spread out in the valley.
David asked God again. God said to him, "Do not go up after them. Circle around them and come at them from in front of the balsam trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then go out to battle. God has gone out before you to strike the Philistine camp."
David did what God had commanded. He and his men struck the Philistine camp from Gibeon to Gezer.
David became famous in all the lands. The LORD put fear of him in all the nations.
David built houses for himself in the city of David. He prepared a place for the ark of God and set up a tent for it.
Then David said, "No one but the Levites may carry the ark of God. the LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to serve Him forever."
David gathered all Israel in Jerusalem to bring the ark of the LORD to the place he had prepared.
He also gathered the sons of Aaron and the Levites.
From the Kohathites, Uriel was the leader, with 120 relatives.
From the Merarites, Asaiah was the leader, with 220 relatives.
From the Gershonites, Joel was the leader, with 130 relatives.
From the Elizaphanites, Shemaiah was the leader, with 200 relatives.
From the Hebronites, Eliel was the leader, with 80 relatives.
From the Uzzielites, Amminadab was the leader, with 112 relatives.
David called the priests Zadok and Abiathar, along with the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.
He said to them, "You are the heads of the Levite families. You and your brothers must become holy before God. Bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I prepared for it.
Because you did not carry it the first time, the LORD our God broke out against us. We did not seek Him in the proper way."
So the priests and Levites set themselves apart to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.
The Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with poles, as Moses had commanded by the word of the LORD.
David told the Levite leaders to appoint their fellow Levites as singers. They were to play harps, lyres, and cymbals loudly and raise a joyful sound.
The Levites appointed Heman son of Joel. From his relatives they appointed Asaph son of Berechiah. From the Merarites they appointed Ethan son of Kushaiah.
With them were their relatives of the second rank: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, the gatekeepers.
The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were to sound the bronze cymbals.
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah were to play harps in a high key.
Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to lead with lyres in a low key.
Chenaniah, leader of the Levites, was in charge of carrying the ark. He gave instructions because he understood the work.
Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.
The priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer blew trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers for the ark.
David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went joyfully to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-Edom.
Because God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David wore a fine linen robe. So did the Levites who carried the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, who led the carriers. David also wore a linen ephod.
All Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with shouting, the sound of a horn, trumpets, and cymbals. They also played harps and lyres.
As the ark of the covenant of the LORD came to the city of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked out a window. She saw King David dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.
They brought the ark of God and set it in the middle of the tent David had pitched for it. Then they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
When David finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the the LORD.
He gave every man and woman in Israel a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake.
David appointed some Levites to serve before the ark of the the LORD, to remember, to thank, and to praise the the LORD, the God of Israel.
Asaph was the leader, and Zechariah was second. Then came Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel. They played harps and lyres, while Asaph played the cymbals.
The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel blew trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of God.
That day David first gave this song of thanks to the the LORD through Asaph and his brothers:
“Give thanks to the the LORD. Call on His name. Tell the nations what He has done.
Sing to Him. Sing praise to Him. Tell of all His wonderful works.
Glory in His holy name. Let the hearts of those who seek the the LORD rejoice.
Seek the the LORD and His strength. Seek His face always.
Remember the wonders He has done, His miracles, and the judgments He spoke.
You are the descendants of Israel His servant, the children of Jacob, His chosen ones.
He is the the LORD our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember His covenant forever, the word He commanded for a thousand generations.
He made that covenant with Abraham and swore an oath to Isaac.
He confirmed it to Jacob as a statute, to Israel as an everlasting covenant.
He said, “I will give you the land of Canaan as your portion to inherit.”
When you were few in number, very few, and strangers in that land,
they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another.
He let no one oppress them. He rebuked kings for their sake:
“Do not touch My anointed ones. Do no harm to My prophets.”
Sing to the the LORD, all the earth. Proclaim His salvation day after day.
Declare His glory among the nations, His wonderful works among all peoples.
For the the LORD is great and worthy of great praise. He is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are idols, but the the LORD made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before Him. Strength and joy are in His place.
Give the the LORD glory and strength, families of the nations.
Give the the LORD the glory due His name. Bring an offering and come before Him. Worship the the LORD in holy splendor.
Tremble before Him, all the earth. The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved.
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad. Let them say among the nations, “The LORD reigns.”
Let the sea roar and all that fills it. Let the fields be joyful and everything in them.
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the the LORD, for He comes to judge the earth.
Give thanks to the the LORD, for He is good. His faithful love endures forever.
Say, “Save us, O God of our salvation. Gather us and deliver us from the nations, so that we may give thanks to Your holy name and praise You.”
Blessed be the the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Then all the people said, “Amen,” and praised the the LORD.
David left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the covenant of the the LORD to serve before the ark regularly, day by day.
Obed-edom and his sixty-eight relatives, along with Obed-edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah, served as gatekeepers.
David left Zadok the priest and his brothers, the priests, before the tabernacle of the the LORD at the high place in Gibeon.

They were to offer burnt offerings to the the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, and to do everything written in the Law of the the LORD, which He had commanded Israel.
With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and named to give thanks to the the LORD, because His faithful love endures forever.
Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for the musicians, and the other instruments for the songs of God. The sons of Jeduthun were gatekeepers.
Then all the people went to their homes, and David went home to bless his household.
When David was settled in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, "Look, I am living in a house of cedar, but the ark of the the LORD's covenant is under tent curtains."
Nathan said to David, "Do everything that is in your heart, for God is with you."
That night the word of God came to Nathan. He said,
"Go and tell My servant David, 'This is what the the LORD says: You will not build a house for Me to live in.'"
"For I have not lived in a house since the day I brought Israel up, until this day. I have moved from tent to tent and from one dwelling place to another.
In all the places I have moved with all Israel, did I ever say to any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd My people, 'Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?'"
"Now then, tell My servant David, 'This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be ruler over My people Israel.'
I have been with you wherever you have gone. I have cut off all your enemies before you, and I have made your name like the names of the greatest on earth."
"I will provide a place for My people Israel and plant them there, so they can have a home of their own and not be disturbed anymore. Wicked people will no longer trouble them, as they did before.
Since the time I appointed judges over My people Israel, I have subdued all your enemies. I also tell you that the the LORD will build a house for you."
"When your days are fulfilled and you go to be with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
He will build a house for Me, and I will establish his throne forever.
I will be his Father, and he will be My son. I will never take My faithful love away from him, as I removed it from the king who ruled before you.
I will set him over My house and My kingdom forever, and his throne will be established forever."
Nathan spoke to David all these words and this vision.
Then King David went in and sat before the the LORD and said, "Who am I, LORD God, and what is my family, that You have brought me this far?
This was a small thing in Your eyes, O God, yet You have spoken about the future of Your servant's house. You have treated me like a man of high rank, LORD God.
What more can David say to You to honor Your servant? You know Your servant."
"LORD, for Your servant's sake and according to Your will, You have done all this great work and made known all these great things.
LORD, there is no one like You, and there is no God besides You, according to all we have heard with our ears.

And who is like Your people Israel, the one nation on earth that God went out to redeem as His own people? You made a name for Yourself by doing great and awesome things, driving out nations before Your people whom You redeemed from Egypt."
"You made Your people Israel Your own people forever, and You, LORD, have become their God.
Now, LORD, let the word You have spoken about Your servant and his house come true forever. Do as You have said.

Let Your name be established and magnified forever, so people will say, 'The the LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel, the God over Israel,' and the house of Your servant David will be established before You."
"For You, my God, have revealed to Your servant that You will build a house for him. That is why Your servant has found courage to pray before You.
Now, LORD, You are God, and You have promised this good thing to Your servant.
Now You have been pleased to bless the house of Your servant, so it will last forever before You. For You, LORD, have blessed it, and it will be blessed forever."
After this, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them. He took Gath and its towns from the Philistines.
He defeated Moab, and the Moabites became David's servants and paid tribute.
David also defeated Hadadezer, king of Zobah, near Hamath, when he went to set up his rule by the Euphrates River.
David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. David hamstrung all the chariot horses but kept 100.
When Arameans from Damascus came to help Hadadezer, king of Zobah, David struck down 22,000 Arameans.
Then David placed military posts in Damascus of Aram, and the Arameans became servants to David and paid tribute. The LORD gave David victory everywhere he went.
David took the gold shields that had been on Hadadezer's servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
From Tibhath and Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took a very large amount of bronze. Solomon later made the bronze Sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels from it.
When Tou, king of Hamath, heard that David had defeated all the army of Hadadezer, king of Zobah,

he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him. Hadadezer had been at war with Tou. Hadoram brought articles of gold, silver, and bronze.
King David dedicated them to the the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations: Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.
Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He put military posts in Edom, and all the Edomites became servants to David. The LORD gave David victory everywhere he went.
David ruled over all Israel and did justice and righteousness for all his people.
Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was scribe.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites, and David's sons were chief officials at the king's side.
After this, Nahash, king of the Ammonites, died, and his son reigned in his place.

David said, "I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me." So David sent messengers to comfort him over his father's death. His servants arrived in the land of the Ammonites to comfort Hanun.

Then the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun, "Do you think David is honoring your father by sending comforters to you? Have his servants not come to you to explore the land, spy it out, and overthrow it?"
So Hanun seized David's servants, shaved them, cut their garments in half at the hips, and sent them away.
When someone told David what had happened, he sent messengers to meet the men, because they were deeply ashamed. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back, then return."
When the Ammonites realized they had made themselves hateful to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent 1,000 talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
They hired 32,000 chariots and the king of Maacah with his army. These forces came and camped near Medeba. The Ammonites also came out from their cities and gathered for battle.
When David heard about this, he sent Joab with the whole army of mighty men.
The Ammonites came out and lined up for battle at the entrance to their city, while the kings who had come stayed by themselves in the open country.
Joab saw that the battle was set against him both in front and behind, so he chose some of Israel's best fighters and lined them up against the Arameans.
He put the rest of the troops under the command of his brother Abishai, and they lined up against the Ammonites.
Joab said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you must come to my rescue; and if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will come to your rescue.
Be strong! Let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. Then the the LORD will do what is good in His eyes."
Joab and the troops with him advanced to fight the Arameans, and they fled before him.
When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled from Joab's brother Abishai and went back into the city. Then Joab returned to Jerusalem.
When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the Euphrates. Shophach, commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.
When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came to them. David lined up his men for battle against them, and they fought.
The Arameans fled from Israel. David killed 7,000 charioteers and 40,000 foot soldiers of the Arameans, and he killed Shophach, the commander of the army.
When Hadadezer's servants saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and became his subjects. The Arameans were no longer willing to help the Ammonites.

In the spring, when kings go out to war, Joab led the army. He destroyed the land of the Ammonites and went to Rabbah and besieged it. David stayed in Jerusalem. Joab attacked Rabbah and destroyed it.
David took the crown from the head of their king. It weighed a talent of gold, and it had a precious stone. It was placed on David's head. He also brought out a great amount of plunder from the city.
He brought out the people who were in it and made them work with saws, iron picks, and axes. David did this to all the Ammonite towns. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
Later, war broke out with the Philistines at Gezer. Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Sippai, one of the descendants of the Rephaim, and they were subdued.
There was another battle with the Philistines. Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite. His spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
There was another battle at Gath. There was a huge man who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He also was descended from the Rephaim.
He taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shimea, David's brother, struck him down.
These were descendants of the Rephaim in Gath. They fell by the hand of David and his men.
Satan turned against Israel and pushed David to count the Israelites.
David said to Joab and the commanders of the troops, "Go count the Israelites from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me the total so I will know how many there are."
Joab replied, "May the LORD make His people a hundred times more numerous. But, my lord the king, are they not all your servants? Why do you want this? Why should this bring guilt on Israel?"
But the king's order won out over Joab. So Joab left and traveled all over Israel. Then he came back to Jerusalem.
Joab gave David the number of men able to fight. In all Israel there were 1,100,000 men who could use a sword. Judah had 470,000 of them.
But Joab did not count Levi and Benjamin, because he hated the king's order.
God saw this order as evil, and He struck Israel.
David said to God, "I have sinned greatly by doing this. Now please take away the sin of Your servant. I have acted very foolishly."
The LORD spoke to Gad, David's prophet, and said,
"Go tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am giving you three choices. Pick one, and I will do it to you.'"
So Gad went to David and said, "This is what the LORD says: Choose one of these:

three years of famine; three months of being beaten by your enemies, with their swords chasing you; or three days of the LORD's sword and sickness in the land, while the angel of the LORD destroys all over Israel. Now decide what answer I should give the One who sent me."
David said to Gad, "I am in great trouble. Let me fall into the LORD's hand, because His mercy is very great. But do not let me fall into human hands."
So the LORD sent a plague on Israel, and 70,000 Israelites died.

God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. But as he was about to destroy it, the LORD saw it and changed His mind about the disaster. He said to the destroying angel, "That is enough! Stop! Put down your hand." The angel of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth with a sword drawn in his hand, stretched out over Jerusalem. David and the elders, wearing sackcloth, fell facedown.

David said to God, "Was it not I who ordered the people counted? I am the one who sinned and did wrong. But these sheep—what have they done? The LORD my God, please let Your hand fall on me and my family, not on Your people as a plague."
The angel of the LORD told Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
So David went up, just as Gad had said in the LORD's name.
Ornan was threshing wheat. He turned and saw the angel, and he and his four sons hid.
When David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David. He left the threshing floor and bowed with his face to the ground before David.
David said to Ornan, "Sell me the site of your threshing floor so I can build an altar to the LORD. Sell it to me at the full price, so the plague may stop for the people."

Ornan said to David, "Take it, my lord the king. Do what seems good to you. Look, I will give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing boards for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I have given everything."
King David replied to Ornan, "No, I insist on paying the full price. I will not take for the LORD what is yours, or offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing."
So David paid Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the site.
David built an altar to the LORD there. He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called on the LORD. The LORD answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.
Then the LORD told the angel, and the angel put his sword back in its sheath.
At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
The tabernacle of the LORD that Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering, were at that time at the high place in Gibeon.
But David could not go there to seek God, because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD.
David said, "This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel."
David ordered the foreigners living in Israel to be gathered. He also put stoneworkers in charge of cutting dressed stones to build God's house.
He prepared a large amount of iron for nails for the doors and gates and for metal brackets. He prepared so much bronze that it could not be weighed.
He had more cedar logs than anyone could count, because the people of Sidon and Tyre brought David a huge amount of cedar wood.

David said, "My son Solomon is young and inexperienced. The house to be built for the LORD must be very great, so that it brings honor and glory to His name in every land. So I will prepare for it." Then David prepared a great amount of material before he died.
Then he called for his son Solomon and commanded him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon, "My son, I wanted to build a house for the name of the LORD my God.
But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 'You have shed much blood and fought great wars. You will not build a house for My name, because you have shed so much blood on the earth before Me.

But a son will be born to you. He will be a man of peace, and I will give him rest from all his enemies around him. His name will be Solomon, and I will give peace and quiet to Israel during his days.
He will build a house for My name. He will be My son, and I will be his Father. I will make his royal throne firm over Israel forever.'
Now, my son, may the LORD be with you. May you succeed and build the house of the LORD your God, as He has spoken concerning you.
Only may the LORD give you wisdom and understanding, and give you charge over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.
Then you will prosper if you are careful to do the statutes and judgments the LORD commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged. "

Now look, in my hardship I have prepared for the house of the LORD one hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver. I have also prepared bronze and iron beyond weighing, because there is so much. I have prepared wood and stone, and you may add to them.
There are many workers with you—stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and skilled workers of every kind.
There is more gold, silver, bronze, and iron than anyone can count. Get up and work, and may the LORD be with you."
David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon, saying, "
Isn't the LORD your God with you? Hasn't He given you rest on every side? For He has given the people of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before His people.

Now set your heart and your soul to seek the LORD your God. Get up and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you can bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy vessels of God into the house built for the name of the LORD."
When David was old and had lived a long life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
He gathered all the leaders of Israel, along with the priests and the Levites.
He counted the Levites who were thirty years old or older. There were 38,000 men.
Of these, 24,000 were to oversee the work of the the LORD’s temple. Six thousand were officers and judges.
