On the third day, Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner courtyard of the palace, facing the king's hall. The king was sitting on his royal throne in the throne room, facing the doorway.
When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the courtyard, she won his favor. He held out the gold scepter in his hand toward her, and Esther came near and touched the top of the scepter.
The king asked her, "What is it, Queen Esther? What do you want? I'll give it to you, even up to half my kingdom."
Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, may the king and Haman come today to the feast I have prepared for him."
The king said, "Hurry and get Haman so he can do what Esther asked." So the king and Haman went to the feast Esther had prepared.
At the wine feast, the king asked Esther, "What do you want? I'll give it to you. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, I'll do it."
Esther answered, "Here is my request and my petition:

If I have found favor with the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my request and do what I ask, may the king and Haman come to the feast I will prepare for them tomorrow. Then I'll tell the king what I want."
That day Haman left happy and in a good mood. But when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate, and Mordecai didn't stand up or move for him, Haman was filled with anger toward Mordecai.
Haman held back his anger. When he got home, he sent for his friends and his wife Zeresh.
Haman bragged to them about his great wealth, his many children, and all the ways the king had honored him. He told how the king had promoted him above the other officials and servants.
Haman also said, "Queen Esther didn't let anyone come with the king to the feast she prepared except me. Tomorrow I'm invited to go with the king to another feast she's giving.
But all of this means nothing to me as long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."

His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a gallows built fifty cubits high. In the morning, ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then you can go happily with the king to the feast." Haman liked the idea, so he had the gallows made.
That night the king could not sleep, so he ordered the book of the records of his reign to be brought in and read to him.
It was found recorded there that Mordecai had exposed Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the doorway, who had plotted to kill King Xerxes.
The king asked, "What honor or recognition has Mordecai received for this?" "Nothing has been done for him," his attendants answered.
The king said, "Who is in the court?" Now Haman had just entered the outer court of the palace to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows he had built for him.
His attendants answered, "Haman is standing in the court." "Bring him in," the king ordered.
When Haman entered, the king asked him, "What should be done for the man the king delights to honor?" Now Haman thought to himself, "Who is there that the king would rather honor than me?"
So Haman answered the king, "For the man the king delights to honor,
have them bring a royal robe the king has worn and a horse the king has ridden, one with a royal crest placed on its head. "

Then let the robe and horse be entrusted to one of the king's most noble princes, and let them robe the man and lead him on horseback through the city streets, proclaiming before him, 'This is what is done for the man the king delights to honor!'"
"Go at once," the king commanded Haman. "Get the robe and the horse and do just as you have suggested for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Do not neglect anything you have recommended."
So Haman got the robe and the horse. He robed Mordecai and led him on horseback through the city streets, proclaiming before him, "This is what is done for the man the king delights to honor!"
Afterward Mordecai returned to the king's gate. But Haman rushed home, with his head covered in grief.

Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him. His advisers and his wife Zeresh said to him, "Since Mordecai is a Jew and your downfall has already begun before him, you cannot stand against him—you will surely be ruined!"
While they were still talking with him, the king's eunuchs arrived and hurried Haman away to the banquet Esther had prepared.
So the king and Haman went to eat with Queen Esther.

On the second day of the wine feast, the king asked Queen Esther again, "What is your petition, Queen Esther? It will be given to you. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be done."
Queen Esther answered, "If I have found favor with you, O king, and if it pleases the king, grant me my life; that is my petition. And spare my people; that is my request.

For I and my people have been sold to be destroyed, killed, and wiped out. If we had only been sold as male and female slaves, I would have kept quiet, because no such trouble would justify disturbing the king."
King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther, "Who is he, and where is he—the man who has dared to do this?"
Esther said, "An enemy and foe is this wicked Haman!" Then Haman was terrified before the king and queen.
The king rose in his anger from the wine feast and went into the palace garden. Haman stayed to beg Queen Esther for his life, because he saw that the king meant to harm him.

When the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall, Haman had fallen on the couch where Esther was. The king said, "Will he even attack the queen while I am in the house?" As soon as the words left the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

Then Harbona, one of the eunuchs serving the king, said, "Look! The gallows fifty cubits high stands by Haman's house. He had it built for Mordecai, who spoke up to help the king." The king said, "Hang him on it!"
So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king's anger died down.
On that day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the house of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Then Mordecai came before the king, because Esther had told the king how Mordecai was related to her.
The king took off his signet ring, the one he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's house.
Esther spoke to the king again. She fell at his feet, cried, and begged him to stop the evil plan of Haman the Agagite and the plot he had made against the Jews.
The king held out his golden scepter to Esther. She got up and stood in front of the king.

Then she said, "If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor with him, and if the king thinks this is right and I am pleasing to him, let a written order be sent to cancel the letters that Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, wrote. He wrote them to destroy the Jews in all the king's provinces.
How could I bear to see the terrible trouble coming to my people? How could I bear to see my own family destroyed?"
The king said to Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew, "I have given Esther Haman's house, and Haman has been hanged on the gallows because he tried to harm the Jews.
Now you write to the Jews in the king's name, whatever you think is best. Seal it with the king's signet ring. A law written in the king's name and sealed with his ring cannot be changed."

In the third month, the month of Sivan, on the twenty-third day, the king's scribes were called. They wrote everything Mordecai commanded for the Jews and for the rulers of the provinces from India to Ethiopia—127 provinces in all. The message was written in each province's own writing and language, and also in the Jews' writing and language.
The letters were written in King Ahasuerus's name and sealed with his signet ring. They were sent by couriers on fast horses from the royal stables.

The letters gave the Jews in every city permission to gather together and defend their lives. They could destroy, kill, and wipe out any armed force from any people or province that attacked them, along with their women and children. They could also take their enemies' property.
This was to happen on one day in all the king's provinces: the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
A copy of the order was to be made into law in every province and shown to all the peoples. This way the Jews would be ready on that day to pay back their enemies.
The couriers, riding the royal horses, left quickly because the king commanded it. The order was also announced in the fortress of Susa.
Mordecai left the king's presence wearing royal clothes of blue and white, a large gold crown, and a robe of fine linen and purple. The city of Susa cheered and celebrated.
For the Jews, it was a time of light, gladness, joy, and honor.

In every province and city, wherever the king's order and law reached, the Jews had gladness and joy. They held feasts and holidays. Many people in the land became Jews, because they were afraid of the Jews.

On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, the king's order was to be carried out. That was the day the enemies of the Jews had hoped to crush them, but instead the Jews gained power over those who hated them.
The Jews gathered in their cities in every province of King Xerxes to attack anyone who wanted to hurt them. No one could stand against them, because all the peoples were afraid of them.
All the officials of the provinces, the governors, and the king's administrators helped the Jews, because they were afraid of Mordecai.
Mordecai was powerful in the king's palace, and his fame spread through all the provinces. He kept growing more and more powerful.
The Jews struck down all their enemies with the sword, killing and destroying them. They did as they pleased to those who hated them.
In the fortress of Susa the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.
They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, and Aspatha,
These were the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not take any plunder.
On that day the number of those killed in the fortress of Susa was reported to the king.

The king said to Queen Esther, "In the fortress of Susa the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman. What must they have done in the rest of the provinces! What is your request? It will be given to you. What else do you want? It will be done."
Esther said, "If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Susa be allowed to do tomorrow what they did today, and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows."
So the king commanded that this be done. An order was issued in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
On the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, the Jews in Susa gathered together and killed three hundred men in the city, but they did not take any plunder.

The rest of the Jews in the king's provinces also gathered to defend themselves and gain relief from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them, but they did not take any plunder.
This happened on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar. On the fourteenth day they rested and made it a day of feasting and joy.
But the Jews in Susa had gathered on the thirteenth and fourteenth days, and they rested on the fifteenth day and made it a day of feasting and joy.
That is why the Jews who live in country villages celebrate the fourteenth day of Adar as a day of joy and feasting, a holiday, and a day for sending food to one another.
Mordecai recorded these events and sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of King Xerxes, both near and far.
He told them to celebrate the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar every year.

He told them to celebrate these days as the time when the Jews got relief from their enemies, and as the month when their sorrow was turned into joy and their mourning into a holiday. They were to celebrate with feasting and joy, sending food to one another and gifts to the poor.
So the Jews agreed to continue the celebration they had begun, doing what Mordecai had written to them.
For Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them and had cast the Pur, that is, the lot, to crush and destroy them.

But when the plot came to the king's attention, he issued written orders that the evil scheme Haman had devised against the Jews should come back on his own head. He and his sons were to be hanged on the gallows.
Therefore these days were called Purim, from the word Pur. Because of everything written in this letter and because of what they had seen and what had happened to them,

the Jews established and accepted as a lasting rule for themselves, their descendants, and all who joined them, that they would not fail to celebrate these two days every year, as written and at the appointed time.

These days were to be remembered and celebrated by every generation, every family, every province, and every city. These days of Purim were never to pass from among the Jews, and their memory was never to die out among their descendants.
So Queen Esther daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter about Purim.
Letters were sent to all the Jews in the one hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Xerxes, with words of peace and truth.

They confirmed these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established them and just as the people had established them for themselves and their descendants, with instructions for their fasting and mourning.
So Esther's command confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.
King Ahasuerus placed a tax on the land and on the islands of the sea.
All the acts of his power and might, and the full account of Mordecai's greatness, which the king raised him to, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Media and Persia?
For Mordecai the Jew was second only to King Ahasuerus. He was great among the Jews and well liked by many of his brothers. He worked for the good of his people and spoke peace to all his kindred.
There was a man named Job who lived in the land of Uz. He was honest and good. He respected God and stayed away from evil.
He had seven sons and three daughters.
He owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and many servants. He was the greatest man in the east.
His sons took turns having feasts at their homes. They invited their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

When the feast days were over, Job would send for his children and make them clean. Early in the morning, he would offer a burnt offering for each of them. He thought, “Maybe my children sinned and turned against God in their hearts.” Job did this all the time.
One day the sons of God came to stand before the LORD, and Satan came with them.
The LORD asked Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered, “I have been walking around the earth.”
The LORD said to Satan, “Have you noticed My servant Job? No one on earth is like him. He is honest and good. He respects God and stays away from evil.”
Satan replied, “Does Job respect God for no reason?
Haven't You protected him, his family, and everything he has? You have blessed his work, and his animals have grown all over the land.
But take away everything he has, and he will curse You to Your face.”
The LORD said to Satan, “Everything he has is in your power. But do not hurt him.” Then Satan left the the LORD's presence.
One day Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at their oldest brother's house.
A messenger came to Job and said, “The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys were grazing nearby.
Then the Sabeans attacked and took them. They killed the servants with swords. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “Fire from God fell from the sky. It burned up the sheep and the servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”

While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “The Chaldeans split into three groups and attacked the camels. They took them and killed the servants with swords. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at their oldest brother's house.
A strong wind came from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It fell on the young people, and they died. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
Then Job stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. He fell to the ground and worshiped.
He said, “I was born with nothing, and I will die with nothing. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. May the name of the LORD be praised.”
In all this, Job did not sin or blame God.
One day the sons of God came to stand before the LORD, and Satan came with them to stand before the LORD.
The LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered, "From roaming through the earth and walking back and forth in it."

The LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered My servant Job? There is no one on earth like him. He is blameless and upright, and he fears God and turns away from evil. He still holds on to his integrity, even though you urged Me to destroy him for no reason."
Satan answered the LORD, "A man will give up everything to save his own life.
But stretch out Your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse You to Your face."
The LORD said to Satan, "Very well, he is in your hands, but you must spare his life."
So Satan left the LORD's presence and struck Job with painful sores from the soles of his feet to the top of his head.
Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself while he sat in the ashes.
His wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your integrity? Curse God and die!"
He answered her, "You are talking like a foolish woman. Should we accept only good from God and not trouble?" In all this, Job did not sin with his lips.

Job's three friends—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite—heard about all the trouble that had come on him. Each one came from his own home, and they met together to go and sympathize with him and comfort him.
When they saw him from far away, they could hardly recognize him. They wept loudly, and each man tore his robe and sprinkled dust on his head.
Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word to him, because they saw how great his suffering was.
After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
"Let the day die on which I was born, and the night that said, 'A boy has been conceived.'
Let that day be darkness. Let God above not look for it, and let no light shine on it.
Let darkness and deep shadow claim it. Let a cloud settle on it. Let the blackness of the day terrify it.
As for that night, let thick darkness take it. Let it not be counted among the days of the year. Let it not enter the number of the months.
Yes, let that night be empty. Let no shout of joy come into it.
Let those who curse days curse it—those who are ready to wake up Leviathan.
Let the stars of its twilight go dark. Let it wait for light but find none. Let it not see the dawn.
For it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb or hide trouble from my eyes. "
Why did I not die at birth? Why did I not breathe my last when I came from the womb?
Why did knees welcome me? Why did breasts let me nurse?
For now I would be lying down and quiet. I would be asleep and at rest.
I would be with kings and counselors of the earth, who rebuilt ruins for themselves.
Or I would be with princes who have gold and fill their houses with silver.
Or why was I not hidden like a baby born too soon, like infants who never saw light?
There the wicked stop causing trouble, and the weary rest.
There prisoners rest together and do not hear the voice of the slave driver.
The small and the great are there, and the slave is free from his master. "
Why is light given to one who suffers, and life to those bitter in soul,
who long for death, but it does not come, and dig for it more than for hidden treasure?
They greatly rejoice and are glad when they find the grave.
Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has shut in?
For my sighs come before my food, and my groans pour out like water.
What I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has happened to me.
I am not at peace. I have no quiet. I have no rest, only trouble."
“If I try to speak to you, will you be upset? But who can keep from speaking?
Look, you have taught many people, and you have strengthened weak hands.
Your words have supported those who stumble, and you have strengthened weak knees.
But now it has come to you, and you are weary; it touches you, and you are dismayed.
Isn't your reverence for God your confidence, and your blameless life your hope?
“Remember, who has ever died while innocent? Or when have honest people been destroyed?
As I have seen, those who do wrong reap what they sow.
By God's breath they perish, and by the blast of His anger they are consumed.
The roaring of the lion, the growl of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions are broken.
The old lion dies for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
“Now a word was secretly brought to me, and my ear received a whisper of it.
In thoughts from night visions, when deep sleep falls on people,
fear and trembling came upon me and made all my bones shake.
A spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body stood up.
It stopped, but I could not tell what it looked like. A shape stood before my eyes. Then I heard a quiet voice:
“‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Can a man be more pure than his Maker?’
‘If He does not trust His own servants and finds fault with His angels,
how much more are people who live in clay houses, built on dust, crushed like a moth!
They are broken from morning to evening; they perish forever, and no one notices.
Aren't their lives taken away? They die without wisdom.’”
Call out now—will anyone answer you? Which of the holy ones will you turn to?
Anger kills a foolish person, and jealousy destroys a naive person.
I have seen a foolish person settle down and prosper, but suddenly I cursed his home.
His children are far from safety. They are crushed at the city gate, and no one rescues them.
The hungry eat his harvest, even taking it from among the thorns. Thieves take his wealth.
For trouble does not come from the soil, and hardship does not grow from the ground.
Yet people are born for trouble, just as sparks fly upward from a fire.
But I would seek God and bring my case to Him.
He does great things that no one can fully understand, and wonders without number.
He sends rain on the earth and waters the fields.
He lifts up the lowly and brings safety to those who mourn.
He stops the plans of the clever, so their hands cannot finish what they start.
He catches wise people in their own tricks, and the plans of crooked people are quickly undone.
They meet darkness in the daytime and grope around at noon as if it were night.
But He saves the poor from the sword, from cruel words, and from the power of the mighty.
So the poor have hope, and evil is silenced.
Look, blessed is the person whom God corrects. Do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
For He wounds and then binds up; He crushes and then His hands heal.
He will rescue you from six troubles; in fact, in seven, no harm will touch you.
In famine He will redeem you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
You will be hidden from the lash of the tongue, and you will not fear destruction when it comes.
You will laugh at destruction and famine, and you will not fear the wild animals.
For you will have peace with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.
You will know your tent is safe, and you will check your home and find nothing wrong.
You will know your children are many, and your descendants are like the grass of the field.
You will come to the grave at a ripe old age, like a pile of grain gathered at the right time.
Look, we have studied this, and it is true. Listen, and know it for yourself.
“If only my grief were weighed, and my trouble were put on the scales with it!
Then it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, so my words have been rash.
The arrows of the Almighty are in me; my spirit drinks their poison. The terrors of God are lined up against me.
“Does a wild donkey bray over grass, or an ox low over its feed?
Is bland food eaten without salt, or is there taste in the white of an egg?
I refuse to touch them. They are like sickening food to me.
“Oh, that I might get what I ask for, that God would grant my desire!
That God would be willing to crush me, to let loose His hand and cut me off!
Then I would still have this comfort. Yes, I would rejoice in pain that will not stop, because I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
“What strength do I have, that I should wait? What end do I have, that I should be patient?
Is my strength like stone, or is my flesh bronze?
Is there no help in me? Has wisdom been driven from me?
“A friend should show kindness to someone who is suffering. Anyone who withholds it forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
My brothers have been as false as a stream, like brooks that dry up,
dark with ice and hidden by snow.
But when it gets hot, they dry up; in the heat, they vanish from their place.
“Caravans turn off their path; they go up into the wasteland and die.
The caravans of Tema look for water; the travelers of Sheba hope to find it.
They are ashamed because they trusted; they arrive and are confused.
So now you are nothing. You see terror and are afraid.
“Did I ever say, ‘Give me something,’ or, ‘Pay a bribe for me from your wealth’?
Or, ‘Save me from the enemy’s hand,’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the cruel’?
Teach me, and I will be quiet. Help me understand what I have done wrong.
“How powerful are honest words! But what do your arguments prove?
Do you mean to correct my words and treat a suffering person’s words as wind?
You would even cast lots for orphans and sell your friend.
“But now, please look at me. I will not lie to your face.
Turn back; let there be no injustice. Turn back; my innocence is still there.
Is there injustice on my tongue? Does my mouth not know what is evil?”
Life on earth is hard work for people. Their days are like those of a hired worker.
Like a slave, a person longs for shade. Like a hired worker, he waits for his pay.
So I have been given months that feel empty, and nights of trouble have been set aside for me.
When I go to bed, I wonder, "When will I get up?" The evening drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.
My body is covered with worms and dirt. My skin cracks and looks sickening.
My days go by faster than a weaver's shuttle. They end with no hope.
Remember that my life is only a breath. My eyes will never see good again.
The person who sees me now will not see me again. Your eyes are on me, and then I will be gone.
A cloud fades and disappears. In the same way, the one who goes down to the grave does not come back.
He will not return to his house, and his home will not know him anymore.
So I will not keep quiet. I will speak out in my troubled spirit. I will complain in my bitter soul.
Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that You put a guard over me?
When I say, "My bed will comfort me, and my couch will ease my complaint,"
You scare me with dreams and terrify me with visions.
My soul would rather choke to death than keep living in this body.
I hate my life. I do not want to live forever. Leave me alone, because my days are only a breath.
What is a person, that You make so much of him, and that You set Your heart on him?
You visit him every morning and test him every moment.
How long will You not look away from me? When will You leave me alone, even for a moment?
If I have sinned, what can I do to You, O Watcher of people? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to myself?
Why do You not pardon my sin and take away my guilt? For soon I will lie down in the dust, and You will look for me, but I will not be there.
"How long will you say such things? Your words are just hot air.
Does God twist justice? Does the Almighty twist what is right?
If your children sinned against Him, He let their own wrongdoing destroy them.
"But if you seek God and plead with the Almighty,
if you are pure and upright, surely now He will rouse Himself for you and restore your rightful place.
Your beginnings will seem small, but your future will grow very great.
"Ask the former generation and learn from what their fathers discovered.
For we have lived only a short time and know nothing, because our days on earth are like a shadow.
Will they not teach you and tell you? Will they not share what they know?
"Can papyrus grow where there is no marsh? Can reeds flourish without water?
While still green and uncut, they wither faster than grass.
Such is the fate of all who forget God; so the hope of the godless dies.
"His confidence is fragile; his security is a spider's web.
He leans on his house, but it gives way; he clings to it, but it does not hold.
"He is like a well-watered plant in the sunshine, with shoots spreading over his garden.
His roots wrap around a rock pile; he looks for a place among the stones.
If he is uprooted from his place, it will disown him, saying, 'I never saw you.'
Surely this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth others will spring up.
"See, God does not reject a blameless person, and He will not help those who do evil.
He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with shouts of joy.
Your enemies will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more."
"I know that is true, but how can a person be right with God?
If someone wanted to argue with Him, he could not answer even one question out of a thousand.
He is wise in heart and strong in power. Who has ever stood against Him and won?"
"He moves mountains, and no one even notices. He flips them over in His anger.
He shakes the earth from its place, and its supports tremble.
He tells the sun not to rise, and it stays dark. He seals up the stars.
He alone stretches out the sky and walks on the waves of the sea.
He made the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the hidden places in the south.
He does great things we cannot search out and wonders too many to count."
"Look, He passes by me, and I do not see Him. He moves on, but I do not notice Him.
Look, He snatches things away. Who can stop Him? Who can say to Him, 'What are You doing?'
God does not hold back His anger. Even the proudest powers bow under Him.
So how could I answer Him or choose my words before Him?
Even if I were right, I could not answer Him. I would have to beg my Judge for mercy.
If I called and He answered, I still could not believe He was listening to me.
He crushes me with a storm and adds to my wounds for no reason.
He will not let me catch my breath; He fills me with bitterness.
If it is a test of strength, look, He is mighty! And if it is a matter of justice, who can bring Him to court?
If I am right, my own mouth would condemn me. If I am blameless, it would show me as twisted.
I am blameless, yet I do not know myself. I hate my life."
"It is all the same. That is why I say, 'He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.'
When trouble suddenly brings death, He mocks the pain of the innocent.
The earth is handed over to the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If it is not Him, then who is it?
My days are faster than a runner. They fly by and see no good.
They pass like boats made of reeds, like an eagle diving for food.
If I say, 'I will forget my complaint and stop looking sad and be cheerful,'
I am afraid of all my pain. I know You will not clear me.
I am guilty, so why should I work so hard for nothing?
Even if I wash myself with snow and clean my hands with soap,
then You will throw me into a pit, and even my clothes will hate me.
He is not a man like me, so I cannot answer Him or take Him to court.
There is no one to settle things between us, to put a hand on us both.
Let Him take His rod away from me, and let fear of Him not terrify me.
Then I would speak without fearing Him, but that is not how it is with me."
I am disgusted with my life, so I will speak my complaint and talk from my bitter heart.
I say to God, 'Do not condemn me. Tell me why You are fighting me.'
Is it right for You to oppress me, to reject what Your hands made, and favor the plans of wicked people?" "
Do You have human eyes? Do You see the way people see?
Are Your days like those of a human, or Your years like those of a mortal?
Why do You look for my guilt and search for my sin?
You know I am not guilty, and no one can rescue me from Your hand." "
Your hands shaped me and made me; now You destroy me.
Please remember that You made me like clay. Will You now return me to dust?
Did You not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and tendons.
You have given me life and love, and Your care has kept my spirit alive.
Yet You hid these things in Your heart; I know this was part of Your plan." "
If I sinned, You would notice, and You would not clear me of my guilt.
If I am guilty, I am doomed. If I am innocent, I still cannot lift my head, because I am full of shame. Look at my suffering!
If I hold my head high, You hunt me like a lion and show Your power against me again.
You bring new witnesses against me and increase Your anger toward me; fresh troubles come against me in waves.
Why did You bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before anyone saw me.
Then I would be as if I had never lived, carried from the womb to the grave." "
Are not my days few? Leave me alone so I can have a little comfort
before I go and never return, to a land of darkness and gloom,
a land of deep darkness and disorder, where even the light is like darkness."
“Should a lot of words go unanswered? Can a person who talks too much be proven right?
Will your empty words make people quiet? Will you mock with no one to correct you?
You say, ‘My teaching is pure, and I am clean in Your eyes.’
“But if only God would speak and open His lips against you,
He would show you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Then you would know that God makes you pay less than your sin deserves.
Can you discover the deep things of God? Can you find the limits of the Almighty?
They are higher than the heavens—what can you do? They are deeper than the grave—what can you know?
God’s wisdom is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
If He passes by and locks you up, or calls a court together, who can stop Him?
He surely knows deceitful people. When He sees evil, He does not overlook it.
A foolish person can gain understanding only when a wild donkey is born human.
“If you prepare your heart and stretch out your hands to Him,
if you put away the sin in your hand and let no evil stay in your tent,
then you will lift up your face without shame; you will stand firm and unafraid.
You will forget your misery; you will remember it like water that has passed by.
Life will be brighter than noon; its darkness will be like morning.
You will be secure because there is hope; you will look around and rest in safety.
You will lie down without fear, and many will seek your favor.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will slip away from them; their hope will become a dying breath.”
"So you think you are the only wise people, and that wisdom will die with you!
But I have a mind like you; I'm not below you. Who doesn't know things like that?"
"I've become a joke to my friends, even though I prayed to God and He answered me. An innocent, honest person has become a joke.
People who are comfortable look down on trouble, but trouble is ready for anyone who stumbles.
Robbers' tents are safe, and people who anger God feel secure, because God holds them in His hand."
"But ask the animals, and they will teach you; or the birds in the air, and they will tell you.
Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; or let the fish of the sea explain things to you.
Which of all these doesn't know that the LORD's hand has done this?
The life of every living thing is in His hand, along with the breath of all people."
"Doesn't the ear test words the way the tongue tastes food?
Wisdom is found among the old, and understanding comes with long life.
Wisdom and strength belong to God; counsel and understanding are His."
"What He tears down can't be rebuilt; the person He locks up can't be set free.
If He holds back the water, it dries up; if He sends it out, it floods the land.
Strength and success belong to Him; both the deceiver and the deceived are His."
"He leads advisors away barefoot and makes judges look foolish.
He loosens the bonds kings put in place and ties a belt around their waists.
He leads priests away barefoot and overthrows those who seemed secure.
He takes speech from trusted people and takes away the good judgment of elders.
He pours contempt on nobles and weakens the strong."
"He reveals deep things hidden in darkness and brings dark shadows into the light.
He makes nations great, and He destroys them; He expands nations, and then He leads them away.
He takes away the understanding of earth's leaders and leaves them wandering in a land with no path.
They feel around in the dark with no light, and He makes them stagger like drunk people."
Look, my eye has seen all this, and my ear has heard and understood it.
What you know, I know too; I am not less than you.
But I want to speak to the Almighty; I desire to argue with God.
Yet you smear people with lies. All of you are worthless doctors.
If only you would be quiet, that would be wisdom for you.
Hear my argument now, and listen to the pleading of my lips.
Will you speak wrongly for God and speak deceitfully for Him?
Will you take His side? Will you argue God's case?
Will it go well when He examines you? Can you deceive Him as you deceive a person?
He will surely rebuke you if you secretly show favoritism.
Will not His majesty terrify you, and His dread fall on you?
Your sayings are as worthless as ashes; your defenses are like clay." "
Be quiet and let me speak; then I will accept whatever comes.
Why should I risk my life?
Even if He kills me, I will still hope in Him. I must still defend my ways to His face.
He will be my salvation, because no godless person comes before Him.
Listen carefully to my words; let what I say reach your ears.
Look, I have prepared my case; I know I will be vindicated.
Who will contend with me? For then I would be silent and die." "
Only grant me two things, and then I will not hide from Your face:
withdraw Your hand from me, and do not let Your terror make me afraid.
Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and You reply to me.
How many wrongs and sins have I done? Show me my rebellion and sin.
Why do You hide Your face and consider me Your enemy?
Will You frighten a windblown leaf? Will You pursue dry chaff?
For You write bitter things against me and make me inherit the sins of my youth.
You put my feet in stocks and watch all my paths; You set a limit around the soles of my feet.
So a person wastes away like rotting wood, like a garment eaten by moths."
Man born of a woman lives only a short time and is full of trouble.
He blooms like a flower and then withers; he runs like a shadow and does not last.
You open Your eyes on him, and You bring him into judgment with Yourself.
Who can bring something clean from something unclean? No one.
If his days are set, and the number of his months is with You, You have set his limit, and he cannot pass it.
Look away from him so he can rest, until he finishes his day like a hired worker.
There is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its new shoots will not stop.
Even if its root grows old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil,
at the scent of water it will bud and grow branches like a new plant.
But a man dies and lies still; a person breathes his last, and where is he?
Water dries up from the sea, and a river becomes dry and parched.
So a man lies down and does not rise again; he will not wake up until the heavens are gone, nor will he be roused from his sleep.
If only You would hide me in Sheol and keep me hidden until Your anger passes! Set a time for me, then remember me.
If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait until my change comes.
You will call, and I will answer; You will long for the work of Your hands.
Then You will count my steps, but not keep watch over my sin.
My sin is sealed in a bag, and You cover over my guilt.
But a mountain falls and crumbles, and a rock is moved from its place.
Water wears away stones; floods wash away the soil of the earth; and You destroy man's hope.
You overpower him forever, and he is gone; You change his appearance and send him away.
His sons are honored, but he does not know it; they are brought low, but he does not see it.
He feels only the pain in his body, and his soul mourns within him.
"Should a wise man answer with empty words and fill his belly with hot air?
Should he argue with useless words, or speak in ways that do no good?
But you even destroy reverence and weaken prayer before God.
Your sin teaches your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.
Your own mouth condemns you, and your lips testify against you.
"Were you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
Do you hear God's secret counsel? Do you keep wisdom for yourself?
What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not with us?
The gray-haired and the aged are among us, men older than your father.
Are God's comforts too small for you, or a gentle word spoken to you?
Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash?
so that you turn your spirit against God and pour out such words from your mouth?
What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
If God puts no trust in His holy ones, and even the heavens are not pure in His sight,
how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who sins as easily as drinking water!
"Listen to me; I will show you, and what I have seen I will declare,
what wise men have declared and have not hidden, passed down from their fathers.
To them alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them.
The wicked person suffers all his days, and the years stored up for the ruthless are hidden.
Sounds of terror are in his ears; in peace the destroyer comes upon him.
He does not believe he will escape the darkness; he is marked for the sword.
He wanders looking for food, knowing that a day of darkness is ready for him.
Distress and anguish terrify him; they overpower him, like a king ready for battle.
For he has stretched out his hand against God and acts arrogantly against the Almighty,
rushing at Him with a thick, strong shield.
Though his face is covered with fat and his waist bulges with flesh,
he will dwell in ruined cities, in houses no one inhabits, which are destined to become rubble.
He will not grow rich; his wealth will not last, and his possessions will not spread over the land.
He will not escape the darkness; a flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of the LORD's mouth will carry him away.
Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself, for emptiness will be his reward.
It will be paid in full before his time, and his branch will not stay green.
He will shake off his unripe grapes like a vine, and cast off his blossoms like an olive tree.
For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of those who take bribes.
They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb prepares deceit."
“I have heard many things like these. You are all terrible comforters.
Will your speeches never end? What makes you keep arguing?
I could talk like you if you were in my place. I could pile words against you and shake my head at you.
But I would encourage you with my mouth, and the comfort from my lips would ease your pain.
If I speak, my pain doesn't get better. If I stay quiet, how much of it goes away?
“But now He has worn me out. You have wiped out my whole family.
You have seized me, and that has become a witness. My thin body rises up and testifies against me.
His anger has torn me and turned against me. He grinds His teeth at me. My enemy stares at me with His piercing eyes.
They open their mouths against me and slap my cheeks in scorn. They gang up on me.
God has handed me over to evil men and thrown me into the hands of the wicked.
“I was at ease, but He shattered me. He grabbed me by the neck and broke me to pieces. He has set me up as His target.
His archers surround me. Without mercy, He pierces my kidneys and pours out my gall on the ground.
He breaks me again and again. He charges at me like a mighty warrior.
“I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and buried my strength in the dust.
My face is red from weeping, and dark shadows cover my eyes.
Even so, my hands are free of violence, and my prayer is pure.
O earth, do not cover my blood. Let my cry find no rest.
“Even now my Witness is in heaven, and my Advocate is on high.
My friends mock me, but my eyes pour out tears to God.
Oh, that someone could plead a man's case before God, as he would for a friend!
For in a few years I will go where I can never return.”
My spirit is broken; my days are running out; the grave waits for me.
Mockers surround me, and my eyes must stay on their insults.
Please put up a pledge for me with Yourself. Who else will shake hands with me?
You have hidden their hearts from understanding, so You will not lift them up.
If someone betrays friends for a share of the reward, his children's eyes will grow weak.
He has made me a joke to people; I have become someone they laugh at.
My eyes have grown weak with sorrow; my whole body is only a shadow.
Good people are shocked by this; innocent people are stirred up against the wicked.
But good people will stay on their path; those with clean hands will grow stronger.
But come back, all of you; I won't find a wise person among you.
My days have passed; my plans are broken; the desires of my heart are gone.
They turn night into day and say, "Light is near," even though it is dark.
If I hope for the grave as my home and make my bed in darkness,
I have said to decay, "You are my father," and to the worm, "My mother and my sister."
So where is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
Will my hope go down to the gates of the grave? Will we rest together in the dust?
“How long will you keep talking? Understand this, and then we will speak.
Why are we treated like cattle? Why do we look stupid to you?
You who tear yourself apart in anger—should the earth be abandoned for you? Should the rock be moved from its place?”
“Yes, the light of the wicked goes out, and the spark of his fire stops glowing.
The light in his tent grows dark, and his lamp above him goes out.
His strong steps get shorter, and his own plan knocks him down.
His own feet throw him into a net, and he walks right into a trap.
A trap grabs him by the heel, and a snare holds him tight.
A rope is hidden in the ground for him, and a trap waits for him on the path.
Terrors scare him from every side and chase him at his heels.”
“His strength gives out, and disaster waits to trip him up.
It eats away pieces of his skin, and death’s firstborn devours his body.
He is torn from the tent he trusted and marched to the king of terrors.
Nothing of his remains in his tent; sulfur is scattered over his home.
His roots dry up below, and his branches wither above.
His name is forgotten on earth, and he has no fame in the streets.
He is pushed from light into darkness and driven from the world.
He has no child or grandchild among his people, and no one survives where he lived.
People who come later are shocked by his ruin, and those who came before are seized with horror.
Surely these are the homes of the wicked, and this is the place of someone who does not know God.”
"How long will you torment me and crush me with words?
You have insulted me over and over, and you are not ashamed to wrong me.
Even if I really did go wrong, my mistake is my own.
If you really put yourselves above me and use my shame against me,
then know that God has treated me unfairly and trapped me in His net.
Look, I cry out that I am being wronged, but no one answers; I shout for help, but there is no justice.
He has blocked my path so I cannot get through, and He has made my roads dark.
He has taken away my honor and removed the crown from my head.
He breaks me down on every side, and I am finished; He pulls up my hope like a tree.
He has become angry with me and treats me like an enemy.
His troops gather, advance against me, and camp around my tent.
"He has driven my brothers away from me, and those who know me have turned away.
My relatives have abandoned me, and my close friends have forgotten me.
The people in my house and my servant girls treat me like a stranger; I am a foreigner to them.
I call my servant, but he does not answer; I have to beg him with my own words.
My breath smells bad to my wife, and even my own brothers find me disgusting.
Even little children look down on me; when I get up, they speak against me.
All my close friends hate me, and the ones I loved have turned against me.
My bones stick to my skin and flesh, and I have barely escaped with my life.
Pity me, pity me, my friends, because God's hand has struck me.
Why do you keep attacking me like God does, and why aren't you satisfied with my suffering?
"If only my words were written down! If only they were recorded in a book!
If only they were carved with an iron tool and lead into the rock forever!
But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand on the earth.
Even after my skin is destroyed, I will see God in my own flesh.
I will see Him for myself; my own eyes will look at Him, not someone else's. My heart aches within me!
"If you say, 'How can we hunt him down?' and 'The real problem is in him,'
then be afraid of the sword, because anger brings the punishment of the sword, so you will know that judgment is real."
"My thoughts push me to answer because I am deeply upset.
I hear a harsh correction that shames me, and my understanding makes me answer.
"Do you know this from long ago, since people were placed on the earth?
It is that the success of wicked people is short, and the joy of those who ignore God lasts only a moment.
Though his pride reaches the heavens and his head touches the clouds,
he will be gone forever, like his own waste; people who saw him will ask, 'Where did he go?'
He will vanish like a dream and not be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.
"The eye that saw him will not see him again, and his home will not see him again.
His children will beg from poor people, and his own hands will have to give back his wealth.
His bones, once strong in youth, will lie with him in the dust.
"Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,
though he enjoys it and won't let it go, but keeps it in his mouth,
yet his food will turn sour in his stomach; it will become cobra venom inside him.
He swallows riches but throws them up; God will force them out of his stomach.
He will suck cobra poison; a viper's fangs will kill him.
"He will not see streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.
He must give back his gains without enjoying them; he cannot enjoy the wealth he has earned.
For he crushed poor people and left them; he seized houses he did not build.
Because he is never satisfied inside, he cannot hold on to what he wants.
Nothing is left for him to eat, so his good times will not last.
"When he has plenty, he will still be in trouble; all the force of misery will come on him.
When his stomach is full, God will pour out His fierce anger on him and rain blows on him while he eats.
If he runs from an iron weapon, a bronze arrow will pierce him.
The arrow is pulled out from his back, its shiny tip from his liver. Terror comes over him.
"Complete darkness is stored up for his treasures; a fire no one fans will burn him and eat what is left in his tent.
The sky will show his sin, and the earth will turn against him.
What he owns will be taken away, flowing off on the day of God's anger.
This is what God gives the wicked person; this is the share God sets for him."
"Listen carefully to my words. Let this be your comfort.
Stay with me while I speak. After I finish, you may mock me.
Am I complaining to another person? Why shouldn't I be impatient?
Look at me and be amazed. Put your hand over your mouth.
When I think about it, I am terrified, and trembling takes hold of my body. "
Why do wicked people keep living, grow old, and gain power?
Their descendants are settled around them, and their children are right in front of them.
Their homes are safe from fear, and God's punishment does not touch them.
Their bulls breed without fail, and their cows have healthy calves.
Their little ones run out like a flock of sheep, and their children dance and play.
They sing with tambourines and harps, and they celebrate to the sound of the flute.
They spend their days in comfort, and they go peacefully to the grave.
But they say to God, 'Leave us alone! We don't want to know Your ways.
Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him? What good would it do us to pray to Him?'
Yet their success is not really in their own hands, so I keep away from the advice of wicked people. "
How often does the light of wicked people go out? Does trouble come on them? Does God, in His anger, hand out destruction?
Are they like straw before the wind, or like chaff a storm blows away?
God saves up a person's wrongdoing for his children. He pays him back, and he knows it.
Let his own eyes see his ruin. Let him drink the anger of the Almighty.
What does he care about his family after he is gone, when his months are cut short?
Can anyone teach God anything? He judges even the powerful.
One person dies at the height of his strength, feeling safe and at ease.
His body is well fed, and his bones are full of marrow.
Another dies with a bitter heart, never having known good times.
Both lie down in the dust, and worms cover them. "
Look, I know your thoughts and the plans you make against me.
For you say, 'Where is the house of the rich man? Where is the tent where wicked people live?'
Haven't you asked travelers on the road? Don't you recognize the signs they see?
Wicked people are spared on the day of disaster and rescued on the day of anger.
Who dares to tell him he is wrong? Who pays him back for what he has done?
He is carried to the grave, and someone watches over his tomb.
The soil of the valley is sweet to him. Crowds follow him, and more go ahead of him than can be counted.
So how can you comfort me with empty words? Your answers are still misleading."
"Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous? Or is it gain to Him that you make your ways perfect?
Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and brings you to trial?
"Is not your wickedness great? Are not your sins endless?
For you have taken pledges from your brothers without cause, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
You have not given water to the weary, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.
But the land belonged to the powerful, and the favored lived in it.
"You have sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless has been crushed.
That is why snares surround you, and sudden terror overwhelms you,
or darkness, so that you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
"Is not God in the heights of heaven? See the highest stars, how lofty they are!
Yet you say, 'What does God know? Can He judge through the thick darkness?'
Thick clouds veil Him so that He cannot see, as He walks on the vault of heaven.
Will you keep to the old path that wicked men have trod?
They were snatched away before their time, and their foundation was swept away by a flood.
"They said to God, 'Depart from us!' What can the Almighty do to us?
Yet He filled their houses with good things. But the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
The righteous see and are glad; the innocent mock them,
saying, 'Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their wealth.'
"Reconcile now with Him, and be at peace; thereby good will come to you.
Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.
If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove wickedness far from your tent,
and lay your gold in the dust and the gold of Ophir among the rocks in the ravines,
then the Almighty will be your gold and the choicest silver for you.
"For then you will delight in the Almighty and look to God with confidence.
You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
What you decide will be done, and light will shine on your ways.
When men are brought low, you will say, 'Lift them up!' Then He will save the lowly.
He will deliver the one who is not innocent, who will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands."
"Even today, my complaint is bitter, and my burden feels heavy despite my groans.
"If only I knew where to find Him, I would go to His throne.
I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.
I would know how He would answer me and understand what He would say.
"Would He use His great power against me? No—He would pay attention to me.
There an upright person could argue with Him, and I would be set free forever from my Judge.
"If I go east, He is not there; if I go west, I cannot see Him.
If He turns to the north, I cannot find Him; if He turns to the south, I do not see Him.
"Yet He knows the path I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come out like gold.
My feet have followed His tracks, and I have kept His way without turning aside.
I have not turned away from the commands of His lips; I have treasured His words more than my daily bread.
"But He never changes, and who can oppose Him? He does what He wants.
He carries out His plan for me, and He has many plans like it.
So I am terrified in His presence; when I think about it, I am afraid of Him.
God has made my heart weak; the Almighty has terrified me.
Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, or by the thick darkness that covers my face."
"Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment? Why do those who know Him look in vain for His days?
"Some move boundary stones and pasture stolen flocks.
They drive away the orphan's donkey and take the widow's ox as a pledge.
They push the needy off the road, so the poor of the land must hide.
Like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go out to work, searching for food; the wasteland gives food to their children.
They gather feed in the fields and pick leftover grapes from the wicked man's vineyard.
Without clothes, they spend the night naked, with no covering in the cold.
Mountain rains soak them, and they cling to rocks because they have no shelter.
They snatch the fatherless from the breast and take a pledge from the poor.
Without clothes, they walk naked; they carry sheaves but still go hungry.
They press olives among the terraces and tread the winepresses, yet they are thirsty.
The dying groan in the city, and the wounded cry for help, but God does not call it a crime.
"There are those who rebel against the light; they do not know its ways or stay on its paths.
The murderer rises at dawn to kill the poor and needy, and at night he is like a thief.
The adulterer's eye watches for twilight; he says, 'No eye will see me,' and he covers his face.
In the dark they break into houses; by day they shut themselves in; they do not know the light.
For them, deep darkness is like morning; they are friends with the terrors of darkness.
"They are like foam on the water. Their land is cursed, so no one goes to their vineyards.
As drought and heat melt the snow, so the grave takes away sinners.
The womb forgets them; worms feast on them; they are remembered no more; and wickedness is broken like a tree.
They mistreat the childless woman and do no good to the widow.
God drags away the mighty by His power; though they rise up, they have no assurance of life.
He may let them rest in safety, but His eyes are on their ways.
For a little while they are lifted up, then they are gone; they are brought down and gathered up like everyone else; they are cut off like heads of grain.
If this is not so, who can prove me a liar and make my words worthless?"
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
“God rules with power and fear. He brings peace in His high places.
Can anyone count His armies? Is there anyone His light does not reach?
How can a person be right with God? How can someone born of a woman be clean?
Even the moon does not shine brightly, and the stars are not pure in His eyes.
How much less a person, who is like a maggot, and a human being, who is like a worm!”
“How have you helped the powerless? How have you saved the weak arm?
What advice have you given to someone without wisdom? What knowledge have you shown so clearly?
To whom have you spoken these words? Whose breath came from you?”
“The dead tremble beneath the waters, and so do those who live there.
Sheol is naked before Him, and Abaddon has no cover.
“He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth on nothing.
He wraps the waters in His thick clouds, but the clouds do not burst under their weight.
He covers the face of the full moon, spreading His cloud over it.
He has marked a boundary on the water's surface, where light and darkness meet.
“The pillars of heaven tremble and are amazed at His rebuke.
By His power He stilled the sea; by His wisdom He shattered Rahab.
By His breath the skies were cleared; His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
“Indeed, these are only the edges of His ways. What a faint whisper we hear of Him! Who can understand the thunder of His power?”
“As surely as God lives, who took away my justice, and the Almighty, who made my soul bitter,
as long as I have breath in me and God’s Spirit is in my nostrils,
my lips will not speak evil, and my tongue will not say anything false.
Far be it from me to say you are right. I will not give up my integrity until I die.
I will hold on to my right living and will not let it go. My heart will not shame me as long as I live.
Let my enemy be like the wicked, and my opponent like an evildoer.”
“For what hope does a godless person have when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him?
Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at all times?”
“I will teach you about God’s hand. I will not hide what belongs to the Almighty.
Look, all of you have seen it. So why do you talk so pointlessly?”
“This is what a wicked person receives from God, and the inheritance that oppressors get from the Almighty:
If his sons increase, it is for the sword, and his children will not have enough bread.
Those who survive him will die and be buried, and his widows will not weep.
Though he piles up silver like dust and stores up clothing like clay,
he may get it ready, but a righteous person will wear it, and an innocent person will divide the silver.
He builds his house like a moth’s, and like a shelter a watchman sets up.
He lies down rich, but he will not be gathered up. He opens his eyes, and he is gone.
Terrors overtake him like a flood; a storm steals him away at night.
The east wind carries him off, and he is gone. It sweeps him out of his place.
It hurls itself against him without pity. He runs from its power.
It claps its hands at him and hisses at him from its place.”
Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place where gold is refined.
Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is melted from stone.
People end the darkness. They search the deepest places for ore in the blackest dark.
They dig a shaft far from where people live. Travelers forget it, and the miners hang far away from others.
The earth, which gives food, is changed below as if by fire.
Its stones hold sapphires, and its dust contains gold.
No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon's eye has seen it.
Proud animals have not walked it, and no lion has crossed it.
People put their hand to hard rock and overturn mountains at the base.
They cut channels through rock, and their eyes see every precious thing.
They dam streams so they do not flow, and bring hidden things into the light.
But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding live?
No one knows its worth, and it is not found in the land of the living.
The deep sea says, "It is not in me." The ocean says, "It is not with me."
It cannot be bought with gold, and its price cannot be weighed in silver.
It cannot be valued with Ophir's gold, with precious onyx, or with sapphire.
Neither gold nor crystal can compare to it, and it cannot be traded for fine gold.
Coral and quartz are not worth mentioning. Wisdom's price is more than rubies.
Cush's topaz cannot compare to it, and it cannot be valued in pure gold.
So where does wisdom come from, and where does understanding live?
It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and kept secret from the birds of the sky.
Destruction and Death say, "We have heard a rumor about it."
God understands its way, and He knows its place.
For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
When He set the weight of the wind and measured the waters,
when He made a rule for the rain and a path for the thunder,
then He saw wisdom and told about it. He set it in place and searched it out.
And He said to people, "Look, the fear of the Lord is wisdom, and turning away from evil is understanding."
"How I wish for the months that have passed, for the days when God watched over me.
His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through darkness.
I was in my prime, and God's close friendship rested on my tent.
The Almighty was still with me, and my children were around me.
I had plenty, with cream on my paths and oil pouring from the rocks.
"When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the square,
young men stepped aside when they saw me, and old men stood up.
Leaders stopped talking and covered their mouths with their hands.
The voices of nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
Everyone who heard me blessed me, and everyone who saw me praised me.
"I rescued the poor who cried for help and the orphan who had no helper.
The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow's heart glad.
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and turban.
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the needy, and I looked into the stranger's case.
I broke the fangs of the wicked and snatched the prey from his teeth.
Then I thought, 'I will die at home, and my days will be as many as grains of sand.
My roots will spread out to the water, and the dew will rest on my branches.
My honor stays new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.'
"People listened to me and waited; they kept silent to hear my advice.
After I spoke, they said no more; my words settled on them like dew.
They waited for me as for rain and opened their mouths as for spring rain.
If I smiled at them, they could hardly believe it; they did not let my favor fade.
I chose their way and sat as their chief; I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts those who mourn."
But now men younger than I laugh at me—men whose fathers I would not even put with the dogs that guard my sheep.
What good is their strength to me? Their power is gone.
Thin from want and hunger, they chew on dry ground in the empty wasteland at night.
They pick mallow among the bushes, and broom tree roots are their food.
People drive them away and shout at them as if they were thieves.
They have to live in dry riverbeds, in holes in the earth and rocks.
They bray like donkeys among the bushes and huddle under thorn plants.
Sons of fools and worthless men, they were driven from the land.
Now I am the subject of their songs; I am a joke to them.
They hate me and stay away, but they do not hold back from spitting in my face.
Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have thrown off all restraint before me.
On my right the mob rises up; they set traps for my feet and build siege ramps against me.
They block my path; they add to my ruin, and no one stops them.
They come at me like an army through a broken wall; they roll in through the ruins.
Terrors turn against me; my honor is blown away like the wind, and my well-being has passed like a cloud.
Now my life drains out of me; days of suffering have taken hold of me.
At night pain pierces my bones; my aching never stops.
By His great power He grips my clothing; He chokes me by the collar of my shirt.
He has thrown me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry out to You, but You do not answer; I stand up, and You merely look at me.
You have turned cruel to me; with the strength of Your hand You persecute me.
You lift me up into the wind and make me ride it; You dissolve me in the storm.
Yes, I know You will bring me down to death, to the place where all living things go.
Yet when someone falls into ruins, doesn't he reach out his hand? Or in disaster, doesn't he cry for help?
Haven't I wept for those in trouble? Hasn't my heart grieved for the poor?
But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness came.
My stomach churns and never stops; days of suffering face me.
I walk around blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the crowd and cry for help.
I have become like a brother to jackals and a friend to owls.
My skin grows black and peels; my bones burn with fever.
My harp is tuned to mourning, and my flute to the sound of weeping.
I made a promise to my eyes not to look at a young woman with lust. How could I stare at her?
Otherwise, what blessing could I expect from God above? What gift would the Almighty send from heaven?
Doesn't disaster come to the wicked, and ruin to those who do wrong?
Doesn't He see everything I do and count every step I take?
If I have lived by lies, or my feet have rushed to cheat others,
let God weigh me on fair scales and know that I am innocent.
If I have wandered off the right path, or let my heart chase what my eyes wanted, or if guilt has stuck to my hands,
then let someone else eat what I plant, and let my children be torn up by the roots.
If my heart has been led astray by a woman, or I have lurked at my neighbor's door,
then let my wife serve another man, and let others sleep with her.
That would be a terrible sin, a crime for judges to punish.
It is like a fire that burns everything up and destroys all I have earned.
If I have ignored the complaints of my servants, male or female,
what will I do when God rises to judge me? When He questions me, what will I answer?
Didn't the God who made me in the womb make them too? Didn't the same God form us both?
If I have kept the poor from what they needed, or made a widow lose hope;
if I have eaten my food alone and not shared it with an orphan,
even though I have cared for the orphan like a father since I was young, and guided the widow all my life—
if I have seen someone freeze for lack of clothes, or a poor person with nothing to cover them;
and they were not warmed by wool from my sheep,
if I have raised my hand against an orphan because I had powerful friends in court,
then let my arm fall from my shoulder and break at the joint.
For I was terrified of disaster from God, and I could not stand against His greatness.
If I have trusted in gold, or called fine gold my safety;
if I have been glad just because I was rich or because I gained a lot;
if I have admired the sun in its brightness or the moon in its glory,
and my heart was secretly drawn to them, and I kissed my hand to them in worship,
that too would be a crime for judges to punish, because I would have denied the God above.
If I have been glad when my enemy was ruined, or felt proud when trouble hit him,
I have not let my mouth sin by asking God to curse his life.
The men in my tent never complained that they weren't filled with my food.
No stranger had to sleep in the street, because I opened my doors to travelers.
If I have hidden my sins like other people, keeping my guilt secret in my heart,
because I was afraid of the crowd and dreaded the scorn of families, so I kept quiet and stayed inside—
if only someone would hear me! Here is my signature; let the Almighty answer me, and let my accuser write his charge.
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.
I would tell Him every step I have taken; I would go to Him like a prince.
If my land accuses me and its furrows weep with it,
if I have eaten its crops without paying, or worn out the people who worked it,
then let thorns grow instead of wheat, and weeds instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
These three men had stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram, became very angry. He was angry at Job for justifying himself rather than God.
He was also angry with Job's three friends, because they had found no answer, yet they had condemned Job.
Elihu had waited to speak to Job because they were older than he was.
When Elihu saw that the three men had no answer, he became very angry.
"I am young in years, and you are old. That is why I was afraid and did not dare to tell you what I know.
I thought age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.
But there is a spirit in man, and the breath of the Almighty gives understanding.
It is not only the old who are wise, nor only the aged who understand justice.
So I say, 'Listen to me; I too will declare what I know.'
"Look, I waited for your words; I listened to your reasoning while you searched for words.
I paid close attention, but none of you proved Job wrong; none of you answered his words.
Do not say, 'We have found wisdom; God will drive him out, not a man.'
He has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
"They are upset and answer no more; words have failed them.
Should I wait because they do not speak, because they stand there and answer no more?
I too will answer; yes, I will declare what I know.
For I am full of words; the spirit within me forces me to speak.
Look, I am so full of words that I feel ready to burst.
I must speak so that I may find relief; I will open my lips and answer.
I will show no favoritism to anyone, and I will not flatter any man.
For I do not know how to flatter; if I did, my Maker would soon take me away."
"But now, Job, please listen to my words; pay attention to everything I say.
I am about to open my mouth; my tongue is ready to speak.
My words come from a sincere heart; my lips speak true knowledge.
The Spirit of God made me; the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Answer me if you can; prepare your case and stand before me.
I am the same as you in God's sight; I too was formed from clay.
So you need not fear me; I will not be harsh with you.
"Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard your words:
"'I am pure and without sin; I am clean and free of guilt.
Yet God finds fault with me; He considers me His enemy.
He puts my feet in stocks; He watches all my paths.'
"But I tell you, you are wrong in this, for God is greater than people.
Why do you argue with Him? He does not have to explain everything He does.
"For God speaks in one way and then another, but people may not notice.
He may speak in a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people as they slumber in their beds.
He opens their ears and disciplines them.
He does this to turn a person from wrong actions and keep him from pride.
He spares his soul from the grave and his life from dying violently.
"Or a man is corrected on his bed with pain and constant distress in his bones.
He loses his appetite for food, and even his favorite meal turns his stomach.
His body wastes away until his bones show.
He comes close to the grave, to the place of death.
"If there is an angel for him, one out of a thousand, to speak up for a man's uprightness,
then God is gracious to him and says, "'Spare him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom.'
"His flesh is restored like a child's; he returns to the days of his youth.
He prays to God and finds favor; he sees His face with a shout of joy, and God restores His righteousness to man.
Then he will say to others, "'I sinned and twisted what was right, but it did me no good.
He has redeemed my soul from going down to the pit, and my life will see the light.'
"Look, God does all these things to a person two or three times,
to bring his soul back from the pit, so that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
If you have something to say, answer me; speak, because I want to clear your name.
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom."
Then Elihu spoke up and said:
"Listen to my words, you wise men; hear me, you who know.
The ear tests words just like the tongue tastes food.
Let's choose what is right. Let's decide among ourselves what is good.
'I am right, but God has taken away my justice. Even though I am right, people call me a liar. My wound will not heal, even though I haven't sinned.'
"What man is like Job? He drinks up scorn like water.
He keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked people.
He said, "'It does no good for a person to try to please God.'
"Therefore, listen to me, you men of understanding: God would never do evil, and the Almighty would never do wrong.
He pays back a person for what they do and makes them face the results of their ways.
Truly, God does not do evil, and the Almighty does not twist justice.
Who put Him in charge of the earth? Who laid the whole world on Him?
If He set His heart on it and gathered His spirit and breath to Himself,
all people would die at once, and everyone would return to dust.
"If you have understanding, hear this; listen to what I say.
Could someone who hates justice rule? Will you condemn the righteous and mighty One?
It is wrong to say such things to a king or noble.
How much more is it wrong to say them to God, who shows no favor to princes and doesn't value the rich over the poor, since all are the work of His hands.
They die in a moment; at midnight people are shaken and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.
"His eyes are on a person's ways, and He sees every step.
There is no darkness or deep shadow where evildoers can hide.
God doesn't need to investigate a person more before judging him.
He breaks the mighty without asking questions and puts others in their place.
Because He knows what they do, He overthrows them at night, and they are crushed.
He punishes them as wicked people where everyone can see,
because they turned away from following Him and didn't care about any of His ways.
So they made the cry of the poor reach Him, and He heard the cry of those who suffer.
If He keeps quiet, who can accuse Him? If He hides His face, who can see Him? This is true for a nation or a person.
So godless people don't rule and don't trap the people.
"Has anyone ever said to God, 'I have been punished; I won't sin anymore'?
'Teach me what I don't see; if I have done wrong, I won't do it again'?
Should God repay you the way you want, just because you refuse His way? You have to decide, not I. So tell me what you know.
