"Men of understanding will say to me, and wise people who hear me will say,
'Job speaks without knowledge; his words show no insight.'
"I wish Job would be tested to the end, because he answers like wicked men.
He adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God."
"Do you think this is fair? You say, 'I am more righteous than God.'
You ask, 'What good does it do me? What do I gain by not sinning?'
I will answer you and your friends who are with you."
"Look up at the sky and see; look at the clouds high above you.
If you sin, what do you do to Him? If your sins are many, what do you do to Him?
If you are righteous, what do you give Him? Or what does He receive from your hand?
Your wrongdoing affects only people like you, and your right living affects only other people."
"Because of heavy oppression, people cry out; they call for help against the power of the mighty.
But no one says, 'Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
who teaches us more than the animals of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?'
There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil people.
Surely God does not listen to empty cries, and the Almighty does not pay attention to them.
How much less, then, when you say you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him!
And now, since He does not punish in anger and does not pay much attention to wrongdoing,
Job opens his mouth for nothing and piles up words without knowledge."
“Give me a little time, and I will show you. I still have more to say for God.
I will bring knowledge from far away and show that my Maker is right.
My words are truly not false. Someone who is fully wise is with you.
“Look, God is powerful, but He does not look down on anyone. He is powerful in understanding.
He does not keep wicked people alive, but He gives justice to those who are hurting.
He does not take His eyes off the people who do right. He sets them on thrones with kings and lifts them up for all time.
“If they are bound in chains and caught in ropes of trouble,
He tells them what they did and how they sinned. He shows that they acted proudly.
He opens their ears to teaching and tells them to turn away from sin.
If they listen and serve Him, they will live out their days in good times and their years in pleasure.
But if they do not listen, they will die by the sword and die without understanding.
“People with godless hearts hold on to anger. They do not cry for help when God binds them.
They die while young, and their lives end among male temple prostitutes.
But God saves suffering people through their suffering and opens their ears while they are in trouble.
He drew you out of trouble into a wide, open place, and your table was full of good food.
“But you are full of the judgment meant for wicked people. Judgment and justice have caught you.
Be careful that anger does not trick you into mocking. Do not let a large payment turn you away.
Will your cry for help save you from trouble, or will all your strength?
Do not long for the night, when people disappear from their place.
Be careful. Do not turn to sin, for you chose this instead of suffering.
“Look, God is lifted up by His power. Who is a teacher like Him?
Who has told Him how to live, or who can say, ‘You have done wrong’?
Remember to praise His work, which people have praised.
All people have seen it. People look at it from far away.
Look, God is great, and we do not know Him. The number of His years cannot be found out.
“He lifts up the drops of water, and they turn into rain from His mist.
The clouds pour it down and shower it heavily on people.
Can anyone understand how He spreads out the clouds or the thunder from His tent?
Look, He spreads His lightning all around Him and covers the depths of the sea.
He uses these things to judge people and to give plenty of food.
He fills His hands with lightning and tells it to hit the target.
His thunder announces Him, and even the cattle sense the storm coming.”
At this my heart trembles and leaps out of its place.
Listen carefully to the thunder of His voice and the rumble that comes from His mouth.
He sends it out under the whole sky, and His lightning to the ends of the earth.
Afterward His voice roars. He thunders with His majestic voice, and He does not hold back the lightning when His voice is heard.
God thunders marvelously with His voice; He does great things we cannot understand.
He tells the snow, "Fall on the earth," and to the rain shower, "Pour down hard."
He stops every person's work, so that everyone may know what He has done.
Then wild animals go into their dens and stay in their hiding places.
The storm comes from its chamber, and cold comes from the scattering winds.
By the breath of God, ice is made, and the wide waters are frozen solid.
He fills the thick cloud with water, and the cloud scatters His lightning.
They turn around and around by His guidance, to carry out everything He commands on the face of the whole world.
He sends it for correction, for His land, or as an act of mercy.
Listen to this, O Job; stand still and think about the wonderful works of God.
Do you know how God gives them their orders and makes the lightning flash from His cloud?
Do you know how the clouds are balanced, the amazing works of Him who is perfect in knowledge—
you whose clothes grow hot when the earth is still because of the south wind?
Can you spread out the sky with Him, hard as a mirror made of cast metal?
Teach us what we should say to Him; we cannot put our case in order because of the darkness.
Should someone tell Him that I want to speak? If a person spoke, would he not be swallowed up?
Now people cannot look at the bright light in the sky after the wind has passed and cleared the skies.
Out of the north comes golden splendor; God is clothed with terrifying majesty.
The Almighty—we cannot find Him; He is great in power, and in justice and great goodness He will not wrong anyone.
So people fear Him; He does not look with favor on those who are wise in their own eyes.
The LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
“Who is this who clouds good advice with words that show no knowledge?
Get ready like a man. I will question you, and you must answer Me.
“Where were you when I laid the earth's foundation? Tell Me, if you know so much.
Who set its size? Surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line across it?
What holds up its pillars? Or who set its cornerstone in place,
when the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy?
“Or who shut up the sea behind doors when it rushed out from the womb,
when I made clouds its clothing and thick darkness its blanket,
and set its limits and put bars and doors in place,
and said, ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here is where your proud waves must stop’?
“Have you ever given orders to the morning or told the dawn where it should be,
so it could grab the edges of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
The land changes like clay stamped with a seal, and its shapes stand out like clothing.
The wicked are denied their light, and their raised arm is broken.
“Have you gone to the springs of the sea or walked in the deepest parts of the ocean?
Have the gates of death been shown to you? Have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
Have you understood how wide the earth is? Tell Me, if you know all of it.
“Where is the road to light's home, and where does darkness live,
so you can take them to their borders and find the paths to their houses?
You must know, because you were born then, and your days are so many!
“Have you entered the storehouses of snow or seen the storehouses of hail,
which I have saved for times of trouble, for days of battle and war?
What is the path to where light is spread out, or where the east wind is scattered over the earth?
“Who dug a channel for the floodwaters and a path for the thunder,
to bring rain on land where no one lives, on the desert where no person is,
to water the empty, ruined land and make grass sprout?
“Does rain have a father? Or who fathered the drops of dew?
From whose womb did ice come? And who gave birth to the frost of heaven?
The water becomes hard like stone, and the surface of the deep freezes.
“Can you tie the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the cords of Orion?
Can you bring out the constellations at the right time? Can you lead the Bear with its cubs?
Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set their rule over the earth?
“Can you raise your voice to the clouds and make a flood of water cover you?
Can you send out lightning so it goes and says to you, ‘Here we are’?
Who put wisdom in the heart? Or who gave understanding to the mind?
“Who can count the clouds with wisdom? Or who can tip over the water jars of heaven,
when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods stick together?
“Can you hunt food for the lion or feed the young lions,
when they crouch in their dens or hide in the bushes waiting to attack?
Who gives the raven its food when its young cry out to God and wander around hungry?”
“Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the deer has her fawn?
Do you count the months until they are ready to give birth? Do you know when that time comes?
They crouch down and bring forth their young. They deliver their little ones.
Their young grow strong in the wild. They leave and do not return.
“Who set the wild donkey free? Who untied the ropes of the fast donkey?
I gave him the wasteland for his home and the salt flats for his place to live.
He ignores the noise of the city. He does not hear the driver’s shouts.
He roams the hills for food and looks for any green plant.
“Will the wild ox be willing to serve you? Will it stay by your feeding trough at night?
Can you tie the wild ox to a plow with a rope? Will it plow the valleys behind you?
Will you trust it because it is so strong? Will you leave your hard work to it?
Can you trust it to bring home your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
“The ostrich’s wings flap proudly, but are her wings and feathers like a stork’s?
She leaves her eggs on the ground and lets the dust warm them.
She forgets that a foot could crush them, or that a wild animal could trample them.
She is hard on her young, as if they were not hers. Her work is wasted, and she feels no fear.
God took wisdom from her and gave her no understanding.
Yet when she runs, she leaves the horse and its rider far behind.
“Do you give the horse its strength? Do you clothe its neck with a mane?
Do you make it jump like a locust? Its proud snorting scares people.
It paws the ground in the valley and is happy in its strength. It charges into battle.
It laughs at danger and is not afraid. It does not turn back from the sword.
The quiver rattles against it, along with the flashing spear and javelin.
It charges so hard that it seems to swallow the ground. It cannot stand still when the trumpet sounds.
When the trumpet blows, it says, ‘Aha!’ It smells the battle from far away and hears the thunder of leaders and the shouting.
“Does the hawk fly by your wisdom and spread its wings toward the south?
Does the eagle soar at your command and build its nest on high?
It lives on a cliff and stays there at night. A rocky peak is its safe place.
From there it looks for food. Its eyes see it from far away.
Its young feed on blood, and where the dead are, there it is.”
Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
“Will the one who argues with the Almighty correct Him? Let him who rebukes God answer Him.”
Then Job answered the LORD and said:
“Look, I am worthless. What can I answer You? I have put my hand over my mouth.
I have spoken once, and I will not answer again; twice, but I will say no more.”
Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
“Brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer Me.
Would you discredit My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?
Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His? “
Then adorn yourself with majesty and dignity; clothe yourself with honor and splendor.
Unleash the fury of your anger; look at every proud man and bring him low.
Look at every proud man and humble him; crush the wicked where they stand.
Bury them together in the dust; hide their faces in the grave.
Then I will also praise you, because your own right hand can save you.”
“Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He eats grass like an ox.
Look at the strength in his hips and the power in the muscles of his belly.
His tail sways like a cedar; the tendons of his thighs are woven together.
His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are like bars of iron.
He ranks first among God’s works; only his Maker can draw near with His sword.
The hills yield him their produce, and all the wild animals play there.
He lies under the lotus plants, in the hiding place of reeds and marsh.
The lotus plants shelter him with their shade; the poplars by the stream surround him.
If the river rages, he does not panic; he is confident even if the Jordan surges against his mouth.
Can anyone capture him by his eyes, or pierce his nose with a snare?”
"Can you pull in Leviathan with a fishhook, or tie down his tongue with a rope?
Can you put a cord through his nose, or pierce his jaw with a hook?
Will he beg you for mercy again and again? Will he speak soft words to you?
"Will he make a promise with you to be your servant forever?
Can you play with him like a bird, or tie him up for your young girls?
"Will traders try to buy him? Will they split him up among merchants?
Can you fill his skin with harpoons, or his head with fishing spears?
If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never do it again.
"Any hope of beating him is false. Just seeing him is enough to knock someone down.
No one is brave enough to wake him up. Who then can stand against Me?
Who has given Me anything that I should pay him back? Everything under heaven is Mine.
"I will not stay quiet about his limbs, his strength, and his graceful shape.
Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can come near him with a bridle?
Who can open the doors of his mouth? His teeth all around are terrifying.
"His back has rows of shields, sealed together tightly.
Each one is so close to the next that no air can pass between them.
They are joined fast to one another. They stick together and cannot be separated.
"His sneezes flash out light, and his eyes are like the first light of morning.
Firebrands stream from his mouth, and sparks of fire shoot out.
Smoke pours from his nostrils like a boiling pot over burning reeds.
His breath sets coals on fire, and flames dart from his mouth.
"Strength lives in his neck, and fear dances in front of him.
The folds of his flesh are stuck together. They are firm and cannot move.
His heart is hard as stone, as hard as the lower millstone.
"When he rises up, even the mighty are afraid. They step back when he thrashes around.
A sword that reaches him does no good. Neither do a spear, a dart, or a javelin.
He treats iron like straw and bronze like rotten wood.
"Arrows cannot make him run away. Slingstones are like chaff to him.
A club seems as light as straw to him. He laughs at the rattling of a lance.
His underside is like sharp broken pottery. He leaves a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
He makes the deep water boil like a pot. He stirs the sea until it foams.
"He leaves a shining wake behind him. It looks like the deep sea has white hair.
Nothing on earth is like him. He is a creature without fear.
He looks down on everything proud. He is king over all who are proud."
Then Job answered the LORD and said:
"I know that You can do all things, and no plan of Yours can be stopped.
Who is this who hides advice without knowledge? So I have said things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
Please listen, and I will speak. I will ask You, and You will teach me.
I had heard about You before, but now my eyes see You.
So I despise myself and repent in dust and ashes."

After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite: "My anger burns against you and against your two friends, because you have not spoken the truth about Me, as My servant Job has.

Now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer and not punish you for your foolish talk. You have not spoken the truth about Me, as My servant Job has."
So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them, and the LORD accepted Job's prayer.
After Job prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his fortunes and gave him twice as much as he had before.

Then all his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came to him. They ate with him in his house, showed him sympathy, and comforted him for all the hardship the LORD had brought on him. Each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
The LORD blessed the later days of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female donkeys.
He also had seven sons and three daughters.
He named the first daughter Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
In all the land there were no women as beautiful as Job's daughters. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
After this Job lived 140 years. He saw his sons and his grandsons for four generations.
Then Job died, old and full of days.
Blessed is the man who does not walk in the advice of the wicked, or stand in the way of sinners, or sit in the seat of mockers.
But his delight is in the law of the LORD, and he thinks about His law day and night.
He is like a tree planted by streams of water. It gives its fruit in season, and its leaves do not dry up. Everything he does succeeds.
The wicked are not like that. They are like chaff that the wind blows away.
So the wicked will not stand when God judges, and sinners will not be in the group of the righteous.
For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will be destroyed.
Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?
The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers gather together against the the LORD and against His Anointed.
"Let us break their chains and throw off their ropes."
The One who sits in heaven laughs; the Lord mocks them.
Then He speaks to them in His anger and terrifies them in His fury:
"As for me, I have set my King on Zion, my holy hill."
I will tell of the decree the the LORD gave me: "You are my Son; today I have become your Father.
Ask me, and I will give the nations to you as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession.
You will break them with an iron rod; you will shatter them like pottery."
So now, kings, be wise; rulers of the earth, take warning.
Serve the the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Show honor to the Son, or He may become angry and you may be destroyed on your way, for His anger can flare up quickly. Blessed are all who take refuge in Him.
O LORD, how many enemies I have! Many are rising against me.
Many say, “God won’t save him.” Selah.
But you, O LORD, are my protector. You are my honor, and You give me new courage.
I call out to the LORD, and He answers me from His holy hill. Selah.
I lie down and sleep. I wake again, for the LORD sustains me.
I won’t be afraid of the thousands of people who surround me on every side.
Arise, O LORD! Save me, O my God! For You defeat all my enemies and take away the power of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the LORD. May Your blessing rest on Your people! Selah.
Answer me when I call, O God who makes me right! You gave me room when I was in trouble; have mercy on me and hear my prayer.
How long will you people turn my honor into shame? How long will you love empty things and chase lies? Selah.
But know that the LORD has chosen those who are faithful for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.
Tremble, and do not sin. Think about these things in your heart while you lie in bed, and be quiet. Selah.
Offer right sacrifices, and put your trust in the LORD.
Many are saying, "Who will show us any good?" Let the light of Your face shine on us, O the LORD.
You have filled my heart with more joy than they have when their grain and new wine are plentiful.
I will lie down and sleep in peace, because You alone, O the LORD, keep me safe.
Listen to my words, the LORD; consider my groaning.
Listen to my cry for help, my King and my God, for I pray to You.
In the morning, the LORD, You hear my voice; in the morning I bring my prayers to You and wait in hope.
For You are not a God who delights in wickedness; no evil can dwell with You.
Proud people cannot stand before You; You hate all who do evil.
You destroy those who speak lies; the LORD detests bloodthirsty and deceitful men.
But I will enter Your house because of Your great mercy; in reverence I will bow down toward Your holy temple.
Lead me, the LORD, in Your righteousness because of my enemies; make Your way straight before me.
For there is no truth in their mouths; their hearts are full of ruin; their throats are open graves; they flatter with their tongues.
Declare them guilty, O God; let them fall by their own plans; throw them out for their many sins, for they have rebelled against You.
But let everyone who trusts in You rejoice; let them shout for joy forever, and shelter them, so that those who love Your name may be glad in You.
For surely, the LORD, You bless those who do right; You surround them with favor like a shield.
The LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger, and do not discipline me in Your wrath.
Be gracious to me, the LORD, for I am weak; heal me, the LORD, for my bones ache.
My soul is deeply troubled. How long, the LORD? How long?
Turn, the LORD, and rescue me; save me because of Your faithful love.
For there is no memory of You in death; who can praise You from the grave?
I am worn out from groaning; all night I soak my bed with tears; I drench my couch with weeping.
My eyes grow dim with grief; they waste away because of all my foes.
Get away from me, all you who do evil, for the LORD has heard my crying.
The LORD has heard my plea; the LORD accepts my prayer.
All my enemies will be ashamed and terrified; they will turn back in sudden shame.
A song of David for the the LORD, about Cush, a man from Benjamin. The LORD, my God, I have run to You for safety. Save me from all who chase me, and rescue me.
Otherwise, they will tear me apart like a lion, ripping me to pieces with no one to save me.
The LORD, my God, if I have done this, if my hands are guilty of wrong,
if I have repaid my friend with evil or robbed my enemy for no reason,
then let my enemy chase me and catch me. Let him trample my life into the ground and throw my honor in the dust. Selah
The LORD, rise up in Your anger. Stand against the fury of those who attack me. Wake up, my God, and bring justice.
Let the nations gather around You, and take Your place above them.
The LORD judges the peoples. The LORD, judge me by my goodness and honesty.
End the evil of the wicked, and strengthen the righteous. You are the God who tests hearts and minds.
My shield is with God, who saves those with pure hearts.
God is a fair judge, and He is angry with the wicked every day.
If a person does not turn back, God will sharpen His sword. He has bent His bow and made it ready.
He has prepared deadly weapons. He makes His arrows burn.
Look, the wicked person is full of trouble. He plans evil and gives birth to lies.
He dug a pit and made it deep, but he fell into the hole he made.
His trouble will come back on his own head. His violence will fall on his own head.
I will thank the the LORD for His fairness. I will sing praise to the name of the the LORD, the Most High.
The LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth! You have set Your glory above the heavens.
From the mouths of children and infants You have established strength, because of Your enemies, to silence the foe and the avenger.
When I look at Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars, which You have set in place,
what is man that You remember him, and the son of man that You care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels, and crowned him with glory and honor.
You made him ruler over the works of Your hands; You put everything under his feet:
all sheep and cattle, and even the beasts of the field,
the birds of the air and the fish of the sea, all that swim the paths of the seas.
The LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!
I will thank the LORD with all my heart. I will tell about all the amazing things You have done.
I will be glad and rejoice in You. I will sing praises to Your name, O Most High.
When my enemies run away, they stumble and die before You.
You have defended my cause and my rights. You sit on Your throne and judge fairly.
You warned the nations and destroyed the wicked. You erased their names forever.
The enemy is finished forever. You tore down their cities, and even their memory is gone.
But the LORD sits on His throne forever. He set it up to bring justice.
He judges the world fairly and rules the nations with justice.
The LORD is a safe place for people who are treated badly, a refuge in times of trouble.
Those who know You trust in You, because You, O the LORD, do not abandon those who look for You.
Sing praises to the LORD, who rules from Zion! Tell the nations what He has done.
He remembers those who were murdered. He does not forget the cries of the suffering.
Show me mercy, O the LORD! See how my enemies hurt me. You pull me back from the edge of death.
Then I will tell of all Your praises in the gates of Zion and rejoice in Your rescue.
The nations sank into the pit they dug. Their own feet got caught in the net they hid.
The LORD has shown Himself. He has judged fairly. The wicked are trapped by what their own hands have done. Pause and think about this.
The wicked will go down to the grave—all the nations that forget God.
The needy will not be forgotten forever, and the hope of the poor will not die.
Rise up, O the LORD! Do not let people win. Judge the nations in Your presence.
Make them afraid, O the LORD! Let the nations know they are only human. Pause.
Why do You stand so far away, the LORD? Why do You hide when trouble comes?
The wicked proudly hunt down the poor. Let them be caught in the traps they set.
The wicked brag about what they want. They praise greedy people and insult the the LORD.
In his pride, the wicked man does not seek God. All his plans say, "There is no God."
He always seems to get his way. Your judgments are far from his mind. He sneers at everyone who opposes him.
He says to himself, "I will never be shaken. I will never face trouble, not for generations."
His mouth is full of curses, lies, and threats. Trouble and evil hide under his tongue.
He hides near villages and waits. In secret places he kills innocent people. His eyes watch for the helpless.
He lurks in secret like a lion in its den. He waits to catch the poor and drags them into his net.
The helpless are crushed and beaten down. They fall under his power.
He says to himself, "God has forgotten. He has hidden His face. He will never notice."
Arise, the LORD! Take action, O God! Do not forget those who are hurting!
Why does the wicked man insult God? He tells himself, "You will not hold me accountable."
But You have seen the trouble and grief. You take it into Your own hands. The victim trusts You. You have been the helper of orphans.
Break the power of the wicked and those who do evil. Search out his wrongdoing until none is left.
The LORD is King forever and ever. The nations will perish from His land.
You have heard the longing of those who are hurting. You will strengthen their hearts. You will listen closely.
You will bring justice to orphans and those who are crushed, so that mere mortals will no longer terrify them.
I trust in the LORD. So how can you tell me, "Run away to your mountain like a bird"?
Look, the wicked are bending their bows and getting their arrows ready. They want to shoot from the dark at people whose hearts are right.
If the foundations are destroyed, what can good people do?
The LORD is in His holy temple. The LORD sits on His throne in heaven. His eyes see everything, and He tests all people.
The LORD tests both good people and wicked people. He hates those who love violence.
He will rain down fire and burning sulfur on the wicked. A scorching wind will be their punishment.
For the LORD is good and right. He loves what is right. Good people will live in His presence.
Help, O the LORD, for godly people are gone; the faithful have disappeared from among people.
They lie to each other; they speak with flattering lips and a heart that says one thing but means another.
May the LORD cut off all flattering lips and the tongue that boasts.
They say, “With our tongues we will win; our lips belong to us. Who is master over us?”
“Because the poor are crushed and the needy groan, now I will act,” says the LORD. “I will give safety to the one who longs for My help.”
The LORD’s words are pure, like silver melted in a furnace and cleaned seven times.
O the LORD, You will keep them safe; You will guard them from this generation forever.
Wicked people walk freely everywhere when what is shameful is praised among people.
How long, O the LORD, will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
How long must I worry and feel sad in my heart all day? How long will my enemy have power over me?
Look at me and answer me, O the LORD my God. Give me strength, or I will die.
Then my enemy would say, “I have beaten him,” and my foes would be glad because I am shaken.
But I trust in your unfailing love; my heart rejoices in your salvation.
I will sing to the LORD, for He has been good to me.
For the choir director. A Psalm of David. The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt, and their actions are vile. No one does good.
The LORD looks down from heaven on the people to see if anyone understands and seeks God.
They have all turned away; together they have become corrupt. No one does good, not even one.
Will those who do evil never learn? They eat up my people like bread, and they do not call on the the LORD.
There they are, filled with dread, for God is with those who do right.
You shame the plans of the poor, but the the LORD is their refuge.
Oh, that salvation for Israel would come from Zion! When the the LORD restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.
A psalm of David. The LORD, who may stay in Your tent? Who may live on Your holy mountain?
The one who walks with honesty and does what is right, speaking truth in his heart.
He does not gossip about others, does no harm to his neighbor, and does not bring shame on his friend.
He has no respect for a worthless person, but he honors those who fear the LORD. He keeps his promise even when it hurts.
He does not charge interest when he lends his money, and he does not take a bribe to hurt an innocent person. The one who does these things will never be shaken.
A poem of David. Protect me, God, because I trust in You.
I said to the LORD, “You are my Lord; I have no good apart from You.”
As for the faithful people in the land, they are the noble ones, and I delight in them.
Those who chase after other gods will have more and more sorrow. I won't pour out their blood offerings or even speak their names.
The LORD is my share and my cup; You hold my future.
My boundaries fell in pleasant places; yes, I have a beautiful inheritance.
I will praise the LORD, who advises me; even at night my heart teaches me.
I always keep the LORD before me. Because He is at my right hand, I won't be shaken.
So my heart is glad and my whole self rejoices; even my body rests safely.
For You won't leave my soul in the grave, and You won't let Your Holy One decay.
You show me the path of life. In Your presence there is complete joy, and at Your right hand are pleasures that last forever.
the LORD, hear my honest prayer; listen to my cry for justice. My lips do not lie.
Let my case be judged fairly by You, and let Your eyes see what is right.
You have tested my heart and checked on me at night. You have refined me and found nothing wrong; I have decided not to sin with my mouth.
As for what people do, by the words of Your lips I have stayed away from the paths of violent men.
My steps have stayed on Your paths, and my feet have not slipped.
I call on You, O God, because You will answer me. Turn Your ear to me and hear my words.
Show Your wonderful faithful love, O Savior of those who find safety at Your right hand against those who rise up against them.
Guard me as something You treasure deeply; hide me in the shadow of Your wings.
Protect me from the wicked who attack me, from my deadly enemies who surround me.
They have shut their hearts to pity; their mouths speak with pride.
They have tracked me down and now surround me; they watch me, ready to throw me to the ground.
They are like a lion eager to tear its prey, like a young lion hiding in ambush.
Rise up, O the LORD; go before them and bring them down. Save my life from the wicked by Your sword.

the LORD, save me by Your hand from people of this world whose share is only in this life. You fill their bellies with Your treasure; their sons are satisfied, and they leave what is left to their children.
But as for me, I will see Your face in righteousness; when I awake, I will be satisfied with Your presence.
I love You, the LORD, my strength.
The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my Savior. My God is my rock. I hide in Him. He is my shield, the strength that saves me, and my safe place.
I will call on the LORD, who deserves praise. Then I will be saved from my enemies.
Death's ropes wrapped around me. Floods of trouble scared me.
The grave's ropes held me. Death's traps came in front of me.
When I was in trouble, I called to the LORD. I cried to my God for help. He heard my voice from His temple. My cry reached His ears.
The earth shook and quaked. The foundations of the mountains trembled. They shook because He was angry.
Smoke rose from His nostrils. Fire came from His mouth and burned. Coals blazed from it.
He opened the sky and came down. Dark clouds were under His feet.
He rode on a cherub and flew. He soared on the wind's wings.
He made darkness His hiding place. Rain clouds surrounded Him.
From the brightness before Him, His clouds passed by with hail and burning coals.
The LORD thundered from heaven. The Most High sent hail and burning coals.
He shot His arrows and scattered His enemies. He flashed lightning and threw them into panic.
The sea beds showed. The world's foundations were laid bare. This happened at Your rebuke, the LORD, at the blast of Your angry breath.
He reached down from heaven and took hold of me. He pulled me out of deep water.
He saved me from my strong enemy and from foes too strong for me.
They attacked me when I was in trouble, but the LORD supported me.
He brought me to a wide open place. He rescued me because He was pleased with me.
The LORD has rewarded me for doing right. He paid me back for my clean hands.
I have kept the LORD's ways. I have not turned from my God to do wrong.
All His rules are in front of me. I have not ignored His laws.
I was innocent before Him. I kept myself from sin.
So the LORD paid me back for my right living. He saw that my hands were clean.
You are faithful to faithful people. You are perfect to those who are perfect.
You are pure to those who are pure. But You are clever with those who twist things.
You save suffering people, but You bring down those with proud eyes.
You, the LORD, light my lamp. My God turns my darkness into light.
With You I can charge through an army. With my God I can climb over a wall.
God's way is perfect. The LORD's word is pure. He is a shield to everyone who trusts in Him.
Who is God besides the LORD? Who is a rock except our God?
God gives me strength and makes my path clear.
He makes my feet like a deer's feet. He sets me on high places.
He trains my hands for war. My arms can bend a bronze bow.
You have given me Your saving shield. Your right hand holds me up. Your gentleness makes me great.
You make my steps wide under me, so my feet do not slip.
I chase my enemies and catch them. I do not turn back until they are destroyed.
I crush them so they cannot get up. They fall under my feet.
You give me strength for the battle. You make my enemies bow under me.
You make my enemies run away. I destroy those who hate me.
They cry for help, but no one saves them. They even cry to the LORD, but He does not answer.
I grind them like dust in the wind. I trample them like mud in the streets.
You save me from fighting with my people. You make me the leader of nations. People I did not know serve me.
As soon as they hear me, they obey me. Foreigners submit to me.
Foreigners lose their strength. They come trembling out of their forts.
The LORD lives! Blessed be my Rock! May the God who saves me be praised.
He is the God who pays back my enemies and brings nations under me.
He saves me from my enemies. You lift me above my foes. You rescue me from violent men.
So I will praise You, the LORD, among the nations. I will sing to Your name.
He gives His king great victories. He shows faithful love to His anointed, to David and his descendants forever.
The heavens tell about God's glory, and the sky shows the work of His hands.
Day after day they pour out speech; night after night they show knowledge.
They have no speech and use no words. No sound is heard from them.
Yet their voice goes out through all the earth, and their words reach the ends of the world. In the heavens God has set a tent for the sun.
The sun is like a bridegroom coming out of his room. It runs its path with joy, like a strong man.
It rises from one end of the sky and travels to the other. Nothing can hide from its heat.
The law of the the LORD is perfect. It gives new life to the soul. The the LORD's testimony is trustworthy. It makes the simple wise.
The the LORD's rules are right. They bring joy to the heart. The the LORD's command is pure. It gives light to the eyes.
Respect for the the LORD is pure. It lasts forever. The the LORD's decisions are true and right in every way.
They are more desirable than gold, even more than much pure gold. They are sweeter than honey, even sweeter than honey from the comb.
By them Your servant is warned. Keeping them brings a great reward.
Who can notice his own mistakes? Clear me of hidden faults.
Keep Your servant from willful sins. Do not let them rule over me. Then I will be blameless and free from great sin.
May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be pleasing to You, O the LORD, my Rock and my Redeemer.
May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob keep you safe.
May He send you help from the holy place and support you from Zion.
May He remember all your gifts and accept your burnt offerings. Selah
May He give you what your heart wants and make all your plans succeed.
May we shout for joy over your victory and lift up our banners in the name of our God. May the LORD grant all your requests.
Now I know that the LORD saves His anointed; He answers him from His holy heaven with the saving power of His right hand.
Some trust in chariots and others in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.
They collapse and fall, but we rise up and stand firm.
May the LORD save the king! Answer us when we call!
O the LORD, the king rejoices in Your strength. How greatly he exults in Your salvation!
You have granted his heart’s desire and have not withheld the request of his lips. Selah.
You welcome him with rich blessings and place a crown of pure gold on his head.
He asked You for life, and You gave it to him—length of days forever and ever.
His glory is great because of Your salvation; You have given him honor and majesty.
You bless him forever, and You fill him with joy by Your presence.
The king trusts in the LORD, and because of the faithful love of the Most High, he will not be shaken.
Your hand will catch all Your enemies; Your right hand will seize those who hate You.
You will make them like a hot oven when You appear. In His wrath the the LORD will swallow them up, and fire will consume them.
You will destroy their children from the earth and their descendants from among people.
They planned evil against You and made a plot, but they cannot carry it out.
You will make them run away, and You will aim Your arrows at them.
Be lifted high, O the LORD, in Your strength! We will sing and praise Your power.
For the director of music. To the tune of "The Doe of the Dawn." A psalm of David. My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? Why are You so far from saving me, and so far from hearing my cries?
My God, I cry out by day, but You do not answer; by night I find no rest.
Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.
In You our fathers trusted; they trusted, and You delivered them.
They cried out to You and were saved; they trusted in You and were not put to shame.
But I am a worm, not a man; I am scorned by men and despised by the people.
All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads:
"He trusts in the the LORD; let the the LORD rescue him. Let Him deliver him, since He delights in him."
Yet You brought me out of the womb; You made me trust in You, even at my mother's breast.
From birth I was cast on You; from my mother's womb You have been my God.
Do not be far from me, for trouble is near and there is no one to help.
Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me.
They open their mouths against me like a roaring lion that tears its prey.
I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax; it melts within me.
My strength is dried up like a piece of pottery, and my tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth; You lay me in the dust of death.
Dogs surround me; a band of evil men encircles me; they have pierced my hands and feet.
I can count all my bones; they stare and gloat over me.
They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.
But You, the the LORD, do not stay far away; my Strength, come quickly to help me.
Save my life from the sword, and my precious life from the dog's power.
Save me from the lion's mouth; save me from the horns of the wild oxen. You have answered me.
I will declare Your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will praise You.
You who fear the the LORD, praise Him! All you descendants of Jacob, honor Him! All you descendants of Israel, revere Him!
For He has not despised or scorned the suffering of the afflicted; He has not hidden His face from him, but has listened to his cry for help.
My praise for You resounds in the great assembly; I will fulfill my vows before those who fear You.
The poor will eat and be satisfied; those who seek Him will praise the the LORD. May your hearts live forever!
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the the LORD, and all the families of the nations will bow down before Him.
For dominion belongs to the the LORD, and He rules over the nations.
All the rich of the earth will feast and worship; all who die will bow before Him—even those who cannot keep themselves alive.
Future generations will serve Him; they will declare the Lord to a future generation.
They will come and proclaim His righteousness to a people yet unborn—that He has done it!
The LORD is my shepherd. I will not be in need.
He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside quiet waters.
He gives me new strength. He guides me on the right paths for the sake of His name.
Even when I walk through the darkest valley, I will not be afraid, because You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.
You prepare a feast for me where my enemies can see. You pour oil on my head, and my cup runs over.
Goodness and faithful love will follow me all my life, and I will live in the house of the LORD forever.
A psalm of David. The earth belongs to the the LORD, and everything in it. The world and all who live in it are His.
He founded it on the seas and set it firm on the rivers.
Who may go up the the LORD’s holy hill? Who may stand in His holy place?
The one with clean hands and a pure heart, who doesn’t lift his soul to an idol or swear falsely.
He will receive a blessing from the the LORD and righteousness from God his Savior.
Such are the people who seek Him, who seek Your face, O God of Jacob. Selah.
Lift up your heads, O gates, and be lifted up, O ancient doors, so the King of glory may come in.
Who is this King of glory? The The LORD, strong and mighty, the the LORD, mighty in battle.
Lift up your heads, O gates, and lift them up, O ancient doors, so the King of glory may come in.
Who is this King of glory? The the LORD of Hosts—He is the King of glory. Selah.
To You, the LORD, I give my whole self.
My God, I trust in You. Do not let me be disgraced. Do not let my enemies win over me.
No one who hopes in You will be disgraced. But those who betray others for no reason will be disgraced.
Show me Your ways, the LORD. Teach me Your paths.
Lead me in Your truth and teach me. You are the God who saves me. I hope in You all day long.
Remember Your mercy and faithful love, the LORD. You have shown them since long ago.
Do not remember the sins of my youth or my rebellious acts. Remember me with Your faithful love, the LORD, because of Your goodness.
The LORD is good and right. So He teaches sinners the right path.
He guides humble people in what is right and teaches them His way.
All the the LORD's paths are faithful love and truth for those who keep His agreement and His commands.
For Your name's sake, the LORD, forgive my guilt, because it is great.
Who is the person who honors the the LORD? The LORD will show him the path to choose.
He will live well, and his children will inherit the land.
The LORD is a friend to those who honor Him, and He shows them His agreement.
My eyes are always on the the LORD, because He will pull my feet out of the trap.
Turn to me and be kind to me. I am alone and suffering.
My heart's troubles are growing worse. Bring me out of my distress.
Look at my suffering and my pain, and forgive all my sins.
See how many enemies I have and how cruelly they hate me.
Guard my life and rescue me. Do not let me be disgraced, because I run to You for safety.
May honesty and right living protect me, because I hope in You.
Rescue Israel, God, from all its troubles.
Judge me, the LORD, for I have walked in my honesty. I have trusted in the LORD, and I will not slip.
Test me, the LORD, and try me; refine my heart and mind.
For Your faithful love is before my eyes, and I have walked in Your truth.
I have not sat with deceitful people, and I will not go with hypocrites.
I have hated the crowd of evildoers, and I will not sit with wicked people.
I will wash my hands in innocence and walk around Your altar, the LORD.
I do this to give thanks out loud and to tell about all Your wonders.
The LORD, I have loved the house where You live, the place where Your glory stays.
Do not gather my soul with sinners, or my life with men who shed blood,
whose hands are full of evil plans and whose right hands are full of bribes.
But I will walk in my honesty; redeem me and be gracious to me.
My foot stands on level ground; in the assemblies I will bless the LORD.
The LORD is my light and my salvation. Who should I fear? The LORD is the strength of my life. Who can make me afraid?
When evil people came close to attack me, my enemies and foes stumbled and fell.
Even if an army camps against me, my heart will not be afraid. Even if war rises against me, I will trust in Him.
I have asked the LORD for one thing, and that is what I seek: to live in the LORD's house all my life, to see how beautiful the LORD is, and to look for guidance in His temple.
For in the day of trouble He will hide me in His shelter. He will conceal me in the secret place of His tent. He will lift me up on a rock.
Now my head will be lifted above my enemies all around me. In His tent I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy. I will sing and make music to the LORD.
Hear my voice when I call, the LORD. Be gracious to me and answer me.
My heart says to You, “Seek His face.” The LORD, I will seek Your face.
Do not hide Your face from me. Do not turn Your servant away in anger. You have been my help. Do not leave me or abandon me, O God of my salvation.
Even if my father and mother leave me, the LORD will take me in.
Teach me Your way, the LORD, and lead me on a straight path because of my enemies.
Do not hand me over to the desire of my foes, for false witnesses have risen against me, breathing out violence.
I would have lost hope unless I believed I would see the LORD's goodness in the land of the living.
Wait for the LORD. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Wait for the LORD.
I call to You, the LORD. You are my Rock. Don't stay silent when I need You. If You stay silent, I'll be like those who go down to the grave.
Hear my prayers when I cry out to You. I lift my hands toward Your holy place.
Don't drag me away with evil people or with those who do wrong. They act friendly to their neighbors, but they plan evil in their hearts.
Pay them back for what they've done. Give them what their evil actions deserve.
They don't understand what the LORD does or the work of His hands. So He will tear them down and not build them up.
Praise the LORD, because He heard my prayers.
The LORD is my strength and shield. My heart trusted in Him, and He helped me. My heart is glad, and I will thank Him with my songs.
The LORD gives strength to His people. He is the safe place that saves His chosen king.
Save Your people and bless the people You chose. Lead them like a shepherd and carry them forever.
Give to the LORD, O sons of God, give to the LORD glory and strength.
Give to the LORD the glory His name deserves; worship the LORD in the beauty of His holiness.
The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders; the LORD is over many waters.
The voice of the LORD is powerful; the voice of the LORD is full of majesty.
The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars; yes, the LORD shatters the cedars of Lebanon.
He makes Lebanon skip like a calf, and Sirion like a young wild ox.
The voice of the LORD strikes with flames of fire.
The voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness; the LORD shakes the Wilderness of Kadesh.
The voice of the LORD twists the oaks and strips the forests bare, and in His temple all cry, "Glory!"
The LORD sits as King over the flood; the LORD is King forever.
the LORD gives strength to His people; the LORD blesses His people with peace.
I will lift You up, the LORD, because You have lifted me up. You did not let my enemies celebrate over me.
The LORD my God, I called to You for help, and You healed me.
The LORD, You brought my soul up from the grave. You kept me alive so I would not go down into the pit.
Sing to the LORD, you who are faithful to Him. Give thanks to His holy name.
His anger lasts only a moment, but His favor lasts a lifetime. Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.
When life was going well, I said, “I will never be shaken.”
The LORD, by Your favor You made me as steady as a mountain. When You hid Your face, I was terrified.
To You, the LORD, I called. To the Lord I cried for mercy:
“What good would my death do? If I go down to the pit, will the dust praise You? Will it tell about Your faithfulness?
Hear me, the LORD, and be gracious to me. The LORD, be my helper.”
You turned my mourning into dancing. You took away my sackcloth and dressed me with joy.
So I will sing Your praise with all my heart and not be silent. The LORD my God, I will thank You forever.
In You, the LORD, I have taken refuge. Let me never be put to shame. Deliver me in Your righteousness.
Turn Your ear to me. Come quickly to save me. Be my rock of refuge, a strong fortress to save me.
For You are my rock and my fortress. Lead me and guide me for Your name's sake.
Free me from the trap they hid for me, for You are my refuge.
Into Your hands I commit my spirit. You have redeemed me, the LORD, God of truth.
I hate those who cling to worthless idols, but I trust in the LORD.
I will be glad and rejoice in Your loving devotion, for You have seen my trouble. You have known my deep sorrow.
You have not handed me over to the enemy. You have set my feet in an open place.
Be gracious to me, the LORD, for I am in trouble. My eyes are worn out from sorrow, and so are my soul and body.
My life is worn out with grief, and my years with groaning. My strength fails because of my sin, and my bones grow weak.
I am a disgrace to all my enemies and a terror to my neighbors. Those who know me run away. Those who see me in the street flee from me.
I am forgotten like a dead man, out of everyone's mind. I am like a broken pot.
For I hear the slander of many. Terror is on every side. They plot together against me and plan to take my life.
But I trust in You, the LORD. I say, "You are my God."
My future is in Your hands. Save me from my enemies and from those who chase me.
Show Your favor to Your servant. Save me in Your loving devotion.
The LORD, don't let me be put to shame, for I called on You. Let the wicked be put to shame. Let them be silent in the grave.
Let their lying lips be silenced—those that speak arrogantly against the righteous with pride and contempt.
How great is Your goodness! You have stored it up for those who fear You and given it to those who take refuge in You, right in front of everyone!
You hide them in the shelter of Your presence from the schemes of men. You conceal them in Your shelter from accusing tongues.
Blessed be the LORD, for He has shown His wonderful loving devotion to me in a city under siege.
In my panic I said, "I am cut off from Your sight!" But You heard my cries for mercy when I called to You.
Love the LORD, all you who are faithful to Him! The LORD protects the faithful and fully punishes the proud.
Be strong and take courage, all you who put your hope in the LORD.
Blessed is the one whose wrongs are forgiven and whose sins are covered.
Blessed is the person the the LORD does not count as guilty, and in whose spirit there is no deceit.
When I kept silent, my bones wore out through my groaning all day long.
For day and night Your hand was heavy on me; my strength dried up like the heat of summer. Selah
Then I told You about my sin and did not hide my guilt. I said, “I will confess my wrongs to the the LORD,” and You forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah
So let every godly person pray to You while You can be found. Surely, when great waters rise, they will not reach him.
You are my hiding place; You keep me safe from trouble; You surround me with songs of rescue. Selah
“I will teach you and show you the way to go; I will give you advice; My eye is on you.
Do not be like a horse or mule, which has no understanding and must be controlled with a bit and bridle, or it will not come near you.”
Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but faithful love surrounds the one who trusts in the the LORD.
Be glad in the the LORD and rejoice, you righteous; shout for joy, all you upright in heart.
Sing for joy in the LORD, you righteous people. Praise looks good on those who are upright.
Give thanks to the LORD with the lyre. Sing praises to Him with the ten-stringed harp.
Sing a new song to Him. Play well with a joyful shout.
For the word of the LORD is upright, and all His work is done in faithfulness.
He loves righteousness and justice. The earth is full of the faithful love of the LORD.
By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and all their stars by the breath of His mouth.
He gathers the waters of the sea like a heap. He stores the deep waters in warehouses.
Let all the earth fear the LORD. Let all who live in the world stand in awe of Him.
For He spoke, and it happened. He gave the command, and it stood firm.
The LORD frustrates the plans of the nations. He stops the schemes of the peoples.
The plans of the LORD stand forever. His heart's thoughts last from generation to generation.
Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people He chose as His own inheritance.
The LORD looks down from heaven. He sees all people.
From where He lives, He watches all who live on the earth.
He forms the hearts of all. He understands all their deeds.
No king is saved by a large army. No warrior is rescued by great strength.
The horse is a false hope for rescue. Even with its great strength, it cannot save.
The eyes of the LORD are on those who fear Him, on those who hope in His faithful love.
He saves their lives from death and keeps them alive in famine.
We wait for the LORD. He is our help and our shield.
For our hearts rejoice in Him, because we trust in His holy name.
May Your faithful love be upon us, O the LORD, as we wait for You.
I will bless the LORD at all times; His praise will always be on my lips.
My soul will boast in the LORD; let those who are hurting hear and be glad.
Magnify the LORD with me; let us lift up His name together.
I sought the LORD, and He answered me; He rescued me from all my fears.
Those who look to Him are radiant with joy; their faces will never be ashamed.
This poor man cried out, and the LORD heard him; He saved him from all his troubles.
The angel of the LORD sets up camp around those who fear Him, and he rescues them.
Taste and see that the LORD is good; blessed is the person who takes refuge in Him.
Fear the LORD, you His holy people, for those who fear Him lack nothing.
Young lions may grow weak and hungry, but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.
Come, my children, listen to me; I will teach you to fear the LORD.
Who is the man who wants life and loves to see good days?
Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from lying words.
Turn from evil and do good; seek peace and chase after it.
The eyes of the LORD are on the righteous, and His ears are open to their cry.
The face of the LORD is against those who do evil, to remove their memory from the earth.
The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears; He rescues them from all their troubles.
The LORD is close to the brokenhearted; He saves those whose spirits are crushed.
The righteous face many troubles, but the LORD rescues them from all of them.
He guards all their bones; not one of them is broken.
Evil will kill the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be condemned.
The LORD redeems the lives of His servants; no one who takes refuge in Him will be condemned.
The LORD, fight those who fight me; stand against those who attack me.
Take up Your shield and armor, and rise to help me.
Draw out Your spear and stop those who chase me. Say to my soul, ‘I am the One who saves you.’
Let those who want to kill me be ashamed and disgraced. Let those who plan to hurt me turn back in fear.
Let them be like dry husks blown by the wind, while the angel of the LORD drives them away.
Let their road be dark and slippery, while the angel of the LORD chases them.
For no reason, they hid a net for me. For no reason, they dug a pit to trap me.
Let ruin hit them by surprise. Let the net they hid catch them. Let them fall into their own pit and be destroyed.
Then I will be glad in the LORD. I will rejoice in His help.
My whole being will say, “the LORD, who is like You? You save the poor from those too strong for them. You save the poor and needy from those who rob them.”
Lying witnesses stand up and ask me things I do not know.
They pay me back with evil for the good I did, and they crush my spirit.
But when they were sick, I wore sackcloth and went without food to humble myself. I prayed for them, and my prayers came back to me unanswered.
I walked around as if they were my friends or brothers. I bowed down in sorrow as if I were mourning my mother.
But when I stumbled, they were happy and gathered together. Strangers I did not know attacked me. They lied about me without stopping.
Like people who mock others at a party, they ground their teeth at me.
How long, O Lord, will You just watch? Rescue my life from their attacks. Save my one life from these lions.
Then I will thank You in the great gathering. I will praise You among many people.
Do not let my enemies be glad over me for no reason. Do not let those who hate me without cause wink at me in mockery.
They do not speak peace. They plan lies against quiet people in the land.
They open their mouths wide against me and say, “Aha! Aha! Our eyes have seen it!”
You have seen this, the LORD. Do not stay silent. Lord, do not stay far from me.
Wake up and rise to defend my case. My God and my Lord, take up my cause.
Judge me by Your righteousness, the LORD my God. Do not let them be glad over me.
Do not let them say in their hearts, “Aha! We have swallowed him up!” Do not let them say, “We have eaten him alive!”
Let all who are glad when I suffer be ashamed and confused. Let those who brag about me be covered with shame and disgrace.
Let those who support my right cause shout with joy and be glad. Let them always say, “The LORD is great! He is happy with the peace of His servant.”
Then my tongue will talk about Your righteousness and praise You all day long.
For the choir director. A Psalm of David, the servant of the LORD. Deep in my heart I know this about the wicked person: There is no fear of God before his eyes.
He flatters himself and thinks his sin will not be found out or hated.
The words from his mouth are evil and deceitful; he has stopped being wise and doing good.
He plans evil while lying in bed; he chooses a path that is not good; he does not turn away from evil.
Your faithful love, O the LORD, reaches to the heavens; Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.
Your goodness is like the mountains of God; Your judgments are like the deep sea. O the LORD, You keep people and animals safe.
How precious is Your faithful love, O God! People find safety in the shadow of Your wings.
They feast on the plenty in Your house; You give them drink from the river of Your delights.
For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light.
Show Your faithful love to those who know You, and Your goodness to those with honest hearts.
Do not let the proud step on me, and do not let the wicked drive me away.
There the evildoers have fallen; they are thrown down and cannot get up.
Do not worry about evil people, and do not envy those who do wrong.
They will soon fade away, like grass that withers, and like green plants they will die.
Trust in the the LORD and do good. Live in the land and rely on His faithfulness.
Delight in the the LORD, and He will give you what your heart desires.
Give your plans to the the LORD; trust in Him, and He will act.
He will make your goodness shine like the dawn, and your fairness like the noonday sun.
Be quiet before the the LORD and wait patiently for Him. Do not worry about people who get ahead by doing wrong or who carry out evil plans.
Turn away from anger and leave rage behind; do not fret, because it leads only to harm.
For evildoers will be destroyed, but those who hope in the the LORD will receive the land.
In a little while, the wicked will be gone. Even if you look for them, they will not be found.
But humble people will receive the land and enjoy great peace.
The wicked plot against those who do right and grind their teeth in anger.
But the Lord laughs at them, because He sees that their day is coming.
The wicked draw their swords and bend their bows to bring down the poor and needy and to kill those whose ways are upright.
But their swords will pierce their own hearts, and their bows will be broken.
It is better to have a little and do right than to have the wealth of many wicked people.
For the strength of the wicked will be broken, but the the LORD upholds those who do right.
The The LORD knows how long those who live with integrity will live, and the land they receive will last forever.
They will not be disgraced in hard times; in days of famine they will have enough.
But the wicked and the the LORD's enemies will perish. Like the beauty of a field, they will vanish, and like smoke they will disappear.
The wicked borrow and do not repay, but those who do right give generously.
Those the the LORD blesses will receive the land, but those He curses will be destroyed.
The The LORD makes firm the steps of the person who pleases Him.
Though he may stumble, he will not fall, because the the LORD holds him up with His hand.
I was young and now am old, yet I have never seen those who do right abandoned, or their children begging for food.
They are always generous and lend freely, so their children are blessed.
Turn from evil and do good, and you will live in the land forever.
For the the LORD loves justice and will not abandon His faithful ones. They are kept safe forever, but the children of the wicked will be destroyed.
Those who do right will receive the land and live in it forever.
The mouth of those who do right speaks wisdom, and their tongue tells what is right.
God's instruction is in their hearts, and their feet do not slip.
The wicked watch those who do right and seek to kill them.
But the the LORD will not leave them in the wicked person's power or let them be found guilty when they are judged.
Wait for the the LORD and keep His way, and He will lift you up to receive the land; you will see the wicked destroyed.
I have seen a wicked and violent person thriving like a healthy tree in its own soil.
But he passed away and was gone. Though I looked for him, he could not be found.
Notice those who live with integrity and watch those who do right, because the future belongs to people of peace.
But rebels will be destroyed together, and the future of the wicked will be destroyed.
The salvation of those who do right comes from the the LORD; He is their safe place in times of trouble.
The The LORD helps them and delivers them. He rescues them from the wicked and saves them, because they take refuge in Him.
The LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath.
For Your arrows have pierced me, and Your hand has come down on me.
There is no health in my body because of Your wrath; there is no peace in my bones because of my sin.
My guilt has overwhelmed me like a heavy burden too heavy to bear.
My wounds stink and fester because of my foolishness.
I am bent over and brought very low; all day long I go about mourning.
My back is filled with searing pain; there is no health in my body.
I am feeble and utterly crushed; I groan in anguish of heart.
Lord, all my longing is before You; my sighing is not hidden from You.
My heart pounds, my strength fails me; even the light of my eyes is gone from me.
My friends and companions keep their distance from my suffering; my relatives stand far off.
Those who seek my life set traps; those who want my ruin speak of destruction and plan deceit all day long.
I am like a deaf man, who cannot hear, like a mute, who cannot speak.
I have become like one who does not hear, whose mouth can offer no reply.
The LORD, I wait for You; You will answer, Lord my God.
For I said, "May they not rejoice over me—those who gloat when my foot slips."
For I am about to fall, and my pain is ever before me.
I confess my wrongdoing; I am troubled by my sin.
But my enemies are vigorous and strong; many are those who hate me without reason.
Those who repay good with evil oppose me because I follow what is good.
Do not forsake me, the LORD; do not be far from me, my God.
Hurry to help me, Lord, my salvation.
I said, "I will watch how I live so I don't sin with my tongue. I will keep my mouth under control like with a muzzle while wicked people are near me."
I stayed quiet and said nothing, not even good things, but my pain grew worse.
My heart burned inside me. As I thought, the fire grew, and then I spoke.
The LORD, show me when my life will end and how long my days are, so I can know how weak I am.
Look, You made my days only a few hand-widths long, and my whole life is nothing compared to You. Truly, every person, even at their best, is only a breath. Selah.
Surely everyone walks around like a shadow. They worry for nothing. They pile up wealth, but they don't know who will take it.
And now, Lord, what am I waiting for? My hope is in You.
Save me from all my sins; don't make me an insult to foolish people.
I stayed quiet and didn't open my mouth, because You did this.
Take Your punishment away from me; I am dying under Your heavy hand.
When You correct people for sin, You wear away what they treasure, like a moth eats cloth. Surely everyone is only a breath. Selah.
Hear my prayer, the LORD, and listen to my cry; don't ignore my tears. I am a stranger living with You, a visitor like all my ancestors.
Look away from me so I can be cheerful again before I go and am no more.
I waited patiently for the LORD, and He turned to me and heard my cry.
He lifted me out of the pit of ruin and out of the sticky clay. He set my feet on a rock and made my steps steady.
He put a new song in my mouth, a song of praise to our God. Many will see this and fear, and they will trust in the LORD.
How happy is the person who trusts in the LORD and does not turn to proud people or to those who follow lies.
The LORD my God, You have done many wonderful things. You have plans for us, and no one can compare with You. If I tried to tell about them, they would be too many to count.
You did not want sacrifices or offerings. Instead, You opened my ears. You did not ask for burnt offerings or sin offerings.
Then I said, "Here I am. I have come, just as it is written about me in the scroll.
I want to do Your will, my God. Your law is in my heart."
I have told the good news of Your righteousness in the great gathering. I did not keep my lips closed. You know that, O the LORD.
I have not hidden Your righteousness in my heart. I have spoken of Your faithfulness and Your saving help. I have not kept back Your love and Your truth from the great gathering.
The LORD, do not hold back Your mercy from me. Let Your love and Your truth always protect me.
Troubles too many to count surround me. My sins have caught up with me, and I cannot see. They are more than the hairs on my head, and my courage has left me.
Please, the LORD, save me. Hurry, the LORD, and help me.
May those who want to take my life be ashamed and confused. May those who want to hurt me be turned back and disgraced.
May those who say, "Aha, aha!" be stunned by their own shame.
May all who look for You be happy and glad in You. May those who love Your saving help always say, "The LORD be praised!"
But I am poor and needy. Lord, please think of me. You are my help and my rescuer. My God, do not wait.
Blessed is the person who cares for someone in need. The LORD will rescue him in times of trouble.
The LORD protects him and keeps him alive. He blesses him in the land, and He won't hand him over to his enemies.
The LORD supports him on his sickbed and helps him recover from his illness.
I said, "O the LORD, be gracious to me. Heal me, because I have sinned against You."
My enemies say bad things about me: "When will he die and his name be forgotten?"
When someone comes to see me, he says empty things. He stores up trouble in his heart, then goes out and spreads it around.
All who hate me whisper together against me and imagine the worst for me:
"A deadly disease has been poured on him. He will never get up from where he lies."
Even my close friend, the one I trusted, who shared my bread, has turned against me.
But You, O the LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up, so I can repay them.
By this I know You are pleased with me: my enemy does not shout in triumph over me.
Because of my integrity, You hold me up and set me in Your presence forever.
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and Amen.
As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul pants for You, O God.
My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and appear before God?
My tears have been my food day and night, while people say to me all day long, "Where is your God?"
These things I remember as I pour out my soul: how I walked with the crowd, leading the procession to the house of God, with shouts of joy and thanksgiving among the festive crowd.
Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the turmoil within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him for the salvation of His presence.
O my God, my soul is downcast within me; therefore I remember You from the land of Jordan and the peaks of Hermon—even from Mount Mizar.
Deep calls to deep in the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and waves have swept over me.
The LORD will command His loving devotion by day, and His song will be with me by night—a prayer to the God of my life.
I say to God my Rock, "Why have You forgotten me? Why must I go about mourning, oppressed by the enemy?"
My bones ache as my enemies taunt me, saying all day long, "Where is your God?"
Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the turmoil within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God.
Defend me, O God, and fight my case against people who don't honor God. Free me from liars and wrongdoers.
You are the God who makes me strong. Why have you turned away from me? Why must I walk in sadness because my enemy treats me badly?
Send your light and your truth to guide me. Let them bring me to your holy mountain and to your house.
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my greatest joy. I will praise you with a harp, O God, my God.
Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why are you upset within me? Put your hope in God, for I will still praise Him. He is the One who saves me and is my God.
We heard with our own ears, O God. Our fathers told us about the great things You did long ago.
With Your hand You drove out the nations and planted Your people. You crushed other peoples and sent them away.
They did not win the land with their swords, and their own strength did not save them. It was Your right hand, Your arm, and the light of Your face, because You were pleased with them.
You are my King, O God. Command victories for Jacob.
Through You we push back our enemies. In Your name we trample those who rise against us.
I do not trust in my bow, and my sword does not save me.
For You have saved us from our enemies and shamed those who hate us.
In God we boast all day long, and we will praise Your name forever. Selah
Yet You have rejected and humbled us. You no longer go out with our armies.
You made us turn back from the enemy, and those who hate us took our goods.
You gave us up to be eaten like sheep and scattered us among the nations.
You sell Your people for almost nothing, and You gain no profit from the sale.
You make us a shame to our neighbors, a mockery and an insult to those around us.
You make us a warning story among the nations, a thing people shake their heads at among all peoples.
All day long my shame is before me, and shame covers my face.
It comes from the voice of those who taunt and insult, because of the enemy and the one who wants revenge.
All this has happened to us, yet we have not forgotten You or broken Your covenant.
Our hearts have not turned back, and our steps have not left Your path.
Yet You have crushed us in the place of wild dogs and covered us with deep darkness.
If we had forgotten the name of our God or spread out our hands to a foreign god,
would not God have found it out? For He knows the secrets of the heart.
Yet for Your sake we are killed all day long. We are treated like sheep to be slaughtered.
Wake up, O Lord! Why do You sleep? Rise up! Do not reject us forever.
Why do You hide Your face and forget our trouble and our hardship?
Our soul has sunk to the dust, and our bodies cling to the ground.
Rise up and help us! Redeem us because of Your faithful love.
My heart is stirred by a noble theme as I recite my verses to the king; my tongue is the pen of a skillful writer.
You are the most handsome of men, and grace has been poured on your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.
Strap your sword on your side, mighty one; appear in your splendor and majesty.
In your majesty ride out victoriously for the cause of truth, humility, and righteousness; let your right hand show awesome deeds.
Your sharp arrows pierce the hearts of the king's enemies; the nations fall beneath your feet.
Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever; a scepter of justice is the scepter of your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of joy over your companions.
All your garments are fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia; from ivory palaces, harps make you glad.
Daughters of kings are among your honored women; at your right hand stands the queen in gold from Ophir.
Listen, daughter, and pay attention; turn your ear. Forget your people and your father's house.
Then the king will desire your beauty; bow down to him, for he is your Lord.
The people of Tyre will bring a gift; the rich among the people will seek your favor.
All glorious is the princess in her chamber; her clothing is woven with gold.
In embroidered garments she is led to the king; her young companions are brought to you.
They are led with joy and gladness; they enter the palace of the king.
Your sons will take the place of your fathers; you will make them princes throughout the land.
I will make your name remembered in every generation; therefore the nations will praise you forever and ever.
God is our refuge and strength. He is always ready to help when we are in trouble.
So we will not be afraid, even if the earth changes and mountains crash into the sea.
Even if the water roars and foams and the mountains tremble as the seas rise. Selah.
A river with streams that bring joy to God's city, the holy place where the Most High lives.
God is in that city, so it will not be shaken. God will help it at dawn.
Nations are in uproar and kingdoms fall. He speaks, and the earth melts away.
The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah.
Come and see what the LORD has done. See the destruction He has brought on the earth.
He stops wars all over the earth. He breaks bows and shatters spears. He burns chariots in the fire.
"Be still, and know that I am God. I will be honored among the nations. I will be honored all over the earth."
The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah.
Clap your hands, all you nations; shout to God with cries of joy!
For the LORD Most High is awesome; He is the great King over all the earth.
He gave us power over nations and peoples.
He chose our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves. Selah.
God has gone up with a shout of joy, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.
Sing praises to God, sing praises! Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
For God is the King of all the earth; sing praises with understanding.
God rules over the nations; God sits on His holy throne.
The leaders of the nations gather together as the people of the God of Abraham, for the rulers of the earth belong to God; He is highly exalted.
A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. Great is the LORD, and He is greatly praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain.
Beautiful in height, the joy of all the earth—Mount Zion, in the far north, the city of the great King.
God is in her strongholds; He is known as a fortress.
For look, the kings gathered together and passed by as one.
