They saw it and were amazed; fear seized them, and they ran away.
Trembling took hold of them there, like pain for a woman giving birth.
With an east wind You shatter the ships of Tarshish.
Just as we heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts, in the city of our God: God will make it stand forever. Selah.
Within Your temple, O God, we think about Your faithful love.
Like Your name, O God, so Your praise reaches the ends of the earth; Your right hand is full of righteousness.
Mount Zion is glad; the daughters of Judah rejoice because of Your judgments.
Walk around Zion and go all the way around her; count her towers.
Look at her walls and walk through her strong towers, so you can tell the next generation.
For this God is our God forever and ever; He will guide us even to death.
Listen to this, all you nations; pay attention, everyone living in the world.
Both common people and leaders, rich and poor together.
My mouth will speak wisdom, and my heart will think about understanding.
I will turn my ear to a wise saying and explain my riddle with a harp.
Why should I be afraid in hard times, when the wrongs I have done surround me?
They trust in their wealth and brag about how rich they are.
No one can buy back another person's life or pay God the price to save him.
It costs too much to redeem a life; the price can never be enough.
No one can pay enough to live forever and never decay.
Everyone sees that wise people die; fools and ignorant people perish too and leave their wealth to others.
Their graves are their homes forever, their houses for all time, even if they named lands after themselves.
But a person does not keep his glory; he is like an animal that dies.
This is the way of foolish people, and those who come after them agree with what they say.
Like sheep they are headed for the grave; death will be their shepherd. In the morning, good people will rule over them. Their bodies will wear away in the grave, and they will have no home.
But God will buy back my life from the grave, because He will take me to Himself.
Do not be afraid when someone gets rich and his family's honor grows.
When he dies, he takes nothing with him; his honor does not go down with him.
While he lives, he thinks he is blessed, and people praise him when he prospers.
He will join the generation of his ancestors and never see light again.
A person who is honored but does not understand is like an animal that dies.
The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks and calls the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.
Out of Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth.
Our God comes and will not stay silent; a fire devours everything before Him, and a fierce storm surrounds Him.
He calls to the heavens above and to the earth to judge His people:
“Gather My faithful people to Me, those who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.”
The heavens declare His righteousness, because God Himself is the judge. Selah
“Hear, My people, and I will speak; Israel, I will testify against you. I am God, your God.
I am not rebuking you for your sacrifices or your burnt offerings, which are always before Me.
I will not take a bull from your house or goats from your pens.
“For every animal of the forest is Mine, and the cattle on a thousand hills.
I know every bird in the mountains, and the creatures of the field are Mine.
If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and everything in it are Mine.
“Do I eat the meat of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and keep your promises to the Most High.
Call on Me in the day of trouble; I will rescue you, and you will honor Me.”
But to the wicked God says: “What right do you have to recite My laws or take My covenant on your lips?
For you hate discipline, and you throw My words away.
If you see a thief, you are happy to join him, and you keep company with adulterers.
“You use your mouth for evil, and your tongue is full of lies.
You sit and talk against your brother; you slander your own mother’s son.
You did all this, and I said nothing. You thought I was like you. But now I correct you and bring charges against you before your eyes.
“Think about this, you who forget God, or I will tear you apart, and no one will save you.
Whoever offers a sacrifice of thanks honors Me, and I will show God’s salvation to the one who lives right.”
Have mercy on me, O God, according to Your faithful love; according to Your great mercy, wipe away my wrongdoings.
Wash me completely from my guilt, and make me clean from my sin!
I know my wrongdoings, and my sin is always before me.
I sinned against You alone. I did what is evil in Your sight. So You are right when You speak, and You are blameless when You judge.
I was born guilty; I have been sinful since my mother conceived me.
You want truth in my deepest self. You teach me wisdom in my secret heart.
Cleanse me with hyssop, and I will be clean. Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
Let me hear joy and gladness. Let the bones You broke rejoice.
Hide Your face from my sins, and wipe away all my guilt.
Create a clean heart in me, O God, and renew a faithful spirit within me.
Do not throw me away from Your presence, and do not take Your Holy Spirit from me.
Give me back the joy of Your salvation, and support me with a willing spirit.
Then I will teach wrongdoers Your ways, and sinners will turn back to You.
Save me from the guilt of murder, O God, God of my salvation. Then my tongue will sing about Your righteousness.
O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.
You do not want a sacrifice, or I would give it. You are not pleased with a burnt offering.
The sacrifices that please God are a broken spirit; a broken and humble heart, O God, You will not reject.
Do good to Zion because it pleases You. Build up Jerusalem's walls.
Then You will be pleased with proper sacrifices, in burnt offerings and whole burnt offerings. Then bulls will be offered on Your altar.
Why do you brag about evil, mighty man? God's faithful love lasts all day.
Your tongue plans ruin. It is like a sharp razor that tricks people.
You love evil instead of good, and lies instead of truth. Selah.
You love every word that destroys, O lying tongue.
But God will break you down forever. He will snatch you up and tear you from your tent. He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah.
Righteous people will see this and be afraid. They will laugh at him.
Look! This man did not make God his safe place. Instead, he trusted in his great wealth and grew strong in his evil.
But I am like a healthy olive tree in God's house. I trust in God's faithful love forever and ever.
I will praise You forever, because You did this. I will put my hope in Your name, for it is good, among Your faithful people.
The foolish person says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt, and they do evil things. No one does what is good.
God looks down from heaven at the people on earth. He wants to see if anyone understands or seeks God.
All of them have turned away. Together they have become corrupt. No one does what is good, not even one person.
Will those who do wrong never learn? They eat up my people like bread, and they do not call on God.
There they are, terrified, even though there was no reason to be afraid. God scattered the bones of your enemies. You put them to shame, because God rejected them.
If only salvation for Israel would come from Zion! When God brings back His captive people, Jacob will rejoice, and Israel will be glad.
Save me, O God, by your name; show I am right by your power.
Hear my prayer, O God; listen to the words of my mouth.
Strangers have risen against me, and cruel men are trying to kill me. They do not care about God.
Surely God is my helper; the Lord keeps me alive.
Let evil turn back on those who attack me; destroy them by your faithfulness.
I will freely sacrifice to you; I will praise your name, O the LORD, because it is good.
For He has rescued me from every trouble, and I have seen my enemies defeated.
Listen to my prayer, God, and do not hide from my plea for mercy.
Pay attention to me and answer me. I am upset by my thoughts, and I am troubled.
I am troubled by my enemy's voice and by the pressure from wicked people, because they bring trouble on me and hate me in anger.
My heart is in pain inside me, and the fear of death falls on me.
Fear and shaking come over me, and horror covers me.
I said, "If only I had wings like a dove, I would fly away and rest.
Look, I would go far away and stay in the desert. Selah
I would hurry to a safe place away from the wild wind and storm."
Lord, confuse their speech, for I see violence and arguing in the city.
Day and night they walk around on its walls, and trouble and sorrow are inside it.
Ruin is in the middle of it. Oppression and lies do not leave its streets.
It is not an enemy who insults me, or I could bear it. It is not someone who hates me who has turned against me, or I could hide from him.
But it is you, a man like me, my companion and close friend.
We used to share friendly advice, and we walked together in God's house with the crowd.
Let death surprise them. Let them go down alive to the grave, because evil is in their homes and among them.
But I will call on God, and the LORD will save me.
Morning, noon, and evening I complain and groan, and He hears my voice.
He rescues my life in peace from the battle against me, because many stand with me.
God will hear and humble them, the One who has ruled from long ago. Selah Because they do not change and do not fear God.
He has reached out against his friends and broken his promise.
His words were smooth as butter, but war was in his heart. His words were softer than oil, but they were like drawn swords.
Give your worries to the LORD, and He will take care of you. He will never let those who do right be shaken.
But You, O God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction. Violent and dishonest men will not live out half their days. But I will trust in You.
Be gracious to me, O God, because people are hunting me down. All day long they fight and crush me.
My enemies trample me all day; many proudly fight against me.
When I am afraid, I will trust in You.
In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are against me for evil.
They conspire and lurk; they watch my steps, waiting to take my life.
Will they escape because of their sin? In Your anger, O God, bring down the nations.
You have counted my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle. Are they not in Your book?
Then my enemies will retreat on the day I call. This I know: God is for me.
In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,
in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
Your vows are upon me, O God; I will bring You thank offerings.
For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life.
Be merciful to me, O God, be merciful to me, for my soul takes refuge in You. In the shadow of Your wings I will take refuge until the danger passes.
I cry out to God Most High, to God who does what He has planned for me.
He will send help from heaven and save me. He will rebuke the one who tramples me. Selah God will send His faithful love and truth.
My soul is among lions. I lie down among beasts that tear apart—people whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.
Be lifted up, O God, above the heavens. Let Your glory be over all the earth.
They set a net for my steps. My soul was bowed down. They dug a pit in front of me, but they fell into it themselves. Selah
My heart is firm, O God; my heart is firm. I will sing and make music.
Wake up, my glory! Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
I will praise You, O Lord, among the nations. I will sing Your praises among the peoples.
For Your faithful love is great to the heavens, and Your truth reaches to the skies.
Be lifted up, O God, above the heavens. Let Your glory be over all the earth.
Do you really speak fairly, you powerful ones? Do you judge people fairly, you people?
No, in your hearts you plan evil, and your hands spread violence across the land.
Wicked people are crooked from birth; liars wander off track from the womb.
Their poison is like a snake's poison, like a deaf cobra that plugs its ears.
It will not listen to the snake charmer, no matter how skilled the enchanter is.
O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O the LORD, tear out the fangs of the young lions.
Let them disappear like water that runs away; when they shoot their arrows, let them lose their power.
Like a slug that melts as it crawls, like a baby born dead, may they never live to see the light of day.
Before your cooking pots can feel the heat of thorn bushes—green or dry—He will sweep them away.
Good people will be glad when they see justice done; they will celebrate victory over the wicked.
Then people will say, “Surely good people receive a reward; surely God judges the earth.”
Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; lift me above those who rise against me.
Rescue me from those who do evil, and save me from bloodthirsty men.
Look, they lie in wait for my life; strong men gather against me, though I have not sinned or done wrong, O the LORD.
They rush to attack me even though I am innocent. Wake up, come to help me, and see.
You, the LORD God of Hosts, God of Israel, wake up to punish all the nations. Do not show mercy to any who are treacherous and do evil. Selah
They return at evening, growling like dogs, and prowl around the city.
Look, they pour out threats with their mouths; their words cut like swords, for they say, “Who will hear us?”
But You, the LORD, laugh at them; You mock all the nations.
O my Strength, I watch for You, for God is my fortress.
My God in His faithful love will go before me; God will let me look on my enemies in triumph.
Do not kill them, or my people may forget. Scatter them by Your power and bring them down, O Lord, our shield.
Let the sin of their mouths and the words of their lips trap them in their pride, for they speak curses and lies.
Consume them in wrath, consume them until they are gone, so that people to the ends of the earth may know that God rules over Jacob. Selah
They return at evening, growling like dogs, and prowl around the city.
They wander about for food and growl if they are not satisfied.
But I will sing of Your strength; in the morning I will sing of Your faithful love, because You have been my fortress and my refuge in my time of trouble.
O my Strength, I will sing praises to You, for God is my fortress, my God of faithful love.
You have rejected us, God. You broke through our defenses, and You were angry. Restore us!
You shook the land and tore it open. Heal its cracks, for it is quaking.
You made Your people suffer. You made us drink wine that makes us stagger.
You raised a flag for those who fear You, so they can run to it and escape the arrows.
Save us with Your right hand. Answer us, so those You love may be rescued.
God has spoken from His holy place: "I will triumph. I will divide Shechem and measure the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine. Ephraim is My helmet, and Judah is My scepter.
Moab is My washbasin. I will throw My sandal on Edom, and I will shout in triumph over Philistia."
Who will bring me to the strong city? Who will lead me to Edom?
Haven't You rejected us, God? Won't You march out with our armies?
Give us help against the foe, for help from people is worthless.
With God we will fight bravely, and He will trample our enemies.
Hear my cry, God; listen to my prayer.
From far away I call to You when I feel weak. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I am.
For You have been my refuge, a strong tower against the enemy.
I will dwell in Your tent forever; I will take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah
For You, God, have heard my vows; You have given me the inheritance of those who honor Your name.
Add days to the king’s life; may his years last through many generations.
May he rule in God’s presence forever; let Your faithful love and truth protect him.
Then I will always sing praise to Your name, keeping my vows day by day.
For the director of music. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David. I wait quietly for God; my salvation comes from Him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress, so I will not be shaken.
How long will you keep attacking one man? Will all of you try to knock him down—like a leaning wall or a shaky fence?
They only plan to push him out of his high place. They enjoy lies. With their mouths they bless, but in their hearts they curse. Selah
Wait quietly for God alone, my soul, because my hope comes from Him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress, so I will not be shaken.
My rescue and my honor depend on God. He is my mighty rock, my safe place.
Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts to Him, for God is our safe place. Selah
Ordinary people are only a breath, and important people are a lie. Put together on a scale, they are lighter than a breath.
Do not trust in money taken by force, and do not hope in stolen goods. Even if your wealth grows, do not set your heart on it.
God has said one thing, and I have heard two: You, O God, are strong,
and You, O Lord, are loving. You will pay back each person for what he has done.
God, You are my God; I seek You eagerly. My soul thirsts for You; my body longs for You in a dry, weary land with no water.
I have seen You in the holy place, to see Your power and Your glory.
Because Your faithful love is better than life, my lips will praise You.
So I will bless You as long as I live; in Your name I will lift my hands.
My soul will be satisfied as with the richest food; with joyful lips my mouth will praise You.
When I remember You on my bed, I think about You through the night watches.
Because You have been my help, I will sing for joy in the shadow of Your wings.
My soul clings to You; Your right hand holds me up.
But those who want to kill me will go down into the depths of the earth.
They will be handed over to the sword; they will become food for jackals.
The king will rejoice in God; all who swear by Him will boast, for the mouths of liars will be silenced.
Hear my voice, O God, when I complain; protect my life from the enemy's terror.
Hide me from the secret plans of the wicked and from the noisy crowd of evildoers.
They sharpen their tongues like swords and aim bitter words like arrows.
From hiding they shoot at the innocent; they shoot suddenly and without fear.
They hold firmly to their evil plan and talk about hiding traps. They ask, "Who will see us?"
They search for ways to do wrong and say, "We have made a perfect secret plan." A person's inner thoughts and heart are deep.
But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded.
Their own tongues will turn against them, and everyone who sees them will shake his head.
Then everyone will fear and tell about what God has done; they will think about His work.
Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him. Let all who are upright in heart celebrate.
For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A Song. Praise waits for You, O God, in Zion, and to You our vows will be fulfilled.
You who hear prayer, all people will come to You.
When my sins overpower me, You forgive our wrongs.
Blessed is the one You choose and bring near to live in Your courts! We are filled with the good things in Your house, Your holy temple.
You answer us with awesome acts of justice, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas.
You formed the mountains by Your power; You are armed with strength.
You calm the roar of the seas, the roar of their waves, and the uproar of the nations.
Those who live at the ends of the earth fear Your signs. You make the dawn and sunset shout for joy.
You visit the earth and water it; You make it very rich. The river of God is full of water. You provide grain, for so You have prepared it.
You water its rows abundantly; You settle its ridges. You soften it with showers and bless its growth.
You crown the year with Your bounty, and Your paths overflow with plenty.
The pastures of the wilderness overflow; the hills are clothed with joy.
The meadows are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are covered with grain. They shout for joy; yes, they sing.
Shout for joy to God, all the earth!
Sing about the glory of His name; make His praise glorious.
Say to God, "How awesome are Your deeds! So great is Your power that Your enemies cringe before You.
All the earth bows down to You and sings praise to You; they sing praises to Your name." Selah
Come and see what God has done. His works for people are amazing!
He turned the sea into dry land, and they crossed the river on foot. Come, let us rejoice in Him.
He rules forever by His power. His eyes watch the nations. Do not let rebels rise up against Him. Selah
Praise our God, all you peoples; let the sound of His praise be heard.
He has kept us alive and has not let our feet slip.
For You, God, have tested us and refined us like silver.
You brought us into a trap and laid heavy burdens on our backs.
You let people walk all over us. We went through fire and water, but You brought us out to a place of abundance.
I will come to Your temple with burnt offerings and fulfill my vows to You—
vows my lips promised and my mouth spoke when I was in trouble.
I will sacrifice fat animals as burnt offerings, with the smoke of rams. I will offer bulls and goats. Selah
Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell you what He has done for me.
I cried out to Him with my mouth, and praise was on my tongue.
If I had held on to sin in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
But God has surely listened; He has heard my prayer.
Praise be to God, who has not rejected my prayer or withheld His love from me!
May God be gracious to us and bless us, and show us His favor. Selah.
May Your way be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples praise You, God; let all the peoples praise You.
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples fairly and guide the nations of the earth. Selah.
Let the peoples praise You, God; let all the peoples praise You.
The land has given its harvest; God, our God, blesses us.
God blesses us, so that all the ends of the earth may fear Him.
For the director of music. A psalm of David. A song. God rises up. His enemies scatter, and those who hate Him run away from Him.
As smoke is blown away, You blow them away. As wax melts before a fire, so the wicked perish before God.
But those who do right will be glad. They will rejoice before God and celebrate with joy.
Sing to God, sing praises to His name. Praise Him who rides on the clouds. His name is the LORD, and rejoice before Him.
God is a father to the fatherless and a defender of widows. He lives in His holy home.
God gives a home to those who are alone. He leads prisoners to freedom, but rebels live in a dry land.
God, when You went out ahead of Your people, when You marched through the desert. Selah.
The earth shook, and rain poured from the sky before God, the God of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
You sent plenty of rain, O God; You refreshed Your tired land.
Your people settled there. In Your goodness, O God, You provided for the poor.
The LORD gives the command, and a large group of women spread the news.
Kings and armies run away quickly. Even the woman who stays home shares the plunder.
Even if you rest among the sheep pens, you will be like a dove's wings covered with silver, with shining gold feathers.
When the Almighty scattered kings, it was like snow falling on Mount Zalmon.
God's mountain is like Mount Bashan, a mountain with many peaks.
Why do you look with envy, you mountains with many peaks? This is the mountain God chose for His home. The LORD will live there forever.
God's chariots number in the tens of thousands—thousands upon thousands. The Lord is among them in His holy place, just as He was at Sinai.
You went up to the high place. You took captives with You. You received gifts from people, even from rebels, so that the LORD God may live there.
Blessed be the Lord, who carries our loads every day—the God who saves us. Selah.
Our God is a God who saves; the Lord—the LORD—gives us a way out of death.
Surely God will crush the heads of His enemies, the hairy scalps of those who keep sinning.
The Lord said, "I will bring them back from Bashan; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
so your feet can wade in their blood, and your dogs can lick their share from the enemy."
People see Your procession, O God, the procession of my God and King into the holy place.
Singers lead the way, musicians follow, and young women play tambourines in the middle.
Bless God among the great gathering. Bless the LORD, you who come from Israel's fountain.
There is Benjamin, the youngest, leading them; the princes of Judah in their group; the princes of Zebulun and Naphtali.
Use Your power, O God; show Your strength, O God, which You have worked for us.
Because of Your temple in Jerusalem, kings will bring gifts to You.
Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls among the calves of the peoples, until they trample those who want silver. Scatter the peoples who love war.
Messengers will come from Egypt. Cush will stretch out her hands to God.
Sing to God, kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord—Selah.
To Him who rides across the ancient heavens. Listen—He speaks with a mighty voice.
Give power to God; His majesty is over Israel, and His power is in the skies.
God, You are awesome in Your holy place; the God of Israel gives power and strength to His people. Blessed be God!
Save me, God, because the water has risen to my neck.
I sink in deep mud where there is no footing. I have gone into deep water, and the flood sweeps over me.
I am tired from crying out; my throat is dry. My eyes grow weak as I look for my God.
Those who hate me for no reason are more than the hairs on my head. Many enemies attack me with lies, and they force me to pay back what I did not steal.
You know my foolishness, God, and my guilt is not hidden from You.
May those who hope in You, O Lord, the LORD of Hosts, not be put to shame because of me. May those who seek You, God of Israel, not be disgraced because of me.
I have carried shame for Your sake, and shame has covered my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother's sons.
Zeal for Your house has eaten me up, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me.
When I cried and fasted, they laughed at me.
When I wore sackcloth, I became a joke to them.
People sitting at the gate mock me, and drunkards sing about me.
But my prayer is to You, O the LORD, at a time You choose to show favor. In Your great faithful love, God, answer me with the truth of Your saving help.
Save me from the mud; do not let me sink. Rescue me from my enemies and from the deep water.
Do not let the flood sweep me away, or the deep water swallow me. Do not let the pit close its mouth over me.
Answer me, O the LORD, because Your faithful love is good. Turn to me because of Your great mercy.
Do not hide Your face from Your servant. Answer me quickly, because I am in trouble.
Come close to my soul and redeem it. Buy me back because of my enemies.
You know my shame and disgrace; all my enemies are before You.
Shame has broken my heart, and I am worn out. I looked for pity, but found none. I looked for comfort, but found no one.
They gave me bitter food and vinegar to drink when I was thirsty.
May their table become a trap, a snare for their friends.
May their eyes grow dark so they cannot see, and may their backs always shake.
Pour out Your anger on them, and let Your burning wrath catch up with them.
May their camp be empty, with no one living in their tents.
They chase the ones You have struck, and they talk about the pain of those You have wounded.
Add their sin to their sin, and do not let them share in Your goodness.
May they be erased from the book of life and not be written with those who do right.
I am poor and in pain. May Your saving help, God, keep me safe.
I will praise God's name with a song and honor Him with thanks.
That will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves.
The humble will see it and be glad. You who seek God, let your hearts live.
For the LORD hears those in need and does not look down on His prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise Him, and the seas and everything that moves in them.
For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah, so people can live there and own it.
The children of His servants will receive it, and those who love His name will live there.
Hurry, God, to save me! Come quickly, the LORD, to help me.
May those who seek my life be ashamed and confused. May those who want to harm me be turned back in disgrace.
May those who say, "Aha! Aha!" turn back in shame.
But may all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You. May those who love Your salvation always say, "Let God be praised!"
But I am poor and needy; hurry to me, God. You are my help and my rescuer; the LORD, do not delay.
In You, the LORD, I have taken refuge. Let me never be put to shame.
Rescue me and save me by Your righteousness. Turn Your ear to me and save me.
Be my safe rock, a place I can always go. You have ordered my rescue, because You are my rock and my fortress.
Save me, my God, from wicked people, from those who are unfair and cruel.
You are my hope, Lord, the LORD, my confidence since I was young.
I have leaned on You since birth. You brought me out of my mother's womb. I will always praise You.
I have become like a sign to many people, but You are my strong safe place.
My mouth is full of praise for You, and I talk about Your greatness all day long.
Do not throw me away when I am old. Do not leave me when my strength is gone.
My enemies speak against me. Those who want to kill me plan together.
They say, "God has abandoned him. Chase him and catch him, because no one will save him."
Do not stay far from me, my God. Hurry, my God, to help me.
Let those who accuse me be ashamed and come to nothing. Let those who want to hurt me be covered with shame and disgrace.
But I will always hope and praise You more and more.
My mouth will tell of Your righteousness and Your saving help all day long, even though I cannot count them all.
I will come in the strength of the Lord, the LORD, and talk about Your righteousness. Yours alone.
God, You have taught me since I was young, and to this day I tell about Your wonderful works.
Even when I am old and gray, do not leave me, my God, until I tell Your power to the next generation and Your strength to everyone who is coming.
Your righteousness reaches up to the heavens, God. You have done great things. Who is like You, God?
You have shown me many troubles and hard times, but You will bring me back to life. From the deepest parts of the earth You will raise me up again.
You will make me more honored and comfort me again.
I will praise You with the harp for Your faithfulness, my God. I will sing praise to You with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
My lips will shout for joy when I sing praise to You, along with my soul, which You have saved.
My tongue will tell of Your righteousness all day long, because those who wanted to hurt me have been put to shame and confusion.
Give your justice to the king, O God, and your righteousness to the king's son.
He will judge your people with righteousness, and your poor with justice.
The mountains will bring peace to the people, and the hills will bring fairness.
He will defend the poor of the people, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.
People will respect you as long as the sun shines, and as long as the moon lasts, through every generation.
He will be like rain falling on a newly mowed field, like showers that water the earth.
In his days good people will thrive, and peace will be plentiful until the moon is no more.
He will rule from sea to sea, from the river to the ends of the earth.
Desert tribes will bow before him, and his enemies will be defeated.
The kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands will bring tribute; the kings of Sheba and Seba will bring gifts.
All kings will bow down to him, and all nations will serve him.
For he will rescue the needy who cry out, and the poor who have no helper.
He will have pity on the poor and needy; he will save the lives of the needy.
He will redeem their lives from oppression and violence, and their lives will be precious to him.
Long may he live! May gold from Sheba be given to him. May people pray for him always; may they bless him all day long.
May the land produce plenty of grain, waving even on the mountain tops. May its harvest be as rich as Lebanon's; may people in the cities grow like grass in a field.
May his name last forever; may his fame continue as long as the sun. May all nations be blessed through him; may they call him blessed.
Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
Blessed be His glorious name forever; may all the earth be filled with His glory. Amen and Amen.
This ends the prayers of David son of Jesse.
Surely God is good to Israel, to those with pure hearts.
But as for me, my feet almost slipped; my steps nearly gave way.
For I envied the proud when I saw how well the wicked were doing.
They have no pain when they die; their bodies are well fed.
They don't suffer like other people, and they aren't troubled like everyone else.
So pride is their necklace, and violence covers them like a robe.
Their wealth leads them to sin, and their minds overflow with wild plans.
They mock others and speak evil; from their high place they threaten people.
They set their mouths against heaven, and their tongues strut through the earth.
So their people turn to them and drink in their words.
They say, "How can God know? Does the Most High really understand?"
Look, these are the wicked—always at ease, they grow richer and richer.
Surely I kept my heart pure for nothing; I washed my hands in innocence for no reason.
I am troubled all day long, and every morning brings new punishment.
If I had said, "I will talk like that," I would have betrayed your children.
When I tried to understand all this, it was too hard for me.
Then I went into God's holy place, and I understood what would happen to them in the end.
Surely You set them on slippery ground; You send them sliding down to ruin.
How suddenly they are destroyed, completely swept away by terror!
Like a dream when someone wakes up, so when You wake up, O Lord, You will despise their form.
When my heart was bitter and I felt pain deep inside,
I was stupid and didn't understand; I was like a wild animal before You.
Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand.
You guide me with Your advice, and afterward You will bring me into glory.
Whom do I have in heaven but You? And on earth I want no one but You.
My body and heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my share forever.
Those far from You will die; You destroy everyone who is unfaithful to You.
But as for me, it is good to be close to God. I have made the Lord, the LORD, my refuge, so I can tell about all Your works.
Why have You rejected us forever, O God? Why does Your anger burn against the sheep of Your pasture?
Remember Your people, whom You bought long ago and redeemed to be the tribe You own—Mount Zion, where You dwell.
Turn Your steps toward the ruins that last forever; the enemy has destroyed everything in Your sanctuary.
Your enemies shouted in Your meeting place and planted their flags as signs of victory.
They acted like men swinging axes in a forest.
They smashed all the carved wood with hatchets and axes.
They burned Your holy place to the ground and dishonored the place where Your name lives.
They said to themselves, “Let’s wipe them out completely!” They burned every place where God’s people met in the land.
We do not see our signs; there is no longer any prophet, and none of us knows how long this will last.
How long, God, will the enemy mock us? Will our foe insult Your name forever?
Why do You pull back Your hand, even Your right hand? Take it out of Your cloak and destroy them!
But God has been my King since long ago, bringing salvation on the earth.
You divided the sea by Your strength and crushed the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.
You crushed the heads of Leviathan and fed him to the wild animals of the desert.
You broke open the springs and streams, and You dried up the rivers that never stop.
The day is Yours, and so is the night; You set the sun and moon in place.
You fixed all the borders of the earth and made summer and winter.
Remember that the enemy has mocked the LORD, and that a foolish people has reviled Your name.
Do not hand over the life of Your dove to wild animals; do not forget the lives of Your suffering people forever.
Look at Your covenant, for the dark places of the earth are full of violence.
Do not let the oppressed go away in shame; may the poor and needy praise Your name.
Rise up, God, and defend Your cause; remember how the foolish insult You all day long.
Do not forget the noise of Your enemies, the uproar of those who rise against You that never stops.
We give thanks to you, O God; we give thanks, for Your presence is near. People tell of Your wonderful works.
“At the time I choose, I will judge fairly.
“When the earth shakes and all who live on it, I hold its pillars steady. Selah
“I say to those who brag, ‘Do not brag,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up your horn.
“Do not lift up your horn on high, or speak arrogantly.’”
Honor does not come from the east or the west, or from the desert.
It is God who judges: He brings one down and lifts another up.
For in the hand of the LORD is a cup full of foaming wine, mixed with spices, and He pours it out. All the wicked people of the earth will drink it to the last drop.
But I will tell of this forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
I will cut off all the power of the wicked, but the power of those who do right will be raised up.
For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm of Asaph. A Song. God is known in Judah; His name is great in Israel.
His tent is in Salem, His dwelling place in Zion.
There He broke the flaming arrows, the shield and sword and weapons of war. Selah
You are radiant with light, more majestic than mountains full of prey.
The valiant lie plundered; they sleep their last sleep; none of the warriors can lift a hand.
At Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, both horse and chariot lie still.
You alone are to be feared. Who can stand before You when You are angry?
From heaven You pronounced judgment, and the earth feared and was still
when God rose up to judge, to save all the afflicted of the earth. Selah
Surely human anger brings You praise; You keep the rest of it under control.
Make and fulfill your vows to the LORD your God; let all who surround Him bring tribute to the Awesome One.
He breaks the spirit of princes; He is feared by the kings of the earth.
For the director of music, according to Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph. I cried out to God for help; I cried out to God, and He listened to me.
In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord; at night my hands stayed stretched out and did not grow tired, but my soul refused to be comforted.
I remembered God and groaned; I thought about Him, and my spirit grew faint. Selah
You kept my eyes open; I was too troubled to speak.
I thought about the days of old, the years long ago.
At night I remembered my song; I thought deeply in my heart, and my spirit searched.
Will the Lord reject forever? Will He never show favor again?
Has His faithful love ended forever? Has His promise failed for all generations?
Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has He in anger withheld His compassion? Selah
Then I said, "This is my grief, that the right hand of the Most High has changed."
I will remember the works of the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders from long ago.
I will meditate on all Your works and think about Your mighty deeds.
Your way, O God, is holy. What god is as great as our God?
You are the God who works wonders; You have made known Your strength among the peoples.
With Your arm You redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and trembled; the depths also shook.
The clouds poured out water; the skies thundered; Your arrows flew back and forth.
The sound of Your thunder was in the whirlwind; Your lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and quaked.
Your way was in the sea, and Your path in the mighty waters, but Your footprints were not known.
You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
Listen, my people, to my teaching. Turn your ears to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth and tell a story. I will share old, hidden truths.
We have heard them and known them, and our fathers told them to us.
We won't hide them from their children. We'll tell the next generation the praises of the LORD, and His power and the wonders He has done.
He made a covenant in Jacob and gave His law in Israel. He commanded our fathers to teach it to their children.
Then the next generation would know it, even children not yet born. They would grow up and tell their own children.
Then they could trust in God and not forget His works, but keep His commands.
They wouldn't be like their stubborn and rebellious fathers, whose hearts weren't steady and whose spirits weren't faithful to God.
The people of Ephraim had bows, but they turned back on the day of battle.
They didn't keep God's covenant, and they refused to walk in His law.
They forgot His works and the wonders He had shown them.
He did wonders for their fathers in Egypt, in the area of Zoan.
He split the sea and led them through it. He made the water stand like a wall.
He led them with a cloud by day and with a light of fire all night.
He split rocks in the desert and gave them water as deep as the ocean.
He brought streams from the rock and made water flow like rivers.
But they kept sinning against Him. They rebelled against the Most High in the desert.
They tested God in their hearts by demanding food they wanted.
They spoke against God and said, "Can God give us food in the desert?
He struck the rock, and water poured out, and streams flowed. Can He also give bread? Can He provide meat for His people?"
So the LORD heard and was very angry. Fire broke out against Jacob, and His anger rose against Israel.
That was because they didn't believe in God or trust His power to save.
Yet He commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of heaven.
He rained manna down for them to eat. He gave them grain from heaven.
They ate heavenly food, and He gave them plenty.
He made the east wind blow in the sky and drove the south wind by His power.
He rained meat on them like dust, and birds like sand on the shore.
He made them fall in the middle of their camp, all around their tents.
They ate and were full, because He gave them what they wanted.
But before they were satisfied, while the food was still in their mouths,
God's anger rose against them. He killed their strongest men and struck down Israel's young men.
Even after all this, they kept sinning. Even after His wonders, they didn't believe.
So He ended their days in emptiness and their years in sudden fear.
When He killed them, they looked for Him. They turned back and searched for God.
They remembered that God was their Rock and that God Most High was their Redeemer.
But they only flattered Him with their mouths and lied to Him with their tongues.
Their hearts weren't faithful to Him, and they weren't true to His covenant.
Still, He was kind. He forgave their sin and didn't destroy them. He often held back His anger and didn't pour out all His wrath.
He remembered that they were only flesh, like a breeze that passes and doesn't come back.
How often they rebelled against Him in the desert and made Him sad in the wasteland!
Again and again they tested God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
They didn't remember His power, the day He saved them from their enemies.
He did signs in Egypt and wonders in the area of Zoan.
He turned their rivers to blood, so they couldn't drink from their streams.
He sent swarms of flies that ate them up, and frogs that ruined them.
He gave their crops to grasshoppers and the fruit of their work to locusts.
He destroyed their grapevines with hail and their fig trees with ice.
He handed their cattle over to hail and their livestock to lightning.
He sent His fierce anger against them—wrath, rage, and trouble—through a band of destroying angels.
He made a path for His anger. He didn't spare them from death but gave their lives to the plague.
He struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, the first children born in the land of Ham.
But He led His people like sheep and guided them like a flock in the desert.
He led them safely, so they weren't afraid, while the sea covered their enemies.
He brought them to His holy land, to the mountain His right hand had won.
He drove out nations before them and gave them their land by lot. He settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
But they tested and rebelled against God Most High. They didn't keep His rules.
They turned back and were unfaithful, like their fathers. They were as unreliable as a bow that doesn't shoot straight.
They made Him angry with their hilltop altars and provoked Him with their idols.
God heard and was furious. He completely rejected Israel.
He abandoned the tent at Shiloh, the place He had set up among people.
He let His strength be taken captive and His glory fall into enemy hands.
He gave His people to the sword and poured out His anger on His own land.
Fire burned up their young men, and their young women didn't get married.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows couldn't even weep.
Then the LORD woke up, as if from sleep, like a strong warrior full of courage.
He beat back His enemies and put them to lasting shame.
He rejected Joseph's tent and didn't choose Ephraim's tribe.
Instead, He chose Judah's tribe and Mount Zion, which He loved.
He built His holy place high like the heavens and firm like the earth He made to last forever.
He chose David, His servant, and took him from the sheep pens.
He brought him from caring for sheep to shepherd His people, Jacob, and Israel, His inheritance.
David led them with an honest heart and guided them with skillful hands.
O God, the nations have invaded Your inheritance; they have defiled Your holy temple and turned Jerusalem into ruins.
They have given the dead bodies of Your servants as food to the birds of the sky, and the flesh of Your faithful ones to the beasts of the earth.
They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury them.
We have become a shame to our neighbors, a mocking and laughingstock to those around us.
How long, O the LORD, will You be angry forever? How long will Your jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not know You, and on the kingdoms that do not call on Your name.
For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place.
Do not remember against us the sins of the past; let Your compassion come quickly to meet us, for we are brought very low.
Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Your name; deliver us and forgive our sins for Your name's sake.
Why should the nations say, "Where is their God?" Let it be known among the nations, before our eyes, that You avenge the shed blood of Your servants.
Let the groaning of the prisoner come before You; by the greatness of Your arm, preserve those condemned to die.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their laps for the reproach they have hurled at You, O Lord.
Then we, Your people, the sheep of Your pasture, will give thanks to You forever; from generation to generation we will declare Your praise.
Listen to us, Shepherd of Israel. You lead Joseph like a flock. You sit enthroned between the cherubim. Show Yourself to us.
Rally Your power before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, and come save us.
Restore us, O God. Make Your face shine on us, so we may be saved.
O the LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger burn against the prayers of Your people?
You have fed them tears for bread. You have made them drink tears in large amounts.
You have made us a joke to our neighbors. Our enemies laugh at us.
Restore us, O God of Hosts. Make Your face shine on us, so we may be saved.
You brought a vine out of Egypt. You drove out the nations and planted it.
You cleared the ground for it. It took root and filled the land.
The mountains were covered by its shade. The tall cedars were covered by its branches.
It sent its branches to the Sea, and its new shoots to the River.
Why have You broken down its walls? Now everyone who passes by picks its fruit.
The wild boar from the forest tears it apart. The animals of the field feed on it.
Return, O God of Hosts! Look down from heaven and see. Take care of this vine,
the root Your right hand planted, the son You raised up for Yourself.
It is burned with fire and cut down. They die at Your angry look.
Let Your hand rest on the man at Your right hand, the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.
Then we will not turn away from You. Give us life, and we will call on Your name.
Restore us, O the LORD God of Hosts. Make Your face shine on us, so we may be saved.
For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing for joy to God our strength; shout aloud to the God of Jacob.
Lift up a song and beat the tambourine, the pleasant harp and lyre.
Sound the ram’s horn at the new moon, and at the full moon on the day of our feast.
For this is a law for Israel, a ruling from the God of Jacob.
He set this as a testimony for Joseph when he went out over the land of Egypt, where I heard a language I did not know.
“I took his shoulder off the burden; his hands were freed from the basket.
In your distress you called, and I rescued you; I answered you from the thundercloud; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah
“Hear, O My people, and I will testify against you, O Israel, if you would only listen to Me!
There must be no foreign god among you; you must not bow down to a foreign god.
I am the the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it.
“But My people did not listen to My voice; Israel refused to obey Me.
So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own plans.
“If only My people would listen to Me, if only Israel would walk in My ways,
I would quickly subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes.
Those who hate the the LORD would pretend to obey Him, and their doom would last forever.
But I would feed you with the finest wheat; with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”
God stands among the heavenly council; He judges among the gods.
How long will you judge unfairly and favor the wicked? Selah.
Defend the poor and orphan; give fair judgment to the afflicted and needy.
Rescue the weak and needy; save them from the hand of the wicked.
They do not know or understand; they walk in darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
I said, "You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High."
But you will die like mortals and fall like one of the princes.
Arise, O God, judge the earth, for You will inherit all the nations.
A song. A psalm of Asaph. God, do not stay silent. Do not be quiet, and do not be still, O God.
See, Your enemies make an uproar, and those who hate You lift their heads in pride.
They plot secretly against Your people and make plans against those You protect.
They say, "Come, let us destroy them as a nation, so that Israel's name is forgotten forever."
Yes, they are united in purpose. They make an alliance against You:
the people of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia with the people of Tyre.
Even Assyria has joined them; they have become a powerful ally for the descendants of Lot. Selah.
Treat them as You treated Midian, Sisera, and Jabin at the Kishon River.
They were destroyed at Endor and became like dung on the ground.
Make their leaders like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their rulers like Zebah and Zalmunna.
They said, "Let us take God's lands for ourselves."
Make them like tumbleweed, my God, like chaff blown by the wind.
Like fire burning through a forest, like flames setting mountains ablaze.
Chase them with Your storm and terrify them with Your windstorm.
Fill their faces with shame so that they will seek Your name, O the LORD.
Let them be ashamed and terrified forever; let them be disgraced and destroyed.
Let them know that You alone, whose name is the LORD, are the Most High over all the earth.
For the music director. According to Gittith. A psalm of the sons of Korah. How lovely are Your dwelling places, the LORD of Hosts!
My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.
Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young—near Your altars, the LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
Blessed are those who dwell in Your house; they are always praising You. Selah
Blessed are those whose strength is in You, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.
As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; the autumn rains also cover it with blessings.
They go from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion.
The LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; listen, God of Jacob. Selah
Look upon our shield, God, and look with favor on the face of Your anointed.
For a day in Your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than live in the tents of the wicked.
For the LORD God is a sun and shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.
The LORD of Hosts, blessed is the person who trusts in You.
The LORD showed favor to Your land, and You restored Jacob from captivity.
You forgave the sin of Your people and covered all their wrongs. Selah
You set aside all Your anger and turned from Your burning rage.
Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your anger toward us.
Will You stay angry with us forever? Will You let Your wrath last for every generation?
Won’t You give us life again so Your people can rejoice in You?
Show us Your faithful love, O the LORD, and grant us Your salvation.
I will listen to what God the LORD says, because He promises peace to His people and to His faithful followers, so they won’t turn back to foolish ways.
Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him, so His glory can live in our land.
Faithful love and truth will meet; righteousness and peace will kiss.
Truth will grow from the earth, and righteousness will look down from heaven.
The LORD will surely give what is good, and our land will produce its crops.
Righteousness will walk before Him and make a path for His steps.
Listen to me, the LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
Guard my life, for I am faithful. Save Your servant who trusts in You, my God.
Be gracious to me, Lord, for I call to You all day long.
Bring joy to Your servant's soul, for I turn my whole self to You, Lord.
For You, Lord, are good and forgiving, and You are full of faithful love for all who call on You.
The LORD, listen to my prayer, and pay attention to my cry for mercy.
I call on You in my trouble because You answer me.
There is no one like You among the gods, Lord, and no works like Yours.
All the nations You have made will come and worship before You, Lord, and they will honor Your name.
For You are great and do wonderful things; You alone are God.
Teach me Your way, the LORD, so I may walk in Your truth. Give me an undivided heart to fear Your name.
I will praise You, Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will honor Your name forever.
For Your faithful love to me is great; You have saved my life from the grave.
God, proud people have risen against me, and a gang of violent men is trying to kill me. They do not keep You in mind.
But You, Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, and full of faithful love and truth.
Turn to me and be gracious to me. Give Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your servant.
Show me a sign of Your favor, so my enemies will see it and be put to shame, because You, the LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
A psalm of the sons of Korah. A song. Its foundation rests on the holy mountains.
The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the homes of Jacob.
Glorious things are said about you, city of God. Selah.
"I will name Rahab and Babylon to those who know Me. Look, Philistia and Tyre are there with Cush. This one was born there."
"And about Zion it will be said, 'This one and that one were born in her,' and the Most High Himself will establish her."
The LORD will count the nations in His book: "This one was born there." Selah.
Singers and dancers will say, "All my fountains are in you."
The LORD, God of my salvation, I cry out before You day and night.
Let my prayer come before You; turn Your ear to my cry.
For my soul is full of troubles, and my life is close to the grave.
I am counted among those who go down to the pit; I am like a man with no strength.
I am abandoned among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom You remember no more, and who are cut off from Your help.
You have put me in the lowest pit, in dark places, in the depths.
Your wrath lies heavy on me; You have overwhelmed me with all Your waves. Selah.
You have taken my friends far from me; You have made me a horror to them. I am shut in and cannot escape.
My eyes grow weak from sorrow. I call on You every day, O the LORD; I spread out my hands to You.
Do You work wonders for the dead? Do the dead rise to praise You? Selah.
Is Your loving devotion declared in the grave, Your faithfulness in destruction?
Are Your wonders known in the darkness, or Your righteousness in the land where people are forgotten?
But I cry out to You, O the LORD; in the morning my prayer comes before You.
Why, O the LORD, do You reject my soul? Why do You hide Your face from me?
Since I was young, I have suffered and been near death. I have endured Your terrors and am worn out.
Your wrath has swept over me; Your terrors have destroyed me.
They surround me all day like water; they close in on me from every side.
You have taken my loved ones and friends far from me; darkness is my only companion.
I will sing of the LORD's faithful love forever; with my mouth I will make known Your faithfulness to every generation.
For I said, "Faithful love will last forever; in the heavens You will make Your faithfulness firm."
"I have made a covenant with My chosen one; I have sworn to David My servant:
'I will establish your offspring forever and build your throne for all generations.'" Selah.
Let the heavens praise Your wonders, the LORD, and Your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.
For who in the skies can be compared to the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like the LORD?
God is greatly feared in the council of the holy ones, and He is awesome above all who are around Him.
the LORD God of Hosts, who is mighty like You? Your faithfulness surrounds You.
You rule the raging of the sea; when its waves rise, You still them.
You crushed Rahab like a corpse; You scattered Your enemies with Your mighty arm.
The heavens are Yours, and the earth is Yours; the world and all that is in it, You founded them.
The north and the south, You created them; Tabor and Hermon sing for joy at Your name.
You have a mighty arm; Your hand is strong, Your right hand is lifted high.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne; faithful love and truth go before Your face.
Blessed are the people who know the joyful shout; they walk in the light of Your face, the LORD.
They rejoice in Your name all day long, and in Your righteousness they are lifted up.
For You are the glory of their strength, and by Your favor our strength is lifted high.
For the LORD is our shield, and our king belongs to the Holy One of Israel.
Then You spoke in a vision to Your faithful ones and said, "I have given help to a warrior; I have exalted one chosen from the people.
I have found David My servant; with My holy oil I have anointed him.
My hand will be with him, and My arm will strengthen him.
The enemy will not deceive him, nor will the son of wickedness afflict him.
I will crush his foes before him and strike down those who hate him.
My faithfulness and My faithful love will be with him, and in My name his strength will be lifted high.
I will set his hand over the sea and his right hand over the rivers.""
He will cry to Me, 'You are my Father, my God, and my saving refuge.'
I will make him My firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
I will keep My faithful love for him forever, and My covenant with him will stand firm.
I will establish his offspring forever and his throne as the days of heaven.
If his sons forsake My law and do not walk in My judgments,
if they break My statutes and do not keep My commandments,"
then I will punish their wrongdoing with a rod and their sin with stripes.
But I will not take My faithful love from him, nor will I be false to My faithfulness.
I will not violate My covenant or change what My lips have spoken.
I have sworn once by My holiness; I will not lie to David:
his offspring will endure forever, and his throne will be before Me like the sun.
Like the moon it will be established forever, a faithful witness in the sky." Selah.
But You have cast off and rejected him; You have been very angry with Your anointed one.
You have renounced the covenant with Your servant; You have profaned his crown in the dust.
You have broken through all his walls; You have brought his strongholds to ruin.
All who pass by plunder him; he has become a disgrace to his neighbors.
You have lifted up the right hand of his foes; You have made all his enemies glad.
You have turned back the edge of his sword and have not supported him in battle.
You have ended his splendor and cast his throne to the ground.
You have cut short the days of his youth; You have covered him with shame. Selah.
How long, the LORD? Will You hide Yourself forever? How long will Your wrath burn like fire?
Remember how short my life is; have You created all people for nothing?
What man can live and never see death? Who can save his soul from the power of the grave? Selah.
Lord, where are Your former acts of faithful love that You swore to David in Your faithfulness?
Remember, Lord, the shame of Your servants; how I carry in my heart the insults of many nations,
the insults Your enemies have hurled, the LORD, the insults they have hurled at the footsteps of Your anointed one.
Blessed be the LORD forever! Amen and Amen.
Lord, You have been our home for every generation.
Before the mountains were born, before You made the earth and the world, You are God from everlasting to everlasting.
You turn people back to dust and say, "Return to dust, O people."
For a thousand years in Your sight are like yesterday when it passes, or like a few hours of the night.
You sweep them away, and they sleep; they are like grass that springs up in the morning.
In the morning it blooms and grows, but by evening it is cut down and dries up.
For we are consumed by Your anger and terrified by Your wrath.
You have set our sins before You, our secret sins in the light of Your presence.
All our days pass away under Your wrath; we finish our years with a sigh.
The days of our life are seventy years, or eighty if we are strong; yet their best is only trouble and sorrow, for they pass quickly, and we fly away.
Who understands the power of Your anger? Your wrath is as great as the fear that is due You.
Teach us to number our days, so that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
Return, O the LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants.
Satisfy us in the morning with Your unfailing love, so that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen trouble.
Let Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children.
May the favor of the Lord our God rest on us; establish the work of our hands for us—yes, establish the work of our hands.
Whoever stays in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
I will say to the LORD, “You are my safe place and my strong tower. My God, I trust in You.”
For He will save you from the hunter’s trap and from the deadly disease.
He will cover you with His wings, and you will find safety under them. His truth will be your shield and protection.
You will not be afraid of the terror at night or of the arrow that flies by day.
You will not fear the disease that stalks in the dark or the ruin that strikes at noon.
A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not come near you.
You will only look with your eyes and see what happens to the wicked.
Because you have made the LORD your home and the Most High your safe place,
no harm will come to you, and no sickness will come near your tent.
For He will tell His angels to watch over you in all your ways.
They will lift you up in their hands so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.
You will step on the lion and the snake; you will trample the young lion and the serpent.
“Because he loves Me, I will save him. Because he knows My name, I will protect him.
When he calls to Me, I will answer him. I will be with him in trouble. I will rescue him and honor him.
I will satisfy him with a long life and show him My saving help.”
A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day. It is good to praise the the LORD, and to sing to Your name, O Most High.
It is good to tell of Your love in the morning and Your faithfulness at night.
Praise Him with a ten-stringed harp and the sound of a lyre.
For You, O the LORD, have made me glad by Your deeds; I sing for joy at the work of Your hands.
How great are Your works, O the LORD! Your plans are very deep.
A foolish person does not know this, and a person without sense does not understand it.
Even when the wicked grow like grass and all who do evil flourish, they will be destroyed forever.
But You, O the LORD, are exalted forever.
For look, Your enemies, O the LORD—yes, Your enemies will perish, and all who do evil will be scattered.
You have made me strong like a wild ox; You have poured fresh oil on me.
My eyes have seen my enemies fall, and my ears have heard the ruin of the wicked who rise against me.
Those who do right will flourish like a palm tree and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
They are planted in the house of the the LORD and grow strong in the courtyards of our God.
Even in old age they will still bear fruit; they will stay fresh and green.
They will say, "The the LORD is just. He is my Rock, and there is no wrong in Him."
The LORD is King! He is dressed in majesty. the LORD is dressed in strength and armed with power. The world is set firmly in place, so it cannot be shaken.
Your throne was set up long ago. You are from everlasting.
The rivers rise, O the LORD. The rivers raise their voice. The rivers throw up their crashing waves.
The LORD on high is stronger than the loud roar of many waters and the mighty waves of the sea.
Your laws are completely true. Holiness makes Your house beautiful, O the LORD, for all time.
O the LORD, God of vengeance, God of vengeance, shine out!
Rise up, Judge of the earth; give the proud what they deserve.
How long, O the LORD, will the wicked win? How long will evil people be happy?
They pour out proud words; all who do evil brag.
They crush your people, O the LORD, and hurt your own.
They kill widows and foreigners and murder orphans.
They say, "The LORD does not see; the God of Jacob does not notice."
Pay attention, you who are slow to understand! You fools, when will you be wise?
He who planted the ear—does He not hear? He who formed the eye—does He not see?
He who corrects nations—will He not warn them? He who teaches people what they know—
the LORD knows human thoughts; He knows they are only a breath.
Happy is the person the LORD corrects, the one He teaches from His law.
He gives that person rest from hard days until a pit is dug for the wicked.
The LORD will not leave His people; He will not give up His own.
Justice will come back to those who do right, and everyone with an honest heart will follow it.
Who will stand up for me against the wicked? Who will stand with me against those who do evil?
If the LORD had not helped me, I would have soon gone to the silent grave.
When I thought my foot was slipping, Your faithful love, O the LORD, held me up.
When worry fills my heart, Your comfort makes me glad.
Can evil rulers join with You, O the LORD, when they make unfair laws?
They gang up against the lives of good people and condemn the innocent to death.
But the LORD has become my safe place; my God is the rock I trust.
He will pay them back for their wrong and destroy them for their evil. The LORD our God will destroy them.
Come, let's sing to the the LORD! Let's shout to the Rock who saves us!
Let's come to Him with thanks, and shout to Him with songs of praise!
For the the LORD is a great God, a great King over all gods.
The deep places of the earth are in His hand, and the mountain peaks belong to Him.
The sea is His, because He made it. His hands shaped the dry land.
Come, let's worship and bow down. Let's kneel before the the LORD, our Maker.
For He is our God, and we are His flock, the sheep He holds in His hand. "Today, if you hear His voice,
do not harden your hearts as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the desert,
where your ancestors tested Me and tried Me, even though they saw My work.
"For forty years I was angry with that generation, and I said, 'They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they do not know My ways.'
"So I swore in My anger, 'They will never enter My rest.'"
Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth.
Sing to the LORD, praise His name; tell of His salvation day after day.
Tell of His glory among the nations, and His wonderful works among all peoples.
For great is the LORD and worthy of much praise; He is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and beauty are in His sanctuary.
Give to the LORD, you families of nations, give to the LORD glory and strength.
Give to the LORD the glory His name deserves; bring an offering and come into His courts.
Worship the LORD in the beauty of His holiness; tremble before Him, all the earth.
Say among the nations, "The LORD reigns! The world is firmly set; it cannot be shaken. He will judge the peoples fairly."
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let the sea roar, and everything in it.
Let the fields and everything in them be joyful; let all the trees of the forest sing for joy.
Let all creation rejoice before the LORD, for He comes, He comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples in His faithfulness.
The LORD rules, so let the earth be glad! Let the distant shores rejoice!
Clouds and thick darkness surround Him. Righteousness and justice are the base of His throne.
Fire goes ahead of Him and burns up His enemies all around.
His lightning lights up the world. The earth sees it and trembles.
The mountains melt like wax before the the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens declare His righteousness, and all nations see His glory.
Everyone who worships idols is put to shame—those who brag about worthless gods. Worship Him, all you gods!
Zion hears and is glad. The daughters of Judah rejoice because of Your judgments, O the LORD.
For You, O the LORD, are the Most High over all the earth. You are lifted up far above all gods.
You who love the the LORD, hate evil! He keeps His faithful people safe and rescues them from the wicked.
Light is given to those who do right, and joy to those with honest hearts.
Rejoice in the the LORD, you righteous people, and give thanks to His holy name!
Sing a new song to the LORD, because He has done amazing things. His right hand and holy arm have won the victory for Him.
The LORD has made His saving power known. He has shown His justice to the nations.
He remembered His faithful love and His faithfulness to Israel. Everyone to the ends of the earth has seen the saving power of our God.
Shout for joy to the LORD, all the earth. Burst into song, sing for joy, and make music.
Sing praises to the LORD with the harp, with music and a joyful song.
Play trumpets and the sound of the ram's horn. Shout for joy before the LORD, the King.
Let the sea roar, and everything in it. Let the world and everyone who lives in it do the same.
Let the rivers clap their hands. Let the mountains sing together with joy.
Let them stand before the LORD, because He is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world with justice and the peoples with fairness.
The LORD reigns; let the peoples tremble. He sits enthroned above the cherubim; let the earth quake.
Great is the LORD in Zion; He is exalted above all the peoples.
Let them praise Your great and awesome name—He is holy.
The King’s strength loves justice. You have established fairness; You have carried out justice and right in Jacob.
Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at His footstool; He is holy.
Moses and Aaron were among His priests, and Samuel among those who called on His name. They called to the LORD, and He answered them.
He spoke to them in a pillar of cloud; they kept His commands and the law He gave them.
O the LORD our God, You answered them. You were a forgiving God to them, yet You punished them for their wrongs.
Exalt the LORD our God and worship at His holy mountain, for the LORD our God is holy.
Shout for joy to the LORD, all the earth!
Serve the LORD with gladness; come before Him with joyful songs.
Know that the LORD is God. It is He who made us, and we are His. We are His people, the sheep of His pasture.
Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise. Give thanks to Him and bless His name.
For the LORD is good; His loving devotion lasts forever, and His faithfulness continues through every generation.
I will sing about Your faithful love and justice. To You, the LORD, I will sing praise.
I will be careful to live a blameless life. When will You come to me? I will walk inside my home with a pure heart.
I won't put anything worthless in front of my eyes. I hate what people do when they turn away from what's right, and I won't let it stick to me.
A twisted heart will leave me, and I won't have anything to do with evil.
I will destroy anyone who secretly talks badly about his neighbor. I can't stand a person with proud eyes and a proud heart.
I keep my eyes on the faithful people of the land so they can live with me. The person who walks in a blameless way will serve me.
No one who practices deceit will live in my house. No one who tells lies will stand in front of me.
Every morning I will destroy all the wicked people in the land. I will cut off all evildoers from the city of the LORD.
Hear my prayer, O the LORD; let my cry come to You.
Do not hide Your face from me when I am in trouble. Turn Your ear to me and answer me quickly when I call.
My days disappear like smoke, and my bones burn as if in a fire.
My heart is crushed and dries up like grass, so I even forget to eat.
Because of my loud groaning, my bones stick to my skin.
I am like a desert owl, like an owl living among ruins.
I lie awake and feel like a lonely bird on a rooftop.
My enemies insult me all day long; those who make fun of me use my name to curse.
I have eaten ashes like bread and mixed my drink with tears
because of Your anger and wrath. You lifted me up and then threw me down.
My days fade like a shadow, and I wither like grass.
But You, O the LORD, sit on Your throne forever; Your name will be remembered in every generation.
You will rise up and show mercy to Zion, because the time has come to be kind to her. The appointed time has arrived.
For Your servants love her stones and even care about her dust.
So the nations will fear the name of the the LORD, and all the kings of the earth will fear Your glory.
For the the LORD will rebuild Zion and appear in His glory.
He will listen to the prayer of the needy and will not look down on their prayers.
Let this be written down for the next generation, so that people not yet born may praise the the LORD.
The The LORD looked down from His holy place above; from heaven He looked at the earth
to hear the groans of the prisoners and to set free those sentenced to death.
Then they will tell about the name of the the LORD in Zion and praise Him in Jerusalem
when peoples and kingdoms come together to serve the the LORD.
He has weakened me on my journey and shortened my life.
I say, "My God, do not take me away in the middle of my life! Your years last through all generations."
Long ago You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
They will die, but You remain. They will all wear out like old clothes. You will change them like clothing, and they will pass away.
But You are the same, and Your years will never end.
The children of Your servants will live safely, and their children will stand firm before You.
Bless the LORD, O my soul; with all my heart, bless His holy name.
Bless the LORD, O my soul, and don't forget all His blessings.
He forgives all your sins; He heals all your diseases.
He rescues your life from destruction; He crowns you with faithful love and compassion.
He fills your years with good things, so your youth is renewed like the eagle's.
The LORD does what is right and fair for all who are treated unfairly.
He showed Moses His ways and the people of Israel His deeds.
The LORD is kind and gracious, slow to anger, and full of faithful love.
He will not always accuse, and He will not hold His anger forever.
He has not treated us as our sins deserve, and He has not paid us back for our wrongs.
For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His faithful love for those who fear Him.
As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our wrongdoings from us.
As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him.
For He knows how weak we are; He remembers that we are dust.
A person's days are like grass; he blooms like a wildflower.
When the wind blows over it, it is gone, and its place no longer remembers it.
But the faithful love of the LORD lasts forever for those who fear Him, and His goodness reaches to their children and grandchildren.
It is for those who keep His promise and remember to obey His commands.
The LORD has set up His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all.
Bless the LORD, you His angels, mighty in strength, who do what He says and listen to His word.
Bless the LORD, all you His heavenly armies, His servants who do His will.
Bless the LORD, all His works, in every place He rules. Bless the LORD, O my soul.
Bless the the LORD, O my soul! O the the LORD my God, You are very great. You are clothed with splendor and majesty.
He wraps Himself in light like a garment. He stretches out the heavens like a tent.
He lays the beams of His upper rooms on the waters. He makes the clouds His chariot. He walks on the wings of the wind.
