He makes the winds His messengers and flames of fire His servants.
He set the earth on its foundations, so it can never be moved.
You covered it with the deep like a garment. The waters stood above the mountains.
At Your rebuke the waters fled. At the sound of Your thunder they ran away.
The mountains rose, and the valleys sank down to the place You appointed for them.
You set a boundary the waters cannot cross. They will never again cover the earth.
He sends springs into the valleys. They flow between the mountains.
They give water to every wild animal. The wild donkeys quench their thirst.
The birds of the sky nest beside them. They sing among the branches.
He waters the mountains from His upper rooms. The earth is satisfied by the fruit of Your works.
He makes grass grow for the livestock and plants for people to use, bringing food from the earth.
Wine makes people glad. Oil makes faces shine. Bread gives strength to the heart.
The trees of the the LORD are well watered. The cedars of Lebanon, which He planted, have plenty of water.
There the birds make their nests. The stork has its home in the pine trees.
The high mountains are for the wild goats. The cliffs are a safe place for the rock badgers.
He made the moon to mark the seasons. The sun knows when to set.
You bring darkness, and it becomes night, when all the beasts of the forest prowl.
The young lions roar for their prey. They seek their food from God.
The sun rises, and they withdraw. They lie down in their dens.
People go out to their work and to their labor until evening.
How many are Your works, O the the LORD! In wisdom You made them all. The earth is full of Your creatures.
There is the sea, vast and wide. It teems with creatures beyond number, living things both great and small.
There the ships pass by. Leviathan, which You formed, plays there.
All creatures look to You to give them their food at the proper time.
When You give it to them, they gather it up. When You open Your hand, they are filled with good things.
When You hide Your face, they are terrified. When You take away their breath, they die and return to the dust.
When You send Your Spirit, they are created. You renew the face of the earth.
May the glory of the the LORD last forever. May the the LORD rejoice in His works.
He looks at the earth, and it trembles. He touches the mountains, and they smoke.
I will sing to the the LORD all my life. I will sing praise to my God as long as I live.
May my thoughts be pleasing to Him. I will rejoice in the the LORD.
May sinners vanish from the earth, and may the wicked be no more. Bless the the LORD, O my soul. Praise the the LORD!
Give thanks to the LORD. Call on His name. Make His deeds known among the nations.
Sing to Him; sing praise to Him. Tell about all His wonderful acts.
Glory in His holy name. Let the hearts of those who seek the LORD be glad.
Seek the LORD and His strength; seek His face always.
Remember the wonders He has done, His miracles, and the judgments He spoke.
Descendants of Abraham, His servant, and sons of Jacob, His chosen ones.
He is the LORD our God. His judgments are over all the earth.
He remembers His covenant forever—the word He commanded for a thousand generations.
He made this covenant with Abraham and swore an oath to Isaac.
He made it a law for Jacob and an everlasting covenant for Israel.
He said, "I will give you the land of Canaan as your inheritance."
When they were only a few people—very few—and strangers in that land,
they wandered from nation to nation and from one kingdom to another.
He let no one oppress them. For their sake He warned kings:
"Do not touch My anointed ones; do no harm to My prophets."
He called famine on the land and broke every supply of bread.
He sent a man ahead of them—Joseph, who was sold as a slave.
They hurt his feet with chains, and iron pierced his soul.
He stayed there until the time came for the LORD's word to come true; His promise tested him.
Then the king sent for him and set him free; the ruler of the peoples released him.
He made Joseph master of his house and ruler over all he owned.
He did this so Joseph could guide the king's officials as he pleased and teach wisdom to the elders.
Then Israel came to Egypt; Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
The LORD made His people grow very strong and more numerous than their enemies.
He turned the enemies' hearts to hate His people and to plot against His servants.
He sent Moses, His servant, and Aaron, whom He had chosen.
They did His signs and wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness, and it became dark; they did not disobey His words.
He turned their water into blood and killed their fish.
Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the royal bedrooms.
He spoke, and flies came; gnats spread through all their country.
He gave them hail instead of rain, and lightning flashed across their land.
He struck their grapevines and fig trees and broke the trees throughout their country.
He spoke, and locusts came—young locusts too many to count.
They ate every plant in the land and the fruit of the soil.
He struck down all the firstborn in their land, the first and best of their strength.
He brought Israel out with silver and gold, and no one among His tribes was weak.
Egypt was glad when they left, because fear of Israel had fallen on them.
He spread a cloud to cover them and fire to give light at night.
They asked, and He brought quail; He filled them with bread from heaven.
He opened the rock, and water poured out; it ran like a river in the dry land.
He did this because He remembered His holy promise to Abraham, His servant.
So He brought out His people with joy and His chosen ones with singing.
He gave them the lands of the nations, and they took over what other peoples had worked for.
He did this so they would keep His laws and obey His teachings. Praise the LORD!
Praise the the LORD! Thank the the LORD, because He is good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Who can speak of the the LORD's mighty acts? Who can tell all His praise?
Happy are the people who keep justice and do what is right all the time.
Remember me, the the LORD, when You show kindness to Your people. Come help me with Your saving power.
Let me see the good things You give Your chosen people. Let me be glad with the joy of Your nation and join in praising You with the people You own.
We have sinned like our ancestors. We have done wrong and acted wickedly.
Our ancestors in Egypt did not understand Your miracles. They did not remember Your great kindness. They rebelled by the Red Sea.
Yet He saved them to honor His name and show His mighty power.
He spoke sharply to the Red Sea, and it dried up. He led them through the deep water like through a desert.
He saved them from their enemies and set them free.
The water covered their enemies, and not one of them was left.
Then they believed His words and sang His praise.
But they soon forgot what He had done and did not wait for His plan.
They became greedy in the desert and tested God in the dry land.
He gave them what they asked for, but He sent a sickness that made them weak.
In the camp they became jealous of Moses and Aaron, the the LORD's holy one.
The ground opened up and swallowed Dathan. It covered Abiram's followers.
Fire broke out among them, and flames burned up the wicked people.
At Mount Horeb they made a calf and worshiped a statue made of metal.
They traded their glorious God for a statue of a bull that eats grass.
They forgot God, their Savior, who did great things in Egypt.
He did amazing things in Egypt and terrifying things at the Red Sea.
So He said He would destroy them. But Moses, His chosen servant, stepped in and turned His anger away so He would not destroy them.
They rejected the good land and did not believe His promise.
They grumbled in their tents and did not listen to the the LORD's voice.
So He raised His hand and swore He would make them die in the desert.
He would scatter their children among the nations and send them to other lands.
They gave themselves to the worship of Baal of Peor and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
They made Him angry by what they did, so a plague broke out among them.
But Phinehas stood up and stepped in, and the plague stopped.
This was counted to him as right living for all time to come.
They made the the LORD angry at the waters of Meribah, and Moses suffered because of them.
They rebelled against His Spirit, and Moses spoke without thinking.
They did not destroy the nations the the LORD had told them to destroy.
Instead, they mixed with the nations and learned their ways.
They worshiped their idols, which became a trap for them.
They sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons.
They shed innocent blood—the blood of their sons and daughters—by sacrificing them to the idols of Canaan. The land was polluted with blood.
They became unclean by their actions and were unfaithful in what they did.
So the the LORD became angry with His people, and He was disgusted with the people He had chosen.
He let other nations take them, and their enemies ruled over them.
Their enemies pressed hard on them, and they were brought low under their power.
Many times He saved them, but they kept rebelling against His plan, and their sin pulled them down.
Yet He saw their trouble and heard their cry.
He remembered His promise to them and showed mercy because of His great faithful love.
He caused their captors to have mercy on them.
Save us, the the LORD our God! Gather us from the nations so we can thank Your holy name and praise You.
May the the LORD, the God of Israel, be praised from everlasting to everlasting. Let all the people say, "Amen!" Praise the the LORD!
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His faithful love lasts forever.
Let the redeemed of the LORD say so—those He rescued from the enemy's hand.
He gathered them from the lands, from the east and the west, from the north and the south.
Some wandered in desert wastelands and could not find a road to a city where they could live.
They were hungry and thirsty, and their strength was failing.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and He delivered them from their distress.
He led them by a straight path to a city where they could live.
Let them thank the LORD for His faithful love and His wonders for people.
For He satisfies the thirsty and fills the hungry with good things.
Some sat in darkness, in the shadow of death, held as prisoners in suffering and chains,
because they had rebelled against God's words and rejected the advice of the Most High.
So He humbled their hearts with hard labor; they stumbled, and there was no one to help.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and He saved them from their distress.
He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death and broke their chains.
Let them thank the LORD for His faithful love and His wonders for people.
For He broke the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron.
Fools suffered because of their rebellious ways and their sins.
They hated all food and came near the gates of death.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and He saved them from their distress.
He sent His word and healed them; He rescued them from the pit.
Let them thank the LORD for His faithful love and His wonders for people.
Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and tell of His works with shouts of joy.
Those who sail the sea in ships and work on the great waters
have seen the works of the LORD and His wonders in the deep.
For He spoke and raised a stormy wind that lifted up the waves.
They rose to the heavens and sank to the depths; their strength melted away in their trouble.
They reeled and staggered like drunk men, and all their skill was useless.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and He brought them out of their distress.
He calmed the storm to a whisper, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
They rejoiced that the waters were quiet, and He guided them to the harbor they wanted.
Let them thank the LORD for His faithful love and His wonders for people.
Let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people and praise Him in the council of the elders.
He turns rivers into a desert, springs of water into thirsty ground,
and a fruitful land into a salt waste, because of the wickedness of its people.
He turns a desert into pools of water and a dry land into springs of water.
There He brings the hungry to live, and they establish a city to dwell in.
They sow fields and plant vineyards that yield a fruitful harvest.
He blesses them, and they multiply greatly; He does not let their herds diminish.
When they are decreased and humbled by oppression, trouble, and sorrow,
He pours scorn on princes and makes them wander in a wasteland with no path.
But He lifts the needy out of affliction and makes their families grow like flocks.
The upright see and rejoice, and all wrongdoing is silenced.
Whoever is wise, let him heed these things and consider the faithful love of the LORD.
My heart is steady, O God. I will sing and make music with my whole self.
Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
I will praise you, the LORD, among the nations. I will sing praises to you among the peoples.
For your love is great above the heavens, and your faithfulness reaches to the skies.
Be lifted up, O God, above the heavens. Let your glory cover all the earth.
Save your loved ones with your right hand. Answer me, so they may be rescued.
God has spoken in His holiness: "I will triumph! I will divide Shechem and measure the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is Mine; Manasseh is Mine. Ephraim is My helmet, and Judah is My scepter.
Moab is My washbasin. Upon Edom I throw My sandal. Over Philistia I shout in triumph."
Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You not march out with our armies?
Give us help against the enemy, for human help is useless.
With God we will act with strength, and He will trample our enemies.
O God of my praise, do not stay silent.
Wicked, lying mouths have opened against me. They have spoken lies about me.
They surround me with hateful words and attack me for no reason.
In return for my love, they accuse me, but I keep praying.
They pay me back evil for good and hatred for my love.
Put a wicked person in charge of him, and let an accuser stand beside him.
When he is judged, let him be found guilty. Let his prayer be seen as sin.
May his days be few. May someone else take his position.
May his children be orphans and his wife a widow.
May his children wander and beg. May they look for food far from their ruined homes.
May a moneylender take everything he owns. May strangers steal what he worked for.
May no one show him kindness. May no one help his orphaned children.
May his family line end. May their name be wiped out in the next generation.
May the LORD remember the sins of his ancestors. May his mother’s sin never be forgiven.
May their sins always be before the LORD, so He can remove their memory from the earth.
For he never thought to show kindness. He hunted down the poor and needy and brokenhearted to kill them.
He loved to curse, so let curses fall on him. He hated blessing, so let it stay far from him.
He wore curses like clothing. They soaked into his body like water and into his bones like oil.
May those curses be like a coat he wears, like a belt he puts on every day.
May the LORD repay my accusers this way, those who speak evil against me.
But You, O the LORD, my Lord, treat me well for Your name’s sake. Because Your faithful love is good, rescue me.
For I am poor and needy, and my heart is wounded inside me.
I fade away like a shadow that grows long. I am shaken off like a locust.
My knees are weak from fasting, and my body has grown thin.
I am a joke to my accusers. When they see me, they shake their heads.
Help me, O the LORD, my God. Save me because of Your faithful love.
Let them know that this comes from You, O the LORD. You have done it.
They may curse, but You will bless. They may rise up, but they will be put to shame. I, Your servant, will be glad.
May my accusers be covered with shame. May they wear their disgrace like a coat.
With my mouth I will thank the LORD greatly. I will praise Him among many people.
For He stands beside the needy, to save them from those who condemn them.
The LORD said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."
the LORD will send out your strong scepter from Zion. Rule in the middle of your enemies.
Your people will freely step forward on the day you show your power. They will shine in holy beauty, and your young people will be like the morning dew.
The LORD has sworn an oath and will not change His mind: "You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek."
The Lord stands at your right hand. He will crush kings on the day He is angry.
He will judge the nations. He will fill the land with dead bodies. He will crush the head of the enemy across the wide earth.
He will drink from a stream beside the road, and then He will hold His head high.
Hallelujah! I will praise the LORD with all my heart, in the meeting of good people and in the crowd.
The works of the LORD are great, and everyone who loves them studies them.
His deeds are glorious and majestic, and His right ways last forever.
He made His miracles unforgettable. The LORD is kind and full of mercy.
He gives food to those who respect Him. He will never forget His promise.
He showed His people how powerful His works are by giving them the land of other nations.
What His hands do is faithful and fair. All His commands can be trusted.
They last forever and ever, built on truth and justice.
He brought freedom to His people. He made His promise last forever. His name is holy and amazing.
Respect for the LORD is the start of wisdom. Everyone who lives by it has good sense. His praise lasts forever.
Praise the LORD! Blessed is the man who fears the LORD and greatly delights in His commands.
His children will be mighty in the land, and the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever.
Light dawns in the darkness for the upright—gracious, compassionate, and righteous.
Good is the man who is gracious and lends; he will uphold his cause in judgment.
For he will never be shaken; the righteous will be remembered forever.
He will not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.
His heart is secure; he will not be afraid until he sees his enemies fall.
He has scattered his gifts to the poor; his righteousness endures forever; his horn will be lifted high in honor.
The wicked will see and be angry; they will grind their teeth and waste away; the desire of the wicked will perish.
Praise the the LORD! Praise Him, servants of the the LORD; praise the name of the the LORD.
Blessed be the name of the the LORD from now and forever.
From sunrise to sunset, the name of the the LORD is praised.
The The LORD is high above all nations; His glory is above the heavens.
Who is like the the LORD our God, who sits enthroned on high,
who looks down on the heavens and the earth?
He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap,
to seat them with princes, with the princes of His people.
He settles the childless woman in a home as a joyful mother of children. Praise the the LORD!
When Israel came out of Egypt, Jacob's family left a people whose language they did not know.
Judah became His sanctuary, and Israel became His kingdom.
The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back.
The mountains skipped like rams, the hills like lambs.
What is wrong with you, sea, that you flee? Why do you turn back, Jordan?
Mountains, why do you skip like rams? Hills, why do you skip like lambs?
Tremble, earth, before the Lord, before the God of Jacob.
He turned the rock into a pool of water and the flint into a flowing spring.
Not to us, the LORD, not to us, but give glory to Your name, because of Your loving devotion, because of Your faithfulness.
Why should the nations say, "Where is their God?"
Our God is in heaven; He does whatever He wants.
Their idols are silver and gold, made by human hands.
They have mouths, but they do not speak; they have eyes, but they do not see.
They have ears, but they do not hear; they have noses, but they do not smell.
They have hands, but they do not feel; they have feet, but they do not walk; and they cannot make a sound with their throats.
Those who make them become like them, and so do all who trust in them.
O Israel, trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield.
O house of Aaron, trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield.
You who fear the LORD, trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield.
The LORD has remembered us; He will bless us. He will bless the house of Israel; He will bless the house of Aaron.
He will bless those who fear the LORD, both the small and the great.
May the LORD give you more and more, you and your children!
You are blessed by the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.
The heavens belong to the LORD, but the earth He has given to people.
The dead do not praise the LORD, nor do those who go down into silence.
But we will bless the LORD from now on and forever. Praise the LORD!
I love the the LORD, because He hears my voice and my cries for mercy.
He turned His ear toward me, so I will call on Him as long as I live.
Death closed in on me. The grave's terror came over me. Trouble and sorrow crushed me.
Then I called on the name of the the LORD: "O the LORD, save my life!"
The the LORD is kind and does what is right. Our God is full of mercy.
The the LORD watches over the helpless. I was brought low, and He saved me.
My soul, return to your rest, for the the LORD has been good to you.
He rescued my life from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from stumbling.
I will walk with the the LORD in the land of the living.
I believed, so I said, "I am in deep trouble."
In my fear I said, "Everyone lies."
What can I give the the LORD for all the good things He has done for me?
I will lift the cup that celebrates His rescue, and I will call on the name of the the LORD.
I will keep my promises to the the LORD where all His people can see.
The death of His faithful people matters greatly to the the LORD.
O the LORD, I am truly Your servant. I am Your servant, the son of Your servant woman. You have set me free from my chains.
I will offer You a sacrifice of thanks, and I will call on the name of the the LORD.
I will keep my promises to the the LORD where all His people can see.
I will praise Him in the courtyards of the the LORD’s house, right in your midst, Jerusalem. Praise the the LORD!
Praise the LORD, all nations. Praise Him, all peoples.
His faithful love for us is strong, and the LORD's truth lasts forever. Praise the LORD!
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His faithful love endures forever.
Let Israel say, "His faithful love endures forever."
Let the house of Aaron say, "His faithful love endures forever."
Let those who fear the LORD say, "His faithful love endures forever."
When I was in trouble, I cried out to the LORD, and He answered me and set me free.
The LORD is with me; I will not be afraid. What can a person do to me?
The LORD is with me; He is my helper. I will look in triumph on those who hate me.
It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in people.
It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in human leaders.
All nations surrounded me, but in the name of the LORD I defeated them.
They surrounded me on every side, but in the name of the LORD I defeated them.
They swarmed around me like bees; they burned out like thorns in a fire, but in the name of the LORD I defeated them.
I was pushed hard, and I was about to fall, but the LORD helped me.
The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.
Shouts of joy and victory are in the tents of those who do right: "The right hand of the LORD does mighty things!"
The right hand of the LORD is lifted high; the right hand of the LORD does mighty things!
I will not die but live, and I will tell what the LORD has done.
The LORD has disciplined me severely, but He has not handed me over to death.
Open the gates of righteousness to me, so I can enter through them and thank the LORD.
This is the gate of the LORD; those who do right will enter through it.
I will thank You, for You answered me and became my salvation.
The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This came from the LORD, and it is amazing in our eyes.
This is the day the LORD has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.
O the LORD, save us, we pray; O the LORD, grant us success, we pray.
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the LORD. From the house of the LORD we bless you.
The LORD is God, and He has made His light shine on us. Tie the festival sacrifice with cords to the horns of the altar.
You are my God, and I will thank You; You are my God, I will praise You.
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His faithful love endures forever.
Happy are those who live without blame and follow the LORD's teachings.
Happy are those who obey His rules and seek Him with all their heart.
They do no wrong; they walk in His ways.
You have commanded us to obey Your rules carefully.
I wish my ways were steady so I could keep Your rules.
Then I would not be ashamed when I look at all Your commands.
I will praise You with an honest heart when I learn Your right decisions.
I will keep Your rules; do not leave me completely.
How can a young person keep his life pure? By living according to Your word.
I seek You with all my heart; do not let me stray from Your commands.
I have stored Your word in my heart so I will not sin against You.
Blessed are You, the LORD; teach me Your rules.
I tell with my lips all the decisions You have spoken.
I find joy in following Your rules as much as in great wealth.
I will think about Your commands and watch Your ways.
I will enjoy Your rules; I will not forget Your word.
Be good to Your servant so I can live and keep Your word.
Open my eyes so I can see wonderful things in Your teaching.
I am only a visitor on earth; do not hide Your commands from me.
I long for Your rules with all my heart all the time.
You correct proud people who are cursed because they turn from Your commands.
Remove scorn and shame from me, for I have obeyed Your rules.
Even when leaders plot against me, I, Your servant, will think about Your rules.
Your rules bring me joy; they guide me like wise friends.
I am crushed to the dust; give me life as Your word promises.
I told You my ways, and You answered me; teach me Your rules.
Help me understand Your commands, and I will think about Your wonderful works.
I am weak with sorrow; make me strong as Your word says.
Keep me from false ways; be gracious and teach me Your law.
I have chosen the path of faith; I keep Your rules in front of me.
I hold tightly to Your rules; the LORD, do not let me be ashamed.
I will run to obey Your commands when You give me a willing heart.
Teach me, the LORD, to follow Your rules, and I will keep them to the end.
Give me understanding so I can keep Your law with all my heart.
Lead me in the path of Your commands, because I enjoy it.
Turn my heart toward Your rules, not toward selfish gain.
Turn my eyes away from worthless things; give me life in Your ways.
Keep Your promise to Your servant so people may honor You.
Take away the shame I fear, for Your rules are good.
See, I long for Your commands; give me life through Your goodness.
Let Your faithful love come to me, the LORD; save me as You promised.
Then I can answer those who mock me, because I trust Your word.
Do not take the word of truth from my mouth, because I hope in Your rules.
I will keep Your law always, forever and ever.
I will walk freely because I have sought Your commands.
I will speak of Your rules before kings and not be ashamed.
I find joy in Your commands, which I love.
I lift my hands to Your commands, which I love, and I think about Your rules.
Remember Your word to Your servant; You gave me hope through it.
This comforts me in my trouble: Your promise gives me life.
Proud people mock me badly, but I do not turn from Your law.
When I think of Your old decisions, the LORD, I find comfort.
I burn with anger because wicked people abandon Your law.
Your rules are my songs in my temporary home.
I remember Your name at night, the LORD, and keep Your law.
This has happened to me because I kept Your commands.
The LORD is my share; I promise to keep Your words.
I ask for Your favor with all my heart; be kind to me as You promised.
When I think about my ways, I turn my steps toward Your rules.
I hurry and do not delay to keep Your commands.
The wicked may trap me, but I do not forget Your law.
At midnight I get up to praise You for Your right decisions.
I am a friend to all who honor You and keep Your commands.
The earth is full of Your faithful love, the LORD; teach me Your rules.
You have been good to Your servant, the LORD, as Your word says.
Teach me good sense and knowledge, because I trust Your commands.
Before I suffered, I went astray, but now I keep Your word.
You are good and do good; teach me Your rules.
Proud people spread lies about me, but I keep Your commands with all my heart.
Their hearts are dull, but I enjoy Your law.
It was good for me to suffer so I could learn Your rules.
Your teaching from Your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver.
Your hands made me and shaped me; give me understanding to learn Your commands.
Those who honor You will see me and be glad, because I hoped in Your word.
I know Your decisions are right, the LORD, and You have disciplined me in faithfulness.
Let Your faithful love comfort me, as You promised Your servant.
Let Your mercy come to me so I can live, for Your law is my joy.
Let proud people be ashamed because they lied about me; I will think about Your commands.
Let those who honor You turn to me so they can know Your rules.
Let my heart be whole in Your rules so I will not be ashamed.
I long for Your rescue; I hope in Your word.
My eyes grow tired waiting for Your promise; I ask, "When will You comfort me?"
I am like a dried wineskin in smoke, but I have not forgotten Your rules.
How long must Your servant wait? When will You judge those who chase me?
Proud people have dug traps for me; they ignore Your law.
All Your commands are faithful; they attack me with lies; help me!
They have almost destroyed me on earth, but I have not left Your commands.
Give me life because of Your faithful love, so I can keep the rules from Your mouth.
Forever, the LORD, Your word stands firm in heaven.
Your faithfulness lasts for every generation; You made the earth, and it stays.
All things serve You, and they stand today by Your decisions.
If Your law had not been my joy, I would have died in my trouble.
I will never forget Your commands, because through them You gave me life.
I am Yours; save me, because I have sought Your commands.
Wicked people wait to destroy me, but I think about Your rules.
I have seen limits to everything perfect, but Your command is very wide.
Oh, how I love Your law! I think about it all day.
Your command makes me wiser than my enemies because it is always with me.
I understand more than my teachers because I think about Your rules.
I understand more than older people because I keep Your commands.
I keep my feet from every evil path so I can keep Your word.
I do not turn from Your rules, because You have taught me.
Your words are sweet to my taste, sweeter than honey in my mouth.
Through Your commands I gain understanding, so I hate every false way.
Your word is a lamp for my feet and a light for my path.
I have promised and will keep it: I will follow Your right rules.
I suffer greatly; the LORD, give me life as Your word says.
Accept my willing praise, the LORD, and teach me Your rules.
My life is always in danger, but I do not forget Your law.
Wicked people set traps for me, but I do not stray from Your commands.
Your rules are my lasting treasure because they bring joy to my heart.
I turn my heart to keep Your rules forever, to the end.
I hate divided hearts, but I love Your law.
You are my hiding place and my shield; I hope in Your word.
Leave me alone, you evildoers, so I can keep the commands of my God.
Support me as You promised so I can live; do not let me be ashamed of my hope.
Hold me up, and I will be safe and keep Your rules always.
You reject all who stray from Your rules, because their tricks are false.
You remove all the wicked from the earth like waste metal, so I love Your rules.
My body trembles with fear of You, and I am afraid of Your decisions.
I have done what is right and fair; do not leave me to those who oppress me.
Promise good to Your servant; do not let proud people oppress me.
My eyes long for Your rescue and for Your right promise to come true.
Treat Your servant with faithful love and teach me Your rules.
I am Your servant; give me understanding so I can know Your rules.
It is time for the LORD to act, because people have broken Your law.
So I love Your commands more than gold, even the finest gold.
So I count all Your commands as right; I hate every false way.
Your rules are wonderful; so I keep them with all my heart.
When Your words are explained, they give light and understanding to simple people.
I open my mouth and pant because I long for Your commands.
Turn to me and be kind to me, as You do for those who love Your name.
Make my steps steady by Your word, and do not let sin rule over me.
Rescue me from being oppressed by people so I can keep Your commands.
Let Your face shine on Your servant and teach me Your rules.
Streams of tears flow from my eyes because people do not keep Your law.
You are right, the LORD, and Your rules are right.
You have commanded Your rules with perfect goodness and faithfulness.
My passion eats me up because my enemies forget Your words.
Your promise has been tested and proven, and Your servant loves it.
I am small and looked down on, yet I do not forget Your commands.
Your goodness is right forever, and Your law is true.
Trouble and distress have found me, but Your commands are my joy.
Your rules are right forever; give me understanding so I can live.
I cry to You with all my heart; answer me, the LORD! I will keep Your rules.
I call to You; save me so I can obey Your rules.
I get up before dawn and cry for help; I hope in Your words.
My eyes stay awake through the night so I can think about Your promise.
Hear my voice, the LORD, in Your faithful love; give me life by Your justice.
People who chase me with evil plans come near; they are far from Your law.
But You are near, the LORD, and all Your commands are true.
Long ago I learned from Your rules that You made them to last forever.
Look at my trouble and rescue me, for I do not forget Your law.
Defend my case and redeem me; give me life as You promised.
Rescue is far from wicked people because they do not seek Your rules.
Your mercy is great, the LORD; give me life by Your rules.
Many chase me and oppose me, but I do not turn from Your rules.
I look at faithless people with disgust because they do not keep Your commands.
See how I love Your commands; give me life by Your faithful love.
The whole of Your word is true, and all Your right rules last forever.
Rulers chase me for no reason, but my heart trembles at Your words.
I rejoice in Your word like someone who finds great treasure.
I hate and despise lies, but I love Your law.
Seven times a day I praise You for Your right decisions.
Those who love Your law have great peace, and nothing makes them stumble.
I hope for Your rescue, the LORD, and I keep Your commands.
My whole being keeps Your rules; I love them very much.
I keep Your commands and rules because all my ways are before You.
Let my cry reach You, the LORD; give me understanding by Your word.
Let my prayer reach You; rescue me as You promised.
My lips pour out praise because You teach me Your rules.
My tongue sings about Your word because all Your commands are right.
Let Your hand be ready to help me, because I have chosen Your commands.
I long for Your rescue, the LORD, and Your law is my joy.
Let me live and praise You, and let Your rules help me.
I have wandered like a lost sheep; seek Your servant, for I do not forget Your commands.
In my trouble I called to the LORD, and He answered me.
Deliver my soul, the LORD, from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue.
What will be given to you, and what more will be done to you, you deceitful tongue?
Sharp arrows of a warrior, with burning coals of a broom bush.
Woe to me, for I live in Meshech; I stay among the tents of Kedar.
I have lived too long with people who hate peace.
I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war.
I look up to the hills. Where does my help come from?
My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
He won't let your foot slip. He who keeps you won't fall asleep.
See, the One who keeps Israel never slumbers or sleeps.
The LORD is your keeper. The LORD is your shade at your right hand.
The sun won't hurt you during the day, and the moon won't hurt you at night.
The LORD will keep you from all evil. He will keep your life safe.
The LORD will watch over your coming and going from now on and forever.
I was glad when they said to me, "Let's go to the house of the LORD."
Our feet are standing in your gates, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is built like a city that is joined together as one.
The tribes go up there—the tribes of the LORD—as a testimony for Israel, to give thanks to the name of the LORD.
There are thrones for judging there, the thrones of the house of David.
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: "May those who love you prosper.
May there be peace within your walls and safety within your palaces."
For the sake of my brothers and friends, I will say, "Peace be within you."
For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good.
A song of ascents. I lift my eyes to You, the One who sits in heaven.
Look, as servants look to their master's hand, and a servant girl looks to her mistress's hand, so our eyes look to the LORD our God until He shows us mercy.
Have mercy on us, O the LORD, have mercy on us, for we have had more than enough contempt.
We have had more than enough scorn from those who are carefree, and contempt from the proud.
If the LORD had not been on our side—let Israel say it now—
if the LORD had not been on our side when people rose up against us,
then they would have swallowed us alive when their anger flared against us.
Then the flood would have swept us away, and the rushing stream would have covered us.
Yes, the proud, raging waters would have swept over us.
Praise the LORD, who did not let our enemies devour us.
We have escaped like a bird from a hunter's trap. The trap is broken, and we have escaped.
Our help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.
Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion. It cannot be shaken, and it lasts forever.
Just as the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds His people now and forever.
The power of wicked people will not stay over the land given to good people, so good people won't be pushed to do wrong.
Do good, O the LORD, to those who are good and to those whose hearts are right.
But those who turn to crooked paths, the LORD will lead away with those who do evil. Peace be on Israel.
When the the LORD restored Zion, we felt like we were dreaming.
Then our mouths were filled with laughter, and our tongues with songs of joy. Then the nations said, "The LORD has done great things for them."
The LORD has done great things for us, and we are glad.
Bring back our people, the LORD, like rivers flowing through the desert.
Those who plant with tears will harvest with songs of joy.
The one who goes out crying, carrying seed to plant, will come home with songs of joy, carrying his bundles of grain.
Unless the LORD builds the house, the builders work for nothing. Unless the LORD guards the city, the guards watch for nothing.
It is useless for you to get up early and stay up late, working hard for food to eat, for He gives sleep to those He loves.
Children are a gift from the LORD. They are a reward from Him, the fruit of the womb.
Like arrows in a warrior's hand are children born in a man's youth.
Happy is the man whose quiver is full of them. They won't be put to shame when they argue with their enemies at the city gate.
Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD and follows His ways.
You will eat what your hands have worked for. You will be blessed, and things will go well for you.
Your wife will be like a fruitful grapevine inside your home. Your children will be like young olive trees around your table.
Look, this is how a man who fears the LORD is blessed.
The LORD will bless you from Zion. May you see good things in Jerusalem all the days of your life.
May you see your grandchildren. Peace be on Israel.
This is a song for going up to worship. Israel should say now,
"They hurt me badly since I was young. Yes, they hurt me badly since I was young, but they could not defeat me."
They beat me and cut deep wounds into my back.
But the LORD is good and fair, and He cut the ropes that held the wicked.
Let everyone who hates Zion be ashamed and turn back.
Let them be like grass on a roof that dries up before it can grow.
A harvester cannot fill his hand with it, and no one gathering sheaves can hold it in his arms.
Then no traveler will say, "The LORD bless you! We bless you in the name of the LORD!"
A Song of Ascents. Out of the depths I called to You, the LORD.
Lord, listen to my voice. Let Your ears pay close attention to my cries for help.
If You, the LORD, kept track of sins, Lord, who could stand?
But with You there is forgiveness, so that You may be revered.
I wait for the LORD; my soul waits, and I hope in His word.
My soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning—yes, more than watchmen wait for the morning.
Israel, hope in the LORD, for with the LORD there is faithful love, and with Him there is great rescue.
He will set Israel free from all his sins.
The LORD, my heart is not proud; my eyes are not lifted up in pride, and I do not walk in things too great or too wonderful for me.
Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a child who no longer nurses, resting with his mother; like that child is my soul within me.
Israel, hope in the LORD from this time on and forever.
The LORD, remember David and all his hardships.
He swore an oath to the the LORD; he made a vow to the Mighty One of Jacob:
"I will not go into my house or go to bed;
I will not let my eyes sleep or my eyelids close
until I find a place for the the LORD, a home for the Mighty One of Jacob."
We heard about it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.
Let us go to His dwelling; let us worship at His footstool.
Arise, the LORD, and go to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength.
May Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and may Your faithful people shout for joy.
For the sake of Your servant David, do not reject Your anointed king.
The the LORD made a faithful promise to David, and He will not break it: "I will place one of your descendants on your throne.
If your sons keep My covenant and the teachings I give them, their sons will also sit on your throne forever."
For the the LORD chose Zion; He wanted it for His home.
"This is My resting place forever; here I will live, because I wanted it.
I will richly bless her food; I will give her poor people enough bread.
I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her faithful people will shout for joy.
There I will make David's family strong; I have prepared a light for My anointed.
I will make his enemies ashamed, but his crown will flourish."
See how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in unity!
It is like fine oil poured on the head, running down on the beard, running down on Aaron's beard, down to the collar of his robes.
It is like the dew of Mount Hermon falling on Mount Zion. For there the LORD has commanded the blessing, life forevermore.
Look! Praise the LORD, all servants of the LORD who stand in the house of the LORD at night.
Lift up your hands in the holy place and bless the LORD.
The LORD, who made heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.
Praise the LORD! Praise the name of the LORD; praise Him, you servants of the LORD.
You who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God.
Praise the LORD, because the LORD is good; sing praises to His name, because it is pleasant.
For the LORD chose Jacob for Himself, Israel as His special treasure.
I know that the LORD is great, and our Lord is above all gods.
The LORD does whatever He pleases, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and all the deep places.
He makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings out the wind from His store rooms.
He struck down Egypt's firstborn, both people and animals.
He sent signs and wonders among you, O Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.
He struck down many nations and killed mighty kings:
Sihon, king of the Amorites; Og, king of Bashan; and all the kingdoms of Canaan.
He gave their land to His people Israel as their own.
The LORD, Your name lasts forever; Your fame, the LORD, lasts through all generations.
For the LORD will judge His people and show mercy to His servants.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, made by human hands.
They have mouths, but they do not speak; they have eyes, but they do not see.
They have ears, but they do not hear; there is no breath in their mouths.
Those who make them become like them, and so do all who trust in them.
House of Israel, bless the LORD! House of Aaron, bless the LORD!
House of Levi, bless the LORD! You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!
Blessed be the LORD from Zion, He who lives in Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to the God of gods, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who alone does great wonders, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who made the heavens with wisdom, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who spread out the earth above the waters, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who made the great lights, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who made the sun to rule by day, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who made the moon and stars to rule by night, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who struck down Egypt's firstborn, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who brought Israel out from among them, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who acted with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who divided the Red Sea in two, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who led Israel through the middle of it, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who swept Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who led His people through the wilderness, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who struck down great kings, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who killed mighty kings, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who defeated Og, king of Bashan, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who gave their land as an inheritance, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who gave that inheritance to Israel His servant, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who remembered us when we were in trouble, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who rescued us from our enemies, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to Him who gives food to all living things, for His faithful love lasts forever.
Give thanks to the God of heaven, for His faithful love lasts forever.
By the rivers of Babylon, we sat down and wept when we remembered Zion.
We hung our harps on the willow trees there.
Our captors asked us to sing, and our tormentors wanted us to be happy. They said, "Sing us one of the songs of Zion."
But how can we sing the the LORD's song in a foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, may I lose the use of my right hand.
May I lose my voice if I do not remember you, if I do not put Jerusalem above my greatest joy.
Remember, O the the LORD, what the sons of Edom did on the day Jerusalem fell. They said, "Tear it down! Tear it down to its foundations!"
O daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, happy is the one who pays you back for what you did to us.
Happy is the one who seizes your little ones and dashes them against the rocks.
I will give You thanks with all my heart. Before the gods I will sing Your praise.
I will bow down toward Your holy temple and give thanks to Your name for Your faithful love and Your truth. For You have raised Your name and Your word above all else.
On the day I called, You answered me. You strengthened me and filled me with courage.
All the kings of the earth will thank You, O the LORD, when they hear the words of Your mouth.
They will sing about the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.
Though the LORD is high above all, He cares for the lowly, but He sees the proud from far away.
Even when I walk through trouble, You keep me alive. You reach out Your hand against my angry enemies, and Your right hand saves me.
The LORD will finish what He has planned for me. O the LORD, Your faithful love lasts forever. Do not give up on the work of Your hands.
The LORD, You have searched me and know me.
You know when I sit down and when I get up. You understand my thoughts even from far away.
You see me when I go out and when I lie down. You are familiar with all my ways.
Before a word is on my tongue, You, the LORD, know all about it.
You are all around me, behind and before, and You have placed Your hand on me.
This knowledge is too amazing for me. It is too high for me to reach.
Where can I go from Your Spirit? Where can I run from Your presence?
If I go up to the heavens, You are there. If I make my bed in the place of the dead, You are there too.
If I fly with the wings of the morning or settle far across the sea,
even there Your hand will guide me, and Your right hand will hold me.
If I say, "Surely the darkness will hide me, and the light will become night around me,"
even the darkness is not dark to You. The night shines like the day, because darkness is like light to You.
You created my deepest self. You knit me together in my mother's womb.
I praise You because I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful, and I know that very well.
My body was not hidden from You when I was made in secret, when I was woven together deep in the earth.
Your eyes saw my unfinished form. All my days were written in Your book before even one of them happened.
How precious Your thoughts are to me, God! How great is the number of them!
If I tried to count them, they would be more than the grains of sand. When I wake up, I am still with You.
If only You, God, would kill the wicked! Get away from me, you bloodthirsty people!
They speak against You with evil plans. Your enemies misuse Your name for no good reason.
the LORD, do I not hate those who hate You? Do I not hate those who rise up against You?
I hate them completely. I count them as my enemies.
Search me, God, and know my heart. Test me and know my worried thoughts.
See if there is any hurtful way in me, and lead me in the way that lasts forever.
Rescue me, the LORD, from evil men; protect me from men of violence,
who plan evil in their hearts and stir up war all day long.
They sharpen their tongues like a snake; viper's venom is under their lips. Selah
Guard me, the LORD, from the hands of the wicked; protect me from men of violence who plan to make me stumble.
Proud men have hidden a trap for me; they have spread cords as a net along my path and set snares for me. Selah
I said to the LORD, “You are my God.” Hear my cry for mercy, the LORD.
the LORD, my Lord, You are my strong Savior; You shield my head in the day of battle.
Do not give the wicked what they want, the LORD; do not let their plans succeed, or they will become proud. Selah
May the heads of those who surround me be covered with the trouble their own lips have caused.
May burning coals fall on them; may they be thrown into the fire, into deep pits, never to rise again.
May slanderers not last in the land; may disaster hunt down men of violence.
I know that the LORD brings justice to the poor and stands up for the needy.
Surely the righteous will praise Your name; the upright will live in Your presence.
The LORD, I call to You; come quickly to me. Hear my voice when I call to You.
May my prayer be set before You like incense, and may my hands lifted up be like the evening sacrifice.
Set a guard, O the LORD, over my mouth; keep watch over my lips.
Do not let my heart turn to evil, or let me join evil people in doing wrong. Do not let me share their rich food.
Let a good person correct me; that is kindness. Let him rebuke me; it will be like oil soothing my head. My head will not refuse it. For my prayer is still against the deeds of evil people.
Their judges are thrown down from cliffs; they will hear my words, because they are pleasant.
As when someone plows and breaks up the ground, so our bones are scattered at the mouth of the grave.
But my eyes are fixed on You, O the LORD, my Lord; in You I take refuge. Do not leave my soul empty.
Keep me from the trap they set for me, and from the snares of evil people.
Let the wicked fall into their own nets, while I pass by safely.
A wise poem by David, when he was in the cave. A prayer. I cry out to the the LORD; I lift my voice to the the LORD and beg for mercy.
I pour out my complaint to Him; I tell Him my troubles.
When my spirit grows faint within me, You know my path. In the way I walk, they have hidden a trap for me.
Look to my right and see; no one is concerned for me. I have no refuge; no one cares for my life.
I cry to You, O the LORD; I say, "You are my refuge, my share among the living."
Listen to my cry, for I am very weak. Rescue me from those who chase me, for they are too strong for me.
Set me free from prison, so I can praise Your name. Then the righteous will gather around me because You have been good to me.
The LORD, hear my prayer; in Your faithfulness listen to my plea; in Your righteousness answer me.
Do not bring Your servant into judgment, for no one living is righteous before You.
For the enemy has pursued my soul; he has crushed my life to the ground; he has made me dwell in darkness like those long dead.
My spirit grows faint within me; my heart is dismayed within me.
I remember the days of old; I think about all Your works; I consider the work of Your hands.
I spread out my hands to You; my soul thirsts for You like a parched land. Selah.
Answer me quickly, the LORD; my spirit fails. Do not hide Your face from me, or I will be like those who go down to the pit.
Let me hear of Your faithful love in the morning, for I trust in You. Make me know the way I should go, for I lift up my soul to You.
Deliver me from my enemies, the LORD; I flee to You for refuge.
Teach me to do Your will, for You are my God. Let Your good Spirit lead me on level ground.
For Your name's sake, the LORD, revive me. In Your righteousness, bring my soul out of trouble.
In Your faithful love, cut off my enemies and destroy all who afflict my soul, for I am Your servant.
Blessed be the LORD, my Rock, who trains my hands for war and my fingers for battle.
He is my loving devotion and my fortress, my stronghold and my deliverer. He is my shield, and in Him I take refuge. He subdues my people under me.
The LORD, what is man, that You regard him? What is the son of man, that You think of him?
Man is like a breath; his days are like a passing shadow.
Part Your heavens, the LORD, and come down; touch the mountains so that they smoke.
Flash forth lightning and scatter them; shoot Your arrows and rout them.
Reach down from on high; rescue me and deliver me from the many waters, from the hand of foreigners,
whose mouths speak deceit and whose right hands are full of lies.
I will sing a new song to You, O God; on a ten-stringed harp I will make music to You—
to the One who gives victory to kings, who delivers His servant David from the deadly sword.
Rescue me and deliver me from the hand of foreigners, whose mouths speak deceit and whose right hands are full of lies.
Then our sons will be like well-grown plants, and our daughters like pillars carved to adorn a palace.
Our barns will be filled with every kind of produce. Our sheep will bring forth thousands and tens of thousands in our fields.
Our oxen will bear heavy loads. There will be no broken wall, no one carried away, and no cry of distress in our streets.
Blessed are the people who are in such a state; blessed are the people whose God is the LORD.
I will lift You up, my God and King; I will bless Your name forever and ever.
Every day I will bless You, and I will praise Your name forever and ever.
The LORD is great and greatly to be praised; His greatness cannot be measured.
One generation will praise Your works to the next, and will declare Your mighty acts.
I will speak of the glorious splendor of Your majesty, and of Your wonderful works.
People will speak of the power of Your awesome deeds, and I will declare Your greatness.
They will pour out the memory of Your great goodness, and will sing of Your righteousness.
The LORD is gracious and full of compassion, slow to anger and great in mercy.
The LORD is good to all, and His tender mercies are over all His works.
All Your works will praise You, the LORD, and Your faithful ones will bless You.
They will speak of the glory of Your kingdom, and talk of Your power,
to make known to the sons of men His mighty acts, and the glorious majesty of His kingdom.
Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and Your rule endures through all generations.
The LORD upholds all who fall, and raises up all who are bowed down.
The eyes of all look to You in hope, and You give them their food at the right time.
You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
The LORD is righteous in all His ways, and kind in all His works.
The LORD is near to all who call on Him, to all who call on Him in truth.
He will do what those who fear Him desire; He will hear their cry and save them.
The LORD watches over all who love Him, but all the wicked He will destroy.
My mouth will speak the praise of the LORD, and all flesh will bless His holy name forever and ever.
Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD, my soul.
I will praise the LORD as long as I live; I will sing to my God while I still have life.
Don't put your trust in princes, in human beings who cannot save.
When a person's breath leaves, they return to the dust; on that very day their plans come to nothing.
Blessed is the one whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God.
He made heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them. He remains faithful forever.
He upholds justice for the oppressed and gives food to the hungry. The LORD sets prisoners free.
The LORD opens the eyes of the blind; the LORD lifts up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.
The LORD watches over the foreigner; He sustains the fatherless and the widow, but He stops the wicked in their path.
The LORD will reign forever—your God, O Zion, for all generations. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! It is good to sing praises to our God, and it is pleasant and fitting to praise Him.
The LORD builds up Jerusalem and gathers the exiles of Israel.
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
He counts the stars and calls each one by name.
Great is our Lord and mighty in power; His understanding has no limit.
The LORD lifts up the humble and throws the wicked down to the ground.
Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make music to our God on the harp.
He covers the sky with clouds and sends rain to the earth. He makes grass grow on the hills.
He feeds the cattle and gives food to young ravens when they call.
He does not delight in the strength of a horse, and He does not take pleasure in a man’s strong legs.
The LORD delights in those who fear Him, in those who hope in His faithful love.
Praise the LORD, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion.
For He has strengthened the bars of your gates and blessed your children within you.
He makes peace within your borders and satisfies you with the finest wheat.
He sends His command to the earth, and His word runs swiftly.
He gives snow like wool and scatters frost like ashes.
He hurls down hail like pebbles. Who can stand against His freezing wind?
He sends His word and melts them; He stirs up His winds, and the waters flow.
He declares His word to Jacob and His laws and judgments to Israel.
He has not done this for any other nation; they do not know His judgments. Praise the LORD!
Hallelujah! Praise the the LORD from the heavens; praise Him in the heights.
Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His heavenly hosts.
Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all you shining stars.
Praise Him, highest heavens, and you waters above the skies.
Let them praise the name of the the LORD, for He commanded and they were created.
He established them forever and ever; He issued a decree that will never pass away.
Praise the the LORD from the earth, all great sea creatures and ocean depths,
lightning and hail, snow and clouds, powerful wind fulfilling His word,
mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars,
wild animals and all cattle, crawling creatures and flying birds,
kings of the earth and all nations, princes and all rulers of the earth,
young men and maidens, old and young alike.
Let them praise the name of the the LORD, for His name alone is exalted; His splendor is above the earth and the heavens.
He has given strength to His people, praise for all His saints, for the Israelites, a people near to Him. Hallelujah!
Hallelujah! Sing to the LORD a new song. Sing His praise among the faithful people gathered together.
Let Israel be glad in their Maker. Let the children of Zion rejoice in their King.
Let them praise His name with dancing. Let them sing to Him with tambourines and harps.
For the LORD is pleased with His people. He gives honor to the humble by saving them.
Let those who are faithful to Him shout for joy because of His glory. Let them sing for joy even on their beds.
May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a double-edged sword be in their hands.
They will carry out God’s judgment on the nations and punishment on the peoples.
They will bind their kings with chains and their nobles with iron shackles.
They will do the judgment written against them. This honor belongs to all who are faithful to Him. Hallelujah!
Praise the LORD! Praise God in His sanctuary; praise Him in His mighty heavens.
Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him for His excellent greatness.
Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet; praise Him with the harp and lyre.
Praise Him with the tambourine and dancing; praise Him with strings and flute.
Praise Him with sounding cymbals; praise Him with loud cymbals.
Let everything that has breath praise the LORD. Praise the LORD!
The proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel:
for gaining wisdom and instruction; for understanding words of insight;
for receiving instruction in wise living, in doing what is right, just, and fair;
for giving good sense to those who are simple, and knowledge and good judgment to the young;
let the wise listen and grow in learning, and let the discerning get guidance;
for understanding proverbs and parables, the sayings and riddles of the wise.
The fear of the the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Listen, my son, to your father's instruction and do not forsake your mother's teaching.
They are a garland to grace your head and a chain to adorn your neck.
My son, if sinful men try to lead you astray, do not go along with them.
If they say, "Come with us; let's wait to ambush someone and kill an innocent person for no reason,
let's swallow them alive, like the grave, and whole, like those who go down to the pit;
we will find all kinds of valuable things and fill our houses with stolen goods;
join us, and we will all share the money"—
my son, do not walk in their path; keep your feet from their way.
For their feet run to evil; they are quick to shed blood.
It is useless to spread a net where every bird can see it.
But these men set a trap for their own lives; they ambush only themselves.
Such is the end of everyone who chases dishonest gain; it takes the life of those who get it.
Wisdom calls out in the street; she raises her voice in the public squares.
She cries out at the busy corners; at the city gates she makes her speech:
"How long will you who are simple love your simple ways? How long will mockers enjoy mocking and fools hate knowledge?
Turn back at my warning! Then I will pour out my thoughts to you and make my words known to you.
But because you refused when I called and no one listened when I reached out my hand,
because you ignored all my advice and would not accept my warning,
I will laugh at your trouble; I will mock when terror strikes you—
when terror strikes you like a storm, when trouble comes on you like a whirlwind, when distress and hardship overwhelm you.
Then they will call to me, but I will not answer; they will look for me, but will not find me.
Because they hated knowledge and did not choose to fear the the LORD,
because they would not accept my advice and spurned my warning,
they will eat the fruit of their own ways and be filled with the results of their own plans.
For the stubbornness of the simple will kill them, and the overconfidence of fools will destroy them.
But whoever listens to me will live in safety and be at ease, without fear of harm."
My son, if you accept my words and store up my commands inside you,
turning your ear to wisdom and giving your heart to understanding—
yes, if you call out for insight and cry aloud for understanding,
and if you search for it like silver and hunt for it like hidden treasure,
then you will understand what it means to revere the the LORD, and you will find the knowledge of God.
For the the LORD gives wisdom; knowledge and understanding come from His mouth.
He stores up wise guidance for those who do right; He is a shield for people who live without blame.
He guards the paths of justice and protects the way of His faithful people.
Then you will understand what is right, fair, and just—every good path.
For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will bring joy to your soul.
Good judgment will protect you, and understanding will keep you safe.
Wisdom will save you from the ways of evil people, from those who speak twisted words,
who have left the straight path to walk in dark ways,
who enjoy doing wrong and celebrate twisted evil,
whose paths are crooked and whose ways are devious.
It will also save you from the wayward woman, from the smooth-talking woman who is unfaithful to her husband,
who has left the partner of her youth and forgotten the promise she made to her God.
Surely her house leads down to death, and her paths lead to the spirits of the dead.
None who go to her come back; they never reach the paths of life.
So you will walk in the ways of good people and keep to the paths of those who do right.
For those who do right will live in the land, and those without blame will stay in it;
but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and those who break faith will be uprooted from it.
My son, don't forget my teaching. Keep my commands in your heart.
They will add years to your life and bring you peace.
Don't let kindness and truth leave you. Tie them around your neck, and write them on your heart.
Then you will find favor and good understanding with God and people.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don't depend on your own understanding.
In everything you do, know Him, and He will make your paths straight.
Don't think you are wise on your own. Fear the LORD, and turn away from evil.
This will bring health to your body and strength to your bones.
Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the first part of all your crops.
Then your barns will be full, and your winepresses will overflow with new wine.
My son, don't reject the LORD's discipline, and don't get tired of His correction.
For the LORD corrects those He loves, just as a father corrects the son He delights in.
Happy is the person who finds wisdom and gains understanding.
Wisdom brings more profit than silver, and her gain is worth more than gold.
She is more precious than rubies. Nothing you want can compare with her.
She holds long life in her right hand, and riches and honor in her left.
Her ways are pleasant, and all her paths bring peace.
She is a tree of life to those who hold on to her. Those who keep her are happy.
The LORD used wisdom to lay the earth's foundation. He used understanding to set the heavens in place.
By His knowledge the deep waters burst forth, and the clouds drop dew.
My son, don't lose sight of these things. Guard good judgment and common sense.
They will give life to you and bring you favor.
Then you will walk safely, and your foot won't trip.
When you lie down, you won't be afraid, and your sleep will be sweet.
Don't be afraid of sudden danger or the ruin that comes on the wicked.
For the LORD will be your support, and He will keep your foot from being caught.
Don't hold back good from those who deserve it when you have the power to do it.
Don't tell your neighbor, "Go and come back tomorrow; I'll give it to you then," when you already have it with you.
Don't plan harm against your neighbor who lives safely beside you.
Don't argue with someone for no reason if he hasn't harmed you.
Don't envy a violent person, and don't choose any of his ways.
For the LORD hates dishonest people, but He shares His plans with those who do right.
The LORD's curse is on the wicked person's house, but He blesses the home of those who do right.
He mocks those who mock, but He gives grace to the humble.
Wise people will inherit honor, but fools will be covered with shame.
Listen, my sons, to your father's teaching. Pay close attention so you can understand.
I'm giving you good lessons, so don't give up my teaching.
When I was a boy, I was my father's son. I was young and the only child my mother had.
He taught me and said, "Hold on to my words with all your heart. Keep my commands, and you will live."
Get wisdom and get understanding. Don't forget them, and don't turn away from what I say.
Don't leave wisdom behind, and she will keep you safe. Love her, and she will guard you.
Wisdom is the most important thing, so get wisdom. With everything you gain, get understanding.
Value wisdom highly, and she will lift you up. She will honor you when you hold her close.
She will put a graceful garland on your head and give you a beautiful crown.
Listen to me, my son, and accept my words. Then you will live many years.
I've taught you the way of wisdom and led you on the path of what's right.
When you walk, nothing will slow you down. If you run, you will not trip.
Hold on to instruction and don't let go. Guard wisdom, because she is your life.
Don't go where wicked people go, and don't follow the path of those who do wrong.
Stay away from it. Don't even go near it. Turn from it and keep moving.
Wicked people can't sleep unless they've done something wrong. They lose sleep unless they make someone fall.
They feed on evil and drink in violence.
But the path of those who do right shines like the morning light. It grows brighter until the day is fully here.
The way of wicked people is like deep darkness. They don't even know what makes them stumble.
My son, listen to my words. Pay attention to what I say.
Don't let them get away from you. Keep them in your heart.
They bring life to everyone who finds them and healing to the whole body.
Guard your heart more than anything else, because everything in life flows from it.
Keep dishonest talk far from you, and keep sly words far from you.
Look straight ahead, and keep your eyes focused on what's in front of you.
Think carefully about where you step, and then everything you do will be steady.
Don't turn to the right or the left. Keep your foot away from evil.
My son, pay attention to my wisdom; turn your ear to my understanding.
So your lips may keep knowledge.
For the lips of a forbidden woman drip honey, and her speech is smoother than oil.
But in the end she is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword.
Her feet go down to death; her steps lead straight to the grave.
She does not think about the path of life; she does not know that her ways are unsteady.
So now, my sons, listen to me, and do not turn aside from the words of my mouth.
Keep your path far from her; do not go near the door of her house,
or you will give your strength to others, and your years to a cruel man.
Strangers will feast on your wealth, and your hard work will enrich a stranger’s house.
At the end of your life you will groan when your flesh and body are spent.
And you will say, “How I hated discipline, and my heart despised correction!
I did not listen to my teachers, or turn my ear to my instructors.
I was almost ruined among the whole crowd.”
Drink water from your own cistern, and running water from your own well.
Should your springs overflow into the streets, streams of water in the public squares?
Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers.
May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth:
a loving doe, a graceful deer— may her breasts satisfy you always; may you be captivated by her love forever.
Why be captivated, my son, by an adulteress, or embrace the bosom of a stranger?
For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD watches all his paths.
The sins of the wicked trap him; the cords of his sin entangle him.
He dies for lack of discipline, led astray by his own great folly.
My son, if you have promised to pay someone else's debt for your neighbor, or given your word with a handshake to guarantee a stranger's loan,
you are trapped by your own words; you are caught by what you said.
Do this now, my son, to free yourself, because you have put yourself in your neighbor's power: go and humble yourself, and beg your neighbor to let you go.
Do not let your eyes sleep, or your eyelids close.
Free yourself like a deer from a hunter's hand, like a bird from a birdcatcher's trap.
Go to the ant, you lazy person; watch its ways and be wise.
It has no boss, officer, or ruler,
yet it gets its food ready in summer and gathers its supplies at harvest time.
How long will you stay in bed, lazy person? When will you get up from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
and poverty will sneak up on you like a thief, and need like an armed robber.
A worthless person, a wicked man, goes around with crooked talk,
winking with his eyes, shuffling his feet, and pointing with his fingers,
with evil plans in his heart, always stirring up trouble and spreading arguments.
So disaster will hit him suddenly; in an instant he will be broken, with no cure.
There are six things the the LORD hates, seven that disgust Him:
proud eyes, a lying tongue, hands that kill innocent people,
a heart that plans evil, feet that rush to do wrong,
a false witness who breathes out lies, and a person who starts fights among brothers.
My son, obey your father's command, and don't ignore your mother's teaching.
Keep them close to your heart always; tie them around your neck.
When you walk, they will guide you; when you sleep, they will protect you; and when you wake, they will talk with you.
For the command is a lamp, the teaching is a light, and the correction that trains you is the way to life.
They will protect you from an immoral woman and from the smooth talk of a wayward wife.
Do not desire her beauty in your heart, and do not let her eyes capture you.
A prostitute can be bought for a loaf of bread, but an adulteress hunts for a man's life.
Can a man carry fire in his lap without his clothes burning?
Can a man walk on hot coals without his feet getting burned?
So is the man who sleeps with another man's wife; no one who touches her will go unpunished.
People don't look down on a thief who steals to fill his stomach.
But if he is caught, he must pay back seven times and give everything in his house.
The man who commits adultery has no sense; he destroys himself.
He will get wounds and shame, and his disgrace will not be erased.
For jealousy makes a husband furious, and he will show no mercy when he takes revenge.
He will not accept any payment, and no amount of money will calm him down.
My son, keep my words, and store my commands with you.
Keep my commands and live; let my teaching be as precious to you as your own eyesight.
Tie them on your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
Say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and call understanding your close friend.
They will keep you from the forbidden woman, from the stranger who flatters with her words.
For at the window of my house I looked out through my lattice,
and I saw among the naive. I noticed among the youths a young man without sense.
He was passing through the street near her corner, taking the road to her house
in the twilight, in the evening, in the dark of night.
And there was a woman coming to meet him, dressed like a prostitute, with a cunning heart.
She is loud and stubborn; her feet do not stay at home.
Now she is in the street, now in the squares; she waits at every corner.
She grabbed him and kissed him; with a bold face she said to him:
"I have peace offerings; today I paid my vows.
So I came out to meet you, to look for you, and I found you.
I have spread my bed with coverings, colored linens from Egypt.
I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Come, let us drink our fill of love until morning; let us delight ourselves with love.
For the man is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.
He took a bag of money with him; he will be home on the day of the full moon."
With her many words she persuades him; with her smooth talk she leads him astray.
He follows her at once, like an ox going to slaughter, like a deer stepping into a trap.
An arrow pierces his liver. He is like a bird rushing into a snare, not knowing it will cost him his life.
Now then, my sons, listen to me, and pay attention to my words.
Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her paths.
For many are the victims she has brought down, and strong men are among her slain.
Her house is a road to the grave, leading down to the rooms of death.
Does not Wisdom call out? Does not Understanding raise her voice?
She stands on the high places along the road, at the crossroads.
Beside the city gates, at the entrance, she cries out:
“To you, I call out, and my voice is for everyone.
Simple ones, learn to be wise; fools, gain understanding.
Listen, because I speak noble things, and my lips say what is right.
My mouth speaks truth, and wickedness is hateful to my lips.
All my words are right; none are twisted or crooked.
They are clear to anyone who understands, and right to those who find knowledge.”
