Receive my teaching instead of silver, and knowledge instead of fine gold.
Wisdom is better than rubies, and nothing anyone desires compares with her.
I, Wisdom, live with Prudence, and I find knowledge and good judgment.
To fear the the LORD is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogance, the evil way, and crooked speech.
I have good advice and sound judgment; I have understanding and strength.
By me kings rule, and rulers make just laws.
By me princes govern, and nobles judge with justice.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me early find me.
With me are riches and honor, lasting wealth and righteousness.
My fruit is better than gold, even pure gold, and what I produce is better than silver.
I walk in the way of righteousness, along the paths of justice.
I give wealth to those who love me and fill their treasuries.
The The LORD possessed me at the beginning of His work, before His deeds of old.
I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth began.
When there were no depths, I was born; when there were no springs heavy with water.
Before the mountains were settled and before the hills, I was born.
Before He made the earth and its fields, or the first dust of the world.
I was there when He established the heavens and drew a circle on the face of the deep.
When He made the clouds above and made the springs of the deep strong.
When He set a boundary for the sea so its waters would not cross His command, and when He laid the earth’s foundations.
Then I was beside Him like a skilled worker, and I was His delight day by day, rejoicing before Him at all times.
I rejoiced in His whole world and delighted in people.
Now, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it.
Blessed is the person who listens to me, watching daily at my doors and waiting at my doorway.
For whoever finds me finds life and receives favor from the the LORD.
But whoever sins against me harms himself; all who hate me love death.
Wisdom has built her house and carved out seven pillars.
She has prepared her meat and mixed her wine, and she has set her table.
She has sent out her young women, and she calls from the highest points of the city.
"Whoever is simple, come in here!" she says to him who lacks understanding.
"Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.
Leave your foolish ways and live, and walk in the path of understanding."
Anyone who corrects a mocker brings shame on himself, and anyone who rebukes a wicked person gets a stain.
Do not correct a mocker, or he will hate you; correct a wise person, and he will love you.
Teach a wise person, and he will become wiser; let a righteous person know, and he will add to his learning.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
For by me your days will be multiplied, and years of life will be added to you.
If you are wise, you are wise for yourself, and if you scoff, you will bear it alone.
A foolish woman is loud; she is simple and knows nothing.
She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,
to call to those who pass by, who go straight on their ways.
"Whoever is simple, come in here!" she says to him who lacks understanding.
"Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant."
But he does not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of the grave.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.
Treasures gained by wrong do no good, but doing right saves from death.
The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but He blocks the wicked from getting what they crave.
Lazy hands lead to poverty, but hard work brings wealth.
A son who gathers crops in summer is wise, but a son who sleeps during harvest brings shame.
Blessings rest on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked hides violence.
The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
A wise heart accepts commands, but a fool who talks too much comes to ruin.
Whoever walks with honesty walks safely, but whoever twists his ways will be found out.
A person who winks to plot trouble brings grief, and a fool who talks too much comes to ruin.
The mouth of the righteous is a spring of life, but the mouth of the wicked hides violence.
Hatred stirs up fights, but love covers all wrongs.
Wisdom is found on the lips of the wise, but a rod is for the back of one who lacks sense.
Wise people store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool brings ruin near.
The rich person's wealth is his strong city, but poverty ruins the poor.
The work of the righteous leads to life, but the gain of the wicked leads to sin.
Whoever listens to correction stays on the path to life, but whoever ignores correction goes astray.
Whoever hides hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads slander is a fool.
When words are many, sin is not far away, but whoever holds back his words is wise.
The tongue of the righteous is like fine silver, but the heart of the wicked is worth little.
The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of sense.
The blessing of the LORD brings wealth, and He adds no sorrow to it.
A fool enjoys wicked plans, but a person of understanding delights in wisdom.
What the wicked fear will come to them, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
When the storm passes, the wicked are gone, but the righteous have a lasting foundation.
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is a lazy person to those who send him.
The fear of the LORD adds days to life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.
The hope of the righteous brings joy, but the hope of the wicked will come to nothing.
The way of the LORD is a safe place for the blameless, but it brings ruin to those who do wrong.
The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not live in the land.
The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a twisted tongue will be cut off.
The lips of the righteous know what is pleasing, but the mouth of the wicked speaks twisted things.
The LORD hates dishonest scales, but accurate weights please Him.
When pride comes, disgrace follows, but wisdom comes with humility.
The honesty of good people guides them, but the crookedness of faithless people destroys them.
Riches do not help on the day of anger, but doing right saves from death.
The right living of the blameless keeps them on the right path, but the wicked fall because of their own evil.
The right living of good people saves them, but treacherous people get caught in their own desires.
When a wicked person dies, his hope dies with him, and all hope in his strength is gone.
Good people are rescued from trouble, but trouble comes to the wicked.
A godless person ruins his neighbor with his mouth, but good people are saved through knowledge.
When good people thrive, a city celebrates; when wicked people die, people shout for joy.
A city is lifted up by the blessing of good people, but it is destroyed by the mouth of the wicked.
Anyone who looks down on his neighbor lacks good judgment, but a person with understanding stays quiet.
A gossip spreads secrets, but a trustworthy person keeps them.
Without good advice a nation falls, but with many advisers there is safety.
Whoever guarantees a stranger's debt will surely suffer, but whoever refuses to make such promises is safe.
A kind woman gains honor, but ruthless men gain wealth.
A person who is kind helps himself, but a cruel person brings trouble on himself.
A wicked person earns empty pay, but whoever lives right reaps a true reward.
True goodness leads to life, but chasing evil leads to death.
The LORD hates twisted hearts, but He delights in those whose ways are blameless.
You can be sure the wicked will not escape punishment, but the children of good people will be saved.
Like a gold ring in a pig's nose is a beautiful woman without good sense.
The desires of good people lead only to good, but the hope of the wicked brings trouble.
One person gives freely and gains even more; another holds back what is right and ends up poor.
A generous person will prosper, and whoever refreshes others will be refreshed.
People curse the one who hoards grain, but blessing crowns the one who sells it.
Whoever looks for good finds favor, but trouble comes to whoever looks for evil.
Whoever trusts in riches will fall, but good people will thrive like green leaves.
Whoever brings trouble on his family will end up with nothing, and the fool will serve the wise in heart.
The fruit of good people is a tree of life, and whoever wins people is wise.
If good people are repaid on earth, how much more will the ungodly and the sinner!
Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is stupid.
A good man wins favor from the the LORD, but the the LORD condemns a man of evil plans.
No one is made secure by wickedness, but the righteous won't be moved.
A wife of noble character is her husband's crown, but a shameful wife is like rot in his bones.
The plans of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.
The words of wicked people set traps to harm others, but the speech of honest people rescues them.
The wicked are overthrown and are no more, but the house of the righteous stands firm.
A person is praised for his wisdom, but a twisted heart is despised.
It is better to be lightly regarded and have a servant than to act important and have no food.
A righteous person cares about the life of his animal, but the kindness of wicked people is cruel.
Whoever works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases empty dreams lacks good sense.
The wicked want the loot of evil men, but the roots of the righteous grow strong.
An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes trouble.
A person is filled with good things from the fruit of his mouth, and the work of his hands comes back to him.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but a wise man listens to advice.
A fool shows his anger right away, but a wise person ignores an insult.
A person who speaks truth tells what is right, but a false witness speaks deceit.
Careless words stab like a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
Truthful lips last forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
Deceit is in the hearts of those who plan evil, but those who advise peace have joy.
No harm comes to the righteous, but wicked people are filled with trouble.
Lying lips are disgusting to the the LORD, but those who act faithfully are the the LORD's delight.
A careful person keeps knowledge to himself, but the heart of fools proclaims foolishness.
Hardworking hands will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.
Anxiety weighs down the heart, but a kind word cheers it up.
The righteous choose their friends carefully, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
A lazy person does not roast his game, but a hardworking person values his possessions.
In the path of righteousness there is life, and along that way there is no death.
A wise son listens to his father's teaching, but a mocker ignores correction.
A man is rewarded by the good things he says, but people who betray others crave violence.
The person who watches his words protects his life, but someone who talks too much brings trouble on himself.
A lazy person wants things but gets nothing, while a hard worker is well fed.
A good person hates lies, but an evil person brings shame and disgrace.
Righteousness protects the honest person's path, but wickedness trips up the sinner.
Some people pretend to be rich but have nothing, while others pretend to be poor but are very wealthy.
A person's wealth can save his life, but a poor person hears no threat.
The light of good people brings joy, but the lamp of the wicked goes out.
Pride only causes fights, but wisdom belongs to those who take advice.
Money gained quickly shrinks, but money gathered little by little grows.
Hope that is delayed makes the heart sick, but a desire that comes true brings life.
A person who ignores good advice brings trouble on himself, but one who respects commands will be rewarded.
The teaching of a wise person is a fountain of life, turning people away from deadly traps.
Good judgment brings favor, but the path of traitors is rough.
A wise person acts with knowledge, but a fool shows his foolishness.
A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful messenger brings healing.
Poverty and disgrace come to those who ignore instruction, but those who listen to correction are honored.
A fulfilled desire is sweet to the soul, but fools hate turning away from evil.
Whoever walks with wise people becomes wise, but a companion of fools will be harmed.
Trouble chases sinners, but good people are rewarded with good.
A good person leaves an inheritance to his grandchildren, but a sinner's wealth is stored up for the righteous.
A poor person's field can produce plenty of food, but injustice sweeps it away.
Whoever spares the rod hates his son, but the one who loves him disciplines him.
A good person eats enough to satisfy himself, but the wicked person goes hungry.
The wise woman builds her house, but the foolish woman tears it down with her own hands.
Whoever walks uprightly fears the LORD, but whoever is crooked in his ways despises Him.
A fool's proud talk brings punishment, but wise lips protect them.
Without oxen, the feeding trough stays empty, but a strong ox brings a big harvest.
A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.
A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
Stay away from a fool, for you will not find knowledge on his lips.
A careful person understands his own path, but a fool is tricked by his own foolishness.
Fools laugh at guilt, but the upright find favor.
The heart knows its own pain, and no outsider can share its joy.
The home of the wicked will be destroyed, but the home of the upright will prosper.
There is a way that seems right to a person, but its end is the way of death.
Even in laughter, the heart may ache, and joy may end in grief.
A person who turns away in heart will get the results of his own choices, but a good person will be rewarded from above.
A simple person believes everything, but a wise person thinks about his next step.
A wise person is careful and stays away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.
A hot-tempered person acts foolishly, and a person who plots evil is hated.
Simple people end up with foolishness, but wise people are crowned with knowledge.
Evil people will bow before good people, and the wicked will bow at the gates of the righteous.
A poor person is disliked even by his neighbor, but a rich person has many friends.
Anyone who looks down on his neighbor sins, but the one who is kind to the poor is blessed.
Don't those who plan evil go the wrong way? But those who plan good find love and faithfulness.
Hard work brings profit, but empty talk leads only to poverty.
The wise are crowned with wealth, but fools are crowned with foolishness.
A truthful witness saves lives, but a lying witness spreads deceit.
Fearing the LORD brings strong confidence, and his children will have a safe place.
Fearing the LORD is a fountain of life that turns a person away from deadly traps.
A large population brings glory to a king, but a lack of people ruins a prince.
A person who is slow to anger has great understanding, but a quick-tempered person shows foolishness.
A peaceful heart brings life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.
The wicked are brought down by their own trouble, but the righteous find refuge even in death.
Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, but it is known even among fools.
Doing what is right lifts up a nation, but sin brings shame to any people.
A king favors a servant who acts wisely, but he is angry with one who brings shame.
A gentle reply calms anger, but a harsh word stirs it up.
Wise people's words share knowledge, but fools' mouths pour out foolishness.
The LORD's eyes are everywhere, watching both evil and good.
A gentle tongue is a tree of life, but twisted words break the spirit.
A fool rejects his father's discipline, but a person who listens to correction is wise.
The righteous person's house holds great wealth, but the wicked's earnings bring trouble.
Wise people's lips spread knowledge, but fools' hearts do not.
The LORD finds the sacrifices of the wicked disgusting, but He delights in the prayers of the upright.
The LORD hates the way of the wicked, but He loves those who chase after what is right.
There is severe discipline for anyone who leaves the right path; whoever hates correction will die.
Death and the grave are open before the LORD; how much more people's hearts!
A mocker does not like to be corrected; he will not go to the wise.
A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but sorrow of heart crushes the spirit.
A wise heart seeks knowledge, but fools feed on foolishness.
All the days of the poor are hard, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.
Better a little with fear of the LORD than great treasure with trouble.
Better a dish of vegetables where love is than a fattened ox with hatred.
An angry person stirs up arguments, but a patient person calms quarrels.
The path of the lazy is like a hedge of thorns, but the way of the upright is a highway.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish person despises his mother.
Folly brings joy to a person without sense, but a person of understanding walks straight.
Plans fail without advice, but with many counselors they succeed.
A person finds joy in a fitting answer, and a word at the right time—how good it is!
The path of life leads upward for the wise, so they may turn away from the grave below.
The LORD tears down the proud person's house, but He sets the widow's boundary firm.
The LORD hates the thoughts of the wicked, but gracious words are pure.
A greedy person troubles his own home, but whoever hates bribes will live.
The heart of the righteous thinks carefully before answering, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil.
The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayers of the righteous.
The light of the eyes brings joy to the heart, and good news strengthens the bones.
An ear that listens to life-giving correction will live among the wise.
Whoever ignores instruction despises himself, but whoever listens to correction gains understanding.
The fear of the LORD teaches wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
People may plan what they want to say, but the answer comes from the LORD.
People often think their own ways are right, but the LORD looks at what is in their hearts.
Give your work to the LORD, and He will make your plans succeed.
The LORD made everything for a reason, even wicked people for a day of trouble.
The LORD hates a proud heart, and a proud person will not go unpunished.
Love and truth can cover sin, and respect for the LORD turns a person away from evil.
When a person's ways please the LORD, even his enemies will be at peace with him.
It is better to have a little with what is right than great wealth gained unfairly.
People plan their path, but the LORD decides their steps.
A king's words carry great weight, and he will not be wrong in judgment.
Honest scales and balances belong to the LORD, and all the weights are His work.
It is wrong for kings to do evil, because a throne is built on doing what is right.
Kings delight in honest words, and they love those who speak the truth.
A king's anger is like a messenger of death, but a wise person can calm it.
A king's smile brings life, and his favor is like refreshing rain.
Getting wisdom is better than getting gold, and choosing understanding is better than silver.
The path of good people turns away from evil, and those who guard their way protect their lives.
Pride comes before ruin, and a proud spirit comes before a fall.
It is better to be humble among poor people than to share stolen goods with the proud.
A person who thinks carefully about a matter will find good, and blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD.
A wise person is called understanding, and pleasant words add to learning.
Understanding is a source of life to those who have it, but fools suffer because of their own foolishness.
A wise person's heart guides his mouth, and his words add to learning.
Pleasant words are like honey, sweet to the soul and healing to the body.
There is a way that looks right to a person, but it leads to death.
A worker's hunger drives him to work hard.
A worthless person digs up trouble, and his words burn like fire.
A twisted person stirs up fights, and a gossip separates close friends.
A violent person tricks his neighbor and leads him down a bad path.
Someone who narrows his eyes to plan evil and tightens his lips to cause harm is plotting trouble.
Gray hair is a crown of glory when it is found in a life of doing right.
Being slow to anger is better than being a strong warrior, and controlling your spirit is better than capturing a city.
People cast lots to decide things, but the LORD controls how they fall.
Better a dry crust with peace and quiet than a house full of feasting with strife.
A wise servant will rule over a shameful son and share the inheritance with the brothers.
A crucible is for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD tests the heart.
A wicked man listens to evil lips; a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue.
Whoever mocks the poor shows contempt for their Maker; whoever rejoices at disaster will not go unpunished.
Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of children is their fathers.
Smooth words don't fit a fool; lying words are even worse for a noble person.
A bribe is like a lucky charm to the one who gives it; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but whoever repeats a matter separates close friends.
A rebuke goes deeper into a person of understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.
An evil person seeks only rebellion, so a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool lost in his folly.
If anyone repays evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
Starting a quarrel is like letting water break through a dam; so drop the matter before a fight breaks out.
Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent—both are detestable to the LORD.
Why should a fool have money in hand to buy wisdom when he has no sense?
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for trouble.
A person lacking judgment shakes hands in pledge and puts up security for his neighbor.
Whoever loves sin loves strife; whoever builds his gate high invites destruction.
A person with a crooked heart will not prosper; one with a deceitful tongue will bring him down.
Whoever fathers a fool brings grief; the father of a fool has no joy.
A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
A wicked man accepts a bribe in secret to twist the course of justice.
Wisdom is the goal of the discerning, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to his mother.
It is not good to punish an innocent person or to flog nobles for their honesty.
A person of knowledge restrains his words, and a person of understanding stays calm.
Even a fool is thought wise if he keeps silent; he seems discerning if he holds his tongue.
A person who keeps to himself chases his own desires and fights against wise advice.
A fool doesn't care about understanding; he only wants to share his own opinions.
A wicked person brings contempt, and shame and disgrace follow him.
A person's words are like deep water, and wisdom flows from him like a bubbling stream.
It's not right to favor a wicked person or to deny justice to a good person.
A fool's words start fights, and his mouth asks for a beating.
A fool's mouth brings his ruin, and his words trap his life.
A gossip's words taste like a tasty treat, but they sink deep into a person's heart.
A lazy worker is no better than someone who destroys.
The name of the LORD is a strong tower; righteous people run to it and are safe.
A rich person's money is like a strong city to him; he imagines it protects him like a high wall.
Pride leads to ruin, but humility leads to honor.
Answering before listening is foolish and shameful.
A person's spirit can endure sickness, but a crushed spirit is too heavy to bear.
A smart person wants to learn, and a wise person listens to learn more.
A gift can open doors for a person and bring him before important people.
The first person to tell his side sounds right until someone else questions him.
Drawing lots can end an argument and settle things between strong opponents.
An offended brother is harder to win over than a walled city, and arguments are like strong castle bars.
A person's words can fill his stomach; what he says can bring satisfaction.
The tongue has power over life and death; those who love to talk will live with the results.
A man who finds a wife finds something good and receives favor from the LORD.
A poor person begs for mercy, but a rich person answers harshly.
A person with many friends may still be ruined, but a true friend sticks closer than a brother.
Better a poor person who walks in honesty than a fool whose lips are crooked.
Even eagerness is no good without knowledge, and a person who rushes into things sins.
A person's own foolishness ruins his way, yet his heart is angry with the LORD.
Wealth brings many friends, but a poor person is deserted by his friend.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and a person who breathes out lies will not escape.
Many seek the favor of a leader, and everyone is a friend to a person who gives gifts.
All a poor person's relatives turn against him; how much more will his friends leave him! He begs them, but they are gone.
Whoever gains wisdom loves his own life; whoever keeps understanding will find good.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and a person who breathes out lies will perish.
It is not fitting for a fool to live in luxury—how much less for a servant to rule over princes!
A person's good sense makes him slow to anger, and it is his glory to overlook an offense.
A king's anger is like a lion's roar, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
A foolish son is his father's ruin, and a nagging wife is like a constant drip.
Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a wise wife is from the LORD.
Laziness brings deep sleep, and an idle person will go hungry.
Whoever keeps a command keeps his life, but whoever is careless in his ways will die.
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and He will repay him for what he has done.
Discipline your son, for there is hope; do not be a party to his death.
A hot-tempered person must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will only have to do it again.
Listen to advice and accept discipline, so that you may be wise for the rest of your days.
Many are the plans in a person's heart, but the counsel of the LORD will stand.
What a person wants is kindness, and a poor person is better than a liar.
The fear of the LORD leads to life, so one may sleep satisfied and untouched by evil.
A lazy person buries his hand in the dish, but he will not even bring it back to his mouth.
Strike a mocker, and the simple will learn good sense; rebuke a wise person, and he will gain knowledge.
A son who robs his father and drives out his mother brings shame and disgrace.
My son, if you stop listening to instruction, you will stray from words of knowledge.
A worthless witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked swallows sin.
Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
Wine makes people act like fools, and strong drink starts fights. Anyone led astray by them isn't wise.
A king's anger is like a lion's roar. Anyone who makes him angry risks his own life.
It's honorable to stay away from a fight, but every fool starts one.
A lazy person doesn't plow when it's time, so at harvest he begs and has nothing.
Advice hidden in a person's heart is like deep water, but someone with understanding can draw it out.
Many people say they are loyal, but who can find a truly faithful person?
A good person who lives with integrity—his children are blessed after him.
A king who sits on the throne of justice sees through all evil.
Who can say, "I have kept my heart pure; I am clean from sin"?
The LORD hates dishonest weights and measures.
Even a child is known by what he does, whether his actions are pure and right.
The LORD made both the ear that hears and the eye that sees.
Don't love sleep, or you'll become poor. Open your eyes, and you'll have enough food.
The buyer says, "It's no good, it's no good," but after he leaves, he brags about the deal.
There may be gold and plenty of pearls, but wise words are the most precious treasure.
If someone guarantees a stranger's debt, take his coat as security. If he does it for a foreigner, get security from him.
Food gained by lying tastes sweet at first, but later it fills his mouth with gravel.
Plans are made firm by good advice, and wise guidance wins wars.
A gossip reveals secrets, so don't associate with someone who can't keep his mouth shut.
If someone curses his father or mother, his future will be snuffed out in darkness.
An inheritance grabbed too quickly at first won't be blessed in the end.
Don't say, "I'll get even for the wrong done to me." Wait for the LORD, and He will rescue you.
The LORD hates dishonest weights, and false scales are wrong.
The LORD directs a person's steps, so how can anyone understand his own way?
It's a trap to dedicate something to God without thinking, and only reconsider it after making the promise.
A wise king sorts out the wicked and crushes them.
A person's spirit is the LORD's lamp, searching his deepest thoughts.
Love and faithfulness protect a king, and love keeps his throne secure.
Young men are proud of their strength, but old men are honored by their gray hair.
Painful wounds can cleanse away evil, and beatings reach a person's deepest thoughts.
A king’s heart is like a stream of water in the hand of the the LORD. He turns it wherever He wants.
Every person thinks his own way is right, but the LORD weighs the heart.
Doing what is right and fair is more pleasing to the LORD than offering a sacrifice.
Proud looks and a proud heart are the lamp of the wicked, and that is sin.
The plans of the diligent bring profit, but everyone who rushes comes to poverty.
Wealth gained by lying is like a mist that disappears, and it brings death.
The violence of the wicked will sweep them away, because they refuse to do what is just.
The way of the guilty is crooked, but the conduct of the pure is upright.
It is better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
The soul of the wicked craves evil, and his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.
When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; and when a wise man is instructed, he gains knowledge.
The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin.
Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor will also cry out and not be answered.
A gift given in secret soothes anger, and a bribe in the pocket calms great wrath.
Justice done brings joy to the righteous, but terror to evildoers.
The man who strays from the path of understanding will rest among the dead.
He who loves pleasure will become poor; whoever loves wine and oil will not become rich.
The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous for the upright.
It is better to live in the desert than with a quarrelsome and ill-tempered wife.
Precious treasure and oil are in the home of the wise, but a foolish man uses them up.
He who pursues righteousness and faithful love finds life, righteousness, and honor.
A wise man climbs the city of the mighty and brings down the stronghold they trust in.
He who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from trouble.
Mocker is the name of the proud and arrogant man who acts with bursts of pride.
The craving of the lazy man kills him, because his hands refuse to work.
All day long he wants more, but the righteous give without holding back.
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable—how much more when it is brought with evil intent!
A false witness will perish, but the man who listens will speak forever.
A wicked man puts on a bold face, but the upright man considers his ways.
There is no wisdom, no understanding, and no counsel that can stand against the LORD.
A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory comes from the LORD.
A good name is better than great wealth, and being well liked is better than silver and gold.
Rich and poor meet together; the LORD makes them all.
A prudent person sees trouble and hides, but simple people keep going and are punished.
The reward of humility and fear of the LORD is wealth, honor, and life.
Thorns and traps lie on the path of the crooked; whoever guards his life stays far from them.
Train up a child in the way he should go, and even when he is old he will not turn from it.
The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is a slave to the lender.
Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble, and the rod of his anger will fail.
A generous person will be blessed, because he shares his bread with the poor.
Drive out the mocker, and fighting will leave; yes, arguing and shame will stop.
Whoever loves a pure heart and speaks with grace will have the king as a friend.
The LORD's eyes watch over knowledge, but He overturns the words of the treacherous.
The lazy person says, "There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!"
The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; a person cursed by the LORD falls into it.
Foolishness is tied to a child's heart, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
Whoever oppresses the poor to get richer, or gives to the rich, will surely come to poverty.
Turn your ear and hear the words of the wise, and set your heart on my knowledge.
For it is pleasant if you keep them inside you; let them be fixed together on your lips.
So that your trust may be in the LORD, I have made them known to you today, yes, even to you.
Have I not written to you excellent sayings of counsel and knowledge?
I did this to make you know the truth of true words, so that you may bring back true words to those who sent you.
Do not rob the poor because he is poor, and do not crush the needy at the city gate.
For the LORD will defend their case and take the life of those who rob them.
Do not be friends with a hot-tempered man, and do not go with a man who is easily angered.
You may learn his ways and get a trap for your own life.
Do not be one of those who shake hands in pledge or put up security for debts.
If you have nothing to pay with, why should they take even your bed from under you?
Do not move an old boundary stone that your fathers set up.
Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will stand before kings; he will not stand before lowly men.
When you sit down to eat with a ruler, pay close attention to what is in front of you.
If you have a big appetite, be very careful not to overeat.
Do not long for his rich food, for it can fool you.
Do not wear yourself out trying to get rich; be wise enough to stop.
When you look at wealth, it can disappear. It seems to grow wings and fly away like an eagle.
Do not eat with someone who is stingy, and do not crave his rich food.
He is the kind of person who keeps track of every bite. He says, “Eat and drink,” but he does not really care about you.
You will throw up the food you ate, and your kind words will be wasted.
Do not speak to a fool, for he will laugh at your wise words.
Do not move an old boundary stone, and do not take over the fields of orphans.
Their Redeemer is strong, and He will take up their case against you.
Give your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge.
Do not refuse to discipline a child. If you discipline him with a rod, he will not die.
You may strike him with a rod and save his life from the grave.
My son, if your heart is wise, my heart will be glad.
My whole heart will rejoice when you speak what is right.
Do not envy sinners in your heart, but keep on living in fear of the LORD all day long.
Surely there is a future for you, and your hope will not be taken away.
Listen, my son, and be wise, and guide your heart on the right path.
Do not spend time with people who drink too much wine or eat too much food.
Drunkards and gluttons become poor, and laziness leaves them in rags.
Listen to your father, who gave you life, and do not look down on your mother when she is old.
Buy the truth and do not sell it. Get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
The father of a righteous child will be very glad, and the one who has a wise son will delight in him.
May your father and mother be glad, and may the one who gave birth to you rejoice.
My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes be happy with my ways.
A prostitute is a deep pit, and an unfaithful woman is a narrow well.
She waits like a robber and leads many men to be unfaithful.
Who has trouble? Who has sorrow? Who has arguments? Who has complaints? Who has wounds for no reason? Who has red eyes?
Those who stay late over wine and go to taste mixed drinks.
Do not stare at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, and when it goes down smoothly.
In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.
Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will say twisted things.
You will be like someone sleeping in the middle of the sea, or like someone sleeping on top of the mast.
“They struck me, but I did not feel it. They beat me, but I did not know it. When will I wake up? I will seek it again.”
Do not envy wicked people, and do not wish to be with them.
Their hearts plan violence, and their lips talk about causing trouble.
By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is made strong.
Through knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.
A wise man is strong, and a man who has knowledge grows stronger.
With wise plans you can fight your battles, and with many advisers there is victory.
Wisdom is too high for a fool; he has nothing to say when important matters are discussed at the city gate.
Anyone who plans evil will be called a schemer.
Foolish plans are sinful, and people hate a mocker.
If you give up in a time of trouble, your strength is small.
Rescue those who are being led away to death, and hold back those stumbling toward slaughter.
If you say, "We did not know about this," does not He who weighs hearts see it? Does not He who guards your life know it? And will He not pay back a person for what he has done?
Eat honey, my son, because it is good, and honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
Know that wisdom is like that for your soul: if you find it, there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
Do not, wicked person, lie in wait against the home of a good person, and do not destroy his resting place.
A good person may fall seven times, but he gets up again, while wicked people stumble into ruin.
Do not be glad when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles.
Otherwise the the LORD will see it and be displeased, and He will turn His anger away from him.
Do not be upset by evil people, and do not envy wicked people.
For evil people have no future, and their hope will be snuffed out.
Fear the the LORD and the king, my son, and do not join those who rebel.
For they will bring sudden trouble; who knows what ruin they both can cause?
These are also sayings for wise people: It is not good to show favoritism in court.
Whoever says to a wicked person, "You are innocent," peoples will curse him, and nations will denounce him.
But it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and a rich blessing will come to them.
An honest answer is as welcome as a kiss on the lips.
Finish your outdoor work and get your field ready; after that, build your house.
Do not testify against your neighbor without a good reason, and do not deceive with your lips.
Do not say, "I will do to him what he did to me; I will pay him back for what he has done."
I walked past the field of a lazy person and by the vineyard of someone with no sense.
Thorns had grown all over the field, weeds covered the ground, and the stone wall was broken down.
I looked at it and thought about it; I saw it and learned a lesson.
"A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,"
and your poverty will come like a robber, and your need like an armed man.
These are more wise sayings of Solomon, copied by the men of King Hezekiah of Judah.
It brings glory to God to keep a matter hidden, and it brings glory to kings to search it out.
The sky is high, the earth is deep, and no one can fully understand a king's heart.
Remove the impurities from silver, and the refiner can shape it into something useful.
Remove wicked people from a king's presence, and his rule will be built on what is right.
Don't show off in front of a king or take the place of important people.
It's better for someone to say, "Come up here," than for you to be moved down in front of a noble you can see.
Don't rush into a fight. You may not know what to do at the end, especially if your neighbor puts you to shame.
Settle your disagreement with your neighbor directly, and don't reveal someone else's secret.
Otherwise, the person who hears it may shame you, and your bad reputation may never go away.
The right word at the right time is like golden apples in silver settings.
A wise correction to a listening ear is like a gold ring or fine gold jewelry.
A faithful messenger refreshes those who send him, just as snow-cooled air refreshes people during harvest.
A person who brags about a gift he never gives is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.
Patience can persuade a ruler, and gentle words can break strong resistance.
If you find honey, eat only what you need. If you eat too much, you may get sick.
Don't visit your neighbor's house too often, or he may get tired of you and hate you.
A person who lies about his neighbor is like a club, a sword, and a sharp arrow.
Trusting an unfaithful person in trouble is like a broken tooth or a sprained ankle.
Singing cheerful songs to a sad person is like taking off someone's coat in cold weather or pouring vinegar on baking soda.
If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
Your kindness will make him feel ashamed, and the LORD will reward you.
A north wind brings rain, and a gossiping tongue brings angry looks.
It's better to live in a corner of the roof than share a house with a nagging wife.
Good news from a faraway land is like cold water to a thirsty person.
A good person who gives in to the wicked is like a polluted spring.
It's not good to eat too much honey, and seeking your own glory isn't glorious.
A person who can't control his temper is like a city with broken walls.
Honor doesn't fit a fool, just like snow in summer or rain during the harvest.
A curse with no reason won't come true, like a bird that never lands.
A horse needs a whip, a donkey needs a bridle, and a fool needs a rod on the back.
Don't answer a fool in his own foolish way, or you will become like him.
Answer a fool in his foolish way, so he won't think he's wise.
Sending a message with a fool is like cutting off your own feet and drinking trouble.
A wise saying in a fool's mouth is as useless as lame legs.
Giving honor to a fool is like tying a stone in a sling—it doesn't help and can hurt.
A wise saying in a fool's mouth is like a thorn in a drunk person's hand.
Hiring a fool—or just anyone passing by—is like an archer shooting wildly.
A fool who keeps repeating his mistakes is like a dog going back to its vomit.
Do you see someone who thinks he's wise? There's more hope for a fool than for him.
The lazy person says, "There's a lion in the road! A fierce lion is in the streets!"
A lazy person turns in bed like a door swings on its hinges.
He buries his hand in the dish but is too tired to bring it back to his mouth.
A lazy person thinks he's wiser than seven people who give good answers.
Grabbing a dog by the ears is like butting into someone else's fight.
A person who tricks his neighbor and says, "I was only joking!" is like a crazy person throwing burning sticks, arrows, and death.
A fire goes out when there's no wood, and a fight dies down when there's no gossip.
Charcoal keeps hot coals glowing, and wood keeps a fire burning; a troublemaker keeps fights going.
Gossip is like tasty food—it goes deep inside a person.
Burning lips and an evil heart are like a shiny coating over a clay pot—they look good but hide something cheap.
A hateful person hides his true feelings behind his words, but he stores up deceit inside.
Don't trust him when he sounds kind, because his heart is full of evil.
His hatred may be hidden for now, but his evil will be shown in public.
Whoever digs a pit for someone else falls into it, and whoever rolls a stone has it roll back on him.
A lying tongue hates the people it hurts, and smooth talk brings ruin.
Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
Let someone else praise you, and not your own mouth; let a stranger praise you, and not your own lips.
A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden, but a fool's anger is heavier than both.
Anger is cruel, and fury is like a flood, but who can stand up to jealousy?
Open correction is better than love that stays hidden.
The wounds of a true friend can be trusted, but an enemy's kisses are deceitful.
A full stomach turns away from honey, but to a hungry person even bitter food tastes sweet.
Like a bird that wanders from its nest, so is a person who wanders from home.
Oil and perfume make the heart glad, and a friend's honest advice brings sweetness to the soul.
Do not abandon your friend or your father's friend, and do not go to your brother's house on the day of your trouble; a nearby neighbor is better than a brother far away.
Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad, so I can answer the one who insults me.
A careful person sees danger and hides, but foolish people keep going and suffer.
Take the clothes of someone who promises to pay for a stranger's debt; hold them as security if he does it for a wayward woman.
If someone loudly blesses a neighbor early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse.
A quarrelsome wife is like a steady drip on a rainy day.
Trying to stop her is like trying to stop the wind, or like holding oil in your right hand.
As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.
Whoever takes care of a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever guards his master will be honored.
As water shows a face, so a person's heart shows the person.
The grave and destruction are never satisfied, and human eyes are never satisfied.
A crucible tests silver, and a furnace tests gold, but praise tests a person.
Even if you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, his foolishness will not leave him.
Be sure you know how your flocks are doing, and pay attention to your herds.
Riches do not last forever, and a crown does not pass to every generation.
When the grass is gone and new growth appears, and the plants on the hills are gathered,
the lambs will give you clothing, and the goats will give you the price of a field.
You will have plenty of goats' milk to feed your family and to nourish your servant girls.
The wicked run away even when no one chases them, but godly people are as brave as a lion.
When a country rebels, it has many rulers, but a wise leader with understanding keeps things in order.
A poor leader who crushes the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.
People who turn away from God's law praise the wicked, but those who obey God's law stand against them.
Evil people do not understand justice, but those who seek the the LORD understand everything.
It is better to be poor and live with honesty than to be rich and walk a crooked path.
A wise son obeys the law, but a friend of gluttons brings shame to his father.
Someone who grows rich by charging interest and fees saves it for a person who will show kindness to the poor.
If someone refuses to listen to God's law, even their prayer is offensive to God.
Whoever leads good people down an evil road will fall into his own trap, but honest people will receive good things.
A rich person may think he is wise, but a poor person with understanding can see through him.
When good people win, there is great honor; when wicked people rise to power, people hide.
Whoever hides their sins will not succeed, but whoever admits them and leaves them behind will receive mercy.
A person who always respects God is blessed, but someone who hardens his heart will fall into trouble.
A wicked ruler over poor people is like a roaring lion or a charging bear.
A ruler who lacks good judgment is a cruel oppressor, but one who hates dishonest gain will live a long time.
A person with blood on his hands will run to the grave; do not support him.
Whoever walks with honesty will be saved, but whoever is crooked in his ways will suddenly fall.
Whoever works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases empty dreams will have plenty of poverty.
A faithful person will be richly blessed, but someone in a hurry to get rich will not go unpunished.
It is not good to show favoritism, yet some people will do wrong for a piece of bread.
A greedy person rushes after wealth and does not know poverty is on its way.
Someone who corrects another person will later find more favor than someone who flatters with smooth words.
Whoever robs his father or mother and says, "It is not a sin," is a friend to a destroyer.
A greedy person stirs up trouble, but whoever trusts in the the LORD will prosper.
Whoever trusts in his own heart is a fool, but whoever walks in wisdom will be kept safe.
Whoever gives to the poor will not lack, but whoever ignores them will receive many curses.
When wicked people rise, people hide; when they are destroyed, good people increase.
A stubborn person who ignores many warnings will be destroyed suddenly, with no cure.
When good people do well, everyone celebrates; when evil people rule, everyone groans.
A son who loves wisdom makes his father happy, but a man who spends time with prostitutes wastes his money.
A king who rules with justice makes the land stable, but a man who takes bribes tears it down.
A man who flatters his neighbor sets a trap for him.
An evil man is trapped by his own sin, but a good person sings and is glad.
Good people care about justice for the poor, but wicked people do not care about it.
Mockers stir up trouble in a city, but wise people calm anger.
If a wise man argues with a foolish man, the fool gets angry and laughs, and there is no peace.
Violent people hate an innocent person, but good people care about his life.
A foolish person lets out all his anger, but a wise person keeps it under control.
If a ruler listens to lies, all his workers become wicked.
The poor person and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives life to both.
A king who judges poor people fairly will have a throne that lasts forever.
A rod and a warning give wisdom, but a child left on his own disgraces his mother.
When wicked people gain power, sin grows, but good people will see them fall.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring joy to your life.
Without a vision, people lose control; but happy is the one who keeps the law.
A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; even if he understands, he will not answer.
Do you see a man who speaks too quickly? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
A servant who is spoiled from childhood will bring grief in the end.
An angry man stirs up fights, and a hot-tempered man sins a lot.
Pride brings a person down, but a humble spirit gains honor.
A person who partners with a thief hates his own life; he is sworn in but says nothing.
Fear of people is a trap, but whoever trusts in the LORD is safe.
Many seek a ruler's favor, but justice for a person comes from the LORD.
The way of an evil person is disgusting to good people, and the way of a good person is disgusting to evil people.
The words of Agur son of Jakeh—an oracle. This man declared to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal.
Surely I am more foolish than any man, and I do not have human understanding.
I have not learned wisdom, and I do not know the Holy One.

Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in His hands? Who has wrapped the waters in His cloak? Who has set up all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is His Son's name? Surely you know!
Every word of God is pure; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
Do not add to His words, or He may rebuke you and prove you a liar.
Two things I ask of You; do not keep them from me before I die:
keep falsehood and lies far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches, but give me only the food I need.
Otherwise, I may have too much and deny You, saying, "Who is the LORD?" Or I may become poor and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will be guilty.
There is a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother.
There is a generation that is pure in its own eyes but is not washed from its filth.
There is a generation whose eyes are proud and whose eyelids are lifted high.
There is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose molars are knives, to devour the poor from the earth and the needy from among men.
The leech has two daughters: "Give! Give!" Three things are never satisfied, and four never say, "Enough!":
Sheol, a barren womb, land that is never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, "Enough!"
The eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother will be pecked out by the ravens of the valley and eaten by young eagles.
Three things are too wonderful for me, four that I cannot understand:
the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship on the high seas, and the way of a man with a young woman.
So is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats and wipes her mouth and says, "I have done nothing wrong."
Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:
a servant who becomes king, a fool who is filled with food,
an unloved woman who marries, and a maidservant who displaces her mistress.
Four things on earth are small, yet they are very wise:
ants are creatures of little strength, yet they store up their food in the summer;
rock badgers are creatures of little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks;
locusts have no king, yet they march in ranks;
a lizard can be caught by hand, yet it is found in kings' palaces.
Three things are stately in their walk, four that move with stately bearing:
a lion, mightiest among beasts, who does not turn back from anything;
a strutting rooster; a he-goat; and a king with his army around him.
If you have acted foolishly by exalting yourself, or if you have planned evil, put your hand over your mouth.
For as churning milk produces butter, and twisting the nose produces blood, so stirring up anger produces strife.
"The words of King Lemuel — an oracle his mother taught him:
What, my son? What, son of my womb? What, son of my vows?
"Don't spend your strength on women, or your ways on those who ruin kings.
"It isn't for kings, Lemuel — it isn't for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to crave strong drink,
lest they drink and forget what's been decreed, and twist the rights of all who are oppressed.
Give strong drink to those who are dying, and wine to those who are in anguish.
Let them drink and forget their poverty, and remember their misery no more.
"Speak up for those who can't speak for themselves, for the rights of all who have nothing.
Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy."
A wife of noble character — who can find her? She is worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trusts her completely, and he lacks nothing of value.
She brings him good, not harm, all the days of her life.
She looks for wool and flax and works with eager hands.
She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from far away.
She rises while it's still night and provides food for her household, and portions for her servant girls.
She considers a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
She dresses herself with strength and makes her arms strong.
She sees that her trading is profitable, and her lamp doesn't go out at night.
She holds the distaff in her hands and grips the spindle with her fingers.
She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
When it snows, she isn't afraid for her household, for all of them are clothed in scarlet.
She makes coverings for her bed; she's dressed in fine linen and purple.
Her husband is respected at the city gate, where he sits among the elders of the land.
She makes linen garments and sells them, and supplies the merchants with sashes.
She's clothed with strength and dignity, and she can laugh at the days to come.
She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful teaching is on her tongue.
She watches over the affairs of her household and doesn't eat the bread of idleness.
Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband too, and he praises her:
"Many women do noble things, but you surpass them all."
Charm is misleading and beauty doesn't last, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
Give her the reward she's earned, and let her works bring her praise at the city gate.
These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David and king in Jerusalem.
"Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless."
What does a person gain from all their hard work under the sun?
Generations come and go, but the earth remains forever.
The sun rises and sets, and hurries back to where it rises.
The wind blows south, then turns north; it goes around and around, then comes back.
All streams flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full. They return to where they began, to flow again.
Everything is tiring; no one can say it all. The eye never gets enough of seeing, and the ear never gets enough of hearing.
What has been will be again; what has been done will be done again. There is nothing new under the sun.
Is there anything someone can point to and say, "Look, this is new"? It has already existed long ago, before our time.
No one remembers the people of long ago, and the people who come later will not be remembered by those who come after them.
I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I applied my mind to study and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a heavy burden God has given people to work on!
I have seen all the things done under the sun. They are all meaningless, a waste of effort.
What is crooked cannot be straightened; what is missing cannot be counted.
I said to myself, "Look, I have grown in wisdom more than anyone who ruled Jerusalem before me. My mind has seen much wisdom and knowledge."
Then I applied my mind to understand wisdom, and also madness and folly. I learned that this too is pointless.
For with much wisdom comes much sorrow; the more knowledge, the more grief.
I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good." But see, this too was meaningless.
I said of laughter, "It is madness," and of pleasure, "What does it accomplish?"

I searched my heart for how to cheer my body with wine—while my heart was still guided by wisdom—and how to take hold of foolishness, until I could see what is good for people to do on earth during the few days of their lives.
I made my works great. I built houses for myself and planted vineyards.
I made gardens and parks for myself, and I planted every kind of fruit tree in them.
I made pools of water to water a forest of growing trees.
I bought male and female slaves, and slaves were born in my house. I also had great herds and flocks, more than anyone before me in Jerusalem.
I gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I got male and female singers for myself, and the delights people enjoy—many concubines.
I became great and surpassed all who were in Jerusalem before me. My wisdom also stayed with me.
I did not keep my eyes from anything they asked for. I did not keep my heart from any pleasure, because my heart was glad in all my work. This was my reward from all my work.
Then I looked at all the things my hands had made and the work I had worked hard to do, and see, it was all meaningless, a waste of effort. There was no lasting benefit in this life.
I turned to look at wisdom, madness, and foolishness. What can the person do who comes after the king? Only what has already been done.
I saw that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
The wise person can see where he is going, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also knew that the same end comes to all of them.
I said in my heart, "What happens to the fool will also happen to me. So why have I been so wise?" Then I said in my heart, "This too is meaningless."
No one remembers the wise person or the fool forever. In the days to come, everything will be forgotten. How can the wise die just like the fool?
So I hated life, because the work done on earth seemed evil to me. Everything is meaningless, a waste of effort.
I hated all my work that I had worked hard at on earth, because I must leave it to the person who comes after me.
Who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? Yet he will rule over all my work that I worked hard at and was wise about on earth. This too is meaningless.
So I turned to despair in my heart over all the work I had worked hard at on earth.
There is a person who works with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, but he must leave his share to someone who did not work for it. This too is meaningless and a great evil.
What does a person get from all his work and from the worry of his heart that he works at on earth?
All his days are pain and grief; even at night his mind does not rest. This too is meaningless.
There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and find joy in his work. I saw that this too comes from the hand of God.
For who can eat or enjoy anything apart from Him?

God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the person who pleases Him. But to the sinner He gives the task of gathering and storing up, only to give it to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless, a waste of effort.
There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity on earth.
There is a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to pull up what was planted.
There is a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to tear down and a time to build.
There is a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance.
There is a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones, a time to hug and a time to turn away from hugging.
There is a time to search and a time to lose, a time to keep and a time to throw away.
There is a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be quiet and a time to speak.
There is a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
What does a worker gain from all his hard work?
I have seen the hard work God has given people to do.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also put eternity in people's hearts, yet no one can understand everything God has done from beginning to end.
I know that there is nothing better for people than to be joyful and do good while they live.
So everyone can eat and drink and enjoy the good from all their work—this is God's gift.
I know that everything God does lasts forever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing can be taken away. God does this so that people will fear Him.
What exists has already been, and what will be has already been. God brings back what has already happened.
I also saw in this world that where justice should be, there was wickedness, and where what is right should be, there was wickedness.
I said in my heart, “God will bring the righteous and the wicked into judgment, for there is a time for every activity and every deed.”
I also said in my heart about people, “God tests them so they can see that they are like animals.”
For people and animals share the same fate. As one dies, so dies the other. They all have the same breath, and people have no advantage over animals. Everything is meaningless.
All go to the same place. All come from dust, and to dust all return.
Who knows whether a person's spirit goes up and an animal's spirit goes down into the earth?
So I saw that the best thing a person can do is enjoy their work, because that is their share. Who can show them what will happen after them?

Then I turned again and looked at all the oppression that happens in this world. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no one to comfort them. Power was on the side of their oppressors, and they had no one to comfort them.
So I said the dead, who have already died, are better off than the living, who are still alive.
But better than both is the person who has never been born, who has not seen the evil things done in this world.
Then I saw that all hard work and every skillful deed come from one person envying another. This too is meaningless and useless.
The fool folds his hands and destroys himself.
It is better to have a little peace and quiet than a lot of hard work that comes to nothing.
Then I turned again and saw something meaningless in this world.

A man may be alone, with no companion. He has no son and no brother, yet he never stops working. His eyes are never satisfied with riches. He asks, "Who am I working so hard for, and why am I denying myself good things?" This too is meaningless—a miserable way to live.
Two people are better than one, because they get a good reward for their work.
If one falls, the other can help him up. But how sad for the person who is alone and falls, with no one to help him up!
Also, if two lie down together, they can keep each other warm. But how can one person stay warm alone?
If someone attacks one person, two can stand against him. A rope made of three strands is not easily broken.
It is better to be a poor but wise young person than an old and foolish king who no longer listens to warnings.
The young man came out of prison to rule, even though he was born poor in his kingdom.
I saw all the living people in this world, along with the young man who would take the king's place.
There is no end to all the people who came before them. Yet the people who come later will not be pleased with him. This too is meaningless and useless.
Be careful when you go to God's house. Listening closely is better than giving a foolish offering, because fools don't realize they're doing wrong.
Don't rush to speak, and don't be quick to say something to God. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so keep your words few.
Dreams come from too much worry, and a fool shows his foolishness by talking too much.
When you make a promise to God, don't delay keeping it. God doesn't delight in fools. Keep what you promised.
It's better not to make a promise than to make one and not keep it.
Don't let your mouth cause you to sin. Don't tell the messenger, "It was a mistake." Why should God get angry at your words and destroy what you have worked for?
With so many dreams and empty words, nothing comes of it. Just fear God.
If you see unfair treatment of the poor and justice twisted in a land, don't be surprised. Officials answer to higher officials, and there are even higher ones above them.
But the land's harvest helps everyone. Even the king depends on the fields.
Anyone who loves money never has enough. Anyone who loves wealth is never satisfied with what they earn. That's empty too.
When wealth grows, more people consume it. What good does it do the owner except to look at it?
A worker sleeps well, whether he eats a little or a lot. But a rich man's full stomach keeps him awake.
I've seen something terrible in this life: people hoard wealth, and it hurts them.
That wealth is lost in a bad deal, and when he has a son, there's nothing left to give him.
We come into the world naked, and we leave the same way. We can't take anything we worked for.
That's another terrible thing: we leave just as we came. What's the point of working so hard for nothing?
He spends all his days eating in gloom, with frustration, sickness, and anger.
Here's what I've found is good: eat, drink, and enjoy the work a person does in this life during the few days of life God gives him. That's his share.
God also gives some people wealth, possessions, and the power to enjoy them, to accept their share, and to be glad in their work. That is God's gift.
He won't spend much time worrying about his short life, because God keeps him busy with joy in his heart.
I have seen something evil in this life, and it weighs heavily on people.

God gives a person wealth, property, and honor, so that he lacks nothing he wants. Yet God does not let him enjoy it; someone else gets to enjoy it instead. That is meaningless and a painful sickness.
A man may have a hundred children and live a very long life. Still, if he is not satisfied with good things and does not even get a proper burial, I say a stillborn child is better off than he is.
That child comes into the world for nothing and leaves in darkness. Its name is lost in darkness.
It never sees the sun or knows anything. Yet it is more at rest than he is.
Even if he lived two thousand years but never saw good—don’t all people end up in the same place?
People work hard to feed themselves, but they are never full.
What does a wise person gain over a fool? What does a poor person gain by knowing how to live among the living?
It is better to enjoy what one has than to keep longing for more. That too is meaningless and pointless.
Everything that exists was named long ago. People know what humans are, but no one can argue with someone stronger.
The more there is, the more meaningless it all becomes. What good does it do a person?
Who knows what is good for a person during his short, meaningless life? His days pass like a shadow. Who can tell him what will happen after he is gone from this life?
A good name is better than fine perfume, and the day of death is better than the day of birth.
It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, because death is the end of every person, and the living should take that to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter, because a sad face can make the heart better.
The heart of wise people is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
It is better to listen to a wise person's warning than to listen to the songs of fools.
For the laughter of fools is like the crackling of thorns under a pot. That too is meaningless.
Oppression can make a wise person foolish, and a bribe can ruin the heart.
The end of a matter is better than its beginning, and patience is better than pride.
Do not be quick to get angry in your spirit, because anger rests in the lap of fools.
Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these?" For you do not ask that out of wisdom.
Wisdom is good when it comes with an inheritance, and it helps those who see the sun.
Wisdom is a shelter, just as money is a shelter, but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom keeps its owner alive.
Look at the work of God: Who can straighten what He has made crooked?
When times are good, be happy; when times are bad, think about this: God made both, so no one can know what will come next.
In my meaningless life I have seen both of these: a righteous person can die even though they are righteous, and a wicked person can live a long time in wickedness.
Do not be too good, and do not make yourself too wise. Why would you ruin yourself?
Do not be too wicked, and do not be a fool. Why would you die before your time?
It is good to hold on to one and not let the other slip from your hand, because the person who fears God will follow both warnings.
Wisdom makes a wise person stronger than ten rulers in a city.
Surely there is no one on earth who always does good and never sins.
Do not listen to everything people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
For you know in your heart that you too have cursed others many times.
I tested all of this with wisdom. I said, "I will be wise," but it was beyond me.
What exists is far away and very deep. Who can find it?
I turned my mind to know, to study, and to seek wisdom and an explanation. I also wanted to understand the foolishness of wickedness and the madness of folly.
I find a woman whose heart is a trap and whose hands are chains more bitter than death. The person who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner will be caught by her.
"Look," says the Teacher, "I have found this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation."
While I was still searching but not finding, I found one upright man among a thousand, but among all these I did not find one upright woman.
See, I have found only this: God made people upright, but they have looked for many schemes.
Who is like a wise person? Who knows how to explain things? Wisdom lights up a person's face and softens a hard look.
I say, keep the king's command because of your oath to God.
Don't be in a hurry to leave his presence, and don't join in an evil plan, because he does whatever he wants.
Since the king's word has power, who can ask him, "What are you doing?"
Whoever obeys a command avoids trouble. A wise heart knows the right time and the right way to act.
There is a time and a way for everything, even when trouble weighs heavy on a person.
No one knows what will happen next, and no one can tell him what is coming.
No one can control the wind, and no one can control the day of death. No one is released during war, and evil won't save the person who does it.
I saw all of this and thought about everything done under the sun. Sometimes one person rules over another and brings harm.
I also saw wicked people buried. They used to come and go from the holy place, and then they were forgotten in the city where they did those things. This too is meaningless.
When a sentence against a bad act isn't carried out quickly, people's hearts are set on doing wrong.
Even though a sinner does wrong a hundred times and lives a long time, I know it will go well for those who fear God, because they fear Him.
But it won't go well for the wicked. He won't live long, like a shadow that passes quickly, because he doesn't fear God.
Here is another meaningless thing that happens on earth: good people sometimes get what the wicked deserve, and wicked people sometimes get what the good deserve. I say this too is meaningless.
So I praised joy. A person has nothing better under the sun than to eat, drink, and be happy. That joy stays with him in his work during the life God gives him under the sun.
When I set my heart to know wisdom and to see the work done on earth—even though a person's eyes get no sleep day or night—
I saw all the work of God. No person can understand the work done under the sun. Even if someone works hard to find it out, he won't. Even if a wise person says he knows, he can't.
I thought hard about all of this and decided that good people, wise people, and what they do are in God's hands. But no one knows whether love or hate is waiting for them.

Everyone has the same future. Good people and bad people, clean people and unclean people, those who offer sacrifices and those who don't, all share one fate. Good people are treated like sinners. People who swear an oath are treated like people who are afraid to swear one.

This is the sad part of everything that happens in this life: everyone has the same end. People's hearts are full of evil while they live, and madness is in their hearts. After that, they join the dead.
But anyone who is still alive has hope. Even a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
Living people know they will die, but dead people know nothing. They get no more reward, and even their name is forgotten.
Their love, hate, and jealousy are gone. They will never again share in anything that happens in this life.
So go eat your food with joy, and drink your wine with a happy heart, because God has already accepted what you do.
Always wear white clothes, and always put oil on your head.
Enjoy life with the wife you love all the days of this meaningless life God has given you in this world. Those meaningless days are your share in life and in the hard work you do in this world.
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your strength, because there is no work, planning, knowledge, or wisdom in the grave, where you are going.

I have seen something else in this life: the fastest runner does not always win the race. The strongest soldier does not always win the battle. Wise people do not always have food. Smart people do not always get rich. People with knowledge do not always find favor. Time and chance happen to all of them.
No one knows when their time will come. People are trapped by hard times that fall on them suddenly, like fish caught in a net or birds caught in a trap.
I also saw this example of wisdom in this life, and it amazed me.
There was a small city with only a few people in it. A powerful king attacked it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.
But a poor, wise man lived there. He saved the city with his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." But the poor man's wisdom was looked down on, and his words were not listened to.
The quiet words of wise people are heard better than a foolish ruler's shouts.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy much good.
Dead flies can make a perfumer's oil stink. In the same way, a little foolishness can outweigh wisdom and honor.
A wise person's heart leans to the right, but a fool's heart leans to the left.
Even when a fool walks down the road, his heart lacks sense, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
If a ruler's anger rises against you, don't leave your place, because calmness can settle even great wrongs.
I've seen something wrong under the sun: a mistake that comes from a ruler.
Foolishness is given high positions, while rich people sit in low places.
I've seen slaves on horseback, while princes walk on the ground like slaves.
Anyone who digs a pit can fall into it, and anyone who breaks through a wall can be bitten by a snake.
Someone who moves stones can get hurt by them, and someone who splits wood can be hurt by it.
If the iron is dull and its edge isn't sharpened, more strength is needed, but wisdom helps you succeed.
If a snake bites before it's charmed, the snake charmer gains nothing.
A wise person's words are kind, but a fool's own words destroy him.
His talk starts with foolishness and ends in wicked madness.
A fool talks too much, even though no one knows what's coming. Who can tell him what will happen after him?
Fools' hard work wears them out, because they don't even know the way to town.
Trouble comes to you, land, when your king is a child and your leaders feast in the morning!
You are blessed, land, when your king comes from noble birth and your leaders eat at the right time—for strength, not for getting drunk!
Because of laziness, the roof sags, and because of idle hands, the house leaks.
Bread is made for laughter, wine makes life happy, and money answers everything.
