Don't curse the king, even in your thoughts, and don't curse a rich person in your bedroom, because a bird of the air may carry your words, and a winged creature may repeat what you said.
Be generous with what you have, because after many days you will see good come from it.
Spread your resources among seven or even eight projects, since you do not know what trouble may come to the land.
If clouds fill with water, they pour rain on the earth. A tree may fall to the south or to the north, but it stays where it falls.
If you wait for perfect weather, you will never plant or harvest.
You do not know how the wind moves or how a baby forms in the womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, who makes everything.
Sow your seed in the morning, and do not let your hands rest in the evening, because you do not know which effort will succeed—this one, that one, or both.
Light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.
If a person lives many years, he should enjoy all of them, but he should remember the dark days, because they will be many. Everything that is coming is meaningless.

Be happy, young man, while you are young, and let your heart give you joy in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways your heart chooses and in what your eyes see, but know that God will bring you into judgment for all these things.
Remove sorrow from your heart, and put away pain from your body, because youth and strength are meaningless.
Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and the years draw near when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them”—
before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds return after the rain;
when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men stoop, when the grinders stop because they are few, and those who look through the windows grow dim;
when the doors to the street are closed and the sound of grinding fades; when people rise at the sound of birds, but all their songs grow faint;

when people are afraid of heights and of dangers in the streets; when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, and desire fails. Then people go to their lasting home, and mourners walk the streets.
Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped, or the golden bowl is broken; before the pitcher is shattered at the spring, or the wheel broken at the well,
and the dust returns to the earth it came from, and the spirit returns to God, who gave it.
“Meaningless! Meaningless!” says the Teacher. “Everything is meaningless!”
Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people. He thought carefully, searched things out, and put many proverbs in order.
The Teacher tried to find the right words, and what he wrote was honest and true.
The words of the wise are like goads. Their collected sayings are like nails driven in firmly, and they are given by one Shepherd.
My son, be careful about anything beyond these. There is no end to making many books, and too much study wears out the body.
Now that everything has been heard, here is the final point: Fear God and keep His commands, for this is the whole duty of people.
For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing, whether it is good or evil.
The Song of Songs, which is Solomon's.
"Let him kiss me with kisses from his mouth, for your love is better than wine.
Because of the fragrance of your perfumes, your name is like perfume poured out; that is why the young women love you.
Draw me after you, and let us run. The king has brought me into his rooms. We will rejoice and be glad in you. We will remember your love more than wine. They are right to love you."
"I am dark but lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like Solomon's curtains.
Do not stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has darkened my skin. My mother's sons were angry with me. They made me guard the vineyards, but I did not guard my own vineyard.
Tell me, you whom I love, where you feed your flock, where you let it rest at noon. Why should I be like a woman who covers her face beside the flocks of your friends?"
"If you do not know, most beautiful of women, follow the tracks of the flock and graze your young goats beside the shepherds' tents.
I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.
We will make you chains of gold with beads of silver."
"While the king was at his table, my perfume gave off its fragrance.
My beloved is to me a small bag of myrrh that lies between my breasts.
My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi."
"Look, you are beautiful, my darling; look, you are beautiful; your eyes are like doves."
"Look, you are handsome, my beloved; yes, you are pleasant. Our couch is green.
The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are firs."
"I am a flower of Sharon, a lily of the valleys."
"Like a lily among thorns, so is my darling among the young women."
"Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the young men.
He has brought me to the banquet hall, and his love is like a banner over me."
"Strengthen me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples, for I am lovesick."
His left arm is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
"Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise by the gazelles or the wild does: do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases."
"Listen! My beloved! Look, he comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills."
"My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice."
My beloved spoke and said to me, "Arise, my darling, and come away with me, my beautiful one.
For winter is past; the rain is over and gone.
Flowers appear in the land; the time of singing has come, and the turtledove's voice is heard in our land.
The fig tree is ripening its early fruit, and the grapevines are blossoming and giving off their fragrance. Arise, come away with me, my darling; come with me, my beautiful one.
"My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountainside, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely."
"Catch the foxes for us—the little foxes that ruin the vineyards, while our vineyards are in bloom."
"My beloved is mine, and I am his; he tends his flock among the lilies."
"Until the evening breeze blows and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether."
On my bed at night, I looked for the one I love. I looked for him, but I did not find him.
"I will get up now and walk around the city, through the streets and squares. I will look for the one I love." I looked for him, but I did not find him.
The watchmen found me as they walked around the city. "Have you seen the one I love?"
Scarcely had I passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let him go until I brought him to my mother's house, to the room of the one who gave birth to me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you by the gazelles or the does of the field: Do not stir up love or wake it before it is ready.
Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and incense made from all the merchant's spices?
Look! It is Solomon's carriage, escorted by sixty warriors, the noblest of Israel.
All of them wear swords. They are trained for battle, and each has his sword at his side, ready for danger at night.
King Solomon made a carriage for himself from the wood of Lebanon.
He made its posts of silver and its base of gold. Its seat was purple, and its inside was decorated with love by the Daughters of Jerusalem.
Daughters of Zion, go out and look at King Solomon wearing the crown his mother placed on him on the day of his wedding, the day his heart rejoiced.
“You are beautiful, my darling; you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep just washed, all of them bearing twins, with none missing.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Your cheeks behind your veil are like halves of a pomegranate.
Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; a thousand shields hang on it, all the shields of mighty men.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, feeding among the lilies.
“Until the day breaks and the shadows disappear, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
You are altogether beautiful, my darling; there is no flaw in you.
“Come with me from Lebanon, my bride; come with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
You have stolen my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one look from your eyes, with one jewel from your necklace.
How beautiful your love is, my sister, my bride! Your love is better than wine, and the smell of your perfume is better than any spice.
Your lips drip honey, my bride; honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your clothes is like the smell of Lebanon.
“You are a locked garden, my sister, my bride, a locked spring, a sealed fountain.
Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with the best fruit, with henna and nard,
nard and saffron, cane and cinnamon, with all kinds of frankincense, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
You are a garden spring, a well of fresh water flowing down from Lebanon.”
“Wake up, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow through my garden so its spices may spread. Let my beloved come into his garden and eat its choice fruits.”

I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh and my spices. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey, and I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, my friends; drink as much as you want, my loved ones.
I am asleep, but my heart is awake. Listen! My love is knocking. He says, “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my perfect one. My head is wet with dew, and my hair is damp with the night.”
I have taken off my robe. Must I put it on again? I have washed my feet. Must I get them dirty again?
My love put his hand through the opening of the door, and my heart began to pound for him.
I got up to open the door for my love. My hands dripped with myrrh, and my fingers were wet with flowing myrrh on the handles of the lock.
I opened the door for my love, but my love had turned away and was gone. My heart sank when he left. I looked for him but could not find him. I called him, but he did not answer.
The watchmen who make their rounds in the city found me. They beat me and bruised me. They took my cloak from me, those watchmen on the walls.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I beg you, if you find my love, tell him I am weak with love.
“What makes your love better than any other, most beautiful of women? What makes your love better than any other, that you made us promise this?”
“My love is bright and strong, the best of ten thousand.
His head is like pure gold. His hair is wavy and black like a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, washed in milk and set like jewels.
His cheeks are like beds of spices that give off perfume. His lips are lilies dripping with liquid myrrh.
His arms are like gold rods set with topaz. His body is like smooth ivory decorated with sapphires.
His legs are like marble pillars set on bases of pure gold. He looks like Lebanon, as fine as its cedars.
His mouth is sweet, and everything about him is lovely. This is my love. This is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.”
Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful of women? Which way has your beloved turned, so we can seek him with you?" "
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to graze among the gardens and gather lilies.
I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine; he grazes among the lilies." "
You are beautiful, my darling, like Tirzah, lovely like Jerusalem, majestic like an army with banners.
Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one is missing.
Your temples behind your veil are like a piece of pomegranate. "
There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and young women without number.

But my dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is the only daughter of her mother, the favorite of the one who bore her. The young women saw her and called her blessed; the queens and concubines praised her." "
Who is this who looks down like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, majestic as an army with banners?" "
I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms in the valley, to see if the vines had budded or the pomegranates were in bloom.
Before I knew it, my desire had set me among the chariots of my people." "
Come back, come back, O Shulammite! Come back, come back, that we may look at you. Why would you look at the Shulammite as on the dance of Mahanaim?"
How beautiful are your feet in sandals, O noble daughter! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, made by a master's hands.
Your navel is like a rounded goblet that never runs out of mixed wine. Your waist is a heap of wheat surrounded by lilies.
Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is like a tower of ivory; your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose is like the tower of Lebanon that looks toward Damascus.
Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, and the hair of your head is like purple cloth. The king is captivated by your flowing hair.
How beautiful and pleasant you are, O my love, with your delights!
Your stature is like a palm tree, and your breasts are like clusters of fruit.
I said, "I will climb the palm tree and take hold of its fruit. May your breasts be like clusters of grapes on the vine, and the fragrance of your breath like apples,
and your mouth like the best wine." "May the wine go straight to my beloved, flowing smoothly over lips and teeth."
I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.
Come, my beloved, let us go out to the country; let us spend the night among the wildflowers.
Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded, if the blossoms have opened, and if the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my love.
The mandrakes give off their fragrance, and at our door are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, that I have saved up for you, my beloved.
"If only you were my brother, nursed at my mother's breast! Then I could kiss you in public, and no one would look down on me.
I would lead you and bring you to my mother's house, where she taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice from my pomegranates.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me."
"Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise: don't stir up love or wake it until it's ready."
"Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved?" "Under the apple tree I awakened you. There your mother conceived you; there the woman who bore you was in labor."
"Put me like a seal on your heart, like a seal on your arm. Love is as strong as death, and jealousy is as stubborn as the grave. Its flashes are fiery flashes, the very flame of the LORD.
Many waters can't put out love, and rivers can't wash it away. If a man gave all the wealth of his house for love, he would be completely scorned."
"We have a little sister, and her breasts aren't grown yet. What should we do for our sister on the day someone asks to marry her?
If she is a wall, we'll build a silver tower on her. If she is a door, we'll cover her with cedar boards."
"I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. Then in his eyes I was like someone who brings peace."
"Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He rented it to workers, and each one was to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
My own vineyard is right here before me. Solomon, you can have the thousand pieces, and two hundred go to those who tend the fruit."
"You who live in the gardens, my friends are listening for your voice. Let me hear it."
"Hurry, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of spices."
This is the vision that Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem. He saw it during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, O heavens, and listen, O earth, for the LORD has spoken: “I raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.”
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey knows its master's manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.

Ah, sinful nation, a people weighed down with guilt, a brood of evildoers, children who act corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel; they have turned their backs on Him.
Why will you be struck down again? Will you keep on rebelling? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart is faint.
From the sole of the foot to the top of the head, there is no soundness—only wounds, bruises, and open sores. They have not been cleaned or bandaged or soothed with oil.
Your land is a wasteland; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields right before your eyes; the land is a wasteland, overturned by strangers.
The Daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city under siege.
If the LORD of Hosts had not left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom and resembled Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
“What are your many sacrifices to Me?” says the LORD. “I am full of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened cattle. I do not delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.
When you come to appear before Me, who has asked this of you—this trampling of My courts?
Stop bringing worthless offerings. Your incense is detestable to Me. New moons, Sabbaths, and holy gatherings—I cannot bear your sin along with your worship.
I hate your new moons and your appointed feasts. They have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them.
When you spread out your hands, I will hide My eyes from you. Even if you pray many times, I will not listen; your hands are full of blood.”
“Wash and make yourselves clean. Remove your evil deeds from My sight. Stop doing wrong.
Learn to do right. Seek justice. Defend the oppressed. Take up the cause of the fatherless. Plead the case of the widow.
Come now, let us settle the matter,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are red as crimson, they will be like wool.
If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the best of the land.
But if you refuse and rebel, you will be killed by the sword. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.”
How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She once was full of justice, and righteousness lived in her, but now she is full of murderers.
Your silver has become dross; your wine is diluted with water.
Your princes are rebellious and companions of thieves. They all love bribes and chase after gifts. They do not defend the fatherless, and the widow's case does not come before them.
Therefore the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: “Ah, I will rid Myself of My foes and avenge Myself on My enemies.
I will turn My hand against you; I will thoroughly purge your dross; I will remove all your impurities.
I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you will be called the City of Righteousness, a Faithful City.”
Zion will be redeemed with justice, and her repentant ones with righteousness.
But rebels and sinners will be destroyed together, and those who forsake the LORD will perish.
For you will be ashamed of the oaks you desired, and you will be disgraced by the gardens you chose.
For you will be like an oak whose leaves wither, like a garden without water.
The strong will become tinder, and their work a spark; both will burn together, with no one to quench them.
This is the message that Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem.
In the last days, the mountain of the house of the LORD will be set up as the highest of the mountains. It will be lifted above the hills, and all nations will stream to it.

Many peoples will come and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us His ways, so we can walk in His paths.” For the law will go out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He will judge between the nations and settle disputes for many peoples. They will turn their swords into plow blades and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not take up the sword against nation, and they will not learn war anymore.
Come, people of Jacob, let us walk in the light of the LORD.
For You have abandoned Your people, the people of Jacob, because they are full of Eastern ways and fortune-tellers like the Philistines, and they make deals with foreigners.
Their land is full of silver and gold, with no end to their treasures. Their land is full of horses, with no end to their chariots.
Their land is full of idols. They bow down to the work of their own hands, to what their fingers have made.
So people are brought low, and everyone is humbled. Do not forgive them!
Go into the rocks and hide in the dust, away from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty.
The proud look of man will be humbled, and the pride of people will be brought low. The LORD alone will be raised high on that day.
For the Day of the LORD of Hosts will come against all who are proud and high, and against all that is lifted up. It will be brought low.
It will come against all the tall cedars of Lebanon and all the oaks of Bashan.
It will come against all the high mountains and all the high hills.
It will come against every high tower and every strong wall.
It will come against every ship from Tarshish and every beautiful treasure.
So human pride will be brought low, and the pride of people will be humbled. The LORD alone will be raised high on that day.
People will run to caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, away from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth.
On that day, people will throw away their silver and gold idols—the idols they made to worship—to the moles and the bats.
They will run to cracks in the rocks and gaps in the cliffs, away from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth.
Stop trusting in people. They are only human, with breath in their noses. What are they worth?
For look, the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, is taking away from Jerusalem and Judah all support and all help—every bit of bread and every drop of water.
He is taking away the hero and the soldier, the judge and the prophet, the fortune-teller and the elder,
the captain of fifty and the honored man, the counselor, the skilled craftsman, and the expert in secret arts.
I will make young people their leaders, and children will rule over them.
People will oppress each other—man against man and neighbor against neighbor. The young will be rude to the old, and the lowly will insult the respected.
For a man will grab his brother in his father's house and say, "You have a coat. Be our leader, and take charge of this ruin."
At that time he will speak up and say, "I can't fix this mess. I have no food and no coat at home, so don't make me leader of the people."
For Jerusalem has stumbled, and Judah has fallen, because their words and their actions are against the LORD. They rebel against His glorious presence.
The look on their faces testifies against them. They show their sin as openly as Sodom did, and they do not hide it. Woe to them! They have brought disaster on themselves.
Tell the righteous that it will go well with them, for they will enjoy the results of their good deeds.
Woe to the wicked! It will go badly for him, for he will be paid back for what his hands have done.
My people are ruled by children, and women are in charge. O My people, your leaders lead you the wrong way and destroy the path you should follow.
The LORD stands up to accuse; He stands to judge the peoples.
The LORD will enter into judgment with the elders and princes of His people: "You have ruined the vineyard; the stolen goods of the poor are in your houses.
"What do you mean by crushing My people and oppressing the poor?" declares the Lord, the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD also says, "Because the daughters of Zion are proud and walk with stretched-out necks and flirty looks, mincing along and jingling their ankle bracelets,
"the Lord will put sores on the heads of the daughters of Zion, and the LORD will make their foreheads bare."
In that day the Lord will take away their beautiful ankle chains, headbands, and crescent ornaments.
He will take away their pendants, bracelets, and veils.
He will take away their headdresses, armlets, sashes, scent bottles, and amulets.
He will take away their signet rings and nose rings.
He will take away their fine robes, shawls, wraps, and purses.
He will take away their mirrors, fine linen, turbans, and veils.
Instead of sweet perfume, there will be a stench; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of styled hair, baldness; instead of a fine robe, sackcloth; and a brand instead of beauty.
Your men will fall by the sword, and your strong warriors in battle.
Her gates will mourn and grieve; she will be left empty and sit on the ground.
On that day seven women will seize one man and say, “We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes. Just let us be called by your name. Take away our shame.”
On that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the land’s crops will be the pride and glory of Israel’s survivors.
Everyone left in Zion and everyone remaining in Jerusalem will be called holy—everyone recorded among the living in Jerusalem.
When the Lord has washed away the filth of Zion’s daughters and cleansed Jerusalem’s bloodstains from within her, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning,
then the LORD will create over every dwelling place of Mount Zion and over her gatherings a cloud of smoke by day and a shining flame of fire by night. Over all the glory there will be a covering.
It will be a shelter from the heat by day and a refuge and hiding place from storm and rain.
I will sing a song for my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hillside.
He dug it up, cleared away the stones, and planted the best vines. He built a watchtower in the middle and cut out a winepress. Then He looked for grapes, but it produced only wild grapes.
Now you who live in Jerusalem and you men of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
What more could I have done for my vineyard that I did not do? Why did I look for good grapes but get only wild ones?
Now let me tell you what I will do to my vineyard. I will take away its hedge, and it will be burned. I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled.
I will make it a wasteland. It will not be pruned or hoed, and briers and thorns will grow there. I will also tell the clouds not to rain on it.

The vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the planting He loves. He looked for justice, but He saw bloodshed. He looked for righteousness, but He heard cries of distress.
Woe to you who add house to house and field to field until there is no more room, so that you live alone in the land.
The LORD of Hosts has spoken in my ears: "Surely many large and beautiful houses will become empty ruins, with no one living in them."
Ten acres of vineyard will produce only one bath of wine, and a homer of seed will yield only an ephah of grain.
Woe to those who rise early in the morning to chase strong drink, and who stay up late at night until wine inflames them.
They have harps and lyres, tambourines and flutes, and wine at their parties, but they do not look at what the LORD is doing or see the work of His hands.
So my people go into exile because they lack knowledge. Their honored men go hungry, and their crowds are parched with thirst.
So the grave opens wide and stretches its mouth beyond measure. Down go their nobles, their crowds, their noise, and their revelers.
So people are humbled and mankind is brought low; the eyes of the proud are lowered.
But the LORD of Hosts is lifted up by justice, and God, the Holy One, is shown holy by righteousness.
Then lambs will graze in their pasture, and strangers will feed among the ruins of the rich.
Woe to those who drag sin along with cords of lies and pull wrongdoing like cart ropes.
They say, "Let Him hurry and do His work quickly, so we can see it. Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come near and happen, so we can know it."
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness in place of light and light in place of darkness, who call bitter sweet and sweet bitter.
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine and champions at mixing strong drink.
They clear the guilty for a bribe and deny justice to the innocent.

So, just as fire burns up dry grass, their roots will rot and their blossoms will blow away like dust. This will happen because they rejected the law of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

That is why the anger of the LORD burned against His people. He stretched out His hand and struck them. The mountains shook, and dead bodies lay like garbage in the streets. Even then, His anger did not turn away, and His hand was still stretched out.
He will raise a banner for nations far away and whistle for them from the ends of the earth. Look, they come quickly and swiftly.
None of them is tired or stumbles. None of them sleeps or dozes. Their belts are tight, and their sandal straps are not broken.
Their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are strung. Their horses' hooves seem like flint, and their wheels spin like a whirlwind.
Their roar is like a lion's roar. They growl like young lions. They grab their prey and carry it off, and no one can save it.
On that day they will roar over it like the roaring of the sea. If anyone looks at the land, there will be darkness and trouble. Even the light will be darkened by the clouds.
In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne. He was high and lifted up, and the train of His robe filled the temple.
Above Him stood seraphim. Each had six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.
And they called to one another: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory."
The sound of their voices shook the doorposts and thresholds, and the temple was filled with smoke.
Then I said, "I'm doomed! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips. My eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts."
Then one of the seraphim flew to me, carrying a glowing coal in his hand. He had taken it with tongs from the altar.
He touched my mouth with it and said, "Look, this has touched your lips. Your guilt is taken away, and your sin is forgiven."
Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?" I answered, "Here I am. Send me!"

He said, "Go and tell this people: 'You will hear but not understand; you will see but not perceive. Make the heart of this people calloused; make their ears dull and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.'"
Then I asked, "How long, Lord?" He answered, "Until cities are ruined and empty, houses have no people, and the land is a wasteland."
The LORD will drive people far away, and the land will be left very empty.
Even if a tenth remains, it too will be burned. Yet as a terebinth or an oak leaves a stump when cut down, so the holy seed will be the stump."
In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to fight against Jerusalem. But they could not overpower it.
When the house of David was told, "Aram has joined forces with Ephraim," the hearts of Ahaz and his people shook like trees in a forest blown by the wind.
Then the the LORD said to Isaiah, "Take your son Shear-jashub and go meet Ahaz at the end of the upper pool, on the road to the washer's field.
Say to him, 'Be careful, keep calm, and do not be afraid. Do not lose heart because of these two dying embers—Rezin of Aram and the son of Remaliah.
For Aram, Ephraim, and Remaliah's son have plotted evil against you,
saying, "Let us go up against Judah and terrify it. Let us break through its walls and set up the son of Tabeel as king over it."'
This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: "It will not stand; it will not happen.
For the capital of Aram is Damascus, and the capital of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be broken and will no longer be a people.
The capital of Ephraim is Samaria, and the capital of Samaria is Remaliah's son. If you do not stand firm in faith, you will not stand at all."
The the LORD spoke to Ahaz again:
"Ask the the LORD your God for a sign. Ask for something as deep as the grave or as high as the heavens."
But Ahaz said, "I will not ask; I will not test the the LORD."
Then Isaiah said, "Listen, house of David! Is it too small a thing for you to wear out people, that you also wear out my God?
Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: The virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and she will call Him Immanuel.
He will eat curds and honey by the time He knows how to refuse evil and choose good.
But before the boy knows how to refuse evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you dread will be deserted."

The the LORD will bring on you and on your people and on your father's house days that have not come since the day Ephraim turned away from Judah. He will bring this about through the king of Assyria.
On that day the the LORD will whistle for the fly from the distant streams of Egypt and for the bee from the land of Assyria.
They will all come and settle in the steep ravines, in the cracks of the rocks, on all the thornbushes, and in all the pastures.
On that day the Lord will use a hired razor—the king of Assyria—shaving off the hair of the head, the legs, and the beard.
On that day a man will keep alive a young cow and two sheep.
Because there will be so much milk, he will eat curds. Yes, everyone left in the land will eat curds and honey.
On that day, in every place where a thousand vines worth a thousand silver coins once grew, there will be only briers and thorns.
People will go there with bows and arrows, because the whole land will be briers and thorns.
As for the hills that were once hoed with a hoe, you will not go there for fear of briers and thorns. They will become places where oxen are turned loose and sheep trample.
Then the LORD said to me, “Take a large scroll and write on it with an ordinary pen, ‘Quick to the Plunder, Swift to the Spoil.’
I will take reliable witnesses for Myself—Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.”
I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. Then the LORD said to me, “Call his name ‘Quick to the Plunder, Swift to the Spoil.’
For before the boy knows how to say, ‘my father’ or ‘my mother,’ the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be carried away before the king of Assyria.”
The LORD spoke to me again:
“Because these people have rejected the calm waters of Shiloah and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son,
the Lord is bringing against them the strong and mighty waters of the River—the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will rise over all its channels and overflow all its banks.
It will sweep through Judah, flooding and passing through, reaching to the neck. Its outstretched wings will fill the breadth of Your land, O Immanuel.”
Be shattered, O peoples, and be dismayed; listen, all distant lands. Prepare for battle, and be dismayed; prepare for battle, and be dismayed.
Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted; speak a word, but it will not stand, for God is with us.
For this is what the LORD said to me with a strong hand, instructing me not to walk in the way of this people:
“Do not call conspiracy everything these people call conspiracy. Do not fear what they fear, and do not dread it.
“The LORD of Hosts is the One you are to regard as holy. Let Him be your fear, and let Him be your dread.
He will be a sanctuary, but to both houses of Israel He will be a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, a trap and a snare to the people of Jerusalem.
Many will stumble over them; they will fall and be broken; they will be snared and captured.”
Bind up the testimony; seal the law among my disciples.
I will wait for the LORD, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob. I will put my hope in Him.
Here I am, with the children the LORD has given me. We are signs and wonders in Israel from the LORD of Hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
When people tell you to consult the spirits of the dead and the spiritists who whisper and mutter, should not a people consult their God? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
To the law and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, they have no hope of a new day.
They will roam the land, distressed and hungry. When they are hungry, they will become enraged; and looking upward, they will curse their king and their God.
Then they will look to the earth and see only distress, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. And they will be driven into darkness.

But there won't be gloom forever for people who were in trouble. In the past, He humbled the lands of Zebulun and Naphtali. But later He will bring honor to the road by the sea, across the Jordan, and to Galilee, where the nations live.
The people walking in darkness have seen a great light. Light has shone on those living in the land of the shadow of death.
You have made the nation larger, but You have not made its joy greater. They rejoice before You like people rejoice at harvest, or like people celebrate when they divide the plunder.
For as in the day of Midian, You have broken the yoke that burdened them, the bar on their shoulders, and the rod of the one who oppressed them.
Every boot that tramples in battle and every coat rolled in blood will be burned as fuel for the fire.
For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will rest on His shoulders. And His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

His government and peace will keep growing, and there will be no end. He will sit on David's throne and rule His kingdom. He will make it strong and support it with justice and right living from now on and forever. The strong desire of the the LORD of Hosts will do this.
The Lord has sent a message against Jacob, and it has fallen on Israel.
All the people will know it—Ephraim and those who live in Samaria. In pride and with an arrogant heart they say:
“The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with cut stones. The sycamore trees have been cut down, but we will replace them with cedar trees.”
So the the LORD has raised up Rezin's enemies against him and stirred up his foes.
Arameans from the east and Philistines from the west have swallowed Israel up. Even after all this, His anger has not turned away; His hand is still raised.
But the people did not turn back to Him who struck them. They did not seek the the LORD of Hosts.
In one day the the LORD will cut off Israel's head and tail—both the leaders and the ordinary people.
The elder and respected man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
The leaders of this people lead them the wrong way, and those who follow them are ruined.

So the Lord will not be happy with their young men, and He will not have mercy on their orphans and widows. Everyone is ungodly and does evil, and every mouth speaks foolish things. Even after all this, His anger has not turned away; His hand is still raised.
Wickedness burns like a fire. It eats up thorns and briars and sets the forest thickets on fire, so smoke rises in columns.
Because of the anger of the the LORD of Hosts, the land is burned, and the people become fuel for the fire. No one spares even his own brother.
They grab food on the right but are still hungry. They eat on the left but are not full. Each one even turns against his own people.
Manasseh fights Ephraim, and Ephraim fights Manasseh. Together they turn against Judah. Even after all this, His anger has not turned away; His hand is still raised.
Woe to those who make unfair laws and write harmful rules.
They keep the poor from getting justice and take rights from the needy among my people. They make widows their prize and rob orphans.
What will you do when punishment comes, when disaster comes from far away? Who will you run to for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
Nothing will be left except to crouch among prisoners or fall among the dead. Even then, His anger will not turn away; His hand will still be raised.
Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger! The club in its hand is My wrath.
I send him against a godless nation. I order him to attack a people who make Me angry, to take loot and grab plunder, and to trample them down like mud in the streets.
But that is not what he plans, and that is not what he thinks. In his heart he plans to destroy and wipe out many nations.
For he says, "Are not all my commanders kings?
Is not Kalno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
Just as my hand seized the kingdoms of the idols, whose carved images were greater than those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
will I not do to Jerusalem and her idols what I did to Samaria and her images?"
When the Lord has finished all His work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, He will punish the king of Assyria for his proud heart and his proud eyes.
For he boasts, "By my own strength I did this. By my wisdom I have understanding. I moved the borders of nations. I plundered their treasures. Like a mighty man I brought down their kings.
My hand found the wealth of the nations like a nest. Like gathering abandoned eggs, I gathered all the countries. No one flapped a wing, opened its beak, or chirped."
Does an ax brag over the one who swings it? Does a saw act greater than the one who uses it? It is as if a rod could lift the one who holds it, or a club could wave the one who carries it!
So the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, will send a wasting sickness among his strong warriors. Under his glory a fire will burn like a blazing flame.
The Light of Israel will become a fire, and their Holy One a flame. In one day it will burn and consume his thorns and briers.
It will completely destroy the glory of his forests and his fruitful fields, body and soul. It will be like a sick person wasting away.
The trees left in his forest will be so few that a child could count them.
In that day, the remnant of Israel and the survivors of Jacob's house will no longer depend on the one who struck them. Instead, they will truly depend on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant will return, a remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.
Though your people, Israel, are like the sand by the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction has been decided, and it will be full of justice.
For the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, will carry out the destruction that has been decided throughout the whole land.
Therefore this is what the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, says: "My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrians. They will beat you with a rod and lift a club against you, as Egypt did.
But in a very short time My wrath will end, and My anger will be turned to their destruction."
The LORD of Hosts will stir up a whip against them, as when He struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will raise His staff over the sea, as He did in Egypt.
In that day their burden will be lifted from your shoulders, and their yoke from your neck. The yoke will be broken because your neck has grown fat.
He has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. At Michmash he stores his supplies.
They have crossed over the pass. They camp at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul runs away.
Cry out, O daughter of Gallim! Listen, O Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is in flight. The people of Gebim hide.
This very day he will stop at Nob. He will shake his fist at the mountain of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, will cut off the branches with terrifying power. The tall trees will be cut down, and the lofty ones will be brought low.
He will clear the thickets of the forest with an iron tool, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.
A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots will bear fruit.
The Spirit of the LORD will rest on Him—the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
He will delight in the fear of the LORD. He will not judge by what His eyes see, or decide by what His ears hear.

But with righteousness He will judge the poor, and with fairness He will decide for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of His mouth, and with the breath of His lips He will slay the wicked.
Righteousness will be His belt, and faithfulness the sash around His waist.
The wolf will live with the lamb, the leopard will lie down with the goat, the calf and the lion and the fattened calf will be together, and a little child will lead them.
The cow and the bear will feed; their young will lie down together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox.
The nursing child will play by the cobra's hole, and the weaned child will put his hand into the viper's den.
They will not hurt or destroy on all My holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
In that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples; the nations will seek Him, and His resting place will be glorious.
In that day the Lord will reach out His hand a second time to bring back the remnant of His people who are left—from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
He will raise a banner for the nations and gather the exiles of Israel; He will collect the scattered people of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
Ephraim's jealousy will fade away, and those who trouble Judah will be cut off. Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah, and Judah will not trouble Ephraim.
They will swoop down on the Philistines to the west; together they will plunder the people of the east. They will lay their hand on Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will be subject to them.
The LORD will dry up the gulf of the Egyptian sea; with a scorching wind He will wave His hand over the Euphrates. He will split it into seven streams, so that people can cross in sandals.
There will be a highway for the remnant of His people who are left from Assyria, as there was for Israel when they came up from the land of Egypt.
In that day you will say, “I will give thanks to You, the LORD, for though You were angry with me, Your anger has turned away, and You comfort me.”
Surely God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For the LORD, the LORD Himself, is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.
With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.
In that day you will say, “Give thanks to the LORD; call on His name; make known His deeds among the peoples; proclaim that His name is exalted.”
Sing to the LORD, for He has done glorious things; let this be known in all the earth.
Cry out and shout, O dweller of Zion, for great is the Holy One of Israel among you.
This is a message against Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
"Raise a banner on a bare hill. Raise your voice to them. Wave your hand, and let them enter the gates of the nobles.
I have commanded My holy ones. I have also called My mighty men to carry out My anger—those who rejoice in My victory."
Listen to the roar on the mountains, like a great crowd! Listen to the uproar among the kingdoms, like nations gathering together! The LORD of Hosts is gathering an army for war.
They come from a faraway land, from the ends of the heavens—the LORD and the weapons of His wrath—to destroy the whole earth.
"Wail, for the day of the LORD is near. It will come like destruction from the Almighty."
So all hands will go limp, and every heart will melt.
They will be terrified. Pain and sorrow will seize them. They will twist in pain like a woman giving birth. They will stare at each other, their faces burning with fear.
See, the day of the LORD is coming—cruel, with fury and burning anger—to make the earth a wasteland and destroy its sinners.
The stars of heaven and their constellations will not give their light. The sun will be dark when it rises, and the moon will not shine.
"I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their sins. I will end the pride of the arrogant and bring down the pride of the ruthless.
I will make people rarer than pure gold, and mankind rarer than the gold of Ophir.
So I will shake the heavens, and the earth will move from its place, because of the wrath of the LORD of Hosts and the day of His burning anger."
Like a hunted deer and like sheep with no shepherd, each person will turn to his own people and run to his own land.
Whoever is found will be stabbed. Whoever is caught will fall by the sword.
Their babies will be smashed before their eyes. Their houses will be looted, and their wives will be abused.
"See, I will stir up the Medes against them. They will not care about silver or want gold.
Their bows will strike down the young men. They will have no mercy on babies, and they will not spare children."
Babylon, the jewel of kingdoms, the glory and pride of the Chaldeans, will be like Sodom and Gomorrah when God destroyed them.
It will never be lived in or settled again. No Arab will pitch a tent there, and no shepherd will make his flock lie down there.
Desert animals will lie there. Owls will fill its houses. Ostriches will live there, and wild goats will jump around.
Hyenas will howl in its forts, and jackals will live in its fancy palaces. Its time is near, and its days will not be long.
For the LORD will have mercy on Jacob. Once again He will choose Israel and settle them in their own land. The foreigner will join them and unite with the house of Jacob.

Nations will take them and bring them to their own place. The house of Israel will own them as male and female servants in the LORD’s land. They will make captives of their captors and rule over their oppressors.
On the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain and torment and the hard labor forced on you,
you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon: “How the oppressor has ceased! The golden city has ceased!”
The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of rulers.
It struck the peoples in anger with blows that never stopped. It ruled the nations with a fury that never held back.
All the earth is at rest and quiet now; they break into singing.
Even the cypresses and the cedars of Lebanon rejoice over you: “Since you have been laid low, no woodcutter comes up against us.”
Sheol below is stirred up to meet you when you come. It wakes the spirits of the dead to greet you—all the leaders of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
They all answer and say to you, “You too have become weak, as we are. You have become like us.”
Your pride is brought down to Sheol, along with the sound of your harps. Maggots are spread out beneath you, and worms cover you.
How you have fallen from heaven, O morning star, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to the earth, O destroyer of nations.
You said in your heart, “I will ascend to heaven. I will raise my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mount of assembly in the far north.
I will rise above the tops of the clouds. I will make myself like the Most High.”
But you will be brought down to Sheol, to the lowest depths of the pit.
Those who see you will stare. They will think, “Is this the man who shook the earth and made kingdoms tremble,
who turned the world into a desert and destroyed its cities, who never let his prisoners go home?”
All the kings of the nations lie in honor, each in his own tomb.

But you are thrown out of your grave like a hated branch. You are covered with the dead, with those pierced by the sword, with those who go down to the stones of the pit, like a body trampled underfoot.
You will not join them in burial, because you destroyed your land and killed your people. May the children of evildoers never be named again.
Get ready to slaughter his sons for the sins of their fathers, so they will never rise again to take the land or fill the world with cities.
“I will rise up against them,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will cut off from Babylon her name and remnant, her children and grandchildren,” declares the LORD.
“I will make her a home for owls and swamps. I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD of Hosts has sworn: “Surely, as I have planned, so it will be; as I have purposed, so it will stand—
to break Assyria in My land and trample him on My mountains. His yoke will be taken from them, and his burden will be removed from their shoulders.”
This is the plan made for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
For the LORD of Hosts has purposed, and who can stop Him? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?
In the year King Ahaz died, this message came:
Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken. For from the root of the snake a viper will come, and its fruit will be a flying serpent.
The firstborn of the poor will eat, and the needy will lie down in safety. But I will kill your root with famine, and your remnant I will slay.
Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt in fear, all you Philistines! For smoke comes from the north, and there is no straggler in its ranks.
What answer will be given to the messengers of the nations? “The LORD has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of His people will find refuge.”
This is a message about Moab. The city of Ar in Moab is ruined—destroyed in one night. The city of Kir in Moab is also ruined—destroyed in one night.
The people of Dibon go up to their temple to cry. Moab wails at its high places of worship. It wails over Nebo and Medeba. Everyone shaves their head, and every beard is cut off.
In the streets, people wear sackcloth. On the rooftops and in the squares, everyone wails and weeps.
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out. Their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. So Moab's soldiers cry out, and their hearts tremble.

My heart cries out for Moab. Her refugees run as far as Zoar and Eglath-shelishiyah. They go up the road to Luhith, weeping as they go. On the road to Horonaim, they cry out that everything is destroyed.
The waters of Nimrim are dried up, and the grass is withered. The pasture is dried up, and the green plants are gone.
So the wealth they saved and stored up, they carry away across the Brook of the Willows.
Their cry of grief has spread around Moab's borders. It reaches Eglaim and Beer-elim.
The waters of Dimon are full of blood. But I will bring even more trouble on Dimon. I will send a lion against those who escape from Moab and against those left in the land.
Send lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela in the desert to Mount Zion.
Like birds pushed from their nests, the women of Moab will gather at the crossing places of the Arnon River.
Give wise advice and make a fair decision. Hide the refugees so well that even at noon it is like night. Do not give them up.
Let my people who were driven out live among you, Moab. Be a safe place for them from the destroyer. The attacker is finished. Destruction has ended. Those who crush the land are gone.
Then a throne will be set up in love, and a faithful ruler from the house of David will sit on it. He will judge, seek justice, and be quick to do what is right.
We have heard of Moab's great pride. He is very proud. His pride, his anger, and his boasting are not right.
So Moab will wail, and everyone will wail for Moab. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, deeply wounded.

The fields of Heshbon are dying. The vines of Sibmah are failing. Foreign rulers have cut down her finest vines. They reached as far as Jazer and wandered into the desert. Her branches spread out and crossed the sea.
So I will weep for Jazer and for the vines of Sibmah. I will water you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh. The joyful shouts over your summer fruit and harvest have stopped.
Joy and gladness are gone from the orchards. No one sings or shouts in the vineyards. The grape treaders do not press wine. I have stopped the harvest shout.
So my heart aches for Moab like a harp. My inner being aches for Kir Hareseth.
When Moab goes up to his high place, worn out, he will go to his temple to pray, but he will not succeed.
This is the word the LORD spoke long ago about Moab.

But now the LORD says, "Within three years—like the years of a hired worker—Moab's glory will be brought low, along with all his great crowd. Only a small remnant will be left, and it will not be strong."
This is a message about Damascus: Look, Damascus will stop being a city and will become a pile of ruins.
The cities of Aroer will be left empty. They will be places where flocks rest, and no one will scare them away.
The fortified city will be gone from Ephraim, and the kingdom will be gone from Damascus. The rest of Aram will be like Israel's glory, says the LORD of Hosts.
In that day, Jacob's glory will fade, and his body will grow thin.
It will be like a worker cutting grain and gathering the heads with his arm. It will be like someone picking grain heads in the Valley of Rephaim.
Only a few olives will be left, like olives left after beating a tree—two or three on the top branch, four or five on the fruitful branches, says the LORD, the God of Israel.
In that day, people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will see the Holy One of Israel.
They will not look to the altars their hands made, and they will not respect what their fingers made—the Asherah poles and the incense altars.
In that day, their strong cities will be like a deserted forest and a leftover high branch, left behind when the Israelites came through. The land will be a wasteland.
You forgot the God who saves you, and you did not remember the Rock who protects you. So you plant pleasant plants and sow vines from other lands.
On the day you plant them, they grow fast, and in the morning your seed blooms. But the harvest will be gone in a day of sickness and deep pain.
How terrible for the many people who roar like the sea! How terrible for the rushing nations that rush like mighty waters!
The nations rush like many waters, but the LORD will warn them, and they will run far away. They will be chased like chaff on a hill before the wind, like a tumbleweed before a storm.
In the evening, trouble comes. By morning, it is gone. That is what happens to those who rob us and take our things.
Woe to the land of whirring wings beyond the rivers of Cush.

It sends messengers by sea in boats made of papyrus, over the water. Go, swift messengers, to a people tall and smooth-skinned, to a people feared far and wide, an aggressive nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers.
All you people of the world, you who live on the earth, when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it, and when a trumpet sounds, you will hear it.
For this is what the LORD says to me: “I will remain quiet and watch from My dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”
For before the harvest, when the blossom is gone and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with pruning knives and prune away the spreading branches.
They will all be left to the mountain birds of prey and to the wild animals; the birds of prey will feed on them all summer, and the wild animals will feed on them all winter.

At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of Hosts from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people feared far and wide, an aggressive nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers—to Mount Zion, the place of the Name of the LORD of Hosts.
A message about Egypt: Look, the LORD rides on a swift cloud and comes to Egypt. Egypt’s idols tremble before Him, and the hearts of the Egyptians melt inside them.
“I will stir up Egyptian against Egyptian—brother against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of the Egyptians will be emptied out inside them. I will confuse their plans, and they will turn to idols, spirits of the dead, mediums, and spiritists.
I will hand the Egyptians over to a harsh master, and a fierce king will rule over them,” declares the Lord, the LORD of Hosts.
The waters of the sea will dry up, and the river will be parched and dry.
The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will shrink and dry up. The reeds and rushes will wither.
The papyrus by the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, and all the fields planted by the Nile will dry up, blow away, and be gone.
The fishermen will mourn, and all who cast hooks into the Nile will grieve; those who spread nets on the water will waste away.
The workers in flax will be ashamed, and the weavers of fine linen will turn pale.
Its pillars will be crushed, and all who work for wages will be sick at heart.
The princes of Zoan are fools; Pharaoh’s wise advisors give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, “I am a son of wise men, a son of ancient kings”?
Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you and reveal what the LORD of Hosts has planned against Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become fools; the princes of Memphis are deluded. The cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
The LORD has poured into her a spirit of confusion. Egypt has been led astray in all she does, like a drunkard staggering around in his vomit.
Egypt will be helpless; no one, from the greatest to the least, will be able to do anything.
In that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble and fear at the waving of the hand of the LORD of Hosts, which He will raise against them.
The land of Judah will bring terror to Egypt; everyone who hears Judah mentioned will be afraid, because of what the LORD of Hosts is planning against them.
In that day five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear loyalty to the LORD of Hosts. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.
In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the heart of Egypt and a pillar to the LORD near her border.
It will be a sign and witness to the LORD of Hosts in Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of their oppressors, He will send them a Savior and Defender, and He will rescue them.
So the LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and on that day the Egyptians will know the LORD. They will worship Him with sacrifices and offerings; they will make vows to the LORD and keep them.
The LORD will strike Egypt with a plague; He will strike and heal. So they will turn to the LORD, and He will answer their prayers and heal them.
In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will go to Egypt, and the Egyptians to Assyria. The Egyptians and Assyrians will worship together.
In that day Israel will be third, along with Egypt and Assyria—a blessing in the middle of the earth.
The LORD of Hosts will bless them and say, “Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance.”
In the year that the Assyrian commander came to Ashdod, when Sargon, king of Assyria, sent him, he fought in Ashdod and captured it.
At that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz. He said, "Go, take the sackcloth off your waist and the sandals off your feet." Isaiah did as he was told and walked around naked and barefoot.

"Just as My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and warning against Egypt and Cush, so the king of Assyria will lead away Egypt's captives and Cush's exiles—young and old—naked and barefoot, with their backsides uncovered, bringing shame on Egypt.
Those who trusted in Cush and boasted in Egypt will be dismayed and ashamed."
On that day the people living along this coast will say, "Look at what happened to those we relied on, those we ran to for help to be saved from the king of Assyria. How can we escape now?"
This is a message about the Desert by the Sea. Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev, an invader comes from the desert, from a land of terror.
A harsh vision has been shown to me. The traitor betrays, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media! I will put an end to all her groaning.
So my body is full of pain. Sharp pains have seized me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am confused by what I hear, and I am terrified by what I see.
My heart pounds, and fear makes me shake. The evening I hoped for has become a horror to me.
They set the table and spread the cloth. They eat and drink. Rise up, you princes, and oil your shields!
For the Lord says to me, "Go, post a lookout, and have him report what he sees."
When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs, riders on donkeys, and riders on camels, let him watch very carefully.
The lookout shouted, "Day after day, my lord, I stand on the watchtower; every night I stay at my post."
Then the lookout saw a man in a chariot with a team of horses coming, and he called out, "Babylon has fallen! It has fallen! All the carved images of her gods lie shattered on the ground!"
My people, crushed on the threshing floor, I tell you what I have heard from the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel.
This is a message about Dumah. Someone calls to me from Seir, "Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?"
The watchman replies, "Morning is coming, but night is coming too. If you would ask, then come back and ask."
This is a message about Arabia. You caravans of Dedanites, camp in the thickets of Arabia.
Bring water for the thirsty, O people of the land of Tema. Meet the runaway with bread.
For they are running from the sword, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heavy battle.
For the Lord says to me, "Within one year, as a hired worker would count it, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end.
The remaining archers and warriors of Kedar will be few." The The LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
This is an oracle about the Valley of Vision: What is wrong with you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops?
O city full of commotion, O town full of noise! Your dead did not die by the sword, nor did they die in battle.
All your leaders have run away together; they were captured without a bow. All who were found were taken together; they fled far away.
So I said, "Turn away from me; let me weep bitterly. Do not try to comfort me about the destruction of my people."
For the Lord, the the LORD of Hosts, has a day of uproar, trampling, and confusion in the Valley of Vision—walls are broken down, and cries for help reach the mountains.
Elam takes up the quiver, with chariots and horsemen, and Kir gets its shields ready.
Your best valleys are full of chariots, and horsemen are posted at the gates.
He has stripped away the defenses of Judah. On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
You saw that there were many breaks in the wall of the City of David. You gathered the water of the lower pool.
You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore down houses to strengthen the wall.
You made a reservoir between the walls for the water of the old pool, but you did not look to the One who made it, or think about Him who planned it long ago.
On that day the Lord, the the LORD of Hosts, called for weeping and wailing, for shaved heads and wearing sackcloth.
But look—joy and gladness! They slaughter cattle and kill sheep, eat meat, and drink wine. "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
The The LORD of Hosts has revealed this to me: "Surely this sin will not be forgiven you until you die," says the Lord, the the LORD of Hosts.
This is what the Lord, the the LORD of Hosts, says: "Go, say to Shebna, the steward in charge of the palace:
"What are you doing here, and who gave you the right to cut out a tomb for yourself here—carving your tomb on the height and hollowing out a resting place for yourself in the rock?
"Look, you strong man! The The LORD is about to shake you violently. He will grab you,
"roll you into a ball and throw you into a wide land. There you will die, and there your glorious chariots will stay—a shame to your master's house.
"I will push you out of your job, and you will be pulled down from your place.
"In that day I will call My servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
"I will clothe him with your robe and tie your sash around him. I will give him your authority, and he will be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
"I will place the key to the house of David on his shoulder. What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.
"I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will become a throne of glory to his father's house.
"All the glory of his father's house will hang on him: the children and the offshoots—all the small containers, from bowls to jars.
"In that day, declares the the LORD of Hosts, the peg driven into a firm place will give way; it will be cut off and fall, and the load hanging on it will be cut down. For the the LORD has spoken."
This is a message about Tyre: Wail, ships of Tarshish, because Tyre is destroyed. There is no house left and no harbor. The news has come to them from the land of Cyprus.
Be quiet, you people who live along the coast, and you merchants of Sidon whose traders crossed the sea.
On the great waters came the grain of the Nile. The harvest of the river was her wealth, and she became the marketplace of the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, fortress of the sea, because the sea says, "I have not been in labor or given birth. I have not raised young men or brought up young women."
When the news reaches Egypt, they will be in pain at the news about Tyre.
Cross over to Tarshish. Wail, you people who live along the coast.
Is this your joyful city? It began long ago, and its people carried it to faraway lands to settle.
Who planned this against Tyre, the city that crowns others? Its merchants are like princes, and its traders are honored people of the earth.
The LORD of Hosts planned it, to bring down all her pride and beauty and to humble all the honored people of the earth.
Flood your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish; the harbor is gone.
He has stretched out His hand over the sea and shaken kingdoms. The LORD has given a command about Canaan to destroy its strongholds.
And He said, "You will no longer rejoice, you crushed virgin daughter of Sidon. Get up and cross over to Cyprus. Even there you will find no rest."
Look at the land of the Chaldeans. They were not a people. Assyria made it a home for desert animals. They built its towers, stripped its palaces, and left it in ruins.
Wail, ships of Tarshish, because your stronghold is destroyed.
In that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the life of one king. At the end of seventy years, Tyre will be like the song of a prostitute.
Take a harp and go around the city, you forgotten prostitute. Play well and sing many songs, so you will be remembered.
After seventy years, the LORD will pay attention to Tyre. She will go back to earning money and will sell herself to every kingdom on earth.
But her profits and her pay will be holy to the LORD. They will not be stored or saved. Instead, her profits will provide food and clothing for those who worship the LORD.
Look, the LORD is going to empty the earth and ruin it. He will twist its surface and scatter the people who live there.
Everyone will face the same fate: the people and the priests, servants and masters, maids and mistresses, buyers and sellers, lenders and borrowers, and creditors and debtors.
The earth will be completely emptied and stripped bare, because the LORD has spoken this word.
The earth dries up and withers. The world wastes away and withers. Even the proud leaders of the earth waste away.
The earth is polluted by those who live on it, because they broke God's laws, changed His rules, and broke His lasting agreement.
So a curse eats up the earth, and the people who live there are guilty. That is why the people of the earth are burned up, and only a few are left.
The new wine is gone, the vine droops, and everyone who was happy is groaning.
The happy sound of tambourines stops. The noise of party people ends. The joy of the harp stops.
No one sings while drinking wine. Strong drink tastes bitter to those who drink it.
The ruined city is broken down. Every house is shut tight, and no one can enter.
In the streets people cry out because there is no wine. All joy has faded. The happiness of the earth has gone away.
The city is left in ruins. Its gate is smashed to pieces.
This is how it will be on earth among the nations: like shaking an olive tree, or like the last grapes picked after the harvest.
They raise their voices and sing. They shout from the sea about the majesty of the LORD.
So give glory to the LORD in the east. In the islands of the sea, honor the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
From the ends of the earth we hear songs: "Glory to the Righteous One." But I said, "I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Woe to me! Traitors betray! Traitors betray completely!"
Terror, pits, and traps wait for you, people of the earth!
Anyone who runs from the sound of terror will fall into a pit. Anyone who climbs out of the pit will be caught in a trap. The windows of heaven are open, and the foundations of the earth shake.
The earth is completely broken. It is split apart. It shakes violently.
The earth staggers like a drunk person and sways like a small shelter. Its sin is heavy on it. It falls and will not rise again.
In that day, the LORD will punish the armies of heaven above and the kings of the earth below.
They will be gathered like prisoners in a pit. They will be locked in a prison. After many days, they will be punished.
Then the moon will be ashamed, and the sun will be embarrassed, because the LORD of Hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem. His glory shines before His elders.
The LORD, you are my God. I will lift you up. I will praise your name, because you have done amazing things. Your plans from long ago are faithful and true.
For you have turned the city into a pile of rubble. You have destroyed the fortified city. The palace of foreigners is gone forever. It will never be rebuilt.
So strong people will honor you, and nations that are cruel will fear you.

For you have been a safe place for the poor, a safe place for people in need when they are in trouble. You have been shelter from the storm and shade from the heat. The cruel people's angry breath is like a storm hitting a wall.
Like heat in a dry land, you quiet the noise of foreigners. Like heat cooled by the shade of a cloud, you bring down the song of cruel people.
On this mountain, the LORD of Hosts will make a feast of rich food for all people. It will be a feast of aged wine, of rich food full of flavor, and of the finest wine.
He will destroy on this mountain the covering spread over all peoples, the veil that is over all nations.
He will swallow up death forever. The Lord the LORD will wipe away tears from every face. He will take away the shame of His people from the whole earth, because the the LORD has spoken.
On that day people will say, "Look, this is our God! We waited for Him, and He saved us. This is the LORD; we waited for Him. Let us be glad and rejoice in His salvation!"
For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain, and Moab will be trampled down where it stands, like straw is trampled in a manure pile.
He will spread his hands in the middle of them, like a swimmer spreading his hands to swim. But the the LORD will bring down their pride, along with all their clever work.
The high walls of your fortress He will bring down. He will level them and throw them to the ground, down to the dust.
In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: “We have a strong city. God will make salvation its walls and defenses.
Open the gates so the righteous nation can come in—the nation that stays faithful.
You will keep him in perfect peace when his mind stays on You, because he trusts in You.
Trust in the LORD forever, because the LORD God is a rock that lasts forever. “
He has brought down the people who live in high places and the proud city. He lays it low to the ground and brings it down to dust.
The poor and needy walk all over it.
The path of those who do right is smooth. You make the road straight for those who do right. “
Yes, we wait for You, the LORD, on the path of Your justice. We long for Your name and Your fame.
My soul longs for You at night, and my spirit searches for You at dawn. When Your judgments come to the earth, the people of the world learn to do right.
Even if the wicked are treated kindly, they still do not learn to do right. In a land of honest people, they act unfairly and ignore the LORD’s greatness. “
The LORD, You lift Your hand, but they do not see it. Let them see how much You care for Your people so they will be ashamed. Let the fire meant for Your enemies burn them up.
The LORD, You will give us peace, because You have done all our work for us.
The LORD our God, other rulers besides You have ruled over us, but we will remember only Your name. “
The dead will not live again. The spirits of the dead will not rise. So You punished and destroyed them, and wiped out all memory of them.
You have made the nation bigger, the LORD. You have made it bigger and are honored. You have pushed its borders to the ends of the earth.
The LORD, when they were in trouble, they looked for You. They whispered a prayer when Your discipline was on them. “
Like a pregnant woman who twists and cries out in pain, so we were before You, the LORD.
We were pregnant and in pain, but we gave birth only to wind. We did not bring salvation to the earth, and we did not bring new life into the world.
Your dead will live. Their bodies will rise. Wake up and sing, you who live in the dust! For Your dew is like the morning dew, and the earth will give birth to the dead.”
“Go, My people. Enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourselves for a little while until the anger passes.”
For the LORD is coming out of His place to punish the people of the earth for their sin. The earth will show its blood and will not hide its murdered people anymore.
On that day, the LORD will use His fierce, great, and strong sword to punish Leviathan, the fleeing serpent—Leviathan the twisting serpent—and He will kill the dragon in the sea.
On that day, people will sing, "A delightful vineyard!"
"I, the LORD, watch over it. I water it all the time. I guard it day and night so no one can harm it.
