I have no anger. If only thorns and briers stood against Me, I would march against them in battle and burn them all up.
Or let them take hold of My strength and make peace with Me—yes, let them make peace with Me."
In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will blossom and bud, and fill the whole world with fruit.
Did the LORD strike Israel the same way He struck its enemies? Was Israel killed like the people who attacked it?
By warfare and exile, You fought against her. He removed her with His fierce wind on the day of the east wind.
So Jacob's guilt will be forgiven, and the result of removing his sin will be this: he will make all the altar stones like crushed chalk, and no Asherah poles or incense altars will remain standing.
The fortified city will be deserted. It will be like a lonely home left in the wilderness. There calves will graze, and there they will lie down and strip its branches bare.

When its branches dry up, they will break off. Women will come and use them for firewood. This is a people without understanding, so their Maker will not have compassion on them, and their Creator will show them no favor.
On that day, the LORD will thresh from the Euphrates River to the brook of Egypt, and you, people of Israel, will be gathered one by one.
On that day, a great trumpet will sound, and those who were perishing in Assyria and those who were exiled in Egypt will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
Woe to the proud crown of Ephraim! Its fading flower of glory sits on the head of a rich valley, but its people are beaten down by wine.
Look, the Lord has a strong and mighty one. He comes like a hailstorm and a destroying wind, like a flood of mighty waters, and He will throw that crown down to the earth.
The proud crown of Ephraim will be trampled underfoot.
Its fading flower of glory, on the head of the rich valley, will be like a ripe fig picked before summer. As soon as someone sees it, he swallows it.
In that day the LORD of Hosts will be a crown of glory and a beautiful wreath for the rest of His people.
He will give a spirit of justice to the one who sits in judgment, and strength to those who turn back the attack at the gate.

But even these stagger with wine and strong drink. Priest and prophet stagger with strong drink; they are swallowed up by wine and stagger with strong drink. They make mistakes in their visions and stumble in their judgments.
All their tables are covered with vomit and filth, so there is no clean place.
They ask, "Who is he trying to teach? Who can understand his message? Is it babies just taken from milk, or little ones taken from the breast?"
They say it is rule after rule, rule after rule, line after line, line after line, a little here, a little there.
So the LORD will speak to this people through people with strange lips and a foreign tongue.
He told them, "This is rest; let the weary rest. This is a quiet place." But they would not listen.

So the word of the LORD will come to them as rule after rule, rule after rule, line after line, line after line, a little here, a little there. They will go and fall backward, be broken, be trapped, and be caught.
So listen to the word of the LORD, you mockers who rule this people in Jerusalem.

You say, "We made a deal with death, and we have an agreement with the grave. When the destroying flood passes through, it will not reach us, because we made lies our shelter and hid behind falsehood."
So the Lord, the LORD, says: "Look, I am placing a stone in Zion. It is a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation. Whoever trusts in it will not be shaken.
I will use justice as a measuring line and righteousness as a plumb line. Hail will sweep away the shelter of lies, and water will flood the hiding place.
Your deal with death will be canceled, and your agreement with the grave will not stand. When the destroying flood passes through, you will be trampled by it.
As often as it passes through, it will take you. Morning after morning it will pass through, day and night. Understanding the message will bring sheer terror.
The bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap up in."
The LORD will rise up like He did at Mount Perazim. He will be angry like He was in the Valley of Gibeon. He will do His strange work, His unusual task.
So now do not mock, or your chains will become stronger. I have heard a decision of destruction from the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, against the whole earth.
Listen and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my words.
Does a farmer plow all day just to plant? Does he keep turning and breaking up his soil?
When he has leveled the ground, does he not scatter dill and sow cumin? Does he not plant wheat in rows, barley in its place, and spelt along the edge?
His God teaches him the right way and instructs him.
Dill is not threshed with a heavy threshing board, and a cart wheel is not rolled over cumin. Dill is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
Grain is crushed for bread, but not forever. He drives his cart and horses over it, but he does not destroy it.
This too comes from the LORD of Hosts, who is wonderful in counsel and great in wisdom.
Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city where David camped! Keep going, year after year; let your festivals come back around.
I will bring trouble on Ariel. There will be mourning and crying, and to Me she will be like an altar hearth.
I will camp all around you. I will set up towers and build siege works against you.

You will be brought low. You will speak from the ground, and your words will come out muffled from the dust. Your voice will sound like a faint spirit from the ground; your speech will whisper from the dust.
But the crowd of your enemies will be like fine dust, and the crowd of cruel people like blowing chaff. Then suddenly, in an instant,
the LORD of Hosts will punish you with thunder and earthquake and a great roar, with windstorm and tempest and flames of a consuming fire.
All the nations fighting against Ariel—all who attack her, lay siege to her, and trouble her—will be like a dream, like a night vision.

It will be like a hungry person who dreams of eating but wakes up still hungry, or like a thirsty person who dreams of drinking but wakes up still thirsty and weak. So it will be with all the nations that fight against Mount Zion.
Be stunned and amazed. Blind yourselves until you cannot see. They are drunk, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
For the LORD has poured a spirit of deep sleep on you. He has shut your eyes—the prophets—and covered your heads—the seers.
The whole vision has become to you like words sealed in a scroll. If it is handed to someone who can read, he will say, "I cannot read it, because it is sealed."
Or if it is handed to someone who cannot read, he will say, "I do not know how to read a scroll."
And the Lord said: "These people draw near to Me with their mouths and honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me. Their worship of Me is only rules taught by men."
Therefore I will again do amazing things for these people—wonder after wonder. The wisdom of the wise will disappear, and the understanding of the clever will be hidden.
Woe to those who go to great depths to hide their plans from the LORD, who do their work in darkness and say, "Who sees us? Who knows what we do?"

You turn things upside down! Shall the potter be treated like the clay? Shall what is formed say to the one who formed it, "he did not make me"? Can the pottery say of the potter, "he has no understanding"?
In just a little while, won't Lebanon become a fertile field, and won't that fertile field look like a forest?
In that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll, and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
The humble will increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
For the ruthless will vanish, the mockers will disappear, and all who look for evil will be cut off.
They trap people with a word, set snares for those who argue for justice at the gate, and push aside the innocent with empty charges.
Therefore this is what the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says to the house of Jacob: "No longer will Jacob be ashamed, and no longer will his face grow pale.
For when he sees his children around him, the work of My hands, they will honor My name. They will set apart the Holy One of Jacob as holy, and they will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
Then those who wander in spirit will gain understanding, and those who grumble will accept instruction."
"Woe to the rebellious children," declares the LORD. "You carry out a plan that is not Mine. You make an agreement, but not by My Spirit, so you keep adding sin to sin.
You go down to Egypt without asking Me. You seek safety in Pharaoh's protection and hide in Egypt's shadow.
But Pharaoh's protection will become your shame, and Egypt's shelter will become your disgrace.
Even though his officials are in Zoan and his messengers have reached Hanes,
everyone will be put to shame by a people that cannot help them. They bring no help and no gain, only shame and disgrace."

This is a message about the animals of the southern desert: The people carry their wealth on donkeys' backs and their treasures on camels' humps. They travel through a hard and dangerous land, where lions and young lions live and vipers and flying serpents are found. They go to a people who cannot help them.
Egypt's help is empty and useless. That is why I call her "Rahab the Do-Nothing."
Now go and write this on a tablet in front of them. Write it in a book so it will stand as a witness for the future, forever.
These people are rebellious. They are deceitful children who refuse to listen to the LORD's teaching.
They tell the seers, "Do not see visions," and the prophets, "Do not tell us what is right. Speak smooth words to us. Prophesy pleasant lies.
Get out of the way! Turn off the road! Keep the Holy One of Israel away from us."
So the Holy One of Israel says, "Because you have rejected this message and relied on oppression and deceit,
this wrong of yours is like a wall about to fall. It bulges out and will break apart all at once, in a single moment.
It will shatter like a clay jar smashed to pieces, so completely that no broken piece will be left big enough to scoop coals from a fire or draw water from a well."
The Lord the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, has said, "By turning back and resting, you would be saved. Your strength would be quiet trust. But you were not willing.
You said you would flee on horses, so you will flee. You said you would ride fast horses, so your pursuers will be fast.
A thousand of you will run from one enemy. Five enemies will make you run, until you are left like a pole on a mountaintop or a flag on a hill."
So the LORD waits to be kind to you. He rises to show you mercy. The LORD is a God of justice. Blessed are all who wait for Him.
O people in Zion, who live in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. When you cry for help, He will be kind to you. When He hears, He will answer you.
The Lord will give you bread of hardship and water of trouble, but your Teacher will not hide Himself anymore. Your eyes will see your Teacher.
Whether you turn right or left, your ears will hear a voice behind you saying, "This is the way. Walk in it."
Then you will defile your silver-plated idols and your gold-covered statues. You will throw them away like dirty rags. You will say to them, "Get out of here!"
Then He will send rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and the food the land produces will be rich and plentiful. On that day your cattle will graze in wide pastures.
The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and fork.
On every high mountain and every hill, streams of water will flow on the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.

The moon's light will be like the sun's light, and the sun's light will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days. This will happen on the day the LORD binds up His people's brokenness and heals the wounds He gave them.
Look, the name of the LORD comes from far away. His anger burns, and thick smoke comes with Him. His lips are full of fury, and His tongue is like a fire that eats everything.
His breath is like a rushing flood that rises to the neck. He comes to sift the nations in a sieve that destroys, and He puts a bridle on the peoples' jaws to lead them astray.
You will sing as on the night of a holy feast. Your heart will rejoice like someone walking to the sound of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
The LORD will make His glorious voice heard. He will show His arm coming down with fierce anger, with a flame of fire that consumes, with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.
Assyria will be terrified at the voice of the LORD, when He strikes with His rod.
Every stroke of the rod He appoints will be to the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight them with His whirling weapons.

Topheth has been ready for a long time. It was prepared for the king. Its fire pit is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a stream of burning sulfur, sets it on fire.

How terrible it will be for those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in many chariots and many horsemen. They do not look to the Holy One of Israel, and they do not seek the LORD.
Yet He is also wise and brings disaster. He will not take back His words. He will rise up against the house of evildoers and against the helpers of evildoers.

But the Egyptians are only people, not God. Their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out His hand, the helper will stumble, and the one being helped will fall. They will all be destroyed together.

For this is what the LORD says to me: “As a lion growls, and a young lion over its prey—and though a whole group of shepherds is called against it, it is not scared by their shouts or quieted by their noise—so the LORD of Hosts will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its hill.
Like birds flying overhead, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem. He will protect and save it; He will pass over and rescue it.”
Return to Him from whom you have deeply revolted, children of Israel.
For on that day each person will reject his silver idols and gold idols, which your own hands have made and which have caused you to sin.
“Then Assyria will fall by a sword that is not from a person. A sword not from a person will destroy him. He will run from the sword, and his young men will become forced labor.
His stronghold will pass away in terror, and his princes will panic at the battle flag,” declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
Look, a king will reign with justice, and princes will rule with fairness.
Each one will be like a shelter from the wind and a hiding place from the storm. He will be like streams of water in a dry land, and like the shade of a huge rock in a tired land.
Then the eyes of those who see will not be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
The heart of the rash will understand, and the tongue of those who stutter will speak clearly.
No longer will a fool be called noble, or a scoundrel be called respected.
A fool speaks foolish things, and his heart plans evil. He does ungodly things and speaks lies about the LORD. He leaves hungry people empty and keeps thirsty people from drink.
The weapons of a scoundrel destroy; he plans tricks to ruin poor people with lies, even when the needy ask for justice.
But a noble man plans noble things, and he stands firm in them.
Rise up, you complacent women; listen to my voice. You daughters who feel secure, hear my words.
In a little more than a year, you complacent women will tremble. The grape harvest will fail, and the fruit harvest will not come.
Tremble, you complacent women; shudder, you daughters who feel secure. Strip off your fine clothes and put on sackcloth.
Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields and the fruitful vine.
Beat them for the land of my people, now overgrown with thorns and briers. Yes, beat them for every happy house and every joyful city.
The palace will be left empty, and the busy city will be abandoned. The hill and the watchtower will become caves forever. They will be a joy for wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks.
This will last until the Spirit is poured out on us from above. Then the desert will become a fertile field, and the fertile field will seem like a forest.
Justice will live in the desert, and righteousness will stay in the fertile field.
The work of righteousness will be peace, and its service will be quiet confidence forever.
Then my people will live in a peaceful place, in safe homes and quiet resting places.
But hail will flatten the forest, and the city will sink into the lowlands.
Blessed are you who sow beside all waters and let the ox and donkey roam free.
Woe to you, destroyer, who have not been destroyed! Woe to you, traitor, who have not been betrayed! When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed; when you stop betraying, you will be betrayed.
The LORD, be gracious to us; we have waited for you. Be our arm every morning, our salvation in time of trouble.
At the sound of Your voice, peoples flee; when You are lifted up, nations scatter.
Your plunder is gathered like caterpillars gather; like locusts swarm, so people swarm over it.
The LORD is lifted high, because He lives on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
He will be the stability of your times, a wealth of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the LORD is His treasure.
Look, their brave men cry out in the streets; the messengers of peace weep bitterly.
The roads are empty; travelers have stopped using them. The agreement is broken; cities are hated; no one pays attention to people.
The land is sad and drying up; Lebanon is ashamed and wilts; Sharon is like a desert; Bashan and Carmel drop their leaves.
"Now I will rise up," says the LORD. "Now I will lift Myself up; now I will be honored.
You conceive chaff; you give birth to straw. Your breath is a fire that consumes you.
"And the peoples will be burned to ashes, like thorns cut down and set on fire.
You who are far away, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My power."
Sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling grips the godless: "Who among us can live with the consuming fire? Who among us can live with everlasting burning?"
He who walks righteously and speaks honestly, who rejects money gained by cheating, who will not take bribes, who refuses to listen to talk of bloodshed, and who will not look at evil.
He will live on high; his safe place will be a mountain fortress; his food will be given to him, and his water will be sure.
Your eyes will see the King in His beauty and view a land that stretches far away.
Your heart will ponder the terror: "Where is the scribe? Where is the weigher? Where is the one who counts the towers?"
You will no longer see the fierce people, a people with strange speech you cannot understand, stammering in a language you cannot understand.
Look at Zion, the city of our festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful home, a tent that will not be moved; its stakes will never be pulled up, and none of its ropes will be broken.
But there the LORD, our Mighty One, will be for us a place of rivers and wide canals, where no boat with oars will go, and no large ship will pass.
For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our Lawgiver, the LORD is our King; He will save us.
Your ropes are untied; they cannot hold the mast firm, nor spread the sail. Then a great amount of spoil will be divided; even the lame will carry off plunder.
And no one living there will say, "I am sick"; the people who live there will be forgiven their sin.
Come close, nations, and listen. Listen, peoples! Let the earth hear, and everything in it. Let the world and all its people hear.
For the LORD is angry with all the nations and furious with all their armies. He has marked them for destruction, and He has given them over to slaughter.
Their dead bodies will be thrown out, and the smell of their corpses will rise. The mountains will run with their blood.
All the stars in the sky will rot away, and the sky will be rolled up like a scroll. Every star will fall like withered leaves from a grapevine, like leaves falling from a fig tree.
For My sword has drunk its fill in heaven; look, it will come down on Edom, on the people I have marked for destruction.
The sword of the LORD is full of blood. It is rich with fat—from the blood of lambs and goats and the fat of rams' kidneys. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in Edom.
Wild oxen will fall along with them, and young bulls with the mighty ones. Their land will be soaked with blood, and their soil will be rich with fat.
For the LORD has a day of revenge, a year of payback to defend Zion.
The streams of Edom will turn into tar, and its dust into sulfur. The land itself will become burning tar.
It will burn day and night and never go out. Its smoke will rise forever. It will be ruined from one generation to the next, and no one will ever pass through it again.
But pelicans and porcupines will take it over. Owls and ravens will live there. He will measure it out for ruin and leave it empty and wasted.
There will be no one left to call it a kingdom, and all its princes will be nothing.
Thorns will grow in its palaces, and thistles and brambles will fill its forts. It will become a home for jackals and a place for ostriches.
Desert animals will meet hyenas there, and wild goats will call to each other. Even the night creature will settle there and find a place to rest.
There the owl will nest, lay eggs, hatch them, and gather her young in her shade. Yes, kites will gather there, each with its mate.
Search the book of the LORD and read it: Not one of these animals will be missing, and none will be without its mate. His mouth has commanded it, and His Spirit has gathered them.
He has cast lots for them, and His hand has measured out their share. They will own it forever; they will live there from generation to generation.
The desert and the dry land will be glad. The wilderness will rejoice and bloom like a crocus.

It will bloom in abundance and rejoice with joy and singing. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, along with the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the the LORD, the splendor of our God.
Strengthen weak hands and steady shaking knees.
Say to those with fearful hearts, “Be strong; do not be afraid! Your God will come with vengeance. He will repay and save you.”
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the mute tongue will shout for joy. Water will break out in the wilderness, and streams will flow in the desert.
The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground will become springs of water. In the place where jackals rest, grass will grow into reeds and papyrus.
A highway will be there, and a road. It will be called the Way of Holiness. Unclean people will not travel on it; it is for God’s people. Travelers, even fools, will not lose their way.
No lion will be there, and no wild beast will go up on it. They will not be found there. Only the redeemed will walk there.

The people the the LORD has rescued will return. They will come to Zion with singing. Everlasting joy will rest on their heads. They will be filled with gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will disappear.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
Then the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem with a large army. He stood by the channel of the upper pool, on the road to the fuller's field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came out to him.
Rabshakeh said to them, "Tell Hezekiah, 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What confidence is this that you trust in?
You say you have a plan and strength for war, but those are only empty words. On whom are you trusting now, that you have rebelled against me?
Look, you are trusting in Egypt, that broken reed staff that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it. Pharaoh king of Egypt is just like that to everyone who trusts in him.
But if you say to me, "We trust in the LORD our God," wasn't it He whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, telling Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship before this altar"?
Now make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses if you can put riders on them.
How could you drive back even one of my master's least officers, when you are relying on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
Besides, have I come up against this land to destroy it without the LORD? The LORD said to me, "Go up against this land and destroy it."'"
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, because we understand it. Don't speak to us in Hebrew where the people on the wall can hear."

Rabshakeh said, "Did my master send me to say this only to your master and to you? Didn't he also send me to the men sitting on the wall, who will eat their own waste and drink their own urine with you?"
Then Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in Hebrew, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
This is what the king says: 'Don't let Hezekiah fool you. He can't save you.
Don't let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, "The LORD will surely save us; this city won't be given to the king of Assyria."
Don't listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: "Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from his own vine and fig tree and drink water from his own well,
until I come and take you to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards."
Don't let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, "The LORD will save us." Has any god of any nation saved his land from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they save Samaria from my hand?
Which of all these gods saved their land from my hand? So how could the LORD save Jerusalem from my hand?'"
But the people were quiet and didn't answer him at all, because the king had commanded, "Don't answer him."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him everything Rabshakeh had said.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the the LORD.
He sent Eliakim, the palace manager, Shebna the writer, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They told him, “This is what Hezekiah says: ‘Today is a day of trouble, correction, and shame. It is like a woman ready to give birth who has no strength to deliver her baby.

Perhaps the the LORD your God will hear the words of the Assyrian commander, whom his master, the king of Assyria, sent to insult the living God. Perhaps He will correct him for the words the the LORD your God has heard. So pray for the people who are left.’”
So King Hezekiah’s servants went to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master that this is what the the LORD says: ‘Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, the words the servants of the king of Assyria used to insult Me.
I will put a spirit in him. He will hear a report and go back to his own country. There I will make him die by the sword.’”
When the Assyrian commander heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he went back and found the king fighting against Libnah.
Sennacherib heard that Tirhakah, king of Cush, had come out to fight against him. So he sent messengers to Hezekiah with this message:
“Tell Hezekiah king of Judah, ‘Do not let your God, the One you trust, fool you by saying that Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.
You have heard what the kings of Assyria did to all the other lands. They destroyed them completely. Do you think you will be saved?
Did the gods of the nations my fathers destroyed save them? What about the gods of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Where are the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’”
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the house of the the LORD and spread it out before the the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed to the the LORD:
“O the LORD of Armies, God of Israel, who sits above the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
Turn Your ear to me, O the LORD, and hear. Open Your eyes, O the LORD, and see. Listen to all the words Sennacherib sent to insult the living God.
It is true, O the LORD, that the kings of Assyria have destroyed all those lands.
They threw their gods into the fire and destroyed them, because those gods were not real gods. They were only wood and stone, made by human hands.
Now, O the LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone are the the LORD.”
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: “This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Because you prayed to Me about Sennacherib king of Assyria,
this is the word the the LORD has spoken against him: “The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and laughs at you. The Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head at you as you leave.
Whom did you insult and mock? Against whom did you raise your voice and lift your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!

Through your servants you insulted the Lord, and you said, “With my many chariots I climbed to the tops of the mountains, to the farthest parts of Lebanon. I cut down its tallest cedars and its best cypresses. I reached its highest point and its thickest forest.
I dug wells and drank water in foreign lands. With the soles of my feet I dried up all the rivers of Egypt.”
Have you not heard? Long ago I planned this. From ancient times I designed it. Now I have made it happen. You were to crush strong cities into piles of rubble.
That is why their people were weak. They were afraid and ashamed. They were like grass in a field, like tender green plants, like grass on a roof, burned before it can grow.
But I know when you sit down, when you go out, and when you come in. I know how you rage against Me.
Because you rage against Me and your pride has reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth. I will send you back the way you came.

“‘This will be a sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself. In the second year you will eat what grows from that. But in the third year you will plant and harvest, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The surviving remnant of the house of Judah will take root below and bear fruit above.
A remnant will go out from Jerusalem, and survivors will come from Mount Zion. The strong love of the the LORD of Armies will make this happen.
Therefore this is what the the LORD says about the king of Assyria: He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow here. He will not come against it with a shield or build a siege ramp against it.
He will go back the way he came. He will not enter this city, declares the the LORD.
I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’”
Then the angel of the the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 soldiers in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up the next morning, they were all dead bodies.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and left. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.

One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with a sword. They escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon became king after him.

In those days Hezekiah became sick and was near death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "This is what the the LORD says: Put your house in order, because you are going to die. You will not live."
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the the LORD.
He said, "Please, the LORD, remember how I have walked before You in truth and with a whole heart. I have done what is good in Your sight." Then Hezekiah cried and wept bitterly.
Then the word of the the LORD came to Isaiah:
"Go and say to Hezekiah, 'This is what the the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. I will add fifteen years to your life.
I will rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria, and I will protect this city.
This will be the sign to you from the the LORD that the the LORD will do what He has promised:
I will make the shadow on the steps of Ahaz go back ten steps.' So the sun moved back the ten steps it had gone down.
This is the writing of Hezekiah king of Judah after he was sick and got well:
I said, "In the middle of my life I must go through the gates of the grave. I am robbed of the rest of my years."
I said, "I will not see the the LORD in the land of the living. I will no longer look at people who live in this world."
My home is pulled up and carried away from me like a shepherd's tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver. He cuts me off from the loom. Day and night, You bring me to an end.
I waited until morning. Like a lion, He breaks all my bones. Day and night, You bring me to an end.
I chirp like a swallow or a crane. I moan like a dove. My eyes are weak as I look to the heights. Lord, I am in trouble; be my guarantee.
What can I say? He has spoken to me, and He has done it. I will walk carefully all my years because my soul is bitter.
Lord, by these things people live. My spirit also lives by them. You restore me to health and keep me alive.
I went through bitter pain, but it led to peace. You have loved my soul and saved it from the pit of destruction, because You have thrown all my sins behind Your back.
The grave does not thank You. Death does not praise You. Those who go down into the pit do not hope for Your truth.
The living, the living, they thank You, as I do today. Fathers tell their children about Your truth.
The the LORD came to save me. We will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the the LORD.
Isaiah had said, "Let them take a cake of figs and put it on the boil, and he will live."
Hezekiah had asked, "What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the the LORD?"
At that time, Merodach-Baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, because he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick and had gotten better.

Hezekiah was glad to see them and showed them his treasure house—the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, all his weapons, and everything in his storerooms. Nothing in his house or in his whole kingdom was left hidden from them.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and asked him, “What did these men say? And where did they come from?” Hezekiah answered, “They came to me from far away, from Babylon.”
Isaiah asked, “What did they see in your house?” Hezekiah replied, “They saw everything in my house. I did not hide anything in my storerooms from them.”
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Listen to the word of the LORD of Hosts:
‘The days are coming when everything in your house, and everything your fathers saved up until now, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left,’ says the LORD.
‘Some of your own sons, born to you, will be taken away. They will serve as eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.’”
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the LORD that you spoke is good.” For he thought, “There will be peace and truth in my days.”
"Comfort, comfort my people," says your God.
Speak kindly to Jerusalem and tell her that her hard service is over, her sin has been paid for, and she has received from the the LORD's hand double for all her sins.
A voice calls out, "Prepare the way for the the LORD in the wilderness. Make a straight road in the desert for our God."
Every valley will be raised up, and every mountain and hill will be made low. The rough ground will become level, and the rugged places will become a plain.
Then the glory of the the LORD will be shown, and all people will see it together. The the LORD has spoken.
A voice says, "Cry out!" And I asked, "What should I cry?" "All people are like grass, and all their glory is like the flowers of the field.
The grass dries up and the flowers fall when the the LORD's breath blows on them. Yes, the people are like grass.
The grass dries up and the flowers fall, but the word of our God lasts forever."

Go up on a high mountain, messenger of good news to Zion. Lift up your voice with strength, messenger of good news to Jerusalem. Lift it up; do not be afraid. Say to the towns of Judah, "Here is your God!"
Look, the Lord the the LORD comes with power, and His arm rules for Him. Look, His reward is with Him, and His pay is before Him.
He will feed His flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in His arms and carry them close to His heart. He will gently lead the mothers with their young.
Who has measured the waters in the hollow of His hand and marked off the heavens with His fingers? Who has measured the dust of the earth and weighed the mountains and hills on a scale?
Who can measure the Spirit of the the LORD, or tell Him what to do?
Who did He ask for advice? Who made Him understand and taught Him the right way? Who taught Him knowledge and showed Him the path of wisdom?
Look, the nations are like a drop in a bucket. They are counted like dust on a scale. Look, He lifts up the islands like fine dust.
Lebanon's trees would not be enough for fuel, and its animals would not be enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are nothing before Him. They are counted by Him as less than nothing, as empty.
To whom, then, will you compare God? What image will you make for Him?
An idol? A worker shapes it, and a goldsmith covers it with gold and makes silver chains for it.
A poor person chooses wood that will not rot and looks for a skilled worker to make an idol that will not fall over.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the earth was founded?
He sits above the circle of the earth, and its people are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them like a tent to live in.
He brings princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth empty.
They are barely planted and barely sown. Their stem has barely taken root in the earth when He blows on them and they dry up, and a storm carries them away like straw.
"To whom, then, will you compare Me?" asks the Holy One. "Who is equal to Me?"
Look up at the sky. Who created all these? He brings out the stars by number and calls each one by name. By His great power and strength, not one of them is missing.
Why do you say, O Jacob, and speak, O Israel, "My way is hidden from the the LORD, and my God overlooks my cause"?
Have you not known? Have you not heard? The the LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not get tired or weary. No one can understand His wisdom.
He gives strength to the tired and increases the power of the weak.
Even young people get tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.
But those who wait for the the LORD will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles. They will run and not get tired. They will walk and not grow weary.
"Be quiet before Me, you islands. Let the nations gain new strength. Let them come near and speak. Let us come together to judge.
"Who stirred up a ruler from the east and called him to do what is right? The LORD gives nations to him and makes kings fall. He turns them to dust with his sword and to straw with his bow.
"He chases them and moves on safely, along a path his feet have never walked.
"Who has done this and made it happen? He calls the generations from the beginning. I am the LORD. I am the first and the last. I am He."
The islands see this and are afraid. The ends of the earth shake with fear. They come close and gather together.
Each person helps the next and tells his brother to be strong.
The worker encourages the metalworker. The one who smooths with a hammer praises the one who hits the anvil. He says the soldering is good. Then he fastens it with nails so it will not move.
"But you, Israel, are My servant. Jacob, I chose you. You are the descendants of Abraham, My friend.
"I brought you from the far ends of the earth. I called you from its farthest corners. I said you are My servant. I chose you and did not reject you.
"Do not be afraid, because I am with you. Do not lose heart, because I am your God. I will make you strong. I will help you. I will hold you up with My right hand, which always does what is right.
"Look, all who are angry with you will be ashamed and disgraced. Those who argue with you will be as nothing and will die.
"You will look for them, but you will not find them. Those who fight against you will be as nothing, with no power.
"I am the LORD your God. I hold your right hand. I say to you not to be afraid, because I will help you.
"Do not be afraid, Jacob, you worm. Israel, you are only a few people. I will help you," says the LORD. "Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
"Look, I will make you like a new, sharp threshing tool with many teeth. You will crush mountains and break them apart. You will make hills like straw.
"You will scatter them, and the wind will carry them away. A storm will spread them out. But you will be glad in the LORD. You will praise the Holy One of Israel."
"The poor and needy look for water, but there is none. Their tongues are dry with thirst. But I, the LORD, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not leave them.
"I will open rivers on bare hills and springs in the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pool of water and dry land into flowing springs.
"I will plant cedar, acacia, myrtle, and olive trees in the desert. I will put juniper, elm, and cypress trees together in the dry land.
"Then people will see and know. They will think and understand that the hand of the LORD has done this. The Holy One of Israel has created it."
"Bring your case to court," says the LORD. "Give your best reasons," says the King of Jacob.
"Let them bring out and tell us what will happen. Tell us what happened before, so we can think about it and know how it ended. Or tell us what is coming.
"Tell us what will happen later, so we may know that you are gods. Yes, do something, good or bad, so we can be afraid and amazed.
"Look, you are nothing, and your work is worth nothing. Anyone who chooses you is disgusting.
"I stirred up someone from the north, and he came. From the east, he calls on My name. He walks on rulers like mud, like a potter trampling clay.
"Who told this from the start, so we would know? Who said it long ago, so we could say he is right? No one told it. No one heard your words.
"I was the first to tell Zion that they are coming. I sent good news to Jerusalem.
"I look, but there is no one. There is no adviser. I ask them, but they give no answer.
"Look, they are all false. Their work is nothing. Their metal statues are only wind and empty air."
Here is My Servant, whom I uphold. He is My Chosen One, and I delight in Him. I have put My Spirit on Him, and He will bring justice to the nations.
He will not shout or raise His voice. He will not make His voice heard in the streets.
He will not break a bruised reed, and He will not put out a smoldering wick. He will bring justice in a faithful way.
He will not grow weak or discouraged until He has set justice in the earth. The distant lands will put their hope in His law.

This is what God the LORD says—He who made the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and all that grows from it, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk on it:
“I, the LORD, have called You in righteousness. I will take hold of Your hand. I will keep You and make You a covenant for the people, a light for the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to bring prisoners out of the dungeon, and to bring out of prison those who sit in darkness.
I am the LORD; that is My name. I will not give My glory to another, or My praise to idols.
See, the former things have come to pass, and now I declare new things. Before they spring up, I tell you about them.”
Sing to the LORD a new song—His praise from the ends of the earth—you who go down to the sea and all that is in it, you islands and the people who live on them.
Let the desert and its towns raise their voices. Let the villages where Kedar lives be glad. Let the people of Sela sing for joy. Let them shout from the tops of the mountains.
Let them give glory to the LORD and announce His praise in the distant lands.
The LORD will go out like a mighty man. He will stir up His zeal like a warrior. He will shout—yes, He will roar—and He will win against His enemies.
“I have been silent for a long time. I have kept still and held Myself back. But now I will cry out like a woman giving birth. I will gasp and pant.
I will destroy mountains and hills. I will dry up all their plants. I will turn rivers into islands. I will dry up the pools.

I will lead blind people along a road they do not know. I will guide them on paths they have not known. I will turn darkness into light before them. I will make rough places smooth. I will do these things for them, and I will not leave them.”
But they will be turned back and put to shame—those who trust in idols, who say to metal statues, “You are our gods.”
Hear, you deaf people! Look, you blind people, so that you may see!
Who is blind but My servant, or deaf like the messenger I send? Who is blind like the one fully committed, or blind like the servant of the LORD?
You have seen many things, but you do not notice them. Your ears are open, but you do not hear.
The LORD was pleased, for the sake of His righteousness, to make His law great and glorious.
But this is a people robbed and plundered, trapped in holes and hidden in prisons. They became plunder with no one to rescue them, and loot with no one to say, “Give it back!”
Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come?
Who gave Jacob up to the robber, and Israel to the plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They would not follow His ways, and they did not obey His law.
So He poured out on them His burning anger, the fury of war. It surrounded them in flames, but they did not know it. It burned among them, but they did not take it to heart.
But now, the LORD says—He who created you, Jacob, and formed you, Israel: “Don’t be afraid, for I have rescued you. I have called you by name; you are Mine.
When you pass through the water, I will be with you, and the rivers won’t sweep you away. When you walk through fire, you won’t be burned, and the flames won’t hurt you.
“For I am the LORD, your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I gave Egypt to buy you back, and Cush and Seba to take your place.
Because you are precious to Me and honored, and I love you, I will give other people in your place and other nations in exchange for your life.
Don’t be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your children from the east and gather you from the west.
“I will say to the north, ‘Give them up!’ and to the south, ‘Don’t hold them back.’ Bring My sons from far away and My daughters from the ends of the earth—
everyone who is called by My name, whom I created for My glory, whom I formed and made.”
Bring out the people who are blind but have eyes, and the deaf but have ears.

Let all the nations gather together, and let the peoples assemble. Who among them can tell us this and show us what happened before? Let them bring their witnesses to prove they are right, and let them hear and say, “It is true.”

“You are My witnesses,” declares the LORD, “and My servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe Me and understand that I am He. Before Me no god was formed, and after Me none will come.”
“I, yes I, am the LORD, and apart from Me there is no savior.”
“I have revealed and saved and proclaimed—I, and not some foreign god among you. You are My witnesses,” declares the LORD, “and I am God.”
“Even from ancient times I am He, and no one can rescue anyone from My hand. When I act, who can undo it?”
This is what the LORD says—your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “For your sake I will send to Babylon and bring them all down as fugitives, even the Chaldeans, in the ships they are so proud of.”
“I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.”
This is what the LORD says—“He who makes a way through the sea and a path through the mighty waters,
who brings out chariot and horse, army and strong warrior. They lie down together; they do not rise again. They are snuffed out, quenched like a wick.”
“Don’t remember the former things; don’t think about the old things.
Look, I am doing something new; now it is springing up. Don’t you see it? I will make a way in the desert and rivers in the wasteland.
The wild animals will honor Me—the jackals and the ostriches—because I give water in the desert and streams in the wasteland, to give drink to My chosen people.
The people I formed for Myself will tell of My praise.”
“But you haven’t called on Me, O Jacob, and you have grown tired of Me, O Israel.
You haven’t brought Me sheep for your burnt offerings, and you haven’t honored Me with your sacrifices. I haven’t burdened you with grain offerings, and I haven’t wearied you with frankincense.
You haven’t bought Me sweet cane with money, and you haven’t satisfied Me with the fat of your sacrifices. But you have burdened Me with your sins, and you have wearied Me with your wrongs.”
“I, yes I, am He who blots out your sins for My own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
Remind Me; let us argue the case together. State your case, so that you may be proved right.”
“Your first father sinned, and your leaders rebelled against Me.
So I disgraced the leaders of the holy place, and I gave Jacob over to be destroyed and Israel to be mocked.”
"But now listen, Jacob, My servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
This is what the LORD says—He who made you and formed you in the womb, and who will help you: Do not be afraid, Jacob, My servant, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
For I will pour water on the thirsty land and streams on the dry ground. I will pour out My Spirit on your offspring and My blessing on your descendants.
They will spring up like grass in a meadow, like poplar trees by flowing streams.
One will say, 'I belong to the LORD,' another will call himself by Jacob's name, and still another will write on his hand, 'The LORD's,' and take the name Israel."
"This is what the LORD says—Israel's King and Redeemer, the LORD of Hosts: I am the first and I am the last; apart from Me there is no God.
Who then is like Me? Let him proclaim it. Let him declare and lay out before Me what has happened since I established My ancient people, and what is yet to come—yes, let them foretell what will come.
Do not tremble; do not be afraid. Did I not proclaim this and foretell it long ago? You are My witnesses. Is there any God besides Me? No, there is no other Rock; I know not one."
All who make idols are nothing, and the things they treasure are worthless. Those who would speak up for them are blind and ignorant; they will be put to shame.
Who would shape a god or cast an idol that cannot help anyone?
People who do such things will be put to shame. Craftsmen are only human. Let them all come together and stand; they will be terrified and ashamed.

The blacksmith takes a tool and works with it in the coals. He shapes an idol with hammers and forges it with his strong arm. He gets hungry and loses his strength; he drinks no water and grows faint.
The carpenter measures with a line and marks it with a pencil. He roughs it out with a plane and marks it with a compass. He shapes it in human form, with human beauty, to live in a shrine.
He cuts down cedars, or perhaps takes a cypress or oak. He lets it grow among the trees of the forest, or plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow.
It is used as fuel for burning. He takes some of it to warm himself, kindles a fire, and bakes bread. But he also makes a god and worships it; he makes an idol and bows down to it.
Half of the wood he burns in the fire. Over the other half he roasts meat, eats his fill, and warms himself. Then he says, "Ah! I am warm; I have seen the fire."
From the rest he makes a god, his idol. He bows down to it and worships. He prays to it and says, "Save me, for you are my god."
They know nothing and understand nothing. Their eyes are plastered over so they cannot see, and their minds are closed so they cannot understand.

No one stops to think. No one has the knowledge or understanding to say, "Half of it I burned in the fire. I also baked bread over its coals, roasted meat, and ate. Shall I make a detestable thing from what is left? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?"
Such a person feeds on ashes. A deluded heart leads him astray. He cannot save himself or say, "Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?"
"Remember these things, Jacob, for you are My servant, Israel. I have made you; you are My servant. Israel, I will not forget you.
I have swept away your offenses like a cloud, your sins like the morning mist. Return to Me, for I have redeemed you.

Sing for joy, you heavens, for the LORD has done this; shout, you depths of the earth; burst into song, you mountains, you forests, and all your trees, for the LORD has redeemed Jacob and displays His glory in Israel.
This is what the LORD says—your Redeemer, who formed you in the womb: I am the LORD, the Maker of all things, who stretches out the heavens and spreads out the earth by Myself,
who foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners, who overthrows the learning of the wise and turns it into nonsense,

who carries out the words of His servants and fulfills the predictions of His messengers, who says of Jerusalem, 'It shall be inhabited,' and of the towns of Judah, 'They shall be rebuilt,' and I will restore her ruins;
who says to the deep waters, 'Be dry,' and I will dry up your streams;
who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd,' and will accomplish all that I please; who says of Jerusalem, 'Let it be rebuilt,' and of the temple, 'Let its foundations be laid.'"

This is what the LORD says to Cyrus, His anointed one. I have taken hold of your right hand to bring nations under your control and to strip kings of their power. I will open doors for you so that gates will not be shut.
I will go before you and level the mountains. I will break the bronze doors and cut the iron bars.
I will give you treasures hidden in darkness and riches stored in secret places. Then you will know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.
For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen one, I called you by name. I gave you a title, even though you do not know Me.
I am the LORD, and there is no other. Besides Me there is no God. I will strengthen you, even though you do not know Me.
I do this so that people from the east and from the west may know that there is no one besides Me. I am the LORD, and there is no other.
I form light and create darkness. I bring peace and create disaster. I, the LORD, do all these things.
Let the heavens rain down from above, and let the clouds pour down righteousness. Let the earth open and bring forth salvation, and let righteousness grow with it. I, the LORD, have created it.
Woe to those who argue with their Maker. They are like a clay pot among many pots. Does the clay say to the potter, "What are you making?" Does your work say, "He has no hands"?
Woe to those who say to their father, "What have you fathered?" or to their mother, "What have you brought into the world?"
This is what the LORD says, the Holy One of Israel and its Maker: "Will you question Me about My children, or give Me orders about the work of My hands?
I made the earth and created mankind on it. My hands stretched out the heavens, and I commanded all the stars.
I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will make all his paths straight. He will rebuild My city and set My exiles free, not for money or reward," says the LORD of Hosts.

This is what the LORD says: "The wealth of Egypt and the trade of Cush, along with the Sabeans—tall men—will come over to you and will be yours. They will follow behind you and bow down to you in chains. They will pray to you and say, 'Surely God is with you, and there is no other; there is no other God.'"
Truly You are a God who hides Himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.
All of them will be put to shame and disgraced. The makers of idols will go away together in shame.
But Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation. You will never be put to shame or disgraced, forever and ever.

For this is what the LORD says, the Creator of the heavens—He is God. He formed the earth and made it; He set it in place. He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in. "I am the LORD, and there is no other.
I did not speak in secret or in a dark place. I did not say to the descendants of Jacob, 'Seek Me in vain.' I, the LORD, speak the truth and declare what is right. "
Come, gather together, and draw near, you survivors of the nations. Those who carry wooden idols and pray to a god that cannot save know nothing.

Speak up and present your case; yes, let them take counsel together. Who foretold this long ago? Who declared it from ancient times? Was it not I, the LORD? There is no other God but Me, a righteous God and Savior; there is none but Me. "
Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am God, and there is no other.
By Myself I have sworn; truth has gone out from My mouth, a word that will not be taken back: Every knee will bow before Me, every tongue will swear allegiance. "
They will say of Me, 'In the LORD alone are righteousness and strength.' All who rage against Him will come to Him and be put to shame.
In the LORD all descendants of Israel will be justified and will glory."
Bel bows down, and Nebo stoops. Their idols are loaded onto animals. The images you carry are heavy burdens for tired animals.
The idols stoop and bow down together. They cannot rescue the heavy load, and they themselves are carried off.
Listen to Me, people of Jacob, and all who are left of the house of Israel. I have carried you since before you were born.
Even in your old age, I am the same. Even when your hair turns gray, I will carry you. I made you, and I will carry you. I will hold you up and save you.
Who will you compare Me to? Who is equal to Me? Who is like Me?
People pour out gold from a bag and weigh silver on scales. They hire a goldsmith to make a god. Then they bow down and worship it.
They lift it onto their shoulders and carry it. They set it in place, and it stands there. It cannot move from its spot. Even if someone cries out to it, it does not answer or save him from trouble.
Remember this and be ashamed. Take it to heart, you who have turned against Me.
Remember the things that happened long ago. I am God, and there is no other. I am God, and no one is like Me.
I tell the end from the beginning. From long ago I tell things that have not happened yet. I say, "My plan will stand, and I will do everything I want."
I call a bird of prey from the east, a man from a far country to carry out My plan. I have spoken, and I will make it happen. I have planned it, and I will do it.
Listen to Me, you stubborn people who are far from doing right.
I bring My righteousness near. It is not far off, and My salvation will not wait. I will give salvation in Zion to Israel, My glory.
Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground with no throne, daughter of the Chaldeans. People will no longer call you tender and delicate.
Take millstones and grind grain. Take off your veil, lift your skirts, bare your legs, and wade through rivers.
People will see your nakedness and your shame. I will take revenge and show no mercy.
Our Redeemer—the the LORD of Hosts is His name—the Holy One of Israel.
Sit quietly and go into the dark, daughter of the Chaldeans. People will no longer call you queen of kingdoms.
I was angry with My people. I let their land be ruined, and I gave them into your hands. You showed them no mercy. You made your heavy yoke very hard, even on old people.
You said, “I will be queen forever,” but you did not think about these things or remember how it would end.
Now listen to this, you who love pleasure and feel safe. You say in your heart, “I am the only one; there is no one else. I will never be a widow or lose my children.”
Both of these things will hit you in one moment, in one day: losing children and becoming a widow. They will come on you fully, even with all your magic and your strong spells.
You trusted in your evil ways. You said, “No one sees me.” Your wisdom and knowledge tricked you. You said in your heart, “I am the only one; there is no one else.”
Disaster will come on you, and you will not know how to make it go away. Ruin will fall on you, and you cannot pay for it. Destruction will come on you suddenly, and you will not expect it.
Keep standing with your spells and your many charms, the things you worked hard at since you were young. Maybe they will help you. Maybe they will scare people.
You are tired from all your advice. Let them stand and save you—those who study the sky, who watch the stars, who tell each month what will happen to you.
Look, they are like dry grass. Fire will burn them up. They cannot save themselves from the flames. There is no warm coal for them, no fire to sit beside.
That is how they will be to you—the people you worked with since you were young. Each one wanders off his own way. No one can save you.
"Listen to this, house of Jacob—you who are called Israel. You came from Judah’s line. You swear by the the LORD’s name and call on the God of Israel, but not with truth or right living.
For they call themselves after the holy city and depend on the God of Israel. The the LORD of Hosts is His name.
"I spoke about things from long ago. They came from My mouth, and I announced them. Then, suddenly, I acted, and they came true.
Because I knew you are stubborn. Your neck is like iron, and your forehead is like bronze.
"So I told you about them long ago. Before they happened, I announced them to you, so you would not say, ‘My idol did them, and my carved image and my metal image commanded them.’
You have heard; look at all this. Will you not declare it? From now on I announce new things to you, hidden things you have not known.
They are new now, not from long ago. You have not heard of them before today, so you cannot say, ‘Look, I knew them.’
"Surely you have never heard; surely you have never known. From long ago your ear has not been open. For I knew you would act very unfaithfully, and you were called a rebel from birth.
"For the sake of My name I will hold back My anger. For the sake of My praise I will restrain it for you, so I do not cut you off.
Look, I have refined you, but not like silver. I have tested you in the furnace of suffering.
For My own sake, for My own sake, I will do it. For how can I let My name be dishonored? I will not give My glory to another.
"Listen to Me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I have called. I am the One; I am the first, and I am the last.
Surely My hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens. When I call them, they stand together.
"Assemble, all of you, and listen: Who among them has declared these things? The the LORD loves him; he will carry out His plan against Babylon, and His arm will be against the Chaldeans.
I, yes I, have spoken. I have called him. I have brought him, and he will succeed.
Come near to Me and listen to this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret. From the time it happened, I was there. And now the Lord, the the LORD, has sent Me, and His Spirit."
Thus says the the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: "I am the the LORD your God, who teaches you what is best, who leads you in the way you should go.
If only you had paid attention to My commands, your peace would have been like a river, and your right living like the waves of the sea.
Your children would have been like the sand, and your descendants like its grains. Their name would never be cut off or destroyed before Me."
"Come out of Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! Announce it with a shout of joy. Proclaim it. Send it to the ends of the earth. Say, ‘The the LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!’"
They did not get thirsty when He led them through the deserts. He made water flow for them from the rock. He split the rock, and water poured out.
"There is no peace," says the the LORD, "for the wicked."
"Listen to me, you islands; pay attention, you distant nations. The LORD called me before I was born; while I was in my mother's womb He named me.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword; He hid me in the shadow of His hand. He made me a polished arrow; He hid me in His quiver."
He said to me, "You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified."
But I said, "I have worked hard for nothing; I have spent my strength for no purpose and for emptiness. Yet my justice is with the LORD, and my reward is with my God."
"And now the LORD says—He who formed me in the womb to be His servant, to bring Jacob back to Him and gather Israel to Himself—for I am honored in the LORD's sight, and my God has been my strength—"

He says, "It is too small a thing for you to be My servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob and restore the preserved of Israel. I will also make you a light for the nations, so that My salvation may reach to the ends of the earth."

This is what the LORD says, the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, to the one despised by people, to the one hated by the nation, to the servant of rulers: "Kings will see you and rise; princes will bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who chose you."

This is what the LORD says: "In the time of favor I will answer you, and in the day of salvation I will help you. I will keep you and appoint you as a covenant for the people, to restore the land and to give back its deserted inheritances,
"to say to the prisoners, 'Come out,' and to those in darkness, 'Show yourselves.' They will feed along the roads, and their pasture will be on every bare height.
They will not hunger or thirst, and the scorching heat and sun will not strike them. For He who has compassion on them will lead them and guide them to springs of water.
"I will make all My mountains a road, and My highways will be raised up.
Look, these will come from far away—some from the north, some from the west, and some from the land of Sinim."
Shout for joy, O heavens; rejoice, O earth; break into singing, O mountains! For the LORD has comforted His people and will have compassion on His afflicted.
But Zion said, "The LORD has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me."
"Can a woman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb? Though she may forget, I will not forget you.
Look, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands; your walls are always before Me.
"Your children will hurry back; your destroyers and those who laid you waste will depart from you.
Lift up your eyes and look around. They all gather and come to you. As surely as I live," declares the LORD, "you will wear them all as ornaments; you will put them on like a bride.
"Your ruined and empty places and your destroyed land will now be too small for your people, and those who devoured you will be far away.
The children you lost will yet say in your ears, 'This place is too small for me; make room for me to live here.'
"Then you will say in your heart, 'Who bore these for me? I was bereaved and barren, exiled and rejected. Who raised these? Look, I was left alone—where did they come from?'"
Thus says the Lord the LORD: "Look, I will lift My hand to the nations and raise My banner to the peoples. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD; those who wait for Me will not be put to shame."
Can the prey be taken from the mighty, or the captives of the righteous be delivered?

But this is what the LORD says: "Even the captives of the mighty will be taken away, and the prey of the tyrant will be delivered. I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children.

I will feed your oppressors their own flesh, and they will be drunk with their own blood as with sweet wine. Then all flesh will know that I am the LORD, your Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob."

This is what the the LORD says: "Where is the paper that says I divorced your mother? Or which of My creditors did I sell you to? Look, you were sold because of your sins, and your mother was sent away because of your rebellion."

"Why was no one here when I came? Why did no one answer when I called? Is My hand too short to buy you back? Or do I have no power to save you? Look, with one strong word I can dry up the sea and turn rivers into a desert. The fish rot without water and die of thirst.
I can cover the sky with darkness and dress it in sackcloth."
The Lord the the LORD has given Me the tongue of a student, so I know how to help tired people with words. He wakes Me up each morning; He opens My ear to listen like a student.
The Lord the the LORD has opened My ear, and I did not refuse. I did not turn back.
I gave My back to those who strike, and My cheeks to those who pull out My beard. I did not hide My face from shame and spit.
The Lord the the LORD helps Me, so I have not been disgraced. That is why I set My face like hard stone and know I will not be put to shame.
The One who says I am right is near. Who will argue with Me? Let us face each other. Who is My accuser? Let him come near Me.
Look, the Lord the the LORD helps Me. Who can say I am guilty? Look, they will all wear out like old clothes, and moths will eat them up.
"Who among you fears the the LORD and obeys His Servant? Who walks in the dark without light? Let that person trust in the the LORD's name and lean on his God."

"Look, all of you who start a fire and arm yourselves with flaming arrows—walk in the light of your own fire and in the flames you lit. This is what you will get from My hand: You will lie down in torment."
Listen to Me, you who chase what is right, you who look for the LORD. Look at the rock you were cut from, and the pit you were dug from.
Look at Abraham, your father, and at Sarah, who gave birth to you. I called him when he was only one man. Then I blessed him and made his family grow.

The LORD will comfort Zion. He will comfort all her ruined places. He will make her desert like Eden and her dry land like the garden of the LORD. Joy and gladness will be found there, along with thanks and singing.
Pay attention to Me, My people, and listen to Me, My nation. A law will come from Me, and My justice will be a light for the nations. I will make it happen soon.
My righteousness is near. My salvation has already gone out. My arms will bring justice to the nations. The faraway lands wait for Me, and they put their hope in My arm.

Lift your eyes to the sky, and look at the earth below. The sky will disappear like smoke, and the earth will wear out like old clothes. The people who live on it will die like gnats. But My salvation will last forever, and My righteousness will never be broken.
Listen to Me, you who know what is right, you people who have My law in your hearts. Do not fear the scorn of people, and do not be crushed by their insults.
The moth will eat them like clothes, and worms will eat them like wool. But My righteousness will last forever, and My salvation will go on for all generations.
Wake up, wake up! Put on strength, arm of the LORD! Wake up like in the old days, in years long ago. Was it not You who cut Rahab to pieces and stabbed the dragon?
Was it not You who dried up the sea, the water of the great deep, and made a road through the deep sea for the saved to cross?
So the saved people of the LORD will return and come to Zion with singing. Everlasting joy will crown their heads. Gladness and joy will catch up with them, and sorrow and sighing will run away.
I, even I, am the One who comforts you. Who are you that you are afraid of a person who dies, or of a human who fades like grass?

You have forgotten the LORD, your Maker, who stretched out the sky and laid the foundations of the earth. You live in fear all day long because of the anger of the one who crushes people, who is ready to destroy. But where is that anger now?
The prisoner will soon be set free. He will not die in the pit, and he will not run out of bread.
I am the LORD, your God, who stirs up the sea so its waves roar. The LORD of Hosts is His name.
I put My words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of My hand. I did this to plant the sky and lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Zion, "You are My people."
Wake up, wake up! Stand up, Jerusalem! You drank from the LORD’s hand the cup of His anger. You drank the bowl of staggering and drained it.
Out of all the sons she has given birth to, no one is there to guide her. Out of all the sons she has raised, no one takes her hand.
These two things have happened to you: ruin and destruction, famine and sword. Who will comfort you? Who will grieve for you?
Your sons have fainted. They lie at the head of every street like an animal caught in a net. They are full of the LORD’s anger and the rebuke of your God.
So listen to this, you who are hurting, drunk but not from wine.
This is what your Lord says—the LORD, your God, who defends His people: "I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering. You will never drink the bowl of My anger again.
I will put it in the hands of your tormentors, who said to you, 'Bow down so we can walk over you.' You made your back like the ground, like a street for people to walk on."
Awake, awake! Put on your strength, O Zion. Put on your beautiful clothes, O Jerusalem, the holy city. The uncircumcised and the unclean will not enter you anymore.
Shake off the dust. Rise up and sit enthroned, O Jerusalem. Loosen the chains from your neck, O captive Daughter of Zion.
For this is what the LORD says: "You were sold for nothing, and you will be bought back without money."
For this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: "At first My people went down to Egypt to live there. Then Assyria treated them badly for no reason."
"And now what do I have here?" declares the LORD. "My people have been taken away for nothing. Their rulers cry out," declares the LORD, "and My name is insulted all day long."
So My people will know My name. In that day they will know that I am the One who says, 'Here I am.'
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the one who brings good news, who announces peace, who brings good news of happiness, who announces salvation, and who says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"
Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices. Together they shout for joy, because they will see the LORD face to face when He returns to Zion.
Break into song together, you ruins of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted His people. He has set Jerusalem free.
The LORD has shown His holy power to all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
Leave, leave! Get out of there! Do not touch anything unclean. Get out from the middle of her. Be pure, you who carry the vessels of the LORD.
You will not leave in a hurry, and you will not run away, because the LORD will go before you, and the God of Israel will guard your back.
Look, My Servant will succeed. He will be raised up and lifted high and greatly honored.
Just as many people were shocked at Him—His face was so damaged that He did not look like a man, and His form was not like that of other people—
so He will sprinkle many nations. Kings will close their mouths because of Him. They will see what they were not told about, and they will understand what they had not heard.
Who has believed our message? To whom has the the LORD's power been revealed?
He grew up before Him like a tender shoot, like a root from dry ground. He had no beauty or majesty to attract us; there was nothing in His appearance that we should desire Him.
He was despised and rejected by people. He was a man of sorrows, familiar with suffering. People turned their faces away from Him. He was despised, and we did not value Him.
Surely He took up our weaknesses and carried our pain, yet we thought God had struck Him, beaten Him, and made Him suffer.
But He was pierced for our sins and crushed for our guilt. The punishment that brought us peace fell on Him, and by His wounds we are healed.
We all have wandered like sheep; each of us has gone his own way. But the the LORD has placed on Him the sin of us all.
He was treated harshly and suffered, yet He did not say a word. He was led like a lamb to be killed, and like a sheep that is quiet before those who shear it, He did not open His mouth.
He was taken away through oppression and unfair judgment. Who thought about His future? He was cut off from the living; He was punished for the sin of My people.
He was given a grave with the wicked and a tomb with the rich, although He had done no violence and had spoken no lies.

Yet it was the the LORD's will to crush Him and cause Him to suffer. When His life is made a guilt offering, He will see His descendants, He will live a long life, and the plan of the the LORD will succeed through Him.
After His suffering, He will see life and be satisfied. By His knowledge, My righteous Servant will make many right with God, and He will carry their sins.

So I will give Him a place among the great, and He will share the reward with the strong, because He poured out His life to death and was counted among sinners. He bore the sin of many and pleaded for the sinners.

Sing, barren woman, you who have never had a child; burst into song and shout for joy, you who have never been in labor. For the woman who was left alone will have more children than the woman with a husband,” says the LORD. “
Enlarge the place of your tent, stretch out the curtains of your shelters; do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your stakes.
For you will spread out to the right and to the left; your descendants will take over nations and settle empty cities.
Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; do not be disgraced, for you will not be humiliated. For you will forget the shame of your youth and remember no more the pain of being a widow.
For your Maker is your husband—the the LORD of Hosts is His name—the Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer; He is called the God of all the earth.
For the the LORD has called you back, like a wife left alone and grieving in spirit, like a wife married young but rejected,” says your God. “
For a short time I left you, but with deep compassion I will bring you back.
