In a flood of anger I hid My face from you for a moment, but with kindness that never ends I will have compassion on you,” says the the LORD, your Redeemer. “
This is like the days of Noah to Me: I swore that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth. So I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or scold you.

Though the mountains may be removed and the hills may be shaken, My faithful love for you will not be removed, and My covenant of peace will not be shaken,” says the the LORD, who has compassion on you. “
O city in trouble, battered by storms and not comforted, I will lay your stones with turquoise and your foundations with sapphires.
I will make your towers of rubies, your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones. “
All your children will be taught by the the LORD, and great will be their peace.
In righteousness you will be made strong. You will be far from oppression, for you will not be afraid. Terror will not come near you. “
If anyone attacks you, it is not from Me; whoever attacks you will surrender to you.
Look, I have created the blacksmith who blows on the coals and makes a weapon for his work; I have also created the destroyer to bring ruin.

No weapon formed against you will succeed, and you will prove wrong every tongue that accuses you. This is the share given to the the LORD’s servants, and their right standing comes from Me,” declares the the LORD.
“Come, everyone who is thirsty, come to the water. Even if you have no money, come, buy food and eat. Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost!
Why spend your money on what is not bread, and your hard work on what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good, so your soul will enjoy the finest food.
Listen closely and come to Me. Hear Me, so you may live. I will make a lasting agreement with you, giving you the faithful love I promised to David.
I made him a witness to the nations, a leader and commander for the peoples.
You will call a nation you do not know, and nations you do not know will run to you, because of the the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, for He has made you glorious.”
Seek the the LORD while He can be found. Call on Him while He is near.

Let the wicked person leave his evil way, and let the sinful person leave his bad thoughts. Let him turn back to the the LORD, and He will show mercy. Let him turn to our God, because He forgives freely.
“For My thoughts are not your thoughts, and My ways are not your ways,” declares the the LORD.
“For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts.”
“For just as rain and snow come down from heaven and do not return without watering the earth, making it bud and sprout, and providing seed to sow and bread to eat,
so My word that goes out from My mouth will not return to Me empty. It will do what I want, and it will succeed in what I sent it to do.”
“For you will go out with joy and be led forth in peace. The mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
Instead of thorns, cypresses will grow, and instead of briers, myrtles will grow. This will be a memorial to the the LORD, an everlasting sign that will never be destroyed.”
This is what the LORD says: "Keep justice and do what is right, because My salvation is near and My righteousness will soon be shown."
Blessed is the person who does this, and the one who holds on to it—keeping the Sabbath without treating it like an ordinary day, and keeping his hand from doing any evil.

The foreigner who has joined the LORD should not say, "The LORD will surely separate me from His people." And the man who cannot have children should not say, "I am like a tree that can never bear fruit."
For this is what the LORD says to the men who cannot have children who keep My Sabbaths, choose what pleases Me, and hold on to My covenant:
"I will give them a place in My house and within My walls, a name better than sons and daughters. I will give them a lasting name that will never be cut off."

And the foreigners who join the LORD to serve Him, to love the name of the LORD, and to be His servants—everyone who keeps the Sabbath without treating it like an ordinary day and holds on to My covenant—

I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar, because My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations."
The Lord, the LORD, who gathers Israel's scattered people, declares: "I will gather even more people to those already gathered."
All of you wild animals in the fields, come and eat. All of you wild animals in the forest, come too.
Israel's watchmen are blind. They all lack knowledge. They are like dogs that cannot bark. They lie around dreaming and love to sleep.
The dogs are greedy and never have enough. They are shepherds who do not understand. They all turn to their own way, each one chasing his own gain.
They say, "Come, let's get wine and drink strong drink. Tomorrow will be like today, only much better!"
The righteous die, and no one pays attention. Faithful people are taken away, and no one understands that they are spared from evil.
Those who live right go in peace; they find rest in their beds.
“But you, come here, you sons of a sorceress, children of an adulterer and a prostitute.
Who are you mocking? Who are you sneering at and sticking out your tongue at? Are you not children of rebellion, offspring of lies,
who burn with lust among the oaks, under every green tree, who slaughter children in the valleys, under the cracks in the rocks?
“Your share is among the smooth stones of the valley; yes, they are your lot. You have even poured out a drink offering to them and offered a grain offering. Should I overlook these things?
On a high and lofty mountain you set your bed, and there you went up to offer sacrifices.

Behind the door and doorpost you set up your memorial. Turning away from Me, you uncovered your bed; you climbed into it and made it wide. You made an agreement with those whose bed you loved; you looked at their nakedness.
“You went to the king with oil and increased your perfumes. You sent your messengers far away; you went down even to the grave.
You wore yourself out on your many journeys, but you did not say, ‘It is hopeless.’ You found new strength, so you did not give up.
Who did you fear and dread, so that you lied and did not remember Me or take it to heart? Have I not been silent for a long time, and you do not fear Me?
“I will point out your righteousness and your works, but they will not help you.

When you cry out, let your collection of idols save you! The wind will carry them off; a breath will take them away. But whoever takes refuge in Me will inherit the land and possess My holy mountain.”
And it will be said: “Build up, build up, prepare the way, remove the stumbling blocks from the path of My people.”

For this is what the high and lifted up One says, the One who lives forever, whose name is Holy: “I live in the high and holy place, and also with the crushed and humble in spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly and to revive the heart of the crushed.
“For I will not argue forever, nor will I always be angry, because then the human spirit would give out before Me, and the people I created.
I was angry because of his sinful greed, so I struck him. I hid My face, and I was angry. Yet he kept going, turning away in the stubbornness of his heart.
I have seen his ways, but I will heal him. I will guide him and give comfort to him and to those who mourn for him,
“bringing praise to their lips. Peace, peace to those far away and those near,” says the LORD, “and I will heal them.”
But the wicked are like the restless sea, which cannot be still. Its waves churn up mud and dirt.
“There is no peace,” says my God, “for the wicked.”
“Cry aloud; do not hold back. Lift up your voice like a trumpet. Tell My people about their sins, and tell the family of Jacob about their wrongs.

They seek Me day after day and seem happy to know My ways. They act like a nation that does what is right and has not left the laws of its God. They ask Me for fair decisions and seem to want to be close to God.”
“Why have we fasted, and You do not see? Why have we humbled ourselves, and You do not notice? Look, on the day you fast, you still do what you want. You drive your workers hard.
You only fast to argue and fight and to hit someone with an evil fist. You cannot fast like this today and expect your voice to be heard in heaven.”

“Is this the kind of fast I want? Is it only a day for a person to humble himself? Is it only to bow his head like a reed and to lie in sackcloth and ashes? Do you call that a fast, a day that pleases the LORD?
Is this not the fast I want: to break the chains of injustice, to untie the ropes of the yoke, to set free those who are crushed, and to break every yoke?
Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, to bring the poor wanderer into your house, to cover the naked when you see them, and not to hide from your own family?”
“Then your light will break out like the dawn, and your healing will come quickly. Your right living will go before you, and the glory of the LORD will guard your back.

Then you will call, and the LORD will answer. You will cry for help, and He will say, ‘Here I am.’ If you remove the yoke of oppression from among you, stop pointing fingers, and stop speaking evil, “and if you spend yourselves for the hungry and satisfy the needs of those who are hurting, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkest time will be like noon. The LORD will guide you always. He will satisfy your needs in a dry land and strengthen your bones. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose water never runs dry. “Your people will rebuild the old ruins and raise up the foundations from long ago. You will be called the one who repairs broken walls and brings back streets where people can live. If you keep your feet from breaking the Sabbath and from doing as you please on My holy day, if you call the Sabbath a joy and the LORD’s holy day an honor, and if you honor it by not going your own way, not doing as you please, and not speaking empty words, then you will find joy in the LORD, and I will make you ride on the high places of the earth. I will feed you with the land that belonged to your father Jacob. The mouth of the LORD has spoken.”
Look, the LORD's hand is not too short to save, and His ear is not too dull to hear.
But your wrongs have separated you from your God. Your sins have hidden His face from you, so He won't listen.
Your hands are stained with blood, and your fingers with sin. Your lips have spoken lies, and your tongue mutters evil.
No one calls for justice, and no one pleads for truth. They trust in empty things and speak lies. They plan trouble and give birth to sin.
They hatch viper eggs and weave spiderwebs. Their plans are deadly and useless—anyone who gets involved is harmed, and even a crushed plan still produces poison.
Their webs won't become clothes, and they won't cover themselves with their deeds. Their deeds are sinful, and violence is in their hands.
Their feet run to do evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are sinful; ruin and destruction are in their paths.
They don't know the way of peace, and there is no justice in their paths. They've made their roads crooked, and no one who walks them knows peace.
So justice is far from us, and righteousness doesn't reach us. We hope for light, but see darkness; we look for brightness, but walk in gloom.
We feel along the wall like blind people, and we stumble as if we had no eyes. At noon we stumble as if it were night, and among the strong we are like the dead.
We all growl like bears and moan like doves. We look for justice, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far from us.
For our rebellions are many before You, and our sins testify against us. Our rebellions are with us, and we know our wrongs.
We have rebelled and lied against the LORD, and turned away from our God. We speak oppression and revolt, and from our hearts we plan and speak lies.
So justice is pushed back, and righteousness stands far away. Truth has fallen in the street, and honesty can't even enter.
Truth is missing, and anyone who turns from evil is attacked. The LORD saw this, and He was displeased that there was no justice.
He saw there was no one, and He was amazed that no one stepped in to help. So His own arm brought salvation, and His righteousness supported Him.
He put on righteousness like armor, and salvation like a helmet. He dressed in vengeance and wrapped Himself in zeal.
He will repay them according to their deeds—fury to His enemies and punishment to His foes. He will repay even the distant lands.
So people will fear the LORD's name from the west, and His glory from the east. When the enemy comes in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD will raise a banner against him.
"The Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from sin," says the LORD.

"As for Me, this is My covenant with them," says the LORD. "My Spirit, which is on you, and My words, which I have put in your mouth, will not leave your mouth, or the mouths of your children, or the mouths of your children's children, from now on and forever," says the LORD.
Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD rises upon you.
See, darkness covers the earth, and thick darkness is over the peoples; but the LORD will rise upon you, and His glory will appear over you.
Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn. “
Lift up your eyes and look around. They all gather and come to you; your sons come from afar, and your daughters are carried on the hip.
Then you will look and be radiant, and your heart will tremble and swell with joy, because the abundance of the sea will be turned to you, and the wealth of the nations will come to you.
Caravans of camels will cover your land—young camels of Midian and Ephah. All from Sheba will come, bearing gold and frankincense and proclaiming the praises of the LORD. “
All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will serve you and be accepted on My altar. I will adorn My glorious house.
Who are these that fly like clouds, like doves to their windows?

Surely the coastlands wait for Me, and the ships of Tarshish will be first, to bring your children from afar, with their silver and gold, to the name of the LORD your God, and to the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you. “
Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you. Though I struck you in anger, in My favor I will show you compassion.
Your gates will always stand open; they will never be shut, day or night, so that the wealth of the nations may be brought to you, with their kings led in procession.
For the nation or kingdom that will not serve you will perish; those nations will be utterly destroyed. “
The glory of Lebanon will come to you—its cypress, box, and pine together—to adorn the place of My sanctuary, and I will glorify the place of My feet.
The sons of your oppressors will come and bow down to you; all who despised you will bow at your feet. They will call you the City of the LORD, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
Though you have been forsaken and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you an everlasting pride, a joy from generation to generation.
You will drink the milk of nations and nurse at royal breasts. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
Instead of bronze I will bring gold; instead of iron, silver; instead of wood, bronze; instead of stones, iron. I will appoint peace as your governor and righteousness as your ruler. “
No longer will violence be heard in your land, nor ruin or destruction within your borders. But you will call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
No longer will the sun be your light by day, nor will the brightness of the moon shine on you; for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
Your sun will never set again, and your moon will wane no more; for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will end.
Then all your people will be righteous; they will possess the land forever. They are the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, for My glory.
The least of you will become a thousand, and the smallest a mighty nation. I am the LORD; in its time I will accomplish it quickly.”

The Spirit of the Lord, the LORD, is on Me, because the LORD has anointed Me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom to the captives, and release to those in prison.
To announce the year of the LORD's favor and the day of our God's justice, and to comfort all who mourn.

To give those who grieve in Zion a crown of beauty instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, and a garment of praise instead of a heavy spirit. They will be called oaks of righteousness, a planting of the LORD to show His glory.
They will rebuild the ancient ruins and restore the places destroyed long ago. They will renew the ruined cities that have been empty for generations.
Strangers will stand and care for your flocks, and foreigners will work your fields and vineyards.
You will be called priests of the LORD, and people will say you are servants of our God. You will enjoy the wealth of the nations and boast in their riches.

Instead of your shame you will receive a double portion, and instead of disgrace you will rejoice in your inheritance. So you will inherit a double portion in your land, and everlasting joy will be yours.
For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and wrongdoing. In My faithfulness I will reward them and make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their children will be known among the nations, and their descendants among the peoples. Everyone who sees them will know they are the people the LORD has blessed.

I will rejoice greatly in the LORD; my soul will be joyful in my God. For He has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, like a groom putting on his wedding turban and like a bride adorning herself with her jewels.
For just as the earth brings forth its plants and a garden makes its seeds grow, so the Lord, the LORD, will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations.
For Zion's sake I will not keep quiet. For Jerusalem's sake I will not rest. I will keep going until her right living shines out like a bright light, and her rescue burns like a torch.
The nations will see your right living, and all kings will see your glory. You will be called by a new name that the LORD Himself will give.
You will be a glorious crown in the LORD's hand, a royal crown in the hand of your God.

People will no longer call you "Abandoned," and they will no longer call your land "Empty." Instead, you will be called "My Delight Is in Her," and your land will be called "Married." This is because the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
As a young man marries a young woman, so your sons will take you as their own. As a groom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
I have put watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem. They will not be quiet day or night. You who call on the LORD, don't let yourselves rest.
Don't give Him rest either, until He makes Jerusalem strong and makes her the praise of the whole earth.
The LORD has sworn by His strong right hand and His powerful arm: "I will never again give your grain to your enemies for food. Foreigners will never drink your new wine that you worked so hard for.
Instead, those who harvest it will eat it and praise the LORD. Those who gather it will drink it in My holy courtyards."
Go through, go through the gates! Clear the way for the people. Build up, build up the road! Remove the stones. Raise a flag for the nations.
Look, the LORD has announced to the ends of the earth, "Tell Daughter Zion, 'Look, your salvation is coming! Look, His reward is with Him, and His payment goes before Him.'"
They will be called God's Holy People, the Redeemed of the LORD. And you will be called "Sought After," a City That Has Not Been Abandoned.
Who is this coming from Edom, from Bozrah, with clothes stained bright red? Who is this, dressed in glory, striding forward with great strength? "It is I, speaking what is right, strong to save."
"Why are Your clothes red? Why do Your garments look like someone trampling grapes in a winepress?"
"I have trampled the winepress alone. No one from the nations helped Me. In My anger I trampled them, and in My fury I crushed them. Their blood splashed on My clothes, and I stained all My garments.
The day of vengeance was in My heart, and the year to rescue My people had come.
I looked, but no one helped. I was shocked that no one stood by Me. So My own power saved Me, and My wrath held Me up.
I trampled the nations in My anger. In My fury I made them drunk and poured their blood on the ground."
I will tell of the the LORD's faithful love — and praise Him — for all He has done for us, for the many good things He has done for Israel, because of His mercy and His great faithful love.
For He said, "Surely they are My people, children who will not lie." So He became their Savior.
In all their distress, He too was distressed, and the angel of His presence saved them. In His love and mercy He redeemed them. He lifted them up and carried them all through the old days.
But they rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit. So He turned and became their enemy, and He Himself fought against them.
Then His people remembered the old days, the days of Moses: "Where is He who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of His flock? Where is He who put His Holy Spirit among them,
who sent His glorious arm to lead them by Moses' right hand, who divided the waters before them to win for Himself everlasting fame,
who led them through the deep like a horse in the desert, so they did not stumble?
Like cattle going down into the valley, the Spirit of the the LORD gave them rest. You led Your people this way to make for Yourself a glorious name."
Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious home. Where are Your passion and Your power? Your tender love and mercy are being held back from us.
Yet You are our Father. Though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not recognize us, You, O the LORD, are our Father. Our Redeemer from long ago is Your name.
Why, O the LORD, do You let us wander from Your ways and harden our hearts so we do not fear You? Come back, for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your inheritance.
For a short time Your people owned Your holy place, but our enemies have trampled Your sanctuary.
We have become like people You never ruled, like people not called by Your name.
If only You would tear open the heavens and come down, so the mountains would shake before You!
Fire burns brushwood, and fire makes water boil. Make Your name known to Your enemies, so the nations would tremble before You!
When You did amazing things we did not expect, You came down, and the mountains shook before You.
Since long ago, no one has heard or listened, and no eye has seen any God besides You, who does such things for those who wait for Him.
You meet those who are glad to do right and who remember You by walking in Your ways. Yet You were angry because we sinned. We have been in our sins a long time. Can we still be saved?
All of us have become unclean, and all our good deeds are like dirty rags. We all fade like a leaf, and our sins blow us away like the wind.
No one calls on Your name or tries to hold on to You, because You have hidden Your face from us and let our sins sweep us away.
Yet You, the LORD, are our Father. We are the clay, and You are our potter. We are all the work of Your hand.
the LORD, do not be angry with us beyond measure, and do not remember our sin forever. Look, we are all Your people.
Your holy cities have become a desert; Zion has become a desert, and Jerusalem is in ruins.
Our holy and beautiful temple, where our fathers praised You, has been burned with fire, and all our treasured places lie in ruins.
After all this, will You still hold back, the LORD? Will You keep silent and let us suffer beyond measure?
I let Myself be found by people who did not ask for Me. I let Myself be found by people who did not look for Me. I said, "Here I am, here I am," to a nation that did not call on My name.
All day long I held out My hands to stubborn people. They walk on a path that is not good. They follow their own thoughts.
They are people who always make Me angry to My face. They sacrifice in gardens and burn incense on brick altars.
They sit among graves and stay in hidden places. They eat pig meat, and their bowls hold broth made from unclean things.
They say, "Stay away from me. Do not come near me, because I am holier than you." These people are like smoke in My nose. They are like a fire that burns all day.
Look, it is written before Me. I will not keep quiet. I will pay them back. I will pay them back in full.
The LORD says, "You and your fathers have sinned together. They burned incense on the mountains and insulted Me on the hills. So I will give them full payment for what they did before."

The LORD says, "When new wine is found in a bunch of grapes, people say not to destroy it, because there is a blessing in it. In the same way, I will act for the good of My servants. I will not destroy everyone."
I will bring children from Jacob. From Judah I will bring someone to take over My mountains. My chosen people will own the land, and My servants will live there.
Sharon will become a pasture for sheep. The Valley of Achor will become a resting place for cattle. This will be for My people who looked for Me.
But you who leave the LORD, who forget My holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and fill cups of mixed wine for Destiny—
I will hand you over to the sword. All of you will bow down to be killed. I called, but you did not answer. I spoke, but you did not listen. You did evil in My eyes. You chose what I did not want.
Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: "My servants will eat, but you will go hungry. My servants will drink, but you will go thirsty. My servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.
My servants will sing for joy from a glad heart, but you will cry out from a hurting heart. You will wail from a broken spirit.
You will leave your name for a curse to My chosen ones. The Lord the LORD will put you to death, but He will call His servants by another name.

Whoever blesses himself in the land will bless himself by the God of truth. Whoever swears in the land will swear by the God of truth. The first troubles will be forgotten. They will be hidden from My eyes."
Look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth. The old things will not be remembered. They will not come to mind.
Be glad and rejoice forever in what I create. Look, I am creating Jerusalem to be a joy and its people to be a delight.
I will rejoice in Jerusalem and be glad in My people. The sound of weeping and crying will not be heard there anymore.
No more will a child die young. No old person will fail to live a full life. A person who dies at one hundred will be thought young. A sinner who dies at one hundred will be cursed.
They will build houses and live in them. They will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

They will not build houses for someone else to live in. They will not plant vineyards for someone else to eat from. My people will live as long as trees. My chosen people will enjoy the work of their hands.
They will not work for nothing. They will not have children who are doomed to trouble. They will be a people blessed by the LORD, and their children will be with them.
Before they call, I will answer. While they are still speaking, I will hear.
The wolf and the lamb will eat together. The lion will eat straw like an ox. Dust will be the snake's food. They will not hurt or destroy on all My holy mountain, says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "Heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool. Where is the house you will build for Me? Where is My place of rest?
Has not My hand made all these things, so they came into being?" declares the LORD. "This is the one I will look to: the person who is humble and sorry in spirit, who trembles at My word.

"Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who kills a man; whoever sacrifices a lamb is like one who breaks a dog's neck; whoever brings a grain offering is like one who offers pig's blood; whoever burns incense is like one who praises an idol. Yes, they have chosen their own ways, and they delight in their disgusting idols.

"So I will choose their punishment and bring on them what they fear. This is because I called, and no one answered; I spoke, and no one listened. They did evil in My sight and chose what I did not delight in."

Listen to the word of the LORD, you who tremble at His word: "Your brothers who hate you and shut you out because of My name say, 'Let the LORD be honored, so we can see your joy!' But they will be put to shame."
Listen to the loud noise from the city; listen to the noise from the temple! It is the sound of the LORD paying back His enemies.
Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before her pain came, she delivered a boy.

Who has ever heard of such a thing? Who has ever seen such things? Can a country be born in one day? Can a nation be brought to life all at once? Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.
"Shall I bring a child to birth and not deliver?" says the LORD. "Shall I, who deliver, close the womb?" says your God.
Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad for her, all you who love her; rejoice greatly with her, all you who mourn over her.
Then you may nurse and be satisfied from her comforting breasts; then you may drink deeply and delight in her glorious wealth.
For this is what the LORD says: "I will extend peace to her like a river, and the wealth of the nations like a flooding stream. You will nurse and be carried on her hip, and bounced on her knees.
As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you, and you will be comforted in Jerusalem."
When you see this, your heart will rejoice, and your bones will flourish like grass. Then the hand of the LORD will be revealed to His servants, but His wrath will be shown to His enemies.
For look, the LORD will come with fire—His chariots are like a whirlwind—to carry out His anger with fury and His rebuke with flames of fire.
For by fire and by sword the LORD will judge all people, and those killed by the LORD will be many.
"Those who set themselves apart and clean themselves to go into the gardens, following one in the middle, eating pork, unclean things, and mice, will come to an end together," declares the LORD.
"And I know their deeds and thoughts. I am coming to gather all nations and languages, and they will come and see My glory.

I will set a sign among them, and I will send survivors from them to the nations—to Tarshish, Pul, those who draw the bow, and Lud, Tubal, and Javan—to the distant shores that have not heard of My fame or seen My glory. And they will tell of My glory among the nations.

"They will bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD—on horses, in chariots, in wagons, on mules, and on camels—to My holy mountain Jerusalem," says the LORD, "just as the Israelites bring a grain offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.
And I will also take some of them as priests and Levites," says the LORD.
"For just as the new heavens and the new earth that I will make will stand before Me," declares the LORD, "so your offspring and your name will endure.
From one New Moon to another and from one Sabbath to another, all people will come to worship before Me," says the LORD.
"And they will go out and look at the dead bodies of those who rebelled against Me; for their worm will not die, their fire will not be put out, and they will be a horror to all people."
The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah. He was one of the priests in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin.
The word of the LORD came to him during the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his rule.

It also came during the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the fifth month of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah. That was when Jerusalem was taken into exile.
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. Before you were born, I set you apart. I appointed you as a prophet to the nations."
I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I don't know how to speak, because I'm only a child."
But the LORD said to me, "Don't say, 'I'm only a child.' You must go to everyone I send you to and say whatever I command you.
Don't be afraid of them, for I am with you and will rescue you," declares the LORD.
Then the LORD reached out His hand and touched my mouth. He said, "I have put My words in your mouth.
See, today I appoint you over nations and kingdoms to uproot and tear down, to destroy and overthrow, to build and to plant."
The word of the LORD came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "I see the branch of an almond tree."
The LORD said to me, "You have seen correctly, for I am watching to see that My word is fulfilled."
The word of the LORD came to me again: "What do you see?" I said, "I see a pot that is boiling. It is tilting toward us from the north."
The LORD said to me, "From the north disaster will be poured out on all who live in this land.

I am calling all the families of the kingdoms of the north," declares the LORD. "They will come, and each will set his throne at the entrance of Jerusalem's gates, against all its walls and against all the towns of Judah.
"I will pronounce My judgments on them because of all their wickedness in forsaking Me, burning incense to other gods and worshiping what their hands have made.
"Get ready; stand up and tell them everything I command you. Do not be terrified by them, or I will terrify you before them.
"Today I have made you a fortified city, an iron pillar and a bronze wall to stand against the whole land—against the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests and the people of the land.
"They will fight against you but will not overcome you, for I am with you and will rescue you," declares the LORD.
The word of the the LORD came to me.

“Go and shout this so Jerusalem can hear: This is what the the LORD says. I remember the kindness you showed Me when you were young. I remember the love you had for Me when you were first married to Me. You followed Me through the desert, through land no one had planted.
Israel was holy to the the LORD. It was the first part of His harvest. Anyone who ate from it became guilty. Trouble came on them, declares the the LORD.
“Hear the word of the the LORD, family of Jacob, and all the families of Israel.
This is what the the LORD says: What wrong did your fathers find in Me? Why did they go far from Me and follow worthless idols until they became worthless themselves?

“They did not say, ‘Where is the the LORD, who brought us up from Egypt and led us through the desert, through a dry and broken land, through a land of darkness and deep shadow, a land no one travels through and no one lives in?’
I brought you into a rich land to eat its fruit and good things. But you came in and made My land unclean. You made the land I gave you a disgusting thing.
The priests did not ask, ‘Where is the the LORD?’ Those who handle the law did not know Me. The leaders rebelled against Me. The prophets prophesied by Baal and followed worthless idols.
“So I will still argue with you, declares the the LORD. I will argue with your children and grandchildren too.
Cross over to the coasts of Cyprus and look. Send to Kedar and study it carefully. See if anything like this has ever happened.
Has any nation ever changed its gods, even though they are not real gods? But My people changed their Glory for something that does not help them.
Be shocked by this, heavens. Be very afraid and empty, declares the the LORD.
My people have done two evil things: They left Me, the spring of living water, and dug broken cisterns for themselves. Those cisterns cannot hold water.
“Is Israel a slave? Is he someone born in the house? Why has he been plundered?
Young lions roar at him. They raise their voices. They make his land a wasteland. His cities are burned, with no one living in them.
“Even the people of Memphis and Tahpanhes have shaved the top of your head.
Didn’t you bring this on yourself by leaving the the LORD your God while He was leading you on the way?
Now what do you gain by going to Egypt to drink the water of the Nile? What do you gain by going to Assyria to drink the water of the Euphrates?

“Your own evil will punish you. Your turning away will correct you. Know and see that it is evil and bitter to leave the the LORD your God. You do not fear Me, declares the Lord the the LORD of Hosts.
Long ago I broke your yoke and tore off your chains. But you said, ‘I will not serve.’ On every high hill and under every green tree you bowed down like a prostitute.
I planted you as a choice vine from the best seed. How did you become a wild vine that is useless to Me?
“Even if you wash yourself with strong soap and use much lye, your guilt is still stained before Me, declares the Lord the the LORD.
How can you say, ‘I am not defiled. I did not follow the Baals’? Look at your path in the valley. Know what you have done. You are like a fast young camel running back and forth.
You are like a wild donkey used to the desert. She sniffs the wind because she is in heat. Who can turn her back? Anyone who looks for her will not get tired. In her mating month, they will find her.
Keep your feet from going bare and your throat from thirst. But you said, ‘It is no use. I love strangers, and I will follow them.’
“As a thief is ashamed when caught, so the people of Israel are ashamed. Their kings, officials, priests, and prophets are ashamed too.
They say to a piece of wood, ‘You are my father,’ and to a stone, ‘You gave birth to me.’ They have turned their backs to Me, not their faces. But when trouble comes, they say, ‘Get up and save us.’
Where are the gods you made for yourself? Let them get up and save you when trouble comes. You have as many gods as you have cities, Judah.
“Why do you argue with Me? You have all sinned against Me, declares the the LORD.
I punished your children for nothing. They did not learn from it. Your sword destroyed your prophets like a destroying lion.
You people of this generation, listen to the word of the the LORD: Have I been a desert to Israel, or a land of deep darkness? Why do My people say, ‘We are free. We will not come to You anymore’?
Can a young woman forget her jewelry, or a bride forget her sash? Yet My people have forgotten Me for days without number.
“How well you plan your way to look for love! So you have even taught evil women your ways.
On your clothes is found the blood of innocent poor people. You did not catch them breaking in. Yet in spite of all this,
you say, ‘I am innocent. Surely His anger has turned away from me.’ But I will judge you because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’
“How you rush around to change your way! You will be ashamed of Egypt just as you were ashamed of Assyria.
You will leave there with your hands on your head. For the the LORD has rejected the people you trusted, and you will not succeed with them.”

“They say, ‘If a man divorces his wife and she leaves him and becomes another man’s wife, would he go back to her? Would not that land be completely polluted? But you have played the prostitute with many lovers. Yet return to Me,’ declares the LORD.”

“Lift up your eyes to the bare hills and see. Where have you not been violated? You sat by the roads waiting for them like an Arab in the desert. You have polluted the land with your prostitution and wickedness.
So the showers were held back, and there was no spring rain. Yet you have the shameless face of a prostitute; you refuse to be ashamed.”
“Have you not just now called to Me, ‘My Father, You are the friend of my youth’?
Will He be angry forever? Will He hold His anger to the end? Yet you have spoken, but you have done evil and had your way.”

In the days of King Josiah, the LORD said to me, “Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She has gone up on every high hill and under every green tree, and there she has played the prostitute.”
“I thought that after she had done all this, she would return to Me. But she did not return, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it.”

“I saw that, although faithless Israel had committed adultery, I gave her a certificate of divorce and sent her away. Yet her treacherous sister Judah was not afraid; she too went and played the prostitute.”
“Because of her careless prostitution, she polluted the land and committed adultery with stone and wood.”
“Yet in spite of all this, her treacherous sister Judah did not return to Me with all her heart, but only pretending,” declares the LORD.
And the LORD said to me, “Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.”
“Go and proclaim these words to the north: ‘Return, faithless Israel. I will not look at you in anger, for I am merciful. I will not stay angry forever.

Only admit your guilt—that you have rebelled against the LORD your God, that you have scattered your favors to strangers under every green tree, and that you have not obeyed My voice,’ declares the LORD.”
“Return, you wayward children,” declares the LORD, “for I am your husband. I will take you—one from a city and two from a family—and bring you to Zion.
Then I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.”

“In those days, when you multiply and increase in the land,” declares the LORD, “they will no longer say, ‘The ark of the covenant of the LORD.’ It will not come to mind, nor will they remember it, nor will they miss it, nor will it be made again.

At that time they will call Jerusalem ‘The Throne of the LORD,’ and all the nations will be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD in Jerusalem. They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and they will come together from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as an inheritance.”
“I said, ‘How I would set you among My sons and give you a pleasant land, the most beautiful inheritance of the nations.’ I thought you would call Me ‘My Father’ and not turn away from following Me.
But like a wife who is unfaithful to her husband, so you have been unfaithful to Me, O house of Israel,” declares the LORD.
A voice is heard on the bare hills, the weeping and pleading of the children of Israel, because they have taken the wrong path and forgotten the LORD their God.
“Return, you wayward children, and I will heal your waywardness.” “Here we are, we come to You, for You are the LORD our God.”
“Truly, the hills and the noise on the mountains are a false hope. Truly, the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel.
But the shameful thing has consumed the labor of our fathers since our youth—their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us. For we have sinned against the LORD our God, both we and our fathers, from our youth even to this day. We have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God.”
"If you return, Israel, return to Me," says the LORD. "If you remove your detestable idols from My presence, you will not be driven away."
If you take an oath in the LORD's name—"As the LORD lives"—with truth, justice, and righteousness, then nations will be blessed through Him and praise Him.
For this is what the LORD says to the people of Judah and to Jerusalem: "Prepare your hearts for Me; don't keep doing things that only bring trouble."

"Give your hearts to the LORD; get rid of the stubbornness in your hearts, people of Judah and residents of Jerusalem. Otherwise My anger will blaze like fire and burn with no one to put it out, because of your evil deeds."
"Announce in Judah, shout in Jerusalem, and say: Blow the trumpet throughout the land. Call out loudly, 'Gather together! Let us run to the walled cities.'"
"Raise a warning flag toward Zion. Seek shelter; don't delay! I am bringing terrible trouble from the north, a great disaster."
"A lion has come out of his thicket; a destroyer of nations is on his way. He has left his den to turn your land into a wasteland and destroy your cities so no one lives there."
"So put on rough mourning clothes, mourn and wail, because the LORD's fierce anger has not turned away from us."
"On that day," says the LORD, "the king and the officials will lose heart. The priests will be shocked, and the prophets will be confused."
Then I said, "Alas, Lord, the LORD! You have completely deceived this people and Jerusalem by saying, 'You will have peace,' when the sword is at our throats."
At that time people will say to this nation and to Jerusalem, "A hot wind from the bare hills of the desert blows toward My people, but not to separate the grain or to cleanse."
"A wind too strong for that comes from Me. Now I will also pronounce judgments against them."
"Look, he advances like clouds; his chariots are like a whirlwind. His horses are faster than eagles. Woe to us, for we are ruined!"
"O Jerusalem, wash the evil from your heart, so you may be saved. How long will you keep wicked thoughts within you?"
"A voice shouts from Dan, and trouble is announced from the hills of Ephraim."
"Tell the nations, and announce to Jerusalem: 'Attackers are coming from a distant land, shouting against the cities of Judah.'"
"They surround her like guards around a field, because she has rebelled against Me," says the LORD.
"Your own ways and deeds have brought this on you. This is your punishment. How bitter it is, because it cuts to your heart!"
"My pain, my pain! I twist in pain. Oh, my heart! My heart pounds within me. I cannot stay silent, for I have heard the trumpet, the alarm of war."
"Disaster after disaster is announced, for the whole land is ruined. Suddenly my tents are destroyed; my tent curtains are torn in a moment."
"How long must I see the battle flag and hear the trumpet?"
"For My people are foolish; they do not know Me. They are senseless children with no understanding. They are skilled at doing evil, but they do not know how to do good."
"I looked at the earth, and it was a wasteland with nothing in it. I looked at the heavens, and their light was gone."
"I looked at the mountains, and they were quaking; all the hills were swaying."
"I looked, and no one was there; all the birds of the sky had flown away."
"I looked, and the fruitful land had become a desert; all its cities were torn down before the LORD, before His fierce anger."
"For this is what the LORD says: 'The whole land will be desolate, but I will not completely destroy it.'"
"The earth will mourn, and the heavens above will grow dark, because I have spoken. I have planned, and I will not change My mind or turn back."
"Every city runs from the sound of the horseman and archer. People hide in the bushes and climb among the rocks. Every city is abandoned; no one lives in them."

"And you, ruined one, what will you do? Though you wear scarlet, though you deck yourself with gold, though you put makeup on your eyes, you make yourself beautiful for nothing. Your allies reject you; they want to kill you."

"For I hear a cry like a woman in labor, a cry of anguish like a woman giving birth to her first child—the cry of the daughter of Zion gasping for breath and stretching out her hands: 'Woe is me, for I am worn out by killers!'"
Roam through the streets of Jerusalem and look. Search its squares. If you can find one person who does what is right and seeks truth, then I will forgive the city.
Even if they say, "I swear by the living the LORD," they are lying.
The LORD, don't Your eyes look for truth? You struck them, but they didn't give in. You wore them down, but they refused to learn. They set their faces like stone and refused to turn back.
Then I said, "They're just poor people. They're foolish. They don't know the the LORD's way or what their God expects."
"I'll go to the leaders and speak to them, because they know the the LORD's way and what their God expects." But they too have broken the yoke and snapped the straps.

So a lion from the forest will kill them, a wolf from the desert will destroy them, and a leopard will prowl around their cities. Anyone who leaves will be torn apart, because their sins are many and their turning away is great.
"Why should I forgive you? Your children have left Me and sworn by gods that aren't real. I fed them well, but they committed adultery and crowded into the prostitute's house."
They were well-fed, lusty horses, each one chasing after his neighbor's wife.
"Shouldn't I punish people like this?" declares the the LORD. "Shouldn't I take revenge on a nation like this?"
Go up through her vine rows and destroy, but don't destroy everything. Strip away her branches, because they don't belong to the the LORD.
"The house of Israel and the house of Judah have been very unfaithful to Me," declares the the LORD.
They have lied about the the LORD and said, "He won't harm us. Disaster won't come on us. We won't see war or starvation."
The prophets are like wind, and the word isn't in them. So that is what will happen to them.
So this is what the the LORD, the God of Armies, says: "Because you have said this, I am making My words like fire in your mouth. These people are like wood, and the fire will burn them up."

"Look, I am bringing a nation against you from far away, house of Israel," declares the the LORD. "It is an old nation, a nation from long ago. You won't know its language, and you won't understand what they say."
Their quiver is like an open grave. All of them are warriors.
They will eat your harvest and food, your sons and daughters, your flocks and herds, and your vines and fig trees. They will use the sword to destroy your fortified cities, the ones you trust in.
"Yet even in those days," declares the the LORD, "I won't destroy you completely."
When they ask, "Why has the the LORD our God done all this to us?" You will answer, "Just as you left Me and served foreign gods in your land, so you will serve strangers in a land that isn't yours."
Declare this in the house of Jacob and proclaim it in Judah:
"Hear this, you foolish and senseless people. You have eyes but don't see. You have ears but don't hear."

"Don't you fear Me?" declares the the LORD. "Don't you tremble before Me? I made the sand a boundary for the sea, an everlasting rule it can't cross. The waves may toss, but they can't win. They may roar, but they can't cross it."
But these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts. They have turned away and left.
They don't say in their hearts, "Let us fear the the LORD our God, who gives rain in its season, both the early and late rain, and keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest."
Your wrongdoing has turned these blessings away, and your sins have kept good from you.
Wicked men are found among My people. They watch like bird catchers lying in wait. They set a trap and catch people.
Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of deceit. That's why they've become great and rich.
They are fat and sleek. They also do evil in matters of justice. They don't defend the orphan's case or judge the poor fairly.
"Shouldn't I punish them for this?" declares the the LORD. "Shouldn't I take revenge on a nation like this?"
A horrible and shocking thing has happened in the land:
The prophets prophesy lies, and the priests rule by their own power. My people love it that way! But what will you do when it ends?
Run away, people of Benjamin, from the middle of Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet in Tekoa. Raise a warning signal on Beth-hakkerem, because a great disaster is coming from the north.
I will destroy the beautiful and gentle daughter of Zion.
Shepherds with their flocks will come to her. They will pitch tents all around her, and each one will graze in his own area.
Get ready for war against her. Get up, let's attack at noon. How terrible for us! The day is fading, and the shadows are getting long.
Get up, let's attack at night and destroy her palaces.
For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: Cut down her trees and build a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This city must be punished. It is full of oppression.
Just as a well keeps its water fresh, she keeps her evil fresh. Violence and destruction are heard in her. Sickness and wounds are always before Me.
Be warned, Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you. I will make you a wasteland, a land no one lives in.
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: The enemies will strip the remnant of Israel like a vine. Go back over the branches again, like a grape picker.
Who can I speak to and warn so they will listen? Their ears are closed, and they cannot hear. The word of the LORD is an insult to them, and they do not want it.

I am full of the LORD's anger. I am tired of holding it back. Pour it out on the children in the street and on the young men gathered together. Husbands and wives will be caught, along with the old and those full of years.
Their houses will be given to others, along with their fields and wives. For I will stretch out My hand against the people of the land, says the LORD.
From the least to the greatest, everyone is greedy for gain. From the prophet to the priest, everyone practices deceit.
They have treated My people's wound as if it were nothing. They say, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.

Were they ashamed of the terrible things they did? No, they were not ashamed. They did not even know how to blush. So they will fall among those who fall. When I punish them, they will stumble, says the LORD.

This is what the LORD says: Stand at the crossroads and look. Ask for the old paths, where the good road is, and walk in it. Then you will find rest for your souls. But they said, “We will not walk in it.”
I set watchmen over you and said, “Listen to the sound of the trumpet!” But they said, “We will not listen.”
So listen, nations, and know, congregation, what will happen to them.
Listen, earth: I am bringing disaster on this people. It is the fruit of their own plans, because they did not listen to My words and rejected My law.
Why do you bring Me frankincense from Sheba and sweet cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices do not please Me.
So this is what the LORD says: I will put stumbling blocks before this people. Fathers and sons will stumble over them together. Neighbors and friends will perish.
This is what the LORD says: Look, an army is coming from the north. A great nation is rising up from the far ends of the earth.
They hold bows and spears. They are cruel and show no mercy. Their voice roars like the sea. They ride on horses, lined up for war against you, daughter of Zion.
We have heard the report. Our hands grow weak. Anguish has seized us. The pain is like a woman in labor.
Do not go out into the field or walk on the road, because the enemy has a sword. Terror is on every side.
Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and roll in ashes. Mourn as for an only son. Make the most bitter lament, for the destroyer will suddenly come upon us.
I have made you a tester of metals among My people, a fortress, so you can know and test their ways.
They are all stubborn rebels. They go around spreading lies. They are like bronze and iron. All of them are corrupt.
The bellows blow fiercely. The lead is consumed by fire. The refiner works in vain, because the wicked are not separated out.
They are called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Stand at the gate of the LORD's house and announce this message there. Say, 'Hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who come through these gates to worship the LORD.'"
"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Fix your ways and your actions, and I will let you live in this place.
Do not trust lying words that say, 'This is the LORD's temple, the LORD's temple, the LORD's temple.'"
"But if you truly fix your ways and your actions, if you truly treat each other fairly,
if you do not oppress the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow other gods to your own harm,
then I will let you live in this place, in the land I gave your ancestors forever.
But look, you are trusting in lying words that cannot help you.
Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear lies, burn incense to Baal, and follow other gods you do not know?
Then will you come and stand before Me in this house that bears My name and say, 'We are safe!'—so you can go on doing all these hateful things?
Has this house that bears My name become a hideout for robbers in your eyes? I have seen it Myself," declares the LORD.
"But go now to My place in Shiloh, where I first made My name dwell, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of My people Israel.
And now, because you do all these things," declares the LORD, "and when I spoke to you again and again, you did not listen, and when I called you, you did not answer.
I will do to the house that bears My name—the one you trust in—and to the place I gave you and your ancestors, what I did to Shiloh.
I will throw you out of My sight, just as I threw out all your brothers, all the descendants of Ephraim."
"As for you, do not pray for this people. Do not lift up a cry or prayer for them, and do not plead with Me, because I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
The children gather wood, the fathers light the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the queen of heaven. They also pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke Me to anger.
Are they provoking Me to anger?" declares the LORD. "No, they are hurting themselves, to their own shame."

"Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: 'Look, My anger and My wrath will be poured out on this place—on people and animals, on the trees of the field and the fruit of the ground. It will burn and not be put out.'"
"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices and eat the meat.'"
"For when I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them about burnt offerings and sacrifices.
But I commanded them this: Obey My voice, and I will be your God, and you will be My people. Walk in all the way I command you, so that it may go well with you.
But they did not listen or pay attention. Instead they followed the stubbornness of their evil hearts. They turned away instead of moving forward.
From the day your ancestors left Egypt until today, I have sent you all My servants the prophets, again and again.
Yet they did not listen to Me or pay attention. They became stubborn and did worse than their ancestors.
So you will speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you. You will call to them, but they will not answer you.
And you will say to them, 'This is the nation that did not obey the voice of the LORD their God and did not accept correction. Truth has disappeared from their mouths.'"
"Cut off your hair and throw it away. Take up a lament on the bare heights, for the LORD has rejected and abandoned the people He is angry with.
For the children of Judah have done evil in My eyes," declares the LORD. "They have set their hateful idols in the house that bears My name and defiled it.
They built high places at Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom to burn their sons and daughters in the fire. I did not command that, and it never entered My mind.

So look, the days are coming," declares the LORD, "when people will no longer call it Topheth or the Valley of Ben Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter. They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no room.
The dead bodies of this people will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth, and no one will scare them away.
I will put an end to the sounds of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, because the land will become a wasteland."
The LORD says, "At that time, they will bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, their leaders, the priests, the prophets, and the people of Jerusalem from their graves.

They will spread them out before the sun, the moon, and all the stars of the sky, which they loved, served, followed, prayed to, and worshiped. The bones will not be gathered or buried. They will be like manure on the ground.
And wherever I have scattered them, the people left from this wicked family will choose death over life," declares the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD says, "Tell them: Do people fall down and not get up? If someone turns away, does he not come back?
Why then do these people keep turning away? Jerusalem is always turning away. They cling to lies and refuse to come back.
I listened carefully, but they do not say what is right. No one is sorry for his wrong and says, 'What have I done?' Everyone runs his own way, like a horse rushing into battle.
Even the stork in the sky knows its seasons. The turtledove, the swift, and the crane know when to come. But My people do not know what the LORD requires.
How can you say, 'We are wise, and we have the LORD's law'? Look, the false pen of the scribes has turned it into a lie.
The wise men are put to shame. They are dismayed and caught. Look, they have rejected the word of the LORD. What wisdom do they have?
So I will give their wives to others and their fields to new owners. Everyone, from the least to the greatest, is greedy for gain. Prophet and priest alike, all practice deceit.
They treat the wound of My people as if it were not serious. They say, 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace.

Are they ashamed of the terrible things they do? No, they are not ashamed at all. They do not even know how to blush. So they will fall with those who fall. When I punish them, they will stumble," says the LORD.
"I will surely take them away," declares the LORD. "There are no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree. Even the leaves have withered. What I gave them is gone.

Why are we sitting here? Let's gather and go into the strong cities and die there. For the LORD our God has doomed us. He has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.
We hoped for peace, but nothing good came. We hoped for healing, but there is only terror.
The snorting of the enemy's horses is heard from Dan. The sound of his stallions neighing shakes the whole land. They come and devour the land and everything in it, the city and its people.
"For look, I am sending poisonous snakes among you, snakes that no one can charm, and they will bite you," declares the LORD.
My joy is gone. Grief is upon me. My heart is sick.
Listen to the cry of my people from a far country: "Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her King not there?" Why have they provoked Me with their carved images and their worthless foreign idols?
The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.
Because my people are hurt, I am hurt. I mourn, and horror has taken hold of me.
Is there no healing medicine in Gilead? Is there no doctor there? Then why hasn't my people's healing come?
I wish my head were a spring of water and my eyes were fountains of tears! Then I could cry day and night for my people who have been killed.
I wish I had a place to stay in the desert. Then I would leave my people and get away from them. They are all unfaithful, a crowd of traitors.
They bend their tongues like bows to shoot lies. Falsehood wins over truth in the land. They go from one evil to the next, and they do not know Me, says the LORD.
Watch out for your neighbors, and do not trust your brothers. Every brother is a trickster, and every friend spreads lies.
Everyone lies to his neighbor and does not speak the truth. They have trained their tongues to lie, and they wear themselves out doing wrong.
You live in the middle of deceit. In their deceit they refuse to know Me, says the LORD.
So the LORD of Hosts says, "I will refine them and test them. What else can I do because of My people?"
Their tongues are like deadly arrows. They speak lies. A person says kind words to his neighbor, but he sets a trap for him in his heart.
The LORD declares, "Should I not punish them for these things? Should I not avenge Myself on a nation like this?"

I will weep and wail for the mountains. I will sing a sad song for the empty grasslands in the wilderness. They are burned, and no one travels through them. No cattle are heard. The birds and animals have fled and gone.
I will turn Jerusalem into a pile of ruins and a home for jackals. I will make the cities of Judah empty and lifeless.
Who is wise enough to understand this? Who has heard the LORD speak, so he can explain it? Why has the land been ruined and burned like a desert, with no one passing through?
The LORD said, "Because they have abandoned My law, which I gave them, and have not obeyed My voice or followed it.
Instead, they followed their stubborn hearts and the Baals, just as their fathers taught them.
So I, the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, will feed this people bitter wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.
I will scatter them among nations they and their fathers never knew. I will send the sword after them until I have destroyed them."
The LORD of Hosts says, "Think about this and call for the women who mourn. Send for the skilled women."
Let them hurry and sing a sad song for us, so our eyes run with tears and our eyelids pour out water.
A voice of wailing is heard from Zion: "We are ruined! We are deeply ashamed, because we have left the land, and our homes have thrown us out."
Hear the word of the LORD, O women. Let your ears hear His word. Teach your daughters to wail, and let each woman teach her neighbor to mourn.
Death has come through our windows and entered our palaces. It cuts off children from the streets and young men from the open squares.
Speak! This is what the LORD says: "Dead bodies will fall like manure on the open field, like grain left behind by the harvesters, and no one will gather them."
The LORD says, "Let not the wise man brag about his wisdom. Let not the strong man brag about his strength. Let not the rich man brag about his riches.

Instead, let the one who brags brag about this: that he understands and knows Me. For I am the LORD, and I do kindness, justice, and goodness on the earth. I take pleasure in these things, says the LORD."
The LORD says, "Look, days are coming when I will punish everyone who is circumcised only in the flesh:
Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who live in the desert. All these nations are uncircumcised, and even all the people of Israel are uncircumcised in heart."
Hear the word that the LORD speaks to you, O house of Israel.
This is what the LORD says: "Do not learn the ways of the nations or be terrified by signs in the heavens, though the nations are terrified by them.
For the customs of the peoples are worthless; they cut a tree out of the forest, and a craftsman shapes it with his chisel.
They adorn it with silver and gold; they fasten it with hammer and nails so it will not topple.
Like a scarecrow in a cucumber field, their idols cannot speak; they must be carried because they cannot walk. Do not fear them, for they can do no harm, nor can they do any good."
No one is like You, O the LORD; You are great, and Your name is mighty in power.
Who would not fear You, O King of the nations? For this is Your due. Among all the wise leaders of the nations and in all their kingdoms, there is no one like You.
They are altogether senseless and foolish; instruction from idols is wood!
Hammered silver is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz. The work of the craftsman and of the goldsmith is clothed in blue and purple—all the work of skilled men.
But the LORD is the true God; He is the living God and eternal King. The earth trembles at His wrath, and the nations cannot endure His anger.
Tell them this: 'These gods, who did not make the heavens and the earth, will perish from the earth and from under the heavens.'
He made the earth by His power; He established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding.
When He thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; He causes the clouds to rise from the ends of the earth. He sends lightning with the rain and brings the wind from His storehouses.
Every man is senseless and without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols. For his molten images are a fraud, and there is no breath in them.
They are worthless, a work of mockery. In the time of their punishment they will perish.
The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for He is the Maker of all things, and Israel is the tribe of His inheritance. the LORD of Hosts is His name.
Gather up your belongings from the ground, O daughter living under siege.
For this is what the LORD says: "Look, I will sling out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and I will bring distress on them so that they may be captured."
Woe to me because of my injury; my wound is painful. Yet I said, 'This is my sickness, and I must bear it.'
My tent is destroyed, and all my ropes are snapped. My children have left me and are no more; no one is left to pitch my tent or to set up my curtains.
For the shepherds are senseless and do not seek the LORD; therefore they do not prosper, and all their flock is scattered.
Listen! The sound of a report is coming—a great commotion from the land of the north to make the cities of Judah a wasteland, a haunt of jackals.
I know, O the LORD, that a man's way is not his own; no one who walks directs his own steps.
Correct me, O the LORD, but only with justice—not in Your anger, or You will bring me to nothing.

Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not acknowledge You, and on the families that do not call on Your name. For they have devoured Jacob; they have devoured him and consumed him, and they have laid waste his homeland.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the the LORD, saying:

"Listen to the words of this covenant, and speak them to the men of Judah and to the people living in Jerusalem. Tell them, 'This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: "Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant—the covenant I commanded your fathers when I brought them out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace. I said, 'Obey My voice, and do everything I command you. Then you will be My people, and I will be your God.' This is so I can keep the promise I made to your fathers, to give them a rich and fertile land, as it is today.'" Then I answered, "Amen, the LORD."
The The LORD said to me, "Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: 'Listen to the words of this covenant and do them.'
From the day I brought your fathers out of Egypt until today, I warned them again and again, saying, 'Obey My voice.'
But they did not listen or pay attention. Each man followed his stubborn, evil heart. So I brought on them all the curses of this covenant, which I commanded them to obey, but they did not."
The The LORD said to me, "A conspiracy has been found among the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem.

They have turned back to the sins of their fathers, who refused to listen to My words. They have followed other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken My covenant, which I made with their fathers."
Therefore this is what the the LORD says: "I am bringing disaster on them that they cannot escape. They will cry out to Me, but I will not listen to them.
The cities of Judah and the people of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods they burn incense to, but those gods will not save them in their time of trouble.
Judah, you have as many gods as you have cities, and Jerusalem has as many altars as its streets—altars you people have set up to burn incense to that shameful thing, to Baal."
"So do not pray for these people. Do not lift up a cry or prayer for them, because I will not listen when they call to Me in their trouble.
What is My beloved doing in My house? She has done many evil things. Can holy meat take away your guilt? When you do evil, you are happy.
The The LORD called your name, 'Green Olive Tree, Beautiful with Fruit.' But with the roar of a great storm He will set fire to it, and its branches will be broken.
The The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has spoken disaster against you because of the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah. They made Me angry by burning incense to Baal."
The The LORD made it known to me, and I knew. Then He showed me what they were doing.
I was like a gentle lamb led to be killed. I did not know they had planned against me, saying, "Let us destroy him and everything he has. Let us kill him so his name will be forgotten."
But the the LORD of Hosts judges fairly. He tests the heart and mind. Let me see Your vengeance on them, for I have brought my case to You.
Therefore this is what the the LORD says about the men of Anathoth, who seek your life and say, "Do not prophesy in the name of the the LORD, or you will die by our hand"—
this is what the the LORD of Hosts says: "I will punish them. The young men will die by the sword. Their sons and daughters will die by famine.
No one will be left, because I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year of their punishment."
You are righteous, the LORD, even though I bring my case to You. Still, I want to talk with You about Your justice. Why does the way of the wicked succeed? Why are all traitors so comfortable?
You planted them, and they took root. They grow and bear fruit. You are always on their lips, but far from their hearts.
But You know me, the LORD. You see me and test my heart for You. Drag them away like sheep to be killed, and set them apart for the day of slaughter.

How long will the land mourn and the grass in every field dry up? The evil of the people who live there has wiped out the animals and birds, because they said, "He will not see how things end for us."
"If you have raced with men on foot and they have worn you out, how can you compete with horses? If you stumble in a peaceful land, what will you do in the thick woods by the Jordan?
For even your brothers and your father's house have betrayed you; even they have called out against you. Do not trust them, though they speak well of you."
"I have forsaken My house; I have abandoned My inheritance. I have given the one I love into the hands of her enemies.
My inheritance has become to Me like a lion in the forest. She has roared against Me; therefore I have hated her.
Is My inheritance to Me like a speckled bird of prey? Birds of prey surround her. Come, gather all the wild animals; bring them to devour her.
"Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard; they have trampled My plot of ground. They have turned My pleasant field into a desolate wasteland.
They have made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns before Me. The whole land is desolate because there is no one who cares.
Over all the bare hilltops in the desert, destroyers have come, for the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the earth to the other. There is no peace for all mankind.
They have sown wheat but reaped thorns; they have worn themselves out but gained nothing. So be ashamed of your harvest because of the fierce anger of the LORD."

"This is what the LORD says: As for all My wicked neighbors who touch the inheritance I have given My people Israel, I will uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
But after I have uprooted them, I will return and have compassion on them and bring them back, each to his inheritance and each to his land.
"And if they will diligently learn the ways of My people and swear by My name, 'As surely as the LORD lives'—as they taught My people to swear by Baal—then they will be built up among My people.
But if they will not obey, then I will uproot that nation and destroy it," declares the LORD.
The LORD said to me, "Go buy a linen belt and put it around your waist, but do not put it in water."
So I bought the belt, just as the the LORD had said, and put it around my waist.
Then the word of the the LORD came to me again.
"Take the belt you bought, the one around your waist. Go at once to the Euphrates and hide it in a crack in the rocks."
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, just as the the LORD had commanded me.
After many days the the LORD said to me, "Get up and go to the Euphrates. Take from there the belt I told you to hide."
So I went to the Euphrates and dug up the belt. I took it from the place where I had hidden it. But the belt was ruined; it was good for nothing.
Then the word of the the LORD came to me.
"This is what the the LORD says: I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem in the same way.
These wicked people refuse to listen to My words. They follow the stubbornness of their hearts and go after other gods to serve and worship them. They will be like this belt—useless.

Just as a belt clings to a man's waist, so I made the whole family of Israel and the whole family of Judah cling to Me. I did this so they would be My people and bring Me fame, praise, and glory. But they would not listen."
Say to them, "This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Every wineskin will be filled with wine." If they say to you, "Don't we already know that every wineskin will be filled with wine?"

then tell them, "This is what the the LORD says: I am going to fill with drunkenness everyone who lives in this land—the kings who sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the people of Jerusalem."
The the LORD declares, "I will smash them against each other, fathers and sons alike. I will not pity or spare or show mercy. I will destroy them."
Listen and pay attention. Do not be proud, for the the LORD has spoken.
Give glory to the the LORD your God before He brings darkness, and before your feet stumble on the dark mountains. While you wait for light, He turns it into deep darkness.
But if you will not listen, I will weep in secret because of your pride. My eyes will weep bitterly and stream with tears, because the the LORD's flock will be taken captive.
Tell the king and the queen mother, "Come down and sit in a low place, for your glorious crowns have fallen from your heads."
The cities of the south will be shut up, with no one to open them. All Judah will be taken away captive, completely.
Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you, your beautiful sheep?
What will you say when He brings rulers over you? You yourself taught them to rule over you. Will not pains seize you like a woman in labor?
And if you say in your heart, "Why is this happening to me?" it is because of your many sins. Your skirts have been stripped off and your heels exposed.
Can an Ethiopian change his skin, or a leopard its spots? Neither can you do good, you who are used to doing evil.
I will scatter them like straw blown by the desert wind.
