This is your lot, the portion I have assigned to you, declares the the LORD, because you have forgotten Me and trusted in lies.
I will pull your skirts up over your face, so your shame is seen.
I have seen your adulteries and your lustful neighings, your shameless acts on the hills and in the fields. I have seen your disgusting acts. Woe to you, Jerusalem! How long will you remain unclean?
This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah about the droughts.
Judah is in mourning, and her city gates grow weak. Her people sit in black on the ground, and Jerusalem cries out.
The leaders send their servants for water. They come to the cisterns, but find no water. They return with empty jars, ashamed and disgraced, and they cover their heads.
The ground is cracked because no rain has fallen in the land. The farmers are ashamed and cover their heads.
Even the doe in the field gives birth and leaves her fawn, because there is no grass.
Wild donkeys stand on the bare hills and pant like jackals. Their eyes grow weak because there is no grass.
Even though our sins speak against us, O the LORD, do something for the honor of Your name. We have turned away from You many times, and we have sinned against You.
You are the hope of Israel and its Savior in times of trouble. Why do You seem like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who stops for the night?
Why do You seem like a man who is stunned, like a strong man who cannot rescue anyone? Yet You are among us, O the LORD, and we are called by Your name. Do not leave us.
The LORD said to this people, "They have loved to wander away. They did not hold back their feet. So the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their guilt and punish their sins."
The LORD said to me, "Do not pray for good for these people.
When they fast, I will not listen to their cry. When they offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead, I will destroy them by war, hunger, and disease."
I said, "Oh, Lord the LORD! Look, the prophets are telling them, 'You will not see war, and you will not have famine. Instead, I will give you lasting peace in this place.'"

The LORD said to me, "The prophets are telling lies in My name. I did not send them, command them, or speak to them. They are giving you false visions, fortune-telling, empty hopes, and lies from their own hearts."

"Therefore this is what the LORD says about the prophets who speak in My name, though I did not send them, and who say, 'There will be no war or famine in this land.' Those same prophets will be destroyed by war and famine.

The people they prophesy to will be thrown into the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and war. No one will bury them, or their wives, sons, and daughters. I will pour out their own evil on them."

The LORD said to me, "Say this to the people: 'My eyes overflow with tears day and night, and they do not stop, because the young women of my people have been broken by a terrible blow, a very bad wound.
If I go out to the fields, I see people killed by war. If I go into the city, I see people sick with hunger. Even prophets and priests have gone to a land they do not know.'"

Have You completely rejected Judah? Has Your soul turned against Zion? Why have You struck us with no healing? We hoped for peace, but nothing good came. We hoped for a time of healing, but there is only terror.
We know our wickedness, O the LORD, and the sins of our fathers, because we have sinned against You.
For Your name's sake, do not reject us. Do not dishonor Your glorious throne. Remember Your covenant with us, and do not break it.
Can any of the worthless idols of the nations bring rain? Can the skies give showers? Are You not the LORD our God? So we will wait for You, because You made all these things.
The LORD said to me, "Even if Moses and Samuel stood before Me, My heart would not turn toward this people. Send them away from Me, and let them go.

When they ask you, 'Where should we go?' you must answer, 'This is what the LORD says: Those meant for death will die; those meant for the sword will be killed by the sword; those meant for famine will starve; and those meant for captivity will be taken captive.'
I will punish them with four kinds of disaster," declares the LORD. "The sword will kill, the dogs will drag them away, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth will eat and destroy.
I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem." "
Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
You have rejected Me," declares the LORD. "You keep going backward. So I will stretch out My hand against you and destroy you. I am tired of showing mercy.
I will winnow them with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land. I will take their children from them; I will destroy My people, because they did not turn from their ways.
Their widows will be more than the sand of the sea. At noon I will send a destroyer against them. I will suddenly bring anguish and terror upon the mother of a young man.

The mother of seven will grow faint and breathe her last. Her sun will set while it is still day; she will be ashamed and disgraced. I will give the rest of them to the sword before their enemies," declares the LORD.
Woe to me, my mother, because you gave birth to me, a man of strife and conflict to the whole land! I have not lent money, and no one has lent money to me, yet everyone curses me.
The LORD said, "Surely I will set you free for a good purpose. Surely I will make your enemies plead with you in times of disaster and times of distress.
Can iron break iron from the north, or bronze?
I will give your wealth and your treasures as plunder, without cost, for all your sins throughout your territory.
I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for My anger has kindled a fire that will burn against you."
You know, O LORD. Remember me and care for me. Take revenge for me on my persecutors. Because You are slow to anger, do not take me away. Know that I suffer insult for Your sake.
Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words became my joy and the delight of my heart, because I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts.
I did not sit with partygoers, and I did not rejoice. Because of Your hand, I sat alone, for You filled me with indignation.
Why is my pain endless and my wound incurable, refusing to heal? Will you be to me like a deceitful brook, like waters that fail?

The LORD said, "If you return, I will restore you, and you will stand before Me. If you bring out the precious from the worthless, you will be like My mouth. They will turn to you, but you will not turn to them.

I will make you a fortified wall of bronze to this people. They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you to save you and rescue you," declares the LORD. "I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless."
The word of the LORD came to me. He said,
"Do not take a wife for yourself, and do not have sons or daughters in this place."
For this is what the LORD says about the sons and daughters born in this place, and about their mothers who bore them and their fathers who fathered them in this land:

They will die of terrible diseases. No one will mourn for them or bury them. They will be like dung on the ground. They will be destroyed by sword and famine, and their dead bodies will be food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.

For this is what the LORD says: Do not go into a house where people are mourning. Do not go to cry with them or comfort them. For I have taken away My peace from this people, declares the LORD—My faithful love and mercy.
Both great and small will die in this land. They will not be buried. People will not mourn for them, cut themselves, or shave their heads for them.
No one will bring them food to comfort them after a death, and no one will give them a drink of comfort for their father or mother.
Do not go into a house where people are feasting, to sit with them and eat and drink.

For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am about to stop in this place, before your eyes and in your days, the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

When you tell this people all these things, they will say to you, "Why has the LORD said all this terrible disaster will come on us? What wrong have we done? What sin have we committed against the LORD our God?"
Then you will say to them, "Your fathers left Me, declares the LORD. They followed other gods, served them, and bowed down to them. They left Me and did not keep My law.
But you have done even worse than your fathers. Look, each of you follows his own stubborn, evil heart instead of listening to Me.
Therefore I will throw you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known. There you will serve other gods day and night, because I will not show you favor."
Therefore, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when people will no longer say, "As the LORD lives who brought the people of Israel up from Egypt."

Instead they will say, "As the LORD lives who brought the people of Israel up from the land of the north and from all the countries where He scattered them." I will bring them back to their own land, the land I gave their ancestors.
Look, I am sending many fishermen to catch them, declares the LORD. Then I will send many hunters to hunt them from every mountain, hill, and rocky cliffs.
For My eyes are on all their ways. They are not hidden from Me, and their wrongdoing is not hidden from My eyes.

First I will repay them double for their wickedness and sin, because they have defiled My land with the dead bodies of their detestable idols and filled My inheritance with their disgusting practices.

The LORD, You are my strength and fortress, my refuge in times of trouble. Nations will come to You from the ends of the earth and say, "Our ancestors inherited only lies, worthless idols that cannot help.
Can a person make gods for himself? They are not gods."
So I will teach them. This time I will show them My power and strength, and they will know that My name is the LORD.
Judah's sin is written with an iron pen and a diamond tip. It is carved into the tablet of their heart and onto the horns of your altars.
Their children remember their altars and their sacred poles beside green trees on the high hills, on the mountains in the fields.
O My mountain in the countryside, I will give your wealth and all your treasures to be looted, because of the sin of your high places in all your borders.
You will lose, yes, lose, the inheritance I gave you. I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for you have lit a fire in My anger; it will burn forever.
This is what the the LORD says: "Cursed is the person who trusts in people and depends on human strength, whose heart turns away from the the LORD.
He will be like a shrub in the desert. He will not see good when it comes. He will live in dry places in the wasteland, in a salty land where no one lives."
"Blessed is the person who trusts in the the LORD, whose confidence is in Him.

He will be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by a stream. It will not fear when heat comes; its leaves will stay green. It will not worry in a dry year, and it will not stop bearing fruit."
The heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure. Who can understand it?
I, the the LORD, search the heart and test the mind, to give each person what his ways deserve, according to the fruit of his deeds.
Like a bird that hatches eggs it did not lay is the person who gets rich unfairly. In the middle of his life it will leave him, and in the end he will be a fool.
A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
O the LORD, the hope of Israel, all who leave You will be put to shame. Those who turn away from You will be written in the dust, because they have forsaken the the LORD, the spring of living water.
Heal me, O the LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for You are my praise.
Look, they keep saying to me, "Where is the word of the the LORD? Let it come now!"
But I have not run away from being a shepherd after You, and I have not wanted the day of incurable pain. You know; what came from my lips was right before You.
Do not be a terror to me; You are my refuge in the day of disaster.
Let my persecutors be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be dismayed, but do not let me be dismayed. Bring on them the day of disaster; destroy them with double destruction!
This is what the the LORD said to me: "Go and stand at the gate used by the people, through which the kings of Judah enter and leave, and at all the gates of Jerusalem.
Say to them: 'Hear the word of the the LORD, you kings of Judah, all Judah, and all the people of Jerusalem who enter through these gates.'"
This is what the the LORD says: "Be careful not to carry a load or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day.
Do not carry a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day or do any work, but keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.
Yet they did not listen or pay attention, but they stiffened their necks and would not listen or accept discipline."
"If you listen to Me," declares the the LORD, "and do not bring a load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and if you keep the Sabbath day holy by doing no work on it,

then kings and princes who sit on David's throne will enter through the gates of this city. They will come with their officials, riding in chariots and on horses, along with the men of Judah and those living in Jerusalem, and this city will be inhabited forever.

People will come from the cities of Judah and from the places around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the lowlands, from the hill country, and from the Negev. They will bring burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and frankincense, and thank offerings to the house of the the LORD.

But if you do not listen to Me to keep the Sabbath day holy, and not to carry a load and enter the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will set a fire in its gates that will burn the palaces of Jerusalem and not be put out."
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD said,
"Go down to the potter's house. I will speak to you there."
So I went down to the potter's house. I saw him working at his wheel.
The pot he was shaping from clay was ruined in his hands. So he made it into a different pot, the way he wanted.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"O house of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does?" declares the LORD. "Look, like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel.
At one moment I might speak about a nation or kingdom to uproot it, tear it down, and destroy it.
But if that nation turns from its evil, I will hold back the disaster I planned to bring on it.
At another moment I might speak about a nation or kingdom to build it and plant it.
But if it does evil in My sight and does not obey My voice, I will hold back the good I had planned to do for it.

Now therefore, say to the men of Judah and to the people living in Jerusalem: 'This is what the LORD says: "Look, I am shaping disaster against you and making a plan against you. Turn now, each of you, from his evil way, and make your ways and deeds good."'
But they say, 'It is hopeless! For we will follow our own plans, and each of us will act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart.'
Therefore this is what the LORD says: "Ask now among the nations: Who has heard such things? The virgin of Israel has done a very horrible thing.
Does the snow of Lebanon ever leave the rocky fields? Or do the cold waters that flow from far away ever dry up?
Yet My people have forgotten Me. They burn incense to worthless idols, and they stumble in their ways on the old paths, walking on side roads instead of the highway.
They have made their land a ruined, empty place, a thing people hiss at forever. Everyone who passes by is shocked and shakes his head.
Like the east wind I will scatter them before the enemy. I will show them My back, not My face, in the day of their disaster."

Then they said, "Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah. The law will not be lost from the priest, nor advice from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, let us attack him with our words, and let us not pay attention to anything he says."
Listen to me, the LORD, and hear what my enemies are saying.
Should good be paid back with evil? They have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before You to speak good for them, to turn Your anger away from them.

So give their children to hunger, and let them be killed by the sword. Let their wives lose their children and become widows. Let their men die by disease, and let their young men be killed by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their houses when You suddenly bring an army against them, because they dug a pit to trap me and hid snares for my feet.

But You, the LORD, know all their plans against me to kill me. Do not forgive their wrongdoing, and do not wipe away their sin from before Your eyes. Let them be overthrown before You. Deal with them in the time of Your anger.
This is what the LORD says: “Go and buy a clay jar from a potter. Take along some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests.
Go out to the Valley of Ben Hinnom, near the entrance of the Potsherd Gate. There proclaim the words I tell you, “

and say: ‘Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah and people of Jerusalem. This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring such disaster on this place that everyone who hears about it will be shocked.

For they have forsaken Me and made this place foreign to Me by burning incense here to other gods that neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah ever knew. They have filled this place with the blood of innocent people.
They have built the high places of Baal to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal—something I never commanded or spoke of, and it never entered My mind.
So listen: the days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

In this place I will ruin the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, at the hands of those who want to kill them. I will give their dead bodies as food to the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.
I will make this city a horror and an object of scorn. Everyone who passes by will be horrified and will scorn it because of all its wounds.
I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and daughters, and they will eat one another’s flesh during the siege and hardship their enemies, who want to kill them, will force on them.’ “
Then break the jar while those who go with you are watching,

and say to them: ‘This is what the LORD of Hosts says: I will smash this nation and this city just as this potter’s jar is smashed and cannot be repaired. They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room.’ “
This is what I will do to this place and to those who live here, declares the LORD. I will make this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be made unclean like this place, Topheth—all the houses where they burned incense on their roofs to all the stars in the sky and poured out drink offerings to other gods.”
Then Jeremiah returned from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy, and stood in the courtyard of the LORD’s house and said to all the people, “

This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘Listen! I am going to bring on this city and all the towns around it every disaster I promised, because they were stubborn and would not listen to My words.’”
When Pashhur the priest, son of Immer and chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things,
he had Jeremiah the prophet beaten and put in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin in the LORD's temple.
The next day Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the stocks. Then Jeremiah said to him, "The LORD doesn't call your name Pashhur. He calls you Terror on Every Side.

For this is what the LORD says: 'I will make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies while you watch. I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon. He will carry them captive to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.

I will give away all the wealth of this city, all its hard work, and all its treasures. I will hand over all the treasures of Judah's kings to their enemies. The enemies will plunder them, take them, and carry them off to Babylon.
And you, Pashhur, and everyone in your house will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon and die there. You will be buried there—you and all your friends to whom you prophesied lies.'"
"O LORD, You tricked me, and I was tricked. You are stronger than I am, and You have won. I have become a joke to everyone. All day long, people mock me.
Every time I speak, I cry out, 'Violence and destruction!' So the word of the LORD has brought me insult and mocking all day long.
If I say, 'I won't mention Him or speak in His name anymore,' His word burns in my heart like a fire shut up in my bones. I get tired of holding it in, and I can't.

I hear many people whispering, 'Terror on every side! Report him; let's report him!' All my close friends watch for me to slip. They say, 'Maybe he'll be fooled, and then we can beat him and get our revenge.'
But the LORD is with me like a mighty warrior. So those who chase me will stumble and fail. They will be completely shamed, because they didn't succeed. Their shame will never be forgotten.
O LORD of Armies, You test the good and see the heart and mind. Let me see Your revenge on them, for I have trusted my case to You.
Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! For He has saved the life of the poor from the hand of wicked people."
"Cursed be the day I was born! May the day my mother bore me not be blessed!
Cursed be the man who brought my father the news, saying, 'You have a son!' and made him so glad.
Let that man be like the cities the LORD overthrew without pity. Let him hear a cry in the morning and an alarm at noon.
For he did not kill me in the womb, so my mother would have been my grave, and her womb pregnant forever.
Why did I come out of the womb to see trouble and sorrow and to end my days in shame?"
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malkijah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to him. They said,
"Please ask the LORD to help us, because King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon is attacking us. Maybe the LORD will do for us one of His wonderful miracles and make Nebuchadnezzar leave."
Then Jeremiah said to them, "Tell Zedekiah this:"

"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I am about to turn the weapons in your hands against you—the ones you are using to fight the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are attacking you outside the wall. I will gather them into the middle of this city.
I will fight against you Myself with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with anger, fury, and great wrath.
I will strike down the people who live in this city and their animals; they will die from a terrible disease.

After that, declares the LORD, I will hand over King Zedekiah of Judah, his officials, and the people left in this city—those who survive the disease, the sword, and the famine—to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, to their enemies, and to those who want to kill them. He will kill them with the sword. He will not spare them or show them pity or mercy."
Jeremiah also said, "Tell these people:" "This is what the LORD says: I am putting before you the way to life and the way to death.
Anyone who stays in this city will die by the sword, famine, or disease. But anyone who goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans who are attacking you will live. He will escape with his life.
I have turned My face against this city to bring trouble, not good, declares the LORD. It will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down."
Concerning the royal family of Judah, Jeremiah said, "Listen to the LORD's word:"

"This is what the LORD says, O house of David: Judge fairly every morning. Rescue the person who has been robbed from the one who oppresses him. Otherwise My anger will break out like fire and burn, and no one will put it out, because of the evil you have done.
I am against you, Jerusalem—you who live in the valley on the rock of the plain, declares the LORD—you who say, 'Who can attack us? Who can enter our homes?'
I will punish you for what your actions deserve, declares the LORD. I will set fire to your forest, and it will burn up everything around you."
This is what the LORD says: "Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and proclaim this message there:
Hear the word of the LORD, O king of Judah, you who sit on David's throne—your officials and your people who come through these gates."

This is what the LORD says: "Do justice and righteousness. Rescue the robbed from the hand of the oppressor. Do not mistreat or rob the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow. Do not shed innocent blood in this place.
For if you really do this, then kings who sit on David's throne will come through the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses—they, their officials, and their people.
But if you do not listen to these words, I swear by Myself, declares the LORD, that this house will become a ruin."
For this is what the LORD says about the house of the king of Judah: "You are like Gilead to Me, like the top of Lebanon. But I will surely make you a desert, cities no one lives in.
I will send destroyers against you, each with his weapons. They will cut down your best cedars and throw them into the fire.
Many nations will pass by this city and ask one another, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this great city?'
And they will answer, 'Because they left the covenant of the LORD their God and worshiped and served other gods.'"
Do not weep for the dead or mourn for them. Weep bitterly for the one who is going away, because he will never return or see his homeland again.
For this is what the LORD says about Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who ruled in place of his father Josiah and has gone out from this place: "He will never return here.
He will die in the place where they took him; he will never see this land again."
"Woe to him who builds his house by wrongdoing and his upper rooms by unfairness, who makes his neighbor work for nothing and does not pay him his wages,
who says, 'I will build myself a spacious house with large upper rooms. I will cut out windows and panel it with cedar and paint it with red paint.'
"Do you think you are a king because you excel in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink and do justice and righteousness? Then it went well with him.
He judged the case of the poor and needy; then it went well. Is that not what it means to know Me?" declares the LORD.
"But your eyes and your heart are set on nothing but dishonest gain, on shedding innocent blood, on taking money by force and on violence."

Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: "They will not mourn for him, saying, 'Alas, my brother!' or 'Alas, my sister!' They will not mourn for him, saying, 'Alas, my lord!' or 'Alas, his glory!'
He will be buried like a donkey, dragged off and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem."
"Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan; cry out from Abarim, for all your lovers have been crushed.
I spoke to you in your prosperity, but you said, 'I will not listen.' This has been your way from your youth, that you have not obeyed My voice.
The wind will drive away all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your wickedness.
O inhabitant of Lebanon, nested in the cedars, how you will groan when pains come upon you, pain like a woman in labor."
"As surely as I live," declares the LORD, "even if Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on My right hand, I would still tear you off.
I will hand you over to those you fear, who seek your life, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans.
I will hurl you and the mother who bore you into another land, where neither of you was born, and there you will both die.
But as for the land they long to return to, they will never return there."
Is this man Coniah a despised, broken pot, a vessel no one wants? Why are he and his descendants hurled out and cast into a land they do not know?
O land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD!
This is what the LORD says: "Write this man down as childless, a man who will not prosper in his days. For none of his descendants will prosper, sitting on David's throne or ruling again in Judah."
“How terrible for the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture!” declares the the LORD.

“So this is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says to the shepherds who tend My people: You have scattered My flock and driven them away. You have not taken care of them. So I will punish you for the evil you have done,” declares the the LORD.
“Then I will gather the rest of My flock from all the lands where I sent them away. I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will grow and increase.
I will raise up shepherds over them who will care for them. They will not be afraid or discouraged anymore, and none will go missing,” declares the the LORD.
“The days are coming,” declares the the LORD, “when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch. He will be a wise King. He will do what is right and fair in the land.
In His days Judah will be saved, and Israel will live in safety. This is the name people will call Him: The LORD Our Righteousness.”
“So the days are coming,” declares the the LORD, “when they will no longer say, ‘As surely as the the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of Egypt,’

but, ‘As surely as the the LORD lives, who brought and led the descendants of the house of Israel up out of the land of the north and all the other lands where I had sent them away.’ Then they will live in their own land.”
As for the prophets: My heart is broken inside me. All my bones tremble. I am like a drunk man, like a man overcome by wine, because of the the LORD, because of His holy words.
For the land is full of unfaithful people. Because of the curse, the land mourns, and the pastures of the wilderness are dry. Their way is evil, and their power is misused.
“For both prophet and priest are ungodly. Even in My house I have found their wickedness,” declares the the LORD.
“So their path will be slippery. They will be pushed into darkness and fall in it. I will bring disaster on them in the year I punish them,” declares the the LORD.
“I have seen something terrible in the prophets of Samaria. They prophesied by Baal and led My people Israel astray.

I have also seen something terrible in the prophets of Jerusalem. They commit adultery and live a lie. They make evil people stronger, so no one turns from his evil. To Me they are all like Sodom, and the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah.”

“This is what the the LORD of Hosts says about the prophets: ‘I will make them eat bitter poison and drink poisoned water, because ungodliness has spread from the prophets of Jerusalem into all the land.’”

“This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Do not listen to the prophets who prophesy to you. They fill you with false hopes. They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.’”
“They keep saying to those who despise Me, ‘The LORD says you will have peace,’ and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart, ‘No harm will come to you.’”
“But which of them has stood in the the LORD’s council to see and hear His word? Who has listened to His word and obeyed?”
“Look, the the LORD’s storm has gone out in anger. It is a whirling wind. It will burst on the heads of the wicked.
The The LORD’s anger will not turn back until He has done everything He planned. In the last days you will understand this clearly.”
“I did not send these prophets, but they ran. I did not speak to them, but they prophesied.
If they had stood in My council, they would have told My people My words. They would have turned them from their evil ways and bad deeds.”
“Am I a God who is only nearby?” declares the the LORD. “Am I not a God from far away?”
“Can anyone hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” declares the the LORD. “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” declares the the LORD.
“I have heard what the prophets say. They prophesy lies in My name. They say, ‘I had a dream! I had a dream!’
How long will this go on in the hearts of these lying prophets, who prophesy false ideas from their own minds?
They tell each other their dreams, hoping My people will forget My name, just as their fathers forgot My name by worshiping Baal.”
“Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream. But let the one who has My word speak My word faithfully. What does straw have in common with grain?” declares the the LORD.
“Is not My word like fire?” declares the the LORD. “And like a hammer that breaks a rock?”
“So I am against the prophets,” declares the the LORD, “who steal My words from one another.”
“I am against the prophets,” declares the the LORD, “who use their own tongues and say, ‘The LORD declares.’”

“I am against the prophets who prophesy false dreams,” declares the the LORD. “They lead My people astray with their reckless lies. I did not send them or command them, and they do not help these people at all,” declares the the LORD.
“When these people or a prophet or priest asks you, ‘What is the the LORD’s message?’ you must say, ‘What message? I will abandon you,’ declares the the LORD.”
“As for the prophet, priest, or anyone who says, ‘This is the the LORD’s message,’ I will punish that man and his family.”
“This is what each of you must say to his neighbor and brother: ‘What has the LORD answered? What has the LORD spoken?’”
“But you must no longer talk about ‘the the LORD’s message,’ because every person's own words will be his burden. You have twisted the words of the living God, the the LORD of Hosts, our God.”
“This is what you must say to the prophet: ‘What has the LORD answered you? What has the LORD spoken?’”
“But if you say, ‘This is the the LORD’s message,’ then this is what the LORD says: ‘Because you said, “The LORD's message,” even though I warned you not to say, “The LORD's message,”’”
“Therefore I will surely forget you and cast you out of My presence, along with the city I gave to you and your fathers.
I will bring on you everlasting shame and lasting disgrace that will not be forgotten.”

After King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon took King Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim of Judah into exile, along with Judah's officials, craftsmen, and metalworkers from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon, the LORD showed me two baskets of figs set in front of the temple of the LORD.
One basket held very good figs, like early figs. The other held very bad figs, too bad to eat.
The LORD said to me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "The good figs are very good, and the bad figs are very bad—too bad to eat."
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so I will treat the exiles of Judah for good—the ones I sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I will watch over them for good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up, not tear them down; I will plant them, not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know Me, for I am the LORD. They will be My people, and I will be their God, for they will return to Me with all their heart.

"But like the bad figs, so bad they cannot be eaten—thus says the LORD—so I will give up Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, the rest of Jerusalem who remain in this land, and those who live in the land of Egypt.
I will make them a horror and an evil to all the kingdoms of the earth—a disgrace, a proverb, a taunt, and a curse in all the places where I drive them.
I will send against them sword, famine, and plague until they are gone from the land I gave to them and their fathers."
The word that came to Jeremiah about all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah. That was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and to all who lived in Jerusalem. He said,
"From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this day—twenty-three years—the word of the LORD has come to me. I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened.
The LORD has sent all His servants the prophets to you again and again, but you have not listened or turned your ears to hear."
They said, "Turn now, each one of you, from your evil way and your evil deeds. Live in the land the LORD gave to you and your fathers forever and ever.
Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them. Do not make the LORD angry with the work of your hands, and He will not bring disaster on you."
"But you did not listen to Me," declares the LORD, "and you made Me angry with the work of your hands, to your own harm."
"Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Because you have not obeyed My words,

look, I will summon all the families of the north,' declares the LORD, 'and I will bring My servant Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, against this land, against its people, and against all these nations around. I will completely destroy them and make them an object of horror and scorn, an everlasting ruin.
I will take away from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bride and bridegroom, the sound of millstones, and the light of the lamp.
This whole land will become a ruined waste, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.'"
"But when seventy years are complete, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation, the land of the Chaldeans, for their guilt," declares the LORD, "and I will make it an everlasting desolation.
I will bring on that land all the words I have spoken against it, everything written in this book that Jeremiah has prophesied against all the nations.
For many nations and great kings will make them serve too, and I will repay them for what they have done and for the work of their hands."
"For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to me: 'Take this cup of the wine of wrath from My hand and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.
They will drink and stagger and go mad because of the sword I am sending among them.'"
So I took the cup from the LORD's hand and made all the nations drink it, the ones the LORD sent me to:
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, her kings and officials, to make them a ruin, a desolation, a hissing, and a curse—as they are today—
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials, and all his people;
all the mixed tribes; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the rest of Ashdod;
all the kings of Tyre and Sidon; the kings of the coastlands across the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who trim the hair at their temples;
all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed tribes who live in the desert;
all the kings of Zimri, Elam, and Media;
all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another; and all the kingdoms of the earth that are on the face of the ground. After all of them, the king of Sheshach will drink it too.
"Then you are to tell them, 'This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk, vomit, and fall. Never rise again, because of the sword I am sending among you.'"
"If they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink it, then you are to tell them, 'This is what the LORD of Hosts says: You must drink it!

Look, I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears My name. Will you then go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am summoning a sword against all the people who live on the earth,' declares the LORD of Hosts."

"So you are to prophesy all these words against them and say to them: 'The LORD will roar from on high; He will raise His voice from His holy dwelling. He will roar loudly against His shepherds. He will shout like those who tread grapes, against all who live on the earth.
The noise will reach the ends of the earth, for the LORD has a case against the nations. He will judge all people. He will put the wicked to the sword,' declares the LORD."
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Look, disaster is going out from nation to nation, and a great storm is being stirred up from the farthest ends of the earth.
Those killed by the LORD on that day will be spread from one end of the earth to the other. They will not be mourned, gathered, or buried. They will be like dung lying on the ground.'"
"Wail, you shepherds, and cry out; roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock. For the days of your slaughter have come; you will fall and be shattered like fine pottery.
Flight will be lost to the shepherds, and escape to the leaders of the flock.
Hear the cries of the shepherds and the wails of the leaders of the flock, for the LORD is destroying their pasture.
The peaceful meadows will be silent because of the fierce anger of the LORD.
Like a lion He has left His thicket, for their land has become a desolation because of the sword of the oppressor and because of His fierce anger."
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the LORD, saying:

“Thus says the LORD: Stand in the courtyard of the LORD’s house, and speak to all the people from the cities of Judah who come to worship in the LORD’s house. Tell them everything I have commanded you to say. Do not leave out a single word.
Perhaps they will listen and each turn from his evil way. Then I will change My mind and not bring on them the disaster I plan to bring because of the evil things they have done.
And say to them, ‘This is what the LORD says: If you do not listen to Me and walk in My law, which I have set before you,
and if you do not listen to the words of My servants the prophets, whom I send to you again and again, though you have not listened,
then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.’”
The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speak these words in the house of the LORD.
When Jeremiah finished saying everything the the LORD had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him. They said, “You must die!”

“Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD that this house will be like Shiloh and this city will be destroyed and left empty?” Then all the people gathered around Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.
When the officials of Judah heard about this, they came up from the king’s palace to the house of the LORD and sat at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD’s house.
Then the priests and prophets said to the officials and all the people, “This man should be sentenced to death, because he has prophesied against this city. You have heard it with your own ears.”
Then Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people, “The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and this city. I have spoken all the words you have heard.
Now change your ways and your actions, and obey the LORD your God. Then the LORD will change His mind and not bring on you the disaster He has announced.
As for me, I am in your hands. Do to me whatever you think is good and right.

But be sure of this: If you kill me, you will make yourselves guilty of an innocent man’s blood. That guilt will fall on you, on this city, and on everyone who lives here. For the LORD has truly sent me to speak all these words to you.”
Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and prophets, “This man does not deserve to die, because he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God.”
Some of the elders of the land stood up and said to the whole crowd, “

Micah of Moresheth prophesied during the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He told all the people of Judah, ‘This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the temple hill will become a forest.’

Did Hezekiah king of Judah or anyone in Judah put him to death? No. Hezekiah feared the LORD and asked the LORD for help, and the LORD changed His mind and did not bring on them the disaster He had threatened. But if we kill Jeremiah, we will bring great harm on ourselves.”
There was another man who prophesied in the name of the LORD. His name was Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath Jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land in the same way Jeremiah did.
When King Jehoiakim and all his officers and officials heard his words, the king wanted to kill him. Uriah heard about it, became afraid, and fled to Egypt.
But King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt. Elnathan son of Achbor went, along with other men.
They brought Uriah back from Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim. The king killed him with a sword and threw his body into the burial place of the common people.
But Ahikam son of Shaphan stood with Jeremiah and kept the people from putting him to death.
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"This is what the LORD said to me: Make for yourself a yoke of straps and bars, and put it on your neck.
Send word to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon through the envoys who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
Give them a message for their masters: This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Tell your masters, "
By My great power and outstretched arm, I made the earth and the people and animals on it, and I give it to whomever I please.
So now I have placed all these lands under the authority of My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I have even given him the wild animals to serve him.
All nations will serve him and his son and grandson, until the time for his own land comes; then many nations and great kings will enslave him.

As for the nation or kingdom that does not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and does not place its neck under his yoke, I will punish that nation by sword, famine, and plague, declares the LORD, until I have destroyed it by his hand.
So do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your fortune-tellers, or your sorcerers who tell you, 'You will not serve the king of Babylon.'
For they prophesy to you a lie that will move you far from your land; I will drive you out, and you will die.
But the nation that brings its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will leave in its own land, to farm it and live there, declares the LORD."
I also spoke this same message to Zedekiah king of Judah: "Put your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon. Serve him and his people, and live!
Why should you and your people die by sword, famine, and plague, as the LORD has said will happen to any nation that does not serve the king of Babylon?
Do not listen to the prophets who say, 'You will not serve the king of Babylon,' because they are prophesying lies to you.
'I have not sent them,' declares the LORD. 'They are prophesying lies in My name, so I will drive you out and you will die—you and the prophets who prophesy to you.'"

Then I said to the priests and all this people, "This is what the LORD says: Do not listen to your prophets who prophesy to you, saying, 'The articles of the LORD's house will soon be brought back from Babylon.' They are prophesying lies to you.
Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon and live! Why should this city become a ruin?
If they are prophets and have the word of the LORD, let them now pray to the LORD of Hosts that the articles left in the LORD's house, the king's house, and Jerusalem not be taken to Babylon."
For this is what the LORD of Hosts says about the pillars, the Sea, the bases, and the rest of the articles left in this city—
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem—
yes, this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says about the articles left in the LORD's house, the king's house, and Jerusalem:
"They will be taken to Babylon and will stay there until the day I attend to them," declares the LORD. "Then I will bring them back and restore them to this place."

In the fourth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, at the start of his rule, in the fifth month, Hananiah son of Azur, a prophet from Gibeon, spoke to me in the house of the the LORD. He spoke before the priests and all the people. He said:
"This is what the the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years, I will bring back to this place all the items from the house of the the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from here and carried to Babylon.

I will also bring back to this place Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the people of Judah who were taken to Babylon,' says the the LORD. 'I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.'"
Then the prophet Jeremiah spoke to the prophet Hananiah before the priests and all the people standing in the house of the the LORD.

Jeremiah the prophet said, "Amen! May the the LORD do that. May the the LORD make your words come true. May He bring back the items from the house of the the LORD and all the captives from Babylon to this place.
But listen to this word that I am speaking to you and to all the people.
The prophets who lived long ago, before us, prophesied against many countries and great kingdoms. They spoke about war, disaster, and disease.
A prophet who promises peace proves he was truly sent by the the LORD only when his words come true."
Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke off Jeremiah's neck and broke it.

Hananiah spoke before all the people. He said, "This is what the the LORD says: 'In the same way, within two years, I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the necks of all the nations.'" Then the prophet Jeremiah went on his way.
After Hananiah the prophet broke the yoke from Jeremiah's neck, the word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah.
The the LORD said to Jeremiah, "Go and tell Hananiah, 'This is what the the LORD says: You broke wooden yokes, but now you must make yokes of iron.'"

"For this is what the the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'I have put an iron yoke on the necks of all these nations, so they will serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. They will serve him. I have even given him the wild animals.'"
Then the prophet Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah, "Listen, Hananiah. The the LORD has not sent you. You have made these people trust in a lie.
So this is what the the LORD says: 'Look, I am removing you from the earth. You will die this year, because you have led people to rebel against the the LORD.'"
So Hananiah the prophet died that same year, in the seventh month.

This is the text of the letter Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the rest of the elders among the exiles, and to the priests, the prophets, and all the people Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers had been taken from Jerusalem into exile.
The letter was carried by Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to King Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon. It said:
"This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles I carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and settle down. Plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Take wives and have sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons and give your daughters in marriage, so they too may have sons and daughters. Have many children there; don't let your numbers drop.
Work for the good of the city where I have sent you into exile. Pray to the LORD for it, because if it does well, you will do well too."
"For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Don't let your prophets and fortune-tellers trick you, and don't listen to the dreams you dream up.
They are prophesying lies to you in My name. I didn't send them," declares the LORD.
"For this is what the LORD says: When Babylon's seventy years are finished, I will take care of you and keep My good promise to bring you back to this place.
For I know the plans I have for you," declares the LORD, "plans for your good and not for harm, to give you a future and a hope.
"Then you will call on Me and come and pray to Me, and I will listen to you.
You will seek Me and find Me when you search for Me with all your heart.

"I will be found by you," declares the LORD, "and I will bring you back from captivity. I will gather you from all the nations and places where I scattered you," declares the LORD. "I will bring you back to the place from which I carried you away into exile."
"Because you may say, 'The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon,'
this is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David's throne and about all the people still in this city—your brothers who didn't go with you into exile:
'I will send sword, famine, and plague against them, and I will make them like rotten figs that are too bad to eat.

I will chase them with sword, famine, and plague. I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth—a curse, a ruin, a thing people hiss at, and a disgrace among all the nations where I have scattered them.
For they haven't listened to My words,' declares the LORD. 'I sent My servants the prophets to them again and again, and you exiles haven't listened either,' declares the LORD."
So now, all you exiles, hear the word of the LORD, which He sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

"This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying to you in My name: I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will put them to death before your eyes.
Because of them, all the exiles of Judah in Babylon will use this curse: 'May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned to death in the fire!'

For they have done a shameful thing in Israel; they have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and have spoken a lying word in My name, which I didn't command them to speak. I am the One who knows, and I am a witness," declares the LORD.
"And you are to tell Shemaiah the Nehelamite,"

"This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Because you sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and to all the priests, saying,

'The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be the chief officer in the house of the LORD, responsible for any crazy person who claims to be a prophet. You are to put him in the stocks and chains.
So why haven't you rebuked Jeremiah from Anathoth, who prophesies to you?
For he has sent to us in Babylon, saying, "It will be a long time. Build houses and settle down, and plant gardens and eat their fruit."'"
Zephaniah the priest read this letter to Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
"Send a message to all the exiles: 'This is what the LORD says: Because Shemaiah the Nehelamite has prophesied to you, even though I didn't send him, and has made you trust in a lie,

therefore, this is what the LORD says: I am about to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. None of them will survive among this people, and none will see the good I am about to do for My people,' declares the LORD, 'because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD.'"
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
The LORD, the God of Israel, said, "Write in a book all the words I have spoken to you.
For the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will bring back My people Israel and Judah from exile. I will bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and they will own it again."
These are the words the LORD spoke about Israel and Judah:
"This is what the LORD says: We have heard a cry of terror, of fear and no peace.
Ask and see: Can a man give birth? Why then do I see every strong man with his hands on his stomach like a woman in labor, with every face turned pale?
How terrible that day will be! No other day is like it. It will be a time of trouble for Jacob, but he will be saved out of it.
In that day, declares the LORD Almighty, I will break the yoke off their necks and tear off their bonds. No longer will foreigners make them slaves.
Instead, they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them."

"So do not be afraid, Jacob My servant, declares the LORD. Do not be dismayed, Israel. I will surely save you from a faraway place, and your descendants from the land of their exile. Jacob will return and live in peace and safety, and no one will make him afraid.

I am with you and will save you, declares the LORD. Though I completely destroy all the nations where I scattered you, I will not completely destroy you. I will discipline you, but only with justice. I will not leave you unpunished."
"This is what the LORD says: Your wound is incurable, and your injury cannot be healed.
No one will plead your case. There is no medicine for your sore, and no healing for you.
All your allies have forgotten you; they do not care about you. I have struck you like an enemy would, with the punishment of a cruel foe, because your guilt is so great and your sins so many.
Why do you cry out over your wound, your pain that has no cure? Because of your great guilt and many sins I have done these things to you.
But those who devour you will be devoured; all your enemies will go into exile. Those who plunder you will be plundered, and all who steal from you I will hand over to be plundered.
But I will restore you to health and heal your wounds, declares the LORD, because you are called an outcast, Zion, whom no one cares for."
"This is what the LORD says: I will restore Jacob's prosperity and have compassion on his dwellings. The city will be rebuilt on its ruins, and the palace will stand in its proper place.
From them will come songs of thanksgiving and the sound of rejoicing. I will add to their numbers, and they will not be decreased. I will bring them honor, and they will not be looked down on.
Their children will be as in days of old, and their community will be established before Me. I will punish all who oppress them.
Their leader will be one of their own; their ruler will arise from among them. I will bring him near, and he will come close to Me, for who would dare to come near Me? declares the LORD.
So you will be My people, and I will be your God."
Look, the storm of the LORD has gone out in fury, a driving wind. It will burst upon the head of the wicked.
The fierce anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart. In days to come you will understand this.
At that time, declares the LORD, I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be My people.
Thus says the LORD: "The people who survived the sword found favor in the wilderness when Israel went to find rest.
The LORD appeared to us from far away and said, 'I have loved you with an everlasting love. That is why I have drawn you with faithful love.'"
"Again I will build you, and you shall be built, O Virgin Israel! Again you shall adorn yourself with tambourines and go out in the dance of those who celebrate.
Again you shall plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria; the planters shall plant and enjoy the fruit.
For there will be a day when watchmen call out in the hill country of Ephraim, 'Arise, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God.'"
For thus says the LORD: "Sing aloud with gladness for Jacob, and shout for the chief of the nations. Proclaim, praise, and say, 'O the LORD, save Your people, the remnant of Israel.'"

"Behold, I will bring them from the north country and gather them from the farthest parts of the earth. Among them will be the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the one in labor. Together, a great company, they will return here.

They will come with weeping, and with pleas for mercy I will lead them back. I will make them walk beside streams of water, on a straight path where they will not stumble. For I am a Father to Israel, and Ephraim is My firstborn."
"Hear the word of the LORD, O nations, and declare it in the distant coastlands. Say, 'He who scattered Israel will gather him and keep him as a shepherd keeps His flock.'
For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he."

"They will come and sing aloud on the heights of Zion, and they will be radiant over the goodness of the LORD—over the grain, the wine, and the oil, and over the young of the flock and herd. Their life will be like a watered garden, and they will not grow weak anymore.
Then the virgin will rejoice in the dance, and the young men and the old will be merry together. I will turn their mourning into joy; I will comfort them and give them gladness instead of sorrow.
I will satisfy the souls of the priests with abundance, and My people will be satisfied with My goodness, declares the LORD."
Thus says the LORD: "A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping for her children; she refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more."
Thus says the LORD: "Keep your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your work, declares the LORD, and they will come back from the land of the enemy.
There is hope for your future, declares the LORD, and your children will come back to their own country."
"I have surely heard Ephraim grieving: 'You have disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like an untrained calf. Bring me back, and I will be restored, for You are the LORD my God.
For after I turned away, I repented; after I was instructed, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed and confused, because I carried the shame of my youth.'
Is Ephraim My dear son? Is he My darling child? For as often as I speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore My heart yearns for him; I will surely have mercy on him, declares the LORD."
"Set up road markers for yourself; make guideposts for yourself. Consider well the highway, the road by which you went. Return, O Virgin Israel, return to these your cities.
How long will you waver, O faithless daughter? For the LORD has created a new thing on the earth: a woman will encircle a man."

Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: "Once more they will use these words in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: 'The LORD bless you, O home of righteousness, O Holy Hill!'
And Judah and all its cities will dwell there together—the farmers and those who wander with their flocks.
For I will satisfy the weary soul, and every weak soul I will fill."
At this I awoke and saw, and my sleep was pleasant to me.
"Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.

And it will come to pass that just as I have watched over them to pluck up and break down, to overthrow, destroy, and bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares the LORD."
"In those days they will no longer say, 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.'
But everyone will die for his own sin. Each man who eats sour grapes—his teeth will be set on edge."
"Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah,
not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt. They broke My covenant, though I was their husband, declares the LORD.

For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I will put My law within them, and I will write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

No longer will each one teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, 'Know the LORD,' for they will all know Me, from the least to the greatest, declares the LORD. For I will forgive their sin, and I will remember their sin no more."
Thus says the LORD, who gives the sun for light by day and the fixed order of the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar—the LORD of Hosts is His name:
"If these fixed orders depart from before Me, declares the LORD, then the offspring of Israel will cease to be a nation before Me forever.

Thus says the LORD: 'If the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below can be explored, then I will cast off all the offspring of Israel for all that they have done, declares the LORD.'"
"Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when the city will be rebuilt for the LORD from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
The measuring line will go out farther, straight to the hill Gareb, and then turn to Goah.

The whole valley of the dead bodies and the ashes, and all the fields as far as the Brook Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, will be sacred to the LORD. It will never again be uprooted or overthrown."
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the courtyard of the guard in the palace of the king of Judah.
Zedekiah king of Judah had put Jeremiah there and asked, "Why do you prophesy that the LORD says He is giving this city to the king of Babylon?
The LORD says Zedekiah will not escape the Chaldeans. He will be handed over to the king of Babylon, speak with him face to face, and see him eye to eye.
He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, where he will stay until the LORD deals with him. The LORD declares that if you fight the Chaldeans, you will not succeed."
Jeremiah said, "The word of the LORD came to me. The LORD said my cousin Hanamel son of Shallum was coming to say, 'Buy my field in Anathoth, because you have the right to redeem it.'

Just as the LORD had said, Hanamel came to me in the courtyard of the guard and said, 'Buy my field in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin. You have the right to inherit it and redeem it, so buy it for yourself.'
Then I knew this was the word of the LORD."
So I bought the field in Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel and weighed out seventeen shekels of silver.
I wrote the deed, sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed the silver on scales.
I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy with its terms and conditions and the open copy.
I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, in front of my cousin Hanamel and the witnesses who signed the deed, and in front of all the Jews sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
In front of them I gave Baruch this command:
"This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Take these deeds, the sealed deed of purchase and the open deed, and put them in a clay jar so they will last many days.
For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Houses, fields, and vineyards will be bought again in this land."
After I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:
"Ah, Lord the LORD! You made heaven and earth with Your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for You.
You show faithful love to thousands, but You repay the sin of the fathers by letting its consequences fall on their children. You are the great and mighty God; the LORD of Hosts is Your name.
You are great in wisdom and mighty in action. Your eyes are open to all the ways of people, and You reward each one according to his ways and the fruit of his deeds.
You performed signs and wonders in Egypt, and You still do to this day, in Israel and among all people. You made a name for Yourself, as it is today.
You brought Your people Israel out of Egypt with signs, wonders, a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and great terror.
You gave them this land that You swore to give their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.
They came in and took possession of it, but they did not obey Your voice or follow Your law. They did none of the things You commanded, so You brought all this disaster on them.

Now the siege ramps have reached the city to capture it. Because of sword, famine, and plague, the city has been handed over to the Chaldeans who attack it. What You said has happened, and You see it.
Yet You, Lord the LORD, told me, 'Buy the field with silver and call witnesses,' even though the city has been handed over to the Chaldeans."
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
"I am the LORD, the God of all people. Is anything too hard for Me?
So this is what the LORD says: I will hand this city over to the Chaldeans and to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

The Chaldeans fighting against this city will come and set it on fire. They will burn it down, along with the houses where people burned incense to Baal on the roofs and poured out drink offerings to other gods to make Me angry.
From their youth, the people of Israel and Judah have done only evil in My sight. The people of Israel have done nothing but provoke Me to anger by what their hands have made, declares the LORD.
This city has provoked My anger and fury from the day they built it until now, so I will remove it from My sight.

All the evil done by the people of Israel and Judah to provoke Me to anger—by their kings, officials, priests, prophets, and by the people of Judah and those living in Jerusalem—has brought this on them.
They turned their backs on Me instead of facing Me. Though I taught them again and again, they would not listen or accept correction.
They set up their disgusting idols in the house that bears My name and made it unclean.

They built high places to Baal in the Valley of Ben Hinnom to sacrifice their sons and daughters to Molech. I never commanded this; it never entered My mind. They did this terrible thing and led Judah into sin.
"So now, this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about this city, which you say will be handed over to the king of Babylon by sword, famine, and plague:
I will gather them from all the lands where I drove them in My anger, fury, and great wrath. I will bring them back to this place and let them live in safety.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one way, so that they will fear Me forever. This will be for their good and for their children after them.
I will make an everlasting covenant with them: I will never turn away from doing good to them, and I will put the fear of Me in their hearts so they will not turn away from Me.
I will gladly do good to them. I will plant them in this land with all My heart and all My soul.
I brought all this great disaster on this people, and in the same way I will bring on them all the good I have promised.
Fields will be bought in this land, though you say, 'It is a wasteland with no people or animals. It has been handed over to the Chaldeans.'

People will buy fields with silver, write deeds, seal them, and call witnesses in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, the hill country, the western foothills, and the Negev. I will restore their fortunes, declares the LORD."
While Jeremiah was still held in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the the LORD came to him a second time.
It said, "This is what the the LORD says: He made the earth and shaped it to set it in place. The the LORD is His name.
Call to Me, and I will answer you. I will tell you great and hidden things you do not know."
"For this is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the houses in this city and the houses of the kings of Judah: They have been torn down to defend against siege ramps and swords.
The Babylonians are coming to fight and to fill these places with the dead bodies of the people I struck down in My anger and wrath. I also hid My face from this city because of all their evil."
"Look, I will bring healing and cure to this city. I will heal them and show them plenty of peace and truth.
I will bring Judah and Israel back from captivity and rebuild them as they were before.
I will cleanse them from all their sin against Me and forgive all their sins and rebellions against Me.

Then this city will be a name of joy to Me, a praise and glory to all nations on earth who hear about all the good I do for them. They will tremble and shake because of all the good and peace I give this city."

'This is what the the LORD says: "In this place you say is a ruin, without people or animals—in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem that are empty, without people, animals, or anyone living there—people will again hear

the voice of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, and the voice of those who bring thank offerings to the house of the the LORD. They will say, "Give thanks to the the LORD of Hosts, for the the LORD is good; His faithful love endures forever." For I will restore the land from captivity as before,' says the the LORD."
'This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: "Again in this empty place, without people or animals, and in all its cities, there will be pastures where shepherds rest their flocks.

In the cities of the hill country, the western foothills, the Negev, the land of Benjamin, the area around Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hands of the one who counts them," says the the LORD.'
"Look, the days are coming, declares the the LORD, when I will fulfill the good promise I made to the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will make a righteous Branch grow for David. He will do what is just and right in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will live in safety. This is the name by which she will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness."
"For this is what the the LORD says: 'David will never fail to have a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel,
and the priests from the tribe of Levi will never fail to have a man before Me to offer burnt offerings, grain offerings, and sacrifices.'"
The word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
"If you can break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night, so that day and night no longer come at their appointed time,
then My covenant with David My servant can be broken, so that he will not have a son to reign on his throne, and My covenant with the priests from the tribe of Levi who serve Me.
Just as the host of heaven cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the descendants of David My servant and the Levites who serve Me."
The word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
"Have you not noticed what these people are saying: 'The the LORD has rejected the two families He chose'? So they despise My people and no longer regard them as a nation.
This is what the the LORD says: If I have not established My covenant with day and night and the fixed laws of heaven and earth,

then I will reject the descendants of Jacob and David My servant, and will not choose a ruler from his descendants to rule over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will restore them from captivity and have compassion on them."

This is the message the the LORD gave Jeremiah when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and his whole army, all the kingdoms under his control, and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and its cities.
"This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, 'This is what the the LORD says:
'You will not escape his power. You will be captured and handed over to him. You will see the king of Babylon with your own eyes, and he will speak to you face to face. Then you will go to Babylon.
'Yet hear the word of the the LORD, O Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what the the LORD says concerning you: You will not die by the sword.

'You will die in peace. Just as people burned spices for your fathers, the kings who came before you, they will burn spices for you and mourn, saying, "Alas, my lord!" For I have spoken this word, declares the the LORD.'"
Then Jeremiah the prophet told all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,
while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and all the remaining cities of Judah—against Lachish and Azekah. Those were the only fortified cities left in Judah.
After King Zedekiah made an agreement with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim freedom,
each man was to release his Hebrew slaves, both male and female, so no one would enslave a fellow Jew.
All the officials and all the people who had entered the agreement agreed to free their male and female servants and no longer hold them in bondage. They obeyed and set them free.
But afterward they changed their minds and took back the men and women they had freed, forcing them to become slaves again.
Then this message came to Jeremiah from the the LORD:
"This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I made a covenant with your fathers when I brought them out of Egypt, out of slavery, saying:

'At the end of seven years, each of you must release his Hebrew brother who has sold himself to you. He may serve you six years, but then you must let him go free. But your fathers did not listen or pay attention.'
"Recently you turned back and did what is right in My eyes by proclaiming freedom to one another. You made a covenant before Me in the house called by My name.
"But then you turned around and dishonored My name. Each of you took back his male and female servants whom you had set free to go where they wanted, and you forced them back into slavery.

"Therefore this is what the the LORD says: You have not obeyed Me; you have not proclaimed freedom to your brothers and neighbors. So I now proclaim freedom for you, declares the the LORD—not freedom to live, but freedom to fall by the sword, plague, and famine. I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
"And those who broke My covenant and did not keep the terms of the covenant they made before Me, I will treat like the calf they cut in two and walked between its pieces.
"The officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the pieces of the calf—
"I will hand them over to their enemies who seek their lives. Their dead bodies will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
