"And I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials to their enemies who seek their lives, to the army of the king of Babylon that has withdrawn from you.

"Look, I will command, declares the the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, capture it, and burn it with fire. I will make the cities of Judah a wasteland, with no one living in them."
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the the LORD during the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
"Go to the Rechabite family and speak to them. Bring them into one of the rooms in the the LORD's temple, and give them wine to drink."
So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, along with his brothers, all his sons, and the whole Rechabite family.

I brought them to the the LORD's temple, into the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God. That room was next to the room of the officials, above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, who guarded the doorway.
Then I set pitchers full of wine and cups before the Rechabites, and I said to them, "Drink wine."
They said, "We will not drink wine. Our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab told us, 'You and your children must never drink wine.

You must not build houses, plant fields, or plant vineyards for yourselves. None of it will be yours. Instead, you must live in tents all your lives, so you may live a long time on the land where you are foreigners.'
We have obeyed our ancestor Jonadab in everything he commanded. We, our wives, our sons, and our daughters have not drunk wine all our lives.
We have not built houses to live in. We have no vineyards, fields, or crops.
We have lived in tents and done everything our ancestor Jonadab commanded us.
"When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came up against this land, we said, 'Let's go to Jerusalem to escape the Babylonian and Aramean armies.' So we have been living in Jerusalem."
Then the word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah:

"This is what the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Go and tell the people of Judah and those living in Jerusalem, 'Will you not learn a lesson and listen to My words?' declares the the LORD."

"The words of Jonadab son of Rechab have been carried out. He ordered his sons not to drink wine, and they have not drunk wine to this day, because they obeyed their father's command. But I have spoken to you again and again, and you have not listened to Me.

I sent all My servants the prophets to you again and again. I said, 'Turn now, each of you, from your evil ways. Do what is right. Do not follow other gods to serve them. Then you will live in the land I gave to you and your ancestors.' But you did not listen to Me or pay attention.
The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept their father's command, but you have not listened to Me."

"Therefore this is what the the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am bringing on Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem all the disaster I have spoken against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer."

Then Jeremiah said to the Rechabite family, "This is what the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Because you obeyed the command of your father Jonadab and kept all his commands, doing everything he told you,
therefore this is what the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Jonadab son of Rechab will never fail to have a descendant to serve Me."
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, the the LORD gave Jeremiah this message:
“Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you against Israel, Judah, and all the nations. Write from the day I first spoke to you in the days of Josiah until today.
Maybe the people of Judah will hear about all the disaster I plan to bring on them. Then each person can turn from his evil way, and I will forgive his sin and guilt.”
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah. Baruch wrote on the scroll, from Jeremiah’s mouth, all the words the the LORD had spoken to Jeremiah.
Jeremiah commanded Baruch, “I am confined. I cannot go to the the LORD’s temple.

You go to the the LORD’s temple on a day of fasting. Read the words of the the LORD from the scroll you wrote from my mouth. Read them to the people, and also to all the people of Judah who come from their towns.
Maybe their prayer will reach the the LORD. Maybe each person will turn from his evil way. The the LORD has spoken great anger and wrath against these people.”
Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet commanded. He read the words of the the LORD from the book in the the LORD’s temple.

In the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, a fast was called before the the LORD for all the people in Jerusalem and for all who came to Jerusalem from the towns of Judah.

Baruch read Jeremiah’s words from the book. He read them in the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper courtyard at the entrance of the New Gate of the the LORD’s temple. He read them to all the people.
Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the the LORD from the book.

He went down to the king’s palace, to the scribe’s room. All the officials were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.
Micaiah told them everything he had heard when Baruch read the book to the people.

The officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch. They said, “Bring the scroll you read to the people, and come here.” So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll and came to them.
They said to him, “Sit down, please, and read it to us.” So Baruch read it to them.
When they heard all the words, they looked at each other in fear. They said to Baruch, “We must tell the king all these words.”
They asked Baruch, “Please tell us how you wrote all these words. Did Jeremiah dictate them to you?”
Baruch answered, “He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them with ink on the book.”
The officials said to Baruch, “Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Do not let anyone know where you are.”
They went to the king in the courtyard. They had left the scroll in the room of Elishama the scribe. They told the king everything.
The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll. He took it from the room of Elishama the scribe. Jehudi read it to the king and to all the officials standing beside the king.
It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in the winter house. A fire was burning in a brazier in front of him.
As Jehudi read three or four columns, the king cut them off with a scribe’s knife and threw them into the fire in the brazier. He kept doing this until the whole scroll was burned up in the fire.
The king and all his servants who heard all these words were not afraid. They did not tear their clothes.
Even Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, but he would not listen to them.
The king ordered Jerahmeel son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the the LORD hid them.
After the king burned the scroll and the words Baruch had written from Jeremiah’s mouth, the word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah:
“Take another scroll and write on it all the words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

“About Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say: ‘This is what the the LORD says: You burned this scroll and said, “Why did you write on it that the king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land and remove both people and animals from it?”’

“Therefore this is what the the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David. His dead body will be thrown out into the heat by day and the frost by night.
“I will punish him, his children, and his servants for their sin. I will bring on them, and on the people of Jerusalem and Judah, all the disaster I spoke against them. But they did not listen.”

Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe. Baruch wrote on it, from Jeremiah’s mouth, all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. Many similar words were added to them.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made Zedekiah son of Josiah king over the land of Judah in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim.
Neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the LORD that He had spoken through Jeremiah the prophet.
Yet King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "Please pray to the LORD our God for us."
Now Jeremiah was free to come and go among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.
Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt, and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report about them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet:

"Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Tell the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of Me: Behold, Pharaoh's army, which has come to help you, is going back to its own land in Egypt. Then the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city. They will capture it and burn it down.' Thus says the LORD: Do not deceive yourselves by saying, 'The Chaldeans will surely go away from us,' for they will not go.
Even if you defeated the whole Chaldean army fighting against you, and only wounded men were left in their tents, they would still rise up and burn this city down."
Now when the Chaldean army withdrew from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to claim his share there among the people.
But when he reached the Benjamin Gate, the captain of the guard, whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah, arrested him and said, "You are going over to the Chaldeans!"
Jeremiah said, "That is a lie! I am not going over to the Chaldeans." But Irijah would not listen to him. He arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
The officials were angry with Jeremiah. They beat him and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe, because they had turned it into a prison.
Jeremiah was put into a cell in the dungeon and stayed there many days.

Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought to the palace. He asked him privately, "Is there a word from the LORD?" "There is," Jeremiah replied. "You will be handed over to the king of Babylon."
Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What have I done against you or your servants or this people, that you have put me in prison?
Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or this land'?
But now, please hear, my lord the king: Let my plea come before you. Do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, or I will die there."

So King Zedekiah ordered that Jeremiah be confined in the courtyard of the guard and be given a loaf of bread each day from the bakers' street until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
Now Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jehucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchijah heard what Jeremiah was saying to all the people:

“This is what the LORD says: ‘Whoever stays in this city will die by sword, famine, or disease, but whoever surrenders to the Chaldeans will live. He will keep his life like treasure taken in war, and he will live.’
‘This is what the LORD says: This city will surely be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.’”

Then the officials said to the king, “This man must be put to death, because he is discouraging the soldiers who are still in this city and all the people by saying things like this to them. He is not looking out for these people; he wants to ruin them.”
“Here he is,” King Zedekiah replied. “He is in your hands, because the king cannot do anything to stop you.”

So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchijah, the king’s son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah with ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
Now Ebed-Melech the Cushite, a eunuch in the king’s palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. While the king was sitting at the Gate of Benjamin,
Ebed-Melech went out from the king’s palace and said to the king,
“My lord the king, these men have done a wicked thing to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into the cistern, where he will die of hunger, because there is no more bread in the city.”
So the king commanded Ebed-Melech the Cushite, “Take thirty men from here with you and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies.”

Then Ebed-Melech took the men with him and went to the king’s palace, to a room under the treasury. He took old rags and worn-out clothes from there and lowered them with ropes into the cistern to Jeremiah.
And Ebed-Melech the Cushite called out to Jeremiah, “Put these rags and worn-out clothes under your arms to pad the ropes.” So Jeremiah did so.
Then they pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to the third entrance of the house of the LORD. “I want to ask you something,” the king said to Jeremiah. “Do not hide anything from me.”
“If I tell you,” Jeremiah replied, “you will surely put me to death. And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me.”
But King Zedekiah secretly swore to Jeremiah, “As surely as the LORD lives, who has given us breath, I will not put you to death, and I will not hand you over to these men who are seeking your life.”

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “This is what the LORD, the God of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘If you surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, then you will live, this city will not be burned down, and you and your household will survive.
But if you do not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, then this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans, who will burn it down, and you yourself will not escape their power.’”
But King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “I am afraid of the Jews who have gone over to the Chaldeans, because the Chaldeans may hand me over to them, and they may mistreat me.”
“They will not hand you over,” Jeremiah replied. “Obey the voice of the LORD in what I am telling you, so that things will go well for you and you will live.”
“But if you refuse to surrender, this is what the LORD has shown me:

‘All the women who are left in the house of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon, and those women will say, “Your trusted friends misled you; they overpowered you. Now that your feet are stuck in the mud, they have turned away.”
All your wives and children will be brought out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself will not escape their grasp. You will be captured by the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned down.’”
Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “Do not let anyone know about this conversation, or you will die.”
“If the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say, ‘Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you. Do not hide it from us, or we will kill you,’
then you are to tell them, ‘I was begging the king not to send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.’”
Then all the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him, and he told them exactly what the king had told him to say. So they left him alone, because they had heard nothing.
And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured. And so it was when Jerusalem was captured.
In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign as king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his whole army and besieged the city.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was broken into.

Then all the officials of the king of Babylon entered and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer of Samgar, Nebo-sarsekim the chief official, Nergal-sharezer the chief magician, and all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.
When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them, they fled. They left the city at night by the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls, and headed toward the Arabah.

But the Babylonian army chased them and caught Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They took him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where the king of Babylon sentenced him.
At Riblah the king of Babylon killed Zedekiah's sons while Zedekiah watched, and he also killed all the nobles of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him with bronze chains, and took him to Babylon.
The Babylonians burned the royal palace and the houses of the people, and they tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, carried into exile the rest of the people who remained in the city, along with the deserters who had gone over to him and the rest of the people.
But Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left in the land of Judah some of the poorest people, who had nothing, and that same day he gave them vineyards and fields.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had given orders about Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard. he said,
"Take him and watch over him. Do not harm him in any way, but do for him whatever he asks you."
So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, Nebushazban the chief official, Nergal-sharezer the chief magician, and all the other officials of the king of Babylon sent for Jeremiah.
They took him out of the courtyard of the guard and handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, to take him home. So he stayed among the people.
While Jeremiah was still locked up in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the the LORD came to him. He said,

"Go and say to Ebed-Melech the Cushite, 'This is what the the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am bringing My words against this city for disaster, not for good. They will come true before you on that day.
But I will rescue you on that day, says the the LORD. You will not be handed over to the men you fear.
I will surely save you. You will not die by the sword. Instead, you will get to keep your life, because you trusted in Me, says the the LORD.'"

This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, released him at Ramah. He had taken Jeremiah in chains with all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried to Babylon.
The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, "The LORD your God said He would bring this disaster on this place.
The LORD has done what He said, because you sinned against the LORD and did not obey His voice. That is why this has happened to you.

Now look, I am releasing you today from the chains on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will take care of you. But if it does not seem good to you to come with me to Babylon, then stay. Look, the whole land is before you. Go wherever you think is good and right."

Before Jeremiah could turn to leave, the captain added, "Go to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon appointed over the cities of Judah. Live with him among the people, or go wherever you think is best." Then the captain gave him food and a gift and sent him away.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land.

All the army commanders in the field heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam to govern the land and had put him in charge of the men, women, children, and poor people who had not been taken to Babylon.

So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah; Johanan and Jonathan, the sons of Kareah; Seraiah son of Tanhumeth; the sons of Ephai from Netophah; and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, along with their men.
Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, promised them and their men, "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for you.
As for me, I will stay at Mizpah to meet the Chaldeans when they come to us. But you, gather wine, summer fruit, and oil, put them in your jars, and live in the cities you have taken."
All the Jews in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and other lands also heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, over them.
So they came back from all the places where they had been scattered. They came into the land of Judah to Gedaliah at Mizpah and gathered a very large amount of wine and summer fruit.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders in the field came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
They said to him, "Do you know that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?" But Gedaliah did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah. He said, "Let me go kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah. No one will know. Why should he kill you and scatter all the Jews who have gathered to you? Then the rest of Judah would be destroyed."
Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this. You are telling lies about Ishmael."

In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, who was from the royal family and one of the king’s top officers, came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. He brought ten men with him. While they were eating together there,
Ishmael and the ten men with him got up and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with a sword. They killed the man the king of Babylon had put in charge of the land.
Ishmael also killed all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, along with the Chaldean soldiers who were there.
The day after Gedaliah was killed, before anyone knew about it,

eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. Their beards were shaved, their clothes were torn, and they had cut themselves. They were bringing grain offerings and incense to the house of the the LORD.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, crying as he walked. When he met them, he said, “Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.”
When they came into the city, Ishmael and his men killed them and threw their bodies into a cistern.
But ten of the men said to Ishmael, “Don’t kill us! We have hidden treasures in the field—wheat, barley, oil, and honey.” So he stopped and did not kill them with the rest.

The cistern where Ishmael threw all the bodies of the men he had killed, including those killed with Gedaliah, was the one King Asa had made because he feared Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael filled it with the dead.

Then Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people in Mizpah—the king’s daughters and all the people left there. Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had placed them under Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael took them captive and started toward the Ammonites.
But when Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him heard about all the evil Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,
they took all their men and went to fight Ishmael. They caught up with him at the large pool in Gibeon.
When all the people with Ishmael saw Johanan and the commanders with him, they were glad.
So all the people Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned and went over to Johanan.
But Ishmael escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

Then Johanan and all the commanders with him took all the survivors from Mizpah whom he had rescued from Ishmael after Ishmael had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam. They included soldiers, women, children, and eunuchs whom he brought back from Gibeon.
They set out and stayed at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, planning to go to Egypt
because they were afraid of the Chaldeans. Ishmael had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
All the army commanders, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, came to Jeremiah the prophet.
They said to him, "Please hear our request and pray to the LORD your God for us—for all of us who are left. We are only a few out of many, as your eyes see us.
May the LORD your God show us the way we should go and what we should do."
Jeremiah the prophet said to them, "I have heard you. I am praying to the LORD your God just as you asked. I will tell you everything the LORD answers, and I will not hold back a single word."
They said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not do everything the LORD your God sends you to tell us.
Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that things will go well for us, because we will obey the LORD our God."
Ten days later, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
He called Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
He said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says—the God to whom you sent me to bring your plea before Him:
'If you will stay in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, for I have changed My mind about the disaster I brought on you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you fear. Do not be afraid of him, says the LORD, for I am with you to save you and rescue you from his power.
I will show you mercy, so that he will show you mercy and bring you back to your land.'"
"But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and you disobey the LORD your God,
saying, 'No, we will go to Egypt, where we will not see war, hear the trumpet, or go hungry for bread, and we will live there'—
then listen to the word of the LORD, O remnant of Judah! This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'If you are determined to go to Egypt and live there,
then the sword you fear will catch up with you there in Egypt. The famine you dread will follow close behind you, and you will die there.
Everyone who is determined to go to Egypt and live there will die by sword, famine, and plague. Not one of them will survive or escape the disaster I will bring on them.

For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Just as My anger and wrath were poured out on the people of Jerusalem, so My wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become an object of cursing, horror, contempt, and reproach, and you will never see this place again.'"
"The The LORD has spoken to you, O remnant of Judah: 'Do not go to Egypt!' Be sure that I have warned you today.
You were deceiving yourselves when you sent me to the LORD your God and said, 'Pray to the LORD our God for us, and tell us everything the LORD our God says, and we will do it.'
But I have told you today, and you have not obeyed the LORD your God or anything He sent me to tell you.
So be sure that you will die by sword, famine, and plague in the place where you want to go and live."
After Jeremiah finished telling all the people everything the LORD their God had sent him to say—all the words the LORD their God had sent him to speak to them—
Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are lying! The LORD our God has not sent you to say, 'You must not go to Egypt to live there.'
Instead, Baruch son of Neriah is turning you against us so we will be handed over to the Babylonians. They will kill us or carry us away to Babylon!"
So Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders, and all the people refused to obey the voice of the LORD and stay in the land of Judah.
Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders took the whole remnant of Judah—those who had returned from all the nations where they had been scattered—to live in the land of Judah.

They took the men, women, and children, the king's daughters, and everyone else Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan. They also took Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They went to the land of Egypt because they did not obey the voice of the LORD, and they traveled as far as Tahpanhes.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes:

"Take some large stones in your hand and hide them in the clay at the brick kiln near the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes. Do this where the men of Judah can see. Then say to them, 'This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and I will set his throne over these stones I have hidden. He will spread his royal canopy over them.
He will come and strike the land of Egypt. Those meant for death will die; those meant for captivity will be taken captive; and those meant for the sword will be killed by the sword.

He will set fire to the temples of Egypt's gods and burn them. He will take their gods captive and wrap himself in the land of Egypt like a shepherd wraps himself in his coat, and he will leave there safely.
He will break the sacred pillars of the temple of the sun in Egypt, and he will burn down the temples of Egypt's gods.'
This is the message that came to Jeremiah for all the Jews living in Egypt—in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the land of Pathros:
"This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah. They lie in ruins today, and no one lives there.
This happened because of the evil they did. They made Me angry by burning incense and serving other gods that neither they nor their ancestors knew.
I sent all My servants the prophets to them again and again. I told them not to do this terrible thing that I hate.
But they did not listen or turn their ears. They did not turn from their evil or stop burning incense to other gods.
So My anger and wrath poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. They became ruins and empty places, as they are today.

"Now this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Why are you bringing such great harm on yourselves? Why are you removing from Judah men and women, children and babies, until no one is left?
You provoke Me with what your hands make. You burn incense to other gods in Egypt, where you have gone to live. You will be cut off and become a curse and a shame among all the nations.
Have you forgotten the wickedness of your ancestors, the kings of Judah, their wives, your own wickedness, and your wives' wickedness in Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
To this day they have not humbled themselves. They have not shown fear. They have not walked in My law and My rules that I gave to you and your ancestors.
"Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am turning against you to bring harm. I will cut off all Judah.

I will take the rest of Judah who decided to go to Egypt and live there. They will all be destroyed in Egypt. They will fall by the sword and die of hunger, from the least to the greatest. They will die by sword and hunger. They will become a curse people use, a horror, and a shame.
I will punish those living in Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem: by sword, hunger, and plague.
None of the rest of Judah who went to live in Egypt will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, even though they long to return and live there. Only a few who escape will make it back."
Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, along with all the women standing there—a great crowd—and all the people living in Egypt in Pathros, answered Jeremiah:
"We will not listen to the message you spoke to us in the name of the LORD.

Instead, we will do everything we said we would do. We will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our officials did in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Back then we had plenty of food. We were well off, and we did not see disaster.
"But since we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything. We have been destroyed by sword and hunger.
When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, we did not do it behind our husbands' backs. We made cakes for her and poured out offerings to her."
Jeremiah spoke to all the people, both men and women, who had answered him:
"The incense you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you, your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—the LORD remembered it. He thought about it.
The LORD could no longer put up with it because of your evil deeds and the terrible things you did. So your land became a ruin, a horror, and a curse, with no one living there, as it is today.

"This happened because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD. You did not listen to the LORD's voice. You did not walk in His law, His rules, or His agreement. So this disaster has come on you, as it is today."
"Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who are in Egypt.

You and your wives have said with your mouths and carried out with your hands that you will surely keep your vows to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her. So keep your vows and do them.

So listen to the word of the LORD, all Judah living in Egypt. The LORD has sworn by His great name that His name will no longer be spoken by any man of Judah in all Egypt. No one will say, 'As the Lord GOD lives.'
I am watching over them to bring harm, not good. Every man of Judah in Egypt will be destroyed by sword and hunger until they are gone.
Only a few who escape the sword will return from Egypt to Judah. Then all the rest of Judah who came to Egypt to live will know whose word comes true—Mine or theirs.
This will be a sign to you that I will punish you in this place. Then you will know that My words against you will surely come true.

"This is what the LORD says: I am going to hand Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, over to his enemies and to those who seek his life, just as I handed Zedekiah, king of Judah, over to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life."
This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah. Baruch wrote these words on a scroll from Jeremiah’s mouth in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
“This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:
‘You said, “How terrible for me! For the LORD has added sorrow to my pain. I am worn out with groaning, and I find no rest.”’
“So this is what you must say to him: ‘This is what the LORD says: I am tearing down what I built, and I am pulling up what I planted. This applies to the whole earth.’
Should you then seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For I am bringing disaster on all people, declares the LORD. But wherever you go, I will let you keep your life.’”
This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet about the nations.

It was about Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt. That army was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, at Carchemish on the Euphrates River. This happened in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
"Prepare your shields and small shields; march into battle!
Harness the horses; mount the riders; take your positions with helmets; sharpen the spears; put on armor!
Why do I see them terrified and running back? Their warriors are beaten. They run away fast and do not look back. Terror is all around," says the LORD.
"The fast runner cannot escape, and the strong soldier cannot get away. In the north, by the Euphrates River, they stumble and fall.
Who is this rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge?
Egypt rises like the Nile; its waters surge like rivers. He says, 'I will rise and cover the earth. I will destroy the city and everyone in it.'
Advance, horses! Race, chariots! Let the warriors march out—Cush and Put, who carry shields, and the Lydians, who bend the bow.

For that day belongs to the Lord, the LORD of Hosts. It is a day of payback, to pay back His enemies. The sword will eat its fill and drink its fill of their blood. For the Lord, the LORD of Hosts holds a sacrifice in the north, by the Euphrates River.
Go up to Gilead and get medicine, people of Egypt! You use many cures for nothing; there is no healing for you.
The nations have heard of your shame, and your cries fill the earth. Warrior stumbles against warrior, and both fall together."
This is the word the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, coming to attack the land of Egypt.
"Announce it in Egypt, and proclaim it in Migdol. Proclaim it in Memphis and in Tahpanhes. Say, 'Take your position and get ready, because the sword is destroying everything around you.'"
"Why have your strong men been swept away? They did not stand, because the LORD pushed them down.
They stumble and fall over each other. They say, 'Get up! Let's go back to our people and our homeland, away from the sword of the enemy.'
There they will cry out, 'Pharaoh, king of Egypt, is only a loud noise. He let the right time slip away.'
'As surely as I live,' says the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, 'someone will come like Mount Tabor among the mountains and like Mount Carmel beside the sea.'"
"Pack your bags for exile, people of Egypt, because Memphis will be ruined and empty, with no one living there.
Egypt is a beautiful young cow, but a stinging fly from the north is coming against her.
Even her hired soldiers will be like well-fed calves. They too will turn and run. They will not stand their ground, because the day of disaster is coming on them—the time of their punishment.
Egypt will hiss like a snake while the enemy marches in. They will come against her with axes, like men cutting wood.
"They will cut down her forest," says the LORD, "though no one can explore it all, because they are more than locusts and cannot be counted.
The people of Egypt will be put to shame. They will be handed over to the people of the north."
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says, "I am going to punish Amon of Thebes, along with Pharaoh, Egypt, her gods, and her kings, and everyone who trusts in Pharaoh.
I will hand them over to those who want to kill them—to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and his servants. But after this, Egypt will be settled again, as it was long ago," says the LORD.

"But you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed, O Israel. For I will surely save you from far away, and your descendants from the land where they are held captive. Jacob will return and be at rest and secure, with no one to make him afraid.

And you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, says the LORD, for I am with you. Though I completely destroy all the nations where I have banished you, I will not completely destroy you. Yet I will discipline you fairly, and I will not leave you unpunished."
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet about the Philistines. It came before Pharaoh attacked Gaza.

This is what the LORD said: "Look! Water is rising from the north. It will become a flooding river. It will overflow the land and everything in it—the city and all who live there. People will cry out, and everyone who lives in the land will wail."
They will hear the sound of horses' hooves and the roar of chariots. They will hear the rumble of wheels. Fathers will not turn to help their children, because their hands will be too weak.

On the day that is coming, the LORD will destroy all the Philistines. He will cut off every survivor and helper from Tyre and Sidon. The LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant from the coast of Caphtor.
Gaza, your head will be shaved in mourning. Ashkelon will be silenced. You who remain in the valley, how long will you keep cutting yourselves?
Ah, sword of the LORD! How long will you not rest? Return to your sheath. Be still and quiet.
How can it rest when the LORD has commanded it? He has set it against Ashkelon and the seacoast.
This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says about Moab: “How terrible for Nebo, because it is destroyed! Kiriathaim is disgraced and captured. The stronghold is shattered and shaken.”
Moab is no longer praised. In Heshbon they plot evil against her and say, “Come, let us cut her off from being a nation.” You too, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will chase you.
A voice cries out from Horonaim: “Ruin and great destruction!”
Moab is shattered; her little ones cry out.
On the road up to Luhith, people go up weeping. On the road down to Horonaim, cries of distress are heard.
Run! Save yourselves! Be like a shrub in the desert.
Because you trusted in your works and treasures, you too will be captured. Chemosh will go into exile, along with his priests and officials.
The destroyer will come against every city, and no city will escape. The valley will be ruined, and the plain will be destroyed, because the LORD has spoken.
Give Moab wings, for she will fly away. Her cities will become empty, with no one living in them.
A curse on anyone who does the LORD’s work carelessly; a curse on anyone who keeps his sword from bloodshed.

Moab has been at ease since he was young. He is like wine left on its dregs; he has not been poured from one jar to another, and he has not gone into exile. So his taste stays the same, and his smell does not change.
So look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send wanderers who will pour him out. They will empty his jars and smash his containers.
Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as Israel was ashamed when they trusted in Bethel.
How can you say, “We are strong warriors, ready for battle”?
Moab is destroyed, and its cities go up in smoke. The best of its young men go down to the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
Moab’s disaster is near; his ruin is coming quickly.
Mourn for him, all who live around him, all who know his name. Say, “How the mighty rod is broken, the glorious staff!”
Come down from your glory and sit on dry ground, daughter who lives in Dibon, because the destroyer of Moab has come against you; he has destroyed your fortresses.
Stand by the road and watch, person living in Aroer. Ask the man running away and the woman escaping, “What has happened?”
Moab is put to shame, for it is shattered. Wail and cry out! Declare by the Arnon that Moab is destroyed.
Judgment has come on the plain—upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the cities of Moab, far and near.
The horn of Moab has been cut off, and his arm is broken, declares the LORD.
Make him drunk, because he has raised himself against the LORD. So Moab will wallow in his own vomit and become a laughingstock.
Wasn’t Israel a laughingstock to you? Whenever you spoke about him, you shook your head.
Leave the cities and live among the rocks, people of Moab. Be like a dove that nests in the cracks of a cliff.
We have heard of Moab’s pride—how very proud and arrogant he is, with a proud and stubborn heart.
I know his pride, declares the LORD, but it is empty. His boasting does nothing.
So I will cry out for Moab; I will cry out for all of Moab. I will mourn for the people of Kir-heres.
Vine of Sibmah, I will weep for you more than for Jazer. Your branches spread past the sea; they reached the Sea of Jazer. The destroyer has fallen on your summer fruit and on your grape harvest.

Joy and gladness are taken away from the fertile fields and from Moab. I will stop the wine from flowing out of the winepresses. No one will stomp the grapes with shouts of joy; their shouts will not be shouts of joy.
From the cry of Heshbon to Elealeh and Jahaz, they raise their voices; from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah. Even the waters of Nimrim will become dry.
I will put an end in Moab, declares the LORD, to the one who offers sacrifices on the high places and burns incense to his gods.
So My heart mourns for Moab like flutes; My heart mourns for the people of Kir-heres, because the wealth he gained is gone.
Every head is shaved, and every beard is cut off. On every hand there are cuts, and on every waist there is sackcloth.
On every rooftop in Moab and in every public square there is mourning, because I have broken Moab like a jar no one wants, declares the LORD.
How shattered she is! How they wail! How Moab has turned away in shame! Moab has become a joke and a horror to everyone around her.
For this is what the LORD says: “Look, an eagle is swooping down and spreading its wings over Moab.”
The cities are captured, and the strongholds are seized. On that day the hearts of Moab’s warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Moab will be destroyed as a nation, because he has raised himself against the LORD.
Terror, pit, and trap wait for you, person living in Moab, declares the LORD.
Whoever runs from the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. For I will bring on Moab the year of their punishment, declares the LORD.
Those who run away will stand tired in the shadow of Heshbon, because a fire has gone out from Heshbon and a flame from Sihon. It has burned the foreheads of Moab and the crowns of the noisy people.
How terrible for you, Moab! The people of Chemosh have died, because your sons have been taken captive and your daughters have been led away.
Yet in the last days I will restore Moab’s fortunes, declares the LORD. This is the end of the judgment on Moab.
Concerning the Ammonites, this is what the LORD says: "Does Israel have no sons? Does he have no heir? Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gad, and his people settled in its cities?"

"Therefore, behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites; and it shall become a heap of ruins, and her villages will be burned with fire. Then Israel will drive out those who drove him out," says the LORD.

"Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is destroyed! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn; run back and forth along the walls. For Milcom will go into exile, together with his priests and officials.
Why do you boast in your valleys, your flowing valleys, O faithless daughter? You trust in your treasures and say, 'Who will come against me?'"
"Behold, I will bring terror upon you, declares the Lord GOD of Hosts, from all around you. You will be driven away, each man in a different direction, and no one will gather the fugitives.
But afterward I will restore the Ammonites from captivity, declares the LORD."
Concerning Edom, this is what the LORD of Hosts says: "Is there no more wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom vanished?"
"Turn and flee! Dwell deep, O inhabitants of Dedan! For I will bring disaster on Esau when I punish him."
"If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, would they not steal only as much as they needed?
But I will strip Esau bare; I will uncover his hiding places, and he will be unable to hide. His offspring will be destroyed, along with his brothers and neighbors, and he will be no more.
Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in Me."
"For this is what the LORD says: 'If those who do not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, should you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, but you must surely drink it.'
For I have sworn by Myself, declares the LORD, that Bozrah will become a desolation, a reproach, a waste, and a curse, and all her cities will be perpetual ruins."
"I have heard a message from the LORD; an envoy has been sent among the nations: 'Gather together and come against her; rise up for battle!'"
"Behold, I will make you small among the nations, despised among men.

Your terror has deceived you, and the pride of your heart, O you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill. Though you make your nest as high as the eagle, from there I will bring you down, declares the LORD."
"Edom will become an object of horror. All who pass by will be appalled and will hiss at all her wounds.
As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring cities, says the LORD, no one will live there, and no son of man will dwell in it.

Behold, one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture. For in an instant I will chase him from it, and I will appoint over it whomever I choose. For who is like Me, and who can challenge Me? What shepherd can stand before Me?"

"Therefore hear the counsel of the LORD that He has planned against Edom, and the thoughts He has intended against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely their pasture will be made desolate because of them.
At the sound of their fall the earth will tremble; the cry will be heard at the Red Sea.
Behold, one will soar like an eagle and swoop down, spreading his wings over Bozrah. In that day the hearts of Edom's mighty men will be like the heart of a woman in labor."
"Concerning Damascus: 'Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard bad news; they are disheartened. Troubled like the sea, they cannot be quiet.'
Damascus has become feeble; she has turned to flee, and panic has seized her. Anguish and pain have gripped her, like a woman in labor.
How is the city of praise not forsaken, the town of My joy?"
"Therefore her young men will fall in her streets, and all her men of war will be silenced in that day, declares the LORD of Hosts.
I will set fire to the walls of Damascus, and it will consume the palaces of Ben-hadad."
"Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated, this is what the LORD says: 'Arise, go up against Kedar, and destroy the people of the east!'
They will take their tents and their flocks, their tent curtains and all their goods, and carry off their camels for themselves. They will proclaim terror on every side.
Flee! Run far away! Dwell deep, O inhabitants of Hazor, declares the LORD; for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devised a plan against you and formed a purpose against you."
"Arise, go up against a nation at ease, one that dwells securely, declares the LORD; a nation with no gates or bars, that dwells alone.
Their camels will become plunder, and their many livestock a spoil. I will scatter to the wind those with shaved temples, and I will bring disaster on them from every side, declares the LORD.
Hazor will become a haunt of jackals, a desolation forever. No one will live there; no son of man will dwell in it."
This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.'
I will bring the four winds against Elam from the four corners of heaven, and I will scatter them to all these winds. There will be no nation to which Elam's exiles will not go.

I will shatter Elam before their enemies, before those who seek their lives. I will bring disaster upon them, My fierce anger, declares the LORD. I will send the sword after them until I have finished them off.
I will set My throne in Elam and destroy its king and officials, declares the LORD.
Yet in the last days I will restore Elam from captivity, declares the LORD."
This is the word the LORD spoke through Jeremiah the prophet about Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans.

"Announce and declare it to the nations. Lift up a banner and proclaim it. Do not hide it. Say, 'Babylon is captured. Bel is disgraced. Marduk is broken. Her false gods are disgraced. Her statues are broken.'"
A nation from the north will attack her. It will turn her land into a wasteland, and no one will live there. People and animals will run away.
"In those days and at that time," says the LORD, "the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come together. They will walk along weeping, and they will look for the LORD their God."
They will ask the way to Zion and turn their faces toward it. They will come and join the LORD in a lasting agreement that will never be forgotten.
"My people have been like lost sheep. Their shepherds led them the wrong way, turning them away on the mountains. They wandered from mountain to hill. They forgot where to rest."
All who found them ate them up. Their enemies said, "We are not guilty, because they sinned against the LORD, their true home, the LORD, the hope of their fathers."
Flee from Babylon! Leave the land of the Chaldeans, and be like the male goats that lead the flock.

Look, I will stir up and bring against Babylon a large group of nations from the north. They will line up against her, and from there she will be captured. Their arrows will be like a skilled soldier's; none will come back empty.
"Chaldea will be plundered. All who plunder her will be satisfied," says the LORD.
"Because you rejoice and celebrate, O plunderers of My people, because you jump around like a young cow treading grain and neigh like horses,
your mother will be very ashamed. The woman who gave birth to you will be disgraced. Look, she will become the least of the nations, a wasteland, a dry land, and a desert."
Because of the LORD's anger, Babylon will not be lived in. It will be completely ruined. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be shocked and whistle at all her wounds.
Line up against Babylon on every side, all you who bend the bow. Shoot at her. Do not spare any arrows, because she has sinned against the LORD.
Shout against her on every side! She has given up. Her towers have fallen. Her walls are torn down. This is the LORD's revenge. Take revenge on her. Do to her what she did to others.
Cut off the farmer from Babylon, and the one who uses the sickle at harvest time. Because of the sword of the enemy, each person will turn to his own people, and each will run to his own land.
Israel is a scattered flock. Lions drove him away. The first to eat him up was the king of Assyria. The last to crush his bones was Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
So this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, just as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back to his pasture. He will feed on Carmel and Bashan. He will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead."

"In those days and at that time," says the LORD, "Israel's guilt will be searched for, but it will not be found. Judah's sins will not be found either, because I will forgive the people I leave behind."
"Go up against the land of Merathaim and against the people of Pekod. Put them to the sword and destroy them completely," says the LORD. "Do everything I have commanded you."
The sound of battle is in the land. It is a great destruction.
How the hammer of the whole earth has been cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
I set a trap for you, Babylon, and you were caught, but you did not know it. You were found and captured, because you fought against the LORD.
The LORD has opened His storehouse and brought out His weapons of anger. This is the work of the Lord, the LORD of Armies, in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from the farthest border. Open her storehouses. Pile her up like heaps of grain. Destroy her completely. Leave her no survivors.
Kill all her young bulls with the sword. Let them go down to the slaughter. How terrible for them! Their day has come, the time of their punishment.
Listen to the people running away from Babylon. In Zion they tell about the LORD our God's revenge, the revenge for His temple.

Summon the archers against Babylon, all who bend the bow. Camp around her. Let no one escape. Pay her back for what she did. Do to her as she did to others, because she defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
So her young men will fall in her streets. All her soldiers will be silenced in that day, says the LORD.
"Look, I am against you, you proud one," says the Lord, the LORD of Armies, "because your day has come, the time of your punishment.
The proud one will trip and fall, with no one to help her up. I will set fire to her cities, and it will burn all around her."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "The people of Israel are treated badly, and the people of Judah too. All who captured them hold them tight and refuse to let them go."
Their Redeemer is strong. The LORD of Armies is His name. He will surely argue their case. He will bring rest to the land, but trouble to the people of Babylon.
A sword is against the Chaldeans, says the LORD, and against the people of Babylon, and against her leaders and wise men.
A sword is against her fortune-tellers, and they will act like fools. A sword is against her soldiers, and they will be terrified.
A sword is against her horses and chariots and against all the foreigners among her. They will become like women. A sword is against her treasures, and they will be stolen.
A drought is on her waters, and they will dry up. She is a land of idols. Her people go crazy over idols.
So desert animals and hyenas will live there, and ostriches will live in it. It will never be lived in again, from one generation to the next.
As God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them, says the LORD, "no man will live there. No son of man will stay in it."
Look, a people is coming from the north. A great nation and many kings are stirred up from the ends of the earth.
They carry bow and spear. They are cruel and show no mercy. Their voice roars like the sea. They ride on horses. They are lined up like a man ready for battle against you, Daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the report about them, and his hands become weak. Fear grips him. Pain grips him like a woman in labor.

Look, he will come up like a lion from the thick brush of the Jordan to a rich pasture. In an instant I will chase them away from her, and I will choose whoever I want to rule over her. Who is like Me? Who can challenge Me? What shepherd can stand against Me?

So listen to the plan the LORD has made against Babylon and the thoughts He has had against the land of the Chaldeans. Surely the young sheep will be dragged away. Surely their pasture will be shocked at them.
At the sound of Babylon's fall, the earth will shake, and a cry will be heard among the nations.
This is what the LORD says: "Look, I am going to stir up a destroying wind against Babylon and against the people of Leb Kamai.
I will send strangers to Babylon to scatter her and empty her land. They will come against her from every side on the day of trouble.
Do not let the archer bend his bow or put on his armor. Do not spare her young men. Destroy all her army.
They will fall dead in the land of the Chaldeans, wounded in her streets."
Israel and Judah have not been abandoned by their God, the LORD of Armies, even though their land was full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.
Flee from Babylon! Run for your life! Do not be destroyed because of her sin. It is time for the LORD to punish her; He will pay her back.
Babylon was a gold cup in the LORD's hand. It made all the earth drunk. The nations drank her wine, so they went mad.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been broken. Wail for her! Get balm for her pain; maybe she can be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Leave her and let each of us go home, because her judgment reaches up to the heavens and rises to the skies.
The LORD has shown that we are right. Come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has done.
Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers! The LORD has stirred up the spirit of the kings of Media, because His plan is to destroy Babylon. This is the LORD's revenge, revenge for His temple.
Raise a banner against the walls of Babylon! Strengthen the guard! Post watchmen! Set up ambushes! For the LORD has planned it and will do what He said against the people of Babylon.
You who live by many waters and have great treasure, your end has come. The thread of your life is cut.
The LORD of Armies has sworn by Himself: "Surely I will fill you with men, as many as locusts, and they will shout a battle cry against you."
He made the earth by His power. He set the world in place by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding.
When He thunders, the waters in the heavens roar. He makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He sends lightning with the rain and brings wind out of His storehouses.
Every man is foolish and without knowledge. Every metalworker is put to shame by his idol, because his cast image is a lie and has no breath in it.
They are worthless, a work of deception. When the time comes to punish them, they will be destroyed.
The Portion of Jacob is not like them, for He is the Maker of all things. Israel is the tribe of His inheritance. The LORD of Armies is His name.
You are My hammer and My weapon of war. With you I shatter nations and destroy kingdoms.
With you I shatter horse and rider. With you I shatter chariot and driver.
With you I shatter man and woman, old and young, young man and young woman.
With you I shatter shepherd and flock, farmer and team, rulers and officials.
But I will repay Babylon and all the people of Chaldea for all the evil they did in Zion, right before your eyes, declares the LORD.
I am against you, O destroying mountain, declares the LORD. You destroy the whole earth. I will stretch out My hand against you, roll you down from the rocks, and make you a burned-out mountain.
No one will take a cornerstone from you or a stone for a foundation. You will be empty forever, declares the LORD.

Raise a banner in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Prepare the nations against her! Call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz against her! Appoint a commander against her! Bring up horses like a swarm of locusts!
Prepare the nations against her—the kings of Media, their governors and officials, and all the land they rule.
The land shakes and writhes, because the LORD's plans against Babylon stand. He will make Babylon a wasteland where no one lives.
Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting. They stay in their forts. Their strength is gone. They have become like women. Her houses are set on fire, and her bars are broken.
One runner tells another runner, and one messenger tells another messenger, to report to the king of Babylon that his city has been taken from end to end.
The river crossings are seized, the marshes are burned, and the soldiers are terrified.
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled. In a little while, her harvest time will come."
"Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured us and crushed us. He has made us an empty jar. He swallowed us like a sea monster and filled his belly with our delicacies. He has driven us away."
"Let the violence done to me and my family be blamed on Babylon," says the one who lives in Zion. "Let my blood be on the people of Chaldea," says Jerusalem.
So this is what the LORD says: "I will take up your case and avenge you. I will dry up her sea and make her spring run dry."
Babylon will become a heap of ruins, a home for jackals, a horror and a hissing, with no one living there.
They will roar together like young lions and growl like lion cubs.
While they are heated, I will prepare their drink and make them drunk, so they may celebrate and then sleep forever and never wake up, declares the LORD.
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams and goats.
How Sheshach has been captured! The praise of the whole earth has been seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
The sea has come up over Babylon. She is covered with its roaring waves.
Her cities have become a wasteland, a dry and empty land. No one travels through them; no person lives there.
I will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spit out what he swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him. Even Babylon's wall has fallen.
Come out of her, My people! Run for your life from the LORD's fierce anger!

Do not let your hearts grow weak or be afraid of the rumors you hear in the land. One rumor comes this year, and another comes the next. There is violence in the land, and rulers fight against rulers.
So the time is coming when I will punish Babylon's idols. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her wounded will fall inside her.
Then heaven and earth and everything in them will sing for joy over Babylon, because destroyers from the north will come against her, declares the LORD.
Babylon must fall because of Israel's dead, just as the dead of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon.
You who have escaped the sword, go away! Do not stand still! Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come into your mind.
We are ashamed because we have heard insults. Shame covers our faces, because foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD's house.
So the time is coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish her idols, and the wounded will groan throughout her land.
Even if Babylon climbs to the sky and fortifies her highest stronghold, destroyers from Me will come against her, declares the LORD.
A cry of distress comes from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
For the LORD is destroying Babylon and silencing her loud noise. When her waves roar like great waters, their voice thunders.
For the destroyer has come against her, against Babylon. Her mighty men are captured, and their bows are broken, because the LORD is a God who repays; He will surely repay.
I will make her leaders and wise men drunk, along with her governors, officials, and warriors. They will sleep forever and never wake up, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.

This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Babylon's thick walls will be completely torn down, and her high gates will be burned. The peoples will work for nothing, and the nations will grow tired in the flames."

This is the message Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when Seraiah went to Babylon with King Zedekiah of Judah in the fourth year of Zedekiah's reign. Seraiah was the officer in charge of supplies.
Jeremiah wrote on a scroll all the disaster that would come on Babylon—all these words written against Babylon.

Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you get to Babylon, read all these words aloud, and say, 'the LORD, You have said You will destroy this place so that no one will live in it—not people or animals. It will be empty forever.' "When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates River. "Then say, 'In the same way Babylon will sink and never rise again, because of the disaster I am bringing on her. Her people will grow tired.' The words of Jeremiah end here."
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah; she was from Libnah.
He did evil in the sight of the the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
Because of the the LORD’s anger, this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, until He cast them out from His presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his whole army. They camped outside the city and built siege works all around it.
The city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city had become so severe that there was no food for the people of the land.

Then the city wall was broken through, and all the soldiers fled and left the city at night through the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden. They fled toward the Arabah, though the Chaldeans had surrounded the city.
But the Chaldean army pursued the king and caught up with Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. All his army scattered from him.
They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he passed sentence on him.
There at Riblah, the king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he also slaughtered all the officials of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon, where he put him in prison until the day of his death.
On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard, who served in the presence of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.
He burned down the house of the the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem; every important building he burned with fire.
The whole Chaldean army under the commander of the guard broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.

Then Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard carried into exile some of the poorest people, along with the rest of the people who remained in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the skilled workers.
But Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard left behind some of the poorest of the land to work the vineyards and fields.
The Chaldeans also broke up the bronze pillars, the stands, and the bronze Sea in the house of the the LORD, and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.
They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and all the other bronze items used in the temple service.
The commander of the guard took away the basins, incense burners, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, pans, and bowls—whatever was made of pure gold or silver.
The two pillars, the Sea, and the twelve bronze bulls under the Sea, and the stands that King Solomon had made for the house of the the LORD—all this bronze was too heavy to weigh.
Each pillar was eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits around; it was hollow and four fingers thick.
The bronze top on one pillar was five cubits high, with a network of bronze pomegranates all around. The second pillar was like the first, with pomegranates.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; in all, one hundred pomegranates were above the network all around.
The commander of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of the second rank, and the three doorkeepers.

From the city he also took the officer who had been in charge of the soldiers, seven trusted royal advisers, the secretary of the commander of the army who gathered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
There at Riblah in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was carried into exile away from its land.
These are the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, 832 people from Jerusalem;
in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard carried into exile 745 Jews. In all, 4,600 people were taken captive.

On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the first year of his reign, Evil-merodach king of Babylon released Jehoiachin king of Judah and freed him from prison.
He spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes, and he ate bread regularly in the king’s presence for the rest of his life.
And from the king, a daily portion was given to him for the rest of his life, until the day of his death.
How lonely the city sits now! It once had many people. It was great among the nations, but now it is like a widow. It was a princess among the regions, but now it pays heavy taxes like a slave.
She cries hard at night, and tears run down her cheeks. No one comforts her, not even those who once loved her. All her friends betrayed her and became her enemies.
Judah was carried away because of suffering and hard work. Now she lives among other nations and finds no rest. Her enemies caught her in narrow places.
The roads to Zion are sad because no one comes for the festivals. The city gates are empty. The priests groan. The young women suffer, and Zion itself is bitter.
Her enemies are now in charge. They succeed because the LORD punished her for her many sins. Her children were taken away as prisoners.
All the beauty has left Zion. Her leaders are like deer with no grass to eat. They had no strength and ran from the hunter.
In her suffering and wandering, Jerusalem remembers all the good things she had long ago. When her people fell to the enemy, no one helped her. Her enemies saw her and laughed at her ruin.
Jerusalem sinned badly, so she became unclean. Everyone who honored her now hates her, because they saw her shame. She groans and turns away.
Her filth was on her clothes. She did not think about what would happen next. Her fall was terrible, and no one comforts her. "Look, the LORD, at my suffering, because the enemy has won!"
The enemy took all her treasures. She saw nations enter her holy place, even though You had said they could not join Your people.
All her people groan while looking for bread. They give up their treasures for food to stay alive. "Look, the LORD, and see, for I am treated with contempt."
Does my pain mean nothing to you who pass by? Look and see if anyone has pain like mine. The LORD brought this on me in His fierce anger.
From above He sent fire into my bones and overpowered me. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He left me empty and weak all day.
My sins were tied into a heavy yoke. By His hand they were fastened together and put on my neck. He made my strength fail. The Lord handed me over to people I cannot resist.
The Lord threw away all my strong men. He gathered an army to crush my young men. The Lord trampled the young women of Judah like grapes in a winepress.
Because of this I cry. My eyes pour out tears. No one comforts me or gives me strength. My children are ruined because the enemy won.
Zion reaches out her hands, but no one comforts her. The LORD ordered that Jacob's neighbors become his enemies. Jerusalem is treated like something dirty among them.
The LORD is right, because I rebelled against Him. Listen, all you nations, and see my pain. My young men and young women were taken captive.
I called to my allies, but they tricked me. My priests and leaders died in the city while searching for food to stay alive.
Look, the LORD, I am in trouble. My stomach turns, and my heart aches inside me, because I rebelled badly. Outside, the sword kills; inside, it feels like death.
They heard my groaning, yet no one comforts me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that You have done it. You brought the day You announced; now let them be like me.
Let all their evil come before You. Treat them as You treated me because of all my sins. My groans are many, and my heart is weak.

How the Lord has covered the Daughter of Zion with a cloud in His anger! He has thrown down from heaven to earth the splendor of Israel. He did not remember His temple, where He rested His feet, in the day of His anger.

The Lord has shown no mercy. He has swallowed up all of Jacob's homes. In His wrath He has torn down Judah's strongholds and brought them crashing to the ground. He has dishonored the kingdom and its leaders.
In His fierce anger He has cut off all of Israel's strength. He has pulled back His right hand from the enemy. He has burned against Jacob like a fire that consumes everything around it.
He has bent His bow like an enemy; His right hand is ready like a foe. He has killed all our loved ones. In the tent of the Daughter of Zion He has poured out His wrath like fire.
The Lord has become like an enemy. He has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces and destroyed her strongholds. He has increased sorrow and mourning in the Daughter of Judah.
He has torn down His shelter like a garden and ruined His meeting place. the LORD has made Zion forget her sacred festivals and Sabbaths. In His fierce anger He has rejected king and priest.
The Lord has rejected His altar and abandoned His sanctuary. He has handed over to the enemy the walls of her palaces. They shouted in the house of the LORD as on a festival day.

The LORD planned to destroy the wall of the Daughter of Zion. He stretched out a measuring line and did not hold back His hand from destroying. He made the city's defenses and its wall mourn, and together they wasted away.
Her gates have sunk into the ground; He has destroyed and broken her bars. Her king and princes are among the nations. There is no law, and her prophets find no vision from the LORD.
The elders of the Daughter of Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.
My eyes are worn out from tears; my stomach churns; my heart is poured out on the ground because of the destruction of my people. Children and infants faint in the streets of the city.
They say to their mothers, "Where is bread and wine?" as they faint in the streets like dying men, and their lives are poured out on their mothers' laps.

What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, Daughter of Jerusalem? To what can I liken you, that I may comfort you, Virgin Daughter of Zion? For your wound is as great as the sea. Who can heal you?
Your prophets have seen false and empty visions for you. They did not expose your sin to bring you back from captivity. Instead, they spoke lies that led you astray.
All who pass by clap their hands in scorn at you. They hiss and shake their heads at the Daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?"
All your enemies open their mouths against you. They hiss and grind their teeth and say, "We have destroyed her! This is the day we longed for. We have finally seen it!"
The LORD has done what He planned. He has carried out His word, which He commanded long ago. He has thrown down without mercy. He has made the enemy rejoice over you and made your enemies strong.
Their hearts cried out to the Lord, "O wall of Zion! Let your tears flow like a river day and night. Give yourself no rest, and do not let your eyes stop crying."

Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the night watches. Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands to Him for the life of your little ones, who faint from hunger on every corner.
Look, O the LORD, and consider: to whom have You done this? Should women eat their own children, the babies they have nurtured? Should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
Young and old lie on the ground in the streets; my young women and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have slain them in the day of Your anger; You have slaughtered them without mercy.
