You have brought terror from every side, as on a festival day. On the day of the LORD's anger no one escaped or survived; those I raised and brought up, my enemy has destroyed.
I am the man who has suffered under the the LORD's angry punishment.
He led me and brought me into darkness instead of light.
He turns His hand against me again and again, all day long.
He has worn out my body and skin and broken my bones.
He has trapped me with bitterness and hardship.
He has made me live in dark places, like people who died long ago.
He has walled me in so I cannot get out; He has made my chains heavy.
Even when I cry out and ask for help, He shuts out my prayer.
He has blocked my path with cut stones and made my roads crooked.
He is like a bear waiting to attack me, like a lion hiding in the bushes.
He has led me off my path and torn me apart; He has left me alone and ruined.
He bent His bow and set me up as a target for His arrows.
He shot His arrows deep into me.
I have become a joke to all my people; they sing about me all day long.
He has filled me with bitterness and made me drink a bitter drink.
He has broken my teeth with gravel and covered me with ashes.
I have lost all peace; I have forgotten what good times feel like.
I said, "My strength is gone, and my hope in the the LORD is gone."
Remember my suffering and my wandering, the bitterness and the poison.
My soul keeps thinking about it and sinks inside me.
But I bring this to mind, and because of that I still have hope.
The LORD's faithful love never ends; His compassion never stops.
They are new every morning. Great is Your faithfulness.
"The the LORD is all I need," says my soul, "that is why I will hope in Him."
The LORD is good to those who wait for Him and seek Him.
It is good to wait quietly for the the LORD to save us.
It is good for a man to carry a heavy load while he is young.
Let him sit alone and be quiet, because the the LORD has put this on him.
Let him put his mouth in the dust—maybe there is still hope.
Let him turn his cheek to the one who hits him and be filled with shame.
The Lord will not reject us forever.
Even when He brings grief, He will show compassion because His faithful love is so great.
He does not enjoy hurting people or making them suffer.
The Lord does not approve of crushing prisoners underfoot,
denying a man justice before the Most High,
or cheating a man in court.
Who can speak and make something happen unless the Lord commands it?
Good and bad both come from the mouth of the Most High.
So why should a living person complain when he is punished for his sins?
Let us look closely at our ways and turn back to the the LORD.
Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God in heaven.
We have sinned and rebelled, and You have not forgiven us.
You have wrapped Yourself in anger and pursued us; You have killed without pity.
You have covered Yourself with a cloud so our prayers cannot get through.
You have made us like garbage and trash among the nations.
All our enemies open their mouths against us.
We have faced panic and traps, ruin and destruction.
My eyes pour out rivers of tears because of the ruin of my people.
My eyes will not stop crying; they will not rest
until the the LORD looks down and sees from heaven.
What I see breaks my heart for all the young women of my city.
My enemies hunted me like a bird for no reason.
They shut me up in a pit and threw stones at me.
Water closed over my head, and I said, "I am lost."
I called on Your name, the the LORD, from the bottom of the pit.
You heard my voice; do not hide Your ear from my cry for help.
You came close when I called on You and said, "Do not be afraid!"
You have stood up for me, O Lord; You have saved my life.
You have seen, O the the LORD, the wrong done to me; judge my case.
You have seen all their revenge and all their plans against me.
You have heard, O the the LORD, their insults and all their plans against me.
My enemies whisper and think about me all day long.
Watch them when they sit and when they stand; I am the one they mock.
Pay them back, O the the LORD, for what their hands have done.
Give them a sorrowful heart; may Your curse fall on them.
Chase them down in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the the LORD.
How the gold has lost its shine, and the fine gold has changed! The sacred stones are scattered at every street corner.
How the precious people of Zion, once as valuable as gold, are now treated like cheap clay jars made by a potter.
Even jackals feed their young, but my people have become cruel, like ostriches in the desert.
The tongue of the nursing baby sticks to the roof of its mouth from thirst. Little children beg for bread, but no one gives them any.
Those who once ate fine food now starve in the streets. Those raised in luxury now cling to garbage heaps.
The punishment of my people is greater than Sodom's, which was destroyed in a moment with no one to help.
Her leaders were purer than snow and whiter than milk. Their bodies were redder than rubies, and their form was like sapphires.
Now their faces are blacker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shrunk over their bones and become dry as wood.
Those killed by the sword are better off than those who die of hunger, who slowly waste away, starved for food from the fields.
Even loving mothers have boiled their own children; they became food for them when my people were destroyed.
The LORD has finished His wrath; He has poured out His fierce anger. He set fire to Zion, and it burned to its foundations.
The kings of the earth did not believe, and no one in the world believed, that an enemy or foe could enter Jerusalem's gates.
This happened because of the sins of her prophets and the wrongs of her priests, who shed the blood of innocent people in the city.
They wandered blind in the streets, stained with blood, so that no one could touch their clothes.
People shouted, "Go away! You are unclean! Go away! Go away! Don't touch us!" So they fled and wandered. Among the nations people said, "They can't stay here."
The LORD Himself scattered them; He no longer shows them favor. People did not respect the priests or show kindness to the elders.
Our eyes wore out watching for help that never came. From our towers we watched for a nation that could not save us.
They hunted our steps, so we could not walk in our streets. Our end was near; our days were numbered, for our end had come.
Our pursuers were faster than eagles in the sky. They chased us over the mountains and waited to ambush us in the desert.
The LORD's anointed, our very life, was caught in their traps. We had said, "Under his shadow we will live among the nations."
Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom, you who live in the land of Uz. But the cup will pass to you too; you will get drunk and strip yourself naked.
Your punishment is complete, daughter of Zion; He will not send you into exile again. But He will punish your sin, daughter of Edom; He will uncover your wickedness.
Remember, the LORD, what has happened to us. Look and see our shame.
Our land has been given to strangers, and our homes to foreigners.
We have become orphans with no father. Our mothers are like widows.
We have to pay for the water we drink, and we must buy wood.
Our enemies chase us and stay close behind us. We are tired and get no rest.
We turned to Egypt and Assyria to get enough food.
Our fathers sinned, and they are gone, but we suffer for their wrongs.
Slaves rule over us, and no one can save us from them.
We risk our lives to get bread because of danger in the desert.
Our skin is hot like an oven because of the burning hunger.
Women have been abused in Zion, and young women in the towns of Judah.
Leaders were hung by their hands, and elders were not respected.
Young men grind grain, and boys stumble under loads of wood.
The elders no longer sit at the city gate, and the young men have stopped their music.
Joy has left our hearts. Our dancing has turned to mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. How terrible for us, because we have sinned!
Because of this, our hearts are weak. Because of these things, our eyes grow dim.
Mount Zion is empty and ruined, and jackals walk over it.
You, the LORD, reign forever. Your throne lasts from generation to generation.
Why do You forget us forever? Why do You leave us for so long?
Bring us back to You, the LORD, so we may return. Make our days new again, like they were before.
Unless You have completely rejected us and are very angry with us.
In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, I was among the captives by the Kebar River. The heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth day of the month, in the fifth year of King Jehoiachin’s exile,
the word of the the LORD came to Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the Kebar River. There the hand of the the LORD was on him.

I looked, and I saw a windstorm coming from the north. It was a great cloud with fire flashing, and bright light shone all around it. In the middle of the fire, there was something like glowing metal.
In the middle of it were four living creatures that looked like humans.
Each had four faces and four wings.
Their legs were straight, and their feet were like a calf’s hoof. They sparkled like polished bronze.
Under their wings on their four sides were human hands. All four had faces and wings.
Their wings touched one another. They did not turn when they moved; each one went straight ahead.
Their faces looked like this: each had a human face; on the right was a lion’s face; on the left was an ox’s face; and each also had an eagle’s face.
Their wings were spread upward. Two wings of each creature touched the wings of the others, and two covered their bodies.
Each one went straight ahead. Wherever the Spirit wanted to go, they went, and they did not turn as they moved.
The living creatures looked like burning coals of fire, like torches. Fire moved back and forth among the creatures, and lightning flashed out of the fire.
The creatures darted back and forth like flashes of lightning.
As I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each creature with its four faces.
The wheels looked like sparkling beryl. All four looked alike, and each wheel seemed to be inside another wheel.
When they moved, they went on their four sides, and they did not turn.
Their rims were high and frightening, and they were full of eyes all around.
When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them. When the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose too.
Wherever the Spirit went, the creatures and wheels went, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

When the creatures moved, the wheels moved; when they stood still, the wheels stood still; and when they rose from the ground, the wheels rose with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
Over the heads of the living creatures was something like a great expanse. It looked like awesome crystal, stretched out above their heads.
Under the expanse, their wings were straight out toward one another. Each creature had two wings covering its body.

When they moved, I heard the sound of their wings. It sounded like the roar of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, and like the noise of an army. When they stood still, they lowered their wings.
A voice came from above the expanse over their heads. When they stood still, they lowered their wings.
Above the expanse over their heads was something like a throne. It looked like sapphire, and on the throne was a figure that looked like a man.
From the waist up, He looked like glowing metal with fire all around. From the waist down, He looked like fire, and bright light shone around Him.
The bright light around Him looked like a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day. This was the appearance of the glory of the the LORD. When I saw it, I fell facedown, and I heard a voice speaking.
He said to me, "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."
As He spoke to me, the Spirit came into me and set me on my feet, and I heard Him speaking to me.
He said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me. They and their fathers have sinned against Me to this very day.
The people I am sending you to are stubborn and hard-hearted children. Say to them, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says.'
Whether they listen or refuse to listen—for they are a rebellious people—they will know that a prophet has been among them. "

And you, Son of man, do not be afraid of them or their words. Do not be afraid, though hostile people surround you like briers and thorns, and you live among dangerous enemies like scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their looks, for they are a rebellious people.
Speak My words to them, whether they listen or refuse to listen, for they are rebellious.
And you, Son of man, listen to what I tell you. Do not rebel like those rebellious people. Open your mouth and eat what I give you."
Then I looked and saw a hand stretched out toward me. In it was a scroll.
He unrolled it before me, and it was written on both sides. On it were written words of mourning, grief, and woe.
He said to me, “Son of man, eat what you find; eat this scroll, then go and speak to the people of Israel.”
So I opened my mouth, and He fed me the scroll.
He also said to me, “Son of man, eat this scroll I am giving you and fill your stomach with it.” So I ate it, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.
He said to me, “Son of man, go now to the people of Israel and speak My words to them.
You are not being sent to people who speak a strange, hard language, but to the people of Israel—
not to many nations whose words you cannot understand. If I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
But the people of Israel will not listen to you, because they will not listen to Me. All of them are stubborn and hard-hearted.
Look, I have made your face as hard as theirs, and your forehead as hard as theirs.
I have made your forehead like a diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them or discouraged by them, because they are a rebellious people.”
He also said to me, “Son of man, take all My words into your heart and listen carefully.
Go to your people in exile and speak to them. Tell them, ‘This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: Whether they listen or refuse to listen.’”
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard a loud rumbling behind me: “Blessed be the glory of the LORD in His place!”
It was the sound of the living creatures’ wings brushing together and the wheels beside them—a loud rumbling sound.
So the Spirit lifted me up and carried me away. I went in bitterness and anger of spirit, with the strong hand of the LORD on me.
I came to the exiles at Tel Abib by the River Chebar. There I sat among them for seven days, overwhelmed.
At the end of seven days the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the people of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, warn them for Me. “

If I tell a wicked person, ‘You will surely die,’ and you do not warn him to turn from his wicked way and save his life, that wicked person will die in his sin, and I will hold you responsible for his blood.
But if you warn him and he does not turn from his wicked ways, he will die in his sin, but you will have saved yourself. “

If a good person turns from doing right and does wrong, and I cause him to fall, he will die. Because you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and his good deeds will not be remembered. I will hold you responsible for his blood.
But if you warn a good person not to sin, and he does not sin, he will live because he listened to the warning, and you will have saved yourself.”
Then the hand of the LORD was upon me there, and He said to me, “Get up and go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you.”
So I got up and went to the plain. There I saw the glory of the LORD standing, like the glory I had seen by the River Chebar, and I fell facedown.
Then the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said to me, “Go, shut yourself inside your house. “
Now, son of man, people will tie you up with ropes and bind you so you cannot go out among them.
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth. You will be silent and unable to correct them, because they are a rebellious people. “

But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, ‘This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: Let the one who will listen, listen; and let the one who refuses, refuse. For they are a rebellious people.’”
Now you, son of man, take a brick and place it in front of you. Draw a city on it—Jerusalem.
Then lay siege against it: build a siege wall, heap up a ramp, set up camps, and place battering rams around it.
Then take an iron pan and set it as an iron wall between you and the city. Turn your face toward it. It will be under siege, and you will besiege it. This will be a sign to the people of Israel.
Then lie on your left side and put the sin of the people of Israel on it. You will bear their sin for the number of days you lie on it.
I have given you 390 days, which matches the years of their sin. So you will bear the sin of the people of Israel.
When you finish these days, lie again on your right side and bear the sin of the people of Judah. I have given you 40 days, one day for each year.
You must turn your face toward the siege of Jerusalem with your arm uncovered, and prophesy against it.
Look, I will tie you with ropes so you cannot turn from side to side until you finish the days of your siege.
Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Put them in one container and make bread for yourself. Eat it for the 390 days you lie on your side.
Weigh out twenty shekels of food each day and eat it at set times.
Measure out a sixth of a hin of water and drink it at set times.
You will eat it as a barley cake, baked over human waste in front of them.
Then the the LORD said, “This is how the Israelites will eat unclean bread among the nations where I scatter them.”

I said, “Ah, Lord GOD! I have never made myself unclean. From my youth until now I have never eaten meat from an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts, and no unclean meat has entered my mouth.”
He said, “Look, I will let you use cow dung instead of human dung. You may bake your bread over that.
Son of man, I am going to cut off the bread supply in Jerusalem. They will anxiously eat bread rationed by weight, and in despair drink water rationed by measure.
So they will lack food and water and be horrified at one another, and waste away because of their sin.”
"And you, son of man, take a sharp sword. Use it as a barber's razor to shave your head and your beard. Then take scales and weigh the hair, and divide it.

When the siege is over, burn a third of the hair in a fire inside the city. Take another third and strike it with the sword all around the city. Scatter the last third to the wind, and I will chase it with a sword."
"Take a few of those hairs and tie them in the folds of your clothes.
Take some of them and throw them into the fire to burn. From that fire, flames will spread to all the people of Israel."
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: This is Jerusalem. I have set her among the nations, with countries all around her.
She turned My laws into wickedness, worse than the nations, and My rules, worse than the countries around her. She rejected My laws and did not follow them.

So this is what the Lord the LORD says: Because you have been more unruly than the nations around you and have not followed My statutes or kept My laws, and have not even lived by the laws of the nations around you,"
"therefore, this is what the Lord the LORD says: I am against you. I will carry out judgments on you while the nations watch.
Because of all your detestable practices, I will do to you what I have never done before and will never do again.
Fathers will eat their sons, and sons will eat their fathers. I will punish you and scatter all your remnant to the wind.
As surely as I live, declares the Lord the LORD, because you made My holy place unclean with all your hateful idols and detestable practices, I will look away and not spare you. I will have no pity.
A third of you will die by plague and be wasted away by famine inside the city. A third will fall by the sword all around you. And a third I will scatter to every wind, chasing them with a sword."

"Then My anger will be finished, and I will calm My fury against them and be satisfied. When I have finished pouring out My fury on them, they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in My jealous anger.
I will make you a ruin and a disgrace among the nations around you, in the sight of everyone who passes by.
It will be a disgrace and an insult, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I carry out judgments on you in anger and fury and harsh discipline. I, the LORD, have spoken.
When I send against them the deadly arrows of famine to destroy you, I will increase the famine on you and break your supply of bread.

I will send famine and wild animals against you, and they will rob you of your children. Disease and bloodshed will pass through you, and I will bring the sword against you. I, the LORD, have spoken."
The word of the LORD came to me and said,
“Son of man, turn your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

Say, ‘Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord the LORD. This is what the Lord the LORD says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: Look, I am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.
Your altars will be ruined, and your incense altars will be smashed. I will throw down your slain in front of your idols.
I will place the bodies of the Israelites in front of their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

In every place where you live, the cities will be destroyed and the high places will be empty. Then your altars will be ruined and left empty, your idols will be broken and abandoned, your incense altars will be cut down, and your works will be wiped out.
The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the LORD.’”
Yet I will leave a few survivors. Some of you will escape the sword when you are scattered among the nations and lands.

Then, in the nations where they are taken captive, your survivors will remember Me. They will remember how I was hurt by their unfaithful hearts that turned away from Me, and by their eyes that lusted after their idols. They will hate themselves for the evil they did and for all their hateful acts.
And they will know that I am the LORD. I did not speak in vain about this disaster coming on them.

This is what the Lord the LORD says: “Clap your hands, stomp your feet, and cry out, ‘Alas!’ because of all the wicked, hateful sins of the house of Israel. They will fall by sword, famine, and plague.
The one who is far away will die of plague; the one who is near will fall by the sword; and the one who remains and is kept safe will die of hunger. So I will pour out My wrath on them.”

Then you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain lie among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on every mountaintop, and under every green tree and every leafy oak—the places where they offered a pleasing smell to all their idols.
I will stretch out My hand against them and make the land empty and ruined, from the desert to Diblah, in every place where they live. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“And you, son of man, thus says the Lord the LORD to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come upon the four corners of the earth.
The end is now upon you, and I will send My anger against you. I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your detestable practices.
My eye will not spare you, and I will have no pity. I will bring your ways upon you, and your abominations will be among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.”
“Thus says the Lord the LORD: Disaster upon disaster! Look, it is coming.
The end has come; the end has come! It has awakened against you. Look, it comes.
Doom has come upon you, O inhabitant of the land. The time has come; the day is near. There is panic on the mountains, not shouts of joy.
Now, very soon, I will pour out My wrath upon you and spend My anger against you. I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your detestable practices.
My eye will not spare you, and I will have no pity. I will repay you according to your ways, and your abominations will be among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD who strikes.”
“Look, the day! Look, it comes! Doom has gone out; the rod has budded; arrogance has blossomed.
Violence has risen into a rod of wickedness. None of them will remain, none of their multitude, none of their wealth, nor anything of value among them.
The time has come; the day has arrived. Let the buyer not rejoice, and the seller not mourn, for wrath is upon all their multitude.
For the seller will not recover what he sold while both remain alive. For the vision concerning all their multitude will not be reversed. Because of their iniquity, no one will preserve his life.
They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes to war, for My wrath is upon all their multitude.”
“The sword is outside; plague and famine are inside. Whoever is in the field will die by the sword, and whoever is in the city will be consumed by famine and plague.
Their survivors who escape will be on the mountains, mourning like doves of the valleys, each for his own iniquity.
Every hand will go limp, and every knee will be weak as water.
They will put on sackcloth, and terror will cover them. Shame will be on every face, and all their heads will be shaved.

They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will be like something unclean. Their silver and gold will not save them in the day of the wrath of the LORD. They will not satisfy their hunger or fill their stomachs, for their iniquity has become a stumbling block.
“They took pride in their beautiful jewelry and used it to make their detestable images and abominations. Therefore I will make it an unclean thing to them.
I will give it into the hands of foreigners as plunder and to the wicked of the earth as spoil, and they will profane it.
I will turn My face away from them, and they will profane My treasured place. Robbers will enter it and profane it.
Forge the chain, for the land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of violence.
I will bring the worst of the nations, and they will possess their houses. I will put an end to the pride of the strong, and their holy places will be profaned.
Anguish is coming; they will seek peace, but there will be none.
Disaster upon disaster will come, and rumor upon rumor. They will seek a vision from a prophet, but the law will be lost from the priest, and counsel from the elders.

The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed with despair, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will deal with them according to their ways, and I will judge them by their own standards. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting in front of me. There the hand of the Lord the LORD fell on me.
I looked, and I saw a figure that looked like a man. From the waist down, it looked like fire. From the waist up, it looked like bright, glowing metal.

He reached out something that looked like a hand and took me by the hair of my head. The Spirit lifted me up between the earth and the sky and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem. He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the inner courtyard, where the idol of jealousy sits, the one that stirs up jealousy.
There I saw the glory of the God of Israel, just like the vision I had seen in the valley.
"Son of man," He said to me, "look toward the north." So I looked toward the north, and there at the entrance of the gate by the altar was this idol of jealousy.

He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they are doing? The people of Israel are doing terrible, detestable things here. They are driving Me far away from My sanctuary. But you will see even more detestable things."
Then He brought me to the entrance of the courtyard, and I looked and saw a hole in the wall.
He said to me, "Son of man, dig through the wall." So I dug through the wall and saw an entrance.
He said to me, "Go in and see the wicked, detestable things they are doing here."
So I went in and looked, and I saw that all around the wall were carved pictures of crawling creatures, unclean animals, and all the idols of the people of Israel.
In front of them stood seventy of the elders of Israel, and Jaazaniah son of Shaphan was standing among them. Each man held a censer in his hand, and a thick cloud of incense was rising.

He said to me, "Son of man, have you seen what the elders of Israel are doing in the dark? Each man is in his own room of idols. They say, 'The LORD does not see us. The LORD has abandoned the land.'"
He also said to me, "You will see them doing even more detestable things."
Then He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and there women were sitting, weeping for Tammuz.
He said to me, "Son of man, do you see this? You will see even more detestable things than these."

He brought me into the inner courtyard of the house of the LORD. There, at the entrance to the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men. Their backs were toward the temple of the LORD, and their faces were toward the east. They were bowing down to the sun in the east.

He said to me, "Son of man, have you seen this? Is it not enough for the people of Judah to do these detestable things here? They have filled the land with violence, and they keep provoking Me to anger. Look, they are thumbing their noses at Me."
So I will act in My anger. My eye will not spare them, and I will have no pity. Even if they shout loudly to Me, I will not listen to them.
Then, in my hearing, a loud voice called out, "Bring the city's destroyers near. Each one carries a weapon of destruction."

I saw six men coming from the upper gate, the one that faces north. Each man had a weapon for breaking things in his hand. One man among them wore linen clothes and had a writer's inkhorn at his waist. They came and stood beside the bronze altar.
The glory of the God of Israel had moved up from the cherub where it rested to the threshold of the house. He called to the man in linen who had the writer's inkhorn at his waist.
The LORD said to him, "Go through the city, through Jerusalem. Put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the horrible things done there."
Then, in my hearing, He said to the others, "Follow him through the city and strike them down. Do not let your eyes spare anyone, and do not show pity."
"Kill the old, the young, girls, women, and children, but do not touch anyone who has the mark. Start at My sanctuary." So they started with the older leaders in front of the temple.
He told them, "Make the temple unclean and fill the courtyards with dead bodies. Go out!" So they went out and struck people in the city.
While they were striking, I was left alone. I fell on my face and cried out, "Oh no, Lord the LORD! Will You destroy all that is left of Israel when You pour out Your anger on Jerusalem?"
He answered me, "The sin of Israel and Judah is very, very great. The land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of injustice. They say, 'The LORD has left the land. The LORD does not see.'"
"As for Me, My eye will not spare, and I will not pity. I will bring their own actions back on their heads."
Then I saw the man in linen with the inkhorn at his waist. He reported, "I have done what You commanded."
I looked, and above the heads of the cherubim there was something that looked like a throne made of sapphire.
He told the man dressed in linen, "Go between the wheels under the cherub. Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim and throw them over the city." The man went in while I watched.
The cherubim were standing on the south side of the temple when he went in, and a cloud filled the inner court.

Then the glory of the LORD rose from above the cherub and moved to the threshold of the temple. The temple was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the LORD.
The sound of the cherubim's wings could be heard as far as the outer court. It sounded like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks.
When He commanded the man dressed in linen, "Take fire from among the wheels, from among the cherubim," the man went in and stood beside a wheel.
Then one of the cherubim reached out his hand to the fire among the cherubim. He took some and put it into the hands of the man dressed in linen, who took it and went out.
The cherubim looked like they had human hands under their wings.
I looked and saw four wheels beside the cherubim, one beside each cherub. The wheels shone like topaz.
All four wheels looked alike, each like a wheel inside another wheel.
When they moved, they could go in any of the four directions without turning. They followed wherever the head faced, without turning as they moved.
Their bodies, backs, hands, and wings were full of eyes all around, and so were their four wheels.
I heard them called "the whirling wheels."
Each cherub had four faces: the first was a cherub's face, the second a man's, the third a lion's, and the fourth an eagle's.
Then the cherubim rose up. They were the living creatures I had seen by the Kebar River.
When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them. When they lifted their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels did not leave their side.
When the cherubim stood still, the wheels stood still. When they rose, the wheels rose with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
Then the glory of the LORD left the threshold of the temple and stopped above the cherubim.

The cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth while I watched. The wheels went with them. They stopped at the east gate of the LORD's house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
These were the living creatures I had seen under the God of Israel by the Kebar River, and I knew they were cherubim.
Each had four faces and four wings, and under their wings were what looked like human hands.
Their faces looked like the faces I had seen by the Kebar River. Each one moved straight ahead.

The Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the house of the LORD, the gate that faces east. At the entrance of the gate I saw twenty-five men. Among them were Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
The LORD said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who plan evil and give bad advice in this city."
They say, "Isn't it almost time to build houses? This city is like a pot, and we are the meat kept safe inside it."
Therefore prophesy against them, Son of man. Prophesy!
Then the Spirit of the LORD fell on me, and He said to me, "Say: This is what the LORD says: You people of Israel have said these things, and I know every thought that comes into your minds.
"You have killed many people in this city and filled its streets with the dead.
"So this is what the Lord the LORD says: The people you killed in this city are the meat, and the city is the pot. But I will bring you out of it.
"You have feared the sword, so I will bring the sword against you, declares the Lord the LORD.
"I will bring you out of the city and hand you over to foreigners. I will punish you.
"You will die by the sword. I will judge you at the border of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
"This city will not be a pot for you, and you will not be the meat inside it. I will judge you at the border of Israel.
"Then you will know that I am the LORD. You did not follow My laws or practice My rules. Instead, you followed the rules of the nations around you."
While I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I fell facedown and cried out in a loud voice, "Alas, Lord the LORD! Will You make a complete end of the people of Israel who are left?"
Then the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, your brothers—your brothers, your relatives, and all the house of Israel—are the ones the people of Jerusalem talk about when they say, 'They are far from the LORD; this land has been given to us as our possession.'

"So say, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: I sent them far away to other nations and scattered them among the countries. Yet for a little while I have been a place of worship for them in the countries where they have gone.'
"So say, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will gather you from the nations and bring you together from the countries where you were scattered. I will give you the land of Israel.'
"They will return to it and remove all its disgusting things and all its evil practices.
"I will give them one heart and put a new spirit in them. I will take away their stubborn heart of stone and give them a tender heart of flesh.
"Then they will follow My laws and keep My rules and do them. They will be My people, and I will be their God.
"But those who set their hearts on their disgusting things and evil practices—I will bring the results of their actions down on their own heads, declares the Lord the LORD."
Then the cherubim, with the wheels beside them, lifted their wings, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
The glory of the LORD rose up from inside the city and stood over the mountain east of the city.
The Spirit lifted me up and, in a vision from the Spirit of God, brought me to the exiles in Chaldea. Then the vision I had seen left me.
I told the exiles everything the LORD had shown me.
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, you live among a rebellious house. They have eyes to see, but they do not see. They have ears to hear, but they do not hear, because they are a rebellious house.”

“As for you, Son of man, pack a bag for exile. Go into exile by day while they watch. Travel from your place to another place while they watch. Maybe they will notice, even though they are a rebellious house.
Bring out your baggage by day while they watch, like baggage for exile. Then go out in the evening while they watch, like people who must go into exile.
While they watch, dig through the wall and bring your baggage out through it.
While they watch, lift the baggage onto your shoulder and carry it out at dusk. Cover your face so you cannot see the land, because I have made you a sign for the house of Israel.”

I did just as I was told. I brought out my baggage by day, like baggage for exile. In the evening I dug through the wall with my own hands. I brought the baggage out at dusk and carried it on my shoulder while they watched.
In the morning the word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, has not the house of Israel, that rebellious house, said to you, ‘What are you doing?’”
“Say to them, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: This message is about the prince in Jerusalem and all the people of Israel who live there.’
Say, ‘I am a sign for you. Just as I did, it will be done to them. They will go into exile and captivity.’
“The prince among them will lift his baggage onto his shoulder at dusk and go out. They will dig through the wall to bring him out through it. He will cover his face so he cannot see the land.
I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My trap. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, but he will not see it, and he will die there.
I will scatter to every wind all who are around him, his helpers and all his troops. I will draw My sword after them.
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I scatter them among the nations and spread them through other lands.
But I will spare a few from the sword, famine, and plague, so they can tell about all their terrible sins among the nations where they go. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, eat your bread with shaking, and drink your water with trembling and worry.”

“Say to the people of the land, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says about the people living in Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They will eat their bread with worry and drink their water in dismay, because their land will be stripped of everything in it due to the violence of everyone who lives there.
The cities where people live will be destroyed, and the land will become empty. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’”
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, what is this proverb you people have in the land of Israel? You say, ‘The days go by, and every vision comes to nothing.’”
“So tell them, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will stop this proverb. They will not use it in Israel anymore.’ Instead, say, ‘The days are near, and every vision will come true.’
There will be no more false visions or smooth-talking fortune-telling among the people of Israel.
For I am the LORD. I will speak, and what I say will happen. It will not be delayed anymore. In your days, you rebellious house, I will speak and do it, declares the Lord the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, the people of Israel are saying, ‘The vision he sees is for many days from now. He prophesies about times far away.’
So tell them, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: None of My words will be delayed anymore. The word I speak will happen, declares the Lord the LORD.’”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are now prophesying. Tell those who prophesy out of their own imagination: 'Hear the word of the LORD!'"
This is what the Lord the LORD says: "Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing!
Your prophets, O Israel, are like foxes prowling through the rubble.
You have not stepped into the gaps or built up a wall for the house of Israel to stand in the battle on the day of the LORD."
"They see false visions and speak lying divinations. They say, 'This is the LORD's declaration,' when the LORD has not sent them, yet they hope their words come true.
Have you not seen a false vision and spoken a lying divination when you say, 'This is the LORD's declaration,' though I have not spoken?"
Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: "Because you have spoken empty words and seen lies, look, I am against you, declares the Lord the LORD.

My hand will be against the prophets who see false visions and speak lying divinations. They will not belong to the council of My people or be recorded in the register of the house of Israel, nor will they enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord the LORD."
"Because they have led My people astray, saying, 'Peace,' when there is no peace, and because when someone builds a flimsy wall, they cover it with whitewash,
tell those who cover it with whitewash that it will fall. A torrential rain will come, and I will send hailstones and violent winds to make it collapse.
When the wall has fallen, will you not be asked, 'Where is the whitewash you applied?'"
Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: "In My wrath I will release a torrential rain, and in My anger hailstones and violent winds will sweep through and destroy.

I will tear down the wall you have plastered with whitewash and bring it to the ground, so that its foundation is exposed. It will collapse, and you will be destroyed in its ruins. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
"I will use up My anger against the wall and against those who plastered it with whitewash. Then I will say to you: 'The wall is gone, and so are those who whitewashed it—
the prophets of Israel who prophesied to Jerusalem and saw visions of peace for her when there was no peace, declares the Lord the LORD.'"
"Now, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own imagination. Prophesy against them

and say: 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: Woe to the women who sew magic charms onto their wrists and make veils for the heads of people of every height to trap people. Will you trap My people but save yourselves?'"

"You have dishonored Me among My people for a few handfuls of barley and scraps of bread. By lying to My people who listen to lies, you kill those who should not die and spare those who should not live."

"Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: I am against your magic charms, which you use to trap people like birds. I will tear them from your arms and set free the people you have trapped like birds.
I will also tear off your veils and rescue My people from your hands. Then they will no longer be prey for you. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
"Because you have broken the hearts of righteous people with your lies, though I never hurt them, and because you have encouraged wicked people not to turn from their evil ways to save their lives,
therefore you will no longer see false visions or practice fortune-telling. I will rescue My people from your hands. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
Some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat down in front of me.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, these men have brought their idols into their hearts. They have put the stumbling block of their sin right in front of their faces. Should I be asked by them? I will answer them.”

“So speak to them and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: When any Israelite sets up idols in his heart and puts the stumbling block of his sin right in front of his face, and then comes to the prophet, I, the LORD, will answer him according to how many idols he has.
I will do this to win back the hearts of the people of Israel, who have all turned away from Me because of their idols.’”
“So tell the people of Israel, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: Turn back! Turn away from your idols and from all your disgusting sins.

When any Israelite or any foreigner living in Israel turns away from Me and sets up idols in his heart, puts the stumbling block of his sin right in front of his face, and then comes to a prophet to ask something of Me, I, the LORD, will answer him Myself.
I will turn against that man. I will make him a warning sign and a story people tell. I will cut him off from My people. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
If a prophet is tricked into giving a message, I, the LORD, am the One who tricked that prophet. I will raise My hand against him and destroy him from among My people Israel.
They will suffer for their guilt. The guilt of the person who asks will be the same as the guilt of the prophet.

Then the people of Israel will no longer wander away from Me. They will no longer make themselves unclean with all their sins. They will be My people, and I will be their God, says the Lord the LORD.’”
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, if a country sins against Me by being unfaithful, I will reach out My hand against it. I will break its supply of bread. I will send famine into it and cut off both people and animals.
Even if these three men—Noah, Daniel, and Job—were in it, they would save only themselves by their righteousness, says the Lord the LORD.
If I send wild animals through the land and they make it childless and empty, so that no one travels through it because of the animals,
as surely as I live, says the Lord the LORD, even those three men would not save sons or daughters. They alone would be saved, but the land would be empty.
Or if I bring a sword against that land and say, ‘Let a sword pass through the land,’ and I cut off both people and animals from it,
as surely as I live, says the Lord the LORD, those three men would not save sons or daughters. They alone would be saved.
Or if I send a plague into that land and pour out My wrath on it in blood, killing both people and animals,
as surely as I live, says the Lord the LORD, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they would save neither son nor daughter. They would save only themselves by their righteousness.

For this is what the Lord the LORD says: How much worse will it be when I send My four terrible judgments—sword, famine, wild animals, and plague—against Jerusalem to cut off both people and animals from it!

Yet there will be survivors left in it—sons and daughters. They will come out to you, and you will see how they live and what they do. Then you will be comforted about the disaster I brought on Jerusalem, about everything I brought on it.
They will comfort you when you see their ways and their deeds. Then you will know that I did not act without a reason for everything I did in it, says the Lord the LORD.”
The word of The LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, what is vine wood compared with all other wood? What is a vine branch among the trees of the forest?
Can wood be taken from it to make something useful? Can a peg be taken from it to hang things on?
See, it is given to the fire for fuel. The fire burns both ends, and the middle is charred. Can it be used for anything then?
Even when it was whole, it could not be used for work. How much less after fire has burned it and charred it!”
“Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: Like vine wood among the trees of the forest, which I gave to the fire for fuel, so I have given the people of Jerusalem.
I will set My face against them. They have come out of the fire, but the fire will consume them. Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I set My face against them.
I will make the land desolate because they have been unfaithful,” declares the Lord the LORD.
The word of the the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her detestable practices.
You are to say, This is what the Lord the the LORD says to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth were from the land of the Canaanites. Your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
On the day you were born your cord was not cut, nor were you washed with water to make you clean, nor were you rubbed with salt or wrapped in cloths.
"No one looked at you with pity or cared enough to do even one of these things for you. Instead, you were thrown into an open field because you were hated on the day you were born.
Then I passed by and saw you wallowing in your blood, and as you lay there in your blood I said to you, 'Live!' Yes, I said to you, 'Live!'
I made you grow like a plant of the field. You grew and matured and became very beautiful. Your breasts were formed and your hair grew, but you were naked and bare.

Later I passed by and saw you, and you were at the age for love. So I made you My wife and covered your nakedness. I gave you an oath and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord the the LORD, and you became Mine.
"Then I bathed you with water, washed the blood off you, and anointed you with oil.
I clothed you in embroidered cloth and gave you sandals of fine leather. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk.
I adorned you with jewelry, and I put bracelets on your wrists and a chain around your neck.
I put a ring in your nose, earrings in your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head.
So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was fine linen, silk, and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You became very beautiful and rose to royalty.
Your fame went out among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect in the splendor I had given you, declares the Lord the the LORD."
"But you trusted in your beauty and became a prostitute. You gave yourself to every passerby, and your beauty became theirs.
You took some of your garments and made high places colorful with them, and there you prostituted yourself. Such things should never have happened and must not happen again.
You also took the fine jewelry I gave you, the gold and silver I gave you, and made male images, and you prostituted yourself with them.
You took your embroidered clothes and covered the idols with them, and you offered My oil and incense to them.
"You also set before them the food I gave you—fine flour, oil, and honey that I fed you—and offered it as a pleasing aroma. That is what happened, declares the Lord the the LORD.
You took your sons and daughters, whom you bore to Me, and sacrificed them as food to the idols. Wasn't that enough?
You slaughtered My children and passed them through the fire for them.
In all your detestable practices and prostitution, you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your blood.
"Woe, woe to you! declares the Lord the the LORD. After all your wickedness—
you built yourself a mound and made a high place in every public square.
At the head of every street you built your high places and degraded your beauty. You offered yourself to every passerby and increased your prostitution.
You prostituted yourself to the Egyptians, your neighbors with strong bodies, and increased your prostitution to provoke Me to anger.
So I stretched out My hand against you and reduced your portion. I gave you over to the desire of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your indecent conduct.
You also prostituted yourself to the Assyrians, because you were not satisfied. Even after that, you were still not satisfied.
Then you increased your prostitution to Chaldea, the land of merchants, but even with this you were not satisfied.
"'How weak is your heart!' declares the Lord the the LORD. 'You did all these things, the acts of a shameless prostitute.'
When you built your mounds at the head of every street and made your high places in every public square, you were not like a prostitute, because you refused to take payment.
You are an adulterous wife who takes strangers instead of her husband.
Men give gifts to all prostitutes, but you gave gifts to all your lovers. You bribed them to come to you from all around for your prostitution.
So you were different from other women in your prostitution: no one solicited you, and you paid instead of being paid. Yes, you were different.
Therefore, O prostitute, hear the word of the the LORD!"

"This is what the Lord the the LORD says: Because you poured out your wealth and exposed your nakedness in your prostitution with your lovers and with all your detestable idols, and because you gave them the blood of your children,

therefore I will gather all the lovers you pleased, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from all around, expose your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.
I will judge you as women who commit adultery and shed blood are judged, and I will bring on you the blood of wrath and jealousy.
I will hand you over to your lovers, and they will tear down your mounds and destroy your high places. They will strip you of your clothes, take your fine jewelry, and leave you naked and bare.
"They will bring a mob against you, stone you, and cut you down with their swords.
They will burn down your houses and punish you in front of many women. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will never again pay your lovers.
Then I will calm My wrath against you, and My jealousy will turn away from you. I will be quiet and no longer angry.

Because you did not remember the days of your youth but made Me angry with all these things, I will bring your own conduct down on your head, declares the Lord the the LORD. Did you not add indecency to all your other detestable practices?
"Everyone who quotes proverbs will quote this proverb about you: 'Like mother, like daughter.'

You are the daughter of your mother, who despised her husband and her children. You are the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
Your older sister is Samaria, who lives to your north with her daughters, and your younger sister is Sodom, who lives to your south with her daughters.
You did not walk in their ways or copy their detestable practices. You were even more corrupt and became worse than they in every way.
As surely as I live, declares the Lord the the LORD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did what you and your daughters have done.
This was the sin of your sister Sodom: She and her daughters were proud, had plenty of food, and lived in comfort, but they did not help the poor and needy.
"They were proud and committed detestable acts before Me. So I removed them, as you have seen.
Samaria did not commit half the sins you did. You have done more detestable things than they, and you have made your sisters look righteous by comparison.

You too must bear your shame, because you have given your sisters an excuse. Your sins were worse than theirs, so they are more righteous than you. Be ashamed and bear your disgrace, because you have made your sisters look better.
I will restore Sodom and her daughters from captivity, and Samaria and her daughters from captivity, and I will restore your captives along with them.
So you will bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you did when you comforted them.
"Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, and Samaria and her daughters, will return to what they were before. And you and your daughters will return to what you were before.
Was not your sister Sodom a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride,
before your wickedness was exposed? Now you are scorned by the daughters of Edom and all her neighbors, and by the daughters of the Philistines—all those around you who despise you.
You must bear the consequences of your indecency and your detestable practices, declares the the LORD.
For this is what the Lord the the LORD says: I will deal with you as you deserve, because you broke the oath and violated the covenant."
"Yet I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.
Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your older and younger sisters. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of your covenant.
I will establish My covenant with you, and you will know that I am the the LORD.
So that you may remember and be ashamed and never open your mouth again because of your disgrace, when I have forgiven you for all you have done, declares the Lord the the LORD."
The word of the the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, give the people of Israel a riddle and tell them a story.
Say, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: A great eagle with big wings and long wing feathers, covered with many colorful feathers, came to Lebanon and took the top of a cedar tree.
He broke off its highest young twigs and carried them to a trading country. He set them in a city of merchants.
Then he took some seed from that land and planted it in fertile soil. He placed it by plenty of water and set it out like a willow branch.
It grew and became a low, spreading vine. Its branches reached toward him, and its roots stayed where they were. So it became a vine and grew branches and sent out shoots.

But there was another great eagle with big wings and many feathers. This vine bent its roots toward him and sent its branches toward him from the garden bed where it was planted, so that eagle could water it.
It had been planted in good soil by plenty of water so it could grow branches, bear fruit, and become a fine vine.'

Say, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: Will it thrive? Won't he pull up its roots and cut off its fruit so it withers? All its fresh new leaves will dry up. It won't need a strong arm or many people to pull it up by the roots.
Look, it is planted. Will it thrive? Won't it completely wither when the east wind hits it? It will wither in the beds where it sprouted.'"
Then the word of the the LORD came to me:
"Say to this rebellious people, 'Don't you know what these things mean? Tell them: The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem. He took its king and its leaders and brought them back to Babylon.
He took one of the royal family and made a covenant with him. He made him swear an oath. He also took away the leading men of the land,
so the kingdom would be humble and not try to rise up, and so it would keep his covenant and stand.

But he rebelled against the king of Babylon by sending his messengers to Egypt to get horses and a large army. Will he succeed? Can a man who does such things escape? Can he break the covenant and still escape?
As surely as I live, declares the Lord the LORD, "he will die in Babylon, in the city of the king who made him king. He looked down on that king's oath and broke his covenant."
Pharaoh, with his mighty army and large force, will not help him in war when siege ramps are built and walls are raised to kill many people.
He looked down on the oath and broke the covenant. He made a pledge, yet he did all these things. So he will not escape.
So this is what the Lord the LORD says: "As surely as I live, I will bring on his head the oath he looked down on and the covenant he broke.
I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My trap. I will bring him to Babylon and judge him there for the betrayal he committed against Me.
All his finest soldiers will fall by the sword, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. Then you will know that I am the the LORD. I have spoken."'
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will take a sprig from the top of the tall cedar. I will break off a tender shoot from its highest young twigs and plant it on a high, lofty mountain.
I will plant it on a high mountain in Israel. It will grow branches and bear fruit and become a splendid cedar. Birds of every kind will live under it. They will nest in the shade of its branches.

Then all the trees in the field will know that I am the the LORD. I bring down the high tree and lift up the low tree. I dry up the green tree and make the dry tree bloom. I am the the LORD. I have spoken, and I will do it."
The word of the LORD came to me. He said,
"What do you mean by using this saying in Israel: 'Parents sin, and their children suffer for it'?
As surely as I live, says the Lord the LORD, you will not use this saying in Israel anymore.
"Look, every life belongs to Me. The life of the father and the life of the son are both Mine. The person who sins will die.
"Suppose a man does what is right and fair.
He does not eat food offered at mountain shrines. He does not look up to the idols of Israel. He does not sin with his neighbor's wife. He does not have sex with a woman during her monthly period.
He does not mistreat anyone. He returns what he took as a pledge. He does not steal. He gives food to the hungry. He gives clothes to people who need them.
He does not lend money for interest or make unfair profit. He stays away from wrong. He judges fairly between people.
He follows My laws and keeps My rules. He lives faithfully. That man is right with God, and he will surely live, says the Lord the LORD.
"But suppose that man has a violent son who murders people and does any of these things, even though his father did none of them.
The son eats food at mountain shrines. He sins with his neighbor's wife.
He mistreats the poor and needy. He steals. He does not return what he took as a pledge. He looks up to idols. He does terrible things.
He lends money for interest and makes unfair profit. Will he live? No, he will not live. He has done all these terrible things, so he will surely die. He is to blame for his own death.
"Now suppose that violent son has a son who sees all his father's sins but does not copy them.
He does not eat food at mountain shrines. He does not look up to idols. He does not sin with his neighbor's wife.
He does not mistreat anyone. He does not take things as a pledge to cheat people. He does not steal. He gives food to the hungry. He gives clothes to those who need them.
He does not take advantage of the poor. He does not lend money for interest or make unfair profit. He does what is right and fair. That son will not die for his father's sin. He will live.
But his father, because he cheated and robbed people and did evil among his people, will die for his own sin.
"But you ask, 'Why doesn't the son pay for his father's sin?' The answer is that the son did what was right and fair. He kept My laws and followed them, so he will live.

The person who sins is the one who will die. A son will not be punished for his father's sin, and a father will not be punished for his son's sin. The good person will be rewarded for his own goodness, and the wicked person will be punished for his own wickedness.
"But if a wicked person turns away from all the sins he has done and keeps My laws and does what is right and fair, he will live. He will not die.
None of his past sins will be remembered. He will live because of the right things he does.
Do I enjoy seeing a wicked person die? says the Lord the LORD. No, I would rather see him turn from his old ways and live.

But if a good person turns away from doing right and starts doing wrong, doing the same terrible things a wicked person does, will he live? No. None of the good things he did will be remembered. He will die because of the wrong he has done.
"But you say, 'The Lord's way is not fair.' Listen, people of Israel: Is My way unfair? Isn't it your ways that are unfair?
When a good person turns from doing right and does wrong, he will die. He will die for the wrong he has done.
When a wicked person turns from his wickedness and does what is right and fair, he will save his life.
Because he thought about his sins and turned away from them, he will live. He will not die.
But you, people of Israel, say, 'The Lord's way is not fair.' Are My ways unfair, people of Israel? Isn't it your ways that are unfair?
"So I will judge you, people of Israel. Each of you will be judged by what he has done, says the Lord the LORD. Turn away from all your sins. Stop doing wrong so that sin will not destroy you.
Throw away all the sins you have done. Get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why do you want to die, people of Israel?
I do not want anyone to die, says the Lord the LORD. So turn back to Me and live."
As for you, take up a sad song for Israel's leaders.
Say, "What was your mother? A lioness among lions. She lay down among young lions and raised her cubs.
She brought up one of her cubs, and he became a young lion. He learned to tear his prey, and he killed people.
The nations heard about him, so they caught him in their pit. They dragged him with hooks to Egypt.
When she saw that her hope was gone, she took another cub and made him a young lion.
He walked among the lions and became a young lion. He learned to tear his prey, and he killed people.
He tore down their strong places and destroyed their cities. The land and everything in it was ruined by the sound of his roaring.
Then nations from all around came against him. They spread their net over him, and he was caught in their pit.
They dragged him with hooks into a cage and brought him to the king of Babylon. They took him to their forts so his voice would never again be heard on Israel's mountains.
Your mother was like a vine planted in your vineyard by the water. It was fruitful and full of branches because of plenty of water.
Its branches were strong enough to be a ruler's staff. It grew tall above the thick branches, and people could see it because of its height and many leaves.
But it was torn up in anger and thrown to the ground. The east wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches broke off and dried up, and fire burned them.
Now it is planted in the desert, in a dry and thirsty land.
Fire has come out from its main branch and burned its fruit. No strong branch is left to be a ruler's staff." This is a sad song, and it will be used as a sad song.
In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month, some of the elders of Israel came to ask the LORD a question. They sat down in front of me.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:

“Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel. Tell them this is what the Lord the LORD says: ‘Have you come to ask Me questions? As surely as I live, I will not let you ask Me anything,’ says the Lord the LORD.
Son of man, will you judge them? Will you judge them? Then make known to them the disgusting things their fathers did.”

“Tell them this is what the Lord the LORD says: On the day I chose Israel, I raised My hand in an oath to the family of Jacob. I made Myself known to them in Egypt. I raised My hand and said, ‘I am the LORD your God.’
On that day I raised My hand to bring them out of Egypt into a land I had chosen for them. It was a rich land, the finest of all lands.
I told them, ‘Each of you must throw away the disgusting things you look at. Do not make yourselves unclean with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.’”
“But they refused to listen to Me. No one threw away the disgusting things he looked at. No one gave up the idols of Egypt. So I said I would pour out My anger on them and destroy them in Egypt.
But I acted for the sake of My name, so it would not be dishonored among the nations where they lived. There I had shown them who I was by bringing them out of Egypt.
So I brought them out of Egypt and led them into the desert.”
“I gave them My laws and taught them My rules. If a person follows them, he will live.
I also gave them My Sabbaths. They were a sign between Me and them, so they would know that I am the LORD, who makes them holy.

But the people of Israel rebelled against Me in the desert. They did not follow My laws. They rejected My rules, even though a person who follows them will live. They badly dishonored My Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out My anger on them and destroy them in the desert.
But I acted for the sake of My name, so it would not be dishonored among the nations who saw Me bring them out.”
“I also raised My hand in the desert. I swore I would not bring them into the land I had given them, a rich land, the finest of all lands.
They rejected My rules and did not follow My laws. They dishonored My Sabbaths, because their hearts went after their idols.
But I felt sorry for them. I did not destroy them completely in the desert.”
“I told their children in the desert, ‘Do not follow your parents’ ways. Do not keep their rules. Do not make yourselves unclean with their idols.’
I am the LORD your God. Follow My laws. Keep My rules and do them.
Keep My Sabbaths holy. They are a sign between Me and you, so you will know that I am the LORD your God.

But the children also rebelled against Me. They did not follow My laws. They did not keep My rules, even though a person who follows them will live. They dishonored My Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out My anger on them and destroy them in the desert.
But I held back My hand. I acted for the sake of My name, so it would not be dishonored among the nations who saw Me bring them out.”
“I also raised My hand in the desert. I swore I would scatter them among the nations and spread them through other countries.
They did not follow My rules. They rejected My laws. They dishonored My Sabbaths. Their eyes were set on their fathers’ idols.
So I also gave them rules that were not good and laws by which they could not live.
I let them become unclean through their gifts. They sacrificed their firstborn children by passing them through the fire. I did this to make them guilty and to show them that I am the LORD.”
“Therefore, Son of man, speak to the people of Israel. Tell them this is what the Lord the LORD says: ‘Your fathers also insulted Me by being unfaithful to Me.’

I brought them into the land I had promised to give them. When they saw every high hill and every green tree, they offered their sacrifices there. They made Me angry by placing their gifts there. They burned their sweet-smelling offerings there. They poured out their drink offerings there.
I asked them, ‘What is this high place you keep going to?’ So it is called High Place to this day.”
“Therefore tell the people of Israel this is what the Lord the LORD says: ‘You are making yourselves unclean the same way your fathers did. You are chasing after their disgusting things.’

When you offer your gifts and sacrifice your children in the fire, you make yourselves unclean with all your idols to this day. Should I let you ask Me questions, people of Israel? As surely as I live, says the Lord the LORD, I will not let you ask Me anything.
What you are thinking will never happen. You say, ‘Let us be like the other nations, like the families of other lands. Let us worship wood and stone.’”
“As surely as I live, says the Lord the LORD, I will rule over you with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and poured-out anger.
I will bring you out from the nations. I will gather you from the countries where you were scattered. I will rule over you with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and poured-out anger.
I will bring you into the desert of the nations. There I will judge you face to face.
I will judge you the same way I judged your fathers in the desert of Egypt, says the Lord the LORD.
I will make you pass under My rod. I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.
I will remove from you those who rebel and sin against Me. I will bring them out of the land where they live, but they will not enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.”

“As for you, people of Israel, this is what the Lord the LORD says: Go and serve your idols, every one of you. But later you will surely listen to Me. You will no longer make My holy name unclean with your gifts and your idols.

For on My holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord the LORD, all the people of Israel will serve Me. There, in the land, I will accept them. There I will ask for your offerings and the best of your gifts, along with all your holy things.
When I bring you out from the nations and gather you from the countries where you were scattered, I will accept you like a pleasing smell. I will show My holiness through you before the nations.
Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land I raised My hand to give to your fathers.
There you will remember your ways and all your actions by which you made yourselves unclean. You will hate yourselves because of all the evil you have done.
Then you will know, people of Israel, that I am the LORD. I will deal with you for the sake of My name, not according to your evil ways or your corrupt actions, says the Lord the LORD.”
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, turn your face toward the south. Speak against the south. Prophesy against the forest of the south.”

“Say to the forest of the south, ‘Hear the word of the LORD. This is what the Lord the LORD says: I am about to set a fire in you. It will burn up every green tree and every dry tree. The bright flame will not be put out. Every face from south to north will be scorched by it.’
Everyone will see that I, the LORD, have set it on fire. It will not be put out.”
Then I said, “Ah, Lord the LORD! They are saying about me, ‘Is he not just telling parables?’”
The word of the LORD came to me. He said,
“Son of man, turn your face toward Jerusalem. Speak against the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel.
Say to the land of Israel, “This is what the LORD says: I am against you. I will draw My sword from its sheath and remove from you both the righteous and the wicked.
Because I will remove both the righteous and the wicked from you, My sword will go out of its sheath against all people, from the south to the north.
Then all people will know that I, the LORD, have drawn My sword from its sheath, and it will not be put back.”
“And you, son of man, groan in front of them. Groan with broken hips and bitter sadness.

When they ask you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ say to them, ‘Because of the news that is coming. Everyone will lose courage, every hand will go limp, every spirit will fail, and every knee will give way. Yes, it is coming, and it will happen,’ says the Lord the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me. He said,
“Son of man, prophesy and say: ‘This is what the Lord says: A sword, a sword, sharpened and polished!
Sharpened to kill, polished to flash like lightning! Should we rejoice? The scepter of My son despises every tree.
It has been given to be polished and held in the hand. It is sharpened and polished to be given to the killer.
Cry out and wail, son of man, because this sword is against My people and against all the leaders of Israel. They are handed over to the sword along with My people. So strike your thigh.
For it has been tested, and what if the scepter that rejects does not last? declares the Lord the LORD.’”
“And you, son of man, prophesy and clap your hands. Let the sword strike twice, three times. It is a sword for the slain, a great sword for the slaughter, cutting deep into them.
So that people lose courage and many stumble, I have set the point of the sword against all their gates. It is made to flash like lightning and polished for slaughter.
Gather yourself, turn right, set yourself, turn left, wherever your face is pointed.
I will also strike My hands together and satisfy My anger. I, the LORD, have spoken.”
The word of the LORD came to me. He said,
“Son of man, make two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to travel. Both roads start from one land. Make a signpost where the road splits toward a city.
Mark one road for the sword to go against Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another against Judah and fortified Jerusalem.
For the king of Babylon stands at the fork in the road, at the head of the two roads, to seek a sign by divination. He shakes his arrows, asks his idols, and looks at the liver.

In his right hand is the sign for Jerusalem: to set up battering rams, to open the mouth with bloodshed, to shout a battle cry, to set up battering rams against the gates, to build a siege ramp, and to build a siege wall.
It will seem like a false sign to them, because they have sworn solemn oaths. But he will remind them of their guilt and capture them.”

“Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: Because you have brought your guilt to mind by uncovering your rebellions and showing your sins in all your actions—because you have done this, you will be captured.
And you, O sinful and wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come at the time of final punishment,
this is what the Lord the LORD says: Remove the turban and take off the crown. Things will not stay as they are. Raise up the lowly and bring down the exalted.
I will ruin it, ruin it, ruin it. It will not be restored until He comes to whom the right to judge belongs, and I will give it to Him.”
“Now prophesy, son of man, and say: ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says about the Ammonites and their insults: A sword, a sword drawn for slaughter, polished to destroy, flashing like lightning!
While they see false visions for you and cast lying divinations for you, it will be laid on the necks of the wicked who are slain, whose day has come at the time of final punishment.
Return it to its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your birth, I will judge you.
I will pour out My wrath on you. I will blow on you with the fire of My fury. I will hand you over to cruel men, skilled in destruction.
You will be fuel for the fire. Your blood will be in the middle of the land. You will not be remembered, for I, the LORD, have spoken.’”
