The word of the the LORD came to me. He said,
"Son of man, will you judge the city of bloodshed? Will you judge it? Then tell her about all her terrible acts. Say this to her:"
'This is what the Lord the LORD says: You are a city that sheds blood inside yourself, so your time has come. You make idols that make you unclean.

You are guilty because of the blood you shed. You made yourself unclean with the idols you made. You brought your day of judgment near, and your time has run out. So I have made you a shame to the nations and a mockery to all the lands.
Those near and far from you will mock you. You are a city with a bad name, and you are full of trouble.
'Look, the leaders of Israel in you have used their power to shed blood.
In you they have treated father and mother lightly. In your midst they have cheated the stranger. They have hurt the fatherless and the widow.
You have shown disrespect for My holy things and treated My Sabbaths as unholy.
In you there are people who spread lies so that blood is shed. In you they eat at the mountain shrines. They commit sexual sins among you.
'In you men sleep with their father's wife. In you they force themselves on women during their monthly periods.
One man does something disgusting with his neighbor's wife. Another man makes his daughter-in-law unclean through sexual sin. Another man in you has sex with his sister, his father's daughter.
In you they take bribes to shed blood. You charge interest and take extra money. You get rich by cheating your neighbors. And you have forgotten Me, says the Lord the LORD.
'Look, I stand against the dishonest money you have made and the bloodshed among you.
Can your heart stay strong? Can your hands stay powerful in the days when I deal with you? I, the the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
I will scatter you among the nations and spread you through other countries. I will burn away your uncleanness from you.
You will be made unclean in front of the nations, and you will know that I am the the LORD.'
The word of the the LORD came to me. He said,
"Son of man, the people of Israel have become like worthless metal to Me. All of them are like bronze, tin, iron, and lead in a furnace. They are the waste left from silver.
Therefore, this is what the Lord the LORD says: 'Because you have all become worthless metal, I will gather you into Jerusalem.
Just as people gather silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin into a furnace and blow fire on it to melt it, so I will gather you in My anger and fury. I will put you in and melt you.
I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of My anger, and you will be melted in it.
As silver is melted in a furnace, so you will be melted in it. Then you will know that I, the the LORD, have poured out My anger on you.'
The word of the the LORD came to me. He said,
"Son of man, say to the land:" 'You are a land that has not been cleansed. No rain has fallen on you in the day of My anger.
Her prophets have made a secret plan among themselves. They are like a roaring lion tearing its prey. They devour people. They take treasure and costly things. They make many widows in her midst.

Her priests have broken My law. They have treated My holy things as unclean. They have not shown the difference between what is holy and what is common. They have not taught the difference between the unclean and the clean. They have ignored My Sabbaths, and I am treated as unclean among them.
'Her leaders in her midst are like wolves tearing prey. They shed blood and destroy lives to make dishonest money.
Her prophets cover up their evil with false comfort. They see false visions and tell lies in My name. They say, "This is what the Lord the LORD says," when the the LORD has not spoken.
The people of the land have cheated and robbed. They have hurt the poor and needy. They have treated the stranger unfairly.
'I looked for someone among them who would rebuild the wall and stand between Me and the land to protect it from destruction. But I found no one.
So I poured out My anger on them. I destroyed them with the fire of My anger. I made them suffer for what they had done, says the Lord the LORD.'
The word of the LORD came to me. He said,
"Son of man, there were two women. They were daughters of the same mother.
They prostituted themselves in Egypt. They did this even in their youth. Their breasts were fondled there, and their virgin breasts were caressed.
The older one was named Oholah, and her sister was Oholibah. They became Mine, and they had sons and daughters. Oholah stands for Samaria, and Oholibah stands for Jerusalem.
"Oholah was unfaithful while she belonged to Me. She lusted after her lovers, the Assyrians,
warriors dressed in blue—governors and commanders. They were all handsome young men, horsemen riding horses.
She offered herself to all of them, even the best of the Assyrians. She made herself unclean with every idol of the people she lusted after.
She did not stop the prostitution she had started in Egypt. In her youth, men slept with her. They caressed her virgin breasts and poured out their lust on her.
"So I handed her over to her lovers, the Assyrians she lusted after.
They stripped her naked. They took her sons and daughters and killed them with swords. She became a warning to other women, and they carried out judgment against her.
"Her sister Oholibah saw this. But she was even more corrupt in her lust than Oholah. She outdid her sister's unfaithfulness.
She lusted after the Assyrians too—governors and commanders, warriors dressed in fine clothes, and handsome young horsemen. All of them were desirable young men.
I saw that both of them had made themselves unclean. They had taken the same path.
"But Oholibah went even further in her prostitution. She saw men carved on a wall—pictures of Chaldeans, carved in red,
wearing belts around their waists and flowing turbans on their heads. They all looked like officers. They looked like Babylonians from Chaldea, the land where they were born.
When she saw them, she lusted after them. She sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
Then the Babylonians came to her, to the bed of love, and made her unclean with their lust. After she had been defiled by them, she turned away from them in disgust.
When she uncovered her prostitution and exposed her nakedness, I turned away from her in disgust, just as I had turned away from her sister.
Yet she increased her prostitution. She remembered the days of her youth, when she had prostituted herself in the land of Egypt.
She lusted after their lovers, whose genitals were like those of donkeys and whose flow was like that of stallions.
So you revisited the indecency of your youth. The Egyptians caressed your bosom and pressed your young breasts.
"Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Lord the LORD says: I will stir up your lovers against you—the ones you turned away from in disgust. I will bring them against you from every side.

They are the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them. They are handsome young men—governors and commanders, officers and famous men. All of them ride horses.

They will come against you with a crowd of peoples. They will bring weapons, chariots, and wagons. They will surround you on every side with shields and helmets. I will hand you over to them for judgment, and they will judge you by their own laws.

I will set My jealousy against you, and they will deal with you in fury. They will cut off your nose and your ears. Your survivors will fall by the sword. They will take your sons and daughters, and your survivors will be consumed by fire.
They will strip off your clothes and take your fine jewelry.
So I will put an end to your indecency and prostitution, which you began in the land of Egypt. You will not look to them anymore, and you will not remember Egypt.
"For this is what the Lord the LORD says: I will hand you over to those you hate, to those you turned away from in disgust.

They will treat you with hatred and take everything you worked for. They will leave you naked and bare. The nakedness of your prostitution will be exposed. Your indecency and prostitution will be revealed.
I will do these things to you because you were unfaithful with the nations and became unclean with their idols.
You have walked in your sister's way, so I will put her cup into your hand.
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: You will drink your sister's cup. It is deep and wide, and it holds much. It will bring you much mockery and scorn.
You will be filled with drunkenness and grief. It is a cup of horror and ruin—the cup of your sister Samaria.
You will drink it and drain it. You will smash it to pieces, and you will tear your breasts. For I have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD.
Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: Because you forgot Me and cast Me behind your back, you must bear your indecency and prostitution."
Then the LORD said to me, "Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their evil practices.
For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their idols. They even sacrificed the children they bore to Me, passing them through the fire.
On that same day they made My sanctuary unclean and dishonored My Sabbaths.
On the very day they sacrificed their children to their idols, they entered My sanctuary to make it unclean. Yes, this is what they did inside My house.
They even sent messengers for men who came from far away. Look, those men came! You bathed for them, painted your eyes, and put on jewelry.
You sat on a fancy couch with a table set before it. On it you had placed My incense and My oil.

The sound of a noisy crowd went with them. Men from the desert, called Sabeans, were brought in, along with ordinary men from the crowd. They put bracelets on the women's wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads.
"Then I said, 'Will she now add these shameful acts to her prostitution?'
Men went to her as they would go to a prostitute. So they went to Oholah and Oholibah, those wicked women.
But righteous men will judge them. They will judge them as unfaithful wives and murderers are judged, because they are unfaithful and blood is on their hands.
For this is what the Lord the LORD says: Bring a mob against them. Hand them over to terror and plunder.
The mob will stone them and cut them down with swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn down their houses.
So I will put an end to indecency in the land. All the women will be warned not to copy your indecency.
They will repay you with your own indecency. You will bear the punishment for your idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord the LORD."
In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, write down the name of this day. This very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem."
"Son of man, tell this parable to the stubborn people. Say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Put a pot on the fire. Put it on, and pour water into it.
Put in the pieces of meat, all the good pieces—thigh and shoulder. Fill it with the best bones.
Take the best sheep. Pile the bones under it. Boil the pieces of meat. Cook the bones in it.'"

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: "How terrible for the city of blood! It is a pot whose rust is in it, and the rust has not come out. Take its pieces out one by one, without choosing any by lot.
For blood is in her. She put it on the bare rock. She did not pour it on the ground to cover it with dust.
To stir up anger and take revenge, I put her blood on the bare rock, so it would not be covered."
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: "How terrible for the city of blood! I too will make the fire great.
Heap wood on it. Light the fire. Cook the meat well. Mix in the spices. Let the bones burn.
Then set the empty pot on the coals so its bronze gets hot and scorched. Let its filth melt inside it, and let its rust be burned away.
She has worn herself out, but her heavy rust has not come out. Even the fire has not removed her rust.
Because of your unclean ways, I tried to make you clean, but you would not be clean. So you will not be clean again until My anger against you is finished.
I, the LORD, have spoken. It is coming, and I will do it. I will not hold back. I will not show pity. I will not change My mind. They will judge you by your ways and your deeds, says the Lord GOD."
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, I am about to take from you the one you love most. She will die suddenly, but you must not mourn or weep. Do not let your tears fall.
Groan quietly. Do not mourn for the dead. Keep your turban on your head and your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your upper lip. Do not eat the food other people bring you."
So I spoke to the people in the morning. In the evening my wife died. The next morning I did what I had been told to do.
The people asked me, "Won't you tell us what these things mean for us, since you are acting this way?"
I said to them, "The word of the LORD came to me.

Say to the people of Israel, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to dishonor My holy place. It is the pride of your strength, the place you love most, and the hope of your heart. Your sons and daughters whom you left behind will die by the sword.
You will do as I have done. You will not cover your upper lip or eat the food other people bring you.
Your turbans will stay on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep. Instead, you will waste away because of your sins and groan to one another.
Ezekiel will be a sign to you. You will do everything he did. When this happens, you will know that I am the Lord GOD.'"
"And you, Son of man, will it not be on the day when I take from them their fortress, their glory, the place they love most, and the burden of their hearts—their sons and daughters—
that on that day a survivor will come to you to tell you the news?
On that day your mouth will be opened to the survivor. You will speak and no longer be silent. You will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of Man, set your face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

"Say to the Ammonites: 'Hear the word of the Lord the LORD. This is what the Lord the LORD says: Because you said, "Aha!" against My sanctuary when it was ruined, against the land of Israel when it was desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into exile,
"therefore I will hand you over to the people of the East as a possession. They will set up their camps among you and pitch their tents among you. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
"I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and Ammon a resting place for sheep. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'
"For this is what the Lord the LORD says: 'Because you clapped your hands and stomped your feet and rejoiced over the land of Israel with all your soul and all your contempt,

"therefore I will stretch out My hand against you and give you over to the nations as plunder. I will cut you off from the peoples and wipe you out of the countries. I will destroy you, and you will know that I am the LORD.'
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: 'Because Moab and Seir said, "Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations,"
"therefore I will open up Moab's side, starting at its border cities—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim—the glory of the land.
"I will give it, along with the Ammonites, to the people of the East as a possession, so that the Ammonites will not be remembered among the nations.
"So I will carry out judgments on Moab, and they will know that I am the LORD.'
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: 'Because Edom took revenge on the house of Judah and became very guilty by taking revenge,

"therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: I will stretch out My hand against Edom and cut off from it both people and animals. I will make it a wasteland from Teman to Dedan; they will fall by the sword.
"I will take vengeance on Edom through My people Israel. They will deal with Edom according to My anger and wrath, and they will know My vengeance, declares the Lord the LORD.'
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: 'Because the Philistines acted in revenge and took vengeance with malice, to destroy them with ancient hatred,
"therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: I will stretch out My hand against the Philistines, cut off the Cherethites, and destroy the rest of the coast.
"I will carry out great vengeance against them with furious rebukes. Then they will know that I am the LORD when I take vengeance on them.' "
In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me. He said,
“Son of man, because Tyre has said about Jerusalem, ‘Aha! The gate to the nations is broken. It has swung open to me. Now that she is ruined, I will be filled.’
“So this is what the Lord the LORD says: Look, I am against you, Tyre. I will bring many nations against you, just as the sea sends up its waves.
“They will destroy your walls and tear down your towers. I will scrape the soil off you and leave you a bare rock.
“She will become a place where people spread nets in the sea, because I have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD. She will be taken as plunder by the nations.
“Her towns on the mainland will be killed by the sword. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
“For this is what the Lord the LORD says: I will bring Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, king of kings, against you, Tyre. He will come with horses, chariots, horsemen, and a large army.
“He will kill your towns on the mainland with the sword. He will build siege ramps against you, pile up a siege mound against you, and raise a shield against you.
“He will aim the blows of his battering rams at your walls and tear down your towers with his axes.
“His many horses will cover you with dust. Your walls will shake at the noise of horsemen, wagons, and chariots when he enters your gates like an army entering a broken city.
“With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets. He will kill your people with the sword, and your strong pillars will fall to the ground.
“They will plunder your wealth and loot your goods. They will destroy your walls and tear down your fine houses. They will throw your stones, wood, and rubble into the sea.
“I will silence your songs, and no one will hear your harps again.
“I will make you a bare rock, and you will become a place to spread nets. You will never be rebuilt, because I, the LORD, have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD.”
“This is what the Lord the LORD says to Tyre: Will not the coastlands tremble at the sound of your fall, when the wounded cry out and slaughter happens among you?

“All the princes of the sea will come down from their thrones. They will take off their robes and strip off their embroidered clothes. They will put on trembling and sit on the ground. They will tremble every moment and be shocked at you.

“They will sing a funeral song about you and say to you, ‘How you have been destroyed, O famous city, once lived in by seafaring people! She was strong at sea, she and her people, and she put fear into everyone who lived near her.’
“Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your fall. The islands in the sea are terrified at your going away.
“For this is what the Lord the LORD says: When I make you a ruined city like other deserted cities, when I bring the deep over you and the waters cover you,

“I will bring you down with those who go down to the grave, to the people of long ago. I will make you live in the world below, like the old ruins, with those who go down to the grave, so that you will no longer be lived in or have a place among the living. I will show My glory in the land of the living.
“I will make you a horror, and you will be no more. People may look for you, but they will never find you again, declares the Lord the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, raise a lament for Tyre.
Say to Tyre, who sits at the gateway to the sea and trades with many nations on the coastlands: This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: You, Tyre, said, 'I am perfect in beauty.' "
Your borders are in the heart of the seas; your builders made your beauty complete.
They built all your planks from cypress trees from Senir. They took cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.
They made your oars from oaks of Bashan. They made your deck from ivory inlaid with wood from the coasts of Kittim.
Your sail was fine linen from Egypt, so it could be your banner. Your awning was blue and purple cloth from the coasts of Elishah. "
The people of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers. Your wise men, Tyre, were your pilots.
The elders of Gebal and its wise men repaired your seams. All the ships of the sea and their sailors were with you to trade your goods.
Men of Persia, Lud, and Put served in your army. They hung shield and helmet in you. They gave you splendor.
Men of Arvad and your army stood on your walls all around. The men of Gamad were in your towers. They hung their shields all around your walls. They made your beauty complete. "
Tarshish traded with you because of your great wealth. They paid for your goods with silver, iron, tin, and lead.
Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you. They paid for your goods with slaves and bronze vessels.
From Beth Togarmah they gave horses, war horses, and mules for your goods.
The men of Dedan traded with you. Many coastlands were your market. They brought you ivory tusks and ebony as payment.
Aram traded with you because of your many works. They paid for your goods with turquoise, purple cloth, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral, and rubies.
Judah and the land of Israel traded with you. They paid for your goods with wheat from Minnith, pannag, honey, oil, and balm. "
Because of your many works and great wealth, Damascus traded with you. They paid with wine from Helbon and wool as white as snow.
Dan and Greece traded with you. They brought wrought iron, cassia, and cane.
Dedan traded with you in saddle blankets.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers. They traded with you in lambs, rams, and goats.
The traders of Sheba and Raamah traded with you. They paid for your goods with the best spices, gold, and precious stones.
Haran, Canneh, Eden, and the traders of Sheba, along with Asshur and Chilmad, traded with you.
They traded with you in beautiful clothes, blue cloth, embroidered cloth, and carpets of richly colored yarn, all tied with cords and packed in cedar boxes. "
The ships of Tarshish carried your goods. You were full and very glorious in the heart of the seas.
Your rowers brought you into deep waters. The east wind broke you in the heart of the seas.

Your wealth, your goods, your merchandise, your sailors, your pilots, your repairers, your traders, all your soldiers, and everyone in your assembly will fall into the heart of the seas on the day you are destroyed. "
The shores will shake at the sound of your pilots' cry.
All who handle the oar, the sailors, and all the pilots of the sea will come down from their ships and stand on the shore.
They will raise their voices over you and cry bitterly. They will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
They will shave their heads for you and wear sackcloth. They will weep for you with bitter grief.
In their wailing they will take up a lament for you and mourn over you: 'Who was ever like Tyre, destroyed in the midst of the sea?' "
When your goods went out from the seas, you satisfied many nations. With your great wealth and trade, you enriched the kings of the earth.
Now you are broken by the seas in the depths of the waters. Your merchandise and all your company have fallen with you.
All who live on the coastlands are appalled at you. Their kings shudder with horror. Their faces are twisted in fear.
The merchants among the nations hiss at you. You have become a horror, and you will be no more forever."
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

“Son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: Your heart became proud, and you said, “I am a god. I sit on a throne of gods in the heart of the seas.” But you are only a man, not a god, and you have made your heart like the heart of a god.
Look, you are wiser than Daniel. No secret is hidden from you.
By your wisdom and understanding you have gained wealth for yourself and gathered gold and silver into your treasuries.
By your great skill in trade you have increased your wealth, and your heart has become proud because of your wealth.
Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: Because you have made your heart like the heart of a god,
I will bring foreigners against you, the most ruthless of nations. They will draw their swords against your beautiful wisdom and defile your splendor.
They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die a violent death in the heart of the seas.
Will you still say, “I am a god,” before your killers? You are a man, not a god, in the hands of those who wound you.
You will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of foreigners. I have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD.’”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, raise a lament for the king of Tyre and say to him, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: You were the model of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

You were in Eden, the garden of God. Every precious stone was your covering: ruby, topaz, diamond, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald. Your settings and mountings were made of gold. They were prepared on the day you were created.
You were an anointed guardian cherub. I placed you on God's holy mountain, and you walked among the fiery stones.
You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created until wrongdoing was found in you.
Through your many trades you were filled with violence, and you sinned. So I drove you in disgrace from God's mountain, and I destroyed you, O guardian cherub, from among the fiery stones.
Your heart became proud because of your beauty. You corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor. So I threw you to the earth and put you on display before kings.
By your many sins and dishonest trade you have defiled your sanctuaries. So I brought fire from within you, and it consumed you. I turned you to ashes on the earth in the sight of all who saw you.
All who knew you among the nations are appalled at you. You have come to a horrible end and will be no more forever.’”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, turn your attention to Sidon and prophesy against it.

Say, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: I am against you, Sidon, and I will show My glory among you. Then they will know that I am the LORD when I execute judgments against her and show My holiness through her.
I will send a plague into her and blood into her streets. The slain will fall in her midst by the sword that comes against her from every side. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
No longer will the house of Israel be hurt by thorns or briers from their neighbors who hate them. Then they will know that I am the Lord the LORD.’”

“This is what the Lord the LORD says: When I gather the house of Israel from the nations where they have been scattered, I will show My holiness among them in the sight of the nations. They will live in their own land, which I gave to My servant Jacob.

They will live there securely, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will live securely when I execute judgments on all their neighbors who treated them with contempt. Then they will know that I am the LORD their God.”
In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month, the word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, turn your face toward Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt." "
Speak and say that this is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Pharaoh, king of Egypt, you great crocodile lying among your rivers. You said the Nile was yours and that you made it yourself." "
I will put hooks in your jaws and make the fish in your rivers stick to your scales. I will pull you up out of your rivers, and all the fish will stick to your scales.

I will leave you in the desert, you and all the fish from your rivers. You will fall on the open field. You will not be gathered or picked up. I will give you as food to the wild animals and the birds of the sky.
Then all who live in Egypt will know that I am the LORD, because they were like a weak reed staff to the people of Israel.
When they took hold of you by the hand, you splintered and tore open their shoulders. When they leaned on you, you broke and made their hips shake." "
So this is what the Lord GOD says: I will bring a sword against you and cut off both people and animals from you.
The land of Egypt will become an empty wasteland. Then they will know that I am the LORD, because you claimed the Nile was yours and that you made it.
So I am against you and your rivers. I will make the land of Egypt a ruined, empty wasteland from Migdol to Syene, all the way to the border of Cush.
No person or animal will travel through it, and no one will live there for forty years.

I will make Egypt the most ruined land among ruined lands, and its cities will lie waste for forty years among ruined cities. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and spread them among the countries. "
For this is what the Lord GOD says: After forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples where they were scattered.
I will bring back the captives of Egypt and return them to the land of Pathros, their homeland. There they will be a lowly kingdom.
It will be the lowliest of kingdoms and will never again be greater than other nations. I will make it so small that it will not rule over other nations.
It will never again be a source of hope for the people of Israel. It will only remind them of their sin when they turn to Egypt for help. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD."
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, the word of the LORD came to me. "

Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made his army work very hard against Tyre. Every soldier's head became bald, and every shoulder was rubbed bare. But he and his army got no pay from Tyre for all that work. "

So this is what the Lord GOD says: I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. He will carry off its wealth, take its plunder, and seize its goods. That will be pay for his army.
I gave him Egypt as his pay for the work he did for Me, declares the Lord GOD.
On that day I will make Israel strong again, and I will open your mouth among them. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, prophesy and say that this is what the Lord the LORD says: Wail! Alas for that day!
For the day is near, the day of the LORD is near—a day of clouds, a time of trouble for the nations. "
A sword will come against Egypt, and terror will come upon Cush. When the slain fall in Egypt, her wealth will be carried away and her foundations torn down.
Cush, Put, Lydia, all Arabia, Libya, and the people of the covenant land will fall by the sword along with Egypt.
This is what the LORD says: Those who support Egypt will fall, and her proud strength will fail. From Migdol to Syene they will fall by the sword within her, declares the Lord the LORD.
They will be desolate among desolate lands, and their cities will lie among ruined cities.
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I set fire to Egypt and all her helpers are broken.
On that day messengers will go out from Me in ships to frighten Cush out of her feeling of safety. Anguish will come upon them on the day Egypt is judged, for it is surely coming. "
This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will put an end to the crowds of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
He and his people with him, the most ruthless of nations, will be brought in to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.
I will dry up the streams of the Nile and sell the land to evil men. I will lay waste the land and everything in it by the hand of foreigners. I, the LORD, have spoken.
This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will destroy the idols and put an end to the images in Memphis. There will no longer be a prince in Egypt, and I will put fear in the land of Egypt.
I will lay waste Pathros, set fire to Zoan, and carry out judgment on Thebes.
I will pour out My wrath on Pelusium, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the crowds of Thebes.
I will set fire to Egypt; Pelusium will writhe in anguish, Thebes will be torn open, and Memphis will be in distress every day.
The young men of On and Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and those cities will go into captivity.
In Tehaphnehes the day will grow dark when I break the yoke of Egypt there. Her proud strength will cease; she will be covered by a cloud, and her daughters will go into captivity.
So I will carry out judgments on Egypt, and they will know that I am the LORD."
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month, the word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. It has not been bound up for healing or wrapped in a bandage to make it strong enough to hold a sword. "

Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I will break his arms, both the strong one and the broken one, and I will make the sword fall from his hand.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.
I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put My sword in his hand, and I will break the arms of Pharaoh. He will groan before him like a wounded man.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall limp. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I put My sword into the hand of the king of Babylon and he uses it against the land of Egypt.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
On the first day of the third month in the eleventh year, the word of the the LORD came to me.
“Son of man, speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to his people: ‘Who are you like in your greatness?’ “
Look, Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches, a shady forest, and very tall. Its top reached up among thick branches.
Water made it grow, and the deep sea made it tall. Rivers flowed around where it was planted, and channels carried water to all the trees in the field.
So it grew taller than every tree in the field. Its branches spread out, and its boughs grew long because water was plentiful.
All the birds of the sky nested in its branches. All the wild animals gave birth under its boughs. Many nations lived in its shade.
It was beautiful in its greatness and in its long branches, because its roots reached down to plenty of water.
The cedars in God’s garden did not compare with it. The cypress trees did not match its branches. The plane trees were not like its boughs. No tree in God’s garden was as beautiful as it.
I made it beautiful by giving it many branches. All the trees of Eden in God’s garden were jealous of it. “
So this is what the Lord, the the LORD, says: Because you grew so tall and lifted your top among the thick branches, and because your heart became proud of your height,
I will hand it over to a powerful ruler among the nations. He will punish it for its wickedness. I have thrown it out.

Strangers, the cruel nations, cut it down and left it. Its branches fell on the mountains and in every valley. Its boughs broke and lay in all the riverbeds. All the peoples of the earth came out from under its shade and left it.
All the birds of the sky settled in its ruins, and all the wild animals lived among its branches.

This happened so that no tree growing by water would become proud of its height or lift its top among the thick branches, and so that no well-watered tree would stand tall on its own. They are all handed over to death, to the lower parts of the earth, among the people, to those who go down to the pit. “

This is what the Lord, the the LORD, says: On the day it went down to the grave, I made people mourn for it. I covered the deep sea over it and stopped its rivers. The many waters were held back. I made Lebanon mourn for it, and all the trees in the field fainted because of it.

I shook the nations with the sound of its fall when I sent it down to the grave with those who go down to the pit. Then all the trees of Eden—the best and finest of Lebanon, all that drink water—were comforted in the lower parts of the earth.
Its allies, who had lived in its shade among the nations, also went down to the grave with it, to those killed by the sword.

Who else are you like in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the lower parts of the earth. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his people, declares the Lord, the the LORD.”
In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, raise a lament for Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him, You are like a lion among the nations; you are like a monster in the seas. You thrash about in your rivers, churn the water with your feet, and muddy their streams.
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will spread My net over you with a crowd of many peoples, and they will haul you up in My dragnet.
"I will throw you on the land and hurl you on the open field. I will let all the birds of the sky settle on you, and I will let all the beasts of the earth feed on you.
"I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains.
"I will water the land with your blood as far as the mountains, and the streams will be filled with you.
"When I snuff you out, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light.
"All the shining lights in the heavens I will darken over you, and I will bring darkness on your land, declares the Lord the LORD.
"I will trouble the hearts of many peoples when I bring your ruin among the nations, in lands you have not known.

"I will make many peoples appalled at you, and their kings will shudder with horror because of you when I brandish My sword before them. On the day of your fall, each man will tremble for his own life every moment.
"For this is what the Lord the LORD says: The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you.
"I will bring down your hordes with the swords of warriors, the most ruthless of nations. They will plunder the pride of Egypt, and all her hordes will be wiped out.
"I will destroy all her livestock near the many waters, and no human foot or animal hoof will stir them up again.
"Then I will let her waters calm down and make her rivers flow like oil, declares the Lord the LORD.
"When I make the land of Egypt a desolation, stripped of everything in it, when I strike down all who live there, then they will know that I am the LORD.
"This is a lament, and the daughters of the nations will chant it. They will chant it over Egypt and over all her hordes, declares the Lord the LORD."
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, wail over the hordes of Egypt and send her down, along with the daughters of mighty nations, to the depths of the earth, to those who go down to the pit.
"Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down and lie with the uncircumcised.
"They will fall among those slain by the sword. The sword is drawn; drag her away with all her hordes.
"From within Sheol, the mighty leaders, along with his allies, will speak to him: "'They have gone down and lie with the uncircumcised, slain by the sword.'
"Assyria is there with all her company; her graves are all around her. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword.
"Her graves are placed in the depths of the pit, and her company surrounds her grave. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword, those who once spread terror in the land of the living.

"Elam is there with all her hordes around her grave. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword. They went down uncircumcised to the lower parts of the earth, those who spread their terror in the land of the living. They bear their shame with those who go down to the pit.

"A bed is made for her among the slain, with all her hordes. Her graves are all around her. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because their terror was spread in the land of the living. They bear their shame with those who go down to the pit; they are placed among the slain.
"Meshech and Tubal are there with all their hordes. Their graves are all around them. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because they spread their terror in the land of the living.

"They do not lie with the fallen warriors of the uncircumcised, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war. They placed their swords under their heads, but their sins rest on their bones, because they terrified the mighty in the land of the living.
"But you will be broken and lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword.
"Edom is there, her kings and all her leaders, who in their strength were laid among those slain by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised, with those who go down to the pit.

"All the princes of the north are there, and all the Sidonians, who went down in shame with the slain, because of the terror they caused by their might. They lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword and bear their shame with those who go down to the pit.
"Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his hordes—Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the Lord the LORD.
"For I have put his terror in the land of the living, and he will be laid among the uncircumcised with those slain by the sword—Pharaoh and all his hordes, declares the Lord the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, speak to your people and tell them: 'When I bring the sword against a land, the people of that land choose one of their men and make him their watchman.
If he sees the sword coming against the land and blows the trumpet to warn the people,
then if anyone hears the trumpet but does not listen to the warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head.
He heard the trumpet but did not listen to the warning; his blood will be on himself. But if he had listened to the warning, he would have saved his life.

But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet, so that the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes one of them, that person is taken away in his sin, but I will hold the watchman accountable for his blood.
"Now, son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; so hear the word I speak and give them warning from Me.

When I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die,' and you do not warn him or speak out to turn him from his wicked way, then that wicked man will die in his sin, and I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you warn the wicked man to turn from his way, and he does not turn, he will die in his sin, but you will have saved your life.
"Son of man, say to the house of Israel: 'You say, "Our offenses and sins weigh us down, and we are wasting away because of them. How can we live?"'

Say to them: 'As surely as I live, declares the Lord the LORD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked turn from their ways and live. Turn! Turn from your evil ways! Why will you die, house of Israel?'

"Therefore, son of man, say to your people: 'The righteousness of a righteous man will not save him on the day he sins, and the wickedness of a wicked man will not cause him to stumble on the day he turns from his wickedness. Nor will a righteous man be able to live by his righteousness on the day he sins.'
If I tell a righteous man that he will surely live, but he trusts in his righteousness and does wrong, then none of his righteous acts will be remembered; he will die for the wrong he has done.
And if I say to the wicked man, 'You will surely die,' but he turns from his sin and does what is just and right—
if he returns what he took as a pledge, pays back what he stole, and follows the laws that lead to life without doing wrong, he will surely live; he will not die.
None of the sins he has committed will be remembered against him. He has done what is just and right; he will surely live.
Yet your people say, 'The way of the Lord is not just.' But it is their own way that is not just.
If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, he will die for it.
And if a wicked man turns from his wickedness and does what is just and right, he will live because of it.
Yet you say, 'The way of the Lord is not just.' But I will judge each of you according to your own ways, house of Israel."
In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a survivor from Jerusalem came to me and said, "The city has been struck down."
Now the evening before the survivor arrived, the hand of the LORD had been upon me, and He opened my mouth. So when the man came to me in the morning, my mouth was opened, and I was no longer silent.
The word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, the people living in the ruins in the land of Israel are saying, 'Abraham was only one man, yet he inherited the land. But we are many; surely the land has been given to us as our possession.'
Therefore tell them: This is what the Lord the LORD says: 'You eat meat with the blood still in it, you look to your idols, and you shed blood. Should you then possess the land?
You rely on your swords, you do detestable things, and each of you defiles his neighbor's wife. Should you then possess the land?'

Tell them that this is what the Lord the LORD says: 'As surely as I live, those in the ruins will fall by the sword; those in the open country I will give to the wild animals to be devoured; and those in the forts and caves will die of plague.
I will make the land a desolate waste, and her proud strength will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will be desolate, with no one to pass through.
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I make the land a desolate waste because of all the detestable things they have done.'"
"As for you, son of man, your people are talking about you by the walls and in the doorways of their houses. They say to one another, 'Come and hear the word that comes from the LORD.'
They come to you as a crowd, and they sit before you as My people. They hear your words, but they do not do them. With their mouths they express love, but their hearts chase after dishonest gain.
Indeed, to them you are like a singer with a beautiful voice who plays an instrument well. They hear your words, but they do not put them into practice.
When all this happens—and it surely will—then they will know that a prophet has been among them."
The word of the the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord the the LORD says: How terrible for the shepherds of Israel who only feed themselves! Should not the shepherds feed the flock?
You eat the fat, wear the wool, and slaughter the fattened sheep, but you do not feed the flock.
You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bandaged the injured, brought back the strays, or searched for the lost. Instead, you have ruled them with force and cruelty.
So they were scattered because there was no shepherd, and when they were scattered they became food for all the wild animals.
My flock strayed on all the mountains and every high hill. They were scattered over the whole earth, and no one searched or looked for them.
"Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the the LORD:

As surely as I live, declares the Lord the the LORD, because My flock has no shepherd and has become prey and food for every wild animal, and because My shepherds did not search for My flock but fed themselves instead of My flock,
therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the the LORD:

This is what the Lord the the LORD says: Look, I am against the shepherds, and I will hold them responsible for My flock. I will remove them from tending the flock, so they may no longer feed themselves. I will rescue My flock from their mouths, and it will no longer be food for them.
"For this is what the Lord the the LORD says: Look, I Myself will search for My flock and look for them.
As a shepherd looks for his scattered sheep when he is among the flock, so I will look for My flock. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of clouds and darkness.

I will bring them out from the nations, gather them from the countries, and bring them into their own land. I will pasture them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys, and in all the places where people live.

I will feed them in good pasture, and the high mountains of Israel will be their grazing land. There they will lie down in good grazing land; they will feed in rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.
I will tend My flock and make them lie down, declares the Lord the the LORD.
I will seek the lost, bring back the strays, bandage the broken, and strengthen the weak; but the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed them with justice.
"As for you, My flock, this is what the Lord the the LORD says: Look, I will judge between one sheep and another, between rams and goats.

Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of your pasture with your feet? Is it not enough for you to drink the clear water? Must you also muddy the rest with your feet?
Why then must My flock feed on what your feet have trampled, and drink what your feet have muddied?
"Therefore, this is what the Lord the the LORD says: Look, I will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.
Because you shove with your side and shoulder and butt all the weak sheep with your horns until you have scattered them away,
I will save My flock, and they will no longer be prey. I will judge between one sheep and another.
"I will appoint over them one shepherd, My servant David, and he will feed them. He will feed them and be their shepherd.
I, the the LORD, will be their God, and My servant David will be a prince among them. I, the the LORD, have spoken.
I will make with them a covenant of peace and remove the dangerous animals from the land, so they may live safely in the wilderness and sleep in the forests.
I will make them and the places around My hill a blessing. I will send down showers in their season—showers of blessing.

The trees of the field will yield their fruit, and the land will yield its produce. They will live safely on their land, and they will know that I am the the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hands of those who enslaved them.
They will no longer be prey for the nations, and the animals of the earth will not devour them. They will live in safety, and no one will frighten them.
I will plant for them a famous garden, so they will no longer be victims of famine in the land or bear the shame of the nations.
Then they will know that I am the the LORD their God, and that they are My people, the house of Israel, declares the Lord the the LORD.
You are My flock, the sheep of My pasture. You are people, and I am your God, declares the Lord the the LORD."
The word of the the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, oppose Mount Seir and prophesy against it.
Say to it, 'This is what the Lord the the LORD says: I am against you, Mount Seir. I will punish you and make you a wasteland and a ruin.
I will destroy your cities, and you will become a wasteland. Then you will know that I am the the LORD.
"'Because you have hated Israel for a long time and handed the Israelites over to the sword when they were in trouble, at the time of their final punishment,
as surely as I live, declares the Lord the the LORD, I will hand you over to bloodshed, and bloodshed will follow you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will follow you.
"'I will make Mount Seir a wasteland and a ruin, and I will remove everyone who travels through it.
I will fill its mountains with the dead. Those killed by the sword will fall on your hills, in your valleys, and in all your ravines.
I will make you a lasting ruin, and your cities will not be lived in. Then you will know that I am the the LORD.
"'Because you said, "These two nations and these two lands will be mine, and I will take them over," even though the the LORD was there,

as surely as I live, declares the Lord the the LORD, I will treat you the way your anger and jealousy deserve, which you showed in your hatred of them. I will make Myself known among them when I judge you.
Then you will know that I, the the LORD, have heard all the insults you spoke against the mountains of Israel. You said, "They are ruined and given to us to destroy."
You bragged against Me with your mouth and piled up your words against Me. I heard it.
"'This is what the Lord the the LORD says: When the whole world rejoices, I will make you a wasteland.

Just as you rejoiced over Israel's inheritance because it was ruined, I will do the same to you. You will become a wasteland, Mount Seir, and all of Edom. Then they will know that I am the the LORD.'"
“You, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel and say, ‘Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the the LORD.’
This is what the Lord the LORD says: Because the enemy said about you, ‘Aha! The old high places are ours now,’

therefore prophesy and say, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: Because they ruined you and swallowed you up from every side, to become a possession for the rest of the nations, and you have become the talk and slander of the people.’

Therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord the LORD: This is what the Lord the LORD says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the ruined and abandoned cities that have become plunder and mockery to the rest of the nations around them.

Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: Surely in the fire of My jealousy I have spoken against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, who took My land for themselves as a possession with wholehearted joy and deep contempt, so that its pastureland became plunder.

“Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: Look, I have spoken in My wrath and jealousy because you have borne the insults of the nations.’
Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: I have raised My hand in an oath that the nations around you will bear their own shame.
But you, mountains of Israel, will grow branches and bear fruit for My people Israel, for they will soon come home.
“For look, I am for you, and I will turn to you, and you will be plowed and planted.
I will multiply people on you, all the house of Israel, all of it. The cities will be lived in, and the ruins will be rebuilt.

I will multiply on you people and animals; they will increase and be fruitful. I will make you inhabited as in the past, and I will make you better than before. Then you will know that I am the the LORD.
I will let My people Israel walk on you. They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance, and you will no longer make them lose their children.
“This is what the Lord the LORD says: Because they say to you, ‘You are a devourer of people and have robbed your nation of children,’
therefore you will no longer devour people or rob your nation of children, declares the Lord the LORD.
I will no longer let you hear the insults of the nations, and you will no longer bear the shame of the peoples. You will no longer make your nation stumble, declares the Lord the LORD.”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, when the house of Israel lived in their own land, they defiled it by their ways and their actions. Their way of life in My sight was like the uncleanness of a woman during her period.
So I poured out My wrath on them because of the blood they had shed on the land and because they had defiled it with their idols.
I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the countries. I judged them according to their ways and actions.
“Wherever they went among the nations, they dishonored My holy name, because people said about them, ‘These are the people of the the LORD, yet they had to leave His land.’
But I had concern for My holy name, which the house of Israel had dishonored among the nations where they had gone.

“Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: It is not for your sake, house of Israel, that I am about to act, but for the sake of My holy name, which you have dishonored among the nations where you have gone.’

I will make My great name holy, which has been dishonored among the nations—the name you dishonored among them. Then the nations will know that I am the the LORD, declares the Lord the LORD, when I show My holiness through you before their eyes.
“For I will take you from the nations and gather you from all the countries and bring you into your own land.
I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. I will cleanse you from all your impurity and from all your idols.
I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your body and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put My Spirit within you and make you follow My rules and carefully obey My laws.
You will live in the land I gave your fathers. You will be My people, and I will be your God.
“I will save you from all your uncleanness. I will call for the grain and make it plentiful, and I will not bring famine on you.
I will also make the fruit of the trees and the crops of the field plentiful, so that you will never again suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.
Then you will remember your evil ways and your deeds that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves for your sins and detestable practices.
It is not for your sake that I am about to act, declares the Lord the LORD. Let that be known to you. Be ashamed and disgraced because of your ways, house of Israel.”
“This is what the Lord the LORD says: On the day I cleanse you from all your sins, I will cause the cities to be inhabited and the ruins to be rebuilt.
The ruined land will be farmed instead of lying empty in the sight of all who pass by.
They will say, ‘This land that was ruined has become like the garden of Eden. The cities that were ruined, empty, and destroyed are now fortified and inhabited.’
Then the nations around you that remain will know that I, the the LORD, have rebuilt what was destroyed and planted what was ruined. I, the the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.”
“This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will also let the house of Israel ask Me to do this for them: I will increase their number like a flock.
Like the sacred flock, like the flock of Jerusalem at her festivals, so the ruined cities will be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the the LORD.”
The LORD's power came over me. He took me away by His Spirit and set me down in the middle of a valley full of bones.
He led me around among them on every side. There were very many bones on the valley floor, and they were very dry.
He asked me, "Son of Man, can these bones live?" I answered, "Lord the LORD, You know."
Then He said to me, "Prophesy over these bones and say to them, 'Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.'"
Then He said, "This is what the Lord the LORD says to these bones: 'I will put breath into you, and you will live.'"
He said, "I will attach tendons to you, put flesh on you, and cover you with skin. Then I will put breath in you, and you will live. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
So I prophesied as I was commanded. While I was prophesying, there was a noise—a rattling sound. The bones came together, bone to bone.
I looked, and I saw tendons and flesh on them, and skin covered them. But there was no breath in them.

Then He said to me, "Prophesy to the breath. Prophesy, Son of Man, and say to the breath, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, that they may live.'"
So I prophesied as He commanded me. Breath entered them, and they came to life. They stood up on their feet—a very large army.
Then He said to me, "Son of Man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. They say their bones are dried up, their hope is gone, and they are finished."
So prophesy and say to them, "This is what the Lord the LORD says: My people, I am going to open your graves and bring you up from them. I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up from them, My people.
I will put My Spirit in you, and you will live. I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken and done it."
The word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of Man, take one stick and write on it, 'For Judah and the Israelites joined to him.' Then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph—the stick of Ephraim—and all the house of Israel joined to him.'
Join the two sticks together so they become one in your hand."
"When your people ask you what this means, say to them, "This is what the Lord the LORD says:

I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim's hand, along with the tribes of Israel joined to him, and put them with the stick of Judah. I will make them one stick, and they will be one in My hand.
The sticks you write on will be in your hand for them to see."

"Then say to them, "This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will take the Israelites out from the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from every side and bring them back to their own land.
I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. One king will rule over all of them. They will no longer be two nations, and they will never again be divided into two kingdoms.

They will no longer make themselves unclean with their idols, their disgusting images, or any of their sins. I will save them from all the places where they sinned, and I will make them clean. They will be My people, and I will be their God.
My servant David will be their king. They will all have one shepherd. They will follow My laws, keep My rules, and do them.

"They will live in the land I gave to My servant Jacob, where your ancestors lived. They and their children and their grandchildren will live there forever. My servant David will be their prince forever.
I will make a peace agreement with them. It will last forever. I will settle them and make them many. I will put My holy place among them forever.
My dwelling place will be with them. I will be their God, and they will be My people.
Then the nations will know that I, the LORD, make Israel holy, when My holy place is among them forever."
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, oppose Gog, the ruler of the land of Magog and chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. Prophesy against him.
Say: This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

I will turn you around and drag you out with hooks in your jaws. I will bring you out with your whole army—horses and horsemen, all wearing full armor, a huge crowd with large and small shields, all holding swords.
Persia, Cush, and Put will be with them, all with shields and helmets.
Gomer and all its troops; Beth Togarmah from the far north with all its troops—many peoples are with you.
"Get ready. Be prepared—you and all your hordes gathered around you. You will be their guard.

After many days you will be called to account. In the last years you will come into a land brought back from war, gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel. That land had long been ruined, but its people were brought out from the nations, and now they live in safety.
You and all your troops and many peoples with you will go up like a storm. You will be like a cloud covering the land.
"This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: On that day, thoughts will come into your mind, and you will devise an evil plan.
You will say that you are going up against a land of villages without walls, to attack a peaceful and unsuspecting people—all living without walls, gates, or bars.
You will plunder and loot, attacking ruined places that are now lived in and a people gathered from the nations, who have livestock and goods and live at the center of the land.

"Sheba, Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish and all its towns will ask you if you have come to plunder, if you have gathered your hordes to carry off silver and gold, to take livestock and goods, and to seize a great spoil.
Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog: This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: On that day, when My people Israel are living safely, will you not know?
You will come from your place in the far north, you and many peoples with you, all riding horses—a huge horde and mighty army.

You will advance against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. In the last days, Gog, I will bring you against My land so the nations may know Me when I show My holiness through you before their eyes.

"This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: Are you not the one I spoke of long ago through My servants the prophets of Israel? In those days they prophesied for years that I would bring you against them.
On that day, when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord, the LORD, My wrath will rise in My anger.
In My zeal and fiery wrath I declare that on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.

"The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the beasts of the field, every creeping thing that moves on the ground, and every person on the face of the earth will tremble at My presence. The mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground.
I will call for a sword against Gog on all My mountains, declares the Lord, the LORD. Everyone will turn his sword against his brother.
I will judge him with plague and bloodshed. I will rain down on him and on his troops and on the many peoples with him a flood of rain, hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
I will show My greatness and holiness and make Myself known in the sight of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
"You, son of man, prophesy against Gog. Tell him this is what the LORD says: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you around and drag you along. I will bring you up from the far north and lead you against the mountains of Israel.
"I will knock your bow out of your left hand and make your arrows fall from your right hand.
You will fall on the mountains of Israel—you and all your troops and the nations with you. I will give you to birds of prey and wild animals to be eaten.
You will fall in the open field, because I have spoken," declares the LORD.
"I will send fire on Magog and on those who live safely on the coasts. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
I will make My holy name known among My people Israel. I will no longer let My holy name be treated as unclean. The nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
It is coming, and it will happen. That is the day I spoke about," declares the LORD.

"Then the people who live in the cities of Israel will go out and burn the weapons for fuel. They will burn shields, armor, bows, arrows, clubs, and spears. They will use them for fire for seven years.

They will not need to gather wood from the fields or cut it from the forests, because they will burn the weapons. They will take the loot of those who looted them and rob those who robbed them," declares the LORD.

"On that day I will give Gog a grave in Israel, in the Valley of the Travelers east of the sea. It will block those who travel through, because Gog and all his crowd will be buried there. People will call it the Valley of Hamon Gog.
"For seven months the people of Israel will bury them to make the land clean.
All the people of the land will help bury them. It will bring them honor on the day I show My glory," declares the LORD.
"They will choose men who travel through the land all the time to bury the bodies left on the ground, to make the land clean. After seven months, they will search.
As they travel, if anyone sees a human bone, he will set up a marker by it until the buriers bury it in the Valley of Hamon Gog.
There will also be a city named Hamonah. In this way they will make the land clean."

"You, son of man, this is what the LORD says: Call to every kind of bird and every wild animal to come together for the feast I am making for you—a huge feast on the mountains of Israel. You will eat meat and drink blood.
"You will eat the meat of strong men and drink the blood of rulers—of rams, lambs, goats, and bulls, all of them fat animals from Bashan.
You will eat fat until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk, at the feast I am making for you.
At My table you will be filled with horses, chariots, strong men, and all kinds of warriors," declares the LORD.
"I will show My glory among the nations. All the nations will see the judgment I carried out and the power I used against them.
From that day on, the people of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God.
"The nations will know that Israel was taken away because of its sin. They turned against Me, so I hid My face from them and handed them over to their enemies. They all died by the sword.
I treated them the way their uncleanness and sins deserved, and I hid My face from them.
"So this is what the LORD says: Now I will bring Jacob back from captivity and have mercy on all Israel. I will be jealous for My holy name.
They will forget their shame and all the wrong they did against Me when they live safely in their own land with no one to scare them.
When I bring them back from the nations and gather them from the lands of their enemies, I will show My holiness through them in front of many nations.
"Then they will know that I am the LORD their God. I sent them into exile among the nations, and then I gathered them back to their own land. I will not leave any of them among the nations.
I will no longer hide My face from them, because I will pour out My Spirit on the people of Israel," declares the LORD.

In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the start of the year, on the tenth day of the month, fourteen years after Jerusalem was struck down, on that very day the hand of the the LORD was on me, and He brought me there.
In visions from God He brought me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain. On its south side was a building like a city.
He brought me there, and I saw a man whose look was like bronze. He stood in the gateway with a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand.

The man said to me, "Son of man, look with your eyes, listen with your ears, and pay attention to everything I show you. You have been brought here so I can show it to you. Tell the people of Israel everything you see."

There was a wall all around the temple area. The measuring rod in the man's hand was six cubits long. Each cubit was a cubit plus a handbreadth. He measured the wall to be one rod thick and one rod high.
Then he went to the gate that faced east and climbed its steps. He measured the threshold of the gate to be one rod deep, and the other threshold to be one rod deep.
Each gate chamber was one rod long and one rod wide, and the space between the chambers was five cubits. The threshold of the gate by the portico facing the temple was one rod deep.
Then he measured the portico of the gate facing the temple: one rod.
He measured the portico of the gate to be eight cubits, and its jambs to be two cubits. The portico faced the temple.
Inside the east gate were three chambers on each side. All three had the same measurements, and the gateposts on either side had the same measurements too.
He measured the width of the gateway to be ten cubits, and the length of the gateway to be thirteen cubits.
In front of the chambers was a ledge one cubit wide, and the chambers were six cubits square. The space between the chambers was one cubit.
Then he measured the gateway from the roof of one chamber to the roof of the opposite chamber: twenty-five cubits. The entrances faced each other.
He measured the gateposts to be sixty cubits, and the courtyard gatepost ran all around.
The distance from the front of the gateway at the entrance to the inner portico was fifty cubits.
The gate chambers and their side pillars had beveled windows all around. The porticoes also had windows all around on the inside, and each pillar was decorated with palm trees.
Then he brought me into the outer courtyard. There were chambers and a pavement laid out all around the courtyard. Thirty chambers faced the pavement.
The pavement ran along the gates and matched the length of the gates. This was the lower pavement.
Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gateway to the front of the inner court: one hundred cubits, on the east side and on the north.
He also measured the length and width of the gateway of the outer court that faced north.
Its three chambers on each side, its gateposts, and its portico had the same measurements as the first gate: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its windows, portico, and palm trees had the same measurements as those of the gate facing east. Seven steps led up to it, and its portico was in front of them.
There was a gate to the inner court facing the north gate, just as there was to the east. He measured the distance from gate to gate: one hundred cubits.
Then he led me to the south side, and I saw a gate facing south. He measured its gateposts and portico, and they had the same measurements as the others.
Both the gate and its portico had windows all around, like the other windows. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Seven steps led up to it, and its portico was in front of them. It had palm trees on its gateposts, one on each side.
The inner court also had a gate facing south, and he measured the distance from gate to gate toward the south: one hundred cubits.
Then he brought me to the inner court through the south gate, and he measured the south gate; it had the same measurements as the others.
Its chambers, gateposts, and portico had the same measurements as the others. Both it and its portico had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
The porticoes around the inner court were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer court, and palm trees decorated its gateposts. Eight steps led up to it.
Then he brought me to the inner court on the east side, and he measured the gate; it had the same measurements as the others.
Its chambers, gateposts, and portico had the same measurements as the others. Both it and its portico had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer court, and it had palm trees on its gateposts on each side. Eight steps led up to it.
Then he brought me to the north gate and measured it; it had the same measurements as the others.
Its chambers, gateposts, and portico had the same measurements as the others. Both it and its portico had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer court, and it had palm trees on its gateposts on each side. Eight steps led up to it.
There was a chamber with a doorway by the gateposts of the gates, where the burnt offering was to be washed.
Inside the portico of the gate were two tables on each side, where the burnt offering, sin offering, and guilt offering were to be slaughtered.
Outside, on the north side of the entrance to the outer court, there were two tables, and on the other side of the portico of the gate there were two tables.
So there were four tables on each side of the gateway, a total of eight tables, on which the sacrifices were to be slaughtered.

There were four tables of cut stone for the burnt offering, each one and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one cubit high. On them were placed the utensils used to slaughter the burnt offering and the other sacrifices.
The double-pronged hooks, each a handbreadth long, were fastened all around the inside of the room. And the flesh of the offering was to be placed on the tables.
Outside the inner gate were chambers for the singers in the inner court, one beside the north gate, facing south, and one beside the south gate, facing north.
The man said to me, "This chamber that faces south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple,
and the chamber that faces north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who alone among the sons of Levi may approach the the LORD to minister before Him."
Then he measured the court: one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, square, with the altar in front of the temple.
Then he brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the jambs of the portico: five cubits on either side. The width of the gateway was three cubits on each side.
The length of the portico was twenty cubits, and its width was eleven cubits. It was reached by steps, and there were pillars beside the jambs, one on each side.
Then the man brought me into the outer sanctuary and measured the side pillars. They were six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other. The entrance was ten cubits wide.
The entrance was ten cubits long, with walls five cubits thick on each side. He also measured the outer sanctuary: forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
He went farther in and measured the jambs of the entrance. They were two cubits wide. The entrance itself was six cubits wide, and each side wall was seven cubits wide.
Then he measured the room next to the inner sanctuary: twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. He said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place.”
Next he measured the temple wall: six cubits thick. Each side room around the temple was four cubits wide.

The side rooms were stacked in three levels, with thirty rooms on each level. Ledges ran all around the temple wall to support the side rooms, so their supports would not be built into the temple wall itself.
The side rooms grew wider at each level because the building around the temple rose in stages. So the upper rooms were wider than the lower ones.
I saw that the temple had a raised base all around it. This base formed the foundation for the side rooms, and it was six cubits high, the full length of a measuring rod.
The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick. There was an open space between the temple's side rooms and the outer chambers.
This open space was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
The side rooms opened into this space. One door faced north and another faced south. The open space was five cubits wide all around.
The building facing the temple courtyard on the west was seventy cubits wide and ninety cubits long. Its walls were five cubits thick all around.
Then he measured the temple: one hundred cubits long. The temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also one hundred cubits long.
