The temple courtyard on the east, including the temple, was one hundred cubits wide.
He also measured the building facing the open area on the west, including its galleries on both sides: one hundred cubits. This included the inner temple and the porches of the courtyard.
The thresholds, the windows, and the galleries around all three sides had wood paneling all around. The floor was wood from the threshold to the windows, and the windows were covered.
Measurements were taken all around, from above the door to the inner sanctuary and to the outside.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the walls. A palm tree stood between each pair of cherubim, and each cherub had two faces.
On one side of a palm tree was a human face, and on the other side was a lion's face. This pattern covered the whole temple.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved from the floor to above the entrance and on the wall of the sanctuary.
The outer sanctuary had square doorposts. The front of the sanctuary had the same appearance as the inner sanctuary.
The altar was made of wood. It was three cubits high and two cubits square. Its corners, base, and sides were wood. He said to me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.”
The outer sanctuary and the inner sanctuary each had double doors.
Each door had two panels. There were two panels for one door and two for the other.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the outer sanctuary, just as they were on the walls. There was a wooden canopy over the front of the outside porch.
The portico had windows with frames and palm trees on both sides. The side rooms of the temple also had canopies.
The man led me out through the north gate into the outer courtyard. Then he brought me to the rooms that faced the separate area and the building on the north side.
That space was one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
The upper rooms were set back from the lower ones, making three levels. They faced the twenty cubits of the inner courtyard and the pavement of the outer courtyard.
In front of the rooms was a walkway ten cubits wide, with an entrance one cubit wide. Their doors faced north.
The upper rooms were smaller because the walkways took more space from them than from the lower and middle rooms.
The rooms had three levels and no pillars like the courtyard pillars, so the upper rooms were set back more than the lower and middle rooms.
An outer wall in front of the rooms was fifty cubits long. It ran along the rooms toward the outer courtyard.
The rooms facing the outer courtyard were fifty cubits long, while the rooms facing the temple were one hundred cubits long.
Below these rooms was an entrance on the east side, used when entering from the outer courtyard.
In the wall of the outer courtyard on the east side, in front of the separate area and the building, there were rooms.
A walkway ran in front of them, just like the one in front of the north rooms. They had the same length and width, and their exits, plans, and doors were the same.
Like the doors of the south rooms, there was a door at the start of the walkway. It faced the garden wall on the east side as people entered.

Then he said to me, "The north rooms and the south rooms that face the separate area are holy rooms. The priests who serve near the LORD will eat the most holy offerings there. They will also place the most holy offerings there, along with the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, because the place is holy."

When the priests enter, they must not leave the holy area for the outer courtyard. They must leave the holy clothes they serve in there, because those clothes are holy. Then they must put on other clothes before they go near the people.
After he finished measuring the inner temple, he brought me out through the east gate and measured all around.
He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds.
He measured the north side: five hundred reeds.
He measured the south side: five hundred reeds.
He measured the west side: five hundred reeds.
He measured the whole area on all four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred reeds long and five hundred reeds wide, to separate the holy place from the common place.
Then he brought me to the gate that faces east.
I saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice sounded like rushing water, and the earth shone with His glory.
The vision I saw was like the one I had seen when He came to destroy the city. It was also like the vision I saw by the Kebar River. I fell facedown.
The glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east.
The Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
A man stood beside me, and I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple.

He said to me, “Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place for the soles of My feet. I will live among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel and their kings must never again defile My holy name with their unfaithfulness or with the dead bodies of their kings on their high places.

When they put their threshold next to My threshold and their doorposts beside My doorposts, with only a wall between Me and them, they defiled My holy name by the detestable things they did. So I destroyed them in My anger.
Now let them keep their unfaithfulness and the dead bodies of their kings far from Me, and I will live among them forever.”
“Son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel so they will be ashamed of their sins. Let them measure its design.

If they are ashamed of all they have done, show them the design of the temple—its layout, exits, and entrances, and its whole design. Tell them all its rules and forms, and write them down before their eyes so they will keep its whole design and all its rules and do them.
This is the law of the temple: The whole area around it on top of the mountain is most holy. This is the law of the temple.”

These are the measurements of the altar in cubits (the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth): Its base shall be a cubit high and a cubit wide, with a rim around its edge of one span. This is the height of the altar.
From the base on the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the width one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge shall be four cubits, and the width one cubit.
The altar hearth shall be four cubits high, with four horns projecting upward from the hearth.
The altar hearth shall be square, twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide.
The ledge shall be square, fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, with a rim around it of half a cubit and a base of a cubit all around. Its steps shall face east.

He said to me, “Son of man, this is what the Lord the LORD says: These are the statutes for the altar on the day it is built, so that burnt offerings may be offered on it and blood may be sprinkled on it.
You are to give a young bull as a sin offering to the Levitical priests of the family of Zadok, who approach Me to minister before Me, declares the Lord the LORD.
You shall take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and all around the rim. Thus you shall cleanse the altar and make atonement for it.
Then take the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the designated place of the temple, outside the sanctuary.
On the second day you are to present an unblemished male goat as a sin offering, and they shall purify the altar just as they purified it with the bull.
When you have finished the sin offering, you are to present an unblemished young bull and an unblemished ram from the flock.
You shall present them before the LORD, and the priests shall sprinkle salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
For seven days you are to provide a male goat daily for a sin offering; also provide an unblemished young bull and an unblemished ram from the flock.
For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar and cleanse it; thus they shall consecrate it.
When these days are complete, on the eighth day and thereafter, the priests shall offer your burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar. Then I will accept you, declares the Lord the LORD.”
He brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east, and it was shut.
The LORD said to me, “This gate will stay shut. It will not be opened, and no one will enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, came in through it. So it will stay shut.”
Only the prince may sit there to eat bread before the LORD. He will enter through the porch of the gate and leave the same way.
He brought me to the front of the house through the north gate. I saw that the glory of the LORD filled the LORD’s house, and I fell facedown.

The LORD said to me, “Son of man, pay attention. Look with your eyes and listen with your ears to everything I tell you about all the rules and laws of the LORD’s house. Pay close attention to who may enter the house and to all the ways out of the sanctuary.”
“Say to the stubborn house of Israel, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: You have gone too far with all your terrible sins, house of Israel.
You let foreigners who were not circumcised in heart or body into My sanctuary, and they made My house unclean. You offered My food—fat and blood—and broke My covenant with all your terrible sins.
You did not take care of My holy things. Instead, you put others in charge of My sanctuary for your own benefit.’
‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: No foreigner who is not circumcised in heart or body may enter My sanctuary—not even a foreigner living among the Israelites.’”
But the Levites who wandered away from Me when Israel went astray after their idols will be punished for their sin.

They can still serve in My sanctuary. They can guard the gates of the house and work in the house. They will slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people and stand before them to serve them.
Because they served the people in front of their idols and led Israel into sin, I swore an oath against them, and they will be punished for their sin, says the Lord the LORD.
They must not come near Me to serve as priests or come near any of My holy things, especially the most holy things. They must be disgraced and punished for the terrible things they did.
I will put them in charge of all the work in the house and everything that needs to be done there.

But the priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of My sanctuary when Israel went astray, will come near to serve Me. They will stand before Me to offer the fat and the blood, says the Lord the LORD.
They will enter My sanctuary and come near My table to serve Me, and they will keep My rules.
When they enter the inner courtyard, they must wear linen clothes. They must not wear wool while they serve at the gates of the inner courtyard or inside the house.
They must wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They must not wear anything that makes them sweat.

When they go out to the outer courtyard to the people, they must take off the clothes they served in and leave them in the holy rooms. They must put on other clothes so they do not make the people holy with their clothes.
They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long. They must keep their hair neatly trimmed.
No priest may drink wine when he enters the inner courtyard.
They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman. They may marry only a virgin from the family of Israel, or a widow of a priest.
They must teach My people the difference between what is holy and what is common, and between what is clean and what is unclean.
When there is a disagreement, they must stand and judge it by My laws. They must follow My instructions and My rules. They must keep My special days holy and respect My Sabbaths.
A priest must not make himself unclean by going near a dead person, unless it is his father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or an unmarried sister. For these, he may become unclean.
After he is made clean again, he must wait seven days.
On the day he goes into the inner courtyard of the sanctuary to serve, he must offer his sin offering, says the Lord the LORD.
The LORD will be their inheritance; I am their inheritance. You must not give them any land in Israel, because I am their share.
They may eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering. Everything set apart to the LORD in Israel will belong to them.
The first of all firstfruits and every contribution from all your gifts will belong to the priests. You must also give the priest the first of your dough so a blessing can rest on your house.
The priests must not eat any bird or animal that died on its own or was torn apart by wild animals.
When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you are to set aside a holy portion for the LORD. It will be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. This whole area will be holy.
Inside it, there will be a square space for the holy place, 500 cubits by 500 cubits, with 50 cubits of open land around it.
From this measured area, you are to measure off 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. The holy place, the Most Holy Place, will be there.
This holy portion of the land will belong to the priests who serve in the holy place and come near to serve the LORD. It will be a place for their houses and a holy area for the holy place.
The Levites who serve in the temple will receive an area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. It will be their land to live in, with twenty rooms.
You are to give the city an area 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long, next to the holy district. It will belong to all the people of Israel.

The prince will have land on both sides of the holy district and the city's land. It will stretch west from the west side and east from the east side, running from the western border to the eastern border.
This land will be his property in Israel. My princes will no longer mistreat My people. They will give the rest of the land to the people of Israel by their tribes.
This is what the Lord the LORD says: “Enough, princes of Israel! Stop your violence and robbery. Do what is fair and right. Stop taking land from My people,” declares the Lord the LORD.
You must use honest scales, a fair ephah, and a fair bath.
The ephah and the bath must be the same size. A bath will hold one-tenth of a homer, and an ephah will hold one-tenth of a homer. So a homer will be the standard measure.
A shekel will be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels will equal one mina.
This is the offering you are to give: one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
The set amount of oil will be one-tenth of a bath from each cor. A cor is ten baths, or one homer.

Also, one sheep must be given from every flock of two hundred from the pastures of Israel. These will be used for grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make atonement for the people, declares the Lord the LORD.
All the people of the land must take part in this offering for the prince in Israel.

It will be the prince's job to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings for the feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths—for all the appointed feasts of the people of Israel. He will provide sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make atonement for the people of Israel.
This is what the Lord the LORD says: “On the first day of the first month, you are to take a young bull without a flaw and purify the sanctuary.

The priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the upper ledge of the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner courtyard.
You are to do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins by mistake or without knowing it. In this way you will make atonement for the temple.
“On the fourteenth day of the first month, you are to observe the Passover. It is a feast of seven days, and unleavened bread is to be eaten.
On that day the prince is to provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
“Each day during the seven days of the feast, he is to provide seven bulls and seven rams without a flaw as a burnt offering to the LORD, along with a male goat for a sin offering.
He is to provide a grain offering of one ephah for each bull and one ephah for each ram, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
During the seven days of the feast that begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he is to make the same provision for sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings.”
The Lord, the LORD, says, “The inner courtyard gate that faces east must stay closed on the six working days, but it must be opened on the Sabbath and on the day of the new moon.”

The prince will come in through the porch of the gate from outside and stand by the gatepost. The priests will offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he will worship at the gate’s threshold. Then he will go out, but the gate will not be closed until evening.
On the Sabbaths and new moons, the people of the land will bow down at the entrance of that gate before the LORD.
The burnt offering the prince gives to the LORD on the Sabbath will be six lambs without blemish and one ram without blemish.
With the ram he will give a grain offering of one ephah, and with the lambs he will give as much as he can, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
On the day of the new moon he will offer one young bull from the herd without blemish, six lambs, and one ram, all without blemish.
He will give a grain offering of one ephah with the bull and one ephah with the ram. With the lambs he will give as much as he can, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
When the prince enters, he will enter through the porch of the gate, and he will go out the same way.

When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed times, anyone who enters through the north gate to worship will go out through the south gate, and anyone who enters through the south gate will go out through the north gate. No one will go back through the gate he used to enter; each person will go straight ahead and leave.
When they enter, the prince will enter with them, and when they leave, he will leave with them.
At the festivals and appointed times, the grain offering will be one ephah with a bull, one ephah with a ram, and with the lambs as much as he can give, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.

When the prince gives a freewill offering to the LORD, whether a burnt offering or a peace offering, the east-facing gate will be opened for him. He will offer his burnt offering or peace offering just as he does on the Sabbath. Then he will go out, and after he leaves, the gate will be closed.
You are to provide a one-year-old lamb without blemish for a burnt offering to the LORD each day. Morning by morning you are to provide it.
You are also to provide a grain offering with it each morning: one-sixth of an ephah, with one-third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour. This grain offering to the LORD is a permanent rule.
So they will provide the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil morning by morning as a regular burnt offering.
The Lord, the LORD, says, “If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is their inheritance. It will belong to his sons and be their property by inheritance.

But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it will belong to that servant only until the year of freedom. Then it will return to the prince. His inheritance belongs to his sons alone.

The prince must not take any of the people’s inheritance or force them from their land. He must give an inheritance to his sons from his own property, so that none of My people are scattered from their property.”
Then he brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate to the north side of the holy rooms for the priests. I saw a place at the far west end of them.

He said to me, “This is the place where the priests will boil the guilt offering and the sin offering and bake the grain offering. They do this so they will not carry them out into the outer courtyard and pass holiness on to the people.”
Then he brought me out into the outer courtyard and led me around to the four corners of the courtyard. In every corner there was another courtyard.
Each of the four corner courtyards was the same size: forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide.
A row of stonework ran around the inside of all four, and hearths were built under the rows all around.
He said to me, “These are the boiling places where the temple servants will boil the people’s sacrifices.”

He brought me back to the entrance of the house. Water was flowing out from under the threshold of the house toward the east, because the house faced east. The water ran down from under the south side of the house, south of the altar.
He brought me out through the north gate and led me around outside to the outer gate that faces east. Water was trickling from the south side.
The man went east with a measuring line in his hand. He measured off a thousand cubits and led me through water that was ankle-deep.
He measured off another thousand and led me through water that reached my knees. He measured off another thousand and led me through water that reached my waist.
He measured off another thousand, but the river was too deep to cross. The water had risen so much that it was deep enough to swim in, and no one could cross it.
He said to me, "Son of man, have you seen this?" Then He led me back along the bank of the river.
When I returned, I saw a great many trees on both banks of the river.
He said to me, "This water flows out to the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah. It flows into the sea, and when it enters the sea, the water becomes fresh.

Every living creature that moves will live wherever the river flows. There will be very many fish, because this water goes there and makes the water fresh. So everything will live wherever the river goes.
"Fishermen will stand along it. From En Gedi to En Eglaim there will be places to spread nets. The fish will be of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea.
But its swamps and marshes will not be healed; they will be left for salt.

"On both banks of the river, every kind of tree that bears fruit will grow. Its leaves will not wither, and its fruit will not fail. It will bear new fruit every month, because its water comes from the sanctuary. Its fruit will be for food, and its leaves will be for healing."
This is what the Lord the LORD says: "This is the boundary by which you will divide the land as an inheritance for the twelve tribes of Israel, with Joseph receiving two portions.
You will inherit it, each like his brother, because I raised My hand and swore to give it to your fathers. This land will fall to you as your inheritance.
"The northern boundary is this: From the Great Sea by the road to Hethlon, as far as Zedad,
Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which lies between Damascus and Hamath, and Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
"So the boundary will run from the sea to Hazar-enan, along the northern border of Damascus and Hamath. This is the north side.
The eastern boundary will run between Hauran and Damascus, along the Jordan between Gilead and the land of Israel, to the eastern sea. This is the east side.
"The southern boundary will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribah Kadesh, then along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea. This is the south side.
The western boundary will be the Great Sea, from the southern border up to a point opposite Lebo-hamath. This is the west side.
"You are to divide this land among yourselves for the tribes of Israel.

You are to allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners living among you who have children among you. They will be to you like native-born Israelites. With you they will receive an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
In whatever tribe a foreigner lives, there you are to give him his inheritance, declares the Lord the LORD."

These are the names of the tribes. Dan will have one share. Its land will run from east to west along the road from Hethlon to Lebo-hamath, as far as Hazar-enan, at the border of Damascus on the north, next to Hamath.
Asher will have one share next to Dan's land, from east to west.
Naphtali will have one share next to Asher's land, from east to west.
Manasseh will have one share next to Naphtali's land, from east to west.
Ephraim will have one share next to Manasseh's land, from east to west.
Reuben will have one share next to Ephraim's land, from east to west.
Judah will have one share next to Reuben's land, from east to west.
Next to Judah, from east to west, will be the special share you are to set apart. It will be 25,000 cubits wide and as long as one tribal share. The holy place will be in the middle of it.
The portion you are to set apart for the LORD will be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide.

This holy portion for the priests will be 25,000 cubits long on the north, 10,000 cubits wide on the west, 10,000 cubits wide on the east, and 25,000 cubits long on the south. The sanctuary of the LORD will be in the middle.
This land will belong to the priests who have been set apart, the sons of Zadok. They kept My charge and did not go wrong when the Israelites went wrong, as the Levites did.
It will be a special gift to them from the land, the most holy portion next to the Levites' land.
Next to the priests' land, the Levites will have a portion 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. The whole area will be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide.
They must not sell any of it or trade it. They must not give away this best part of the land, because it is holy to the LORD.
The rest of the land will be 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long. It will be ordinary land for the city, for houses and open fields. The city will be in the middle of it,
and its measurements will be 4,500 cubits on the north, 4,500 on the south, 4,500 on the east, and 4,500 on the west.
The city's open fields will extend 250 cubits to the north, 250 to the south, 250 to the east, and 250 to the west.
The rest of the holy portion, next to the holy district, will be 10,000 cubits to the east and 10,000 cubits to the west. Its crops will provide food for the city workers.
Workers from all the tribes of Israel will farm it.
The whole portion will be a square, 25,000 cubits by 25,000 cubits. You are to set apart the holy portion along with the city's property.

The rest of the land on both sides of the holy portion and the city property will belong to the prince. It will stretch eastward from the 25,000 cubits of the holy portion to the eastern border, and westward from the 25,000 cubits to the western border. The holy portion and the temple sanctuary will be in the middle.
So the Levites' property and the city's property will lie in the middle of the prince's land. The prince's portion will be between the borders of Judah and Benjamin.
As for the rest of the tribes, Benjamin will have one share next to Judah, from east to west.
Simeon will have one share next to Benjamin, from east to west.
Issachar will have one share next to Simeon, from east to west.
Zebulun will have one share next to Issachar, from east to west.
Gad will have one share next to Zebulun, from east to west.
Along Gad's border, from east to west, will be the southern portion. It will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribah Kadesh, then along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea.
This is the land you are to divide as an inheritance for the tribes of Israel, and these are their shares, declares the Lord the LORD.
These are the exits of the city. On the north side, which is 4,500 cubits long,
the city gates will be named for the tribes of Israel. There will be three gates on the north: the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
On the east side, which is 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
On the south side, which is 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
On the west side, which is 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
The city will measure 18,000 cubits all the way around, and from that day on its name will be the LORD is there.
In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem and surrounded it.

The Lord gave Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into his hand, along with some of the objects from the house of God. Nebuchadnezzar brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and put the objects in his god's treasury.
Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, his chief official, to bring in some of the Israelites from the royal family and the nobles.

They were to be young men with no physical flaws, good-looking, and wise. They had to know a lot, understand what they learned, and be able to serve in the king's palace. They also had to learn the language and writings of the Babylonians.
The king gave them a daily amount of his own food and wine. They were to be trained for three years, and after that they would stand before the king.
Among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah from the tribe of Judah.
The chief official gave them new names: Daniel he called Belteshazzar, Hananiah he called Shadrach, Mishael he called Meshach, and Azariah he called Abednego.
But Daniel decided he would not make himself unclean with the king's food or wine. So he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself.
God caused the chief official to show Daniel kindness and mercy.

The chief official said to Daniel, "I am afraid of my lord the king, who chose your food and your drink. Why should he see you looking worse than the other young men your age? Then you would put my life in danger with the king."
Then Daniel said to the guard the chief official had put in charge of Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
"Please test your servants for ten days. Give us only vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Then compare our looks with the looks of the young men who eat the king's food, and treat your servants based on what you see."
So the guard listened to them and tested them for ten days.
After ten days, they looked better and healthier than all the young men who ate the king's food.
So the guard took away their regular food and wine and gave them vegetables instead.
God gave these four young men knowledge and skill in every kind of writing and wisdom. Daniel also understood all visions and dreams.
When the time was up, the chief official brought them to Nebuchadnezzar.
The king talked with them, and none of them was found to be like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were allowed to serve before the king.
In every matter of wisdom and understanding that the king asked them about, he found them ten times better than all his magicians and enchanters in his whole kingdom.
Daniel stayed there until the first year of King Cyrus.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign, he had dreams. His spirit was troubled, and sleep left him.
The king ordered that the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and astrologers be brought in to tell him his dreams. When they came, they stood before the king.
The king said to them, "I had a dream, and my spirit is anxious to know what it means."
The astrologers answered the king in Aramaic, "May the king live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will explain its meaning."
The king replied, "This is my decision: If you do not tell me the dream and its meaning, you will be cut to pieces and your houses destroyed.
But if you tell me the dream and its meaning, you will receive gifts, rewards, and great honor from me. So tell me the dream and its meaning."
They answered, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will explain its meaning."
The king said, "I know you are trying to buy time, because you see that my word is final.

If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one fate for you. You have agreed to tell me lies and nonsense until things change. So tell me the dream, and I will know that you can truly explain it."
The astrologers answered, "No one on earth can do what the king asks. No king, no matter how great and powerful, has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or astrologer.
What the king asks is too hard. No one can reveal it except the gods, and they do not live among people."
Because of this, the king became very angry and furious. He ordered that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed.
So the order went out, and the wise men were about to be killed. Men were sent to find Daniel and his friends so they could be executed.
Then Daniel spoke wisely and carefully to Arioch, the captain of the king's guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
He asked Arioch, "Why has the king made such a harsh rule?" Then Arioch explained the situation to Daniel.
Daniel went to the king and asked for time, so he could explain the dream's meaning to him.
Then Daniel went home and told his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah what had happened.
He urged them to ask the God of heaven for mercy about this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends would not be destroyed with the rest of Babylon's wise men.
During the night, the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision. Then Daniel praised the God of heaven.
"Praise be to God's name forever and ever, for wisdom and power belong to Him.
He changes times and seasons. He removes kings and sets up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who understand.
"He reveals deep and hidden things. He knows what lies in darkness, and light lives with Him.
I thank and praise You, God of my fathers, because You have given me wisdom and strength. You have now shown me what we asked of You, for You have made known to us the king's matter."
Then Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy Babylon's wise men, and said, "Do not destroy Babylon's wise men. Take me to the king, and I will explain the dream to him."
Arioch quickly brought Daniel before the king and said, "I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can explain the dream's meaning to the king."
The king asked Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Are you able to tell me the dream I saw and its meaning?"
"No wise man, enchanter, magician, or diviner can explain to the king the mystery he asked about.

"But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries. He has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the days to come. Your dream and the visions that came into your mind as you lay on your bed are these:
"As you lay on your bed, O king, your thoughts turned to what would happen after this, and the Revealer of Mysteries showed you what is to come.
"This mystery was revealed to me, not because I have more wisdom than anyone else, but so that the interpretation may be made known to the king and you may understand the thoughts of your heart.
"You looked, O king, and there before you stood a huge statue—enormous and dazzling. It stood in front of you, and its appearance was terrifying.
"The head of the statue was pure gold, its chest and arms were silver, and its belly and thighs were bronze.
"Its legs were iron, and its feet were partly iron and partly baked clay.
"While you watched, a stone was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them.

"Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were all broken to pieces and became like chaff on a threshing floor in summer. The wind carried them away, and no trace of them was left. But the stone that struck the statue became a huge mountain and filled the whole earth.
"This was the dream. Now we will explain its meaning to you.
"You, O king, are the king of kings. The God of heaven has given you kingdom, power, strength, and glory.
"Wherever people, wild animals, and birds live, He has given them into your hand and made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.
"After you, another kingdom will rise, not as strong as yours. Then a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule over the whole earth.
"Finally, there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron—for iron breaks and smashes everything. As iron crushes all things, so it will crush and break the others.
"Just as you saw feet and toes partly of baked clay and partly of iron, so this kingdom will be divided. Yet it will have some of the strength of iron in it, just as you saw iron mixed with clay.
"As the toes were partly iron and partly clay, so this kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
"And just as you saw iron mixed with clay, people will mix but will not truly unite, any more than iron mixes with clay.

"In the time of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed. It will not be handed over to another people. It will crush all those kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will stand forever.

"This is the meaning of the vision of the stone cut from the mountain without hands—the stone that crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. The great God has shown the king what will happen after this. The dream is true, and its meaning can be trusted."
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell facedown and honored Daniel. He ordered that an offering and incense be presented to him.
The king said to Daniel, "Truly your God is the God of gods and the Lord of kings, and the Revealer of Mysteries, for you were able to reveal this mystery."
Then the king promoted Daniel and gave him many great gifts. He made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief official over all its wise men.
At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to manage the affairs of the province of Babylon, while Daniel stayed at the king's court.
King Nebuchadnezzar made a gold statue. It was about ninety feet tall and nine feet wide. He set it up in the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to gather the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other rulers of the provinces. They were to come to the dedication of the statue he had set up.
So all these officials came for the dedication of the statue King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood in front of it.
Then a herald shouted, "People of every nation, tribe, and language, listen to this command:
When you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and every kind of music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
Anyone who does not fall down and worship it will be thrown at once into a blazing furnace."
So when all the people heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and every kind of music, they fell down and worshiped the gold statue King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
At that time some Babylonians came forward and accused the Jews.
They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "O king, live forever!
You gave a command, O king, that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and every kind of music must fall down and worship the gold statue.
And anyone who does not fall down and worship it must be thrown into a blazing furnace.
But there are some Jews you put in charge of the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—who do not obey your command. They do not serve your gods or worship the gold statue you set up."
Then Nebuchadnezzar became furious. In his rage he ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be brought in. So they were brought before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar said to them, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, is it true that you do not serve my gods or worship the gold statue I set up?

Now when you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and every kind of music, be ready to fall down and worship the statue I made. But if you do not worship it, you will be thrown at once into a blazing furnace. Then what god will be able to rescue you from my power?"
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king, "Nebuchadnezzar, we do not need to defend ourselves before you about this.
If the God we serve is able to save us from the blazing furnace and from your hand, O king, He will save us.
But even if He does not, we want you to know, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the gold statue you set up."
Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with anger. His face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual.
He ordered some of the strongest soldiers in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the blazing furnace.
So these men were tied up in their robes, trousers, turbans, and other clothes, and thrown into the blazing furnace.
Because the king's command was so harsh and the furnace so hot, the flames killed the men who carried Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego up.
And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell into the blazing furnace while still tied up.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar jumped up in alarm. He asked his advisers, "Didn't we throw three men, tied up, into the fire?" They answered, "Yes, O king."
He said, "Look! I see four men walking around in the fire, unharmed. And the fourth looks like a son of the gods."
Then Nebuchadnezzar went to the opening of the blazing furnace and shouted, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out!" So they came out of the fire.

The satraps, prefects, governors, and royal advisers gathered around. They saw that the fire had not harmed the men's bodies. The hair on their heads was not singed. Their robes were not scorched, and there was no smell of fire on them.

Nebuchadnezzar said, "Praise be to the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He sent His angel and rescued His servants. They trusted in Him and refused to obey the king's command. They were willing to give up their bodies rather than serve or worship any god except their own God."

"So I make this decree: Anyone of any nation or language who says anything against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be cut into pieces, and his house will be turned into a pile of rubble. For no other god can save like this."
And the king gave Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego more important jobs in the province of Babylon.
King Nebuchadnezzar to all peoples, nations, and languages that live in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you.
It seemed good to me to show the signs and wonders that the Most High God has done for me.
How great are His signs, and how mighty His wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and His rule lasts from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at rest in my house and doing well in my palace.
I had a dream that made me afraid. The thoughts on my bed and the visions in my head troubled me.
So I gave an order to bring all the wise men of Babylon before me, so they could tell me what the dream meant.
Then the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and astrologers came in. I told them the dream, but they could not explain it to me.
At last Daniel came in before me. His name is Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and the spirit of the holy gods is in him. I told him the dream and said,
“Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no secret is too hard for you. Tell me the visions I saw in my dream and what they mean.
“These were the visions in my mind as I lay on my bed: I saw a tree in the middle of the earth, and it was very tall.
The tree grew and became strong. Its top reached to heaven, and it could be seen from the ends of the whole earth.

Its leaves were beautiful, and its fruit was plentiful. It had food for everyone. The wild animals found shade under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches. All living things were fed from it.
“In the visions of my head as I lay on my bed, I saw a watcher, a holy one, come down from heaven.
He called out loudly: ‘Cut down the tree and cut off its branches. Strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the animals run away from under it and the birds from its branches.

But leave the stump and its roots in the ground, bound with a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be wet with the dew of heaven, and let him live with the animals in the grass of the earth.
Let his mind be changed from a man’s mind, and let him be given an animal’s mind. Let seven periods of time pass over him.

This sentence comes by the decree of the watchers, and this decision is a command of the holy ones, so that living people may know that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of men and gives them to anyone He chooses, even to the lowliest of men.’

“This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now, Belteshazzar, tell me what it means, because none of the wise men of my kingdom can explain it. But you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”

Then Daniel, whose name is Belteshazzar, was silent for a while, and his thoughts frightened him. The king said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its meaning frighten you.” Belteshazzar answered, “My lord, may the dream be for your enemies and its meaning for your foes!
“The tree you saw, which grew and became strong, whose top reached to heaven and could be seen by all the earth,
whose leaves were beautiful and whose fruit was plentiful, and which had food for everyone—under it the wild animals lived, and in its branches the birds of the sky nested—
it is you, O king. You have grown and become strong. Your greatness has reached to heaven, and your rule reaches to the ends of the earth.

“You also saw a watcher, a holy one, come down from heaven. He said, ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump and its roots in the ground, bound with a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be wet with the dew of heaven, and let him live with the wild animals, until seven periods of time pass over him.’
“This is the meaning, O king. It is the decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:

You will be driven away from people, and you will live with the wild animals. You will be made to eat grass like an ox. You will be wet with the dew of heaven, and seven periods of time will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of men and gives them to anyone He chooses.
Just as it was commanded to leave the stump with the roots of the tree, your kingdom will be given back to you when you know that Heaven rules.
So, O king, please accept my advice: Stop your sins by doing right, and stop your wrongs by being kind to the poor. Then your good times may last longer.”
All this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Twelve months later, he was walking on the roof of the royal palace in Babylon.
The king said, “Is this not great Babylon, which I built by my great power as a royal home and for the glory of my majesty?”
While the words were still in the king’s mouth, a voice from heaven said, “King Nebuchadnezzar, your kingdom has been taken from you.

You will be driven away from people and live with the wild animals. You will be made to eat grass like an ox, and seven periods of time will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of men and gives them to anyone He chooses.”

Right away the word was fulfilled against Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven away from people and ate grass like an ox. His body was wet with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like eagle feathers and his nails like bird claws.

At the end of that time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my mind came back to me. Then I blessed the Most High and praised and honored Him who lives forever. His rule is an everlasting rule, and His kingdom lasts from generation to generation.
All the people on earth are like nothing before Him. He does what He wants with heaven’s armies and the people of the earth. No one can hold back His hand or say to Him, “What have You done?”

At that time my mind came back to me. My honor and glory were given back to me for the glory of my kingdom. My advisors and nobles came to me, and I was put back on my throne. I became even greater than before.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, lift up, and honor the King of Heaven, because all His works are true and all His ways are just. He is able to bring down those who walk in pride.
King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand nobles and drank wine with them.

While he was tasting the wine, Belshazzar ordered that the gold and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem be brought in. He wanted the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines to drink from them.
So they brought in the gold vessels taken from God's temple in Jerusalem, and the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank from them.
They drank wine and praised gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
At that very hour fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall opposite the lampstand in the king's palace. The king watched the hand as it wrote.
Then the king's face grew pale, and his thoughts terrified him. His legs gave way, and his knees knocked together.

The king shouted for the enchanters, Chaldeans, and astrologers to be brought in. He said to Babylon's wise men, "Whoever reads this writing and tells me what it means will be clothed in purple, have a gold chain placed around his neck, and rule as third in the kingdom."
Then all the king's wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or explain its meaning to the king.
So King Belshazzar became even more terrified. His face turned pale, and his nobles were bewildered.
Because of what the king and his nobles had said, the queen entered the banquet hall. She said, "May the king live forever! Do not let your thoughts terrify you, and do not let your face change.

There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods. In the days of your father he was found to have insight, understanding, and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods. Your father, King Nebuchadnezzar, appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and astrologers.

Because Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, was found to have an extraordinary spirit, knowledge, and understanding, and because he can interpret dreams, explain riddles, and solve problems, let Daniel be called, and he will give the interpretation."
Then Daniel was brought before the king. The king said to Daniel, "Are you Daniel, one of the exiles my father the king brought from Judah?
I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that insight, understanding, and extraordinary wisdom are found in you.
Now the wise men and enchanters were brought before me to read this writing and explain its meaning, but they could not.

But I have heard that you can give interpretations and solve problems. If you can read the writing and explain it, you will be clothed in purple, wear a gold chain around your neck, and be the third ruler in the kingdom."
"Keep your gifts for yourself, and give your rewards to someone else. Still, I will read the writing for the king and explain it.
O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar kingdom, greatness, honor, and majesty.

Because of the greatness He gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him. He killed whom he wanted and spared whom he wanted. He raised up whom he wanted and humbled whom he wanted.
But when his heart became proud and his spirit hardened in pride, he was removed from his royal throne and stripped of his glory.

He was driven away from people, and his mind became like an animal's. He lived with wild donkeys and ate grass like an ox. His body was wet with the dew of heaven until he learned that the Most High God rules over human kingdoms and sets over them whomever He chooses."
"But you, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, even though you knew all this.

Instead, you raised yourself against the Lord of heaven. You had the vessels from His temple brought before you, and you and your nobles, your wives, and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised gods of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which cannot see, hear, or know anything. But the God who holds your breath and all your ways in His hand, you did not honor.
Therefore He sent the hand that wrote this inscription."
"This is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.
This is the meaning: MENE—God has numbered the days of your kingdom and brought it to an end.
TEKEL—you have been weighed on the scales and found lacking.
PERES—your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians."
Then Belshazzar gave the order. They clothed Daniel in purple, put a gold chain around his neck, and announced that he would be the third ruler in the kingdom.
That very night Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, was killed.
Darius the Mede took over the kingdom at about sixty-two years old.
Darius decided to put 120 governors in charge of different parts of his kingdom.
He also chose three supervisors over them, and Daniel was one of them. The governors had to report to these three men so the king would not lose anything.
Daniel did so well that he stood out above all the other supervisors and governors, because he had an excellent spirit. So the king planned to put him in charge of the whole kingdom.

Then the supervisors and governors tried to find a reason to accuse Daniel of wrongdoing in his government work. But they could not find any reason or fault, because he was faithful. They found no mistake or corruption in him.
So these men said, "We will not find any reason to accuse Daniel unless it has to do with the law of his God."
Then those men rushed to the king and said, "Long live King Darius!

All the leaders of the kingdom—the supervisors, governors, advisors, and local officials—agree that the king should make a law and enforce it. For thirty days, no one may pray to any god or person except to you, King. Anyone who does must be thrown into the lions' den.
Now, King, put this rule into effect and sign the document so it cannot be changed. It must follow the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked."
So King Darius signed the document and the law.

When Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went home. In his upstairs room, the windows were open toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he got down on his knees. He prayed and thanked his God, just as he had always done.
Then those men came together and found Daniel praying and asking his God for help.

They went to the king and said, "King, didn't you sign a law saying that for thirty days no one may pray to any god or person except to you? Anyone who does must be thrown into the lions' den?" The king answered, "Yes. That is the law of the Medes and Persians, and it cannot be changed."
Then they said to the king, "Daniel, one of the captives from Judah, does not obey you, King, or the law you signed. He still prays three times a day."
When the king heard this, he was very upset. He tried hard to save Daniel. He worked until sunset to rescue him.
Then those men came together to the king and said, "Remember, King, that under the law of the Medes and Persians, no law or rule the king makes can be changed."
Then the king gave the order. They brought Daniel and threw him into the lions' den. The king said to Daniel, "May your God, whom you serve all the time, save you!"
A stone was brought and placed over the opening of the den. The king sealed it with his own ring and with the rings of his nobles. That way, no one could change anything about Daniel's case.
Then the king went to his palace. He did not eat that night. No entertainment was brought to him, and he could not sleep.
At dawn, the king got up and hurried to the lions' den.
As he got close, he called out in a sad voice. The king said to Daniel, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve all the time, been able to save you from the lions?"
My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths. They did not hurt me, because I was innocent before Him. I also have done you no wrong, King."
The king was very glad. He ordered that Daniel be lifted out of the den. They pulled Daniel out, and he had no injury at all, because he had trusted in his God.

Then the king ordered that the men who had falsely accused Daniel be brought and thrown into the lions' den. Their children and wives were thrown in too. Before they even reached the bottom, the lions attacked them and crushed all their bones.
Then King Darius wrote to all the nations and peoples of every language: "May you have great peace!

I order that in every part of my kingdom, people must tremble and fear before the God of Daniel. He is the living God. He lasts forever. His kingdom will never be destroyed, and His rule will never end.
He saves and rescues. He does signs and wonders in heaven and on earth. He saved Daniel from the lions."
So Daniel did well during the rule of Darius and during the rule of Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of Belshazzar's rule as king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream. Visions passed through his mind while he lay on his bed. Then he wrote down the dream and told its main points.
Daniel said, "In my vision at night I saw the four winds of heaven stirring up the great sea.
Four great beasts came up out of the sea. Each one was different from the others.

The first beast was like a lion, but it had eagle's wings. I watched until its wings were torn off. It was lifted from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a person. A human heart was given to it."
Another beast, which looked like a bear, was raised up on one side. It had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. It was told, "Get up and eat plenty of flesh."
After that, I looked, and there was another beast, like a leopard. It had four wings like a bird's wings on its back. It also had four heads, and it was given authority to rule.

After that, in my vision at night, I saw a fourth beast. It was dreadful, terrifying, and very strong. It had large iron teeth. It devoured and crushed its victims, and it trampled down whatever was left with its feet. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.

While I was thinking about the horns, another horn, a little one, came up among them. Three of the first horns were pulled out by the roots to make room for it. This horn had eyes like a person's eyes and a mouth that spoke boastfully.

As I watched, thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days sat down. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of His head was like pure wool. His throne was flaming with fire, and its wheels were all ablaze.
A river of fire was flowing out from before Him. Thousands upon thousands served Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him. The court sat to judge, and the books were opened.
Then I kept watching because of the boastful words the horn was speaking. I watched until the beast was killed. Its body was destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.
The other beasts had their power taken away, but they were allowed to live for a while longer.
In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a Son of Man. He was coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into His presence.

He was given authority, glory, and royal power. All nations and peoples of every language worshiped Him. His rule is an everlasting rule that will not pass away, and His kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.
I, Daniel, was deeply troubled in my spirit, and the visions in my mind terrified me.
I approached one of those standing there and asked him the true meaning of all this. So he told me and gave me the interpretation.
"These four great beasts are four kings that will rise from the earth."
"But the holy people of the Most High will receive the kingdom and will possess it forever—yes, forever and ever."

Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast. It was different from all the others. It was dreadful, with iron teeth and bronze claws. It devoured and crushed its victims, and it trampled down whatever was left with its feet.

I also wanted to know about the ten horns on its head and about the other horn that came up. That horn made three horns fall. It looked greater than the others. It had eyes and a mouth that spoke boastfully.
As I watched, this horn was waging war against the holy people and was defeating them.
Then the Ancient of Days came and pronounced judgment in favor of the holy people of the Most High. The time came when they took possession of the kingdom.
"The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will appear on earth. It will be different from all the other kingdoms. It will devour the whole earth, trampling it down and crushing it.
The ten horns are ten kings who will come from this kingdom. After them another king will arise. He will be different from the earlier ones and will subdue three kings.
He will speak against the Most High and oppress His holy people. He will try to change the set times and the laws. The holy people will be given into his power for three and a half years.
But the court will sit to judge, and his power will be taken away and completely destroyed forever.

Then the sovereignty, power, and greatness of all the kingdoms under heaven will be handed over to the holy people of the Most High. His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will worship and obey Him."
This is the end of the matter. I, Daniel, was greatly troubled by my thoughts, and my face turned pale, but I kept the matter to myself.
In the third year of King Belshazzar’s reign, I, Daniel, had another vision. It came after the one I had seen before.
In the vision I saw myself in the fortified city of Susa, in the province of Elam. I was standing by the Ulai Canal.
I looked up and saw a ram with two horns standing by the canal. Both horns were high, but one was higher than the other. The higher one grew up last.
I watched the ram push west, north, and south. No animal could stand up to it, and no one could rescue them from its power. It did whatever it wanted and became great.
While I was thinking about this, a goat came from the west. It moved across the whole earth without touching the ground. It had one large horn between its eyes.
It came up to the ram with the two horns that I had seen standing by the canal. It ran at the ram with all its strength.

I saw it reach the ram. It was furious with the ram and struck it, breaking both horns. The ram had no strength to stand against it. The goat threw the ram to the ground and trampled it. No one could rescue the ram from its power.
The goat became very great. But at the height of its power, its large horn broke. In its place, four large horns grew toward the four winds of heaven.
From one of those horns came a small horn. It grew very large toward the south, the east, and the beautiful land.
It grew until it reached the army of heaven. It threw some of that army and some of the stars to the ground and trampled them.
It even set itself up against the Prince of the army. It took away the daily offering and threw down the place of His sanctuary.
Because of rebellion, the army and the daily offering were given over to it. It threw truth to the ground, and it succeeded in what it did.

Then I heard a holy one speaking. Another holy one said to him, “How long will the vision about the daily offering and the sin that causes ruin last? How long will the holy place and the army be trampled?”
He said to me, “It will last 2,300 evenings and mornings. Then the holy place will be made right.”
After I, Daniel, saw this vision, I tried to understand it. Then someone who looked like a man stood in front of me.
I heard a human voice call from the banks of the Ulai Canal, “Gabriel, help this man understand the vision.”
Gabriel came near where I stood. I was terrified and fell facedown. He said, “Son of man, understand that this vision is about the time of the end.”
While he was speaking, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground. Then he touched me and stood me up.
He said, “I will tell you what will happen at the end of the time of wrath, because the vision is about the appointed time of the end.”
“The ram you saw with two horns stands for the kings of Media and Persia.
The goat is the king of Greece. The large horn between its eyes is the first king.
The horn that broke and was replaced by four horns means four kingdoms will rise from that nation, but they will not be as strong as the first king.
Near the end of their rule, when those who rebel have filled up their sin, a harsh and clever king will rise up.”
“His power will be great, but not his own. He will cause terrible destruction and succeed in what he does. He will destroy powerful people and the holy people.

Because of his cleverness, his deceit will succeed. He will think highly of himself. In a time of peace, he will destroy many. He will even stand against the Prince of princes, but he will be broken without human help.
The vision about the evenings and mornings is true. But seal up the vision, because it is for many days in the future.”
I, Daniel, was exhausted and sick for days. Then I got up and did the king’s work. I was amazed by the vision, but no one could explain it.
In the first year of King Darius, son of Ahasuerus, who was from the Medes and had been made king over the Babylonian kingdom,
I, Daniel, was reading the Scriptures. I understood the number of years that the LORD had spoken about through Jeremiah the prophet: Jerusalem would lie in ruins for seventy years.
So I turned to the Lord God and sought Him in prayer and in requests for mercy. I fasted and showed deep sorrow for my sins.
I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed my sins. I said, "Lord, You are great and awesome. You keep Your covenant and show faithful love to everyone who loves You and obeys Your commands.
"We have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled against You. We have turned away from Your commands and laws.
"We did not listen to Your servants the prophets. They spoke in Your name to our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and all the people of the land.

"Lord, You are right and good, but we are filled with shame. This is true for the people of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel—both those nearby and those far away in every country where You sent us because we broke faith with You.
"The LORD, we are covered with shame—our kings, our leaders, and our ancestors—because we sinned against You.
"The Lord our God is full of mercy and forgiveness, even though we have rebelled against Him.
"We have not obeyed the LORD our God. We have not followed the laws He gave us through His servants the prophets.

"All Israel has broken Your law and turned away from You. We refused to obey You. So the curse and the oath written in the Law of Moses, God's servant, have come down on us, because we sinned against You.
"You kept Your word against us and our rulers. You brought a terrible disaster on us. Nothing like it has ever happened anywhere under heaven, not even to Jerusalem.
"Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster came on us. But we did not ask the LORD our God for help. We did not turn from our sins or learn Your truth.
"So the LORD kept this disaster ready and brought it on us. The LORD our God is right in everything He does. But we did not obey Him.
"Now, Lord our God, You brought Your people out of Egypt with great power and made Your name famous, even to this day. But we have sinned and done wickedly.

"Lord, because You always do what is right, please turn Your anger and wrath away from Jerusalem, Your holy mountain. Our sins and the sins of our ancestors have made Jerusalem and Your people an object of shame to everyone around us.
"So now, our God, listen to the prayer and request of Your servant. For Your sake, Lord, make Your face shine on Your holy place, which is now in ruins.
"My God, listen and hear. Open Your eyes and see our ruins and the city that bears Your name. We are not asking You for help because we have done right, but because You are so merciful.
"Lord, hear us! Lord, forgive us! Lord, pay attention and act! For Your own sake, my God, do not wait, because Your city and Your people bear Your name."
While I was still speaking, praying, confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and asking the LORD my God for help for His holy mountain,
Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.
He explained things to me and said, "Daniel, I have come to give you understanding and insight.
"As soon as you began to pray, an answer was given. I have come to tell you, because you are greatly loved. So pay attention to the message and understand the vision.

"Seventy sets of seven years are set for your people and your holy city. They will put an end to rebellion, put an end to sin, pay for wrongdoing, bring in lasting right living, complete the vision and prophecy, and anoint the Most Holy Place.

"So know and understand this: From the time the order is given to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Messiah, the ruler, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. The city will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but it will be a time of trouble.

"After those sixty-two weeks, the Messiah will be put to death and have nothing. Then the people of the coming ruler will destroy the city and the holy place. The end will come like a flood. War and destruction will continue until the end, as has been decreed.

"He will make a strong covenant with many for one week. But in the middle of that week, he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And on the wing of the temple he will set up a disgusting thing that causes ruin, until the destruction that has been decreed is poured out."

In the third year of Cyrus, king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar. The message was true and concerned a great war. Daniel understood the message and gained understanding from the vision.
In those days I, Daniel, mourned for three full weeks.
I ate no rich food. No meat or wine touched my mouth, and I did not put oil on myself, until the three weeks were over.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing beside the great river, the Tigris.
I looked up and saw a man dressed in linen. A belt of fine gold from Uphaz was around his waist.
His body was like beryl. His face shone like lightning, and his eyes were like flaming torches. His arms and legs gleamed like polished bronze, and his voice sounded like a crowd.
Only I, Daniel, saw the vision. The men with me did not see it, but great fear came over them, and they ran away to hide.
So I was left alone, staring at this great vision. I had no strength left. My face grew deathly pale, and I could not hold myself up.
Then I heard the sound of his words. As I heard them, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground.
Suddenly a hand touched me and made me tremble on my hands and knees.
He said to me, "Daniel, man greatly loved, understand the words I am speaking to you. Stand up, for I have now been sent to you." While he spoke this word to me, I stood up trembling.
"Do not be afraid, Daniel," he said, "for from the first day you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard. I have come because of your words.
The prince of the kingdom of Persia stood against me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I was left there with the kings of Persia.
Now I have come to help you understand what will happen to your people in the last days, for the vision concerns days yet to come."
While he spoke these words to me, I bowed my face to the ground and could not speak.

Then someone who looked like a son of man touched my lips. I opened my mouth and spoke to the one standing before me. "My lord, because of the vision, anguish has come upon me, and I have no strength.
How can this servant of my lord speak with my lord? I have no strength left, and no breath is left in me."
Again the one who looked like a man touched me and strengthened me.
He said, "Do not be afraid, man greatly loved. Peace be to you. Be strong, yes, be strong!" When he spoke to me, I was strengthened. Then I said, "Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me."
Then he said, "Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will return to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I leave, the prince of Greece will come.
But I will tell you what is written in the Book of Truth. No one helps me against them except Michael, your prince."
In the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to support and strengthen him.

Now I will tell you the truth. Look, three more kings will stand up for Persia. The fourth will be richer than all of them. When he becomes strong through his riches, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
Then a mighty king will stand up and rule with great authority. He will do as he pleases.

But as soon as he stands up, his kingdom will be broken and split toward the four winds of heaven. It won't go to his children, and it won't be ruled with the power he had, because his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others.
The king of the South will grow strong, but one of his commanders will grow stronger than him and rule a greater kingdom.

After some years they will make an alliance. The daughter of the king of the South will come to the king of the North to make an agreement, but she won't keep her power. Neither will he and his power last. She will be given up, along with those who brought her, her father, and the one who supported her in those times.
But a branch from her roots will stand up in his place. He will come against the army of the king of the North, enter his fortress, fight against them, and overcome.
He will also carry off their gods to Egypt, along with their metal images and their valuable vessels of silver and gold. Then for some years he will stay away from the king of the North.
Then the king of the North will invade the realm of the king of the South, but he will return to his own land.
His sons will stir up war and gather a great army. They will advance, sweep through, and then return. They will stir up war again, all the way to his fortress.
The king of the South will be furious. He will go out and fight against the king of the North. The king of the North will raise a great army, but it will be handed over to him.
When the army is carried away, his heart will be lifted up. He will throw down tens of thousands, but he won't grow stronger.
The king of the North will raise another army, greater than the first. After some years, he will come with a great army and much equipment.
In those times, many will stand against the king of the South. Also violent men among your people will lift themselves up to fulfill a vision, but they will fail.
Then the king of the North will come. He will build siege ramps and capture a fortified city. The forces of the South won't be able to stand. Even his best troops won't have strength to stand.
The one who comes against him will do as he pleases, and no one will stand before him. He will stand in the Beautiful Land, and destruction will be in his hand.

He will set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom. He will make an agreement with him, and he will give him a daughter in marriage to ruin the kingdom. But she won't stand with him or be for him.
After this, he will turn his face to the coastlands and capture many. But a commander will put an end to his taunting. Instead, he will turn the taunt back on him.
Then he will turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land. But he will stumble and fall, and he won't be found.
Then someone will stand in his place. He will send a tax collector through the glorious kingdom, but within a few days he will be broken, not in anger or in battle.
Then a contemptible person will stand in his place. The honor of the kingdom won't be given to him, but he will come in peacefully and seize the kingdom by flattery.
An overwhelming army will be swept away before him. Both it and a prince of the covenant will be broken.
After an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully. He will become strong with a small nation.

In a time of peace, he will invade the richest parts of the province. He will do what his fathers and his fathers' fathers never did. He will scatter plunder, spoil, and wealth among them. He will plan attacks against fortresses, but only for a time.

He will stir up his strength and courage against the king of the South with a great army. The king of the South will wage war with an exceedingly great and mighty army, but he won't stand, because plots will be made against him.
Those who eat his food will destroy him. His army will be swept away, and many will fall slain.
Both kings will have evil in their hearts. They will speak lies at the same table, but it won't succeed, because the end is still set for the appointed time.
He will return to his land with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant. He will take action and then return to his own land.
At the appointed time, he will return and go into the South, but it won't be like the first time or the last.

Ships from Kittim will come against him, and he will be discouraged. He will turn back and vent his rage against the holy covenant. He will take action and show favor to those who forsake the holy covenant.
His forces will rise up and desecrate the sanctuary fortress. They will remove the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination that causes desolation.
With smooth words he will corrupt those who break the covenant, but the people who know their God will be strong and take action.
Those who are wise among the people will instruct many, though for a time they will fall by sword and flame, by captivity and plunder.
When they fall, they will receive a little help, and many will join them by flattery.
Some of the wise will stumble, so that they may be refined, purified, and made white until the time of the end, for it is still for the appointed time.

The king will do as he pleases. He will exalt and magnify himself above every god. He will speak astonishing things against the God of gods. He will prosper until the wrath is completed, for what is determined will be done.
He won't regard the gods of his fathers, or the desire of women, or any god, for he will magnify himself above all.
Instead, he will honor a god of fortresses. A god his fathers didn't know, he will honor with gold, silver, precious stones, and valuable things.
He will attack the strongest fortresses with the help of a foreign god. He will give great honor to those who acknowledge him. He will make them rulers over many and divide the land for a price.

At the time of the end, the king of the South will charge at him. The king of the North will storm against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. He will invade countries and sweep through them.
