He will also enter the Beautiful Land, and many countries will fall. But Edom, Moab, and the leaders of the Ammonites will escape from his hand.
He will stretch out his hand against the countries. The land of Egypt won't escape.
He will gain control of the treasures of gold and silver and all the valuables of Egypt. The Libyans and Cushites will follow at his heels.
But news from the east and the north will alarm him. He will go out with great fury to destroy and devote many to destruction.
He will pitch his royal tents between the sea and the beautiful holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.

At that time Michael, the great prince who stands up for your people, will rise up. There will be a time of trouble like none since nations began until then. At that time your people—everyone found written in the book—will be rescued.
Many who sleep in the dust of the earth will wake up. Some will rise to live forever, and others will rise to shame and lasting contempt.
Those who are wise will shine like the bright sky, and those who lead many to do right will shine like stars forever and ever.
But you, Daniel, close up these words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will travel everywhere, and knowledge will grow.
Then I, Daniel, looked and saw two other men standing there. One stood on this bank of the river, and the other stood on the other bank.
One of them said to the man clothed in linen, who stood above the water of the river, "How long will it be until these amazing things are finished?"

The man clothed in linen, who stood above the water, raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven. He swore by Him who lives forever, "It will be three and a half years. When the power of the holy people has been completely broken, all these things will end."
I heard this, but I did not understand. So I asked, "My lord, what will happen at the end?"
He said, "Go, Daniel. These words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end."
Many will be made clean, made white, and refined. The wicked will keep doing wrong, and none of the wicked will understand. But those who are wise will understand.
From the time the daily sacrifice is stopped and the terrible thing that causes ruin is set up, there will be 1,290 days.
Blessed is the one who waits and reaches 1,335 days.
But you, go to the end. You will rest, and then you will rise to receive your share at the end of the days.

This is the message from the the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri. It came during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

When the the LORD first spoke through Hosea, He said, "Go and find yourself a wife who will be unfaithful, and have children with her. The people of this land have completely turned away from following the the LORD."
So Hosea went and married Gomer, daughter of Diblaim. She became pregnant and had a son.
Then the the LORD said to him, "Name the boy Jezreel, because soon I will punish the family of Jehu for the bloodshed at Jezreel. I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel.
On that day I will break Israel's bow in the Valley of Jezreel."

Gomer became pregnant again and had a daughter. The the LORD said to Hosea, "Name her Lo-Ruhamah, meaning 'No Mercy,' because I will no longer show mercy to the people of Israel. I will completely take them away.
But I will show mercy to the people of Judah. I will save them, not with bows, swords, or war, and not with horses or horsemen, but by the the LORD their God."
After Gomer stopped nursing Lo-Ruhamah, she became pregnant again and had a son.
Then the the LORD said, "Name him Lo-Ammi, because you are not My people, and I am not your God."

Yet the number of Israelites will be like the sand on the seashore, too many to measure or count. In the very place where it was said, "You are not My people," they will be called "children of the living God."
The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be gathered together. They will choose one leader for themselves, and they will go up from the land. For the day of Jezreel will be great.
Say to your brothers, "My people," and to your sisters, "My loved one."
Plead with your mother, plead, for she is not My wife, and I am not her husband. Let her put away her unfaithfulness from her face and her adultery from between her breasts.
Otherwise I will strip her naked and expose her as on the day she was born. I will make her like a desert, turn her into dry land, and kill her with thirst.
I will not show love to her children, because they are children born from unfaithfulness.
Their mother has been unfaithful. The one who gave birth to them has disgraced herself. She said, "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and water, my wool and linen, my oil and drinks."
So I will block her path with thorns. I will build a wall so she cannot find her way.
She will chase her lovers but not catch them. She will look for them but not find them. Then she will say, "I will go back to my first husband, because life was better for me then than now."
She did not know that I gave her the grain, new wine, and oil. I gave her plenty of silver and gold, but she used it for Baal.
So I will take back My grain in its season and My new wine at harvest time. I will take back My wool and linen that were meant to cover her nakedness.
I will expose her shame before her lovers' eyes. No one will rescue her from My hand.
I will end all her joy—her festivals, new moons, Sabbaths, and all her special feasts.
I will ruin her vines and fig trees, which she said were her wages from her lovers. I will turn them into a thicket, and wild animals will eat them.
I will punish her for the days she burned incense to the Baals. She put on rings and jewelry and went after her lovers, but she forgot Me, says the LORD.
So I will win her back. I will lead her into the desert and speak tenderly to her.
There I will give her back her vineyards. I will make the Valley of Achor a door of hope. There she will sing as she did in her youth, as on the day she came up from Egypt.
In that day, says the LORD, you will call Me "My husband," and you will no longer call Me "My master."
I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth. Their names will not be remembered anymore.

In that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild animals, the birds of the sky, and the creatures that move along the ground. I will remove bow, sword, and war from the land, so they can lie down in safety.
I will betroth you to Me forever. I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in love and compassion.
I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.
In that day, says the LORD, I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth.
The earth will answer the grain, new wine, and oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
I will plant her in the land for Myself. I will show mercy to "No Mercy." I will say to "Not My People," "You are My people," and they will say, "You are my God."

The LORD said to me, "Go, love a woman who is loved by another man and is unfaithful, just as the LORD loves the people of Israel, even though they turn to other gods and love sweet cakes offered to idols."
So I bought her for fifteen pieces of silver and about nine bushels of barley.
Then I said to her, "Live with me for many days. Don't be unfaithful, and don't belong to another man. I will do the same for you."
The people of Israel will live for many days without a king or leader, without sacrifices or sacred stone pillars, and without the priest's vest or household idols.
Later, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days.
Hear the word of the the LORD, you Israelites, because the the LORD has a charge against you who live in the land: There is no faithfulness, no love, and no knowledge of God in the land.
Cursing, lying, murder, stealing, and adultery are everywhere. They break all limits, and one act of bloodshed follows another.
Because of this, the land mourns, and everyone who lives in it wastes away. The wild animals, the birds of the sky, and even the fish of the sea are dying.
But let no one bring a charge, and let no one accuse another, for your people are like those who argue with a priest.
You will stumble during the day, and the prophet will stumble with you at night. I will destroy your mother.
My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also reject you as My priests. Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.
The more they grew, the more they sinned against Me. I will turn their glory into shame.
They feed on the sin of My people and set their hearts on their iniquity.
And it will be: Like people, like priest. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
They will eat but not be satisfied; they will be unfaithful but not grow in number, because they have forsaken the the LORD to practice prostitution.
Wine and new wine take away their understanding.
My people ask their wooden idols for advice, and their divining rods answer them. A spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they have been unfaithful to their God.

They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because the shade is pleasant. Therefore your daughters turn to prostitution, and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.

I will not punish your daughters when they prostitute themselves, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because the men themselves go with prostitutes and sacrifice with temple prostitutes. So a people without understanding will come to ruin.
Though you prostitute yourself, O Israel, let not Judah become guilty. Do not go to Gilgal; do not go up to Beth Aven. And do not swear, “As surely as the the LORD lives!”
For Israel is as stubborn as a stubborn heifer. How can the the LORD now feed them like lambs in an open field?
Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!
When their drinking is finished, they turn fully to prostitution; their rulers dearly love disgrace.
A wind has wrapped them in its wings, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.
Hear this, you priests; listen, people of Israel; pay attention, king. Judgment is coming for you, because you have been a trap at Mizpah and a net spread over Tabor.
The rebels have gone deep into slaughter, but I will punish them all.
I know Ephraim well, and Israel is not hidden from Me. Now, Ephraim, you have been unfaithful; Israel is defiled.
Their actions do not let them return to their God, because a spirit of unfaithfulness is in them, and they do not know the the LORD.
Israel's pride speaks against them. Israel and Ephraim stumble in their sin, and Judah stumbles with them.
They will go with their flocks and herds to seek the the LORD, but they will not find Him; He has withdrawn from them.
They have been unfaithful to the the LORD; they have had children by strangers. Now the new moon will destroy them and their fields.
Blow the horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah; shout the alarm in Beth-aven: "Look behind you, Benjamin!"
Ephraim will be ruined on the day of punishment; among Israel's tribes I have made known what is sure.
The princes of Judah are like men who move boundary stones; I will pour out My wrath on them like water.
Ephraim is oppressed and crushed in judgment, because he was determined to follow false gods.
So I am like a moth to Ephraim and like decay to the house of Judah.
When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah saw his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent a message to King Jareb. But he cannot heal you or take away your wound.
For I will be like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, even I, will tear them to pieces and go away; I will carry them off, and no one will rescue them.
I will go back to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face; in their trouble they will earnestly seek Me.
“Come, let us return to the the LORD. He has torn us apart, but He will heal us. He has wounded us, but He will bandage our wounds.
After two days He will bring us back to life. On the third day He will raise us up, so we can live in His presence.
Let us know the LORD. Let us press on to know Him. He will appear as surely as the dawn. He will come to us like rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.”
“What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your faithfulness is like morning fog and like early dew that disappears.
Therefore I have cut them down by the prophets. I have killed them by the words of My mouth, and My judgments go forth like the light.
For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
But, like Adam, they broke the covenant; there they betrayed Me.”
Gilead is a city of evildoers, stained with blood.
Like robbers waiting to ambush someone, priests band together. They murder on the road to Shechem and commit terrible crimes.
In Israel I have seen a horrible thing: Ephraim prostitutes itself, and Israel is defiled.
“Also for you, Judah, a harvest is appointed when I bring My people back from captivity.”
When I wanted to heal Israel, Ephraim's guilt and Samaria's crimes came to light. They lie and cheat. Thieves break in, and robbers attack in the streets.
They do not think about the fact that I remember all their evil. Their sins surround them, and they are right in front of Me.
They make the king happy with their evil, and the leaders happy with their lies.
They are all unfaithful. They are like an oven a baker heats. He stops tending the fire while the dough rises, until it is ready.
On our king's special day, the leaders got drunk on wine, and he joined hands with mockers.
In their hearts they are like that hot oven. They wait to attack. Their baker sleeps all night, but by morning the oven blazes like a fire.
All of them are as hot as an oven, and they destroy their judges. All their kings fall, and none of them calls on Me.
Ephraim mixes with other nations. Ephraim is like a flatbread that was never flipped, so it is only half-baked.
Strangers have eaten up his strength, but he does not know it. Gray hair has spread over him, but he does not know it.
Israel's pride speaks against them. Still, they do not return to the LORD their God, and they do not seek Him, even after all this.
So Ephraim is like a silly dove with no sense. It calls to Egypt, then flies to Assyria.
As they go, I will spread My net over them. I will bring them down like birds in the sky. I will punish them as their community has heard.
It will be terrible for them, because they have wandered away from Me. They will be destroyed, because they rebelled against Me. Even though I wanted to save them, they tell lies about Me.
They do not cry out to Me from their hearts. Instead, they wail on their beds. They cut themselves to beg for grain and new wine, but they turn away from Me.
I trained them and made their arms strong, but they plan evil against Me.
They turn, but not to the Most High. They are like a bow that does not shoot straight. Their leaders will fall by the sword because of their cursing. People in Egypt will laugh at them.
Put the trumpet to your mouth! Like an eagle he swoops down on the house of the LORD, because they broke My agreement and rebelled against My law.
Israel cries out to Me, "My God, we know You!"
But Israel has turned away from what is good, so an enemy will chase him.
They chose kings without My help and picked leaders I did not know. They used their silver and gold to make idols for themselves, so they will be cut off.
Your calf has been rejected, Samaria. My anger burns against them. How long will they be unable to be clean?
The calf came from Israel; a craftsman made it. It is not God. Samaria's calf will be smashed to pieces.
They plant worthless plans and harvest disaster. The grain has no stalk that stands; it makes no flour. If it does make grain, foreigners will eat it.
Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations like a jar no one wants.
They went up to Assyria like a wild donkey going its own way. Ephraim has paid other nations to be its friends.
Even if they pay allies among the nations, I will gather them now. They will soon shrink under the load of the king of princes.
Ephraim built many altars for sin, and those altars became places for sin.
I wrote ten thousand laws for him, but they treated them like something foreign.
They bring sacrifices and eat the meat, but the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their guilt and punish their sins. They will go back to Egypt.
Israel forgot his Maker and built palaces. Judah built many walled cities. So I will send fire on its cities, and it will burn up its fortresses.
Do not celebrate, Israel, with joy like other nations, because you turned away from your God. You loved the pay a prostitute gets on every threshing floor.
The threshing floor and winepress will not feed the people, and the new wine will run short.
They will not stay in the LORD’s land. Ephraim will go back to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria.

They will not pour out wine to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please Him. Their bread will be like bread eaten at a funeral. Anyone who eats it will become unclean, because their food is only for themselves. It will not go into the LORD’s house.
What will you do on a feast day, on the LORD’s festival day?
Look, they are going to Assyria. Egypt will gather them up. Memphis will bury them. Their silver treasures will be overgrown with weeds, and thorns will fill their tents.

The days of punishment have come. The days of paying back have come. Israel will know it. The prophet is a fool. The man of the Spirit is crazy, because your sin is great and your hostility is strong.
The prophet is Ephraim’s lookout with my God, but a trap waits on all his paths. Hostility is in the house of his God.
They have become deeply corrupt, like in the days of Gibeah. He will remember their guilt and punish their sins.

I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers like the first ripe fig on a fig tree in its first season. But they went to Baal Peor and gave themselves to shame. They became as disgusting as the thing they loved.
Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird. There will be no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.
Even if they raise children, I will take them away. Yes, it will be terrible for them when I leave them.
I have seen Ephraim, planted like Tyre in a pleasant field. But Ephraim will bring its children out to be killed.
Give them, O the LORD—what will You give? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that give no milk.
All their wickedness is in Gilgal, for there I hated them. Because of their evil deeds, I will drive them out of My house. I will no longer love them. All their leaders are rebellious.
Ephraim is struck down. Its root is dried up. It will bear no fruit. Even if they have children, I will kill the children they love most.
My God will reject them because they did not listen to Him. They will wander among the nations.
Israel was like a vine that produced fruit for itself. The more fruit it had, the more altars it built. The better its land was, the better its sacred pillars were.
Their hearts are divided, so now they are guilty. He will break down their altars and destroy their sacred pillars.
Now they will say, “We have no king because we did not fear the LORD. What can a king do for us?”
They speak empty words and make false promises. They make agreements, but justice grows like a poisonous weed in the rows of a plowed field.
The people of Samaria are afraid for the calf idol at Beth-aven. Its people mourn for it, and its priests rejoice over its glory, because it has been taken from them.
It will be carried to Assyria as a gift for the great king. Ephraim will be put to shame, and Israel will be ashamed of its plan.
Samaria’s king will be destroyed like foam on the water.
The sinful shrines of Aven will be destroyed—the sin of Israel. Thorns and thistles will grow on their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall on us!”
Israel, you have sinned since the days of Gibeah. You have stood your ground there. Will war at Gibeah not catch up with these wicked people?
When I choose, I will punish them. Nations will gather against them and put them in chains for their double sin.
Ephraim is like a trained young cow that loves to thresh grain. But I put a yoke on her fair neck. I will make Ephraim pull a load; Judah will plow; Jacob will break up the hard ground.
Sow righteousness for yourselves. Reap faithful love. Break up your unplowed ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, until He comes and sends righteousness on you like rain.
You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice. You have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you trusted in your own way and in your many warriors,
a storm will rise among your people, and all your forts will be destroyed. It will be like when Shalman destroyed Beth-arbel in battle—when mothers were killed along with their children.
So Bethel will do to you because of your great wickedness. At dawn the king of Israel will be completely destroyed.
When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son.
The more they were called, the more they turned away from Me. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to idols.
It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms, but they did not know it was I who healed them.
I led them with cords of human kindness and with ropes of love. I lifted the yoke from their jaws and bent down to feed them.
Will they not return to Egypt, and will Assyria not rule over them because they refuse to repent?
A sword will sweep through their cities. It will destroy their defenses and consume them because of their own plans.
My people are set on turning away from Me. Even when they call to the Most High, He will not lift them up.
How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I treat you like Zeboiim? My heart is torn within Me; all My compassion is stirred.
I will not carry out My fierce anger, nor will I destroy Ephraim again. For I am God, and not a man—the Holy One among you. I will not come against their cities.
They will follow the the LORD; He will roar like a lion. When He roars, His children will come trembling from the west.
They will come trembling like birds from Egypt, like doves from Assyria. I will settle them in their homes, declares the the LORD.
Ephraim surrounds Me with lies, and the house of Israel surrounds Me with deceit. Judah is still unruly toward God, even toward the faithful Holy One.
Ephraim chases empty, destructive things all day long. He piles up lies and violence. He makes a treaty with Assyria and sends oil to Egypt.
The LORD has a case against Judah. He will punish Jacob for what he has done. He will pay him back for his deeds.
In the womb, Jacob grabbed his brother’s heel. In his strength, he wrestled with God.
He wrestled with the angel and won. He cried and begged for God’s favor. God found him at Bethel, and there He spoke with us.
The LORD is the God of Hosts. The LORD is His name.
So you should return to your God. Keep showing love and doing what is right. Wait for your God all the time.
A merchant loves to cheat with false scales in his hand.
Ephraim says, “I have become very rich. I have found wealth for myself. No one will find any wrong or sin in all my work.”
“I am the LORD, your God, who brought you out of Egypt. I will make you live in tents again, like in the days of the festival.
I spoke through the prophets. I gave many visions. I used the prophets to teach lessons.”
If there is sin in Gilead, it is worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls. Their altars are like piles of stones in a plowed field.
Jacob fled to the land of Aram. Israel worked for a wife, and he tended sheep for a wife.
The LORD used a prophet to bring Israel out of Egypt. He used a prophet to protect them.
Ephraim has made the LORD very angry. So his Lord will hold him guilty for his bloodshed and repay him for his scorn.
When Ephraim spoke, people trembled; he was lifted up in Israel. But he became guilty because of Baal worship, and he died.

Now they sin more and more. They make metal idols for themselves from their silver, shaped by their own skill. All of them are made by craftsmen. People say about them, “They sacrifice people and worship calf idols.”
So they will be like the morning mist, like the early dew that disappears, like chaff blown from a threshing floor, and like smoke drifting through a window.
“But I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt. You will know no God but Me, and no Savior besides Me.
“I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of burning heat.
“When I fed them, they were satisfied. When they were full, their hearts became proud, and they forgot Me.
“So I will be like a lion to them, like a leopard waiting by the road.
“Like a bear robbed of her cubs, I will attack them and tear them open. I will devour them like a lion, and wild animals will tear them apart.
“You are destroyed, Israel, because you are against Me—against your Helper.
“Where is your king now to save you in all your cities? Where are the rulers you asked for when you said, ‘Give us a king and leaders’?
“In My anger I gave you a king, and in My wrath I took him away.”
Ephraim's guilt is stored up; his sin is kept on record.
Labor pains come on him, but he is a foolish son. When the time comes, he does not come out of the womb.
“I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death. Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting? I will show no compassion.”

Even though he thrives among his brothers, an east wind will come—a wind from the LORD rising from the desert. His spring will dry up, and his well will fail. It will strip his treasury of every precious thing.
Samaria will be punished because she rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women will be ripped open.
Return, Israel, to the the LORD your God. You have stumbled because of your sin.
Take words with you and return to the the LORD. Say to Him, "Take away all our guilt and receive us graciously, so we can offer You praise with our lips.
Assyria will not save us. We will not ride on horses, and we will no longer call the work of our hands our god. In You the orphan finds compassion."
"I will heal their turning away. I will love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him.
I will be like dew to Israel. he will blossom like a lily and put down roots like Lebanon.
his branches will spread. his beauty will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon.
Those who live in his shade will return. They will flourish like grain and blossom like a vine. his fame will be remembered like the wine of Lebanon.
Ephraim, what do I have to do with idols anymore? I answer him and take care of him. I am like a green cypress; your fruit comes from Me."

Who is wise? Let them understand these things. Who has good judgment? Let them know them. For the ways of the the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them, but those who do wrong stumble in them.
This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel.
Hear this, you elders, and listen, all who live in the land. Has anything like this happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?
Tell it to your children, and let your children tell their children, and their children tell the next generation.
What the first locusts left behind, the second locusts ate; what the second left, the third ate; and what the third left, the fourth ate.
Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you who drink wine, because the sweet wine has been taken from your mouths.
For a mighty nation has come up against my land. It is too strong to count. Its teeth are like a lion's teeth, and it has the fangs of a lioness.
It has ruined my vine and broken my fig tree. It has stripped off the bark and thrown it away, so the branches have turned white.
Mourn like a young bride in sackcloth, grieving for the husband she married when she was young.
Grain offerings and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD. The priests who serve the LORD mourn.
The fields are ruined, and the land mourns. The grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, and the olive oil is gone.
Be ashamed, you farmers! Wail, you grape growers, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest in the field has been lost.
The vine is dried up, and the fig tree is withered. The pomegranate, the palm, and the apple tree—with all the trees of the field—have dried up. Surely the joy of people has faded away.

Put on sackcloth and mourn, you priests! Wail, you who serve at the altar. Come and spend the night in sackcloth, you servants of my God, because grain offerings and drink offerings are no longer brought to the house of your God.
Set apart a day of fasting and call a special meeting. Gather the elders and everyone who lives in the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
Oh, what a terrible day! The day of the LORD is near. It comes like destruction sent by the Almighty.
Hasn't our food been cut off right before our eyes? Joy and gladness have left the house of our God.
The seeds rot under the soil. The storehouses are empty. The barns are torn down because the grain has dried up.
How the animals groan! The herds of cattle are confused because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep have been ruined.
To You, the LORD, I cry out, for fire has eaten the pastures of the wilderness, and flames have burned all the trees of the field.
Even the wild animals cry out to You, because the streams have dried up, and fire has eaten the pastures of the wilderness.
Blow the trumpet in Zion. Sound the alarm on My holy mountain. Let everyone who lives in the land tremble, because the day of the LORD is coming. It is very close.

That day will be dark and gloomy, a day of clouds and thick darkness. Like dawn spreading over the mountains, a great and mighty army is coming. Nothing like it has happened since long ago, and nothing like it will happen again for many generations.
Fire burns in front of them, and flames blaze behind them. The land in front of them is like the garden of Eden, but behind them it is an empty desert. Nothing escapes them.
They look like horses, and they run like war horses.
They sound like chariots as they leap over the mountaintops. They crackle like fire burning dry stalks. They are a mighty army ready for battle.
Nations shake with fear when they see them. Every face turns pale.
They charge like warriors and climb walls like soldiers. They march straight ahead and do not turn aside.
They do not push one another. Each one stays in his own path. They break through defenses, but their ranks do not break.
They rush into the city and run along the walls. They climb into houses and enter through windows like thieves.
The earth shakes before them, and the sky trembles. The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars stop shining.
The LORD thunders at the head of His army. His forces are too many to count, and mighty are those who obey His command. The day of the LORD is great and terrifying. Who can survive it?
“Even now,” declares the LORD, “return to Me with all your heart, with fasting and weeping and mourning.”
Tear your heart, not just your clothes, and return to the LORD your God. He is gracious and kind. He is slow to anger and full of faithful love, and He may hold back the disaster He planned.
Who knows? He may turn and show mercy and leave a blessing behind Him—grain and drink offerings for the LORD your God.
Blow the trumpet in Zion. Set apart a fast. Call a special meeting.
Gather the people and make the meeting holy. Bring the elders together. Gather the children, even babies who are still nursing. Let the groom leave his room and the bride leave her wedding room.

Let the priests who serve the LORD cry out between the porch and the altar. Let them say, “Spare your people, the LORD. Do not make your inheritance a shame among the nations. Why should the nations say, ‘Where is their God?’”
Then the LORD was jealous for His land and felt sorry for His people.
The LORD answered them: “I am sending you grain, new wine, and olive oil, enough to fill you up. I will never again make you a shame among the nations.

I will drive the army from the north far away from you. I will push it into a dry and empty land. Its front rows will fall into the eastern sea, and its back rows will fall into the western sea. Its bad smell will rise up.” Yes, He has done great things!
Do not be afraid, land of Zion. Be glad and rejoice, because the LORD has done great things.
Do not be afraid, wild animals, because the open pastures are turning green again. The trees are bearing fruit, and the fig tree and vine are giving their harvest.
Be glad, people of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God. He has given you the autumn rains because He is faithful. He sends you showers in the fall and in the spring, just as before.
The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the wine vats will overflow with new wine and olive oil.
“I will pay you back for the years the locusts ate—the big locust, the young locust, the other locusts, and the locust swarm. That was My great army that I sent against you.
You will have plenty to eat, until you are full. You will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has done amazing things for you. My people will never be shamed again.
Then you will know that I am with Israel. I am the LORD your God, and there is no other. My people will never be shamed again.”
“After that, I will pour out My Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
I will pour out My Spirit even on My servants, both men and women, in those days.
I will show wonders in the sky and on the earth: blood, fire, and thick smoke.
The sun will turn to darkness, and the moon will turn to blood, before the great and terrifying day of the LORD comes.
Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved. On Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be rescue, just as the LORD has said. It will even reach the survivors the LORD calls.”
"For look, in those days and at that time, when I bring Judah and Jerusalem back from captivity,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will judge them for what they did to My people, My very own Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, and to My land, which they divided.
"They gambled for My people. They sold a boy for a prostitute and traded a girl for wine to drink.
Tyre, Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia, what do you have against Me? Are you trying to pay Me back? If you are, I will quickly bring that trouble back on your own heads.
"You took My silver and gold and carried My finest treasures into your temples.
You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to send them far from their homeland.
"Now I will wake them up from the place where you sold them, and I will pay you back on your own heads.
I will sell your sons and daughters to the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, a distant nation. For the LORD has spoken."
"Proclaim this among the nations: Get ready for war! Wake up the mighty men! Let all the soldiers step forward and get ready to fight.
"Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, "'I am strong.'
"Hurry and come, all you nations from every side, and gather there. Bring down Your mighty ones, O the LORD.
Let the nations wake up and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come and trample the grapes, for the winepress is full and the vats overflow, because their evil is great."
"Multitudes, multitudes in the Valley of Decision! For the day of the LORD is near in the Valley of Decision.
The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will stop shining.
"The LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem. The heavens and the earth will shake, but the LORD will be a safe place for His people and a strong tower for the people of Israel."
"Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who lives in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and no foreigner will ever pass through it again.

In that day, the mountains will drip with sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all the streambeds of Judah will run with water. A spring will flow from the house of the LORD and water the Valley of Acacias.
"Egypt will become a wasteland and Edom a dry desert, because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they spilled innocent blood.
But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged, for the LORD lives in Zion."

These are the words of Amos. He was one of the shepherds from Tekoa. He saw this message about Israel during the time of Uzziah, king of Judah, and Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
The LORD roars from Zion and speaks from Jerusalem. The shepherds' pastures mourn, and the top of Mount Carmel dries up.
This is what the LORD says: "Damascus has sinned again and again, so I will not hold back My punishment. They crushed Gilead with iron threshing sledges.
So I will send fire on the house of Hazael, and it will burn up Ben-Hadad's palaces.
I will break the bar of Damascus's gate and remove the ruler from the Valley of Aven and the one who holds the scepter from Beth Eden. The people of Aram will be taken captive to Kir, says the LORD."
This is what the LORD says: "Gaza has sinned again and again, so I will not hold back My punishment. They dragged off whole communities and sold them to Edom.
So I will send fire on the wall of Gaza, and it will burn up its palaces.
I will remove the ruler from Ashdod and the one who holds the scepter from Ashkelon. I will turn My hand against Ekron, and the rest of the Philistines will be wiped out, says the Lord the LORD."
This is what the LORD says: "Tyre has sinned again and again, so I will not hold back My punishment. They sold whole communities into exile to Edom and forgot their treaty of brotherhood.
So I will send fire on the wall of Tyre, and it will burn up its palaces."

This is what the LORD says: "Edom has sinned again and again, so I will not hold back My punishment. He chased his brother with a sword and showed no mercy. His anger burned all the time, and his wrath never ended.
So I will send fire on Teman, and it will burn up the palaces of Bozrah."
This is what the LORD says: "Ammon has sinned again and again, so I will not hold back My punishment. They ripped open pregnant women in Gilead to enlarge their territory.
So I will set fire to the wall of Rabbah, and it will burn up its palaces amid war cries on the day of battle and a storm on the day of a whirlwind.
Their king will go into exile, along with his officials, says the LORD."
This is what the LORD says: "For Moab's many sins, and even more, I will not hold back My anger. Because he burned the bones of Edom's king to lime.
I will send fire on Moab, and it will burn up the forts of Kerioth. Moab will die in the noise of war, with shouts and the blast of a trumpet.
I will destroy Moab's ruler and kill all its officials with him," says the LORD.

This is what the LORD says: "For Judah's many sins, and even more, I will not hold back My anger. They rejected the law of the LORD and did not keep His rules. Their lies led them astray, the same lies their ancestors followed.
I will send fire on Judah, and it will burn up the forts of Jerusalem."
This is what the LORD says: "For Israel's many sins, and even more, I will not hold back My anger. They sell innocent people for silver and poor people for a pair of sandals.
They trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the ground and deny justice to the oppressed. Father and son sleep with the same young woman, and so they dishonor My holy name.
They lie down beside every altar on clothes taken as security, and in the house of their god they drink wine paid as fines."
"Yet I destroyed the Amorites before them. They were as tall as cedars and as strong as oaks. I destroyed their fruit above and their roots below.
I brought you up out of Egypt and led you forty years in the desert to give you the land of the Amorites.
I raised up prophets from among your sons and Nazirites from among your young men. Is this not true, people of Israel?" declares the LORD.
"But you made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets not to prophesy."
"Now then, I will crush you as a cart crushes when loaded with grain.
The fast will not escape, the strong will not keep their strength, and the warrior will not save his life.
The archer will not stand his ground, the fast runner will not get away, and the horseman will not save his life.
Even the bravest warriors will run away naked on that day," declares the LORD.
Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, people of Israel, against the whole family I brought up from Egypt.
“Only you have I chosen among all the families on earth. That is why I will punish you for all your sins.”
Do two people walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does a young lion growl from its den unless it has caught something?
Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground if there is no bait for it? Does a trap spring up from the ground without catching something?
If a trumpet sounds in a city, won’t the people tremble? If trouble comes to a city, hasn’t the LORD done it?
Surely the Lord the LORD does nothing without first showing His plan to His servants the prophets.
A lion has roared—who will not be afraid? The Lord the LORD has spoken—who can keep from prophesying?
Announce this to the palaces of Ashdod and to the palaces of Egypt: “Gather on the mountains of Samaria and see the great trouble inside her and the cruelty among her people.”
“They do not know how to do what is right,” declares the LORD, “those who store up violence and robbery in their palaces.”
Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: “An enemy will surround the land. He will tear down your strongholds and rob your palaces.”

This is what the LORD says: “As a shepherd saves from a lion’s mouth only two legs or a piece of an ear, so the people of Israel living in Samaria will be saved—with just a corner of a bed or a piece of a couch.”
Hear and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord the LORD, the God of Armies.
“On the day I punish Israel for their sins, I will also punish the altars of Bethel. The horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
I will strike the winter house along with the summer house. The houses of ivory will be destroyed, and the great houses will come to an end,” declares the LORD.
Listen to this, you pampered women of Samaria who live on Mount Samaria. You crush the poor and push down the needy. You say to your husbands, "Bring us something to drink."
The Lord the LORD has sworn by His holiness: "Days are coming when enemies will drag you away with hooks, and your descendants with fishhooks.
You will go out through the breaks in the wall, each woman straight ahead, and you will be thrown toward Harmon," declares the LORD.
"Go to Bethel and sin; go to Gilgal and sin even more. Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days.
Offer a thank offering made with yeast, and brag about your freewill offerings. This is what you love to do, people of Israel," declares the Lord the LORD.
"I gave you empty stomachs in every city and a lack of bread in every place, yet you did not return to Me," declares the LORD.
"I also held back the rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. I sent rain on one city, but not on another. One field got rain, while another field without rain dried up.
People from two or three cities wandered to another city for water, but they did not get enough to drink. Yet you did not return to Me," declares the LORD.
"I struck you with blight and mildew. Locusts ate your many gardens and vineyards, your fig trees and olive trees. Yet you did not return to Me," declares the LORD.

"I sent a plague on you like the plagues of Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword, and your horses were taken. I made the stench of your camps rise into your nostrils. Yet you did not return to Me," declares the LORD.
"I destroyed some of you like I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. You were like a burning stick pulled from a fire. Yet you did not return to Me," declares the LORD.
"Therefore this is what I will do to you, O Israel: Because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, O Israel!"

For behold, He who forms the mountains, creates the wind, and reveals His thoughts to man, who turns the dawn to darkness and treads on the heights of the earth—the LORD, the God of Hosts, is His name.
Listen to this message I speak against you, people of Israel. It is a sad song:
Virgin Israel has fallen and will never rise again. She lies abandoned in her own land, and no one will help her up.

For this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: "The city that sent out a thousand soldiers will have only a hundred left. The city that sent out a hundred will have only ten left for the people of Israel."
For this is what the LORD says to the people of Israel: "Seek Me, and you will live."
Do not seek help at Bethel. Do not go to Gilgal. Do not travel to Beersheba. Gilgal will surely be taken away, and Bethel will become worthless.
Seek the the LORD, and you will live. Otherwise, He may sweep through like fire against the family of Joseph and burn it up, and no one in Bethel will be able to put it out.
You turn justice into bitterness and throw righteousness to the ground.
He made the Pleiades and Orion. He turns the deepest darkness into morning and makes day dark as night. He calls the waters of the sea and pours them out over the earth. The LORD is His name.
He brings sudden destruction on the strong, so that their strongholds are destroyed.
They hate anyone who corrects them at the city gate, and they despise anyone who speaks honestly.
Therefore, because you crush the poor and take grain taxes from them, you have built stone houses but will not live in them. You have planted beautiful vineyards but will not drink their wine.
For I know how many wrongs you have done and how great your sins are. You crush the righteous, take bribes, and push the needy aside in the courts.
So the wise person stays quiet at such a time, because these are evil days.
Seek good, not evil, so that you may live. Then the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you, just as you have claimed.
Hate evil and love good. Make justice fair in the courts. Perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will show mercy to the people of Joseph who are left.

Therefore, this is what the LORD, the God of Hosts, the Lord, says: "There will be crying in every square, and in every street people will cry, 'How terrible! How terrible!' They will call the farmers to mourn, and those who know how to sing funeral songs will wail.
There will be crying in all the vineyards too, because I will pass through your land," says the the LORD.
How terrible for you who long for the day of the the LORD! Why do you want that day? It will be darkness, not light.
It will be like a man running from a lion, only to meet a bear; or like someone going home, leaning his hand on the wall, and getting bitten by a snake.
The day of the the LORD will be dark, not light, with no brightness in it.
"I hate and reject your festivals. I do not enjoy your sacred gatherings."
"Even if you bring Me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. I will not even look at your fellowship offerings from your fattened animals."
"Take away the noise of your songs from Me. I will not listen to the music of your harps."
Instead, let justice flow like a river, and let righteousness flow like a never-ending stream.
"Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings during the forty years in the wilderness, people of Israel?
You will carry Sikkuth, your king, and Chiun, your star god, along with the idols you made for yourselves.
I will send you into exile beyond Damascus," says the the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts.
Woe to those who are at ease in Zion and to those who feel secure on Mount Samaria, the distinguished leaders of the foremost nation, to whom the house of Israel comes.
Cross over to Calneh and see; go from there to great Hamath; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than your territory?
You push off the day of disaster, yet you bring near a reign of violence.
You lie on beds of ivory and sprawl on your couches. You eat lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.
You strum on harps like David and make up songs on musical instruments.
You drink wine from bowls and anoint yourselves with the finest oils, but you do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
So now you will be the first to go into exile, and your feasts and lazy lounging will come to an end.
The Lord, the LORD, has sworn by Himself—the the LORD God of Hosts declares: "I abhor the pride of Jacob and detest his citadels; I will deliver up the city and everything in it."
If ten men are left in one house, they will die.

When a relative who is to burn the bodies picks them up to carry them out of the house, he will say to one inside, "Is anyone else with you?" "No," the man will reply. Then the relative will say, "Hush! We must not mention the name of the LORD."
For look, the LORD gives a command, and He will smash the great house to pieces and the small house into bits.
Do horses run on rocky cliffs? Does anyone plow rocks with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness.
You who celebrate over nothing, who say, "Didn't we gain power by our own strength?"
"For look, I will raise up a nation against you, O house of Israel," says the LORD, the God of Hosts, "and they will oppress you from the entrance of Hamath to the Arabah Valley."
This is what the Lord the LORD showed me: He was forming swarms of locusts just as the late spring crop was starting to grow. It was after the king's harvest.
When they had eaten every plant in the land, I cried out, "Lord the LORD, please forgive! How can Jacob survive? He is so small!"
So the LORD changed His mind. "It will not happen," said the LORD.
This is what the Lord the LORD showed me: The Lord the LORD was calling for judgment by fire. It burned up the great deep and ate up the land.
I said, "Lord the LORD, please stop! How can Jacob survive? He is so small!"
So the LORD changed His mind. "This will not happen either," said the Lord the LORD.
This is what He showed me: The Lord was standing by a wall built with a plumb line, and He held a plumb line in His hand.
The LORD asked me, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Look, I am putting a plumb line among My people Israel. I will not spare them anymore.
The high places of Isaac will be ruined, and Israel's holy places will be destroyed. I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent a message to Jeroboam king of Israel: "Amos has plotted against you among the people of Israel. The land cannot stand all his words.
For this is what Amos says: 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will be carried away from its land.'"
Then Amaziah said to Amos, "Go away, you seer! Flee to Judah. Earn your living there and prophesy there.
But do not prophesy anymore at Bethel, because it is the king's holy place and a royal temple."
Amos answered Amaziah, "I was not a prophet, and I was not a prophet's son. I was a shepherd, and I took care of sycamore trees.
But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, 'Go, prophesy to My people Israel.'
Now listen to the word of the LORD: You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac.'

So this is what the LORD says: 'Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, and your sons and daughters will fall by the sword. Your land will be divided up, and you will die in an unclean land. Israel will surely be taken from its land.'"
This is what the Lord the LORD showed me: a basket of summer fruit.
The LORD asked, "Amos, what do you see?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come for My people Israel. I will not spare them anymore."
"In that day," declares the Lord the LORD, "the temple songs will turn into crying. There will be many dead bodies thrown everywhere! Hush!"
Listen to this, you who trample the needy and crush the poor of the land.
You say, "When will the New Moon be over so we can sell grain? When will the Sabbath end so we can sell wheat? We will make the measure smaller, raise the price, and cheat with dishonest scales.
That way we can buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and sell even the chaff of the wheat."
The LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: "Surely I will never forget any of their deeds."
Will not the land shake because of this, and everyone living in it mourn? The whole land will rise like the Nile, surge and settle like the Nile of Egypt.
"On that day," declares the Lord the LORD, "I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

"I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into songs of grief. I will make everyone wear sackcloth and shave their heads. I will make it like mourning for an only child, and its end will be like a bitter day."
"Look, the days are coming," declares the Lord the LORD, "when I will send a famine on the land—not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD."
People will stagger from sea to sea and wander from north to east, looking for the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.
In that day the beautiful young women and young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, "As your god lives, O Dan," or, "As the way of Beersheba lives"—they will fall and never rise again.

I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said, "Strike the tops of the pillars so the thresholds shake. Bring them down on the heads of all the people. Those who are left I will kill with the sword. Not one will escape; no fugitive will get away.
If they dig down to the grave, My hand will take them from there. If they climb up to heaven, I will bring them down from there.
If they hide on top of Mount Carmel, I will search and take them from there. If they hide from My eyes at the bottom of the sea, I will command the serpent to bite them there.
If they are led away captive by their enemies, I will command the sword to kill them there. I will set My eyes on them for harm, not for good."
The Lord the LORD of Hosts touches the earth, and it melts. All who live in it mourn. It rises like the Nile and sinks like the river of Egypt.
He builds His upper rooms in heaven and sets their foundation on the earth. He calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out over the earth. The LORD is His name.
"Are you not like the Cushites to Me, O people of Israel?" declares the LORD. "Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir?"
"Behold, the eyes of the Lord the LORD are on the sinful kingdom. I will destroy it from the face of the earth. Yet I will not completely destroy the house of Jacob," declares the LORD.
"For behold, I am commanding, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is shaken in a sieve, but not a single pebble will fall to the ground.
All the sinners of My people will die by the sword—those who say, 'Disaster will not catch up with us or happen to us.'"
"In that day I will raise up David's fallen tent. I will repair its broken walls, rebuild its ruins, and make it as it was in days of old.
I do this so they may possess what is left of Edom and all the nations that are called by My name," declares the LORD.

"Behold, the days are coming," declares the LORD, "when the plowman will catch up to the reaper, and the grape treader will catch up to the seed sower. The mountains will drip with sweet wine, and all the hills will flow with it.
I will restore My people Israel. They will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine. They will make gardens and eat their fruit.
I will plant them in their own land, and they will never again be uprooted from the land I have given them," says the LORD your God.

The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Lord, the LORD, says about Edom: We have heard a message from the LORD. A messenger has been sent to the nations, saying, "Get up! Let's rise up and fight against her!"
Look, I will make you small among the nations. You will be very despised.
Your pride has tricked you. You live in the cracks of the rock and make your home high up. You say in your heart, "Who can bring me down to the ground?"
Even if you fly as high as an eagle, even if you make your nest among the stars, I will bring you down from there, declares the LORD.
If thieves came to you, or robbers at night—how ruined you would be!—wouldn't they steal only what they needed? If grape pickers came, wouldn't they leave a few grapes behind?
But Esau will be searched out. His hidden treasures will be found.
All your allies will push you to the border. The men who were at peace with you will trick you and overpower you. Those who ate your bread will set a trap beneath you. He has no understanding.
On that day, declares the LORD, won't I destroy the wise men from Edom and understanding from Mount Esau?
Your mighty men, Teman, will be terrified. Every man from Mount Esau will be cut off in the slaughter.
Because of the violence you did to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you. You will be cut off forever.
On the day you stood aside, when strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were like one of them.
Do not gloat over your brother on the day of his disaster. Do not rejoice over the people of Judah on the day they are destroyed. Do not boast on the day of trouble.
Do not enter the gate of My people on the day of their disaster. Do not gloat over their trouble on the day of their disaster. Do not take their wealth on the day of their disaster.
Do not stand at the crossroads to cut off those who escape. Do not hand over those who survive on the day of trouble.
For the day of the LORD is near for all nations. As you have done, it will be done to you. Your deeds will return on your own head.
Just as you drank on My holy mountain, so all the nations will drink without stopping. They will drink and swallow and be as if they had never existed.
But on Mount Zion there will be those who escape, and it will be holy. The house of Jacob will take back its own land.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame. But the house of Esau will be like straw. They will set it on fire and burn it up. No one will be left from the house of Esau, for the LORD has spoken.
Those from the Negev will take over Mount Esau. Those from the lowlands will take over Philistia. They will take over the fields of Ephraim and Samaria. Benjamin will take over Gilead.
The people of Israel who were carried away will take over the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath. The people of Jerusalem who were taken to Sepharad will take over the cities of the Negev.
Rescuers will go up to Mount Zion to rule Mount Esau. And the kingdom will belong to the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai.
The LORD said, "Get up and go to the great city of Nineveh. Speak out against it, because I have seen how evil its people are."
But Jonah got up to run away to Tarshish, away from the LORD. He went down to Joppa, found a ship going to Tarshish, paid his fare, and got on board to sail with them to Tarshish, away from the LORD.
Then the LORD sent a powerful wind on the sea. A huge storm came up, and the ship was about to break apart.

The sailors were afraid. Each man prayed to his own god. They threw the cargo into the sea to make the ship lighter. But Jonah had gone down into the bottom of the ship. He lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
The captain came to him and said, "Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray to your god! Maybe your god will notice us and keep us from dying."
The sailors said to each other, "Come, let's throw lots to find out who caused this trouble." They threw lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
They said to him, "Tell us, please, who brought this trouble on us. What do you do for a living? Where do you come from? What country are you from? What people do you belong to?"
He answered, "I am a Hebrew. I worship the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
The men were very afraid. They asked him, "What have you done?" They knew he was running away from the LORD, because he had told them.
The sea was getting rougher and rougher. So they asked him, "What should we do to you so the sea will calm down for us?"
He said to them, "Pick me up and throw me into the sea. Then it will calm down for you. I know this terrible storm has come on you because of me."
Instead, the men rowed hard to get back to land. But they could not, because the sea was getting rougher and rougher against them.
Then they cried out to the LORD, "O LORD, please do not let us die for taking this man's life. Do not blame us for killing an innocent man, because You, O LORD, have done what You wanted."
Then they picked up Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea calmed down.
The men were very afraid of the LORD. They offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made promises to Him.
The LORD sent a huge fish to swallow Jonah. Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God.
He said, “In my trouble I called to the LORD, and He answered me. From the depths of the grave I cried for help, and You heard my voice.
You threw me into the deep water, into the middle of the sea. The currents surrounded me, and all Your waves and breakers swept over me.
“I said I was driven from Your sight, but I will look again toward Your holy temple.
The waters closed in on me and threatened my life. The deep sea surrounded me, and seaweed wrapped around my head.
“I sank down to the bottoms of the mountains. The earth locked me in forever. But You, the LORD my God, brought my life up from the pit.
When I was about to give up, I remembered the LORD. My prayer reached You in Your holy temple.
“Those who worship worthless idols turn away from God’s faithful love.
But I will offer You a sacrifice of thanks. I will keep my promises. Salvation comes from the LORD.”
Then the LORD commanded the fish, and it spit Jonah out onto dry land.
The word of the the LORD came to Jonah a second time.
The LORD said, "Get up and go to Nineveh, that great city. Proclaim to it the message I am giving you."
Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, just as the the LORD had said. Nineveh was a very large city. It took three days to walk across it.
Jonah went into the city and traveled one day. Then he cried out, "In forty days, Nineveh will be destroyed!"
The people of Nineveh believed God. They called for a fast, and everyone—from the greatest to the least—put on rough cloth.
When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he got up from his throne. He took off his royal robe, put on rough cloth, and sat in ashes.
He sent this order through Nineveh: "By the command of the king and his nobles, no person or animal may eat or drink anything.

Do not let the herds or flocks graze or drink water. Instead, cover both people and animals with rough cloth. Let everyone pray hard to God. Let each person turn from his evil ways and stop the violence in his hands.
Who knows? Maybe God will change His mind, turn from His fierce anger, and not destroy us."
When God saw what they did and that they turned from their evil ways, He changed His mind about the disaster He had planned to bring on them, and He did not do it.
But Jonah was very upset about this, and he became angry.

He prayed to the the LORD and said, "O the LORD, wasn't this what I said while I was still in my own country? That's why I ran away to Tarshish first. I knew that You are a kind and caring God. You are slow to anger and full of faithful love, and You are willing to hold back from sending disaster.
And now, O the LORD, please take my life, because it is better for me to die than to live."
The the LORD replied, "Do you have a good reason to be angry?"
Then Jonah left the city and sat down east of it. He made himself a shelter and sat in its shade, waiting to see what would happen to the city.
The the LORD God made a plant grow up over Jonah. It gave shade over his head and saved him from his discomfort. Jonah was very happy about the plant.
But at dawn the next day, God sent a worm. It attacked the plant, and the plant dried up.
When the sun came up, God sent a hot east wind. The sun beat down on Jonah's head, and he became faint. He wished he could die and said, "It is better for me to die than to live."
Then God said to Jonah, "Do you have a good reason to be angry about the plant?" Jonah answered, "Yes, I do. I am angry enough to die!"
The the LORD said, "You have had pity on the plant. You did not work for it or make it grow. It came up in one night and died in one night.
Should I not have pity on Nineveh, that great city? More than 120,000 people live there. They do not know their right hand from their left. Many animals live there too."
This is the word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. He saw a vision about Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear, all you peoples; listen, earth and everything in it. Let the Lord, the LORD, be a witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple.
Look, the LORD is coming from His place. He will come down and walk on the high places of the earth.
The mountains will melt under Him, and the valleys will split open, like wax near a fire, like water poured down a hill.
All this is because of Jacob's sin and the sins of Israel's family. What is Jacob's sin? Isn't it Samaria? What is Judah's high place? Isn't it Jerusalem?
So I will make Samaria a pile of rubble in an open field, a place to plant vineyards. I will throw her stones into the valley and uncover her foundations.
All her carved images will be smashed. All her wages will be burned with fire. I will destroy all her idols. She gathered them like a prostitute's pay, and they will be used that way again.
Because of this I will cry and wail. I will walk barefoot and naked. I will howl like a jackal and mourn like an ostrich.
Her wound cannot be healed. It has reached Judah. It has touched the gate of my people, all the way to Jerusalem.
Do not tell it in Gath. Do not weep at all. Roll in the dust in Beth-leaphrah.
Pass on in naked shame, people of Shaphir. The people of Zaanan will not come out. Beth-ezel mourns and takes away its support from you.
The people of Maroth wait for something good, but disaster has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
Harness the chariot to the fast horse, people of Lachish. She was the beginning of sin for the Daughter of Zion, because Israel's sins were found in you.
So you will give farewell gifts to Moresheth-gath. The houses of Achzib will prove false to the kings of Israel.
I will bring another conqueror against you, people of Mareshah. The glory of Israel will reach Adullam.
Shave your head and cut off your hair for the children you loved. Make yourself as bald as an eagle, because they have gone from you into exile.
Woe to those who plan evil and do wrong while lying on their beds! When morning comes, they do it because they have the power to do so.
They covet fields and seize them, and houses, and they take them. They oppress a man and his home, a man and his inheritance.
Therefore, this is what the LORD says: "Look, I am planning disaster against this family. You will not be able to lift your necks from it, and you will not walk proudly, because it is an evil time."

On that day people will use a saying against you and mourn with bitter sorrow: "We are ruined! He has changed the share of my people. How He has taken it from me! He has given our fields to traitors."
So you will have no one in the LORD's assembly to measure out land for you by lot.
"Do not prophesy," they say. "Do not prophesy such things; disgrace will not overtake us."
House of Jacob, is the Spirit of the LORD short-tempered? Are these His actions? Don't My words help those who walk uprightly?
But lately My people have risen up as an enemy. You strip the robe from peaceful travelers, like men returning from war.
You drive the women of My people from their pleasant homes; you take away My blessing from their children forever.
Arise and go, for this is no place to rest, because of the uncleanness that destroys, even with a grievous destruction.
If a man walks after wind and lies, saying, "I will prophesy to you about wine and strong drink," he would be the prophet for this people!

I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will gather the remnant of Israel. I will put them together like sheep in a pen, like a flock in the middle of a pasture. They will make a lot of noise because so many people are there.
The one who breaks through goes ahead of them; they break through and pass through the gate and go out. Their king goes before them, with the LORD at their head.
Then I said, "Listen, you leaders of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel. Should you not know justice?
You hate good and love evil. You skin my people and strip the flesh from their bones.
You eat the flesh of my people, strip off their skin, and break their bones. You chop them up like meat for the pot, like flesh in a cauldron.
Then they will cry out to the LORD, but He will not answer them. At that time He will hide His face from them because of the evil they have done."
This is what the LORD says about the prophets who lead my people astray. They proclaim "Peace" to those who feed them, but declare war on those who do not feed them.
Therefore night will come upon you without visions, and darkness without any fortune-telling. The sun will set on the prophets, and the day will go dark around them.
Then the visionaries will be ashamed and the fortune tellers disgraced. They will all cover their mouths because there is no answer from God.
But as for me, I am filled with power, with the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and strength, to declare to Jacob his wrongdoing and to Israel his sin.
Hear this, you leaders of the house of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel, who despise justice and twist everything that is right.
who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with wrongdoing.
Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets tell fortunes for money. Yet they lean on the LORD, saying, "Is not the LORD among us? No disaster will come upon us."
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, and the temple mount a forested height.
In the last days, the mountain of the LORD's house will stand firm at the top of the mountains. It will be raised above the hills, and peoples will stream to it.

Many nations will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us His ways, and we will walk in His paths." For the law will go out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He will judge between many peoples and settle disputes for strong nations far away. They will turn their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not take up sword against nation, and they will not train for war anymore.
Each man will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, with no one to make them afraid. For the mouth of the LORD of Hosts has spoken.
For all the peoples follow their own gods, but we will follow the LORD our God forever and ever.
In that day, declares the LORD, "I will gather the lame. I will assemble the exiles and those I have afflicted.
I will make the lame a remnant, and the weak a strong nation. The LORD will rule over them in Mount Zion from then on and forever."
And you, watchtower of the flock, fortress of Daughter Zion, the former rule will come to you; the kingdom will come to Daughter Jerusalem.
Why do you now cry aloud? Is there no king in you? Has your counselor perished, so that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?

Writhe and groan, Daughter Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you will leave the city and live in the fields. You will go to Babylon; there you will be rescued. There the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
Now many nations are gathered against you, saying, "Let her be defiled, and let our eyes look on Zion."
But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD; they do not understand His plan, that He has gathered them like sheaves for the threshing floor.

Arise and thresh, Daughter Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze. You will crush many peoples, and I will devote their profits to the LORD and their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
Now, O city of soldiers, gather your troops. They have set a siege against us. They will strike the ruler of Israel on the cheek with a rod.
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, are small among the clans of Judah. Yet from you will come for Me a ruler over Israel. His origins are from long ago, from ancient times.
So He will let them go until the woman in labor has her child. Then the rest of His brothers will return to the people of Israel.
He will stand and shepherd His people with the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD His God. They will live in safety, because now He will be great to the ends of the earth.
This One will be our peace. When Assyria invades our land and marches through our palaces, we will raise up seven shepherds and eight leaders against him.
They will rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod at its gates. He will rescue us from Assyria when it invades our land and crosses our borders.
The remnant of Jacob will be among many nations like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass. It comes without waiting for people and does not depend on human help.

The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the middle of many peoples, like a lion among forest animals and like a young lion among sheep. It tramples and tears as it passes through, and no one can rescue them.
Your hand will be raised over your enemies, and all your foes will be destroyed.
On that day, says the LORD, I will remove your horses from among you and destroy your chariots.
I will destroy the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds.
I will remove sorcery from your hand, and you will have no more fortune-tellers.
I will remove your carved idols and your sacred pillars from among you, and you will no longer bow down to what your hands have made.
I will tear out your Asherah poles from among you and destroy your cities.
In anger and wrath I will take revenge on the nations that did not listen.
Hear what the LORD says: "Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice."
Hear, O mountains, the LORD's case, and you lasting foundations of the earth. For the LORD has a case against His people, and He will contend with Israel.
"My people, what have I done to you? How have I worn you out? Answer Me!
"For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses before you, along with Aaron and Miriam.
"My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned and what Balaam son of Beor answered him. Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal, so you may know the LORD's righteous acts."
"With what shall I come before the LORD when I bow before the God on high? Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
"Would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my sin, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?"
He has shown you, people, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
The voice of the LORD calls to the city (and wisdom fears Your name): "Heed the rod and the One who ordained it.
"Are there still treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and a short measure that is cursed?
"Can I clear the man with wicked scales and a bag of false weights?
"For her rich men are full of violence; her residents speak lies, and their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.
"Therefore I am striking you with a severe blow, bringing ruin on you because of your sins.
"You will eat but not be satisfied, and your hunger will stay inside you. You will store things up but not save them, and what you save, I will give to the sword.
"You will sow but not reap; you will press olives but not anoint yourselves with oil; you will tread grapes but not drink wine.

"You have kept the statutes of Omri and all the practices of the house of Ahab; you have followed their advice. Therefore I will make you a ruin, and your people an object of scorn; you will bear the shame of My people."
Woe is me! I am like someone gathering summer fruit after the harvest, like someone picking leftover grapes. There is no cluster to eat, no ripe fig that I crave.
The faithful have vanished from the land; no honest person remains. They all lie in wait for blood; they trap each other with a net.
Their hands are skilled at doing evil. The prince and the judge ask for a bribe. The powerful man says whatever he wants, and they plot together to do wrong.
The best of them is like a briar; the most honest is worse than a thorn hedge. The day your watchmen warned about has come—your day of punishment. Now they will be confused.
Do not trust a friend; do not rely on a close companion. Guard the doors of your mouth from the one who lies in your arms.
For a son dishonors his father, a daughter rises against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the people in his own house.
But I will look to the the LORD; I will wait for the God who saves me. My God will hear me.
Do not rejoice over me, my enemy. Though I have fallen, I will rise again. Though I sit in darkness, the the LORD will be my light.
I have sinned against Him, so I will endure the the LORD's anger until He argues my case and does what is right for me. He will bring me into the light, and I will see His goodness.
Then my enemy will see and be covered with shame—she who said to me, 'Where is the the LORD your God?' My eyes will see her; now she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
The day will come to rebuild your walls; on that day your borders will be extended.
In that day people will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the Euphrates, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
