The earth will become empty because of those who live in it, as a result of what they have done.
Shepherd Your people with Your staff, the flock of Your inheritance, who live alone in a forest, in the middle of Carmel. Let them feed in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show them wonders.
The nations will see and be ashamed of all their power. They will put their hands over their mouths, and their ears will be deaf.

They will lick dust like a snake, like creatures that crawl on the ground. They will come trembling out of their strongholds. They will turn in fear to the the LORD our God, and they will be afraid of You.
Who is a God like You, who forgives sin and passes over the wrongdoing of the remnant of His people? He does not stay angry forever, because He delights in showing faithful love.
He will have compassion on us again; He will trample our sins underfoot. You will throw all their sins into the depths of the sea.
You will show faithfulness to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as You promised our ancestors long ago.
A message about Nineveh. This is the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD is avenging and full of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on His foes and stores up wrath for His enemies.
The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will not let the guilty go unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and the storm, and clouds are the dust of His feet.
He rebukes the sea and dries it up; He dries up all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the bloom of Lebanon fades.
The mountains shake before Him, and the hills melt away. The earth trembles at His presence, along with the world and everyone who lives in it.
Who can stand before His anger? Who can survive the heat of His wrath? His fury is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered before Him.
The LORD is good, a safe place in times of trouble. He knows those who trust in Him.
But with a rushing flood He will completely destroy its place, and darkness will chase His enemies.
What do you plan against the LORD? He will completely destroy; trouble will not rise up a second time.
For they are tangled like thorns, and like drunkards they are destroyed; they burn like dry stubble.
From you came a person who plans evil against the LORD, a worthless counselor.
This is what the LORD says: "Though they are strong and many, they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
Now I will break his yoke off you and snap your bonds."

The LORD has commanded concerning you: "Your name will no longer be passed on. I will cut off the carved idol and the metal idol from the house of your gods. I will make your grave, for you are worthless."

Look, on the mountains are the feet of one who brings good news, who announces peace! Celebrate your feasts, O Judah; keep your vows. For the wicked will never again march through you; he is completely cut off.
A scatterer advances against you. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Brace yourself! Gather all your strength!
For the LORD will restore Jacob's glory like Israel's glory, because destroyers have stripped them bare and ruined their branches.
The shields of his mighty men are red; his soldiers are dressed in scarlet. The chariots flash like fire when he prepares for battle, and the cypress spears are brandished.
The chariots race through the streets and rush through the squares. They look like torches; they dart like lightning.
He remembers his officers. They stumble as they march. They hurry to the wall; the siege shield is set up.
The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace melts away.
It is decided: she is stripped and carried away. Her servant girls moan like doves and beat their breasts.
Nineveh is like a pool of water, but its people are fleeing. "Stop! Stop!" they cry, but no one turns back.
Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure, and wealth comes from every precious thing.
She is emptied! She is drained! She is stripped! Hearts melt, knees shake, bodies tremble, and every face grows pale.
Where is the lions' den, the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and lioness walked with their cubs, with no one to make them afraid?
The lion tore prey for his cubs and strangled it for his lionesses. He filled his caves with prey and his dens with torn flesh.

Look, I am against you, declares the LORD of Hosts. I will burn up your chariots in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will be heard no more.
Woe to the city of blood, full of lies, full of plunder, never without victims!
The crack of the whip and the rumble of wheels, galloping horses and bouncing chariots!
Charging horsemen, flashing swords, and shining spears! Many are slain, piles of dead bodies, corpses without end—they trip over their dead.
Because of the prostitute's many acts of prostitution—she is charming but deadly—she sells whole nations through her prostitution and families through her sorcery.
"I am against you," declares the LORD of Hosts. "I will lift your skirt over your face; I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.
I will throw filth on you and treat you with contempt; I will make you a public disgrace."
Then everyone who sees you will shrink back and say, 'Nineveh is destroyed! Who will mourn for her?' Where can I find anyone to comfort you?
Are you better than Thebes, which sits by the Nile with water all around it? The river was her protection, and water was her wall.
Cush and Egypt were her endless strength; Put and Libya were her allies.
Yet she became an exile and went into captivity. Her infants were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her nobles, and all her great men were bound in chains.
You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding. You too will seek refuge from the enemy.
All your fortresses are like fig trees with ripe figs: when shaken, the figs fall into the mouth of the eater.
Look, your people are women in your midst; the gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire has eaten away your bars.
Draw water for the siege; strengthen your fortresses. Go into the clay and tread the mortar; repair the brick kiln.
There the fire will consume you; the sword will cut you down. It will devour you like the young locust. Multiply like the young locust; multiply like the swarming locust!
You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of heaven. The young locust strips the land and flies away.
Your leaders are like swarming locusts, and your officials like clouds of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where.
O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber; your leaders are asleep. Your people are scattered on the mountains with no one to gather them.
There is no healing for your wound; your injury is fatal. All who hear the news of you clap their hands over you, for who has not felt your endless cruelty?
This is the message that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
“How long, the LORD, must I call for help, but You do not listen? I cry out to You, ‘Violence!’ but You do not save.
Why do You make me see wrongdoing, and why do You make me look at trouble? Harm and violence are in front of me. Fighting and arguing keep happening.
So the law has lost its power, and justice never happens. Wicked people surround good people, so justice is turned upside down.”
The LORD says, “Look at the nations and watch. Be completely amazed, because I am doing something in your days that you would not believe, even if someone told you.
I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hot-tempered nation. They march across the whole earth to take homes that are not theirs.
They are frightening and terrible. They make their own rules and honor themselves.
“Their horses are faster than leopards and fiercer than wolves at evening. Their horsemen charge ahead. Their riders come from far away. They fly like an eagle swooping down to eat.
They all come to do violence. Their faces look straight ahead. They gather captives like sand.
They make fun of kings and laugh at rulers. They laugh at every strong city. They pile up dirt and capture cities.
Then they sweep by like the wind and move on. They are guilty, because their strength is their god.”
“Are You not from long ago, the LORD my God, my Holy One? We will not die. The LORD, You have appointed them for judgment. You, the Rock, have set them up to correct us.
Your eyes are too pure to look at evil. You cannot stand wrongdoing. Why do You look at traitors? Why are You silent while the wicked destroy people more righteous than themselves?
You have made people like fish in the sea, like sea creatures with no ruler.
“The Chaldeans pull all of them up with a hook. They catch them in their net and gather them in their dragnet. Then they are happy and glad.
So they sacrifice to their net and burn incense to their dragnet, because by them they get rich and have plenty of food.
Will they keep emptying their net and destroying nations without mercy?”
I will stand at my watch and take my place on the wall. I will look to see what He will say to me and what answer I am to give to this complaint.
The LORD answered me: “Write down the revelation and make it plain on tablets, so that a messenger can run with it.
For the vision waits for an appointed time; it speaks of the end and will not prove false. Though it lingers, wait for it, because it will surely come and will not be late.
See, the enemy is puffed up; his desires are not upright. But the righteous person will live by his faithfulness.

“Indeed, wine betrays him; he is proud and never rests. Because he is as greedy as the grave and like death is never satisfied, he gathers all the nations to himself and takes all the peoples captive.
“Will not all of them taunt him with ridicule and scorn, saying, ‘ “Woe to him who piles up stolen goods and gets rich by cheating others! How long must this go on?’
“Will not your creditors suddenly rise up? Will they not wake up and make you tremble? Then you will become their prey.
Because you have plundered many nations, the peoples who are left will plunder you. For you have shed human blood; you have destroyed lands and cities and everyone in them.
“Woe to him who builds his house by unjust gain, setting his nest on high to escape ruin!
You have planned shame for your house by cutting off many peoples and forfeiting your life.
The stones of the wall will cry out, and the beams of the woodwork will answer.
“Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town by injustice!
Has not the LORD Almighty determined that the people's labor is only fuel for the fire, that the nations exhaust themselves for nothing?
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
“Woe to him who gives drink to his neighbor, pouring from the wineskin until they are drunk, so that he can gaze on their naked bodies!

You will be filled with shame instead of glory. Now it is your turn! Drink and let your nakedness be exposed! The cup from the LORD's right hand is coming around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory.

The violence you committed against Lebanon will overwhelm you, and your destruction of animals will terrify you. For you have shed human blood; you have destroyed lands and cities and everyone in them.
“Of what value is an idol carved by a craftsman? Or an image that teaches lies? For the one who makes it trusts in his own creation; he makes idols that cannot speak.
Woe to him who says to wood, ‘Come to life!’ or to lifeless stone, ‘Wake up!’ Can it give guidance? It is covered with gold and silver; there is no breath in it.
The LORD is in His holy temple; let all the earth be silent before Him.”
This is a prayer of Habakkuk the prophet.
The LORD, I have heard what people say about You, and I am afraid. the LORD, bring Your work back to life in our time. Make it known in our time. Even when You are angry, remember mercy.
God came from Teman, and the Holy One came from Mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens, and His praise filled the earth.
His brightness was like the light. Rays flashed from His hand, and His power was hidden there.
Sickness went before Him, and burning trouble followed at His feet.
He stood and measured the earth. He looked and made the nations tremble. The old mountains broke apart, and the lasting hills bowed down. His ways last forever.
I saw the tents of Cushan in trouble, and the tent curtains of Midian shook.
Were You angry with the rivers, O the LORD? Was Your wrath against the rivers? Did You ride on Your horses, Your chariots of salvation?
You uncovered Your bow and called for many arrows. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
The mountains saw You and shook. A flood of water rushed by. The deep sea roared and raised its waves high.
The sun and moon stood still in the sky. They moved at the light of Your arrows, at the flash of Your shining spear.
You marched through the earth in anger. You crushed the nations in fury.
You came to save Your people, to save Your chosen one. You crushed the leader of the wicked house, laying him bare from top to bottom. Selah.
You struck their warriors with their own arrows. They rushed like a whirlwind to scatter me, and they rejoiced as if they were secretly swallowing up the poor.
You trampled the sea with Your horses, stirring up many waters.
I heard, and my body shook. My lips trembled at the sound. Weakness entered my bones, and I shook all over. Yet I will wait quietly for the day of trouble, when the enemy comes against my people.

Even if the fig tree does not bloom and the vines have no grapes; even if the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food; even if the sheep are taken from the pen and there are no cattle in the stalls.
Yet I will rejoice in the the LORD. I will be glad in the God who saves me.
The LORD, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like the feet of a deer and lets me walk on the high places. For the music leader, with stringed instruments.
This is the word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah. It came during the time of King Josiah son of Amon of Judah.
“I will sweep away everything from the face of the earth,” declares the LORD.

“I will sweep away people and animals. I will sweep away the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea. I will remove the idols that make wicked people fall. I will destroy the wicked and remove people from the earth,” declares the LORD.

“I will stretch out My hand against Judah and against all who live in Jerusalem. I will remove from this place what is left of Baal worship, along with the names of the pagan priests and the other priests.
I will punish those who bow down on their rooftops to the stars, those who bow down and swear loyalty to the LORD but also swear loyalty to Milcom,
and those who turn away from following the LORD, and those who do not look for the LORD or ask Him for help.”
Be silent before the Lord the LORD, for the day of the LORD is near. The LORD has prepared a sacrifice; He has set apart His guests.
“On the day of the LORD's sacrifice, I will punish the leaders, the king's sons, and everyone who wears clothes from other nations.
On that day I will punish everyone who jumps over the doorway and fills his master's house with violence and lies.”
“On that day,” declares the LORD, “a cry will come from the Fish Gate, a wail from the Second District, and a loud crash from the hills.”
“Wail, you who live in the market district, for all the traders are ruined; everyone who weighs silver is destroyed.”
“At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps and punish the men who are comfortable in their sins and do not care, who say in their hearts, ‘The LORD will not do good or evil.’”
Their wealth will be taken, and their houses will be destroyed. They will build houses but not live in them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.
The great day of the LORD is near, very near and coming fast. The sound of the day of the LORD is bitter; even strong warriors cry out.
That day is a day of anger, a day of trouble and distress, a day of ruin and destruction, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness.
It is a day of trumpet blasts and war cries against the fortified cities and the high towers.
“I will bring trouble on people, so they walk like blind men, because they sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their bodies like garbage.”

Neither their silver nor their gold will save them on the day of the LORD's anger. The whole earth will be burned up by the fire of His jealousy. For He will quickly destroy all who live on the earth.
Gather together, yes, gather, O nation with no shame,
before the decree takes effect and the day passes like chaff, before the LORD's fierce anger comes on you, before the day of the LORD comes on you.
Seek the LORD, all you humble people of the land, who carry out His justice. Seek what is right; seek humility. Perhaps you will be hidden on the day of the LORD's wrath.
For Gaza will be left empty, and Ashkelon will be ruined. Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron will be torn up.
How terrible for the people who live by the sea, the nation of the Cherethites! The LORD's word is against you, O Canaan, land of the Philistines. I will destroy you until no one is left.
The seacoast will become pastures, with wells for shepherds and sheep pens.

It will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; there they will graze. In the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down in the evening, for the LORD their God will care for them and bring back their captives.
I have heard the insults of Moab and the taunts of the Ammonites, when they insulted My people and made threats against their land.

Therefore, as surely as I live, declares the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, Moab will become like Sodom, and the Ammonites like Gomorrah—a place of weeds and salt pits, ruined forever. The remnant of My people will plunder them, and the survivors of My nation will take their land.
This is what they will get for their pride, because they insulted and boasted against the people of the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD will be terrifying to them when He starves all the gods of the earth. Then the nations on every shore will bow down to Him, each in its own place.
You Cushites will also be killed by My sword.
He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria. He will make Nineveh a wasteland, dry as the desert.

Flocks and herds will lie down in her, along with all kinds of animals. Even the owl and the porcupine will live among her pillars. Their calls will echo from the windows; rubble will be on the thresholds, for her cedar beams will be exposed.

This is the city that used to be so happy, that lived in safety and said in her heart, "I am the one, and there is no one else." What a ruin she has become, a place where wild animals rest! Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.
How terrible for the city that oppresses people! It is rebellious and unclean.
It did not listen. It did not accept correction. It did not trust in the LORD. It did not draw near to its God.
Its leaders are like roaring lions. Its judges are like wolves that hunt at night. They leave nothing for the morning.
Its prophets are reckless and treacherous. Its priests have made the holy place unclean and have twisted the law.
The LORD is in the city. He is good and does no wrong. Every morning He gives fair judgment, and it never fails. But the wicked do not know shame.
I have destroyed nations. Their strong towers are empty. I ruined their streets so no one walks there. Their cities are destroyed, with no one left to live in them.
I said, "Surely you will fear Me and accept My correction. Then your home will not be destroyed, and I will not punish you as I planned." But they were quick to do every evil thing.

"So wait for Me," declares the LORD, "until the day I rise to judge. I have decided to gather the nations and kingdoms and pour out My anger on them—all My burning anger. The whole earth will be burned up by My jealous anger."
For then I will give the nations pure speech, so all of them can call on the LORD's name and serve Him side by side.
From beyond the rivers of Cush, My worshipers, the children of My scattered people, will bring Me their gifts.
On that day you will not be ashamed of the wrong things you did against Me. For then I will remove from you the proud boasters, and you will stop being proud on My holy mountain.
I will leave among you people who are humble and poor, and they will trust in the LORD's name.
The rest of Israel will not do wrong or tell lies. No deceitful words will be found in their mouths. They will eat and rest, and no one will scare them.
Sing, people of Zion! Shout, Israel! Be glad and celebrate with all your heart, people of Jerusalem!
The LORD has taken away your punishment. He has turned your enemy away. The LORD, the King of Israel, is among you. You will never again be afraid of disaster.
On that day people will say to Jerusalem, "Do not be afraid, Zion. Do not let your hands become weak."
The LORD your God is with you. He is mighty to save. He will take great delight in you. He will calm you with His love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
I will gather those among you who are sad because the festivals are gone, so you will not be shamed anymore.
At that time I will deal with all who hurt you. I will save the lame and gather the outcast. I will give them praise and honor in every land where they were shamed.
"At that time I will bring you home. When I gather you, I will make you famous and praised among all the nations, when I bring your people back from captivity before your eyes," says the LORD.

In the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Haggai to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: "These people say, 'The time has not come. It is not time to build the LORD's house.'"
Then the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet:
"Is it time for you to live in your paneled houses while this house is in ruins?"
Now this is what the LORD of Hosts says: "Think carefully about how you are living.

You plant a lot, but you harvest little. You eat, but you are still hungry. You drink, but you are still thirsty. You put on clothes, but you are still cold. And the worker who earns money puts it in a bag with holes."
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: "Think carefully about how you are living.
Go up to the mountains, bring wood, and build the house. Then I will take pleasure in it and be honored," says the LORD.

"You expected a big harvest, but it was small. And when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why?" declares the LORD of Hosts. "Because My house is in ruins while each of you is busy with his own house.
That is why the sky has held back its dew and the ground has held back its crops.
I have called for a drought on the land and hills, on grain, new wine, olive oil, and on everything the ground produces, on people and animals, and on all the work of your hands."

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and all the rest of the people obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, because the LORD their God had sent him. And the people feared the LORD.
Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, gave the LORD's message to the people: "I am with you," declares the LORD.

Then the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people. They came and worked on the house of the LORD of Hosts, their God.
They did this on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet.
The LORD told him to speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah; to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest; and to the rest of the people. He said,
"Who is left among you who saw this temple in its first glory? How does it look to you now? Does it not seem like nothing to you?

Yet now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the LORD. Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, says the LORD, and work, for I am with you, says the LORD of Hosts.
I made a promise to you when you came out of Egypt, and My Spirit stays among you, so do not be afraid."
"For the LORD of Hosts says: In a little while I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
I will shake all the nations, and the wealth of all the nations will come. I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of Hosts.
The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine, says the LORD of Hosts.
The glory of this later house will be greater than the glory of the first one, says the LORD of Hosts. In this place I will give peace, says the LORD of Hosts."
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet.
The LORD of Hosts said, "Ask the priests about the law.
If a man carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and that fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, will that food become holy?" The priests answered, "No."
Then Haggai said, "If someone is unclean because of a dead body and touches any of these things, will they become unclean?" The priests answered, "Yes, they will become unclean."
Then Haggai said, "So it is with this people and this nation before Me, says the LORD. So is every work of their hands, and what they offer there is unclean."
Then the LORD said, "Now think carefully about this from today on, remembering the time before a stone was laid on a stone in the LORD's temple.
When you came to a heap of grain expecting twenty measures, there were only ten. When you came to the winepress to draw fifty measures, there were only twenty.
I struck you with blight, mildew, and hail in all the work of your hands, yet you did not turn to Me, says the LORD.
Think carefully from this day on—from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the LORD's temple foundation was laid. Think carefully.
Is the seed still in the barn? Have the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree not yet produced fruit? From this day on I will bless you."
A second time, on the twenty-fourth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to Haggai.
The LORD told Haggai to speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, and say, "I will shake the heavens and the earth.
I will overthrow the thrones of kingdoms and destroy the power of the nations' kingdoms. I will overthrow chariots and their riders; horses and their riders will fall, each by his brother's sword.
On that day, says the LORD of Hosts, I will take you, My servant Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, says the LORD, and make you like My signet ring, for I have chosen you, says the LORD of Hosts."
In the eighth month, in the second year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo. He said:
"The LORD was very angry with your fathers.
Therefore tell the people, 'This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Return to Me, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will return to you,' says the LORD of Hosts.

"Do not be like your fathers. The earlier prophets called out to them and said, 'This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Turn from your evil ways and your evil deeds.' But they did not listen or pay attention to Me, declares the LORD.
"Where are your fathers now? And the prophets—do they live forever?

But did not My words and My laws, which I commanded My servants the prophets, catch up with your fathers? Then they turned back and said, 'Just as the LORD of Hosts planned to do to us because of our ways and our deeds, so He has done to us.'"
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo. He said:
I saw during the night. There was a man riding a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees in the ravine. Behind him were red, reddish-brown, and white horses.
Then I asked, "What are these, my lord?" The angel who was speaking with me said, "I will show you what they are."
The man standing among the myrtle trees said, "These are the ones the LORD has sent to patrol the earth."
They answered the angel of the LORD who was standing among the myrtle trees, "We have patrolled the earth, and look, all the earth is sitting still and quiet."
Then the angel of the LORD said, "O LORD of Hosts, how long will You have no compassion for Jerusalem and the cities of Judah? You have been angry with them these seventy years."
The LORD answered the angel who was speaking with me with good and comforting words.
So the angel who was speaking with me told me, "Proclaim this: 'This is what the LORD of Hosts says: I am very jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion.
I am very angry with the nations that are at ease. I was only a little angry, but they helped bring disaster.'

Therefore this is what the LORD says: 'I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion. My house will be built in it,' declares the LORD of Hosts, 'and a measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.'
Proclaim again: 'This is what the LORD of Hosts says: My cities will again overflow with prosperity, and the LORD will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.'"
Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there were four horns.
So I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these?" He said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.

I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, so that no man could lift up his head. But these craftsmen have come to terrify them and to throw down the horns of the nations who lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
I looked up and saw a man. He was holding a measuring line in his hand.
I asked him, “Where are you going?” He said, “I am going to measure Jerusalem. I want to see how wide it is and how long it is.”
Then the angel who had been talking with me came out. Another angel came out to meet him.
The other angel said to him, “Run and tell that young man, ‘Jerusalem will be a city without walls because of the many people and animals living in it.’”
“For I will be a wall of fire around her,” declares the LORD. “I will be the glory inside her.”
“Get up! Get up! Run away from the land of the north,” declares the LORD. “For I have scattered you in every direction,” declares the LORD.
“Get up! Escape to Zion, you who live in Babylon!”
For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “After He was honored, He sent me to the nations that robbed you. Anyone who touches you touches something very dear to Him.
I will wave My hand over them, so they will become loot for their own servants. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me.”
“Sing and be happy, people of Zion, for I am coming to live among you,” declares the LORD.
“On that day many nations will join the LORD and become My people. I will live among you, and you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you.”
The LORD will take Judah as His own land in the Holy Land, and He will choose Jerusalem again.
Be quiet before the LORD, all people, for He has awakened from His holy home.
Then I was shown Joshua the high priest standing before the Angel of the LORD, with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him.
And the LORD said to Satan, “The LORD rebuke you, Satan! The LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebuke you! Is this not a burning stick pulled from the fire?”
Now Joshua was wearing filthy clothes as he stood before the angel.
The angel spoke to those standing before him and said, “Take off his filthy clothes.” Then he said to Joshua, “See, I have taken away your sin, and I will dress you in fine clothes.”
Then I said, “Put a clean turban on his head.” So they put a clean turban on his head and clothed him, while the Angel of the LORD stood by.
The Angel of the LORD gave Joshua this charge:
“This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘If you walk in My ways and keep My charge, you will judge My house and guard My courtyards. I will also let you walk among these who are standing here.
‘Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your friends who sit before you. They are men who are a sign. I am bringing My servant, the Branch.
‘Look, the stone I have set before Joshua has seven eyes on one stone. I will carve its inscription, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will remove the sin of this land in one day.
‘In that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, each of you will invite your neighbor to sit under his vine and under his fig tree.’”
The angel who had been speaking with me came back and woke me, like someone waking up from sleep.
He asked, “What do you see?” I answered, “I see a lampstand made of solid gold, with a bowl on top and seven lamps on it. There are seven channels to the lamps on top.”
There are two olive trees beside it—one on the right of the bowl and one on the left.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”
The angel answered, “Don’t you know what these are?” “No, my lord,” I said.
He said, “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: ‘Not by might and not by power, but by My Spirit,’ says the LORD of Hosts.”
“What are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain. He will bring out the capstone while people shout, ‘Grace, grace to it!’”
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
“The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house. His hands will finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you.”
“For who despises the day of small things? These seven are the eyes of the LORD. They range through all the earth. They will be glad when they see the plumb line in Zerubbabel’s hand.”
Then I asked him, “What are these two olive trees on the right and left of the lampstand?”
I asked a second time, “What are these two olive branches beside the two gold pipes that pour out golden oil?”
He said, “Don’t you know what these are?” “No, my lord,” I said.
He said, “These are the two anointed ones who stand by the Lord of all the earth.”
I turned and looked up again, and I saw a flying scroll.
The angel asked me, "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a flying scroll. It is twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."

He said to me, "This is the curse that is going out over the whole earth. On one side it says every thief will be removed, and on the other side it says every person who swears falsely will be removed."

The LORD of Hosts declares, "I will send it out. It will enter the house of the thief and the house of the person who swears falsely by My name. It will stay in that house and destroy it, along with its wood and stones."
The angel who was speaking with me came forward and said, "Look up and see what this is that is going out."
I asked, "What is it?" He answered, "It is a measuring basket that is going out. This is what their sin looks like all over the earth."
Then I saw a heavy lead cover being lifted, and inside the basket sat a woman.
The angel said, "This is Wickedness." He threw her back into the basket and put the heavy lead cover over its opening.
I looked up again and saw two women coming out with the wind in their wings. Their wings were like stork wings. They lifted the basket up between heaven and earth.
I asked the angel, "Where are they taking the basket?"
He answered, "They are taking the basket to build a house for the woman in the land of Shinar. When the house is ready, she will be placed there on her base."
I turned and lifted my eyes and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains. The mountains were made of bronze.
The first chariot had red horses, the second had black horses,
the third had white horses, and the fourth had strong, spotted horses.
I asked the angel who was speaking to me, "What are these, my lord?"
The angel answered, "These are the four spirits of heaven. They go out from where they stood before the Lord of all the earth.
The chariot with black horses goes to the north country, the white horses follow them, and the spotted horses go to the south country.
The strong horses went out and wanted to patrol the earth. He said, 'Go and patrol the earth!' So they patrolled the earth."
Then he called out to me and said, "Look! The horses going to the north have brought My Spirit to rest in the north country."
The word of the the LORD came to me:
"Take silver and gold from the exiles—Heldai, Tobiah, and Jedaiah—who came from Babylon. On that same day, go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
Make crowns from the silver and gold, and put them on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest."
Tell him, "This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: 'Here is a man whose name is the Branch. He will grow where He is and build the temple of the the LORD.'
He will build the temple of the the LORD, wear royal glory, sit and rule on His throne, and be a priest on His throne. There will be peace between the two.'"
The crowns will be kept in the temple of the the LORD as a reminder for Helem, Tobiah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah.

People from far away will come and help build the temple of the the LORD. Then you will know that the the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you. This will happen if you carefully listen to the voice of the the LORD your God."
In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Kislev.
Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, along with their men, to seek the the LORD's favor.
They asked the priests of the house of the the LORD of Hosts and the prophets, "Should I keep mourning and fasting in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?"
Then the word of the the LORD of Hosts came to me:
"Say to all the people of the land and to the priests, 'When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months these seventy years, were you really fasting for Me?
And when you ate and drank, were you not eating and drinking for yourselves?

Are these not the words the the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets when Jerusalem and its surrounding towns were at rest and prosperous, and the Negev and the western foothills were inhabited?'"
And the word of the the LORD came to Zechariah:
"This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: 'Administer true justice, and show mercy and compassion to one another.
Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor. Do not plot evil against one another in your hearts.'"
But they refused to listen and stubbornly turned away; they would not hear.
They hardened their hearts and would not listen to the law or to the words the the LORD of Hosts had sent by His Spirit through the earlier prophets. So great anger came from the the LORD of Hosts.
"Therefore, just as they would not listen when I called, so I will not listen when they call," says the the LORD of Hosts.

"I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations they had not known, and the land was left so empty and ruined behind them that no one could come or go. Thus they made the pleasant land a wasteland."
The word of the LORD of Hosts came to me.
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I burn with great anger for her.'"
"This is what the LORD says: 'I have returned to Zion and will live in Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of Hosts will be called the Holy Mountain.'"
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Old men and old women will again sit in the streets of Jerusalem. Each one will hold a cane because of old age.
The streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing there.'"
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'If this seems amazing to the people who are left in those days, should it seem amazing to Me?' declares the LORD of Hosts."
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'I will save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the west.
I will bring them back to live in Jerusalem. They will be My people, and I will be their God in truth and righteousness.'"

"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Let your hands be strong, you who now hear these words from the prophets who were there when the foundation of the house of the LORD of Hosts was laid, so the temple could be built.
Before those days, people and animals earned no wages. No one was safe from enemies when coming or going, because I had turned everyone against his neighbor.
But now I will not treat the rest of this people as I did in the past,' declares the LORD of Hosts."
"For the seed will prosper. The vine will give its fruit, the land will give its crops, and the sky will give its dew. I will give the people who are left all these things.
Just as you have been a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong."
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Just as I planned to bring disaster on you when your fathers made Me angry, and I did not change My mind,' says the LORD of Hosts."
"So now I have planned to do good for Jerusalem and the house of Judah. Do not be afraid."
"These are the things you must do: Speak the truth to one another. Give true and fair judgments in your gates.
Do not plan evil against one another in your hearts. Do not love to swear falsely, because I hate all these things," declares the LORD.
The word of the LORD of Hosts came to me, saying,

"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will become times of joy and gladness and happy festivals for the house of Judah. So love truth and peace.'"
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Peoples will still come, even people from many cities.
The people of one city will go to another and say, "Let us go at once to ask the LORD for favor and to seek the LORD of Hosts. I will go too."
Many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem and to ask the LORD for favor.
In those days, ten men from all nations and languages will grab the corner of a Jewish man's robe and say, "Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you."'"
An oracle: The word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach and Damascus, its resting place. For the eyes of all people and all the tribes of Israel are on the LORD.
Hamath too borders it; Tyre and Sidon, though very wise.
Tyre has built herself a fortress; she has piled up silver like dust and gold like mud in the streets.
Look, the Lord will take her over and strike her wealth into the sea; she will be consumed by fire.
Ashkelon will see and be afraid; Gaza will writhe in pain; Ekron too, because her hope is gone. The king will die in Gaza, and Ashkelon will no longer be lived in.
A mixed people will live in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
I will remove blood from their mouths and forbidden things from between their teeth. The survivors will belong to our God and be like a clan in Judah; Ekron will be like the Jebusites.
I will camp around My house to guard it from armies. No one will pass through or return, and no oppressor will pass over them again, for now I have seen with My own eyes.
Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion! Shout, Daughter Jerusalem! Look, your King is coming to you. He is righteous and brings salvation. He is humble and rides on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem. The bow of war will be cut off, and He will speak peace to the nations. His rule will stretch from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.
As for you, by the blood of your covenant I have sent your prisoners out of the pit with no water.
Return to the stronghold, you prisoners of hope. Even today I declare that I will restore double to you.
For I have bent Judah as My bow and filled it with Ephraim. I will stir up your sons, Zion, against the sons of Greece, and I will make you like a warrior's sword.
Then the LORD will appear over them, and His arrow will shoot out like lightning. The Lord the LORD will blow the trumpet and march in the storms of the south.
The LORD of Hosts will protect them. They will devour and conquer sling stones. They will drink and roar like wine. They will be filled like bowls, like the corners of the altar.
On that day the LORD their God will save them as the flock of His people, for they are like jewels in a crown lifted over His land.
How great is His goodness and beauty! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women.
Ask the LORD for rain when the spring rains come. The LORD makes the lightning, and He will give you showers of rain, and the fields will grow grass.
Household gods speak lies, and fortune-tellers see false visions. They tell empty dreams and give false comfort. So the people wander like sheep and suffer because there is no shepherd.
“My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the leaders. For the LORD of Hosts cares for His flock, the people of Judah. He will make them like a proud war horse.
From Judah will come the cornerstone, the tent peg, the battle bow, and every ruler.
They will be like warriors trampling mud in the streets. They will fight because the LORD is with them, and they will put the horsemen to shame.

“I will strengthen the people of Judah and save the people of Joseph. I will bring them back because I have had mercy on them. They will be as if I had never rejected them, for I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
Ephraim will be like a strong man. Their hearts will be glad, like people who have drunk wine. Their children will see it and be glad; their hearts will rejoice in the LORD.
I will whistle for them and gather them, for I have set them free. They will grow as they grew before.
“I will plant them among the nations. In faraway lands they will remember Me, and they and their children will live and return.
I will bring them back from Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon, but there will not be enough room for them.

He will pass through the sea of trouble and strike the waves of the sea. All the deep places of the Nile will dry up. The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and Egypt’s rod of power will pass away.
I will make them strong in the LORD, and they will walk in His name,” says the LORD.
Open your gates, Lebanon, so fire can burn your cedar trees.
Wail, cypress, because the cedar has fallen and the mighty trees are ruined. Wail, oaks of Bashan, because the thick forest has been cut down.
Listen to the shepherds wail, because their glory is destroyed. Listen to the young lions roar, because the Jordan's thickets are ruined.
This is what the LORD my God says: “Pasture the flock that is marked for slaughter.
Their buyers kill them and are not punished. Their sellers say, ‘Praise the LORD, because I am rich!’ Even their shepherds show them no pity.

For I will no longer pity the people who live in this land,” says the LORD. “Instead, I will hand every person over to his neighbor and to his king. They will crush the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their power.”
So I pastured the flock marked for slaughter, especially the oppressed among them. I took two staffs. I named one Favor and the other Union, and I pastured the flock.
In one month I got rid of three shepherds. I grew tired of them, and they hated me.
Then I said, “I will not shepherd you anymore. Let the dying die, the perishing perish, and let the survivors eat one another's flesh.”
I took my staff called Favor and broke it, ending the covenant I had made with all the nations.
So it was broken that day. The poor sheep who watched me knew that this was the LORD's word.
Then I said to them, “If it seems good to you, give me my pay; if not, keep it.” So they weighed out my pay: thirty pieces of silver.
Then the LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter—the handsome price they put on Me!” So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter in the LORD's house.
Then I broke my second staff, Union, to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
Then the LORD said to me, “Take for yourself the gear of a foolish shepherd.

For I am about to raise up a shepherd in the land who will not care for the lost, will not look for the young, will not heal the injured, and will not feed the healthy. Instead, he will eat the meat of the fat sheep and tear off their hooves.
Woe to the worthless shepherd who abandons the flock! A sword will strike his arm and right eye. His arm will dry up completely, and his right eye will go blind.”
This is a message from the LORD about Israel. The LORD declares it. He is the One who stretches out the heavens, lays the earth’s foundation, and forms the human spirit inside each person.
“Look, I will make Jerusalem like a cup of strong drink that makes all the surrounding nations stagger. Judah will be surrounded and attacked along with Jerusalem.
On that day, when all the nations of the earth gather against her, I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone that no one can move. Everyone who tries to lift it will hurt themselves.
On that day, declares the LORD, I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness. I will keep My eyes on Judah, but I will strike all the horses of the nations with blindness.”
Then the leaders of Judah will say in their hearts, “The people of Jerusalem are my strength through the LORD of Hosts, their God.”

“On that day I will make the leaders of Judah like a firepot in a pile of wood and like a torch among dry grain. They will burn up all the surrounding nations on every side. Jerusalem will be lived in again, safe in its own place.
The LORD will save the people of Judah first, so that the glory of David’s family and the glory of the people of Jerusalem will not be greater than Judah’s glory.
On that day the LORD will defend the people of Jerusalem. The weakest among them will be like David, and David’s family will be like God, like the Angel of the LORD going before them.
On that day I will destroy every nation that comes against Jerusalem.”

“Then I will pour out on David’s family and on the people of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and prayer. They will look on Me, the One they have pierced, and they will mourn for Him as one mourns for an only child. They will grieve bitterly for Him as one grieves for a firstborn.”
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning for Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
The whole land will mourn, family by family, each alone. The family of David’s house and their wives will mourn alone. The family of Nathan’s house and their wives will mourn alone.
The family of Levi’s house and their wives will mourn alone. The family of Shimei’s house and their wives will mourn alone.
All the other families left, and their wives, will mourn alone too.
On that day a spring will be opened for the house of David and for the people living in Jerusalem. It will wash away sin and impurity.

The LORD of Armies says, “On that day I will wipe out the names of the idols from the land, so they will not be remembered anymore. I will also remove the prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.”

If anyone still prophesies, his father and mother who gave birth to him will say, “You must not live, because you have spoken lies in the name of the LORD.” If he keeps prophesying, they will stab him.
On that day the prophets will be ashamed of the visions they prophesy. They will not wear a hairy coat to trick people.
He will say, “I am not a prophet. I work the land. I have been a farmer since I was young.”
If someone asks him, “What are these wounds on your body?” he will answer, “I was wounded in the house of my friends.”

“Awake, sword, against My shepherd, against the man who is My companion,” declares the LORD of Armies. “Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered. I will turn My hand against the little ones.”
“In all the land,” declares the LORD, “two-thirds will be cut off and die, but one-third will be left.”

“I will bring that third through fire and refine them like silver. I will test them like gold. They will call on My name, and I will answer them. I will say, ‘They are My people,’ and they will say, ‘The LORD is my God.’”
Look, the day of the LORD is coming. Your plunder will be divided among you.

I will gather all the nations to fight against Jerusalem. The city will be taken. Houses will be robbed. Women will be violated. Half the people will be taken away, but the rest won't be completely removed from the city.
Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations, just like He fights on a day of battle.

On that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The Mount of Olives will split in two from east to west, making a very large valley. Half the mountain will move north, and the other half will move south.

You will flee through the valley of My mountains, because that valley will reach to Azal. You will flee just like you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones will come with Him.
On that day there won't be any light. The bright lights in the sky will fade.
It will be a unique day that only the LORD knows. It won't be day or night, but in the evening there will be light.
On that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem. Half will go to the eastern sea, and half will go to the western sea. It will flow in summer and in winter.
On that day the LORD will be King over all the earth. The LORD will be the only one, and His name will be the only name.

All the land from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem, will be like the Arabah. But Jerusalem will be lifted up and stay where it is, from the Benjamin Gate to the place of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the royal winepresses.
People will live there, and there won't be a curse anymore. Jerusalem will live in safety.

This is the plague the LORD will use to strike all the nations that fought against Jerusalem: Their flesh will rot while they are still standing. Their eyes will rot in their sockets. Their tongues will rot in their mouths.
On that day the LORD will send a great panic among them. Each person will grab his neighbor's hand, and then his hand will be raised against his neighbor.
Judah will also fight in Jerusalem, and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered up—gold, silver, and clothes in great amounts.
A similar plague will strike the horses, mules, camels, donkeys, and all the other animals in those camps.
Then all the survivors from the nations that attacked Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, and to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
If any of the families of the earth don't go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, then no rain will fall on them.
If the Egyptians don't go up and take part, then no rain will fall on them. This will be the plague the LORD uses against the nations that don't go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
This will be the punishment for Egypt and for all the nations that don't go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
On that day, HOLY TO the LORD will be written on the bells of the horses. The cooking pots in the LORD's house will be like the bowls before the altar.

In fact, every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts. Everyone who sacrifices will come and take some of them and cook in them. On that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Hosts.
This is a message from the the LORD to Israel, brought by Malachi.
"I have loved you," says the the LORD. But you ask, "How have you loved us?" "Was not Esau Jacob's brother?" declares the the LORD. "Yet I have loved Jacob,
but Esau I have hated. I made his mountains a wasteland and left his inheritance to the jackals of the desert."

Edom may say, "We have been crushed, but we will rebuild the ruins." This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: "They may build, but I will tear it down. People will call them the Wicked Land, a people the the LORD has cursed forever.
You will see it with your own eyes and say, "The The LORD is great, even beyond Israel's borders!"

"A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is My respect?" says the the LORD of Hosts. "It is you priests who dishonor My name. But you ask, 'How have we dishonored Your name?'"
"By offering polluted food on My altar. But you ask, 'How have we polluted You?' By saying that the the LORD's table is worthless."

"When you offer blind animals for sacrifice, is that not wrong? When you offer the lame or sick, is that not wrong? Try offering them to your governor. Would he be pleased with you? Would he accept you?" says the the LORD of Hosts.
"Now plead with God to be gracious to us. With such offerings from your hands, will He accept you?" says the the LORD of Hosts.

"If only one of you would shut the temple doors, so that you would not light useless fires on My altar! I am not pleased with you," says the the LORD of Hosts, "and I will accept no offering from your hands."

"My name will be great among the nations, from the rising of the sun to its setting. In every place incense and pure offerings will be brought to My name, because My name will be great among the nations," says the the LORD of Hosts.
"But you dishonor it when you say, 'The Lord's table is defiled, and its food is worthless.'"
"And you say, 'What a burden!' and you treat it with scorn," says the the LORD of Hosts. "When you bring injured, lame, or sick animals, should I accept them from your hands?" says the the LORD.

"Cursed is the cheat who has an acceptable male in his flock and vows to give it, but then sacrifices a blemished animal to the Lord. For I am a great King," says the the LORD of Hosts, "and My name is to be feared among the nations."
And now this command is for you priests.

"If you do not listen, and if you do not set your heart on honoring My name," says the LORD of Hosts, "I will send a curse on you, and I will curse your blessings. Yes, I have already cursed them, because you do not take it to heart."
"Look, I am going to rebuke your descendants. I will smear dung on your faces—the dung from your festival offerings—and you will be carried away with it."
"Then you will know that I sent this command to you, so that My covenant with Levi can continue," says the LORD of Hosts.
"My covenant with him was life and peace. I gave them to him. It called for respect, and he respected Me and stood in awe of My name."
True teaching was in his mouth, and no wrong was found on his lips. He walked with Me in peace and honesty, and he turned many people away from sin.
A priest's lips should guard knowledge, and people should seek teaching from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the LORD of Hosts.
"But you have turned from the way. You have caused many to stumble in your teaching. You have broken the covenant of Levi," says the LORD of Hosts.
"So I have made you hated and low before all the people, because you do not keep My ways. You also play favorites when you teach the law."
Don't we all have one Father? Didn't one God create us? Then why do we turn against each other and break the covenant our fathers made?
Judah has been unfaithful. A terrible thing has been done in Israel and Jerusalem. Judah has made unclean the holy place the LORD loves. He has married the daughter of a foreign god.
May the LORD remove from Jacob's tents anyone who does this, no matter who he is, even if he brings an offering to the LORD of Hosts.
Here is another thing you do: You cover the LORD's altar with tears, weeping, and groaning, because He no longer looks at your offering or accepts it with favor from your hand.
You ask, "Why?" Because the LORD has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth. You have been unfaithful to her, even though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.
Didn't God make them one, with a share of His Spirit? And what is He looking for? Godly children. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not betray the wife of your youth.

"For I hate divorce," says the LORD, the God of Israel. "I also hate when a man harms the wife he should protect," says the LORD of Hosts. "So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not be unfaithful."

You have worn out the LORD with your words. Yet you ask, "How have we worn Him out?" By saying, "Everyone who does evil is good in the LORD's eyes, and He is pleased with them," or, "Where is the God of justice?"

The LORD says, "Look, I am sending My messenger, and he will prepare the way before Me. Then the Lord you are looking for will suddenly come to His temple. The messenger of the covenant, whom you want, is coming," says the LORD of Hosts.
But who can survive the day He comes? Who can stand when He appears? He will be like a fire that refines metal or like strong soap that cleans.
He will sit and refine silver. He will purify the Levites and refine them like gold and silver. Then they will bring offerings to the LORD in the right way.
Then the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will please the LORD, as they did long ago, in earlier years.

"So I will come to judge you. I will be quick to speak against those who practice witchcraft, those who commit adultery, those who lie under oath, those who cheat workers out of their pay, those who take advantage of widows and orphans, and those who treat foreigners among you unfairly and do not fear Me," says the LORD of Hosts.
"I am the LORD, and I do not change. That is why you, Jacob's descendants, have not been destroyed.
Since the days of your ancestors, you have turned away from My laws and have not obeyed them. Return to Me, and I will return to you," says the LORD of Hosts. "But you ask, 'How can we return?'"
"Will a person rob God? Yet you rob Me. But you ask, 'How do we rob You?' In tithes and offerings."
Your whole nation is under a curse because you are robbing Me.

"Bring all the tithes into the storehouse so there will be food in My house. Test Me in this," says the LORD of Hosts. "See if I will not open the windows of heaven and pour out so much blessing that you will not have enough room for it."
"I will stop the pests from destroying your crops, and your vines in the field will not lose their fruit before harvest," says the LORD of Hosts.
"Then all the nations will call you blessed, because your land will be a delight," says the LORD of Hosts.
"You have spoken harsh words against Me," says the LORD. "Yet you ask, 'What have we said against You?'
You have said, 'Serving God is useless. What do we gain by obeying His rules and walking around sadly before the LORD of Hosts?
But now we call proud people blessed. Evildoers get ahead. They even test God and escape punishment.'"
Then those who feared the LORD spoke with each other. The LORD listened and heard them. A book of remembrance was written before Him for those who feared the LORD and honored His name.
"They will be Mine," says the LORD of Hosts, "on the day I act. I will spare them as a man spares his son who serves him."
"And you will again see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between those who serve God and those who do not."

Look, the day is coming, burning like a furnace, and all the proud and all who do evil will be like dry straw. The day that is coming will burn them up, says the LORD of Hosts, so that nothing is left of them—not even a root or a branch.
But for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its rays. You will go out and leap like calves released from the stall.
You will trample the wicked, because they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day I do this, says the LORD of Hosts.
Remember the law of My servant Moses—the rules and decisions I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel.
Look, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and frightening day of the LORD comes.
He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers. Otherwise, I will come and strike the land with total destruction.
This is the family history of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac was the father of Jacob, and Jacob was the father of Judah and his brothers.
Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez was the father of Hezron, and Hezron was the father of Ram.
Ram was the father of Amminadab, Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon was the father of Salmon.
Salmon was the father of Boaz by Rahab, Boaz was the father of Obed by Ruth, and Obed was the father of Jesse.
Jesse was the father of King David, and David was the father of Solomon by Uriah's wife.
Solomon was the father of Rehoboam, Rehoboam was the father of Abijah, and Abijah was the father of Asa.
Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat was the father of Joram, and Joram was the father of Uzziah.
Uzziah was the father of Jotham, Jotham was the father of Ahaz, and Ahaz was the father of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh, Manasseh was the father of Amon, and Amon was the father of Josiah.
Josiah was the father of Jechoniah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.
After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah was the father of Shealtiel, and Shealtiel was the father of Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud, Abiud was the father of Eliakim, and Eliakim was the father of Azor.
Azor was the father of Zadok, Zadok was the father of Achim, and Achim was the father of Eliud.
Eliud was the father of Eleazar, Eleazar was the father of Matthan, and Matthan was the father of Jacob.
Jacob was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, and Mary gave birth to Jesus, who is called the Christ.
So there were fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to the Christ.
This is how the birth of Jesus Christ happened. His mother Mary was engaged to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, was a good man. He did not want to shame her in public, so he planned to divorce her quietly.

While he was thinking about this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream. The angel said, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The child in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will give birth to a son, and you are to name Him Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins."
All this happened to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet:
"Look, the virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son. They will call Him Immanuel," which means "God with us."
When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded. He took Mary as his wife.
But he did not have relations with her until she gave birth to a son. He named Him Jesus.
After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea during the time of King Herod, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem.
They asked, "Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw His star in the east and have come to worship Him."
When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
He called together all the chief priests and teachers of the law and asked them where the Christ was to be born.
They said, "In Bethlehem in Judea, because this is what the prophet wrote:
'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah, for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd My people Israel.'"
Then Herod secretly called the wise men and found out from them the exact time the star had appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Go and search carefully for the child. When you find Him, report to me, so that I too may go and worship Him."
After they heard the king, they went on their way, and the star they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, they were overjoyed.
They went into the house and saw the child with His mother Mary. They bowed down and worshiped Him. Then they opened their treasures and gave Him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
They were warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they returned to their own country by another road.

After they left, an angel of the LORD appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, "Get up, take the child and His mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod is going to search for the child to kill him."
So Joseph got up, took the child and His mother during the night, and left for Egypt.
Joseph stayed there until Herod died. This happened so that what the LORD had said through the prophet would come true: "Out of Egypt I called My Son."

When Herod realized that the wise men had tricked him, he was very angry. He sent soldiers to kill all the boys in Bethlehem and in the surrounding area who were two years old or younger, based on the time he had learned from the wise men.
Then what the prophet Jeremiah had said came true:
"A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning. Rachel wept for her children and refused to be comforted, because they are gone."
After Herod died, an angel of the LORD appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt.
The angel said, "Get up, take the child and His mother and go to the land of Israel, for those who were trying to kill the child are dead."
So Joseph got up, took the child and His mother, and went to the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was ruling Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. After being warned in a dream, he went to the region of Galilee.
Joseph settled in a town called Nazareth. This fulfilled what the prophets had said: "He will be called a Nazarene."
In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea.
He said, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
This is he who was spoken of through the prophet Isaiah: "A voice of one calling in the wilderness, 'Prepare the way for the LORD, make straight paths for Him.'"
John's clothes were made of camel's hair, and he had a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
Then Jerusalem and all Judea and the whole region around the Jordan went out to him.
Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.
When he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to be baptized, he said to them, "You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
And do not think you can say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.
The ax is already at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
I baptize you with water for repentance, but the One who comes after me is more powerful than I. I am not worthy to carry His sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing fork is in His hand, and He will clear His threshing floor and gather His wheat into the barn, but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire."
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.
But John tried to stop Him, saying, "I need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?"
Jesus replied, "Let it be so now. It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way." Then John consented.
As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.
And a voice from heaven said, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
After fasting forty days and forty nights, He was very hungry.
The tempter came to Him and said, "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread."
Jesus answered, "It is written: 'Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.'"
Then the devil took Him to the holy city and set Him on the highest point of the temple.

"If you are the Son of God," he said, "throw yourself down. For it is written: 'He will command His angels concerning you, and they will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus answered, "Again it is written: 'Do not test the Lord your God.'"
Again, the devil took Him to a very high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
"All this I will give you," he said, "if you will bow down and worship me."
Jesus said to him, "Get away from me, Satan! For it is written: 'Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.'"
Then the devil left Him, and angels came and served Him.
When Jesus heard that John had been put in prison, He went to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum, which is by the sea in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali.
This happened to fulfill what the prophet Isaiah had said:
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way to the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles—
"the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death a light has dawned."
From that time on, Jesus began to preach, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near."
As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon (called Peter) and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, because they were fishermen.
"Come, follow Me," He said, "and I will make you fishers of people."
At once they left their nets and followed Him.
Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, fixing their nets. He called them.
Right away they left the boat and their father and followed Him.
Jesus went all through Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.

News about Him spread all over Syria, and people brought to Him everyone who was sick—those with different diseases and pains, people who were demon-possessed, those having seizures, and the paralyzed. He healed them.
Large crowds followed Him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and the region across the Jordan.
When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on the mountain. After He sat down, His disciples came to Him.
He opened His mouth and began to teach them, saying:
"Blessed are those who know they need God, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
Blessed are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who deeply want to do what is right, for they will be satisfied.
Blessed are those who show mercy, for they will be shown mercy.
Blessed are those whose hearts are clean, for they will see God.
Blessed are those who make peace, for they will be called sons of God.
Blessed are those who are treated badly for doing what is right, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs."
"Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me.
Rejoice and be glad, because your reward in heaven is great. That is how they persecuted the prophets who came before you."
"You are the salt of the earth. But if salt loses its saltiness, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by people.
You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.
People do not light a lamp and put it under a basket. Instead, they put it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good deeds and praise your Father in heaven."
"Do not think that I have come to destroy the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to destroy them, but to fulfill them.
I tell you truly, until heaven and earth pass away, not even the smallest letter or tiny stroke of the Law will pass away until everything is accomplished.

So anyone who breaks one of the least of these commands and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
I tell you, unless you are more devoted to doing what is right than the teachers of the law and the Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven."
"You have heard that it was said to the people long ago, 'Do not murder,' and anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.

But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. And anyone who says, 'You empty-headed person,' to his brother will be subject to the council. And anyone who says, 'You fool,' will be in danger of the fire of hell."
"So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there before the altar and go. First make peace with your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

Settle matters quickly with your opponent while you are on the way to court. Otherwise, your opponent may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the guard, and you may be thrown into prison.
I tell you truly, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny."
"You have heard that it was said, 'Do not commit adultery.'
But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
If your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go into hell."
"It has been said, 'Anyone who divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.'
But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery. And anyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
"Again, you have heard that it was said to the people long ago, 'Do not break your oath, but keep the promises you have made to the Lord.'
But I tell you, do not swear at all: not by heaven, for it is God's throne;
not by the earth, for it is His footstool; not by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
And do not swear by your head, for you cannot make even one hair white or black.
Let your word be 'Yes, yes' or 'No, no.' Anything more than this comes from the evil one."
"You have heard that it was said, 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.'
But I tell you, do not resist an evil person. If someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn the other cheek to him also.
If someone wants to sue you and take your shirt, let him have your coat as well.
