"Abba, Father," He said, "everything is possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I want, but what You want."
Then He came and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, "Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for one hour?"
"Watch and pray so that you will not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak."
He went away again and prayed, saying the same thing.
When He came back, He again found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy. They did not know what to say to Him.
The third time He came, He said, "Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners."
"Get up! Let us go. See, My betrayer is near."
Just as He was speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived. With him was a crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the elders.
Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: "The one I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away under guard."
Going at once to Jesus, Judas said, "Rabbi!" and kissed Him.
Then the men seized Jesus and arrested Him.
One of those standing near drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
Jesus said to them, "Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as if I were a robber?"
"Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me. But this has happened so that the Scriptures would be fulfilled."
Then everyone deserted Him and fled.
A young man, wearing nothing but a linen cloth, was following Jesus. When they seized him,
he fled naked, leaving his linen cloth behind.
They took Jesus to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and teachers of the law came together.
Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. There he sat with the guards and warmed himself by the fire.
The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for evidence against Jesus so that they could put Him to death, but they did not find any.
Many testified falsely against Him, but their statements did not agree.
Then some stood up and gave this false testimony against Him:
"We heard Him say, 'I will destroy this man-made temple and in three days build another, not made by hands.'"
Yet even then their testimony did not agree.
Then the high priest stood up before them and asked Jesus, "Are You not going to answer? What is this testimony that these men are bringing against You?"
But Jesus remained silent and gave no answer. Again the high priest asked Him, "Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
"I am," said Jesus. "And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Mighty One and coming on the clouds of heaven."
The high priest tore his clothes and said, "Why do we need any more witnesses?"
"You have heard the blasphemy. What do you think?" They all condemned Him as worthy of death.
Then some began to spit on Him. They blindfolded Him, struck Him with their fists, and said, "Prophesy!" And the guards took Him and beat Him.
While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest came by.
When she saw Peter warming himself, she looked closely at him and said, "You also were with that Nazarene, Jesus."
But he denied it. "I don't know or understand what you are talking about," he said, and went out into the entryway. And the rooster crowed.
When the servant girl saw him there, she began again to say to the bystanders, "This fellow is one of them."
But he denied it again. After a little while, those standing near said to Peter, "Surely you are one of them, for you are a Galilean."
He began to curse and swear, "I don't know this man you are talking about."
Immediately the rooster crowed the second time. Then Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken to him: "Before the rooster crows twice, you will disown Me three times." And he broke down and wept.

Very early in the morning, the chief priests met with the elders, the teachers of the law, and the whole Sanhedrin. They made a plan, tied up Jesus, and took Him away. Then they handed Him over to Pilate.
Pilate asked Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?" Jesus answered, "You have said so."
The chief priests accused Him of many things.
Pilate asked Him again, "Won't You answer anything? See how many things they accuse You of."
But Jesus still didn't answer, so Pilate was amazed.
At the feast, Pilate used to release one prisoner whom the people asked for.
A man named Barabbas was in prison with the rebels who had killed someone during a riot.
The crowd came up and began to ask Pilate to do what he usually did for them.
Pilate answered, "Do you want me to release the King of the Jews for you?"
He knew the chief priests had handed Jesus over because they were jealous.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to ask for Barabbas instead.
Pilate asked them again, "Then what do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?"
Pilate said, "Why? What crime has He done?" But they shouted even louder, "Crucify Him!"
Wanting to please the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. He had Jesus whipped, and then he handed Him over to be crucified.
The soldiers led Him away into the governor's palace. They called together the whole company of soldiers.
They put a purple robe on Him. They twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on Him.
They began to greet Him, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
They hit His head with a reed. They spit on Him. They knelt down and bowed before Him.
After they mocked Him, they took off the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.
They forced a man named Simon from Cyrene to carry His cross. Simon was the father of Alexander and Rufus. He was coming in from the country.
They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means "Place of the Skull."
They offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He didn't take it.
They crucified Him. They divided His clothes by casting lots to see who would get what.
It was nine in the morning when they crucified Him.
The sign with the charge against Him read, "The King of the Jews."
They crucified two robbers with Him, one on His right and one on His left.
People walking by insulted Him. They shook their heads and said, "Aha! You said You could destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days."
"Come down from the cross and save Yourself!"
The chief priests and teachers of the law also mocked Him among themselves. They said, "He saved others, but He can't save Himself!"
"Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down from the cross now, so we can see and believe." The men crucified with Him also insulted Him.
From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness came over the whole land.
At three in the afternoon, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" This means, "My God, My God, why have You abandoned Me?"
Some people standing there heard it and said, "Listen, He's calling Elijah."
Someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and gave it to Jesus to drink. He said, "Wait, let's see if Elijah comes to take Him down."
Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
The curtain in the temple tore in two from top to bottom.
When the Roman officer standing in front of Jesus saw how He died, he said, "Truly this Man was the Son of God!"
Some women were watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
They had followed Jesus and helped Him while He was in Galilee. Many other women had also come with Him to Jerusalem.
It was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day, the day before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea came. He was a respected member of the council, and he was waiting for God's kingdom. He was brave enough to go to Pilate and ask for Jesus' body.
Pilate was surprised that Jesus was already dead. He called the Roman officer and asked if Jesus had been dead for a while.
When the Roman officer told him, Pilate gave the body to Joseph.
Joseph bought a linen cloth. He took Jesus down, wrapped Him in the cloth, and placed Him in a tomb cut out of rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where Jesus was placed.
After the Sabbath, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices. They wanted to go and anoint Jesus' body.
Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.
They asked each other, "Who will roll the stone away from the tomb entrance for us?"
When they looked up, they saw that the stone had already been rolled away. It was very large.
They went into the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right side. He was wearing a white robe. They were amazed.
He said to them, "Don't be amazed. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has been raised! He is not here. Look at the place where they laid Him.
Go and tell His disciples and Peter, 'He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.'"
The women left the tomb and ran away. They were shaking and amazed, and they were afraid. So they said nothing to anyone.
Early on the first day of the week, after He had risen, Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene. He had driven seven demons out of her.
She went and told the people who had been with Him. They were mourning and crying.
When they heard that He was alive and that she had seen Him, they did not believe her.
After that, He appeared in a different form to two of them while they were walking to the country.
They went and told the rest, but they did not believe them either.
Later He appeared to the eleven while they were eating. He scolded them for not believing and for their stubborn hearts, because they had not believed the people who saw Him after He had been raised.
He said to them, "Go into all the world and preach the good news to all creation.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
These signs will follow those who believe: In My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new languages;
they will pick up snakes with their hands; and if they drink anything deadly, it will not hurt them. They will place their hands on sick people, and those people will get well."
After the Lord Jesus had spoken to them, He was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
The disciples went out and preached everywhere. The Lord worked with them and proved His word true through the miracles that followed.
Many people have tried to write about the things that have been fulfilled among us.
They passed on to us what the first eyewitnesses and servants of the message handed down from the beginning.
So, after I had carefully studied everything from the start, it seemed good to me to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus.
I did this so you could know how sure these things are—the things you were taught.
In the days of King Herod of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah. He was from the priestly group of Abijah. His wife was Elizabeth, from Aaron’s family.
Both were right with God. They lived without blame in all the Lord’s commands and rules.
But they had no child, because Elizabeth could not have children. Both were very old.
One day, while Zechariah was serving as priest before God in his group’s turn,
he was chosen by lot, as priests usually were, to go into the Lord’s temple and burn incense.
The whole crowd of people was praying outside while the incense was offered.
Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the incense altar.
Zechariah was shaken and afraid when he saw him.
But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will have a son, and you will name him John.
He will bring you joy and gladness, and many people will be glad when he is born.
He will be great in the Lord’s sight. He will not drink wine or strong drink. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit even before he is born.
He will turn many of the people of Israel back to the Lord their God.

He will go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah. He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children. He will turn people who do not obey to the wise thinking of those who do right. He will make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”
Zechariah said to the angel, “How can I know this? I am an old man, and my wife is old too.”
The angel answered, “I am Gabriel. I stand before God, and I was sent to speak to you and bring you this good news.
But now you will be silent. You will not be able to speak until these things happen, because you did not believe my words. They will come true at the right time.”
The people were waiting for Zechariah. They wondered why he stayed so long in the temple.
When he came out, he could not speak to them. They knew he had seen a vision in the temple. He kept making signs to them, and he stayed unable to speak.
When his time of service was over, he went home.
After that, his wife Elizabeth became pregnant. She stayed hidden for five months.
She said, “The Lord has done this for me. He has shown me favor and taken away my shame among people.”
In the sixth month, God sent the angel Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth.
He was sent to a virgin named Mary. She was engaged to a man named Joseph, from David’s family.
The angel came to her and said, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you.”
Mary was troubled by his words and wondered what kind of greeting this was.
The angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary. You have found favor with God.
You will become pregnant and have a son. You will name Him Jesus.
He will be great. He will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David.
He will rule over Jacob’s family forever. His kingdom will never end.”
Mary said to the angel, “How will this happen? I have not been with a man.”
The angel answered, “The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will cover you. So the holy Child will be called the Son of God.
Look, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age. This is the sixth month for her, the one called unable to have children.
For nothing is impossible with God.”
Mary said, “I am the Lord’s servant. Let it happen to me as you have said.” Then the angel left her.
Soon after that, Mary got up and traveled quickly to a town in the hill country of Judea.
She went into Zechariah’s home and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb. Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She called out loudly, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the child you are carrying!
Why am I so favored that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
As soon as I heard your greeting, the baby in my womb leaped for joy.
Blessed is she who believed that the Lord would keep His promise to her.”
Mary said, “My soul praises the Lord.
My spirit rejoices in God my Savior.
He has looked on the lowly state of His servant. From now on all generations will call me blessed.
The Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is His name.
His mercy is for those who fear Him, from generation to generation.
“He has shown strength with His arm. He has scattered those who are proud in their thoughts.
He has brought down rulers from their thrones and lifted up the humble.
He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
He has helped His servant Israel, remembering His mercy.
He promised this to our fathers, to Abraham and his children forever.”
Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months. Then she went back home.
When it was time for Elizabeth to have her baby, she gave birth to a son.
Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy. They rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day, they came to circumcise the child. They were going to name him after his father, Zechariah.
But his mother said, “No. He will be called John.”
They said to her, “No one in your family has that name.”
Then they motioned to his father to ask what he wanted to name the child.
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” Everyone was amazed.
Right away his mouth was opened and his tongue was freed. He spoke and praised God.
All the neighbors were filled with awe. Throughout the hill country of Judea, people talked about all these things.
Everyone who heard about them wondered, “What will this child become?” They said, “The Lord’s power was with him.”
Zechariah, his father, was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied,
“Praise the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has come to help His people and set them free.
He has raised up a mighty Savior for us from the house of His servant David.
He spoke through His holy prophets long ago.
He promised to save us from our enemies and from everyone who hates us.
He promised to show mercy to our fathers and remember His holy covenant.
He swore to our father Abraham
to rescue us from our enemies, so we could serve Him without fear.
We would be holy and right before Him all our days.
“And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High. You will go before the Lord to prepare His ways.
You will give His people knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins.
Because of our God’s tender mercy, the rising sun will visit us from heaven.
It will shine on those who live in darkness and in the shadow of death. It will guide our feet into the path of peace.”
The child grew and became strong in spirit. He lived in the wilderness until he was shown to Israel.
In those days, Caesar Augustus sent out an order that everyone in the empire should be counted in a census.
This was the first census taken while Quirinius was governor of Syria.
Everyone went to their own town to be registered.
Joseph went up from Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to Bethlehem, the city of David, because he belonged to the family line of David.
He went there to register with Mary, who was engaged to him and was expecting a baby.
While they were there, the time came for her baby to be born.
She gave birth to her firstborn Son, wrapped Him in strips of cloth, and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the guest room.
In that same area, shepherds were staying out in the fields and watching over their sheep at night.
An angel of the Lord appeared to them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them. They were terrified.
The angel said to them, "Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will bring great joy to all people.
Today in the city of David a Savior has been born for you. He is Christ the Lord.
This will be a sign for you: You will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth and lying in a manger."
Suddenly a great crowd of angels from heaven appeared with the angel. They were praising God and saying,
"Glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth to those He favors."
When the angels had gone back into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, "Let's go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has told us about."
They hurried and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger.
When they saw Him, they told everyone what they had been told about this child.
Everyone who heard it was amazed at what the shepherds said.
But Mary kept all these things in her heart and thought about them often.
The shepherds went back, praising and glorifying God for everything they had heard and seen, just as they had been told.
Eight days later, when it was time to circumcise Him, He was named Jesus. This was the name the angel had given before Mary became pregnant.
When the time came for them to be purified, as the Law of Moses required, they took Him to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord.
This followed what is written in the Lord's Law: "Every firstborn male must be set apart as holy to the Lord."
They also offered a sacrifice, as the Lord's Law says: "a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons."
In Jerusalem there was a man named Simeon. He was good and faithful, and he was waiting for God to comfort Israel. The Holy Spirit was on him.
The Holy Spirit had told him that he would not die before he saw the Lord's Messiah.
Led by the Spirit, he went into the temple. When Jesus' parents brought the child in to do what the Law required for Him,
Simeon took Him in his arms, praised God, and said,
"Lord, now you can let Your servant go in peace, as You promised.
For my eyes have seen Your salvation,
which You have prepared for all people to see.
He will be a light to show the way to the nations and bring glory to Your people Israel."
Jesus' parents were amazed at what was said about Him.
Then Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, His mother, "This child is meant to cause many in Israel to fall and to rise. He will be a sign that people speak against.
A sword will pierce your own soul too, so that the secret thoughts of many hearts will be brought into the open."
There was also a prophet named Anna. She was the daughter of Phanuel from the tribe of Asher. She was very old. After she married, she lived with her husband seven years.
Then she was a widow until she was eighty-four. She never left the temple. She worshiped God day and night with fasting and prayer.
At that very moment, she came up and began to thank God. She spoke about Jesus to everyone who was waiting for God to rescue Jerusalem.
When Joseph and Mary had finished everything the Lord's Law required, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong. He was filled with wisdom, and God's grace was on Him.
Every year Jesus' parents went to Jerusalem for the Passover Feast.
When He was twelve years old, they went up to the feast as usual.
After the feast days were over and they started home, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. His parents did not know it.
Thinking He was with the group, they traveled for a whole day. Then they began to look for Him among their relatives and friends.
When they could not find Him, they went back to Jerusalem to search for Him.
Three days later they found Him in the temple. He was sitting with the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
Everyone who heard Him was amazed at His understanding and His answers.
When His parents saw Him, they were astonished. His mother said to Him, "Child, why have you treated us like this? Your father and I have been searching for You in great pain."
He said to them, "Why were you looking for Me? Didn't you know that I must be in My Father's house?"
But they did not understand what He said to them.
Then He went down with them to Nazareth and obeyed them. His mother kept all these things in her heart.
And Jesus grew in wisdom and age and in favor with God and people.

In the fifteenth year of Emperor Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea. Herod was ruler of Galilee, his brother Philip was ruler of Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was ruler of Abilene.
Annas and Caiaphas were high priests. At that time, God's word came to John, son of Zechariah, in the desert.
John traveled all around the Jordan area. He preached that people should be baptized and turn from sin so their sins could be forgiven.
This was like Isaiah the prophet wrote: "A voice is calling in the desert, 'Prepare the way for the Lord. Make straight paths for Him.'"
Every valley will be filled. Every mountain and hill will be made low. Crooked roads will become straight, and rough roads will become smooth.
Then all people will see God's saving power.
John said to the crowds coming to be baptized, "You snakes' children! Who warned you to run from the coming anger?
Produce fruit that shows you have truly changed. Do not start saying to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' I tell you, God can make children for Abraham from these stones.
The ax is already at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."
The crowds asked him, "What should we do?"
He answered, "If anyone has two shirts, share with someone who has none. Do the same with food."
Tax collectors also came to be baptized. They said, "Teacher, what should we do?"
He said, "Collect no more than you are ordered to collect."
Soldiers asked him, "What should we do?" He said, "Do not force money from anyone. Do not make false charges. Be happy with your pay."
The people were waiting. They all wondered in their hearts if John might be the Messiah.
John answered everyone, "I baptize you with water. But someone stronger than me is coming. I am not worthy to untie His sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing fork is in His hand. He will clean His threshing floor. He will gather the wheat into His barn. But He will burn the chaff with fire that never goes out."
John used many other words like this to encourage people as he preached the good news to them.
But Herod the ruler got in trouble with John. John corrected him about Herodias, his brother's wife, and about all the other evil things Herod had done.
Herod added this to his other sins: he locked John in prison.
While all the people were being baptized, Jesus was baptized too. As He prayed, heaven opened.
The Holy Spirit came down on Him in bodily form, like a dove. A voice came from heaven: "You are My beloved Son. I am very pleased with you."
Jesus was about thirty years old when He began His work. He was thought to be the son of Joseph, son of Heli,
son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Melchi, son of Jannai, son of Joseph,
son of Mattathias, son of Amos, son of Nahum, son of Esli, son of Naggai,
son of Maath, son of Mattathias, son of Semein, son of Josech, son of Joda,
son of Joanan, son of Rhesa, son of Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, son of Neri,
son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmadam, son of Er,
son of Joshua, son of Eliezer, son of Jorim, son of Matthat, son of Levi,
son of Simeon, son of Judah, son of Joseph, son of Jonam, son of Eliakim,
son of Melea, son of Menna, son of Mattatha, son of Nathan, son of David,
son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Boaz, son of Salmon, son of Nahshon,
son of Amminadab, son of Admin, son of Arni, son of Hezron, son of Perez, son of Judah,
son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Terah, son of Nahor,
son of Serug, son of Reu, son of Peleg, son of Eber, son of Shelah,
son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Shem, son of Noah, son of Lamech,
son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalaleel, son of Cainan,
son of Enos, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.
Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness.
There He was tempted by the devil for forty days. He ate nothing during those days, and when they ended, He was hungry.
The devil said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread."
Jesus answered, "It is written: 'Man shall not live on bread alone.'"
The devil led Him up to a high place and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in an instant.
"I will give You all this authority and glory, because it has been given to me, and I can give it to anyone I want.
So if You worship me, it will all be Yours."
Jesus answered, "It is written: 'Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.'"
The devil led Him to Jerusalem and set Him on the highest point of the temple. "If You are the Son of God," he said, "throw Yourself down from here.
For it is written: 'He will command His angels concerning You to guard You carefully.
They will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus answered, "It is said: 'Do not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
When the devil had finished all this tempting, he left Him until a better time.
Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about Him spread through the whole countryside.
He taught in their synagogues, and everyone praised Him.
He went to Nazareth, where He had been brought up. As usual, He went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day and stood up to read.
They gave Him the scroll of the prophet Isaiah. He unrolled it and found the place where it is written:

"The Spirit of the Lord is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free,
to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor."
Then He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. Everyone in the synagogue was looking at Him closely.
He began to say to them, "Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing."
Everyone spoke well of Him and was amazed at the gracious words coming from His mouth. "Isn't this Joseph's son?" they asked.
"Surely you will quote this proverb to Me: 'Physician, heal Yourself!' And you will tell Me, 'Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.'
Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.
"I assure you that there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and a half years and a severe famine spread over all the land.
Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to a widow in Zarephath in the region of Sidon.
And there were many in Israel with leprosy in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet not one of them was cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian."
When everyone in the synagogue heard this, they were furious.
They got up, drove Him out of the town, and took Him to the brow of the hill on which the town was built, in order to throw Him off the cliff.
But He walked right through the crowd and went on His way.
Then He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and on the Sabbath He was teaching the people.
They were amazed at His teaching, because His words had authority.
In the synagogue there was a man possessed by a demon, an impure spirit. He cried out in a loud voice,
"Go away! What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!"
"Be quiet!" Jesus said sternly. "Come out of him!" Then the demon threw the man down before them all and came out of him without hurting him.
All the people were amazed and said to each other, "What is this teaching? With authority and power He gives orders to impure spirits, and they come out!"
And the news about Him spread to every place in the surrounding region.
Jesus left the synagogue and went to Simon's house. Now Simon's mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they asked Jesus to help her.
He bent over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. She got up at once and began to serve them.
At sunset, the people brought to Jesus all who were sick with various diseases. He laid His hands on each one of them, and He healed them.
Demons also came out of many people, shouting, "You are the Son of God!" But He rebuked them and would not let them speak, because they knew He was the Messiah.
At daybreak, Jesus went out to a solitary place. The crowds looked for Him and came to where He was. They tried to keep Him from leaving them.
But He said, "I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns too, because that is why I was sent."
And He kept on preaching in the synagogues of Judea.
One day Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret. The crowd was pressing in on Him to hear God's word.
He saw two boats at the water's edge. The fishermen had gotten out of them and were washing their nets.
Jesus got into one of the boats, which belonged to Simon, and asked him to put out a little from the shore. Then He sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
When He had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water, and let down your nets for a catch.”
Simon answered, “Master, we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”
When they did this, they caught so many fish that their nets began to break.
They signaled their partners in the other boat to come and help them. The men came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus' knees and said, “Go away from me, Lord! I am a sinful man!”
For he and all who were with him were amazed at the catch of fish they had taken.
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, were Simon's partners and were amazed too. Then Jesus said to Simon, “Don't be afraid; from now on you will catch people.”
So they pulled their boats up on shore, left everything, and followed Him.
While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came who was full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged Him, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”
Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. He said, “I am willing. Be clean!” And right away the leprosy left him.
Then He ordered him, “Don't tell anyone. But go and show yourself to the priest and offer the sacrifices Moses commanded for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”
Yet the news about Him spread even more. Large crowds gathered to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.
But Jesus often withdrew to lonely places and prayed.

One day Jesus was teaching. Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was with Him to heal.
Some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him in and lay him before Jesus.
When they could not find a way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.
When Jesus saw their faith, He said, “Man, your sins are forgiven.”
The scribes and Pharisees began to think, “Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Jesus knew what they were thinking. He answered them, “Why are you questioning these things in your hearts?”
“Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?”
“But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins,” He said to the paralyzed man, “I tell you, get up, take your mat, and go home.”
Right away he stood up in front of them. He took what he had been lying on and went home, praising God.
Everyone was amazed. They praised God and were filled with awe. They said, “We have seen remarkable things today.”
After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at his tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him.
Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.
Then Levi held a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors and others were eating with them.
But the Pharisees and their scribes grumbled to His disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick do.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
They said to Him, “John's disciples often fast and pray, and so do the disciples of the Pharisees. But Your disciples eat and drink.”
Jesus said to them, “Can you make the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them?”
“But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them. Then they will fast.”
He told them this parable: “No one tears a piece from a new garment and puts it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment, and the patch from the new will not match the old.”
“No one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins. The wine will be spilled and the wineskins ruined.
Instead, new wine must be poured into new wineskins.
And no one after drinking old wine wants the new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
One Sabbath, Jesus was walking through grainfields, and His disciples were picking heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands, and eating them.
Some Pharisees asked, "Why are you doing what isn't allowed on the Sabbath?"
Jesus answered, "Haven't you read what David did when he and his men were hungry?
He went into God's house, took the bread of the Presence, ate it, and gave some to his men. That bread is allowed only for the priests to eat.
The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."
On another Sabbath, Jesus went into the synagogue and taught. A man was there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes and Pharisees watched Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath, so they could accuse Him.
But Jesus knew what they were thinking. He said to the man with the withered hand, "Get up and stand here in the middle." The man got up and stood there.
Then Jesus said to them, "I ask you: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to destroy it?"
He looked around at all of them and said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man did, and his hand was restored.
But they were filled with rage and talked with each other about what they might do to Jesus.
In those days Jesus went out to a mountain to pray, and He spent the whole night praying to God.
When day came, He called His disciples and chose twelve of them, whom He also named apostles:
Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot;
Judas son of James and Judas Iscariot, who became the traitor.
He came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a huge crowd from all Judea, Jerusalem, and the coast of Tyre and Sidon.
They came to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases. Those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
The whole crowd tried to touch Him, because power came from Him and healed everyone.
He looked at His disciples and said, "Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, avoid you, insult you, and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
Rejoice in that day and jump for joy, because your reward is great in heaven. That is how their ancestors treated the prophets.
"But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.
Woe to you who are full now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when everyone speaks well of you, for that is how their ancestors treated the false prophets.
"But I say to you who are listening: Love your enemies. Do good to those who hate you.
Bless those who curse you. Pray for those who mistreat you.
If someone strikes you on the cheek, offer the other cheek too. If someone takes your coat, don't stop him from taking your shirt.
Give to everyone who asks you, and if someone takes what is yours, don't demand it back.
Treat others the way you want them to treat you.
"If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do that.
If you lend to those you expect to pay you back, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners to get the same amount back.
But love your enemies, do good, and lend without expecting anything back. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because He is kind to the ungrateful and the wicked.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
"Don't judge, and you won't be judged. Don't condemn, and you won't be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.

Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be poured into your lap. The way you measure to others is the way it will be measured back to you.
He also told them a parable: "Can a blind man lead a blind man? Won't they both fall into a pit?
A student is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye but fail to notice the log in your own eye?

How can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,' when you don't even see the log in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly enough to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
"No good tree makes bad fruit, and no bad tree makes good fruit.
Every tree is known by its own fruit. People don't pick figs from thornbushes, and they don't gather grapes from brambles.
A good person brings good things out of the good stored in his heart, and an evil person brings evil things out of the evil stored there. What a person says flows from what fills his heart.
"Why do you call Me 'Lord, Lord' and not do what I say?
I will show you what everyone is like who comes to Me, hears My words, and does them.
He is like a man who builds a house. He digs down deep and lays the foundation on rock. When a flood comes and the river beats against that house, it can't shake it, because it was well built.

But the one who hears My words and doesn't do them is like a man who builds a house on the ground without a foundation. When the river beats against it, it collapses at once, and the ruin of that house is great."
After Jesus had finished saying all this to the people, He went into Capernaum.
There a centurion's servant, whom his master valued highly, was sick and about to die.
When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to Him, asking Him to come and heal his servant.
They came to Jesus and begged Him earnestly, saying, "He is worthy for You to do this for him,
because he loves our nation and has built our synagogue."
Jesus went with them. He was not far from the house when the centurion sent friends to say to Him, "Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.
That is why I did not even consider myself worthy to come to You. But say the word, and my servant will be healed.
For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell this one, 'Go,' and he goes; and that one, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
When Jesus heard this, He marveled at him. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, "I tell you, I have not found such great faith even in Israel."
Then those who had been sent returned home and found the servant well.
The next day Jesus went to a town called Nain, and His disciples and a large crowd went with Him.
As He approached the town gate, a dead man was being carried out. He was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. A large crowd from the town was with her.
When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said to her, "Do not weep."
Then He came up and touched the coffin, and the bearers stopped. He said, "Young man, I say to you, get up!"
The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.
Everyone was filled with awe and praised God. "A great prophet has risen among us!" they said. "God has visited His people!"
This news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and the surrounding country.
John's disciples told him about all these things.
So John called two of his disciples and sent them to the Lord to ask, "Are You the One who is to come, or should we expect someone else?"
When the men came to Jesus, they said, "John the Baptist sent us to You to ask, 'Are You the One who is to come, or should we expect someone else?'"
At that very hour Jesus healed many people of diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.

He replied to them, "Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, those with leprosy are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
Blessed is the one who is not offended by Me."
After John's messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swayed by the wind?
What did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear splendid clothes and live in luxury are in royal palaces.
What did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: 'Behold, I send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.'
I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John. Yet the one who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."
All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged that God's way was right, because they had been baptized by John.
But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God's plan for themselves, because they were not baptized by John.
"To what, then, can I compare the people of this generation? What are they like?
They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another, 'We played the flute for you, but you did not dance; we sang a sad song, but you did not cry.'
For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, 'He has a demon.'
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
But wisdom is proved right by all her children."
One of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him. So Jesus went to the Pharisee's house and reclined at the table.
A woman in that town who lived a sinful life learned that Jesus was eating at the Pharisee's house. She brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
She stood behind Him at His feet, weeping, and began to wet His feet with her tears. Then she wiped them with her hair, kissed His feet, and poured perfume on them.
When the Pharisee who had invited Him saw this, he said to himself, "If this man were a prophet, He would know who is touching Him and what kind of woman she is—that she is a sinner."
Jesus answered him, "Simon, I have something to tell you." "Tell me, Teacher," he said.
"Two people owed money to a certain moneylender. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
Neither of them could pay him back, so he forgave both debts. Now which of them will love him more?"
Simon replied, "I suppose the one who had the larger debt forgiven." "You have judged correctly," Jesus said.

Then He turned toward the woman and said to Simon, "Do you see this woman? I came into your house. You did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You did not give Me a kiss, but this woman, from the time I entered, has not stopped kissing My feet.
You did not pour oil on My head, but she has poured perfume on My feet.
Therefore, I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven, for she loved much. But whoever has been forgiven little loves little."
Then Jesus said to her, "Your sins are forgiven."
The other guests began to say among themselves, "Who is this who even forgives sins?"
Jesus said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you; go in peace."
After this, Jesus traveled from town to town and village to village. He preached and shared the good news of God's kingdom. The Twelve were with Him.
Some women were there too. They had been healed from evil spirits and sickness. Mary, called Magdalene, was one of them. Seven demons had come out of her.
Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's manager, was another. Susanna was there too, along with many other women. They helped support Jesus and His disciples with their own money.
A large crowd gathered. People came to Jesus from town after town. He told them this story:
"A farmer went out to plant seed. As he scattered it, some seed fell on the path. People walked on it, and birds ate it."
"Some fell on rocky ground. It grew, but it dried up because it had no moisture."
"Some fell among thorns. The thorns grew with it and choked it."
"Other seed fell on good soil. It grew and produced a crop a hundred times more than was planted." When He said this, He called out, "Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."
His disciples asked Him what this story meant.

"You have been given the chance to understand the secrets of God's kingdom. But I speak to others in stories. That way, even though they see, they may not really see. Even though they hear, they may not understand."
"This is what the story means: The seed is God's word.
The seed on the path stands for people who hear the word. Then the devil comes and takes it from their hearts. He does this so they won't believe and be saved.
The seed on rocky ground stands for people who hear the word and receive it with joy. But they have no root. They believe for a while, but when trouble comes, they turn away.
The seed among thorns stands for people who hear the word. But as they go through life, worries, money, and pleasure choke it. So they never grow to maturity.
The seed on good soil stands for people with honest and good hearts. They hear the word, hold on to it, and keep going. In time, they produce a good crop."
"No one lights a lamp and hides it in a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a stand so people who come in can see the light.
Nothing is hidden that won't be shown. Nothing is secret that won't be known and brought into the open.
So be careful how you listen. Whoever has will be given more. Whoever doesn't have, even what they think they have will be taken away."
Jesus' mother and brothers came to see Him. But they couldn't get near Him because of the crowd.
Someone told Him, "Your mother and brothers are standing outside. They want to see You."
He replied, "My mother and brothers are those who hear God's word and do it."
One day Jesus said to His disciples, "Let's go over to the other side of the lake." So they got into a boat and set out.
As they sailed, He fell asleep. A storm came down on the lake. The boat filled with water, and they were in danger.
The disciples went and woke Him. They said, "Master, Master, we're going to drown!" He got up and spoke sharply to the wind and waves. They stopped, and the water became calm.
"Where is your faith?" He asked them. They were afraid and amazed. They asked each other, "Who is this? He gives orders to the wind and water, and they obey Him."
They sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.
When Jesus stepped ashore, a man from the town met Him. He had demons. For a long time he had not worn clothes or lived in a house. He lived among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell at His feet. He shouted, "What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You, don't torture me!"

Jesus had commanded the evil spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him. He was chained hand and foot and kept under guard. But he broke the chains. The demon drove him into lonely places.
Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" "Legion," he said, because many demons had gone into him.
They begged Jesus not to send them into the Abyss.
A large herd of pigs was feeding on the hillside. The demons begged Jesus to let them go into the pigs. He gave them permission.
The demons came out of the man and went into the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
The men who were watching the pigs ran away. They reported this in the town and countryside.
People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man the demons had left. He was sitting at Jesus' feet. He was dressed and in his right mind. They were afraid.
Those who had seen it told how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
All the people in the area asked Jesus to leave. They were overcome with fear. So He got into the boat and left.
The man the demons had left begged to go with Him. But Jesus sent him away.
"Go back home and tell how much God has done for you." So the man went away. He told all over town how much Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed Him. They had all been waiting for Him.
A man named Jairus came. He was a leader of the synagogue. He fell at Jesus' feet and begged Him to come to his house.
His only daughter, about twelve years old, was dying. As Jesus went, the crowds pressed around Him.
A woman was there who had been bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all her money on doctors, but no one could heal her.
She came up behind Him and touched the edge of His cloak. At once her bleeding stopped.
"Who touched Me?" Jesus asked. Everyone denied it. Peter said, "Master, the people are crowding and pressing against You."
But Jesus said, "Someone touched Me. I know that power went out from Me."
The woman saw that she couldn't hide. She came trembling and fell at His feet. In front of everyone, she told why she had touched Him and how she had been healed at once.
He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace."
While He was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader's house. "Your daughter is dead," he said. "Don't bother the Teacher anymore."
Hearing this, Jesus said to Jairus, "Don't be afraid. Just believe, and she will be healed."
When He arrived at the house, He didn't let anyone go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child's father and mother.
Everyone was crying and mourning for her. Jesus said, "Don't cry. She is not dead but asleep."
They laughed at Him, knowing she was dead.
But He took her by the hand and said, "My child, get up!"
Her spirit returned, and she stood up at once. Then Jesus told them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were amazed. But He ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to cure diseases.
He sent them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
He told them, "Take nothing for the trip—no walking stick, no bag, no bread, no money, and not even two shirts."
"Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that town."
"If people do not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town as a warning against them."
So they left and went through the villages, preaching the good news and healing people everywhere.
Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening. He was confused because some people said John had been raised from the dead.
Others said Elijah had appeared, and still others that one of the old prophets had come back to life.
Herod said, "I beheaded John. Who is this I hear such things about?" And he tried to see Jesus.
When the apostles came back, they told Him everything they had done. Then He took them away privately to a town called Bethsaida.
The crowds found out and followed Him. He welcomed them and spoke about the kingdom of God, healing those who needed healing.
As the day began to end, the Twelve came to Him and said, "Send the crowd away so they can go to the nearby villages and farms to find food and a place to stay, because we are in a deserted place."
He said to them, "You give them something to eat." They said, "We have only five loaves of bread and two fish—unless we go buy food for all these people."
There were about five thousand men. He said to His disciples, "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty."
They did so, and everyone sat down.
Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
Everyone ate and was full. They picked up twelve baskets of leftover pieces.
One time, while Jesus was praying alone, the disciples were with Him. He asked them, "Who do the crowds say I am?"
They answered, "Some say John the Baptist. Others say Elijah. And others say one of the old prophets has risen."
He said to them, "But who do you say I am?" Peter answered, "The Christ of God."
Jesus strictly warned them not to tell this to anyone.
He said, "The Son of Man must suffer many things. He will be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law. He will be killed, and on the third day He will rise."
Then He said to everyone, "If anyone wants to follow Me, he must deny himself, take up his cross every day, and follow Me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.
What good is it for a person to gain the whole world but lose or ruin himself?
If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
I tell you truly, some who are standing here will not die until they see the kingdom of God."
About eight days after these words, He took Peter, John, and James up a mountain to pray.
As He prayed, the look of His face changed, and His clothes became dazzling white.
Two men, Moses and Elijah, appeared and talked with Him.
They spoke about His departure, which He was about to complete in Jerusalem.
Peter and those with him were very sleepy, but when they woke up, they saw His glory and the two men standing with Him.
As the men were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, "Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." He did not know what he was saying.
While he was speaking, a cloud came and overshadowed them. They were afraid as they entered the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud: "This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!"
When the voice had spoken, Jesus was alone. The disciples kept quiet and in those days told no one anything about what they had seen.
The next day, when they came down the mountain, a large crowd met Him.
A man in the crowd shouted, "Teacher, I beg You, look at my son, for he is my only child.
A spirit seizes him, and he suddenly cries out. It throws him into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth. It hardly leaves him, and it is destroying him.
I begged Your disciples to drive it out, but they could not."
Jesus answered, "You unbelieving and twisted generation! How long shall I stay with you and put up with you? Bring your son here."
As the boy was coming, the demon threw him to the ground and convulsed him. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
Everyone was amazed at God's great power. While everyone was still marveling at all Jesus did, He said to His disciples,
"Listen carefully to what I am about to tell you: The Son of Man is going to be handed over to men."
But they did not understand this saying, and it was hidden from them so that they would not grasp it. They were afraid to ask Him about it.
An argument started among them about which of them was the greatest.
Jesus knew what they were thinking, so He took a little child and stood him by His side.
He said to them, "Whoever welcomes this child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. For the one who is least among all of you is the greatest."
John answered, "Master, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him because he does not follow with us."
"Do not stop him," Jesus said, "for whoever is not against you is for you."
As the time approached for Him to be taken up to heaven, He was determined to go to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of Him. They went and entered a Samaritan village to get things ready for Him.
But the people there did not welcome Him because He was heading for Jerusalem.
When His disciples James and John saw this, they said, "Lord, do You want us to call fire down from heaven to destroy them?"
But He turned and rebuked them.
Then they went on to another village.
As they traveled along the road, someone said to Him, "I will follow You wherever You go."
Jesus said to him, "Foxes have holes and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to rest His head."
He said to another man, "Follow Me." But the man said, "Lord, first let me go and bury my father."
Jesus said to him, "Let the dead bury their own dead, but you go and proclaim the kingdom of God."
Still another said, "I will follow You, Lord, but first let me go say goodbye to my family at home."
Jesus said to him, "No one who starts plowing and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God."
After this, the Lord chose seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to go.
He told them, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into His harvest.
Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Do not carry a money bag, a travel bag, or sandals, and do not greet anyone on the road."
"When you enter a house, first say, 'Peace to this house.'
If someone there loves peace, your peace will rest on him. If not, it will come back to you.
Stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they give you, because the worker deserves his pay. Do not move from house to house."
"When you enter a town and the people welcome you, eat what is set before you.
Heal the sick there and tell them, 'God's kingdom has come near to you.'"
"But when you enter a town and the people do not welcome you, go into its streets and say,
'We wipe off even the dust of your town that stuck to our feet. But know this: God's kingdom has come near.'
I tell you that on that day it will be easier for Sodom than for that town."
"Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! If the miracles done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago.
But it will be easier for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you."
"And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will go down to Hades.
Whoever listens to you listens to Me, and whoever rejects you rejects Me. Whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me."
The seventy-two returned with joy and said, "Lord, even the demons obey us when we use Your name!"
He said to them, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven."
"Look, I have given you power to walk on snakes and scorpions, and power over all the enemy's strength. Nothing will harm you.
But do not rejoice that the spirits obey you. Rejoice instead that your names are written in heaven."

At that same hour, Jesus was full of joy through the Holy Spirit and said, "I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You hid these things from the wise and learned, and showed them to little children. Yes, Father, this is what You wanted.
My Father has given Me everything. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those the Son chooses to reveal Him to."
Then He turned to His disciples and said privately, "Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
I tell you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it."
A law expert stood up to test Him and asked, "Teacher, what must I do to gain eternal life?"
He asked him, "What is written in the Law? How do you read it?"
He answered, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind. Love your neighbor as yourself."
He said to him, "You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live."
But he wanted to show he was right, so he asked Jesus, "And who is my neighbor?"
Jesus replied, "A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho. Robbers attacked him, stripped him, beat him, and left him half dead.
By chance, a priest was going down that road. When he saw the man, he passed by on the other side.
A Levite also came to that place. When he saw the man, he passed by on the other side."
"But a Samaritan who was traveling came to where the man was. When he saw him, he felt deep pity.
He went to him, bandaged his wounds, and poured oil and wine on them. Then he put the man on his own animal and took him to an inn, where he cared for him."
"The next day he took out two silver coins and gave them to the innkeeper. He said, 'Take care of him. When I come back, I will pay you back for anything extra you spend.'
Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell among robbers?"
The man said, "The one who showed mercy to him." He said to him, "Go and do the same."
As they traveled, Jesus entered a village. A woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.
She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet and listened to His teaching.
Martha was busy with all the work to be done. She came to Jesus and said, "Lord, don't You care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me."
The Lord answered, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things.
But only one thing is needed. Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her."
One day Jesus was praying in a certain place. When He finished, one of His disciples said to Him, "Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples."
He said to them, "When you pray, say: 'Father, may Your name be kept holy. May Your kingdom come.
Give us each day our daily bread.
Forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us. And do not lead us into temptation.'"
Then Jesus said to them, "Suppose one of you has a friend and goes to him at midnight and says, 'Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
because my friend has arrived from a trip, and I have nothing to set before him.'
The one inside answers, 'Don't bother me. The door is already locked, and my children and I are in bed. I can't get up and give you anything.'
I tell you, even if he won't get up and give him bread because he is his friend, yet because of the man's bold asking he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
"So I say to you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives; everyone who seeks finds; and to everyone who knocks, the door will be opened.
Which of you fathers, if your son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?
Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
If you, then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!"
Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute. When the demon left, the man who had been mute spoke, and the crowd was amazed.
But some of them said, "By Beelzebul, the prince of demons, He drives out demons."
Others tested Him by asking for a sign from heaven.
Jesus knew their thoughts and said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself will be ruined, and a house divided against itself will fall.
If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? You say I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your followers drive them out? So they will be your judges.
But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
"When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own house, his possessions are safe.
But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor the man trusted in and divides up his plunder.
Whoever is not with Me is against Me, and whoever does not gather with Me scatters.
"When an impure spirit comes out of a person, it goes through dry places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, 'I will return to the house I left.'
When it arrives, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.
Then it goes and takes seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and live there. And the final condition of that person is worse than the first."
While Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd called out, "Blessed is the mother who gave birth to you and nursed you."
He replied, "Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it."
As the crowds increased, Jesus said, "This is a wicked generation. It asks for a sign, but no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah.
For as Jonah was a sign to the people of Nineveh, so also the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.

The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the people of this generation and condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to listen to Solomon's wisdom, and now something greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now something greater than Jonah is here."
"No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place or under a bowl. Instead, they put it on a stand, so that those who come in may see the light.
Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eye is healthy, your whole body also is full of light. But when it is unhealthy, your body is full of darkness.
See to it, then, that the light within you is not darkness.
If then your whole body is full of light, with no dark part, it will be completely light, as when a lamp shines on you."
When Jesus had finished speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to eat with him; so He went in and reclined at the table.
But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.
Then the Lord said to him, "Now then, you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
You foolish people! Did not the one who made the outside make the inside also?
But give to the poor from what you have, and everything will be clean for you.

"Woe to you Pharisees, because you give a tenth of your mint, rue, and all other garden herbs, but you neglect justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without leaving the former undone.
Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the most important seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you, because you are like unmarked graves, which people walk over without knowing it."
One of the experts in the law answered Him, "Teacher, when you say these things, you insult us too."
Jesus replied, "And you experts in the law, woe to you, because you load people down with heavy burdens, but you yourselves will not lift one finger to help them.
Woe to you, because you build tombs for the prophets, and it was your ancestors who killed them.
So you testify that you approve of what your ancestors did; they killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
"Because of this, God in His wisdom said, 'I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.'
Therefore this generation will be held responsible for the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the beginning of the world,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be held responsible for it all.
"Woe to you experts in the law, because you have taken away the key to knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering."
When Jesus went outside, the teachers of the law and the Pharisees began to oppose Him fiercely and to question Him about many things,
waiting to catch Him in something He might say.
While a huge crowd gathered—so many people that they stepped on each other—Jesus began to speak first to His disciples. "Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees. It means pretending.
Nothing is covered up that won't be uncovered, and nothing is hidden that won't be known.
So what you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you whispered in a room will be shouted from the rooftops."
"I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and can do nothing more after that.
But I will show you whom to fear: Fear the One who, after killing the body, has power to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him.
Aren't five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
Even the hairs on your head are all counted. Don't be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows."
"I tell you, everyone who confesses Me before people, the Son of Man will also confess before God's angels.
But whoever denies Me before people will be denied before God's angels.
Everyone who speaks against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but anyone who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, don't worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.
For the Holy Spirit will teach you at that time what you should say."
Someone in the crowd said to Him, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me."
Jesus replied, "Man, who appointed Me judge or divider over you?"
"Watch out! Guard yourselves against every kind of greed. Life is not about having many things."
Then He told them this parable: "A rich man's land produced a big crop.
He thought to himself, 'What should I do? I have no place to store my crops.'
Then he said, 'I know what I'll do. I'll tear down my barns and build bigger ones, and there I'll store all my grain and goods.'
And I'll say to myself, 'You have plenty of good things saved up for many years. Take it easy; eat, drink, and be merry.'"
But God said to him, "You fool! This very night your life will be demanded from you. Then who will get what you have prepared?"
"That's how it is for anyone who piles up wealth for himself but isn't rich toward God."
Then Jesus said to His disciples, "So I tell you, don't worry about your life, about what you will eat, or about your body, about what you will wear.
Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothes."
"Look at the ravens. They don't plant or harvest. They have no storeroom or barn, yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than birds!
Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to your life?
Since you can't do that small thing, why do you worry about the rest?"
"Think about how the wildflowers grow. They don't work or spin thread. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of them.
If God dresses the grass of the field like that—grass that is here today and thrown into the fire tomorrow—how much more will He clothe you, you who have little faith!"
"And don't keep worrying about what you will eat or drink.
The people of the world run after all these things, but your Father knows you need them.
Instead, seek His kingdom, and these things will be given to you as well."
"Don't be afraid, little flock, because your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Make purses for yourselves that won't wear out—a treasure in heaven that never runs out, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be too."
"Stay dressed for work and keep your lamps burning.
Be like servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him right away.
Those servants are blessed when the master finds them awake at his coming. I tell you the truth: He will dress himself to serve, have them sit at the table, and wait on them.
They will be blessed whether he comes in the second or third watch of the night, if he finds them ready."
"But understand this: If the owner of the house had known when the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you don't expect."
Peter said, "Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everyone?"
The Lord answered, "Who then is the faithful and wise manager? The master will put him in charge of the servants to give them their food at the right time.
That servant is blessed if the master finds him doing this when he returns.
I tell you the truth, he will put him in charge of all he owns."
"But suppose that servant says to himself, 'My master is taking a long time to come,' and then starts beating the other servants, men and women, and eating and drinking and getting drunk.
The master of that servant will come on a day he doesn't expect and at an hour he doesn't know. He will punish him severely and put him with the unbelievers."
"The servant who knows his master's will but doesn't get ready or do what the master wants will be beaten with many blows.

But the one who doesn't know and does things deserving punishment will be beaten with few blows. From everyone who has been given much, much will be demanded. And from the one who has been trusted with much, much more will be asked."
"I have come to bring fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already burning!
But I have a baptism to go through, and I am troubled until it is finished.
Do you think I came to bring peace on earth? No, I tell you, but division.
From now on, five in one home will be divided, three against two and two against three.
They will be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law."
He said to the crowd, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say right away, 'It's going to rain,' and it does.
And when the south wind blows, you say, 'It's going to be hot,' and it is.
You hypocrites! You know how to read the signs of the earth and sky. How is it that you don't know how to read this time?"
"Why don't you judge for yourselves what is right?

As you go with your opponent to the ruler, try hard to settle with him on the way. Otherwise he may drag you before the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell you, you won't get out until you have paid the very last penny."
At that time, some people told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
He answered, "Do you think these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered this way?
No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way."
"Or those eighteen who died when the tower in Siloam fell on them—do you think they were worse sinners than all the other people living in Jerusalem?
No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way."
Then Jesus told this parable: "A man had a fig tree growing in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it, but he found none.
"So he said to the gardener, 'Look, for three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and I have found none. Cut it down! Why should it waste the soil?'
"The gardener answered, 'Sir, leave it alone for one more year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
"'If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, then cut it down.'"
On a Sabbath, Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues.
A woman was there who had been crippled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up at all.
When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, "Woman, you are set free from your disability."
Then He put His hands on her, and right away she stood up straight and praised God.
The synagogue leader was angry because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. He said to the crowd, "There are six days for work. So come and be healed on those days, not on the Sabbath."
The Lord answered him, "You hypocrites! Doesn't each of you untie his ox or donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead it out to give it water?
Shouldn't this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be set free on the Sabbath day from what bound her?"
When Jesus said this, all His opponents were put to shame, but all the people were glad about all the wonderful things He was doing.
Then Jesus asked, "What is the kingdom of God like? What shall I compare it to?"
