Five days later, the high priest Ananias went down to Caesarea with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus. They brought charges against Paul before the governor.
When Paul was called in, Tertullus began to accuse him. He said, “Because of you, most excellent Felix, we enjoy great peace, and because of your care, good reforms have come to this nation.
We accept this everywhere and in every way with full thanks.
But so I will not take more of your time, I ask you, in your kindness, to listen to us for a short time.”
“We have found this man to be a troublemaker. He stirs up riots among all the Jews throughout the world. He is a leader of the Nazarene group.
He even tried to make the temple unclean, and we seized him.
If you examine him, you yourself can learn the truth about all these charges we are making against him.”
The Jews agreed and said these things were true.
The governor motioned for Paul to speak. Paul replied, “I know you have judged this nation for many years, so I am glad to defend myself.
You can check and see that it has not been more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
No one found me arguing with anyone in the temple, causing a crowd in the synagogues, or stirring up trouble in the city.
They cannot prove to you the charges they are making against me now.
But I admit this to you: I worship the God of our fathers according to the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything in the Law and what the Prophets wrote.
I have hope in God, which these men also share: there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
Because of this, I always try to keep a clear conscience before God and before people.
After many years, I came to bring gifts to help my people and to offer sacrifices.
They found me in the temple after I had been purified. There was no crowd and no uproar. Some Jews from Asia started the trouble.
They should be here before you to accuse me if they have anything against me.
Or let these men here say what wrong they found when I stood before the Jewish council.
The only thing is this one cry I shouted while standing among them: ‘It is about the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’”
Felix knew a lot about the Way, so he put the case off. He said, “When Commander Lysias comes down, I will decide your case.”
He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard, but to give him some freedom and let his friends care for him.
Several days later, Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He sent for Paul and listened to him talk about faith in Christ Jesus.
As Paul talked about doing what is right, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became afraid. He said, “Go away for now. When I have time, I will send for you.”
At the same time, he hoped Paul would give him money. So he sent for him often and talked with him.
After two years, Porcius Festus took Felix’s place. Because Felix wanted to please the Jews, he left Paul in prison.
Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
The chief priests and the leading men of the Jews brought charges against Paul to him and urged him
to send for Paul to come to Jerusalem, planning to ambush and kill him on the way.
Festus answered that Paul was being kept at Caesarea and that he himself was about to leave soon.
"So," he said, "let those among you who are leaders go down with me and accuse him, if there is anything wrong with the man."
After staying no more than eight or ten days among them, he went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered Paul to be brought.
When Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges that they could not prove.
Paul defended himself, saying, "I have done nothing wrong against the Jewish law, or the temple, or Caesar."
Festus, wanting to do the Jews a favor, answered Paul, "Do you want to go up to Jerusalem and be tried there before me about these things?"
Paul said, "I am standing before Caesar's judgment seat, where I must be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.
If I am guilty and have done something worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if none of their charges are true, no one can hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar."
Then Festus, after talking with his council, answered, "You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you will go."
After some days, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to greet Festus.
While they stayed there many days, Festus told the king about Paul's case, saying, "There is a man left as a prisoner by Felix.
When I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews informed me about him, asking that he be condemned.
I answered them that it is not Roman custom to hand over any man before the accused has faced his accusers and had a chance to answer the charge.
So when they came here, I did not delay. The next day I sat on the judgment seat and ordered the man to be brought.
When the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of the evil things I had suspected.
Instead, they had some questions against him about their own religion and about a dead man named Jesus, whom Paul claimed was alive.
Being unsure how to investigate these things, I asked if he wanted to go to Jerusalem and be tried there about them.
But Paul appealed to be kept for the decision of the Emperor, and I ordered him kept until I could send him to Caesar."
Agrippa said to Festus, "I would like to hear the man myself." "Tomorrow," Festus said, "you will hear him."
The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great show, and they entered the hearing room with the commanders and the leading men of the city. At Festus's command, Paul was brought in.
Festus said, "King Agrippa and all the men here with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish crowd has urged me both here and in Jerusalem, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.
But I found that he had done nothing deserving death. Since he himself appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.
I have nothing certain to write to my lord about him. Therefore I have brought him before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this examination I may have something to write.
For it seems unreasonable to me to send a prisoner without also stating the charges against him."
King Agrippa said to Paul, "You may speak for yourself." Then Paul stretched out his hand and defended himself.
"King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to defend myself before you today about all that the Jews accuse me of.
You are an expert in all the Jewish customs and questions, so I beg you to listen to me patiently.
"All the Jews know my life from the start, from my youth among my own people and in Jerusalem.
They have known me for a long time, and if they are willing, they can say that I lived as a Pharisee, following the strictest part of our religion.
"Now I stand on trial because of the hope in God's promise to our ancestors.
Our twelve tribes hope to reach that promise as they worship day and night. King, it is because of this hope that the Jews accuse me.
Why do you think it is unbelievable that God raises the dead?
"I myself thought I should do many things against the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
I did this in Jerusalem. I got authority from the chief priests, and I put many holy people in prison. When they were killed, I voted against them.
I punished them often in every synagogue and tried to make them speak against God. I was very angry with them, and I even chased them to cities outside our land.
"While I was going to Damascus with authority and a commission from the chief priests,
at midday, King, I saw a light from heaven. It was brighter than the sun, and it shone around me and the men traveling with me.
"We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, "'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to keep resisting.'
"I said, 'Who are You, Lord?' and the Lord said, "'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.'
"'But get up and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you as a servant and witness of the things you have seen and of the things I will show you.
I will rescue you from your people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you,
to open their eyes so they may turn from darkness to light and from Satan's power to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those made holy by faith in Me.'
"So, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.
First to those in Damascus, then in Jerusalem and all Judea, and also to the Gentiles, I preached that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
"For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.
But I have had God's help to this day, and I stand testifying to everyone, from the least to the greatest, saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:
that the Christ would suffer, that He would be the first to rise from the dead, and that He would proclaim light to the people and to the Gentiles."
As Paul was saying this in his defense, Festus shouted loudly, "Paul, you are out of your mind! Your great learning is driving you insane."
Paul said, "I am not insane, most excellent Festus, but I am speaking true and sensible words.
The king knows about these things, and I speak openly to him. I am sure none of this is hidden from him, because it was not done in secret.
King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you believe."
Agrippa said to Paul, "In a short time you are trying to persuade me to become a Christian."
Paul replied, "I would pray to God that whether in a short time or a long time, not only you but all who hear me today would become like me, except for these chains."
Then the king, the governor, Bernice, and those sitting with them got up.
As they left, they talked to each other and said, "This man has done nothing deserving death or chains."
Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."
When it was decided that we would sail to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners over to a centurion named Julius, who was in the Augustan Regiment.
We boarded a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail along the coast of Asia, and we set sail. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
The next day we landed at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and allowed him to go to his friends to receive care.
From there we put out to sea and sailed along the sheltered side of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
When we had sailed across the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.
There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship bound for Italy and put us on board.
We sailed slowly for many days and barely reached Cnidus. The wind did not let us go on, so we sailed along the sheltered side of Crete, off Salmone.
Coasting along it with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
Much time had passed, and the voyage was now dangerous because the Jewish day of fasting had already gone by. So Paul warned them.
He said, "Men, I can see that this voyage will end in disaster and great loss—not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives."
But the centurion paid more attention to the pilot and the owner of the ship than to what Paul said.

Since the harbor was not a good place to spend the winter, most of the men decided to sail on, hoping to reach Phoenix, a harbor in Crete that faces southwest and northwest, and stay there for the winter.
When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their chance. So they pulled up anchor and sailed along the coast of Crete.
But before long, a violent wind called the Northeaster swept down from the island.
When the ship could not face the wind, we stopped trying to steer and were driven along.
As we passed under the shelter of a small island called Cauda, we could barely bring the lifeboat under control.
After hoisting it aboard, the crew passed ropes under the ship to hold it together. Fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and let the ship drift.
Because we were being pounded by the storm, the next day the crew began to throw the cargo overboard.
On the third day, they threw the ship's equipment overboard with their own hands.
When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and the storm kept raging, we finally gave up all hope of being saved.

After they had gone a long time without eating, Paul stood up among them and said, "Men, you should have listened to me and not sailed from Crete. Then you would have spared yourselves this harm and loss.
But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because not one of you will be lost; only the ship will be destroyed.
For last night an angel of God stood beside me—the God I belong to and serve. He said,
'Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand trial before Caesar. And God has graciously given you the lives of all who sail with you.'
"So take courage, men, for I have faith in God that it will happen just as He told me.
But we must run aground on some island."
On the fourteenth night, we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors thought they were approaching land.
They measured the depth and found twenty fathoms. A short time later they measured again and found fifteen fathoms.
Fearing that we would be dashed against the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daylight.
In an attempt to escape from the ship, the sailors let down the lifeboat into the sea, pretending they were going to lower anchors from the bow.
Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay with the ship, you cannot be saved."
So the soldiers cut the ropes holding the lifeboat and let it drift away.
Just before dawn, Paul urged everyone to eat. He said, "For fourteen days you have been waiting and going without food, and you haven't eaten anything.
So I urge you to eat. You need it to survive. Not one of you will lose even a single hair from your head."
After he said this, he took bread, gave thanks to God in front of everyone, broke it, and began to eat.
They all were encouraged and ate food themselves.
Altogether there were 276 of us on board.
When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
When daylight came, they did not recognize the land. But they saw a bay with a beach and decided to run the ship aground there if they could.
They cut the anchors loose and left them in the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that held the rudders. Then they raised the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, but the stern began to break up from the force of the waves.
The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so that none of them could swim away and escape.
But the centurion wanted to spare Paul's life, so he stopped them. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
The rest were to follow, some on planks and some on pieces of the ship. In this way everyone reached land safely.
After we were brought safely to shore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
The local people showed us unusual kindness. They lit a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
Paul gathered a pile of brushwood and put it on the fire. A poisonous snake came out of the heat and bit his hand.
When the local people saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “This man must be a murderer. He was saved from the sea, but Justice will not let him live.”
But Paul shook the snake off into the fire and was not hurt.
The people expected him to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. After they waited a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
Near that place were fields belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and took care of us kindly for three days.
Publius’s father was in bed, sick with fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, prayed, placed his hands on him, and healed him.
After this happened, the rest of the sick people on the island came and were healed.
They honored us in many ways and gave us what we needed for our trip.
After three months, we sailed in a ship from Alexandria that had spent the winter on the island. Its sign was the Twin Brothers.
We landed at Syracuse and stayed there three days.
From there we traveled along the coast and reached Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.
There we found some brothers and were invited to stay with them seven days. After that, we came to Rome.
The brothers there had heard about us and came as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he took courage and thanked God.
When we got to Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

Three days later, Paul called together the leading men of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, I have done nothing against our people or against the customs of our fathers. Yet I was arrested in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
The Romans questioned me and wanted to release me, because they found no reason for me to die.
But when the Jews objected, I was forced to appeal to Caesar. I did not do this to accuse my own people.
That is why I asked to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am wearing this chain.”
They replied, “We have not received any letters from Judea about you, and none of the brothers who came here has reported or said anything bad about you.
But we would like to hear what you think, because people everywhere are speaking against this group.”

They set a day to meet with him. Many people came to his lodging. From morning until evening, he explained and testified about the kingdom of God. He tried to convince them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
Some were convinced by what he said, but others did not believe.
They did not agree with each other and were leaving after Paul said one thing: “The Holy Spirit spoke well to your fathers through the prophet Isaiah: ‘Go to this people and say, “
You will hear by hearing and not understand, and seeing you will see and not perceive.

For the heart of this people has grown dull, and they hear with difficulty with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, turn, and I would heal them.”’
Therefore, let it be known to you that this salvation from God has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen.”
Paul stayed two full years in a house he rented. He welcomed everyone who came to him.
He preached the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without anyone stopping him.
Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, was called to be an apostle. He was set apart for the gospel of God.
God promised this gospel long ago through His prophets in the holy Scriptures.
The gospel is about His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. As a man, He came from the family line of David.
But by the power of the Holy Spirit, He was shown to be the Son of God when He was raised from the dead.
Through Him, we received grace and the work of being apostles. We do this so people from all nations will obey God because they trust in Him. This brings honor to Jesus' name.
You are among those people, since you are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
To everyone in Rome who is loved by God and called to be His holy people: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is talked about all over the world.
God is my witness. I serve Him with my whole spirit by sharing the gospel about His Son. I never stop praying for you.
In my prayers, I always ask that, if it is God's will, I may finally be able to visit you.
I really want to see you so I can share a spiritual gift with you. It will make you stronger.
I mean that we can encourage each other by the faith we share—you and I.

Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that I have planned to come to you many times, but I have been stopped until now. I want to do some good work among you, just as I have done among other nations.
I owe a debt to Greeks and non-Greeks, and to wise people and foolish people.
That is why I am eager to preach the gospel to you in Rome too.
I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is God's power to save everyone who believes. It is for the Jew first, and then for the Greek.
In the gospel, God shows His way of making people right with Him. It begins with faith and grows into more faith. The Bible says, "The righteous will live by faith."
God's anger is shown from heaven against every kind of godlessness and wickedness. People push down the truth by their evil.
What can be known about God is clear to them, because God has made it clear.
Since the world was made, God's invisible qualities—His lasting power and divine nature—have been easy to see. People can understand them through what God made. So no one has an excuse.
They knew God, but they did not honor Him as God or thank Him. Their thinking became useless, and their foolish hearts became dark.
They said they were wise, but they became fools.
They traded the glory of the God who lives forever for images that look like mortal people, birds, animals, and reptiles.
So God let them follow the sinful desires of their hearts. They became impure, and they dishonored their bodies with each other.
They traded God's truth for a lie. They worshiped and served created things instead of the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
Because of this, God let them have shameful desires. Even their women traded natural sexual relations for unnatural ones.

The men did the same. They stopped having natural relations with women and burned with desire for each other. Men did shameful things with other men. They received in themselves the punishment their wrong choices deserved.
Since they did not think it was important to know God, God let them have a mind that is no good. They do things that should not be done.
They are full of every kind of wrong: evil, greed, and meanness. They are full of envy, murder, fighting, trickery, and spite. They gossip
and slander. They hate God. They are rude, proud, and boastful. They invent new ways to do evil. They disobey their parents.
They are foolish, unfaithful, unloving, and without mercy.
They know God's rule: people who do these things deserve death. But they not only do them; they also approve of others who do them.
So you have no excuse, whoever you are, when you judge someone else. When you judge another person, you condemn yourself, because you who judge do the same things.
We know that God’s judgment on people who do such things is true.
Do you think you will escape God’s judgment, you who judge others for doing these things but do them yourself?
Or do you look down on the riches of His kindness, patience, and self-control? Don’t you know that God’s kindness leads you to turn from sin?
But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.
He will repay each person according to what they have done.
To those who patiently do good and seek glory, honor, and life that never ends, He will give eternal life.
But to those who are selfish, who do not obey the truth but follow evil, there will be wrath and anger.
There will be trouble and distress for every person who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Gentile.
But there will be glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Gentile.
For God does not show favoritism.
All who sin without the law will also perish without the law. All who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
For it is not those who hear the law who are right with God, but those who do what the law says who will be made right.
When people who do not have the law do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.
They show that the work of the law is written on their hearts. Their conscience also bears witness, and their thoughts sometimes accuse them and sometimes defend them.
This will take place on the day when God, through Jesus Christ, judges people’s hidden secrets, as my good news says.
Now, if you call yourself a Jew and rely on the law and take pride in God,
and you know His will and can choose what is best because you have been taught from the law,
and you are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for people in the dark,
and you are a teacher of foolish people and a teacher of children, because you have in the law the form of knowledge and truth.
So, you teach others, but do you not teach yourself? You preach, “Do not steal,” but do you steal?
You say, “Do not commit adultery,” but do you commit adultery? You hate idols, but do you rob temples?
You brag about the law, but do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
As it is written, “Because of you, God’s name is insulted among the Gentiles.”
Circumcision has value if you obey the law. But if you break the law, your circumcision becomes like no circumcision at all.
So, if an uncircumcised man keeps the law’s requirements, won’t he be treated as if he were circumcised?
And the one who is uncircumcised by nature but keeps the law will judge you, who have the written law and circumcision but break the law.
A person is not a true Jew just because he looks like one on the outside, and circumcision is not just a physical act.
No, a true Jew is one inwardly, and true circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written law. That person’s praise comes from God, not from people.
What advantage, then, does a Jew have? Or what good does circumcision do?
Much in every way! First of all, the Jews were trusted with God's very words.
What if some did not believe? Does their lack of faith cancel God's faithfulness?
Not at all! Let God be true, and every person a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right in Your words, and win when You are judged.”
But if our wrong shows how right God is, what should we say? Is God unfair to bring His anger? (I am speaking in human terms.)
Not at all! If that were true, how could God judge the world?
But if my lie makes God's truth stand out more and brings Him glory, why am I still judged as a sinner?
And why not say, as some falsely claim we say, “Let us do evil so that good may come”? They deserve to be condemned.
What then? Are we better than others? Not at all! We have already shown that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.
As it is written: “No one is right with God, not even one.
No one understands; no one looks for God.
They have all turned away and become worthless. No one does good, not even one.
Their throats are open graves. They use their tongues to lie. The poison of snakes is on their lips.
Their mouths are full of curses and bitterness.
Their feet are quick to spill blood.
Ruin and pain are in their paths.
They do not know the way of peace.
Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law. It stops every mouth and makes the whole world answer to God.
So no one will be made right with God by obeying the law. The law only shows us our sin.
But now God's way of making people right with Him has been shown. It does not depend on the law, but the Law and the Prophets point to it.
This right standing with God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no difference.
For all have sinned and fall short of God's glory.
Yet they are made right with God freely by His grace through the rescue that is in Christ Jesus.

God offered Jesus as the sacrifice that turns away His anger. We take hold of this through faith in His blood. God did this to show that He is right. In His patience, He had not punished sins committed earlier.
He did this to show that He is right at this time. He is right, and He makes right the person who has faith in Jesus.
So where is there room to boast? It is gone. What kind of law removes boasting? Not a law of works, but a law of faith.
For we say that a person is made right with God by faith, without obeying the law.
Is God only the God of the Jews? Is He not also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, He is the God of the Gentiles too.
There is only one God. He will make people who are circumcised right with Him by faith, and He will make people who are not circumcised right with Him through that same faith.
Do we destroy the law by this faith? Not at all! Instead, we show that the law is true.
What then shall we say Abraham, our forefather in the flesh, discovered?
For if Abraham was justified by works, he had something to boast about—but not before God.
For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness."
Now to the one who works, his wages are not credited as a gift but as something owed.
But to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness.
David says the same thing when he talks about the blessing of the person to whom God credits righteousness without works:
"Blessed are those whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
Blessed is the man whose sin the LORD will never count against him."
Is this blessing only for the circumcised, or also for the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham's faith was credited to him as righteousness.
How then was it credited? Was it after he was circumcised, or before? It was not after, but before.

And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but have not been circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.
And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith is made useless and the promise is cancelled.
For the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no breaking of it.

Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may be by grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham's offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.
As it is written: "I have made you a father of many nations." He is our father in the sight of God, in whom he believed—the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being things that were not.
Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as it had been said to him, "So shall your offspring be."
Without weakening in his faith, he faced the fact that his body was as good as dead—since he was about a hundred years old—and that Sarah's womb was also dead.
Yet he did not waver through unbelief regarding the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God.
Being fully sure that God had the power to do what He had promised.
This is why "it was credited to him as righteousness."
The words "it was credited to him" were written not for him alone,
but also for us, to whom God will credit righteousness—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
He was handed over to die for our sins and was raised to life to make us right with God.
So, since we have been made right with God by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Through Him we have also gained access by faith into this grace where we now stand. We boast in the hope of God's glory.
Not only that, but we also boast in our troubles. We know that trouble produces patience.
Patience produces character, and character produces hope.
That hope will not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.
While we were still weak, Christ died for ungodly people at just the right time.
It is rare for someone to die for a righteous person. Maybe someone would dare to die for a good person.
But God shows His love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
Since we have now been made right with God by His blood, we will be saved from God's anger through Him even more.
If we were brought back to God through the death of His Son while we were enemies, then we will be saved by His life even more, now that we are brought back.
Not only that, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ. Through Him we have now been brought back to God.
So, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, death spread to all people because all sinned.
Sin was in the world before the law was given, but sin is not counted when there is no law.
Yet death ruled from Adam to Moses, even over people who did not sin in the same way Adam did. Adam is a pattern of the One who was to come.

But God's free gift is not like Adam's sin. If many died because of one man's sin, then God's grace and the gift that come through the grace of one man, Jesus Christ, overflowed to many people even more.
The gift is not like the result of one man's sin. One sin brought judgment and punishment, but the free gift brings right standing with God after many sins.
If death ruled because of one man's sin, then those who receive God's rich grace and the gift of being made right with Him will rule in life through one man, Jesus Christ, even more.
So, just as one sin brought punishment to all people, one act of doing right brings life and being made right with God to all people.
Just as one man's disobedience made many people sinners, one man's obedience will make many people right with God.
The law was added so that sin would increase. But where sin increased, grace increased even more.
Sin once ruled in death. Now grace rules through being made right with God, leading to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
So what should we say? Should we keep on sinning so that grace can increase?
Absolutely not! We died to sin. How can we still live in it?
Don't you know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
We were buried with Him through baptism into death. This happened so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the Father's glory, we too can live a new life.
If we have been joined to Him in a death like His, then we will also be joined to Him in a resurrection like His.
We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that sin's power over the body would be broken. Then we would no longer be slaves to sin.
Anyone who has died has been set free from sin.
If we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.
We know that Christ was raised from the dead and will never die again. Death no longer rules over Him.
The death He died, He died to sin once for all. The life He lives now, He lives to God.
In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
So do not let sin rule in your mortal body. Do not obey its evil desires.

Do not offer the parts of your body to sin as tools for wickedness. Instead, offer yourselves to God as people who have been brought from death to life. Offer the parts of your body to Him as tools for righteousness.
Sin will not be your master, because you are not under the law but under grace.
What then? Should we sin because we are not under the law but under grace? Absolutely not!

Don't you know that when you offer yourselves as slaves to obey someone, you are slaves to the one you obey? You are slaves either to sin, which leads to death, or to obedience, which leads to righteousness.
But thanks be to God! You used to be slaves to sin, but now you have obeyed from the heart the teaching you were given.
You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.

I am using a human example because your human nature is weak. Just as you once offered the parts of your body as slaves to impurity and to more and more wrong, now offer them as slaves to righteousness that leads to holiness.
When you were slaves to sin, you were free from the control of righteousness.
What benefit did you get then from the things you are now ashamed of? The result of those things is death.
But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the result you get leads to holiness, and the end is eternal life.
The payment for sin is death, but God's gift is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Or don't you know, brothers and sisters—for I am speaking to those who know the law—that the law has power over a person only as long as that person lives?
For example, a married woman is bound by law to her husband while he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law that bound her to him.

So then, if she marries another man while her husband is still alive, people call her an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is free from that law, and she is not an adulteress if she marries another man.

In the same way, my brothers and sisters, you died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you could belong to another—to Him who was raised from the dead—so that we can produce good results for God.
For when we were ruled by our sinful desires, the sinful passions stirred up by the law were at work in our bodies, and that produced results that led to death.
But now we have died to what held us captive, so we are released from the law. We serve in the new way of the Spirit, not in the old way of written rules.

What shall we say, then? Is the law sin? Not at all! Yet I would not have known what sin was except through the law. For I would not have known what coveting was if the law had not said, "You shall not covet."
But sin used the commandment to stir up in me every kind of coveting. For without the law, sin had no power.
Once I was alive apart from the law, but when the commandment came, sin became active and I died.
I found that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death.
For sin used the commandment to deceive me, and through it put me to death.
So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, right, and good.

Did what is good, then, become death to me? By no means! But sin used what is good to bring about my death, so that sin might be shown for what it is. Through the commandment, sin became utterly sinful.
We know that the law is spiritual, but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.
I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do; but what I hate, I do.
And if I do what I do not want to do, I agree that the law is good.
As it is, it is no longer I who do it, but sin living in me.
For I know that nothing good lives in me—that is, in my sinful nature. For I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.
For I do not do the good I want to do, but the evil I do not want to do—this I keep on doing.
Now if I do what I do not want to do, it is no longer I who do it, but sin living in me.
So I find this law at work: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.
For in my inner being I delight in God's law.
But I see another law at work in my body, fighting against the law of my mind and making me a prisoner of the law of sin that lives in my body.
What a miserable person I am! Who will rescue me from this body that is subject to death?
Thanks be to God, who rescues me through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my sinful nature I serve the law of sin.
So now there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and death.
For what the law could not do, because it was weak through the flesh, God did. He sent His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin He condemned sin in the flesh.
He did this so that what the law requires would be fulfilled in us, who do not live by the flesh but by the Spirit.
For those who live by the flesh think about fleshly things, but those who live by the Spirit think about spiritual things.
The mindset of the flesh brings death, but the mindset of the Spirit brings life and peace.
The mindset of the flesh is hostile to God. It does not obey God's law, and it cannot.
People who are controlled by the flesh cannot please God.
But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed God's Spirit lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, that person does not belong to Him.
But if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit gives life because of righteousness.
And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you, then He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit who lives in you.
So then, brothers and sisters, we do not owe the flesh anything, so we should not live by it.
For if you live by the flesh, you are about to die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
For all who are led by God's Spirit are God's sons.
For you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry out, "Abba, Father!"
The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God's children.
And if we are children, then we are heirs—heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ—if indeed we suffer with Him so that we may also share His glory.
I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is going to be revealed to us.
For the creation waits with eager longing for the revealing of the sons of God.
For the creation was subjected to frustration, not willingly, but because of Him who subjected it, in hope
that the creation itself will be set free from its slavery to decay and brought into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
For we know that the whole creation has been groaning together and suffering birth pains until now.
And not only the creation, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for adoption as sons—the redemption of our bodies.
For in this hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope, for who hopes for what he sees?
But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience.
In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself prays for us with groans too deep for words.
And He who searches the hearts knows what the mind of the Spirit is, because He prays for the saints according to God's will.
And we know that God works all things together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to His purpose.
For those whom He foreknew He also destined ahead of time to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters.
And those whom He destined ahead of time He also called, and those whom He called He also made right with God, and those whom He made right with God He also gave glory to.
What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
He who did not spare His own Son, but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, with Him, freely give us all things?
Who will bring any charge against God's chosen ones? God is the One who makes us right.
Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is the One who died, and more than that, who was raised. He is at the right hand of God, and He also prays for us.
Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will hardship, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?
As it is written, "For your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered."
No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.
For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor authorities, neither things present nor things to come, nor powers,
neither height nor depth, nor anything else in creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
I speak the truth in Christ. I am not lying. My conscience, with the Holy Spirit as my witness, agrees with me.
I have great sorrow and pain that never stops in my heart.
I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own people by birth.
They are Israelites. God gave them adoption as sons, His glory, the covenants, the law, true worship, and the promises.
They have the patriarchs. And from them, by human descent, came the Christ, who is God over all, praised forever. Amen.
But it is not as if God's word has failed. Not everyone born into Israel truly belongs to Israel.
Not all of Abraham's descendants are his true children. Instead, God said, "Through Isaac your descendants will be counted."
This means the children born by human effort are not God's children. The children born through God's promise are the ones counted as His descendants.
This is what the promise said: "At the right time I will come back, and Sarah will have a son."
Not only that, but Rebecca also had children by one man, our father Isaac.
Before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, God's plan to choose stood firm.
It was not because of their works, but because of God's call. She was told, "The older will serve the younger."
As Scripture says, "I chose Jacob, but I rejected Esau."
What should we say then? Is God unfair? Not at all!
He said to Moses, "I will have mercy on anyone I choose, and I will show compassion to anyone I choose."
So it does not depend on human desire or effort. It depends on God's mercy.
Scripture says to Pharaoh, "I raised you up for this purpose: to show My power in you and to make My name known everywhere on earth."
So God has mercy on whom He wants, and He hardens whom He wants.
You might say to me, "Then why does God still blame us? Who can resist His will?"
But who are you, a mere man, to argue with God? Will the thing made say to its maker, "Why did You make me like this?"
Does the potter not have the right to make from the same clay one pot for special use and another for ordinary use?
What if God, wanting to show His anger and make His power known, put up with the people who deserved His anger—people prepared for destruction?
What if He did this to show the riches of His glory to the people He shows mercy to—people He prepared in advance for glory?
That includes us, whom He called—not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles.
As He says in Hosea: "I will call them 'My people' who are not My people, and I will call her 'My loved one' who is not My loved one."
"And in the very place where it was said to them, 'You are not My people,' they will be called 'children of the living God.'"
Isaiah cries out about Israel: "Even if the number of Israelites is like the sand by the sea, only a remnant will be saved."
For the Lord will carry out His judgment on the earth quickly and completely.
And as Isaiah said before, "If the Lord of Hosts had not left us a few descendants, we would have become like Sodom and been like Gomorrah."
What should we say then? The Gentiles, who were not chasing righteousness, have gained righteousness—the righteousness that comes from faith.
But Israel, who chased a law of righteousness, did not reach it.
Why? Because they did not pursue it by faith. They tried to get it by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone.
As it is written: "Look, I place in Zion a stone that makes people stumble and a rock that makes them fall. But the one who trusts in Him will never be put to shame."
Brothers, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for them is that they may be saved.
I can testify that they have a strong zeal for God, but it is not based on true knowledge.
Because they did not know God’s righteousness, and they tried to set up their own righteousness, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.
Christ is the end of the law, bringing righteousness to everyone who believes.
Moses writes about the righteousness that comes from the law: “The person who does these things will live by them.”
But the righteousness that comes from faith says this: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will go up to heaven?’” (That is, to bring Christ down.)
“Or, ‘Who will go down into the abyss?’” (That is, to bring Christ up from the dead.)
But what does it say? “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart.” (That is, the word of faith we are preaching.)
If you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
For with the heart a person believes and is made right with God, and with the mouth a person confesses and is saved.
For the Scripture says, “Everyone who believes in Him will not be put to shame.”
For there is no difference between Jew and Greek. The same Lord is Lord of all, and He richly blesses all who call on Him.
For, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
But how can they call on Him if they have not believed in Him? And how can they believe if they have not heard about Him? And how can they hear without someone preaching?
And how can anyone preach unless they are sent? As it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
But not all of them obeyed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
So faith comes from hearing, and hearing comes through the word of Christ.
But I ask, did they not hear? Yes, they did: “Their voice has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.”
But I ask, did Israel not know? First Moses says, “I will make you jealous with those who are not a nation; I will make you angry with a nation that has no understanding.”
And Isaiah boldly says, “I was found by those who were not looking for Me; I showed Myself to those who did not ask for Me.”
But to Israel He says, “All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and stubborn people.”
I ask then: Did God reject His people? Never! For I myself am an Israelite, from Abraham's family line, from the tribe of Benjamin.
God did not reject His people, whom He knew long ago. Don't you know what Scripture says about Elijah? He pleaded with God against Israel:
"Lord, they killed Your prophets and tore down Your altars. I'm the only one left, and they're trying to kill me."
But what did God's answer say? "I have kept seven thousand men for Myself, men who didn't bow to Baal."
So too, right now there is a small group chosen by grace.
And if it's by grace, then it's no longer by works. Otherwise grace wouldn't be grace.
What then? Israel didn't find what it was looking for, but the chosen ones did. The rest were hardened.
As it is written: "God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that don't see and ears that don't hear, to this very day."
And David says: "May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a payback to them.
May their eyes be darkened so they can't see, and may their backs be bent forever."
I ask then: Did they stumble so as to fall? No! Instead, because they fell, salvation came to the Gentiles, to make Israel jealous.
Now if their fall brought riches to the world, and their loss brought riches to the Gentiles, how much greater riches will come when they are fully restored!
I am speaking to you Gentiles. Because I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I take pride in my work,
hoping I might make my own people jealous and save some of them.
For if their rejection brought the world back to God, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
If the first part of the dough is holy, then the whole batch is holy. And if the root is holy, so are the branches.
If some of the branches were broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and now share in the good sap from the olive root,
don't brag over those branches. If you do brag, remember that you don't hold up the root, but the root holds you up.
You will say then, "Those branches were broken off so I could be grafted in."
That's true. They were broken off because of unbelief, and you stand by faith. Don't be proud, but stand in awe.
For if God didn't spare the natural branches, He won't spare you either.
So look at both God's kindness and His sternness: sternness to those who fell, but kindness to you, if you keep on in His kindness. Otherwise, you too will be cut off.
And if they don't keep on in unbelief, they will be grafted in again, for God is able to graft them in again.

For if you were cut out of an olive tree that is wild by nature, and against nature were grafted into a good olive tree, how much more will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!
I don't want you to miss this secret, brothers and sisters, so you won't be proud: A hardening has come upon Israel in part, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.
And in this way all Israel will be saved, as it is written: "The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will turn ungodliness away from Jacob.
And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins."
As far as the gospel is concerned, they are enemies for your sake; but as far as God's choice is concerned, they are loved because of their ancestors,
for God's gifts and His call can't be taken back.
Just as you were once disobedient to God but now have received mercy because of their disobedience,
so they have now become disobedient in order that they too may now receive mercy as a result of God's mercy to you.
For God has locked everyone up in disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.
Oh, the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable His judgments and untraceable His paths!
"For who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been His counselor?"
"Or who has ever given to God, that God should repay him?"
For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be glory forever. Amen.
So I urge you, brothers and sisters, because of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God. This is your true worship.
Do not copy the ways of this world. Instead, let God change you by making your minds new, so you can know God's will—what is good, pleasing, and perfect.

Because of the grace God gave me, I tell everyone among you not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think. Instead, he should think clearly and wisely, because God has given each person a measure of faith.
Just as one body has many parts, and not all parts do the same job,
so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each part belongs to the others.
We have different gifts, according to the grace God has given us. If a person has the gift of prophecy, let them use it in keeping with their faith.
If it is serving, serve; if teaching, teach.
If encouraging, encourage; if giving, give generously; if leading, lead with care; if showing mercy, do it cheerfully.
Love must be sincere. Hate what is evil; hold on to what is good.
Love each other deeply as brothers and sisters. Honor one another more than yourselves.
Never be lazy in your zeal. Be full of spirit, and serve the Lord.
Be joyful in hope, patient in trouble, and faithful in prayer.
Share with God's people who are in need, and welcome strangers into your home.
Bless those who persecute you; bless them and do not curse them.
Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but be willing to associate with people who are humble. Do not think you are smarter than you really are.
Do not pay back anyone evil for evil. Try to do what is right in the eyes of everyone.
If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
Dear friends, do not take revenge. Leave room for God's anger, because it is written: "Vengeance belongs to Me; I will pay it back," says the Lord.
Instead, "If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink. In doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head."
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Everyone must submit to the governing authorities, because no authority exists except from God, and the authorities that do exist have been appointed by God.
So whoever resists the authority resists what God has appointed, and those who resist will bring judgment on themselves.
For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be free from fear of the authority? Do what is good, and you will receive praise from it.
For it is God's servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for it does not bear the sword in vain. It is God's servant, an avenger who brings wrath on the one who practices evil.
So you must submit, not only to avoid punishment, but also to keep a clear conscience.
For this reason you also pay taxes, because the authorities are servants of God who give their full time to this work.
Pay everyone what you owe: taxes to those who collect taxes, customs to those who collect customs, respect to those who deserve respect, and honor to those who deserve honor.
Owe no one anything, except to love one another, for the one who loves another has fulfilled the law.

For the commandments, "You shall not commit adultery," "You shall not murder," "You shall not steal," "You shall not covet," and any other commandment, are summed up in this word: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
Do this, understanding the present time: it is already the hour for you to wake up from sleep, because our salvation is closer now than when we first believed.
The night is far gone; the day is at hand. So let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.
Let us live decently, as in the daytime, not in wild parties or drunkenness, not in sexual sin or shameless behavior, not in fighting or jealousy.
But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the flesh, to gratify its desires.
Accept the person whose faith is weak, but don't argue about opinions.
One person believes he can eat anything, but the weak person eats only vegetables.
The one who eats should not look down on the one who doesn't eat, and the one who doesn't eat should not judge the one who eats, because God has accepted him.
Who are you to judge someone else's servant? He stands or falls before his own master. And he will stand, because the Lord is able to make him stand.
One person thinks one day is more important than another; another thinks every day is the same. Each person should be fully sure in his own mind.
The one who honors a special day does it for the Lord. The one who eats does it for the Lord and gives thanks to God. The one who doesn't eat also does it for the Lord and gives thanks to God.
None of us lives for himself, and none of us dies for himself.
If we live, we live for the Lord; if we die, we die for the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
Christ died and came back to life for this reason, so that He might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
But why do you judge your brother? Or why do you look down on your brother? We will all stand before God's judgment seat.
For it is written, "As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow to Me, and every tongue will confess to God."
So each of us will give an account of himself to God.
So let's stop judging each other. Instead, make up your mind not to put a stumbling block or a trap in front of a brother.
I know and am sure in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean by itself. But if someone thinks something is unclean, then it is unclean for him.
If your brother is hurt because of food, you are no longer living by love. Don't destroy with food the person Christ died for.
Don't let your good be called evil.
For God's kingdom is not about eating and drinking. It is about doing right, having peace, and having joy in the Holy Spirit.
The person who serves Christ in this way pleases God and is approved by people.
So let's chase after the things that bring peace and build each other up.
Don't tear down God's work because of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a person to eat something that makes another person stumble.
It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything that makes your brother stumble.
Keep the faith you have between yourself and God. The person who doesn't condemn himself for what he approves is blessed.
But the person who doubts is condemned if he eats, because he doesn't eat from faith. And everything that is not from faith is sin.
We who are strong should carry the weaknesses of those who are not strong. We should not try to please ourselves.
Each of us should please our neighbor for his good, to build him up.
For even Christ did not please Himself. As it is written, “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”
Everything written in the past was written to teach us. It was written so that, through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.
May the God who gives endurance and encouragement give you the same attitude toward one another that Christ Jesus had.
Then, with one heart and one voice, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So accept one another, just as Christ accepted you, to bring glory to God.
For I tell you that Christ became a servant to the circumcised to show God's truth. He did this to confirm the promises made to the fathers.
He also came so that the Gentiles would glorify God for His mercy. As it is written, “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing to Your name.”
Again it says, “Rejoice, Gentiles, with His people.”
And again, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and let all the peoples praise Him.”
And again, Isaiah says, “The Root of Jesse will come. He will rise to rule over the Gentiles, and in Him the Gentiles will hope.”
May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him. Then you will overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
I am sure about you, my brothers and sisters. You are full of goodness and filled with all knowledge. You are able to teach one another.
Still, I have written to you quite boldly in part, to remind you of these things. I do this because of the grace God gave me.
He made me a servant of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles. I serve like a priest for God's good news. I do this so that the Gentiles may be an offering God accepts, made holy by the Holy Spirit.
So in Christ Jesus I can be proud of my work for God.
I will not talk about anything except what Christ has done through me. He led the Gentiles to obey God by what I said and did.
He worked through the power of signs and wonders, and through the power of God's Spirit. In this way, I have fully shared the good news of Christ from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum.
I have made it my goal to preach the good news where Christ is not known. I do not want to build on someone else's foundation.
As it is written, “Those who were not told about Him will see. Those who have not heard will understand.”
That is why I have often been kept from coming to you.
But now I have finished my work in these areas. I have wanted to visit you for many years.
I hope to see you on my way to Spain. I hope you will help me on my journey after I have enjoyed being with you for a while.
Right now, though, I am going to Jerusalem to serve God's people there.
For Macedonia and Achaia were happy to make a gift for the poor among God's people in Jerusalem.
They were happy to do it, and they owed it to them. The Gentiles have shared in the spiritual blessings of the believers in Jerusalem, so they should help them with material blessings.
So after I finish this task and safely deliver this gift, I will go to Spain and visit you on the way.
I know that when I come to you, I will come with the full blessing of Christ.
I urge you, brothers and sisters, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle. Pray to God for me.
Pray that I will be rescued from those in Judea who do not believe. Pray that my service in Jerusalem will be accepted by God's people there.
Then, by God's will, I may come to you with joy and be refreshed with you.
May the God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.
Welcome her in the Lord in a way worthy of God's people, and help her with anything she may need from you. She has helped many people, and she has helped me too.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, my coworkers in Christ Jesus.
They risked their lives for me. I am thankful to them, and so are all the churches of the Gentiles.
Greet the church that meets in their home. Greet my dear friend Epenetus, who was the first person in Asia to trust in Christ.
Greet Mary, who has worked hard for you.
Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and fellow prisoners. They are well known among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.
Greet Ampliatus, my dear friend in the Lord.
Greet Urbanus, our coworker in Christ, and my dear friend Stachys.
Greet Apelles, who has proved himself in Christ. Greet those who belong to Aristobulus's household.
Greet Herodion, my relative. Greet those in Narcissus's household who are in the Lord.
Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, women who have worked hard in the Lord. Greet my dear friend Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been like a mother to me too.
Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.
Brothers, I urge you to watch out for people who cause divisions and create obstacles that go against the teaching you learned. Stay away from them.
Such people do not serve our Lord Christ. They serve their own desires. By smooth talk and flattery they fool innocent people.
Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
Timothy, my coworker, sends greetings to you, and so do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
I, Tertius, who wrote this letter, greet you in the Lord.
Gaius, who hosts me and the whole church, sends greetings to you. Erastus, the city treasurer, and our brother Quartus send greetings to you.
Now to Him who can strengthen you according to my gospel and the message of Jesus Christ, and according to the revealing of the mystery that was hidden for long ages,
but is now shown and made known through the prophetic writings, by the command of the eternal God, to bring about the obedience of faith among all the nations—
to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ. Amen.
Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,
to the church of God in Corinth—to those made holy in Christ Jesus and called to be His holy people—along with all who everywhere call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God for you because of the grace God gave you in Christ Jesus.
For in Him you have been enriched in every way—in all your speaking and in all your knowledge.
This happened because our testimony about Christ was confirmed in you.
So you do not lack any spiritual gift as you wait for our Lord Jesus Christ to be revealed.
He will also keep you strong to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful. He called you into fellowship with His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be made complete in the same mind and the same purpose.
My brothers and sisters, some from Chloe’s household have told me that there are quarrels among you.
What I mean is this: One of you says, "I follow Paul"; Another says, "I follow Apollos"; Another says, "I follow Peter"; And still another says, "I follow Christ."
Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Were you baptized in the name of Paul?
I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
so that no one can say you were baptized in my name.
Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas. After that, I do not remember if I baptized anyone else.
For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the Good News—not with clever words, so that the cross of Christ would not lose its power.
For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are dying, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
For it is written: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise; the understanding of the clever I will set aside."
Where is the wise person? Where is the teacher of the law? Where is the philosopher of this age? Has not God made the wisdom of the world foolish?
For since the world, in God’s wisdom, did not know God through its own wisdom, God chose to save those who believe through the foolishness of preaching.
Jews ask for signs, and Greeks look for wisdom,
but we preach Christ crucified—a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles.
But to those God has called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
For the foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than human strength.
Brothers and sisters, think about your calling. Not many of you were wise by human standards; not many were powerful; not many were from noble families.
But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
God chose the lowly things of this world and the despised things—things that are not—to bring to nothing the things that are,
so that no one may boast before Him.
It is because of Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God—our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.
So, as it is written: "Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord."
Brothers, when I came to you, I did not come with fancy words or human wisdom. I came to tell you God’s truth.
I had decided to know only one thing among you: Jesus Christ, and Him nailed to a cross.
I was with you in weakness, fear, and much shaking.
My words and my preaching were not clever speeches meant to win you with human wisdom. They were proof of the Spirit and His power.
I did this so your faith would not rest on human wisdom, but on God’s power.
Yet among mature believers, we do speak wisdom. But it is not the wisdom of this world or of its rulers, who are fading away.
Instead, we speak God’s secret wisdom, which was hidden. God planned it before time began for our glory.
None of the rulers of this world understood it. If they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
But as it is written, “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined what God has prepared for those who love Him.”
But God has shown it to us through the Spirit. The Spirit searches everything, even the deep things of God.
Who knows a person’s thoughts except that person’s own spirit? In the same way, no one knows God’s thoughts except the Spirit of God.
We have not received the spirit of the world. We have received the Spirit who comes from God, so we can know the gifts God has given us.
We speak about these things not with words taught by human wisdom, but with words taught by the Spirit. We explain spiritual things with spiritual words.
A person who follows only human nature does not accept the things of God’s Spirit. To him they seem foolish, and he cannot understand them, because they can be understood only by the Spirit.
But a spiritual person judges all things, and no one judges him.
“Who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to teach Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.
Brothers, I could not speak to you as spiritual people. I had to speak to you as people who still follow the world. You were like babies in Christ.
I gave you milk, not solid food, because you were not ready for it. Even now you are not ready.
You are still following the world. When jealousy and arguing are among you, doesn't that show you are still following the world? Aren't you living like ordinary people?
When one person says he follows Paul, and another says he follows Apollos, aren't you just acting like ordinary people?
So what is Apollos? And what is Paul? We are only servants. Through us you believed, and the Lord gave each of us our job.
I planted the seed. Apollos watered it. But God made it grow.
So the one who plants is not important, and the one who waters is not important. Only God, who makes things grow, is important.
The one who plants and the one who waters are working together. Each will get his own reward for his own work.
We work together with God. You are God's field. You are God's building.
Because of God's grace given to me, I laid a foundation like a wise builder. Someone else is building on it. But let each person be careful how he builds.
No one can lay a different foundation. The foundation already laid is Jesus Christ.
If anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,
his work will be shown for what it is. The day will show it, because it will be revealed in fire. The fire will test the quality of each person's work.
If what he built lasts, he will receive a reward.
If it burns up, he will lose his work. But he himself will be saved, though only as through fire.
Don't you know that you are God's temple? Don't you know that God's Spirit lives in you?
If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy him. God's temple is holy, and you are that temple.
Let no one fool himself. If anyone among you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool so he can become wise.
The wisdom of this world is foolishness to God. It is written, "He catches the wise in their clever tricks."
And again, "The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are useless."
So let no one boast about people. All things are yours.
Whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or things present or things to come—all are yours.
And you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.
So then, people should think of us as servants of Christ and managers of God's mysteries.
The main thing asked of a manager is to be faithful.
I care very little if I am judged by you or by any human court. In fact, I don't even judge myself.
My conscience is clear, but that doesn't make me right. The Lord is the One who judges me.

So don't judge anything before the right time. Wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and show the true motives of people's hearts. Then each person will receive praise from God.

Now, brothers and sisters, I have used myself and Apollos as an example for your benefit, so you may learn from us the saying, "Do not go beyond what is written." Then you won't become proud by favoring one of us over the other.
Who makes you different from anyone else? What do you have that you didn't receive? And if you did receive it, why do you brag as if you didn't?
You already have everything you want! You are already rich! You have started to reign, and you did it without us! I wish you really had started to reign, so we could reign with you too.
It seems to me that God has put us apostles on display last, like men sentenced to die. We have become a show for the whole world, for angels and for people.
We are fools for Christ, but you are so wise in Christ! We are weak, but you are strong! You are honored, but we are dishonored!
Right up to this moment, we are hungry and thirsty. We wear rags, we are treated badly, and we have no home.
We work hard with our own hands. When people insult us, we bless them. When they persecute us, we put up with it.
When they say bad things about us, we answer with kindness. Even now, we have become like the trash of the world, the garbage everyone throws away.
I'm not writing this to shame you. I'm writing to warn you, because you are my dear children.
Even if you had ten thousand guides in Christ, you don't have many fathers. In Christ Jesus, I became your father through the good news.
So I urge you to follow my example.
That's why I sent Timothy to you. He is my dear and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which is the same everywhere in every church.
Some of you have become proud, as if I weren't coming to you.
But I will come to you very soon, if the Lord is willing. Then I will find out not just what these proud people are saying, but what power they have.
For God's kingdom isn't about talk. It's about power.
What do you want? Should I come to you with strict discipline, or with love and a gentle spirit?
It is actually reported that there is sexual sin among you, and the kind of sin that even people who don't know God don't commit: a man is in a sexual relationship with his father's wife.
And you are proud! Shouldn't you be sad instead and remove the man who did this from among you?
Even though I am not with you in body, I am with you in spirit. I have already judged the man who did this, as if I were there.
When you meet together in the name of our Lord Jesus, and my spirit is with you with the power of our Lord Jesus,
hand this man over to Satan to destroy his sinful nature, so that his spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.
Your pride is not good. Don't you know that a little yeast makes the whole batch of dough rise?
Get rid of the old yeast so you can be a new batch of dough without yeast. You are already like dough without yeast, because Christ, our Passover Lamb, has been sacrificed.
So let us celebrate, not with old yeast or yeast of evil and wickedness, but with bread without yeast, which stands for sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.
I did not mean people in this world who are sexually immoral, or greedy people, or cheats, or people who worship idols. If that were true, you would have to leave the world.

But now I am telling you not to associate with anyone who calls himself a brother if he is sexually immoral, greedy, worships idols, insults people, gets drunk, or cheats. Don't even eat with a person like that.
Why should I judge people outside the church? Aren't you the ones who should judge people inside?
God will judge those outside. "Remove the evil person from among you."
If one of you has a disagreement with another believer, does he dare to bring it before people who do wrong instead of before God's holy people?
Don't you know that God's holy people will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, aren't you good enough to handle small cases?
Don't you know that we will judge angels? How much more, then, the things of this life!
