So if you have ordinary disputes, why do you set as judges people whom the church looks down on?
I say this to make you ashamed. Is there really not one wise person among you who can settle a disagreement between believers?
Instead, one brother takes another to court, and that before unbelievers.
The fact that you have lawsuits with one another already means you have lost. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?
Instead, you cheat and wrong others, even your own brothers.

Don't you know that people who do wrong will not inherit God's kingdom? Don't be fooled. No sexually immoral person, idol worshiper, adulterer, or man who submits to or performs homosexual acts will inherit it.
Neither will thieves, greedy people, drunkards, people who insult others, or swindlers.
Some of you used to be like that. But you were washed clean, set apart for God, and made right with God in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
"Everything is allowed for me," but not everything is helpful. "Everything is allowed for me," but I will not be controlled by anything.
Food is for the stomach, and the stomach is for food, but God will destroy both. The body is not for sexual sin but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body.
By His power, God raised the Lord and will raise us too.
Don't you know that your bodies are parts of Christ? Should I take parts of Christ and join them to a prostitute? Never!
Or don't you know that anyone who joins himself to a prostitute becomes one body with her? For it is written, "The two will become one flesh."
But anyone who joins himself to the Lord becomes one spirit with Him.
Run away from sexual sin. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the person who is sexually immoral sins against his own body.
Don't you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you and whom you received from God, so you are not your own.
For you were bought with a price, so honor God with your body.
Now about what you wrote: It is good for a man not to have sexual relations with a woman.
But because of sexual sin, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.
A husband should fulfill his duty to his wife, and a wife should do the same for her husband.
A wife does not have authority over her own body; her husband does. In the same way, a husband does not have authority over his own body; his wife does.
Do not refuse to be intimate with each other, except when you both agree to take time apart to pray. Then come together again, so Satan will not tempt you because you lack self-control.
I say this as a suggestion, not as a command.
I wish everyone were like me. But each person has a different gift from God.
To unmarried people and widows I say: It is good to stay single, as I am.
But if they cannot control themselves, they should get married. It is better to marry than to burn with desire.
To married people I give this command—not I, but the Lord: A wife must not separate from her husband.
But if she does leave, she should stay single or make peace with her husband. A husband must not divorce his wife.
To the rest I say—I, not the Lord: If a Christian brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.
And if a woman has an unbelieving husband, and he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce her husband.
For the unbelieving husband is made holy through his wife, and the unbelieving wife is made holy through her husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but as it is, they are holy.
But if the unbeliever leaves, let them leave. A believing brother or sister is not bound in such cases. God has called you to live in peace.
Wife, how do you know if you will save your husband? Husband, how do you know if you will save your wife?
Each person should live the life the Lord has given them, just as God called them. This is the rule I give in all the churches.
Was a man circumcised when he was called? He should not try to undo it. Was a man uncircumcised when he was called? He should not be circumcised.
Circumcision does not matter, and uncircumcision does not matter. What matters is obeying God's commands.
Each person should stay in the situation they were in when God called them.
Were you a slave when you were called? Do not worry about it. But if you can become free, take that chance.
For a slave who was called in the Lord is the Lord's freed person. In the same way, a free person who was called is Christ's slave.
You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of human beings.
Brothers and sisters, each person should remain with God in the state in which they were called.
Now about unmarried people: I have no command from the Lord, but I give my opinion as someone the Lord has shown mercy to and made trustworthy.
Because of the present trouble, I think it is good for a person to stay as they are.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not try to get free. Are you free from a wife? Do not look for a wife.
But if you marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But those who marry will have trouble in this life, and I want to spare you.
What I mean, brothers and sisters, is that the time is short. From now on, those who have wives should live as if they did not.
Those who mourn should live as if they were not mourning; those who are happy should live as if they were not; those who buy things should live as if they did not own them.
And those who use the things of this world should not become too attached to them. For this world in its present form is passing away.
I want you to be free from worry. An unmarried man cares about the Lord's work and how to please the Lord.
But a married man cares about the things of this world and how to please his wife.

His attention is divided. An unmarried woman or virgin cares about the Lord's work, wanting to be holy in both body and spirit. But a married woman cares about the things of this world and how to please her husband.
I am saying this for your own good, not to restrict you, but so that you can live in a proper way and serve the Lord without being pulled in many directions.

If a man thinks he is not treating the woman he is engaged to fairly, and if she is past the usual age to marry, and he feels he should marry, he may do what he wants. He does not sin. They should get married.
But the man who has made up his mind and is under no pressure, who has control over his own will, and who has decided to keep her as she is, does well.
So the man who marries the woman he is engaged to does right, but the man who does not marry her does even better.
A woman is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.
In my opinion, she is happier if she stays as she is. And I think I too have the Spirit of God.
Now about food offered to idols: We know that all of us have knowledge. But knowledge makes people proud, while love builds them up.
If anyone thinks he knows something, he does not yet know as he should.
But if anyone loves God, that person is known by Him.
So about eating food offered to idols: We know that an idol is nothing in this world, and that there is only one God.
For even if there are so-called gods in heaven or on earth—and there are many gods and many lords—
yet for us there is one God, the Father. All things come from Him, and we live for Him. There is also one Lord, Jesus Christ. All things come through Him, and we live through Him.
But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are so used to idols that they still eat food as if it were offered to an idol, and their weak conscience becomes unclean.
Food does not bring us closer to God. We are not worse off if we do not eat, and we are not better off if we do.
But be careful that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to those who are weak.
For if someone with a weak conscience sees you, who have knowledge, eating in an idol's temple, won't that person feel encouraged to eat food offered to idols?
So the weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
When you sin against the brothers this way and wound their weak consciences, you sin against Christ.
Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I won't cause my brother to stumble.
Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven't I seen Jesus, our Lord? Aren't you my work in the Lord?
If I am not an apostle to other people, I am at least an apostle to you. You are the proof that I am an apostle in the Lord.
This is how I defend myself to those who question me.
Don't we have the right to eat and drink?
Don't we have the right to take a believing wife with us, like the other apostles, the Lord's brothers, and Peter?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who don't have the right to stop working?
Who ever serves as a soldier and pays his own way? Who plants a vineyard and doesn't eat its fruit? Who takes care of a flock and doesn't drink some of the milk?
Am I only using human reasoning? Doesn't the Law say the same thing?
For it is written in the Law of Moses, "Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain." Is God really concerned about oxen?
Or is He speaking entirely for our benefit? Surely it was written for us. The one who plows should plow with hope, and the one who threshes should thresh with hope of sharing in the crop.
If we planted spiritual things among you, is it too much to harvest material things from you?
If others have this right over you, don't we have an even greater right? But we did not use this right. Instead, we endure everything so that we won't get in the way of the gospel of Christ.
Don't you know that those who work in the temple eat from the temple, and those who serve at the altar share in what is offered on it?
In the same way, the Lord has commanded that those who preach the gospel should earn their living from the gospel.
But I have not used any of these rights. I am not writing this to get something from you. I would rather die than let anyone take away my reason to boast.
If I preach the gospel, I have nothing to boast about. I have to do it. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
If I do this because I want to, I get a reward. But if I do it because I have to, I have been trusted with a responsibility.
What is my reward then? It is that when I preach the gospel, I can offer it free of charge. That way, I do not make full use of my rights in the gospel.
I am free from everyone, but I have made myself a slave to everyone, so that I might win more people.

To the Jews I became like a Jew, so that I could win Jews. To those under the law, I became like someone under the law, even though I am not under the law myself, so that I could win those under the law.
To those not under the law, I became like someone not under the law. I am not free from God's law, but I am under Christ's law. I did this so that I could win those not under the law.
To the weak I became weak, so that I could win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that I might save some of them.
I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I can share in its blessings with them.
Don't you know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? So run in a way that you will win.
Everyone who competes trains in every way. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get one that will last forever.
So I do not run without a goal. I do not fight like someone who punches the air.
Instead, I discipline my body and make it obey me, so that after I preach to others, I won't fail the test myself.
I don't want you to be unaware, brothers, that all our ancestors were under the cloud and all passed through the sea.
They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
They all ate the same spiritual food.
They all drank the same spiritual drink, because they drank from a spiritual rock that went with them. That rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them, and they died in the wilderness.
These things happened to teach us a lesson. We should not crave evil things the way they did.
Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and then they got up to play.”
We must not be sexually immoral, as some of them were. Twenty-three thousand of them died in one day.
We must not put the Lord to the test, as some of them did. They were killed by snakes.
We must not grumble, as some of them did. They were killed by the destroyer.
All these things happened to them as warnings, and they were written down to teach us. We are the people who are living at the end of the ages.
So if anyone thinks he is standing firm, he should be careful not to fall.

No temptation has come to you that people have not faced before. God is faithful. He will not let you be tempted more than you can bear. He will give you a way out when you are tempted, so you can endure it.
So, my dear friends, run away from worshiping idols.
I am speaking to sensible people. Judge for yourselves what I say.
The cup of blessing that we give thanks for—isn't it a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break—isn't it a sharing in the body of Christ?
Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body. We all share in that one loaf.
Look at the people of Israel in the usual way. Aren't those who eat the sacrifices partners at the altar?
What am I saying then? That food offered to idols means anything, or that an idol is anything?
No. I mean that when people who don't know God offer sacrifices, they are really offering them to demons, not to God. I don't want you to share in what demons do.
You can't drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too. You can't share in the Lord's table and the table of demons.
Are we trying to make the Lord jealous? Are we stronger than He is?
Everything is allowed, but not everything helps. Everything is allowed, but not everything builds people up.
No one should look out only for himself. Each person should look out for the good of others.
Eat anything sold in the meat market. Don't ask questions about it because of conscience.
For the earth belongs to the Lord, and everything in it.
If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat whatever is put in front of you. Don't ask questions about it because of conscience.
But if someone says to you, “This food was offered to an idol,” then don't eat it. Do it for the sake of the person who told you and for the sake of conscience.
I'm not talking about your conscience. I'm talking about the other person's conscience. Why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience?
If I eat with thankfulness, why should I be criticized for food I thank God for?
So whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.
Don't cause anyone to stumble—not Jews, not Greeks, and not God's church.
I try to please everyone in everything I do. I don't look for what helps me. I look for what helps many people, so they can be saved.
Be like me, just as I am like Christ.
I praise you because you remember me in everything and hold on to the teachings I gave you.
But I want you to know that Christ is the head of every man, man is the head of woman, and God is the head of Christ.
Every man who prays or speaks God's message with his head covered brings shame on his head.
But every woman who prays or speaks God's message with her head uncovered brings shame on her head. It is the same as if her head were shaved.
If a woman will not cover her head, she should cut her hair short. But if it is shameful for a woman to cut her hair short or shave her head, then she should cover her head.
A man should not cover his head, because he is the image and glory of God. But woman is the glory of man.
Man did not come from woman, but woman came from man.
Man was not created for woman, but woman was created for man.
That is why a woman should have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
But in the Lord, woman is not separate from man, and man is not separate from woman.
Just as woman came from man, man is born through woman. But everything comes from God.
Decide for yourselves: is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Does not nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him?
But if a woman has long hair, it is her glory, because her hair was given to her as a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this, we have no other custom, and neither do God's churches.
But in giving these instructions, I do not praise you, because when you come together it is not for the better but for the worse.
First of all, I hear that when you meet as a church there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.
There must be differences among you so that those who are genuine may be recognized.
So when you come together, it is not really the Lord's Supper you are eating.
For when it is time to eat, each person goes ahead with his own meal. One person is hungry, and another has too much to drink.
Don't you have homes where you can eat and drink? Or do you look down on God's church and shame those who have nothing? What should I say to you? Should I praise you? I will not praise you for this.
For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: On the night He was betrayed, the Lord Jesus took bread.
After giving thanks, He broke it and said, "This is My body, which is for you. Do this in memory of Me."
In the same way, after supper He took the cup and said, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in memory of Me."
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you announce the Lord's death until He comes.
So then, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy way is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
Let each person examine himself, and then eat the bread and drink from the cup.
For anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.
That is why many among you are weak and sick, and some have died.
But if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.
When we are judged by the Lord, we are being trained so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
So, my brothers and sisters, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that when you come together it will not lead to judgment. I will give directions about the other matters when I come.
Now about spiritual gifts, brothers and sisters, I don't want you to be unaware.
You know that when you were pagans, you were led astray to mute idols, however you were led.
So I make known to you that no one who speaks by the Spirit of God says, "Jesus is cursed," and no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit gives them.
There are different kinds of service, but the same Lord.
There are different kinds of working, but the same God works all of them in everyone.
Each person is given a way the Spirit makes Himself known for the good of all.
To one person the Spirit gives a message of wisdom; to another, a message of knowledge by the same Spirit.
To another, faith by that same Spirit; to another, gifts of healing by the one Spirit.
To another, the power to do miracles; to another, prophecy; to another, the ability to tell spirits apart; to another, different kinds of tongues; and to another, the ability to explain tongues.
All these gifts are the work of one and the same Spirit. He gives them to each person, just as He chooses.
The body is like this: it is one, but it has many parts. Even though there are many parts, they all make up one body. It is the same with Christ.
We were all baptized by one Spirit into one body—whether Jews or Greeks, slaves or free—and we were all given the one Spirit to drink.
The body is not just one part; it has many parts.
If the foot said, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it stop being part of the body.
And if the ear said, "Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it stop being part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, where would hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would smelling be?
But God has placed the parts in the body, each one just as He wanted.
If all the parts were the same, where would the body be?
As it is, there are many parts, but one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, "I don't need you!" And the head cannot say to the feet, "I don't need you!"
In fact, the parts that seem weaker are needed even more.
We give special honor to the parts we think are less honorable. The parts we are ashamed to show are treated with more respect.
The parts we are not ashamed to show do not need that. But God has put the body together and given more honor to the part that lacked it.
He did this so there would be no division in the body, but so the parts would care for each other.
If one part suffers, all the parts suffer with it. If one part is honored, all the parts rejoice with it.
You are the body of Christ, and each of you is a part of it.
God has placed people in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then those who do miracles, then gifts of healing, helping, guiding, and different kinds of tongues.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And I will show you a way that is even better.
If I speak in human languages or even in the language of angels, but I do not have love, I am only a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal.
If I have the gift of prophecy and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so that I could move mountains, but I do not have love, I am nothing.
If I give everything I own to feed the poor, and if I hand over my body so that I can brag, but I do not have love, I gain nothing.
Love is patient and kind. Love does not envy, does not brag, and is not proud.
It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, and it keeps no record of wrongs.
It does not rejoice in evil, but it rejoices with the truth.
It always protects, always trusts, always hopes, and always perseveres.
Love never fails. But prophecies will cease, tongues will be stilled, and knowledge will pass away.
For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
but when completeness comes, what is partial will disappear.
When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, and I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.
For now we see only a dim reflection, as in a mirror; then we will see face to face. Now I know in part; then I will know fully, even as I am fully known.
And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love. But the greatest of these is love.
Pursue love, and be eager for spiritual gifts, but especially for prophecy.
For the one who speaks in a tongue does not speak to people but to God. No one understands him; he speaks mysteries by the Spirit.
But the one who prophesies speaks to people for their strengthening, encouragement, and comfort.
The one who speaks in a tongue builds up himself, but the one who prophesies builds up the church.
I wish all of you could speak in tongues, but I would rather you prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so the church may be built up.
Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I help you unless I bring you a revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching?
Even lifeless instruments, like a flute or harp, must make clear sounds. How will anyone know the tune unless the notes are different?
If a trumpet gives an unclear call, who will get ready for battle?
In the same way, unless you speak clear words with your tongue, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.
There are many kinds of languages in the world, and none is without meaning.
If I do not understand the meaning of a language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and he is a foreigner to me.
So it is with you. Since you are eager for spiritual gifts, strive to excel in the gifts that build up the church.
Therefore, the one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind gets no benefit.
What then? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.
Otherwise, if you bless with your spirit, how can someone who does not understand say “Amen” to your thanksgiving? He does not know what you are saying.
You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not built up.
I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
But in the church I would rather speak five clear words with my mind to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.
Brothers, do not be children in your thinking. Be like babies in evil, but be mature in your thinking.
It is written in the Law: “With strange tongues and foreign lips I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to Me,” says the Lord.
So tongues are a sign, not for believers but for unbelievers. Prophecy, however, is for believers, not for unbelievers.
So if the whole church comes together and everyone speaks in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?
But if an unbeliever or an outsider comes in while everyone is prophesying, he will be corrected and examined by all.
The secrets of his heart will be made plain. So he will fall on his face and worship God, saying, “God is really among you!”
What then, brothers? When you come together, each one has a hymn, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. Everything must be done to build up the church.
If anyone speaks in a tongue, two or at most three should speak, one at a time, and someone should interpret.
But if there is no interpreter, the speaker should be quiet in the church and speak to himself and to God.
Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should judge carefully what is said.
If a revelation comes to someone else while he is sitting, the first speaker should stop.
For you can all prophesy one at a time, so that everyone may learn and be encouraged.
The spirits of prophets are under the control of prophets.
For God is not a God of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints.
Women should remain silent in the churches. They are not permitted to speak, but must be submissive, as the Law says.
If they want to learn something, they should ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.
Did the word of God come from you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual person, he should recognize that what I am writing to you is the Lord's command.
But if anyone ignores this, he will be ignored.
So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
But everything should be done properly and in order.
Now, brothers and sisters, I want to remind you of the good news I preached to you. You received it, and you are standing firm in it.
Through it you are being saved, if you hold on to the message I preached to you—unless you believed for no reason.
I passed on to you what I received first: Christ died for our sins, just as the Scriptures say.
He was buried, and He rose again on the third day, just as the Scriptures say.
He appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at once. Most of them are still alive, though some have died.
Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
Last of all, He appeared to me too, as if I were born at the wrong time.
I am the least of the apostles. I am not even fit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted God's church.
But by God's grace I am what I am. His grace to me was not wasted. I worked harder than all of them, yet it was not really me, but God's grace with me.
So whether it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
Now, if we preach that Christ rose from the dead, how can some of you say there is no resurrection of the dead?
If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not been raised.
If Christ has not been raised, our preaching is empty, and your faith is empty too.
Then we are found to be false witnesses about God, because we said God raised Christ. But if the dead are not raised, He did not raise Him.
If the dead are not raised, Christ has not been raised either.
If Christ has not been raised, your faith is useless, and you are still in your sins.
Then those who died in Christ are lost.
If our hope in Christ is only for this life, we are the most pitiful of all people.
But Christ has been raised from the dead! He is the first of those who have died to be raised.
Since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead also comes through a man.
Just as everyone dies because of Adam, everyone will be made alive because of Christ.
But each in his own turn: Christ first, then those who belong to Christ when He comes.
Then comes the end, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father, after He has destroyed every ruler, authority, and power.
Christ must rule until He has defeated all His enemies.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
For Scripture says, "He has put everything under His control." But when it says everything is under His control, it does not include the One who gave Him that control.
When everything is under His control, then the Son Himself will submit to the One who gave Him control over everything, so that God may be all in all.
What will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?
And why do we put ourselves in danger every hour?
I face death every day, brothers and sisters. As surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord, this is true.
If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human reasons, what good did it do me? If the dead are not raised, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
Do not be fooled: bad company ruins good habits.
Wake up and do what is right, and stop sinning. Some of you do not know God. I say this to shame you.
But someone will ask, "How are the dead raised? What kind of body will they have?"
You fool! What you plant does not come to life unless it dies.
When you plant, you do not plant the body that will grow. You plant a bare seed, maybe wheat or something else.
But God gives it a body just as He wants. He gives each kind of seed its own body.
Not all flesh is the same. People have one kind of flesh, animals another, birds another, and fish another.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. The glory of the heavenly bodies is one kind, and the glory of the earthly bodies is another.
The sun has one kind of glory, the moon another, and the stars another. Even one star differs from another in glory.
So it is with the resurrection of the dead. What is planted decays; what is raised will never decay.
It is planted in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is planted in weakness; it is raised in power.
It is planted a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
That is why Scripture says, "The first man Adam became a living being." The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
The spiritual did not come first. The natural came first, then the spiritual.
The first man was made from dust. The second man is from heaven.
Just as the earthly man was, so are the earthly people. Just as the heavenly man is, so will the heavenly people be.
We wore the image of the earthly man, and we will wear the image of the heavenly man.
I tell you this, brothers and sisters: flesh and blood cannot inherit God's kingdom. What decays cannot inherit what will never decay.
Listen! I tell you a secret: we will not all die, but we will all be changed.
In a flash, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. The trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised so they will never decay, and we will be changed.
This body that can decay must become a body that will never decay, and this mortal body must become immortal.
When this body that can decay becomes a body that will never decay, and this mortal body becomes immortal, then the saying that is written will come true: "Death has been defeated by victory."
"Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?"
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
So, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always work hard for the Lord, because you know your work in the Lord is not wasted.
Now about the collection for God's people, you should do what I told the churches in Galatia to do.
On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside money at home and save as much as you can, so that when I come, we won't need to collect money then.
When I arrive, I will send letters with the people you choose to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
If it seems right for me to go too, they will travel with me.
I will come to you after I go through Macedonia, because I am traveling through Macedonia.
Maybe I will stay with you for a while, or even spend the winter, so you can help me on my way wherever I go next.
I don't want to see you only in passing now. I hope to stay with you for some time, if the Lord allows it.
But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost.
A big door for useful work has opened for me, but many people oppose me.
If Timothy comes, make sure he has nothing to fear while he is with you, because he is doing the Lord's work, just as I am.
No one should look down on him. Send him on his way in peace so he can come to me, because I am waiting for him along with the brothers.
Now about our brother Apollos: I urged him many times to come to you with the brothers, but he did not want to come now. He will come when he has a chance.
Be on guard. Stand firm in the faith. Be brave. Be strong.
Let everything you do be done in love.
You know that the family of Stephanas was the first to believe in Achaia, and they have given themselves to serving God's people. Brothers, I urge you
to submit to people like that and to everyone who works hard with them.
I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have come, because they made up for what you could not do.
They refreshed my spirit, and yours too. So respect people like them.
The churches in Asia send you their greetings. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, along with the church that meets in their home.
All the brothers and sisters send greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand.
If anyone does not love the Lord, let that person be cursed. Maranatha!
May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
My love is with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and Timothy our brother, to God's church in Corinth, along with all the saints throughout Achaia:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort.
He comforts us in all our troubles, so we can comfort anyone who is in trouble with the comfort we ourselves received from God.
For just as Christ's sufferings overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.
If we are troubled, it is for your comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which helps you patiently endure the same sufferings we go through.
Our hope for you is strong, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, you will also share in our comfort.
We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardship we faced in the province of Asia. We were weighed down far beyond what we could handle, so much that we gave up hope of living.
In fact, we felt we had already received a death sentence. But that happened so we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.
He has delivered us from such a deadly danger, and He will deliver us. We have put our hope in Him that He will keep delivering us.
You also help us by your prayers. Then many people will thank God for us because of the gracious gift given to us through the prayers of many.

This is what we are proud of: Our conscience tells us that we lived in the world, and especially with you, with the holiness and sincerity that come from God. We did not do it with worldly wisdom, but with God's grace.
We are not writing you anything other than what you can read and understand. I hope you will understand us fully,
just as you have partly understood us. Then you can be proud of us, just as we will be proud of you on the day of our Lord Jesus.
Because I was sure of this, I planned to visit you first, so you could receive a double blessing.
I planned to pass through you on my way to Macedonia, then come back to you from Macedonia, and have you send me on to Judea.
When I planned this, did I do it lightly? Or do I make plans in a merely human way, so that I would say "Yes, yes" when I mean "No, no"?
But as God is faithful, our message to you is not "Yes" and "No."
For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we preached among you—by me, Silvanus, and Timothy—was not "Yes" and "No." In Him it has always been "Yes."
For all of God's promises are "Yes" in Christ. And so through Him our "Amen" is spoken to God's glory.
Now God is the One who makes us stand firm with you in Christ and anointed us.
He has also sealed us and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a pledge.
I call on God as my witness that it was to spare you that I did not come back to Corinth.
Not that we rule over your faith, but we are fellow workers with you for your joy, because you stand firm by faith.
For I decided on my own not to come to you again in sorrow.
For if I make you sad, who can make me glad except the one I made sad?
I wrote what I did so that when I came, I would not have sorrow from the people who should make me happy. I trust all of you, because I know my joy is your joy.
I wrote to you with many tears, out of great trouble and a heavy heart. I did not write to make you sad, but to show you how much love I have for you.
If anyone has caused sorrow, he has not caused it to me alone, but in part to all of you. I say this so I will not be too hard on him.
The punishment this man received from the majority is enough.
So now you should forgive and comfort him, so he will not be swallowed up by too much sorrow.
So I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
I also wrote for this reason: to test you, to see if you obey everything.
Anyone you forgive, I also forgive. And if I have forgiven anything, I did it for your sake in the presence of Christ.
We do this so Satan will not outsmart us, because we know his evil plans.
When I came to Troas to preach the good news about Christ, the Lord opened a door for me.
But I had no peace in my spirit because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ and, through us, spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him.
For we are to God the pleasing aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and among those who are dying.
To some, we are a smell that leads from death to death; to others, a smell that leads from life to life. Who is able to do this work?
For we are not like many who sell God's word for profit. Instead, in Christ we speak with sincerity, as from God, in the sight of God.
Are we starting to praise ourselves again? Or do we need letters that recommend us to you, or from you, like some people do?
You are our letter, written on our hearts. Everyone knows it and reads it.
You show that you are a letter from Christ, which we delivered. It is not written with ink but with the Spirit of the living God. It is not written on stone tablets but on human hearts.
We have this kind of confidence toward God through Christ.
Not that we can take credit for anything on our own. Our ability comes from God.
He has made us able to be servants of a new covenant. It is not based on the written code but on the Spirit. The written code kills, but the Spirit gives life.
The old way, which brought death, was written in letters on stone. It came with glory, so the people of Israel could not look steadily at Moses' face. That glory was fading.
Then won't the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?
If the ministry that brought condemnation had glory, how much more does the ministry that brings righteousness overflow with glory!
In fact, what once had glory now has no glory at all, because the glory that surpasses it is so great.
And if what was fading away came with glory, how much more glorious is what lasts!
Since we have such a hope, we speak with great boldness.
We are not like Moses, who put a veil over his face so the Israelites would not see the glory fading away.
But their minds were made dull. To this day the same veil remains when the old covenant is read. It has not been removed, because only in Christ is it taken away.
Yes, even today, when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.
But whenever anyone turns to the LORD, the veil is taken away.
Now the LORD is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the LORD is, there is freedom.
And we all, with unveiled faces, are looking at the glory of the LORD as in a mirror. We are being changed into His image with ever greater glory. This comes from the LORD, who is the Spirit.
Since God has been merciful and given us this ministry, we do not give up.

Instead, we have turned away from secret and shameful ways. We do not use tricks, and we do not twist God's word. By speaking the truth openly, we show that we are honest before every person's conscience and before God.
Even if our gospel is hidden, it is hidden from people who are being lost.
The god of this age has blinded the minds of people who do not believe. They cannot see the light of the gospel that shows Christ's glory. Christ is the image of God.
We do not preach about ourselves. We preach Jesus Christ as Lord, and we are your servants for Jesus' sake.
For God, who said, "Let light shine out of darkness," has made His light shine in our hearts. He gives us the light of knowing God's glory, and we see that glory in the face of Jesus Christ.
But we have this treasure in jars of clay. This shows that the great power is from God, not from us.
We are pressed hard on every side, but not crushed. We are confused, but not hopeless.
We are persecuted, but not abandoned. We are struck down, but not destroyed.
We always carry Jesus' death in our bodies, so that Jesus' life may also be shown in our bodies.
We who are alive are always being handed over to death for Jesus' sake, so that His life may be shown in our dying bodies.
So death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
It is written, "I believed; therefore I spoke." We have that same spirit of faith, so we also believe and speak.
We know that God, who raised the Lord Jesus, will also raise us with Jesus. He will bring us and you into His presence.
All this is for your benefit. As God's grace reaches more and more people, thanksgiving will overflow to God's glory.
So we do not give up. Even if our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being made new day by day.
Our troubles are light and last only a moment. But they are producing for us an eternal glory that is far greater than they are.
We do not focus on what can be seen, but on what cannot be seen. What is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.
For we know that if the tent we live in on earth is destroyed, we have a building from God. It is an eternal house in heaven, not made by human hands.
In this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling.
If we are clothed with it, we will not be found naked.
While we are in this tent, we groan and feel weighed down. We do not want to be unclothed, but clothed, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
God made us for this very purpose, and He gave us the Spirit as a guarantee.
So we are always confident. We know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.
For we walk by faith, not by sight.
We are confident, and we would rather be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
So we make it our goal to please Him, whether we are at home or away.
For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each of us may receive what is due for what we did in the body, whether good or bad.
Since we know the fear of the Lord, we persuade people. But we are well known to God, and I hope we are also well known in your consciences.

We are not trying to praise ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you a reason to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who boast about outward things and not about what is in the heart.
If we are out of our minds, it is for God; if we are in our right minds, it is for you.
For the love of Christ controls us, because we have decided this: One died for all, so all died.
He died for all so that those who live would no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised.
So from now on we do not view anyone from a human point of view. Even though we once knew Christ from a human point of view, we do not know Him that way anymore.
So if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away; look, new things have come.
All this comes from God. He reconciled us to Himself through Christ, and He gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
In Christ, God was reconciling the world to Himself. He did not count people’s sins against them, and He has given us the message of reconciliation.
So we are Christ’s ambassadors, as though God were making His appeal through us. We beg you on Christ’s behalf: “Be reconciled to God.”
For our sake, God made Him who knew no sin to be sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
As God's coworkers, we urge you not to let God's grace go to waste.
For He says, “In a time of favor I heard you, and on the day of salvation I helped you. Look, now is the time of favor; look, now is the day of salvation.”
We try not to put any obstacle in anyone's way, so our work for God will not be blamed.
But as servants of God, we prove ourselves in every way: in great patience, in troubles, in hardships, and in distress.
We have faced beatings, prisons, riots, hard work, sleepless nights, and hunger.
We have lived in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness, with the help of the Holy Spirit and sincere love.
We speak the truth and rely on God's power, using the weapons of righteousness in our right and left hands.
We have been honored and shamed, praised and criticized; people call us deceivers, but we speak the truth.
We are treated as unknown, yet we are well known; as dying, and yet we live; as punished, but not killed.
We are sad, yet always glad; poor, yet we make many rich; having nothing, yet we have everything.
We have spoken openly to you, Corinthians; our hearts are wide open.
You are not held back by us; you are held back by your own hearts.
In return, I speak to you as to my children. Open your hearts wide too.
Do not team up with unbelievers. What do righteousness and lawlessness share? Or what does light have in common with darkness?
What agreement can Christ have with Belial? Or what does a believer share with an unbeliever?

What does God's temple have in common with idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God said, “I will live with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.”
Therefore, “Come out from among them and be separate,” says the Lord. “Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”
“And I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters,” says the Lord Almighty.
Therefore, dear friends, since we have these promises, let us make ourselves clean from everything that makes the body or spirit dirty. Let us keep growing in holiness, with a healthy fear of God.
Make room for us in your hearts. We have not wronged anyone. We have not ruined anyone. We have not taken advantage of anyone.
I am not saying this to judge you. I have already said that you are in our hearts. We are ready to live or die with you.
I speak very openly to you. I am very proud of you. I am full of comfort. Even in all our trouble, I overflow with joy.
When we came to Macedonia, our bodies had no rest at all. We were troubled in every way. There were fights outside and fears inside.
But God, who comforts discouraged people, comforted us when Titus came.
He comforted us not only by coming, but also by the comfort you gave him. He told us about your strong desire to see me, your sorrow, and your strong support for me. That made me even happier.
Even if my letter made you sad, I do not regret it. I did feel bad for a moment, but I see that the letter made you sad only for a short time.
Now I am glad. I am not glad that you were sad, but I am glad that your sadness led you to repent. You were sad in the way God wants, so we did not harm you at all.
Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation, and no one regrets it. But worldly sorrow brings death.

Look at what this godly sorrow has done for you. It made you eager to do right. It gave you a defense. It made you angry at the wrong. It made you afraid. It made you long for what is right. It made you care deeply. It made you want justice. In every way you have shown that you are pure in this matter.
So when I wrote to you, it was not only because of the person who did wrong or the person who was wronged. I wrote so that your strong care for us would be clear to you before God.
Because of this, we have been comforted. We were even happier when we saw Titus's joy, because all of you refreshed his spirit.
I had told Titus good things about you, and I was not embarrassed. Just as everything we said to you was true, what we told Titus about you proved true too.
His love for you has grown even more because he remembers how all of you obeyed. You welcomed him with fear and trembling.
I am happy because I can trust you in everything.
Now, brothers, we want you to know about the grace God has given to the churches in Macedonia.
In the middle of a very hard test, their overflowing joy and their extreme poverty produced rich generosity.
I can say they gave as much as they could, and even more than they could.
They begged us again and again for the chance to share in this service to God's people.
They did more than we expected. They gave themselves first to the Lord, and then to us, because that was God's will.
So we urged Titus to finish this act of grace among you, just as he had started it.
You already do well in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in full dedication, and in the love we stirred up in you. So make sure you also do well in this grace of giving.
I am not giving an order. I want to test how real your love is by comparing it with the dedication of others.
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ. He was rich, but for your sake He became poor, so that through His poverty you might become rich.
Here is my advice. It is best for you to finish this. You were the first to start giving last year, and you were the first to want to do it.
Now finish the work, so your eager willingness may be matched by your finishing it, using what you have.
If the willingness is there, the gift is accepted based on what a person has, not on what they do not have.
I do not want others to be relieved while you are hard pressed. I want things to be fair.
Right now your plenty can supply what they need, so that later their plenty can supply what you need. The goal is fairness.
As it is written, "The one who gathered much did not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have too little."
Thanks be to God, who put the same dedicated care for you into Titus's heart.
He accepted our request, and because he was already eager, he went to you on his own.
We are sending with him the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in spreading the Good News.
And that is not all. He was also chosen by the churches to travel with us as we carry this gift, which we are handling for the glory of the Lord and to show our eagerness.
We are taking care with this so that no one can blame us for how we handle this generous gift.
We want to do what is right, not only before the Lord but also before people.
We are sending with them our brother, whom we have often found to be eager in many things, and who is now even more eager because of his confidence in you.
As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you. As for our brothers, they are representatives of the churches and an honor to Christ.
So show them, in front of the churches, proof of your love and of the pride we have in you.
It is not necessary for me to write to you about the help being sent to God's people.
I know how eager you are. I boast about you to the people of Macedonia. I tell them that you in Achaia have been ready since last year. Your excitement has stirred many of them to act.
But I sent the brothers ahead so our boasting about you in this matter would not be empty. I want you to be ready, just as I said you would be.
If some Macedonians come with me and find you not ready, we would be ashamed of our confidence in you.
So I thought it was necessary to ask the brothers to visit you first and get your promised gift ready. Then it will be a real gift given freely, not something taken by pressure.
Remember this: Whoever plants only a little will gather only a little. But whoever plants generously will gather generously.
Each person should give what he has decided in his heart to give. He should not give with sadness or because he feels forced, because God loves a cheerful giver.
God is able to give you more than enough grace. Then you will always have what you need and be able to do every good work.
As it is written, “He scattered His gifts to the poor. His goodness lasts forever.”
God, who gives seed to the farmer and bread for food, will give you seed and make it grow. He will increase the harvest that comes from your right living.
You will be made rich in every way so you can be generous. Your generosity will lead many people, through us, to thank God.
This service does more than provide for the needs of God's people. It also causes many people to thank God.
Because you have proved your faith by this service, people will praise God. They will see that you obey the good news of Christ and share generously with them and with everyone.
They will pray for you. They will long to see you because of the great grace God has given you.
Thanks be to God for His gift that is too wonderful for words!
Now I, Paul, appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ. I am humble when I am face to face with you, but I am bold toward you when I am away.
I beg you that when I come, I will not have to be as bold as I expect to be toward some people. They think we live by human standards.
We do live in the body, but we do not fight our battles the way the world does.
The weapons we fight with are not human weapons. They are powerful through God to tear down strongholds.
We tear down arguments and every proud idea that rises against the knowledge of God. We take every thought captive and make it obey Christ.
We are ready to punish every act of disobedience, but only after your obedience is complete.
You look at the outside of things. If anyone is sure he belongs to Christ, he should think again. We belong to Christ just as much as he does.
Even if I boast a little too much about the authority the Lord gave us to build you up, not tear you down, I will not be ashamed.
I do not want to seem like I am trying to scare you with my letters.
Some say, "His letters are heavy and strong, but when he is here in person he is weak, and his speaking is not impressive."
Anyone who says that should remember this: What we say in our letters when we are away, we will also do when we are there with you.

We do not dare to put ourselves in the same class as some people who praise themselves. They measure themselves by their own standards and compare themselves with themselves, and that shows no wisdom.
We will not boast about things beyond our limits. We will stay within the area God has given us, and that area includes you.
We are not going too far, as if we had not reached you. We were the first to bring the good news of Christ to you.
We do not boast about work done by others. Instead, we hope that as your faith grows, our work among you will grow even more.
Then we can preach the good news in places beyond you. We do not want to boast about work already done in someone else's area.
"Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord."
It is not the person who praises himself who is approved. It is the person the Lord praises.
I hope you will put up with a little foolishness from me. Yes, please put up with me!
I am jealous for you with a jealousy that comes from God. I promised you to one husband, Christ, so I could present you to Him as a pure virgin.
But I am afraid that, just as Eve was tricked by the snake's cleverness, your minds may be led away from your sincere and pure devotion to Christ.

If someone comes to you and preaches a different Jesus than we preached, or you receive a different spirit than the one you received, or a different good news than the one you accepted, you put up with it easily enough.
I do not think I am any less than those "super-apostles."
I may not be a skilled speaker, but I do have knowledge. We have shown this to you in every way.
Was it a sin for me to lower myself so you could be lifted up, because I preached God's good news to you for free?
I took support from other churches so I could serve you.

When I was with you and needed something, I was not a burden to anyone, because the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied what I needed. I have kept myself from being a burden to you in any way, and I will keep doing so.
As surely as Christ's truth is in me, no one in Achaia will stop me from boasting about this.
Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
I will keep doing what I am doing so I can cut off the chance for those who want to be seen as equal to us in what they boast about.
Those men are false apostles. They are deceitful workers who disguise themselves as apostles of Christ.
And no wonder, for Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
It is not surprising, then, if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will be what their actions deserve.
I say again: No one should think I am a fool. But if you do, then accept me as a fool so I can boast a little.
When I talk with this confident boasting, I am not speaking the way the Lord would. I am speaking like a fool.
Since many boast about worldly things, I will boast too.
You gladly put up with fools since you are so wise!
In fact, you even put up with anyone who enslaves you or takes advantage of you or acts superior or slaps you in the face.
I say this to my shame: We were too weak to do that! But if someone else dares to boast about something—I am speaking like a fool—I dare to boast about it too.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they Abraham's descendants? So am I.
Are they servants of Christ? I am out of my mind to talk like this, but I am more. I have worked much harder, been in prison more often, been beaten more severely, and faced death many times.
Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was pelted with stones, three times I was shipwrecked, and I spent a night and a day in the open sea.

I have been constantly on the move. I have been in danger from rivers, in danger from bandits, in danger from my fellow Jews, in danger from Gentiles; in danger in the city, in danger in the country, in danger at sea; and in danger from false believers.
I have labored and toiled and have often gone without sleep; I have known hunger and thirst and have often gone without food; I have been cold and naked.
Besides all this, every day I feel the pressure of caring for all the churches.
Who is weak without me feeling weak? Who is led to sin without me burning inside?
If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is praised forever, knows that I am not lying.
In Damascus the governor under King Aretas had the city of the Damascenes guarded in order to arrest me.
But I was lowered in a basket from a window in the wall and escaped from him.
I must go on boasting, even though it does no good. I will move on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
I know a man in Christ who was caught up to the third heaven fourteen years ago. I do not know whether it happened in the body or out of the body. God knows.
I know that this man—whether in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows—
was caught up to Paradise and heard words that cannot be spoken, words a person is not allowed to tell.
I will boast about a man like that, but I will not boast about myself, except in my weaknesses.
Even if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be telling the truth. But I hold back, so no one will think more of me than what he sees in me or hears from me.
To keep me from becoming proud because of these great revelations, I was given a thorn in my flesh. It is a messenger from Satan to torment me, to keep me from becoming proud.
Three times I begged the Lord to take it away from me.
But He said to me, "My grace is enough for you, because My power is made perfect in weakness." So I will boast even more gladly in my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may rest on me.
That is why, for Christ's sake, I am glad to have weaknesses, insults, hard times, persecutions, and troubles. When I am weak, then I am strong.
I have become a fool, but you drove me to it. You should have praised me, because I am not in any way less than the "super-apostles," even though I am nothing.
The signs of an apostle—signs, wonders, and miracles—were done among you with great patience.
What did you have that was less than the other churches, except that I did not burden you? Forgive me for this wrong!

Look, I am ready to come to you a third time, and I will not be a burden. I am not looking for your money but for you. Children should not have to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.
I will gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more, am I to be loved less?
Even so, I did not burden you. Yet, crafty as I am, I caught you by trickery.
Did I take advantage of you through any of the men I sent to you?
I urged Titus to go and sent our brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow the same path?
Have you been thinking all along that we have been defending ourselves before you? We speak before God in Christ, and everything we do, dear friends, is to build you up.

I am afraid that when I come, I may not find you as I want, and you may not find me as you want. I fear there may be quarreling, jealousy, anger, selfish ambition, slander, gossip, pride, and disorder.
I am afraid that when I come again, My God will humble me before you, and I will be sad about many who sinned before and have not turned from their impurity, sexual sin, and wild living.
This is the third time I am coming to you. Every charge must be proved by the words of two or three witnesses.
I already warned you the second time when I was with you, and now, while I am away, I warn those who sinned before and all the rest: If I come again, I will not spare you.
Since you are looking for proof that Christ is speaking in me, He is not weak toward you, but He is powerful among you.
He was crucified in weakness, but He lives by God's power. We too are weak in Him, but we will live with Him by God's power for you.
Test yourselves to see if you are in the faith. Check yourselves. Do you not know that Jesus Christ is in you, unless you fail the test?
I hope you will know that we are not failing.
I pray to God that you do no evil. I do not pray this so we may look approved, but so you may do what is good, even if we seem disapproved.
We cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
We are glad when we are weak and you are strong. This is what we pray: that you may be made complete.
That is why I write these things while I am away, so that when I am with you, I will not have to use sharp words, using the authority the Lord gave me to build you up, not tear you down.
Finally, brothers and sisters, rejoice. Aim to be restored. Be comforted. Agree with one another. Live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss.
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the sharing of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.
Paul, an apostle—not from people or through a person, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead—
and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches in Galatia:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
who gave Himself for our sins to save us from this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
to Him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
I'm amazed that you are turning away so quickly from the One who called you by the grace of Christ and are following a different gospel.
It is not that there is another gospel, but some people are troubling you and want to twist the gospel of Christ.
But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you a gospel different from the one we preached to you, let that person be cursed.
As we said before, I now say again: If anyone preaches to you a gospel different from the one you received, let that person be cursed.
Am I now trying to win the approval of people or of God? Am I trying to please people? If I were still trying to please people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
For I want you to know, brothers, that the gospel I preached is not a human message.
I did not receive it from a person, and I was not taught it. I received it through a revelation from Jesus Christ.
For you have heard about my former life in Judaism—how I persecuted the church of God terribly and tried to destroy it.
I was moving ahead in Judaism faster than many others my age among my people, and I was extremely devoted to the traditions of my ancestors.
But when God, who set me apart before I was born and called me by His grace, was pleased
to reveal His Son in me so that I might preach Him among the nations, I did not immediately ask advice from any person.
I did not go up to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before me. Instead, I went to Arabia, and later I returned to Damascus.
Then, after three years, I went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas, and I stayed with him for fifteen days.
I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord's brother.
Before God, I'm not lying in what I'm writing to you.
Then I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
The churches in Judea that belong to Christ did not know me in person.
They had only heard that the man who once persecuted us was now preaching the faith he had tried to destroy.
And they praised God because of me.
Fourteen years later, I went up to Jerusalem again. Barnabas went with me, and I took Titus along.
I went because God told me to. I told the leaders there the good news I preach to the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to the ones who seemed important, so my work would not be wasted.
Even Titus, who was with me, was not forced to be circumcised, even though he is a Greek.
This happened because some false brothers sneaked in. They came in secretly to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus and to make us slaves.
We did not give in to them for even a moment, so the truth of the good news would stay with you.
The leaders who seemed important did not add anything to my message. It does not matter to me what they once were, because God does not show favoritism.
Instead, they saw that God had trusted me with the good news for the Gentiles, just as He had trusted Peter with the good news for the Jews.
The same God who worked through Peter as an apostle to the Jews also worked through me for the Gentiles.
James, Peter, and John seemed to be pillars. They understood the grace God had given me. They shook hands with Barnabas and me as partners. We would go to the Gentiles, and they would go to the Jews.
They only asked us to remember the poor, and that was something I was already eager to do.
But when Peter came to Antioch, I stood up to him face to face, because he was clearly wrong.
Before some men came from James, Peter ate with the Gentiles. But when they came, he pulled back and separated himself because he was afraid of the Jewish Christians.
The other Jews joined him in this hypocrisy, and even Barnabas was led astray.

When I saw that they were not acting in line with the truth of the good news, I said to Peter in front of everyone, "If you are a Jew but live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you force Gentiles to live like Jews?"
We are Jews by birth, not Gentile sinners.

But we know that a person is not made right with God by obeying the law. A person is made right through faith in Jesus Christ. So we have put our faith in Christ Jesus, so we may be made right by faith in Christ and not by obeying the law. No one will be made right by obeying the law.
But if we are trying to be made right in Christ and we are still found to be sinners, does that make Christ a servant of sin? Of course not!
If I build again what I tore down, I show that I am a lawbreaker.
Through the law I died to the law, so I could live for God.
I have been crucified with Christ. I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in my body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me.
I do not reject God's grace. If being right with God came through the law, then Christ died for nothing.
You foolish Galatians! Who has put a spell on you? Jesus Christ was shown to you as crucified, right before your eyes.
I want to know just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by doing what the law says, or by hearing and believing?
Are you so foolish? You started with the Spirit. Are you now trying to finish by your own human effort?
Have you suffered so much for nothing? I hope it was not all for nothing.
Does the One who gives you the Spirit and works miracles among you do this because you follow the law, or because you heard and believed?
Abraham believed God, and God counted that as righteousness.
So you should know that people who have faith are Abraham's children.
The Scripture saw ahead that God would make the Gentiles right with Him through faith. So it gave Abraham the good news ahead of time: "All nations will be blessed through you."
So people who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the faithful man.
All who depend on obeying the law are under a curse. Scripture says, "Cursed is everyone who does not keep doing everything written in the Book of the Law."
It is clear that no one is made right with God by the law, because "The righteous will live by faith."
The law does not rest on faith. Instead, "The person who does these things will live by them."
Christ bought us back from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. Scripture says, "Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree."
He did this so that the blessing Abraham received would come to the Gentiles through Christ Jesus, and so that we could receive the promised Spirit by faith.
Brothers, I am using a human example. Even a person's agreement, once it is approved, cannot be canceled or added to by anyone.
The promises were given to Abraham and to his descendant. Scripture does not say "and to descendants," as if many. It says "and to your descendant," meaning one person, and that person is Christ.
Here is what I mean. The law came 430 years later. It does not cancel the agreement God had already approved, and it does not make the promise useless.
If the inheritance comes from the law, then it does not come from a promise. But God gave it to Abraham through a promise.
So why was the law given? It was added because of people's sins, until the descendant came to whom the promise was made. The law was given through angels and put into effect by a go-between.
A go-between means there are at least two sides. But God is one.
So is the law against God's promises? Not at all! If a law had been given that could give life, then people would be made right with God by following the law.
But Scripture has locked up everything under sin. It did this so that the promise, which comes through faith in Jesus Christ, could be given to those who believe.
Before faith came, we were kept under guard by the law. We were locked up until faith was revealed.
So the law was like a guardian for us until Christ came. Its purpose was to lead us to be made right with God by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under that guardian.
For through faith, you are all children of God in Christ Jesus.
For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
There is no Jew or Greek, no slave or free person, no male or female. You are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's descendants and heirs according to the promise.
I mean that as long as an heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, even though he owns everything.
He is under guardians and managers until the time his father has set.
In the same way, when we were children, we were slaves to the basic principles of the world.
But when the right time had come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
to buy freedom for those under the law, so that we could be adopted as His sons.
Because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying, "Abba! Father!"
So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and if you are a son, then you are an heir through God.
At one time, when you did not know God, you were slaves to things that are not really gods.
But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how can you turn back again to the weak and worthless basic principles? Do you want to be their slaves all over again?
You are observing special days, months, seasons, and years!
I am afraid for you, that my work among you may have been wasted.
Brothers, I beg you to become like me, for I became like you. You did me no wrong.
You know it was because of an illness that I first preached the good news to you.
Even though my illness tested you, you did not look down on me or reject me. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God, as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.
What happened to your joy? I can tell you that, if it were possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?
Those people are eager to win you over, but not for a good reason. They want to cut you off from us so that you will be eager for them.
It is always good to be eager for a good purpose, and not only when I am with you.
My children, I am in the pains of childbirth for you again until Christ is formed in you.
I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I am confused about you.
Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not understand what the law says?
For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by a slave woman and one by a free woman.
The son of the slave woman was born in the ordinary way, but the son of the free woman was born because of God's promise.
This can be understood as a picture: these two women stand for two covenants. One covenant comes from Mount Sinai and gives birth to children who are slaves. That woman is Hagar.
Now Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia, and she matches the present Jerusalem, because she is in slavery with her children.
But the Jerusalem in heaven is free, and she is our mother.
For it is written, "Rejoice, you who have no children! Shout for joy, you who have never given birth! For the woman left alone will have more children than the woman with a husband."
Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of the promise.
But just as the one born in the ordinary way persecuted the one born through the Spirit, so it is now.
But what does the Scripture say? "Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman will not share the inheritance with the son of the free woman."
So, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman but of the free woman.
Christ set us free so we could be free. So stand firm, and don't let yourselves be tied up again under a heavy load of slavery.
Look, I, Paul, tell you that if you get circumcised, Christ won't help you at all.
I warn every man who gets circumcised that he must obey the whole law.
You who try to be made right with God by the law have cut yourselves off from Christ. You have fallen away from God's grace.
But through the Spirit, by faith, we eagerly wait for the hope of being made right with God.
In Christ Jesus, being circumcised or not being circumcised means nothing. What matters is faith that shows itself through love.
You were doing well. Who stopped you from following the truth?
That kind of persuasion doesn't come from Him who calls you.
A little yeast spreads through the whole batch of dough.
I trust the Lord that you won't think differently. The one who is troubling you will face judgment, whoever he is.
Brothers, if I were still preaching circumcision, why would people still persecute me? Then the cross wouldn't be a stumbling block anymore.
I wish those troublemakers would cut themselves off completely.
You were called to freedom, brothers. Just don't use your freedom as an excuse to follow your sinful nature. Instead, serve each other with love.
The whole law is summed up in one command: "You must love your neighbor as yourself."
But if you bite and tear each other apart, watch out, or you will destroy each other.
So I say, live by the Spirit, and you won't give in to sinful desires.
The sinful nature wants what goes against the Spirit, and the Spirit wants what goes against the sinful nature. They fight each other, so you don't do the things you want to do.
But if the Spirit leads you, you are not under the law.
The sinful nature shows itself in obvious ways, such as sexual sin, impurity, and reckless living.
It also shows up as worshiping false gods, sorcery, hatred, quarrels, jealousy, angry outbursts, selfish ambition, divisions, factions,
envy, drunkenness, wild parties, and other things like these. I warn you now, just as I warned you before, that people who live like this won't inherit God's kingdom.
But the Spirit produces love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness, and self-control. There is no law against these things.
Those who belong to Christ Jesus have nailed their sinful nature to the cross, along with its passions and desires.
Since we live by the Spirit, let's also follow the Spirit's lead.
Let's not become proud, stirring up trouble with each other or being jealous of each other.
