Brothers, if someone is caught in a sin, you who are spiritual should restore that person gently. Watch yourself, so you won't be tempted too.
Carry each other's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he fools himself.
Each person should test his own work. Then he can be proud of himself alone, not by comparing himself to someone else.
For each person will carry his own load.
The person who is taught the word should share all good things with the one who teaches.
Don't be fooled: God cannot be mocked. A person reaps what he sows.
The one who sows to please his own sinful nature will reap ruin from that nature. But the one who sows to please the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
Let us not get tired of doing good, for at the right time we will reap a harvest if we don't give up.
So then, while we have the chance, let us do good to everyone, especially to those in the family of faith.
See what large letters I use to write to you with my own hand.
Those who want to look good in the flesh try to force you to be circumcised. They do this only so they won't be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
Even those who are circumcised don't keep the law. They want you circumcised so they can brag about your body.
But I will never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. Through that cross, the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything. What matters is a new creation.
Peace and mercy to all who follow this rule, and to the Israel of God.
From now on, let no one trouble me, for I carry in my body the marks of Jesus.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, writes to God's holy people in Ephesus who are faithful in Christ Jesus.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! He has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places.
He chose us in Him before the world was made, so that we would be holy and blameless before Him in love.
He planned ahead of time to adopt us as His children through Jesus Christ. This was His good and happy will.
So we praise the glory of His grace, which He freely gave us in His dearly loved Son.
In Him we have freedom through His blood. He forgave our sins because His grace is so rich.
He poured out that grace on us with all wisdom and understanding.
He made known to us the secret of His will. It matched His good plan, which He set in Christ.
This plan will bring everything together in Christ when the time is right. That includes things in heaven and things on earth.
In Christ we were chosen. God planned this ahead of time. He works everything out by His own will and plan.
We were the first to hope in Christ, so we would bring praise to His glory.
You also heard the true message, the good news of your salvation. When you believed, you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.
The Spirit is a down payment on our inheritance. He guarantees it until God fully redeems His people. This brings praise to His glory.
I have heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all God's holy people.
So I never stop thanking God for you. I keep you in my prayers.
I pray that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, will give you a spirit of wisdom and understanding. Then you will know Him better.
I pray that the eyes of your hearts will be opened. Then you will know the hope He has called you to. You will know the riches of His glorious inheritance among His holy people.
You will also know His great power for us who believe. It works by His mighty strength.
He used that power in Christ when He raised Him from the dead. He seated Him at His right hand in heaven.
Christ is far above every ruler, authority, power, and leader. He is above every name that is named, now and in the future.
God put everything under His feet. He made Christ head over everything for the church.
The church is His body. It is filled by Him who fills everything in every way.
You were dead in your sins and wrong choices.
You used to live that way, following the ways of this world and the ruler of the evil spirits in the air, the spirit that is now working in people who refuse to obey.
We all lived like that too at one time. We followed our selfish desires and did what our bodies and minds wanted. Like everyone else, we were under God's anger by nature.
But God is rich in mercy. Because He loved us so much,
He made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our sins. You are saved by grace.
God raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus.
He did this so that in the coming ages He might show the amazing riches of His grace through His kindness to us in Christ Jesus.
You are saved by grace through faith. This is not from your own doing; it is God's gift.
It is not from works, so no one can brag.
For we are God's work, created in Christ Jesus for good works. God prepared these works ahead of time so that we would walk in them.
So remember that you Gentiles by birth were called "uncircumcised" by those called "circumcised" in the flesh by human hands.
At that time you were without Christ. You were cut off from Israel's community, strangers to God's promises, with no hope and without God in the world.
But now in Christ Jesus, you who were far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
For He Himself is our peace. He made the two groups one. He broke down the dividing wall of hostility in His flesh.
He set aside the law with its commands and rules in order to create in Himself one new people out of the two, making peace.
He reconciled both to God in one body through the cross, killing the hostility there.
He came and preached peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near.
For through Him we both have access to the Father by one Spirit.
So you are no longer strangers and aliens. You are fellow citizens with the saints and members of God's household.
You are built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus Himself as the cornerstone.
In Him the whole building is joined together and grows into a holy temple in the Lord.
In Him you too are being built together into a dwelling place for God by the Spirit.
Because of this, I, Paul, am a prisoner of Christ Jesus for you Gentiles.
Surely you have heard about the work God gave me to share His grace with you.
God showed me His secret plan by revealing it to me, just as I wrote briefly before.
When you read this, you can understand the insight I have into Christ's secret plan.
In past times, this was not made known to people the way it is now. God has revealed it through the Spirit to His holy apostles and prophets.
The secret plan is this: through the good news, the Gentiles share in God's inheritance, belong to the same body, and share in the promise in Christ Jesus.
I became a servant of this good news by the gift of God's grace, given to me by the working of His power.
I am the least of all God's holy people, yet this grace was given to me to preach to the Gentiles the riches of Christ, which are too great to measure.
I was also sent to make clear to everyone how this secret plan works. It was hidden in God, who made everything, for ages past.
Now God's many-sided wisdom is made known through the church to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly places.
This was God's eternal purpose, which He carried out in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Through Him and through faith in Him, we can come to God freely and with confidence.
So I ask you not to lose heart because of my troubles for you. They are your glory.
For this reason I bow my knees before the Father,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth gets its name.
I pray that, out of the riches of His glory, He will give you strength through His Spirit in your inner self.
I pray that Christ will live in your hearts through faith, and that you will be rooted and grounded in love.
Then you will be able, with all God's holy people, to understand how wide, long, high, and deep Christ's love is.
You can know this love that goes beyond knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to Him who is able to do far more than all we ask or think, by the power working in us,
be glory in the church and in Christ Jesus for all generations, forever and ever. Amen.
I am a prisoner because I serve the Lord, and I beg you to live in a way that matches the call you have received.
Be completely humble and gentle. Be patient, and put up with each other in love.
Work hard to keep the unity that the Spirit gives, joined together by peace.
There is one body and one Spirit. You were also called to one hope when you were called.
There is one Lord, one faith, and one baptism.
There is one God and Father of all. He is over everything, through everything, and in everything.
But each of us received grace as Christ gave it, measured out by His gift.
That is why Scripture says, "When He went up to heaven, He led captives with Him and gave gifts to people."
What does "He went up" mean? It means He also came down to the lower parts of the earth.
The One who came down is the same One who went up above all the heavens, so He could fill everything.
Christ gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers.
He did this to prepare God's people for service and to build up the body of Christ.
We will keep growing until we all reach unity in the faith and in knowing the Son of God. Then we will be mature, fully grown like Christ.
Then we won't be like little children anymore, tossed around by waves and blown by every new teaching. We won't be tricked by clever people who make evil plans.
Instead, by speaking the truth in love, we will grow in every way into Christ, who is the head.
From Him the whole body is joined and held together. Every part does its work, and the body grows and builds itself up in love.
So I say this, and I say it strongly in the Lord: You must no longer live like the people who don't know God. They live in empty thinking.
Their minds are dark, and they are cut off from the life God gives because they don't know Him. Their hearts are hard.
They have lost all feeling and have given themselves over to wild living. They are greedy to do every kind of impure thing.
But that is not how you learned about Christ.
If you truly heard Him and were taught in Him, then the truth is in Jesus.
You were taught to take off your old self, which is ruined by lying desires.
Let your mind be made new.
Put on the new self, created to be like God in true right living and holiness.
So each of you must stop lying and speak truth to your neighbor, because we are parts of one another.
"Be angry, but do not sin." Do not let the sun go down while you are still angry.
Do not give the devil a chance.
The one who steals must stop stealing. Instead, he should work hard with his hands to do good, so he can share with people in need.
Do not let any bad words come out of your mouths. Speak only what is good and helpful, so your words can help those who hear.
Do not make God's Holy Spirit sad. You were sealed by Him for the day when you will be set free.
Get rid of all bitterness, anger, yelling, and hurtful talk, along with every kind of evil.
Be kind and tender to each other. Forgive each other, just as God forgave you through Christ.
Therefore, be imitators of God, as dearly loved children.
Live in love, just as Christ loved us and gave Himself up for us as a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.
But sexual immorality and every kind of impurity or greed must not even be named among you, as is proper for God's holy people.
There should be no obscenity, foolish talk, or coarse joking, which are not fitting. Instead, there should be thanksgiving.
For you can be sure of this: no one who is sexually immoral, impure, or greedy—that is, an idolater—has any share in the kingdom of Christ and God.
Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things God's wrath is coming on those who disobey.
For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Live as children of light.
The light produces goodness, righteousness, and truth.
Test and approve what pleases the Lord.
Have nothing to do with the fruitless deeds of darkness. Instead, expose them.
It is shameful even to talk about what disobedient people do in secret.
But everything exposed by the light becomes visible, because anything shown by the light becomes light.
That is why it says, "Wake up, sleeper, rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you."
So be very careful how you live. Do not live like foolish people but like wise people, making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil.
Therefore, do not be foolish, but understand what the Lord wants.
Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to wild living. Instead, be filled with the Spirit.
Speak to one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Sing and make music in your heart to the Lord.
Always give thanks to God the Father for everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ.
Wives, submit to your own husbands as to the Lord,
because the husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the church and the Savior of the body.
But as the church submits to Christ, so wives should submit to their husbands in everything.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave Himself up for her,
to make her holy. He cleansed her by washing her with water through the word,
so that He could present her to Himself as a glorious church without stain or wrinkle or anything like that, but holy and blameless.
In the same way, husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. A man who loves his wife loves himself.
After all, no one ever hated his own body, but he feeds and cares for it, just as Christ does for the church,
because we are members of His body.
"For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh."
This is a great mystery, but I am talking about Christ and the church.
Still, each one of you must love his wife as he loves himself, and the wife must respect her husband.
Children, obey your parents in the Lord, because this is right.
“Honor your father and mother”—this is the first commandment with a promise—
“so that it may go well with you and you may live a long time on the earth.”
Fathers, do not make your children angry, but bring them up with the Lord’s training and teaching.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters with respect and fear, and with an honest heart, just as you would obey Christ.
Do not work only to please them when they are watching. Instead, work as slaves of Christ, doing what God wants from the heart.
Serve with a good attitude, as if you were serving the Lord and not people.
You know that the Lord will reward each person for whatever good they do, whether they are a slave or free.
And masters, treat your slaves the same way. Do not threaten them, because you know that their Master and yours is in heaven, and He does not show favoritism.
Finally, be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power.
Put on the full armor of God so that you can stand against the devil’s tricks.
For our fight is not against people made of flesh and blood, but against rulers, authorities, and powers of this dark world, and against evil spiritual forces in the heavenly places.
So take up the full armor of God. Then, when the day of evil comes, you will be able to stand your ground. After you have done everything, you will still be standing.
Stand firm, then. Buckle the belt of truth around your waist, and put on the breastplate of righteousness.
Put on shoes that make you ready to share the good news of peace.
In every situation, take up the shield of faith. With it you can put out all the flaming arrows of the evil one.
Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
Pray in the Spirit at all times. Use every kind of prayer and request. Stay awake and keep praying with all your strength for all of God’s people.
Pray for me too, so that whenever I speak, I may be given the right words. Then I can boldly tell the secret of the good news.
I am in chains because of this message. Pray that I may speak about it boldly, as I should.
Tychicus, our dear brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will tell you everything. That way you will know how I am and what I am doing.
I am sending him to you for this reason, so that you will know how we are and so that he can encourage your hearts.
Peace to the brothers and sisters, and love with faith from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace to everyone who loves our Lord Jesus Christ with a love that never ends.
Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all God's holy people in Christ Jesus at Philippi, along with the overseers and deacons:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God every time I remember you.
In every prayer for all of you, I always pray with joy,
because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now.
I am confident of this: He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.
It is right for me to feel this way about all of you, because I have you in my heart. In my chains and in my defense and confirmation of the gospel, all of you share in God's grace with me.
God is my witness that I long for all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus.
And this is my prayer: that your love may grow more and more in knowledge and deep understanding,
so that you may know what is best and may be pure and blameless until the day of Christ,
filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
Now I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has really helped the gospel move forward.
As a result, it has become clear to the whole palace guard and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ.
Because of my chains, most of the brothers in the Lord have become more confident and dare to speak God's word without fear.
It is true that some preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others do it out of goodwill.
Those who act in love know that I am here to defend the gospel.
The others preach Christ out of selfish ambition, not sincerely. They think they can make my chains harder to bear.
But what does it matter? The important thing is that Christ is preached in every way, whether from false motives or true. I rejoice in that, and I will keep rejoicing.
I know that through your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ, this will lead to my salvation.
I eagerly expect and hope that I will not be ashamed in any way. Instead, I will have complete boldness, so that now as always Christ will be honored in my body, whether by life or by death.
For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
If I go on living in the body, that means fruitful work for me. Yet I do not know which to choose.
I am torn between the two. I desire to leave this life and be with Christ, which is far better.
But it is more necessary for you that I remain in the body.
Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and continue with all of you for your progress and joy in the faith,
so that through my coming to you again, your pride in Christ Jesus will grow because of me.

Whatever happens, live in a way worthy of the gospel of Christ. Then, whether I come and see you or only hear about you while I am away, I will know that you stand firm in one spirit, working side by side for the faith of the gospel.
Do not be frightened by those who oppose you. This is a sign to them that they will be destroyed, but that you will be saved—and that by God.
For it has been granted to you on behalf of Christ not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for Him.
Since you are going through the same struggle you saw I had, and now hear that I still have.
So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any sharing in the Spirit, and any kindness and mercy,
then make my joy complete by being of one mind. Have the same love, be united in spirit, and think the same way.
Do nothing out of selfish ambition or pride. Instead, in humility, think of others as more important than yourselves.
Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others.
Have the same attitude among yourselves that Christ Jesus had.
Though He was in God's very nature, He did not cling to His equality with God.
Instead, He gave up His divine privileges and became a servant. He was born as a human.
And being found as a man, He humbled Himself and obeyed God all the way to death, even death on a cross.
Because of this, God raised Him to the highest place and gave Him the name that is above every other name.
So that at the name of Jesus every knee will bow, in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.
And every tongue will say that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
So, my dear friends, just as you have always obeyed, not only when I was with you but even more now that I am away, work hard to live out the salvation God has given you, with deep respect and awe.
For God is the One working in you, giving you the desire and the power to do what pleases Him.
Do everything without complaining or arguing.
Then you will be pure and without fault, God's children without blame in the middle of a crooked and twisted generation. Among them, you shine like lights in the world.
Hold tightly to the message that gives life. Then on the day Christ returns, I can be proud that my work and effort were not wasted.
Even if I give my life for your faith, I am glad and share your joy.
In the same way, you should be glad and share my joy.
I hope, with the Lord Jesus' help, to send Timothy to you soon, so I can be encouraged by news about you.
I have no one else like him who truly cares about your well-being.
Everyone else looks out for their own interests, not Christ's.
But you know how he has proven himself. He served with me in spreading the good news, like a son serving with his father.
So I hope to send him as soon as I know how things will turn out for me.
I trust in the Lord that I will come to you soon too.
I felt I had to send Epaphroditus back to you. He is my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier. He is also your messenger and the one who helped meet my needs.
He has been longing to see all of you, and he was upset because you heard he was sick.
He really was sick, almost to the point of death. But God had mercy on him, and on me too, so I would not have grief on top of grief.
So I am even more eager to send him, so you can be glad to see him again and I can worry less.
Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honor people like him.
He almost died for Christ's work. He risked his life to make up for the help you were unable to give me.
Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you, and it keeps you safe.
Watch out for the dogs, watch out for evil workers, and watch out for those who mutilate the flesh.
For we are the true circumcision. We worship by the Spirit of God, we boast in Christ Jesus, and we do not put our trust in human effort.
I could put confidence in human effort too. If anyone else thinks he has reason to trust in human effort, I have even more.
I was circumcised on the eighth day. I am from the people of Israel and the tribe of Benjamin. I am a Hebrew, born of Hebrews. As for the law, I was a Pharisee.
As for zeal, I persecuted the church. As for righteousness under the law, I was blameless.
But whatever used to be gain to me, I now count as loss for Christ.
Yes, I count everything as loss because knowing Christ Jesus my Lord is worth far more. For His sake I have lost everything, and I count it all as garbage so I can gain Christ.
I want to be found in Him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but one that comes through faith in Christ. It is the righteousness that comes from God and depends on faith.
I want to know Him and the power of His resurrection. I want to share in His sufferings and become like Him in His death.
Then I hope to reach the resurrection from the dead.
I have not already reached it or already become perfect. But I press on to take hold of that for which Christ Jesus took hold of me.
Brothers, I do not think I have taken hold of it yet. But one thing I do: I forget what is behind and reach forward to what is ahead.
I press on toward the goal to win the prize of God's upward call in Christ Jesus.
All of us who are mature should think this way. And if you think differently about anything, God will make that clear to you too.
Only let us live up to what we have already reached.
Brothers, join in following my example, and watch those who live the way we do. You have us as a model.
Many people walk as enemies of the cross of Christ. I have told you this often, and now I tell you again with tears.
Their end is destruction. Their god is their stomach. They are proud of what should shame them. They think only about earthly things.
But our citizenship is in heaven. We eagerly wait for a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ.
He will change our weak bodies to be like His glorious body. He does this by the power that lets Him bring everything under His control.
So, my dear brothers and sisters, whom I love and long to see, you are my joy and my crown. Stand firm in the Lord, dear friends.
I urge Euodia, and I urge Syntyche, to agree with each other in the Lord.
Yes, and I ask you, my true partner, to help these women. They worked hard with me for the good news, along with Clement and the rest of my coworkers. Their names are in the book of life.
Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!
Let everyone see your gentle spirit. The Lord is near.
Do not worry about anything. Instead, in everything, pray and ask God for what you need, with a thankful heart.
Then God's peace, which is greater than we can understand, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers and sisters, think about whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, and whatever is admirable. If anything is excellent or worthy of praise, think about those things.
Practice what you learned, received, heard, and saw in me. Then the God of peace will be with you.
I rejoiced greatly in the Lord because you finally showed care for me again. Earlier you had cared, but you had no chance to show it.
I am not saying this because I need something. I have learned to be content with whatever I have.
I know how to live with little, and I know how to live with plenty. I have learned the secret of being content in any and every situation, whether I am full or hungry, whether I have plenty or need.
I can do all things through Him who gives me strength.
Yet you did well to share in my trouble.
And you Philippians know that in the beginning of the good news, when I left Macedonia, no church shared with me in giving and receiving except you alone.
Even in Thessalonica you sent help for my needs more than once.
I do not say this because I want a gift. I want the reward that grows for your benefit.

I have received everything, and I have more than enough. I am fully supplied now that I have received from you the gifts brought by Epaphroditus. They are like a sweet-smelling offering, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
And my God will supply all your needs according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet every believer in Christ Jesus. The brothers and sisters with me send their greetings to you.
All the believers send greetings to you, especially those from Caesar's household.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and Timothy, our brother,
to the holy people and faithful brothers and sisters in Christ at Colossae: Grace and peace to you from God our Father.
We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you.
We have heard about your faith in Christ Jesus and your love for all God's people.
This faith and love come from the hope stored up for you in heaven, which you first heard about in the true message, the good news.
That good news has come to you. It is bearing fruit and growing all over the world, just as it has been doing among you since the day you heard it and truly understood God's grace.
You learned it from Epaphras, our dear fellow servant. He is a faithful helper of Christ for you.
He also told us about your love in the Spirit.
Because of this, since the day we heard about you, we have not stopped praying for you. We ask that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will, with all spiritual wisdom and understanding.
Then you can live in a way that honors the Lord. You can please Him in every way by bearing fruit in every good work and by growing in the knowledge of God.
You will be strengthened with all power, according to His glorious might, so you can have great endurance and patience, and you can be joyful.
Give thanks to the Father, who has made you able to share in the inheritance of God's people in the light.
He has rescued us from the power of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His dear Son.
In Him we have freedom, the forgiveness of sins.
The Son is the image of the invisible God. He is the firstborn over all creation.
For in Him all things were created: things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or powers or rulers or authorities. All things were created through Him and for Him.
He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.
He is the head of the body, which is the church. He is the beginning and the firstborn from the dead, so that He may have first place in everything.
For God was pleased to have all His fullness live in Him.
Through Him God made peace and brought all things back to Himself, whether things on earth or things in heaven, by the blood of His cross.
At one time you were far from God and were enemies in your minds because of your evil deeds.
But now He has brought you back to Himself through Christ's body and His death. He did this to present you holy, without fault, and blameless before Him.

This is true if you keep on believing. Stay strong and steady, and do not move away from the hope of the good news you heard. That good news has been preached to all creation under heaven, and I, Paul, became its servant.
Now I am glad to suffer for you. In my body I am filling up what is still needed in Christ's sufferings for His body, which is the church.
I became a servant of this message by the job God gave me: to fully share God's word with you.
This message was a secret hidden for ages and generations, but now it has been shown to God's holy people.
God chose to make known to the nations the glorious riches of this secret. The secret is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
We tell people about Him. We warn and teach everyone with all wisdom, so that we can present everyone fully grown in Christ.
For this reason I work hard and struggle with all His strength, which works powerfully in me.
For I want you to know how much I am struggling for you and for those in Laodicea, and for all who have never met me in person.
I want your hearts to be encouraged. I want you to be joined together in love and to gain the full riches of complete understanding, so you can know the mystery of God, which is Christ.
In Him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
I say this so no one will trick you with smooth talk.
Even though I am away from you in body, I am with you in spirit. I am happy to see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
So, just as you received Christ Jesus as Lord, keep walking in Him.
Be rooted and built up in Him. Be made strong in the faith you were taught, and overflow with thankfulness.
Watch out so no one takes you captive through philosophy or empty deceit. These follow human tradition and the basic principles of the world, not Christ.
For in Him all the fullness of Deity lives in bodily form.
And you have been made complete in Him, who is the head of every rule and authority.
In Him you were also circumcised. This was not done by human hands. It was the removal of the body of flesh, through the circumcision of Christ.
You were buried with Him in baptism, and in baptism you were raised with Him through faith in God's power. God raised Christ from the dead.
You were dead in your sins and in the uncircumcision of your flesh. But God made you alive with Christ. He forgave us all our sins.
He canceled the record of debt that stood against us, with its legal demands. He took it away by nailing it to the cross.
He stripped the rulers and authorities of their power. He made a public show of them and triumphed over them through Christ.
So let no one judge you about food or drink, or about a festival, a new moon, or a Sabbath.
These are only a shadow of things to come. The reality is Christ.
Let no one disqualify you by insisting on false humility and worship of angels. Such a person goes into detail about visions. He is puffed up without reason by his fleshly mind.
He does not hold on to the Head. From the Head, the whole body is nourished and joined together through its joints and ligaments. It grows with the growth that comes from God.
Since you died with Christ to the basic principles of the world, why do you still submit to rules as if you were living in the world?
"Do not handle! Do not taste! Do not touch!"
These things are all meant to be used up and destroyed. They come from human commands and teachings.
They look wise because they promote self-made religion, false humility, and harsh treatment of the body. But they do not really stop the flesh from sinning.
Since you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.
Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
For you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.
So put to death whatever belongs to your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry.
Because of these, God's anger is coming on those who refuse to obey.
You also used to do these things when you lived in them.
But now you must get rid of all these: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy talk from your mouth.
Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices
and have put on the new self, which is being made new in knowledge after the image of its Creator.
Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave or free, but Christ is all and is in all.
Therefore, as God's chosen people, holy and dearly loved, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
Bear with one another and forgive one another if any of you has a complaint against someone. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
And over all these virtues put on love, which binds them all together in perfect unity.
Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, since as members of one body you were called to peace. And be thankful.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly as you teach and warn one another with all wisdom, singing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with thankfulness in your hearts to God.
And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
Wives, submit yourselves to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.
Children, obey your parents in everything, for this pleases the Lord.
Fathers, do not provoke your children, or they will lose heart.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything. Do not work only to please them when they are watching, but work with a sincere heart, fearing the Lord.
Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as for the Lord and not for people.
Since you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as a reward, it is the Lord Christ you are serving.
Anyone who does wrong will be repaid for what he has done, and there is no favoritism.
Masters, treat your slaves fairly and justly, because you know that you also have a Master in heaven.
Stay devoted to prayer, and stay alert in it with thanksgiving.
Pray for us too, so that God will open a door for us to share His message and explain the mystery of Christ. That is why I am in chains.
Pray that I will make it clear, as I should.
Live wisely among people outside the church, and make good use of every opportunity.
Let your speech always be gracious and thoughtful, so that you will know how to answer each person.
Tychicus will tell you everything about my situation. He is a dear brother, a faithful servant, and a fellow worker in the Lord.
I am sending him to you for this very reason, so that you may know how we are doing and so that he may encourage your hearts.
With him is Onesimus, the faithful and dear brother, who is one of you. They will tell you everything that is happening here.
Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, sends his greetings, and so does Mark, the cousin of Barnabas. You have already received instructions about him; if he comes to you, welcome him.
Jesus, who is called Justus, also greets you. These are the only Jewish believers among my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, greets you. He always struggles in prayer for you, asking that you may stand firm, mature and fully sure of God's will in every way.
I can testify that he works hard for you and for the people in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
Luke, the dear doctor, and Demas greet you.
Greet the brothers in Laodicea, and greet Nympha and the church that meets in her home.
After this letter has been read among you, have it read also to the church of the Laodiceans, and be sure that you also read the letter from Laodicea.
Tell Archippus, "See that you complete the ministry you received in the Lord."
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write to the church in Thessalonica, which belongs to God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace and peace to you.
We always thank God for all of you. We mention you in our prayers.
Before God our Father, we never stop remembering your work of faith, your hard work of love, and your steady hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.
Brothers loved by God, we know that He chose you.
Our good news came to you not only with words, but also with power, with the Holy Spirit, and with strong confidence. You know what kind of people we were among you while we were there for your good.
You became followers of us and of the Lord. You received the message with joy from the Holy Spirit, even while you suffered a lot.
So you became an example to all believers in Macedonia and Achaia.
The Lord's message spread out from you not only in Macedonia and Achaia. Your faith in God has become known everywhere. So we do not need to say anything.
People everywhere tell how warmly you welcomed us. They tell how you turned away from idols to serve the living and true God.
They also tell how you are waiting for His Son to come from heaven. God raised Him from the dead. His Son is Jesus, and He saves us from the coming wrath.
You know, brothers and sisters, that our visit to you was not a waste.
As you know, we had already suffered and been insulted in Philippi. But with the help of our God, we were bold enough to tell you His gospel, even though we faced strong opposition.
Our appeal doesn't come from false beliefs, impure motives, or trickery.
Instead, we speak as people God has tested and trusted with the gospel. We aren't trying to please people, but God, who tests our hearts.
You know we never used flattery or hid greedy motives behind our words. God is our witness.
We didn't look for praise from people—not from you or anyone else—even though, as Christ's apostles, we could have used our authority.
Instead, we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother caring for her children.
We cared so much for you that we were happy to share with you not only God's gospel but our own lives, because you had become dear to us.
Surely you remember, brothers and sisters, how hard we worked. We labored night and day so we wouldn't be a burden to any of you while we preached God's gospel to you.
You are witnesses, and so is God, of how holy, right, and blameless we were among you who believed.
You know we dealt with each of you the way a father deals with his own children.
We encouraged you, comforted you, and urged you to live in a way that honors God, who calls you into His kingdom and glory.
We never stop thanking God because, when you received the word of God that you heard from us, you accepted it not as a human word but as God's word, which is truly at work in you who believe.
Brothers and sisters, you became like the churches of God in Judea that are in Christ Jesus. You suffered the same things from your own people that those churches suffered from the Jews.
They killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and they drove us out. They don't please God, and they are against all people.
They try to stop us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they won't be saved. In this way, they keep adding to their sins. But God's wrath has finally come upon them.
Brothers and sisters, after we were separated from you for a short time—in person, not in heart—we wanted very much to see you again, so we tried hard to do it.
We wanted to come to you—I, Paul, tried more than once—but Satan stopped us.
After all, what is our hope, our joy, or the crown we will boast about in the presence of our Lord Jesus when He comes? Isn't it you?
Yes, you are our glory and our joy.
At last we could not stand it any longer. We decided to stay in Athens by ourselves.
We sent Timothy, our brother and God's helper in sharing the good news about Christ. He came to strengthen you and encourage you in your faith.
We did not want anyone to give up because of these troubles. You know that we are meant to face hard times.
When we were with you, we told you ahead of time that we would suffer. That is what happened, as you know.
That is why, when I could not wait any longer, I sent Timothy to find out about your faith. I was afraid the tempter might have tested you, and our work would be wasted.
But now Timothy has come back from you with good news. He told us about your faith and love. He said you always remember us kindly and long to see us, just as we long to see you.
Because of this, brothers and sisters, we were comforted in all our trouble and distress by your faith.
Now we feel alive again if you are standing firm in the Lord.
How can we thank God enough for you? We have so much joy because of you as we pray to our God.
Night and day we pray with all our heart that we may see you face to face. We also pray that we can fill in what is missing in your faith.
May our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, make our way to you.
May the Lord make your love grow and overflow for each other and for everyone, just as ours does for you.
May He strengthen your hearts so you will be blameless and holy before our God and Father when our Lord Jesus comes with all His holy people. Amen.
Finally, brothers and sisters, we ask and urge you in the Lord Jesus to live the way we taught you, a way that pleases God. You are already living that way, but we want you to do even more.
You already know these instructions, because we gave them to you through the Lord Jesus.
God wants you to be holy, so stay away from sexual sin.
Each of you should learn to control your own body in a holy and respectful way.
Do not let strong desire control you, like people who do not know God.
No one should wrong or cheat a fellow believer in this matter, because the Lord punishes all such sins. We have already told you this and warned you.
God did not call us to live in uncleanness, but in holiness.
So anyone who rejects this teaching is not rejecting a human being, but God, who gives you His Holy Spirit.
Now about loving each other as brothers and sisters, you do not need anyone to write to you, because God Himself has taught you to love one another.
In fact, you are already doing this for all the brothers and sisters throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers and sisters, to do it even more.
Make it your goal to live a quiet life, mind your own business, and work with your hands, just as we told you.
Then you will earn the respect of outsiders, and you will not have to depend on anyone.
Brothers and sisters, we do not want you to be uninformed about those who have died, so that you will not grieve like people who have no hope.
Since we believe that Jesus died and rose again, we also believe that God will bring with Jesus those who have died in Him.
We tell you this by the Lord's own word: We who are still alive when the Lord comes will not go ahead of those who have died.
For the Lord Himself will come down from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet call of God. And the dead in Christ will rise first.
After that, we who are still alive and are left will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so we will be with the Lord forever.
Therefore encourage one another with these words.
Now, brothers, I do not need to write to you about the times and seasons.
You know very well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.
When people say, "Peace and safety," then sudden destruction will come on them, like labor pains on a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that day should not surprise you like a thief.
You are all children of light and children of the day. We are not children of the night or of darkness.
So let us not sleep like the others do. Instead, let us stay awake and be clear-minded.
People who sleep, sleep at night, and people who get drunk, get drunk at night.
But since we belong to the day, let us be clear-minded. Let us put on faith and love like a breastplate, and hope of salvation like a helmet.
For God did not choose us to face His anger. He chose us to receive salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.
He died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.
So encourage each other and build each other up, just as you are already doing.
Brothers, we ask you to respect those who work hard among you, who lead you in the Lord, and who warn you.
Hold them in the highest respect and love because of their work. Live in peace with each other.
We urge you, brothers, to warn those who are out of line, comfort those who are discouraged, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
Make sure no one pays back evil for evil. Instead, always try to do good for each other and for everyone.
Give thanks in everything, because this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus.
Do not put out the Spirit's fire.
Do not look down on prophecies.
Test everything, and hold on to what is good.
Stay away from every kind of evil.
May the God of peace make you completely holy. May your whole spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless until our Lord Jesus Christ comes.
He who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.
Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
I ask you to promise by the Lord that this letter will be read to all the brothers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write to the church in Thessalonica. You are in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Brothers and sisters, we always need to thank God for you. That is right, because your faith is growing more and more. Also, each of you loves the others more and more.
So we brag about you to God's churches. We tell them about your patience and faith. You stay strong through all the trouble and hardship you face.
This shows that God judges fairly. He is making you worthy of His kingdom. You are suffering for that kingdom.
God is fair. He will give trouble to the people who trouble you.
He will give rest to you who are troubled, and to us too. This will happen when the Lord Jesus comes from heaven with His powerful angels.
He will come in blazing fire. He will punish those who do not know God. He will also punish those who do not obey the good news about our Lord Jesus.
They will be punished with lasting destruction. They will be kept away from the Lord's presence and from His glorious power.
This will happen on the day He comes. He will be honored among His holy people. Everyone who believed will be amazed at Him. You believed the message we brought you.
So we always pray for you. We ask God to make you worthy of His call. We ask Him to use His power to complete every good desire and every act of faith.
Then the name of our Lord Jesus will be honored in you. You will also be honored in Him. This comes from the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Now about the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering to Him, we ask you, brothers.
Don't be quickly shaken in your mind or alarmed by a spirit, a spoken message, or a letter that seems to be from us saying the day of the Lord has already come.
Don't let anyone trick you in any way. That day won't come until the rebellion happens first and the man of lawlessness—the son of destruction—is revealed.
He opposes and lifts himself above every so-called god or thing people worship. He even sits in God's temple and claims that he is God.
Don't you remember that I told you these things while I was still with you?
And you know what is holding him back now, so he will be revealed when the time is right.
The hidden power of lawlessness is already at work. But the one who holds it back will keep doing so until he is taken out of the way.
Then the lawless one will be revealed. The Lord Jesus will destroy him with the breath of His mouth and bring him to nothing by the brightness of His coming.
The lawless one will come with Satan's power. He will do all kinds of miracles, signs, and false wonders.
He will use every kind of evil trick to fool those who are on their way to ruin, because they refused to love the truth and be saved.
That's why God sends them a powerful delusion so they will believe the lie.
This happens so everyone who didn't believe the truth but enjoyed doing wrong will be condemned.
But we should always thank God for you, brothers loved by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning to be saved through the Holy Spirit making you holy and through your faith in the truth.
He called you to this through our good news, so you could share in the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers, stand firm and hold on to the teachings we passed on to you, whether by word of mouth or by letter.
Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope by His grace,
comfort your hearts and strengthen you in every good deed and word.
Finally, brothers, pray for us that the word of the Lord may spread quickly and be honored, just as it was among you.
Pray also that we may be saved from harmful and evil people, because not everyone has faith.
But the Lord is faithful. He will make you strong and guard you from the evil one.
We trust in the Lord that you are doing and will keep doing what we command.
May the Lord guide your hearts into God’s love and into Christ’s patience.
Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to stay away from every brother who lives in a disorderly way and not according to the teaching we gave you.
For you yourselves know how you should follow our example, because we were not disorderly among you.
We did not eat anyone’s bread for free. Instead, we worked hard day and night so we would not be a burden to any of you.
We did this not because we lack authority, but to give you an example to follow.
Even when we were with you, we gave you this rule: “If anyone is not willing to work, he should not eat.”
We hear that some among you are living in a disorderly way. They do no work, but they meddle in other people’s business.
We command and urge such people in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread.
But you, brothers, do not get tired of doing good.
If anyone does not obey our message in this letter, take note of that person. Do not associate with him, so he may be ashamed.
Do not treat him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
This greeting is in my own hand—Paul. This is a sign in every letter, and this is how I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope,
to Timothy, my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
As I urged you when I was going to Macedonia, stay in Ephesus so you can command certain people not to teach false ideas.
They must not spend time on myths and endless family lists. These things lead to useless arguments instead of God's plan, which depends on faith.
The goal of this command is love that comes from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a real faith.
Some people have missed this goal and turned to empty talk.
They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying or what they are so sure about.
We know the law is good if someone uses it the right way.

We also know the law is not made for good people. It is made for lawbreakers and rebels, for ungodly people and sinners, for unholy and unclean people, for those who attack their fathers or mothers, and for murderers.

It is also for sexually immoral people, for men who have sex with men, for slave traders, for liars, for people who break their promises under oath, and for anything else that goes against healthy teaching.
This teaching agrees with the glorious good news of the blessed God, which He trusted me to share.
I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who gave me strength. He counted me faithful and chose me to serve Him.
I used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man. But I was shown mercy because I acted in ignorance and unbelief.
The grace of our Lord overflowed to me, along with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
This is a true saying and worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and I am the worst of them.
But I was shown mercy so that in me, the worst sinner, Christ Jesus might show His complete patience as an example for those who would believe in Him and receive eternal life.
To the King of the ages, the immortal and invisible God, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
Timothy, my child, I entrust this command to you in keeping with the prophecies made about you, so that by them you may fight the good battle.
Hold on to faith and a good conscience. Some people have rejected these and ruined their faith.
Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander. I have handed them over to Satan so they may learn not to blaspheme.
First of all, I urge that people pray, ask God for help, pray for others, and give thanks for everyone.
Pray for kings and all who are in authority, so that we can live peaceful and quiet lives with godliness and respect.
This is good and pleasing to God our Savior.
He wants all people to be saved and to come to know the truth.
For there is one God and one mediator between God and people: the man Christ Jesus.
He gave Himself as a ransom for all people. This truth was made known at the right time.
For this I was appointed a preacher and apostle. I am telling the truth; I am not lying. I am a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
So I want the men in every place to pray. They should lift up holy hands, without anger or arguing.
In the same way, I want the women to dress modestly, with decency and self-control. They should not focus on fancy braided hair, gold, pearls, or expensive clothes.
Instead, they should do good works, which is proper for women who claim to worship God.
A woman should learn quietly and be fully submissive.
I do not allow a woman to teach or to have authority over a man. She must be quiet.
For Adam was made first, and then Eve.
Adam was not deceived. The woman was deceived and sinned.
But she will be saved through having children, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness with self-control.
This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone wants to be an overseer, he wants a noble task.
An overseer must be above reproach, the husband of one wife, sober, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, and able to teach.
He must not be a drunkard or violent. Instead, he should be gentle, peaceable, and not greedy for money.
He must manage his own home well and keep his children under control with all dignity.
For if someone cannot manage his own home, how can he take care of God's church?
He must not be a new believer, or he might become proud and fall under the devil's judgment.
He must also have a good reputation with outsiders, so he will not fall into disgrace and the devil's trap.
Deacons must also be respectable, not two-faced, not addicted to much wine, and not greedy for dishonest gain.
They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
They must first be tested. Then, if they are blameless, they can serve as deacons.
Women likewise must be respectable, not slanderers, sober, and faithful in everything.
Deacons must be husbands of one wife and manage their children and homes well.
Those who serve well as deacons gain a good standing for themselves and great confidence in the faith in Christ Jesus.
I hope to come to you soon, but I am writing these things to you now.
If I am delayed, you will know how to act in God's household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and support of the truth.

By common confession, the mystery of godliness is great: He appeared in the flesh, was proven right by the Spirit, was seen by angels, was preached among the nations, was believed on in the world, and was taken up in glory.
The Spirit clearly says that in later times some people will turn away from the faith. They will pay attention to spirits that trick them and to teachings that come from demons.
These teachings spread through hypocrites who lie. Their consciences have been burned so they no longer feel guilt.
They forbid people to marry and tell them to stay away from certain foods. But God made those foods to be received with thanks by people who believe and know the truth.
Everything God created is good. Nothing should be rejected if it is received with thanks,
because God's word and prayer make it holy.
If you point these things out to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and of the good teaching you have followed.
But turn away from godless and silly stories. Instead, train yourself to live a godly life.
Physical training helps for a little while, but godliness helps in every way. It carries a promise for this life and for the life to come.
This is a true saying, and it deserves full acceptance.
That is why we work hard and struggle. We have put our hope in the living God, who saves all people, and especially those who believe.
Don't let anyone look down on you because you are young. Instead, be an example to believers in what you say, how you live, in love, in faith, and in purity.
Until I come, pay attention to reading aloud, to encouraging others, and to teaching.
Don't neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy when the elders laid their hands on you.
Think about these things. Live by them, so that your progress will be clear to everyone.
Watch yourself and your teaching. Stay with them, because if you do this, you will save both yourself and the people who listen to you.
Do not scold an older man. Instead, speak to him as a father. Treat younger men like brothers.
Treat older women like mothers and younger women like sisters, with complete purity.
Honor widows who are truly alone.
If a widow has children or grandchildren, they should first learn to care for their own family and repay their parents. This pleases God.
A widow who is truly alone puts her hope in God and keeps praying day and night.
But a widow who lives only for pleasure is spiritually dead, even though she is still alive.
Give these commands so no one can be blamed.
If anyone does not take care of his own family, especially those in his home, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
A widow should be added to the list only if she is at least sixty years old and has been married to only one husband.
She must be known for good works, such as raising children, welcoming strangers, washing the feet of God's people, helping those in trouble, and doing every kind of good deed.
But do not add younger widows to the list. When their strong desires pull them away from Christ, they want to marry again.
They bring judgment on themselves because they have broken their first promise to Christ.
Besides that, they learn to be lazy and go from house to house. They not only become lazy but also talk too much and meddle in other people's business, saying things they should not say.
So I want younger widows to marry, have children, and manage their homes. That way they give the enemy no reason to speak badly about us.
Some have already turned away and followed Satan.
If a believing woman has widows in her family, she should help them. Then the church is not weighed down and can help the widows who are truly alone.
Elders who lead well deserve to be respected and well paid, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
For the Scripture says, "Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading grain," and, "The worker deserves his pay."
Do not listen to an accusation against an elder unless two or three witnesses support it.
But those who keep sinning, correct in front of everyone, so the others will be afraid to sin.
I charge you before God, Christ Jesus, and the chosen angels to keep these rules without bias, doing nothing out of favoritism.
Do not quickly appoint anyone to leadership, and do not share in other people's sins. Keep yourself pure.
Stop drinking only water. Use a little wine for your stomach and your frequent illnesses.
The sins of some people are easy to see and lead the way to judgment. The sins of others follow later.
In the same way, good deeds are easy to see. Even those that are not obvious cannot stay hidden.
All who are slaves under a yoke should treat their own masters as worthy of full honor. Then God’s name and teaching won’t be spoken against.

Those who have believing masters shouldn’t look down on them just because they are brothers. Instead, they should serve them even better, because the masters who benefit from their good work are faithful and loved. Teach and urge these things.
If anyone teaches a different message and doesn’t agree with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with teaching that leads to godly living,
that person is proud and knows nothing. He is sick with arguing and word fights. These things lead to envy, quarreling, insults, evil suspicions,
and constant friction among people whose minds are ruined and who are robbed of the truth. They think godliness is a way to get rich.
But godliness with contentment is great gain.
We brought nothing into the world, and we can’t take anything out.
So if we have food and clothing, we should be content with that.
People who want to get rich fall into temptation and a trap. They are caught by many foolish and harmful desires that drag them down to ruin and destruction.
The love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. Some people, eager for money, have wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows.
But you, man of God, run from these things. Chase after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, and gentleness.
Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of eternal life, to which you were called and about which you made the good confession before many witnesses.
I charge you before God, who gives life to everything, and before Christ Jesus, who gave the good confession before Pontius Pilate.
Keep this command pure and blameless until our Lord Jesus Christ appears.
God will reveal it at the right time. He is the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
He alone has immortality and lives in unapproachable light. No human has seen Him, and no one can see Him. To Him be honor and eternal power. Amen.

Command those who are rich in this present world not to be proud and not to put their hope in wealth, which is so uncertain. Instead, they should put their hope in God, who richly gives us everything to enjoy.
Tell them to do good, to be rich in good works, and to be generous and willing to share.
In this way they store up treasure for themselves, a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of the life that is truly life.
Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Turn away from godless, empty talk and from the opposing ideas of what is falsely called knowledge.
Some people who claim to have it have wandered from the faith. Grace be with you.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, in keeping with the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus.
To Timothy, my beloved child: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience, as my ancestors did. I remember you constantly, night and day, in my prayers.
I long to see you, remembering your tears, so that I may be filled with joy.
I've been reminded of the sincere faith that lives in you, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice. I'm convinced that it lives in you too.
For this reason I remind you to rekindle the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God did not give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
So don't be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, and don't be ashamed of me, His prisoner. Instead, join me in suffering for the good news, by God's power.
God saved us and called us to a holy calling. He didn't do this because of our works, but because of His own purpose and grace. This grace was given to us in Christ Jesus before time began.
Now it has been revealed through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus. He destroyed death and revealed life and immortality through the good news.
I was appointed a preacher, apostle, and teacher for this good news.
That's why I'm suffering these things. But I'm not ashamed, because I know the One I have believed in. I'm convinced that He is able to guard what I've entrusted to Him until that day.
Hold on to the pattern of sound teaching that you heard from me, with faith and love in Christ Jesus.
Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit, who lives in us.
You know that everyone in Asia has turned away from me. Phygelus and Hermogenes are among them.
May the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus. He often refreshed me, and he wasn't ashamed of my chains.
When he was in Rome, he searched hard until he found me.
May the Lord grant that he finds mercy from the Lord on that day. You know very well how much he helped in Ephesus.
You then, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
And what you heard from me among many witnesses, entrust to faithful men who will be able to teach others.
Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No one serving as a soldier gets tangled up in everyday business, because he wants to please his commanding officer.
Also, if anyone competes, he is not crowned unless he competes by the rules.
The hardworking farmer should be the first to share in the crops.
Think about what I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, a descendant of David, as my gospel says.
I suffer for it to the point of being chained like a criminal, but the word of God is not chained.
So I endure everything for the sake of the chosen people, so that they too may receive the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
This is a trustworthy saying: If we died with Him, we will also live with Him.
If we endure, we will also reign with Him. If we deny Him, He will also deny us.
If we are faithless, He remains faithful, because He cannot deny Himself.
Remind them of these things, and warn them before God not to argue about words. That does no good and only ruins those who listen.
Make every effort to present yourself to God as one approved, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, who rightly handles the word of truth.
But avoid godless chatter, because it will lead to more ungodliness.
Their message will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus.
They have wandered away from the truth by saying that the resurrection has already happened, and they are upsetting the faith of some.
Still, God's solid foundation stands firm. It carries this seal: "The Lord knows those who are His," and, "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from wickedness."
In a large house there are not only gold and silver dishes, but also wooden and clay ones. Some are for honorable use, and some are for dishonorable use.
So if anyone cleanses himself from the dishonorable things, he will be a dish for honor, set apart, useful to the Master, and ready for every good work.
Flee from youthful passions, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.
Reject foolish and ignorant arguments, knowing that they lead to fights.
The Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome. Instead, he should be kind to everyone, able to teach, and patient.
He should gently correct those who oppose him, hoping that God may grant them repentance that leads to knowing the truth.
Then they may come to their senses and escape the trap of the devil, who has captured them to do his will.
But know this: In the last days, hard times will come.
People will love only themselves and money. They will be boastful, proud, and abusive. They will disobey their parents, be ungrateful, and be unholy.
They will have no natural affection, refuse to forgive, slander others, lack self-control, be brutal, and hate what is good.
They will be traitors, reckless, full of pride, and lovers of pleasure instead of lovers of God.
They will keep up the look of godliness, but deny its power. Have nothing to do with them.
Some of them sneak into homes and take advantage of weak-willed women who are loaded down with sins and led astray by all kinds of evil desires.
These women are always learning, but they can never come to know the truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, these people also oppose the truth. Their minds are corrupted, and they are rejected in matters of faith.
But they will not get far. Their foolishness will be clear to everyone, just as the foolishness of those men was.
You, however, know all about my teaching, my way of life, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, and my endurance.
You know about my persecutions and sufferings—what happened to me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. I endured those persecutions, and the Lord rescued me from all of them.
Everyone who wants to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
But evil people and impostors will go from bad to worse. They will deceive others and be deceived themselves.
But as for you, stay with what you have learned and are sure of, because you know who taught you.
From childhood you have known the Holy Scriptures, which can make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and training in righteousness.
It does this so that the servant of God may be fully equipped for every good work.
I charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who is going to judge the living and the dead, and by His appearing and His kingdom:
Preach the word. Be ready whether the time seems right or not. Correct, rebuke, and encourage with complete patience and teaching.

For the time will come when people will not tolerate sound teaching. Instead, to suit their own desires, they will gather around themselves a great number of teachers to say what their itching ears want to hear.
They will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths.
But you, stay clear-minded in all situations, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and fully carry out your ministry.
For I am already being poured out like an offering, and the time for my departure is near.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, and I have kept the faith.
Now there is stored up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will give me on that day—and not only to me, but also to all who have longed for His appearing.
Do your best to come to me quickly,
because Demas loved this present world, so he deserted me and went to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is helpful to me in my ministry.
When you come, bring the cloak I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.
Alexander the metalworker did me a great deal of harm. The Lord will repay him for what he has done.
You too should be careful around him, because he strongly opposed our message.
At my first defense, no one came to my support, but everyone deserted me. May it not be held against them.
But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the Gentiles might hear it. And I was rescued from great danger.
The Lord will rescue me from every evil attack and will bring me safely to His heavenly kingdom. To Him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
Do your best to get here before winter. Eubulus greets you, and so do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers and sisters.
The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.
Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, writes for the faith of God’s chosen people and their knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness.
He writes in the hope of eternal life, which God, who never lies, promised before time began.
At the right time, He made His word known through the preaching He trusted to me, by the command of God our Savior.
To Titus, my true son in our shared faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
I left you in Crete so you could put in order what still needed work and appoint elders in every town, as I told you.
An elder must be without blame. He must have one wife, and his children must be believers. They must not be accused of wild living or of refusing to obey.
Because an overseer manages God’s work, he must be without blame. He must not be proud, quick to anger, drunk, violent, or eager for dishonest gain.
Instead, he must welcome strangers, love what is good, be self-controlled, right, holy, and disciplined.
He must hold firmly to the trustworthy message, as it was taught, so he can encourage others with sound teaching and correct those who argue against it.
There are many rebellious people who say empty things and fool others. This is especially true of those who insist on circumcision.
They must be stopped from talking, because they upset whole families by teaching what they should not teach, just to make dishonest money.
One of their own prophets even said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, and lazy gluttons.”
This statement is true. So rebuke them sharply, so they may be sound in their faith.
They should not pay attention to Jewish myths or to human commands from people who turn away from the truth.
To pure people, everything is pure. But to corrupt and unbelieving people, nothing is pure. Even their minds and consciences are stained.
They claim to know God, but they deny Him by what they do. They are detestable, disobedient, and useless for any good work.
But you should speak what fits sound teaching.
Older men should be sober, worthy of respect, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love, and endurance.
Older women should be reverent in how they live. They shouldn't be slanderers or slaves to much wine. They should teach what is good.
Then they can train the young women to love their husbands and children,
to be self-controlled and pure, to work at home, to be kind, and to submit to their own husbands. That way, no one will speak badly of God's word.
Likewise, urge the young men to be self-controlled.
In everything, set yourself as an example of good works. In your teaching, show integrity and seriousness.
Use sound speech that no one can condemn. Then anyone who opposes you will be ashamed, because they'll have nothing bad to say about us.
Slaves should obey their own masters in everything. They should try to please them and not talk back.
They shouldn't steal, but should show complete honesty, so that in every way they make the teaching about God our Savior attractive.
For God's grace has appeared, bringing salvation to all people.
It trains us to say no to ungodliness and worldly desires, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in this present age.
We wait for the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.
He gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people who are His own, eager to do good works.
Speak these things, encourage, and correct with all authority. Don't let anyone look down on you.
Remind them to obey rulers and authorities and to be ready for every good work.
Tell them not to insult anyone, to be peaceable and gentle, and to show true humility to everyone.
At one time we too were foolish and disobedient. We were led astray and served all kinds of desires and pleasures. We lived in evil and envy, and people hated us while we hated each other.
But when the kindness of God our Savior and His love for people appeared,
He saved us. It was not because of good things we had done, but because of His mercy. He washed us clean through the new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
God poured out the Spirit on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior.
Because we were made right by His grace, we can now hope to receive eternal life.
This is a trustworthy saying, and I want you to stress these things. Then believers will be careful to do good works. These things are good and helpful for everyone.
But stay away from foolish arguments, family histories, fights, and quarrels about the law. They are useless and empty.
Warn a person who causes division once, and then again. After that, have nothing to do with him.
Keep in mind that such a person is twisted and keeps on sinning. He brings judgment on himself.
