When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, try to come to me at Nicopolis. I have decided to spend the winter there.
Help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, so they will not need anything.
Our people must also learn to do good works to meet real needs, so they will not be unproductive.
Everyone with me sends you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. May grace be with all of you.
Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our dear friend and fellow worker,
to Apphia our sister, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your home:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God as I remember you in my prayers,
because I hear about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints.
I pray that your partnership in the faith will be active as you know every good thing we have in Christ.
Your love has given me great joy and comfort, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
So, although in Christ I could be bold and order you to do what is right,
I would rather appeal to you out of love. I, Paul, am an old man, and now I am a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whom I fathered while in chains.
He was once useless to you, but now he is useful to both you and me.
I am sending him back to you—he is my very heart.
I wanted to keep him with me so that he could serve me on your behalf while I am in chains for the gospel.
But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your kindness would not be forced but freely given.
Maybe this is why he was separated from you for a short time, so that you could have him back forever.
He is no longer just a slave, but a beloved brother—especially to me, and even more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
So if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
If he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will pay it back. I will not even mention that you owe me your very self.
Yes, brother, let me have this benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.
I write this trusting your obedience, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.
Also, prepare a guest room for me, because I hope that through your prayers I will be restored to you.
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings.
So do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
Long ago, God spoke to our ancestors in many ways through the prophets.
But in these last days, He has spoken to us through His Son. God made His Son the heir of all things, and He created the world through Him.

The Son shines with God's glory and shows exactly what God is like. He holds everything together by His powerful word. After He had made us clean from sin, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty in heaven.
So He became far greater than the angels, because the name He received is much better than theirs.
For God never said to any angel, "You are My Son; today I have become your Father." Or again, "I will be his Father, and he will be My Son."
And again, when He brings His firstborn Son into the world, He says, "Let all of God's angels worship Him."
He also says about the angels, "He makes His angels spirits, and His servants a flame of fire."
But about the Son He says, "Your throne, O God, lasts forever and ever, and the scepter of Your kingdom is a scepter of justice.
You have loved what is right and hated what is wrong. So God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of joy more than Your companions."
And, "You, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
They will pass away, but You remain. They will all wear out like a piece of clothing.
You will roll them up like a robe, and they will be changed like clothes. But You are the same, and Your years will never end."
But God never said to any angel, "Sit at My right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."
Are not all angels serving spirits sent to help those who will receive salvation?
So we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, or we may drift away.
For if the message given through angels was binding, and every sin and disobedience received a fair punishment,
how can we escape if we ignore such a great salvation? It was first announced by the Lord, and those who heard Him confirmed it to us.
God also gave His witness with signs, wonders, and all kinds of miracles, and with gifts from the Holy Spirit given as He chose.
For God did not put the world to come under angels' control, the world we are talking about.
But someone has testified somewhere, saying, "What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.
You put everything under his feet." Now when He put everything under him, He left nothing outside his rule. But right now we do not yet see everything under his rule.
But we do see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by God's grace He could taste death for everyone.
For it was fitting that God, who brings many sons to glory, should make Jesus—the leader of their salvation—perfect through suffering. He is the One for whom and through whom everything exists.
For the One who makes people holy and those who are made holy all come from one family. That is why Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.
He says, "I will declare Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the middle of the assembly."
And again, "I will put My trust in Him." And again, "Here am I, and the children God has given Me."
Since the children share flesh and blood, Jesus also shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy the one who holds the power of death—that is, the devil.
He did this to free those who were held in slavery all their lives by their fear of death.
For surely He does not help angels; He helps Abraham's descendants.
So He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He could become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, to pay for the sins of the people.
Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.
So, holy brothers and sisters, you share in a heavenly calling. Think carefully about Jesus, the Apostle and High Priest of the faith we profess.
He was faithful to the One who made Him, just like Moses was faithful in all God's house.
Jesus has been found worthy of more glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has more honor than the house itself.
Every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.
Moses was faithful as a servant in all God's house. He gave witness to what would be spoken later.
But Christ is faithful as a Son over God's house. We are His house if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope we boast about.
So, as the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear His voice,
do not harden your hearts as you did in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness.
There your fathers tested Me and tried Me, and they saw My works for forty years.
So I was angry with that generation, and I said, 'They are always going astray in their hearts. They have not known My ways.'
So I swore in My anger, 'They will not enter My rest.'"
Watch out, brothers and sisters, so that none of you has an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
Instead, encourage one another every day, as long as it is called Today, so that none of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin.
We have become partners with Christ if we hold firmly to the confidence we had at first, all the way to the end.
As it says, "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion."
Who were the ones who heard God's voice and still rebelled? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt with Moses?
And who was God angry with for forty years? Was it not those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
And to whom did He swear they would not enter His rest? Was it not those who disobeyed?
So we see that they could not enter because of unbelief.
So, since the promise still stands that we can enter God's rest, let us be careful. None of you should think you have missed it.
We heard the good news too, just like those people did. But the message they heard did not help them, because they did not believe it.
We who believe are entering that rest. God said, "As I swore in My anger, 'They will never enter My rest.'" Yet His work was finished when the world was made.
In one place He said about the seventh day, "God rested on the seventh day from all His work."
And again He said, "They will never enter My rest."
So it is still open for some people to enter. Those who first heard the good news did not enter because they would not obey.
So God set another day, called "Today." Long after that time, He spoke through David, as it was said before: "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts."
If Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
So a Sabbath rest is still left for God's people.
Anyone who enters God's rest also rests from his own work, just as God rested from His.
So let us work hard to enter that rest. Then no one will fall into the same kind of disobedience.
God's word is alive and powerful. It is sharper than any sword with two edges. It cuts deep, even to the place where soul and spirit meet, and to joints and marrow. It judges what we think and want.
Nothing is hidden from God. Everything is open and uncovered before the eyes of the One we must answer to.
Since we have a great high priest who has gone through the heavens—Jesus, the Son of God—let us hold firmly to what we believe.
Our high priest can feel our weaknesses. He was tested in every way, just like we are, but He never sinned.
So let us come boldly to the throne of grace. Then we will receive mercy and find grace to help us when we need it.
Every high priest is chosen from among people and is put in charge of things between God and people. He offers gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He can be gentle with people who don't know better and who wander off the path, because he himself struggles with weakness.
Because of that weakness, he must offer sacrifices for his own sins as well as for the sins of the people.
No one takes this honor for himself. He receives it only when God calls him, just as Aaron was called.
In the same way, Christ did not give Himself the glory of becoming high priest. Instead, God said to Him, “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”
In another place God says, “You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek.”

While He lived in a human body, Christ offered prayers and requests to God. He cried out loudly and with tears to the One who could save Him from death, and God heard Him because He deeply respected God.
Even though He was the Son, He learned to obey through what He suffered.
After He was made complete, He became the source of eternal salvation for everyone who obeys Him.
God named Him a high priest in the order of Melchizedek.
We have a lot to say about this, but it is hard to explain because you have become slow to listen.
By now you should be teachers, but you still need someone to teach you the basic truths of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food.
Anyone who lives on milk is still a baby and does not understand the teaching about living right.
Solid food is for mature believers. Their senses have been trained by practice to tell good from evil.
So let us leave the basic teaching about Christ and move on toward maturity. We should not start over by laying again the foundation of turning away from actions that bring death and of faith in God,
or of teaching about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the rising of the dead, and eternal judgment.
And we will do this if God allows.
It is impossible to bring back to repentance those who were once enlightened, who tasted the heavenly gift, who shared in the Holy Spirit,
who tasted God's good message and the powers of the coming age, and then fell away.
They are crucifying the Son of God again for themselves and putting Him to public shame.
Land that soaks up the rain that often falls on it and produces useful crops for the farmers receives a blessing from God.
But land that grows thorns and weeds is worthless and close to being cursed. In the end, it will be burned.
Dear friends, even though we speak like this, we are sure that you have better things—things that go with salvation.
God is not unfair. He will not forget the work you have done and the love you have shown for His name by serving God's people and by continuing to serve them.
We want each of you to show this same eagerness to the very end, so that you may be fully sure of your hope.
Then you will not be lazy. Instead, you will follow the example of those who receive what God has promised because of their faith and patience.
When God made His promise to Abraham, He could not swear by anyone greater, so He swore by Himself.
He said, "I will surely bless you and multiply you."
And so, after waiting patiently, Abraham received what was promised.
People swear by something greater than themselves, and an oath settles every argument for them.
God wanted to make it very clear to those who would receive the promise that His plan would never change. So He added an oath.
God cannot lie. So by these two unchangeable things, we who have run to Him for safety can hold on to the hope set before us with strong encouragement.
We have this hope as an anchor for the soul. It is safe and sure, and it goes into the inner place behind the curtain.
Jesus has gone there ahead of us. He has become a high priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek.
For this Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham as he was coming back from defeating the kings, and he blessed him.
Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. First, Melchizedek's name means “king of righteousness.” Then it also means “king of Salem,” which is “king of peace.”
He has no father or mother and no family line. He has no beginning of days and no end of life. Instead, he is like the Son of God and remains a priest forever.
Think how great this man was. Even Abraham, the great ancestor, gave him a tenth of the best things taken in war.
The law says that the sons of Levi who become priests can collect a tenth from the people. That means they collect it from their own brothers, even though those brothers also come from Abraham.
But Melchizedek did not come from Levi's family line, yet he collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed the man who had God's promises.
Everyone knows that the greater person blesses the lesser one.
In one case, men who die receive the tenth. In the other case, it is received by someone who is said to live.
In a way, even Levi, who receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham.
This is because Levi had not yet been born; he was still part of Abraham's family line when Melchizedek met Abraham.
If the Levite priesthood had made people perfect, why would another priest need to come, one like Melchizedek instead of one from Aaron's family? The people received the law under that priesthood.
When the priesthood changes, the law must change too.
The One this speaks about belongs to a different tribe. No one from that tribe ever served at the altar.
It is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, and Moses never said anything about priests from that tribe.
This point becomes even clearer if another priest like Melchizedek appears.
He became a priest not because of a rule about family descent, but because of the power of a life that cannot be destroyed.
Scripture says about Him, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
So the old command is set aside because it was weak and useless.
The law did not make anything perfect. But a better hope has been brought in, and through it we come near to God.
This change came with an oath. The earlier priests became priests without an oath.
But Jesus became a priest with an oath. God said to Him, “The LORD has sworn and will not change His mind, ‘You are a priest forever.’”
Because of this, Jesus is the guarantee of a better covenant.
There were many priests before because death kept them from continuing in office.
But Jesus lives forever, so He holds a priesthood that never ends.
That is why He can save completely those who come to God through Him. He always lives to pray for them.
It was right for us to have such a high priest: holy, innocent, pure, set apart from sinners, and lifted above the heavens.
He does not need to offer sacrifices every day, first for His own sins and then for the people's sins. He offered Himself once for all.
The law appoints weak men as high priests. But the oath, which came after the law, appoints the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
Now the main point of what we are saying is this: We have a high priest like that. He sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven.
He serves in the holy place and in the true tabernacle, which the Lord set up, not people.
Every high priest is chosen to offer gifts and sacrifices. So this One must have something to offer too.
If He were on earth, He would not be a priest, because there are already priests who offer gifts the way the law says.

They serve a copy and a shadow of the heavenly things. That is why God warned Moses when he was about to build the tabernacle: “See that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.”
But now He has received a ministry that is much better. He is also the go-between for a better covenant, which is based on better promises.
If the first covenant had been perfect, there would have been no need for a second one.
Because God found fault with the people, He says, “The days are coming, says the the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and with the people of Judah.
“It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors when I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt. They did not keep My covenant, so I turned away from them, says the the LORD.

“This is the covenant I will make with the people of Israel after those days, says the the LORD: I will put My laws in their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be My people.
“No one will need to teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, ‘Know the the LORD,’ because they will all know Me, from the least to the greatest.
“For I will forgive their wickedness and remember their sins no more.”
By calling this covenant “new,” God has made the first one old. What is old and aging is close to disappearing.
The first covenant had rules for worship and an earthly holy place.
A tabernacle was set up. In its first room were the lampstand, the table, and the bread set out for God. This room was called the Holy Place.
Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place.

It held the gold incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered with gold all around. Inside the ark were the gold jar of manna, Aaron's staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.
Above the ark were the cherubim of glory, spreading their wings over the mercy seat. We won't go into all these details now.
Once everything was arranged this way, the priests went into the first room again and again to do their work.
But only the high priest went into the inner room, and only once a year. He never went without blood, which he offered for himself and for the sins the people had done without knowing.
The Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been opened while the first tabernacle was still in use.
This picture points to the present time. It shows that the gifts and sacrifices being offered could not make the worshiper's conscience fully clean.
They had to do with food, drink, and different washings. These were rules for the body, and they lasted until the time of the new order.
But Christ came as High Priest of the good things that are now here. He went through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made by human hands and not part of this created world.
He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves. Instead, He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, and He won eternal redemption.
The blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a young cow sprinkled on people who were unclean, made them clean on the outside.

How much more will the blood of Christ make us clean! Through the eternal Spirit, He offered Himself without fault to God. His blood cleans our consciences from dead works so we can serve the living God.

Because of this, Christ is the go-between for a new covenant. Those who are called can receive the promised eternal inheritance. This happened because His death set them free from the sins done under the first covenant.
Where there is a covenant, the death of the one who made it must be shown.
A covenant is valid only after someone has died. It has no power while the person who made it is still alive.
That is why even the first covenant was not started without blood.
After Moses had told all the people every command of the law, he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, red wool, and hyssop. He sprinkled the scroll and all the people.
He said, "This is the blood of the covenant, which God has commanded you to keep."
In the same way, he sprinkled the tabernacle and all the tools used in worship.
The law says that almost everything is made clean with blood. Without blood being poured out, there is no forgiveness.
So the copies of the heavenly things had to be purified with these sacrifices. But the heavenly things themselves need better sacrifices than these.
Christ did not enter a holy place made by human hands, which was only a copy of the true one. He entered heaven itself to stand for us before God's face.
He did not enter heaven to offer Himself again and again, the way the high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.
If that were true, Christ would have had to suffer many times since the world was made. But now He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to remove sin by sacrificing Himself.
People are meant to die once, and after that comes judgment.
In the same way, Christ was offered once to take away the sins of many. He will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to bring salvation to those who are waiting for Him.
The law is only a shadow of the good things to come, not the real things themselves. So it can never make perfect, by the same sacrifices offered year after year, those who come to worship.
If it could, wouldn't the sacrifices have stopped? Then the worshipers would have been made clean once for all, and they wouldn't feel guilty for their sins anymore.
But those sacrifices remind people of their sins every year.
It is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
So when Christ came into the world, He said: "Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me.
In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no delight.
Then I said, 'Here I am—it is written about Me in the scroll—I have come to do Your will, O God.'"
First He said, "Sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not desire, nor were You pleased with them," although they are offered according to the law.
Then He said, "Here I am, I have come to do Your will." He takes away the first to establish the second.
And by that will, we have been made holy through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
Day after day every priest stands and performs his religious duties. Again and again he offers the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
But when this Priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, He sat down at the right hand of God.
Since that time, He waits for His enemies to be made His footstool.
Because by one sacrifice He has made perfect forever those who are being made holy.
The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First He says:
"This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the the LORD. I will put My laws in their minds and write them on their hearts.
Their sins and lawless acts I will remember no more."
And where these have been forgiven, there is no longer any sacrifice for sin.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus,
by a new and living way opened for us through the curtain, that is, His body,
and since we have a great Priest over the house of God,
let us draw near to God with a sincere heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience and having our bodies washed with pure water.
Let us hold firmly to the hope we profess, for He who promised is faithful.
And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds.
Let us not give up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
If we deliberately keep on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins is left,
but only a fearful expectation of judgment and of raging fire that will consume the enemies of God.
Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

How much more severely do you think someone deserves to be punished who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, who has treated as an unholy thing the blood of the covenant that made him holy, and who has insulted the Spirit of grace?
For we know Him who said, "Vengeance is Mine; I will repay," and again, "The The LORD will judge His people."
It is a dreadful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Remember those earlier days after you received the light, when you endured a great struggle in the face of suffering.
Sometimes you were publicly exposed to insult and persecution; at other times you stood side by side with those who were so treated.
You sympathized with those in prison and joyfully accepted the taking of your property, because you knew that you yourselves had better and lasting possessions.
So do not throw away your confidence; it will be richly rewarded.
You need to persevere so that when you have done the will of God, you will receive what He has promised.
For, "In just a little while, He who is coming will come and will not delay.
But My righteous one will live by faith. And if he shrinks back, I will take no pleasure in him."
But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who believe and are saved.
Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and proof of what we do not see.
By faith, the people of old won God's approval.
By faith we understand that God created the universe by His word, so what we see was not made from things that are visible.
By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain. Because of it, he was declared right with God. God spoke well of his gifts. Even though Abel died, his faith still speaks.
By faith Enoch was taken away so he would not see death. He could not be found because God had taken him. Before that, he was known as someone who pleased God.
Without faith, no one can please God. Anyone who comes to Him must believe that He exists and that He rewards those who seek Him.

By faith Noah, warned about things not yet seen, built an ark in holy fear to save his family. Through his faith he condemned the world and became an heir of the right standing with God that comes by faith.
By faith Abraham obeyed when God called him to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance. He left, even though he did not know where he was going.
By faith he lived in the promised land like a stranger. He stayed in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who shared the same promise.
He was looking forward to the city with strong foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
By faith Sarah, though she was barren and past the age to have children, received strength to have a child. She trusted God because she believed the One who promised was faithful.
So from one man, whose body was as good as dead, came descendants as many as the stars in the sky and as countless as the sand on the seashore.
All these people died in faith. They did not receive what was promised, but they saw it and welcomed it from far away. They admitted they were strangers and foreigners on earth.
People who talk like that show they are looking for a homeland.
If they had been thinking about the country they left, they could have gone back.
Instead, they long for a better country, a heavenly one. So God is not ashamed to be called their God, because He has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham, when tested, offered Isaac. He who had received the promises was ready to sacrifice his only son.
God had said to him, "Through Isaac your descendants will be called."
Abraham believed God could raise the dead. In a way, he received Isaac back from death.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau about things to come.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, near the end of his life, spoke about the Israelites leaving Egypt and gave orders about his bones.
By faith Moses' parents hid him for three months after he was born. They saw he was a beautiful child and were not afraid of the king's order.
By faith Moses, when he grew up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.
He chose to suffer with God's people rather than enjoy sin's short-lived pleasures.
He thought suffering for Christ was worth more than Egypt's treasures, because he looked ahead to his reward.
By faith he left Egypt and did not fear the king's anger. He kept going because he saw the One who cannot be seen.
By faith he kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood, so the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
By faith the people crossed the Red Sea as if on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried, they were drowned.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell after the people marched around them for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not die with those who disobeyed, because she welcomed the spies peacefully.
What more can I say? Time would run out if I told about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets.
Through faith they conquered kingdoms, did what was right, received what was promised, and shut the mouths of lions.
They put out raging fires, escaped the sword, became strong after being weak, grew mighty in battle, and made enemy armies run away.
Women received their dead back, raised to life again. Others were tortured and refused release, so they might gain a better resurrection.
Others suffered mocking, whipping, chains, and prison.
They were stoned, sawed in two, and killed by the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, needy, suffering, and mistreated.
The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains and lived in caves and holes in the ground.
All these, though praised for their faith, did not receive what was promised.
God had planned something better for us, so they would not be made perfect without us.
We are surrounded by a huge crowd of witnesses. So let us throw off everything that slows us down and the sin that trips us up. Let us run with patience the race that is set before us.

Let us keep our eyes on Jesus. He is the one who starts and finishes our faith. He endured the cross for the joy that was set before Him. He thought nothing of the shame. Now He sits at the right hand of God's throne.
Think about Him. He endured so much hate from sinners. Think about Him so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.
In your fight against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding blood.
Have you forgotten the words that speak to you as sons? They say, "My son, do not take the Lord's discipline lightly, and do not lose heart when He corrects you.
For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He punishes every son He accepts."
Endure hardship as discipline. God is treating you as sons. What son is there whose father does not discipline him?
If you are not disciplined, and everyone undergoes discipline, then you are not true sons. You are illegitimate children.
Besides, we had human fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Should we not obey the Father of spirits even more and live?
They disciplined us for a short time as they thought best. But God disciplines us for our good, so that we can share in His holiness.
No discipline feels good at the time. It hurts. Later, though, it produces a harvest of right living and peace for those who have been trained by it.
So strengthen your weak arms and your weak knees.
Make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame will not be turned aside but healed.
Try hard to live in peace with everyone and to be holy. Without holiness, no one will see the Lord.
Watch out that no one misses God's grace. Watch out that no bitter root grows up to cause trouble and make many people unclean.
Watch out that no one is sexually immoral or godless like Esau. He sold his rights as the oldest son for one meal.
You know that later he wanted to receive the blessing. But he was rejected. He could not change what had happened, even though he begged for it with tears.
You have not come to a mountain that can be touched, a mountain burning with fire. You have not come to darkness, gloom, and storm.
You have not come to the sound of a trumpet or to a voice speaking words. The people who heard that voice begged that no more be said to them.
They could not bear what was commanded: "If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned."
The sight was so terrifying that Moses said, "I am trembling with fear."
But you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have come to thousands upon thousands of angels gathered in joy.
You have come to the gathering of the firstborn, whose names are written in heaven. You have come to God, the Judge of all, and to the spirits of righteous people made perfect.
You have come to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.

See to it that you do not refuse Him who speaks. If the people did not escape when they refused the One who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we turn away from the One who warns us from heaven?
At that time His voice shook the earth. But now He has promised, "Once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heavens."
The words "once more" show that what can be shaken—that is, created things—will be removed, so that what cannot be shaken will remain.
So, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us be thankful. Then we can worship God in a way that pleases Him, with reverence and awe.
For our God is a consuming fire.
Keep loving one another as brothers and sisters.
Do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, because some people have welcomed angels without knowing it.
Remember people in prison as if you were locked up with them. Remember those who are mistreated, because you also have bodies that can suffer.
Marriage should be honored by everyone, and the marriage bed kept pure, because God will judge those who are sexually immoral and those who commit adultery.
Keep your lives free from the love of money, and be content with what you have, because God has said, "I will never leave you or abandon you."
So we can say with confidence, "The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can anyone do to me?"
Remember your leaders, who spoke God's word to you. Think about how their lives ended, and copy their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange teachings. It is good for your heart to be strengthened by grace, not by rules about food, which have not helped those who follow them.
We have an altar, and those who serve in the tabernacle have no right to eat from it.
The high priest carries the blood of animals into the holy place to pay for sin, but the animals' bodies are burned outside the camp.
So Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through His own blood.
So let us go to Him outside the camp and share the shame He suffered.
For we do not have a lasting city here. Instead, we look for the city that is coming.
Through Jesus, then, let us always offer God a sacrifice of praise. That means words from our lips that honor His name.
Do not forget to do good and to share with others, because God is pleased with sacrifices like that.
Obey your leaders and submit to them, because they watch over your souls and will have to answer to God. Let them do this work with joy, not with groaning, because that would not help you.
Pray for us, because we are sure we have a clear conscience. We want to live honorably in every way.
I especially urge you to pray this so I can be restored to you sooner.
Now may the God of peace, who raised our Lord Jesus from the dead—the great Shepherd of the sheep—through the blood of the eternal covenant,
equip you with everything good so you can do His will. May He work in us what pleases Him, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Brothers and sisters, I beg you to listen patiently to this word of encouragement, for I have written to you only briefly.
You should know that our brother Timothy has been released. If he arrives soon, I will come with him to see you.
Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send their greetings to you.
Grace be with all of you.
James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, sends greetings to the twelve tribes scattered among the nations.
My brothers and sisters, think of it as pure joy whenever you face trials of many kinds.
You know that the testing of your faith produces perseverance.
Let perseverance finish its work so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.
If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to you.
But when you ask, you must believe and not doubt, because the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.
That person should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.
Such a person is double-minded and unstable in all they do.
A believer who is in humble circumstances should be proud of being raised up.
But rich people should be proud that God has humbled them, because they will fade away like a wildflower.
The sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls, and its beauty is destroyed. In the same way, the rich will fade away even while they go about their business.
Blessed is the person who keeps going under trial, because after standing the test, that person will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love Him.
When tempted, no one should say, "God is tempting me." For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.
But each person is tempted when they are dragged away by their own evil desire and enticed.
Then, after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.
Don't be fooled, my dear brothers and sisters.
Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, who does not change like shifting shadows.
He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, so that we would be a kind of first harvest of everything He created.
My dear brothers and sisters, remember this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to become angry.
For human anger does not produce the righteousness that God desires.
So get rid of all moral filth and the evil that is so common, and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save you.
Don't just listen to the word and fool yourselves. Do what it says.
Anyone who listens to the word but does not do what it says is like someone who looks at their face in a mirror.
They look at themselves and then go away, and right away they forget what they look like.
But whoever looks closely into the perfect law that gives freedom and keeps on doing it—not forgetting what they have heard, but doing it—will be blessed in what they do.
Those who think they are religious but don't control their tongues fool themselves, and their religion is worthless.
Religion that God our Father accepts as pure and faultless is this: to look after orphans and widows in their distress and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.
My brothers and sisters, don't hold on to faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ while showing favoritism.
Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in dirty clothes comes in too.
If you give special attention to the well-dressed man and say, "Sit here in a good seat," but say to the poor man, "You stand there," or "Sit on the floor by my feet,"
haven't you made unfair distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my dear brothers and sisters: Hasn't God chosen poor people in the world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
But you have insulted the poor. Aren't the rich the ones who oppress you and drag you into court?
Don't they speak against the good name that was given to you?
If you really keep the royal law found in Scripture, "Love your neighbor as yourself," you are doing well.
But if you show favoritism, you sin. The law convicts you as a lawbreaker.
Whoever keeps the whole law but trips up in one part is guilty of breaking all of it.
He who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." If you don't commit adultery but you do murder, you have become a lawbreaker.
So speak and act like people who will be judged by the law that gives freedom.
Judgment without mercy will come to anyone who has not shown mercy. Mercy wins over judgment.
What good is it, my brothers and sisters, if someone says he has faith but has no good deeds? Can that faith save him?
Suppose a brother or sister has no clothes and not enough food for the day.
If one of you says to them, "Go in peace. Stay warm and eat well," but doesn't give them what their body needs, what good is that?
In the same way, faith by itself, if it has no deeds, is dead.
But someone will say, "You have faith and I have deeds." Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.
You believe that God is one. Good for you! Even the demons believe that—and they shake with fear.
Do you want proof, you foolish person, that faith without deeds is useless?
Wasn't our ancestor Abraham counted right with God because of what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
You see that his faith worked together with his deeds, and his faith was made complete by his deeds.
Scripture was fulfilled when it said, "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness." He was also called God's friend.
You see, then, that a person is counted right with God by deeds and not by faith alone.
In the same way, wasn't Rahab the prostitute counted right with God by deeds when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another road?
Just as the body without breath is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.
My brothers, not many of you should become teachers, because we who teach will be judged more strictly.
We all stumble in many ways. If someone never slips in what they say, that person is mature and can control their whole body.
When we put a bit in a horse's mouth, it obeys us, and we can steer its whole body.
Look at ships. They may be huge and pushed by strong winds, but a tiny rudder turns them wherever the pilot wants.
In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts about big things. See how a tiny spark can set a huge fire.
The tongue is like a fire. It is a world of evil among the parts of our body. It stains the whole body, sets life's path on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.
People can tame all kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures.
But no one can tame the tongue. It is an unstable evil, full of deadly poison.
With it we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse people who are made in God's likeness.
Blessing and cursing both come from the same mouth. My brothers, this should not happen.
Can a spring send out both fresh water and bitter water from the same opening?
My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine grow figs? No, and a salty spring cannot give fresh water.
Who among you is wise and understanding? Show it by living well and doing good things with gentle wisdom.
But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not brag about it or lie against the truth.
That kind of "wisdom" is not from above. It is earthly, unspiritual, and demonic.
Where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there is disorder and every kind of evil practice.
But wisdom from above is first pure, then peace-loving, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruit, fair and sincere.
People who make peace plant seeds of peace, and they harvest a crop of right living.
Where do wars and fights among you come from? Don't they come from the desires inside you that battle in your bodies?
You want things and don't have them. You kill and are jealous, but you still can't get them. You fight and go to war. You don't have, because you don't ask.
When you do ask, you don't receive, because you ask for the wrong things. You just want to spend them on your own pleasures.
You unfaithful people! Don't you know that friendship with the world makes you an enemy of God? So anyone who wants to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God.
Do you think Scripture says this for no reason? The Spirit He placed in us longs for us with jealous love.
But He gives even more grace. That is why it says, "God opposes the proud, but He gives grace to the humble."
So submit to God. Stand up to the devil, and he will run away from you.
Come near to God, and He will come near to you. Wash your hands, you sinners, and make your hearts pure, you who can't make up your minds.
Be sad, mourn, and cry. Let your laughter turn into mourning, and your joy turn into gloom.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will lift you up.

Brothers and sisters, don't speak badly about each other. Anyone who speaks against a brother or sister, or judges them, speaks against the law and judges the law. If you judge the law, you are not obeying it but judging it.
There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who can save and destroy. So who are you to judge your neighbor?
Now listen, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to this city and stay there a year, trading and making a profit."
You don't even know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? You are like a mist that shows up for a little while and then disappears.
Instead, you should say, "If the Lord wants us to, we will live and do this or that."
But now you brag about your proud plans. All that kind of bragging is evil.
So if someone knows the good they should do and doesn't do it, that is sin.
Come now, you rich people! Weep and cry out because of the suffering that is coming on you.
Your wealth has rotted, and moths have eaten your clothes.
Your gold and silver have rusted, and that rust will be a witness against you. It will eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in these last days.
Look! The pay you kept back from the workers who harvested your fields is crying out against you. The cries of those harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.
You have lived in luxury on the earth and chased pleasure. You have pampered your hearts for the day of slaughter.
You have condemned and murdered the righteous person, and he does not fight back against you.
So be patient, brothers, until the Lord comes. Look at the farmer who waits for the valuable crop from the earth. He is patient with it until it gets the early and late rains.
You too must be patient. Make your hearts strong, because the Lord's coming is near.
Don't complain about each other, brothers, so that you won't be judged. Look! The Judge is standing at the door.
Brothers, take the prophets who spoke in the Lord's name as an example of suffering and patience.
We say that those who endured are blessed. You have heard about Job's endurance, and you have seen what the Lord finally did, because the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven, not by earth, and not by any other oath. Let your "Yes" be yes and your "No" be no, so that you won't fall under judgment.
Is anyone among you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.
Is anyone among you sick? He should call for the elders of the church, and they should pray over him. They should anoint him with oil in the Lord's name.
The prayer of faith will save the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.
So confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. A righteous person's prayer is powerful and effective.
Elijah was an ordinary man like us. He prayed hard that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the earth for three and a half years.
Then he prayed again, and the sky gave rain. The earth produced its crops.
My brothers, if someone among you wanders from the truth and someone brings him back,
let that person know that whoever turns a sinner from his wrong path will save his soul from death and cover many sins.
Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, writes to God's chosen people who live like strangers in the world. You are scattered through Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
You were chosen because God the Father knew you ahead of time. The Spirit makes you holy so you can obey Jesus Christ and be cleansed by His blood. May grace and peace be given to you more and more.
Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! In His great mercy He has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
He has given us an inheritance that can never perish, spoil, or fade. This inheritance is kept in heaven for you.
Through faith you are shielded by God's power until the salvation that is ready to be shown in the last time.
In all this you greatly rejoice, even though now for a little while you may have to suffer grief in all kinds of trials.
These troubles test your faith. Your faith is worth more than gold, which can be destroyed even though fire tests it. When Jesus Christ is revealed, your faith will bring praise, glory, and honor.
You have not seen Him, but you love Him. You do not see Him now, but you believe in Him. You are filled with a joy too great for words and full of glory.
You are receiving the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
The prophets who spoke about the grace that was coming to you searched and studied carefully.
They tried to learn what time or situation the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing to. He spoke ahead of time about Christ's sufferings and the glory that would follow.

It was shown to them that they were not serving themselves but you. They spoke about things that have now been told to you by those who preached the good news to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. Even angels long to look into these things.
So get ready for action. Keep your minds clear, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be given to you when Jesus Christ is revealed.
As obedient children, do not let your lives be shaped by the evil desires you had when you did not know better.
Instead, be holy in all you do, just as the One who called you is holy.
For it is written, "Be holy, because I am holy."
Since you call on a Father who judges each person's work fairly, live with reverent fear during your time as strangers in the world.
You know you were not set free from your empty way of life, handed down by your ancestors, by things that can perish, like silver or gold.
Instead, you were bought with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without fault or stain.
Christ was known before the world was made, but He was shown to you in these last times for your sake.
Through Him you believe in God, who raised Him from the dead and gave Him glory. So your faith and hope are in God.
Now that you have made your souls pure by obeying the truth, love one another deeply from a clean heart.
You have been born again, not from seed that can die, but from seed that cannot die, through the living and lasting word of God.
For, "All people are like grass, and all their glory is like the flowers of the field. The grass dries up, and the flowers fall."
"But the word of the Lord lasts forever." And this is the word that was preached to you.
So get rid of all evil, all lying, pretending, jealousy, and all bad talk about others.
Like newborn babies, long for the pure spiritual milk, so that by it you can grow up in your salvation,
since you have tasted that the Lord is good.
As you come to Him, the living Stone—rejected by people but chosen by God and precious to Him—
you also, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices that God accepts through Jesus Christ.
For in Scripture it says, "See, I lay a stone in Zion, a chosen and precious cornerstone, and whoever trusts in Him will never be put to shame."
Now to you who believe, this stone is precious. But to those who do not believe, "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,"
and, "A stone that makes people stumble and a rock that makes them fall." They stumble because they disobey the word, and that is what they were destined for.

But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession, so that you may tell about the wonderful deeds of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.
Once you were not a people, but now you are God's people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
Dear friends, I urge you, as strangers and temporary residents, to stay away from sinful desires that fight against your soul.
Keep your behavior good among the people around you, so that when they speak against you as if you were doing wrong, they may see your good deeds and give glory to God on the day He visits us.
For the Lord's sake, submit to every human authority, whether to the emperor as the supreme ruler,
or to governors, who are sent by Him to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right.
For it is God's will that by doing good you silence the ignorant talk of foolish people.
Live as free people, but do not use your freedom as a cover for evil; live as God's servants.
Honor everyone. Love the family of believers. Fear God. Honor the emperor.
Slaves, submit to your masters with all respect, not only to those who are good and gentle, but also to those who are harsh.
For it is to your credit if you endure pain while suffering unfairly because you are mindful of God.
What credit is it if you are beaten for doing wrong and you endure it? But if you suffer for doing good and endure it, this is pleasing to God.
For you were called to this, because Christ suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in His steps.
"He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in His mouth."
When He was insulted, He did not insult back; when He suffered, He did not threaten, but trusted Himself to the One who judges fairly.
"He Himself bore our sins" in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sins and live for what is right; "by His wounds you have been healed."
For "you were like sheep going astray," but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
Wives, in the same way, submit yourselves to your own husbands. That way, even if some do not believe the message, they may be won over without words by the way you live.
They will see your pure and respectful lives.
Your beauty should not come from the outside, like fancy hairstyles, gold jewelry, or fine clothes.
Instead, it should come from the inner self, with the lasting beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit. That is very valuable to God.
This is how the holy women of the past who hoped in God made themselves beautiful. They submitted to their own husbands.
Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him her lord. You are her daughters if you do what is right and do not give in to fear.

Husbands, in the same way, live with your wives with understanding. Treat them with respect as the weaker partner, and as heirs with you of the gracious gift of life. Do this so that nothing blocks your prayers.
Finally, all of you, live in harmony, show sympathy, love one another, be kind, and be humble.
Do not pay back evil for evil or insult for insult. Instead, pay back with a blessing. You were called to this so that you may receive a blessing.
“Whoever wants to love life and see good days must keep their tongue from evil and their lips from lying.
They must turn from evil and do good. They must seek peace and go after it.
For the eyes of the Lord are on those who do right, and His ears listen to their prayers. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”
Who will hurt you if you are eager to do good?
But even if you suffer for doing right, you are blessed. “Do not fear what they threaten; do not be shaken.”
But in your hearts honor Christ as Lord. Always be ready to give an answer to anyone who asks you for the reason for the hope you have. Do it with gentleness and respect.
Keep a clear conscience. Then those who speak badly about your good life in Christ will be ashamed of their lies.
It is better, if God wants it, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.
Christ also suffered once for sins. The innocent suffered for the guilty to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive by the Spirit.
In that Spirit He went and preached to the spirits in prison.
These were the spirits of those who disobeyed long ago, when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. Only a few people, eight in all, were saved through water.

This water stands for baptism, which now saves you too. It is not about washing dirt from the body. It is about asking God for a clear conscience. It saves you through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
He has gone into heaven and is at God’s right hand. Angels, authorities, and powers are under His control.
Since Christ suffered in His body, you too should arm yourselves with the same way of thinking. The person who has suffered in the body is done with sin.
From now on, you should live the rest of your earthly life not following human desires, but following God's will.
You have already spent enough time doing what unbelievers want—living in wild parties, strong desires, drunkenness, wild dancing, drinking parties, and illegal worship of idols.
They are surprised that you don't join them in the same flood of reckless living, and they insult you.
They will have to answer to God, who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
That's why the good news was preached even to those who have died. They were judged in the body as people are, but they live in the spirit the way God wants.
The end of all things is near. So be clear-minded and self-controlled so you can pray.
Above all, love each other deeply, because love covers a lot of sins.
Welcome one another into your homes without complaining.
Each person has received a gift. Use it to serve one another, like good managers of God's grace in all its different forms.

If anyone speaks, he should speak as if he were sharing God's words. If anyone serves, he should serve with the strength God gives. Do this so that in everything God will be praised through Jesus Christ. Glory and power belong to Him forever and ever. Amen.
Dear friends, don't be surprised by the painful test that is happening among you, as if something strange were happening to you.
Instead, be glad that you share in Christ's sufferings. Then you will be full of joy when His glory is shown.
If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.
Make sure none of you suffers as a murderer, a thief, a person who does evil, or a busybody.
But if you suffer as a Christian, don't be ashamed. Instead, praise God for that name.
The time has come for judgment to begin with God's family. If it begins with us, what will happen to those who don't obey the good news of God?
If it's hard for a good person to be saved, what will happen to ungodly people and sinners?
So those who suffer because it's God's will should entrust their souls to their faithful Creator and keep doing good.
I am a fellow elder and a witness of Christ’s sufferings, and I will share in the glory that is about to be revealed. So I urge the elders among you:
Care for God’s flock among you. Watch over them—not because you must, but because you want to. Don’t do it for shameful profit, but do it with eagerness.
Don’t act like bosses over the people God has given you. Instead, be examples to the flock.
Then, when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that never fades.
In the same way, younger people, submit to the elders. All of you, put on humility toward one another, because God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
So humble yourselves under God’s mighty hand, so that He may lift you up at the right time.
Throw all your worries on Him, because He cares for you.
Be clear-minded and watchful. Your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour.
Resist him. Stand firm in your faith. Remember that believers all over the world are going through the same kinds of suffering.

After you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you, make you strong, give you power, and set you on a firm foundation.
To Him be the power forever and ever. Amen.
With the help of Silvanus, whom I trust as a faithful brother, I have written this short letter to encourage you and to show that this is God’s true grace. Stand firm in it.
The believers in Babylon, who are chosen along with you, send greetings, and so does my son Mark.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.
Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, writes to those who received a faith as precious as ours through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ.
May grace and peace be given to you in growing measure as you know God and Jesus our Lord.
His divine power has given us everything we need for a godly life through knowing Him who called us by His own glory and goodness.
Through these, He has given us His great and precious promises. Because of them, you can share in God's nature, since you have escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.
For this reason, make every effort to add goodness to your faith. Then add knowledge to goodness.
Add self-control to knowledge, perseverance to self-control, and godliness to perseverance.
Add brotherly love to godliness, and love to brotherly love.
If you have these qualities and they keep growing, they will keep you from being useless or unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
But anyone who lacks them is nearsighted and blind. He has forgotten that he was cleansed from his past sins.
So, brothers and sisters, be all the more eager to make your calling and election sure. If you do these things, you will never fall.
You will be richly welcomed into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
So I will always remind you of these things, even though you know them and are firmly grounded in the truth you have.
I think it is right to refresh your memory as long as I am in this body.
I know I will soon leave this life, just as our Lord Jesus Christ has shown me.
I will also work hard so that after I am gone, you will always be able to remember these things.
We did not follow made-up stories when we told you about the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. We were eyewitnesses of His greatness.
He received honor and glory from God the Father when a voice came to Him from the Majestic Glory. It said, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
We heard this voice from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.
We also have the prophetic word, and it is very reliable. You will do well to pay attention to it, like a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
Above all, know this: no prophecy in Scripture comes from a person's own explanation.
Prophecy never came from human will, but people spoke from God as they were moved by the Holy Spirit.

But long ago there were false prophets among God's people. In the same way, there will be false teachers among you. They will secretly bring in destructive teachings that pull people away. They will even deny the Master who bought them, and they will bring quick ruin on themselves.
Many people will follow their shameful ways. Because of them, the way of truth will be spoken against.
In their greed, they will use you with made-up words. Their judgment was set long ago, and their ruin is not sleeping.
For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but threw them into hell and chained them in dark gloom until judgment;
if He did not spare the ancient world, but saved Noah, a preacher of right living, along with seven others, when He brought a flood on a world of ungodly people;
if He turned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes and condemned them to ruin, making them a warning for ungodly people in the future;
and if He rescued Lot, a good man who was worn down by the evil lives of lawless people—
for that good man lived among them and was troubled day after day by the lawless things he saw and heard—
then the Lord knows how to rescue godly people from trials and to hold ungodly people for punishment until the day of judgment.
This is especially true for those who follow dirty desires and look down on authority. They are bold and stubborn. They do not tremble when they speak evil of glorious beings.
Even angels, who are stronger and more powerful, do not accuse them with insults before the Lord.
But these people are like animals that cannot think. They are born to be caught and destroyed. They speak evil about things they do not understand. They will be destroyed by their own corruption.
They will suffer harm as pay for their wrongdoing. They think it is fun to live in luxury during the day. They are spots and stains. They enjoy tricking people while they eat with you.
Their eyes are full of adultery, and they never stop sinning. They lure weak souls. Their hearts are trained in greed. They are children under a curse!
They have left the straight path and wandered off. They followed the path of Balaam son of Beor, who loved pay for doing wrong.
But he was corrected for his own sin. A donkey that could not speak talked with a human voice and stopped the prophet's crazy plan.
These people are like wells with no water and like clouds blown by a storm. The blackest darkness is kept for them.
They speak proud, empty words. With sinful human desires, they lure people who have only just escaped from those living in error.
They promise freedom, but they are slaves to corruption. A person is a slave to whatever controls him.
If people have escaped the world's filth through knowing our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and then get tangled up in it again and are overcome, their last condition is worse than their first.
It would have been better for them not to have known the way of right living than to know it and turn away from the holy command given to them.
This true saying has come true for them: “A dog returns to its own vomit,” and, “A pig that has washed goes back to rolling in the mud.”
Dear friends, this is the second letter I have written to you. In both of them I am stirring your honest minds by reminding you.
I want you to remember the words spoken long ago by the holy prophets and the command our Lord and Savior gave through His apostles.
First, understand this: In the last days, mockers will come, following their own evil desires.
They will say, “Where is the promise that He will come again? Ever since our ancestors died, everything goes on just as it has since the beginning of creation.”
They choose to forget that long ago God spoke, and the heavens and earth were made. The earth was formed from water and through water.
By these waters the world of that time was destroyed in a flood.
But by the same word, the present heavens and earth are stored up for fire. They are being kept for the day of judgment, when ungodly people will be destroyed.
But do not forget this one thing, dear friends: With the Lord, a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.
The Lord is not slow to keep His promise, as some people think. Instead, He is patient with you. He does not want anyone to be destroyed, but He wants everyone to turn from sin and be saved.

But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will disappear with a loud noise. The elements will be destroyed by fire, and the earth and everything done on it will be laid bare.
Since all these things will be destroyed, what kind of people should you be? You should live holy lives and honor God.
Look forward to the day of God and be eager for it to come. On that day the heavens will be destroyed by fire, and the elements will melt in the heat.
But we are looking forward to what He promised: new heavens and a new earth where everything is right.
So, dear friends, since you are looking forward to these things, make every effort to be found living at peace with Him, without spot or blame.
Think of our Lord's patience as an opportunity for people to be saved. Our dear brother Paul wrote to you about this too, using the wisdom God gave him.

He talks about these things in all his letters. Some of what he says is hard to understand. People who are uneducated and unstable twist his words, just as they do with the rest of Scripture. That leads to their own destruction.
So, dear friends, since you already know this, be on guard. Do not be led away by the errors of people who break God's law. Then you will not lose your firm footing.
Instead, grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be glory now and forever. Amen.
We are telling you about something that was there from the very beginning. We heard it. We saw it with our own eyes. We looked at it, and our hands touched it. This is about the Word of life.
That life showed itself to us. We saw it, and now we tell others about it. We announce to you the life that lasts forever. That life was with the Father, and it showed itself to us.
We are telling you what we saw and heard so that you can share life with us. Our shared life is with the Father and with His Son, Jesus Christ.
We are writing these things so that our joy may be full.
This is the message we heard from Him and now tell you: God is light, and there is no darkness in Him at all.
If we say we share life with Him but live in darkness, we are lying. We are not living by the truth.
But if we live in the light, as He is in the light, we share life with one another. Also, the blood of Jesus, His Son, washes us clean from every sin.
If we say we have no sin, we fool ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
But if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just. He will forgive our sins and make us clean from all wrong.
If we say we have never sinned, we make Him out to be a liar, and His word is not in us.
My dear children, I am writing this to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have a Helper with the Father—Jesus Christ, who is right with God.
He is the sacrifice that pays for our sins. This is not only for us, but also for the sins of the whole world.
We know that we have come to know Him if we keep His commands.
Anyone who says, "I know Him," but does not keep His commands is a liar. The truth is not in that person.
But if anyone keeps His word, God's love is made complete in that person. This is how we know we are in Him:
whoever says he stays in Him must live the way Jesus lived.
Dear friends, I am not writing you a new command. I am writing an old command that you have had since the beginning. This old command is the message you heard.
Yet I am also writing you a new command. It is true in Him and in you, because the darkness is passing away, and the true light is already shining.
Anyone who says he is in the light but hates his brother is still in the dark.
Anyone who loves his brother stays in the light, and there is nothing in him that makes others stumble.
But anyone who hates his brother is in the dark. He walks in the dark. He does not know where he is going, because the dark has blinded his eyes.
I am writing to you, dear children, because your sins are forgiven through His name.

I am writing to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I have written to you, children, because you know the Father.
I have written to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, God's word stays in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
Do not love the world or anything in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father's love is not in that person.
All that is in the world comes down to these things: the cravings of the body, the cravings of the eyes, and pride in what we own. These things are not from the Father. They are from the world.
The world and its desires are passing away. But whoever does God's will lives forever.
Children, this is the last hour. You have heard that the antichrist is coming. Even now many antichrists have come. This is how we know it is the last hour.
They went out from us, but they did not really belong to us. If they had belonged to us, they would have stayed with us. But they left so it would be clear that not all of them belong to us.
But you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all know the truth.
I did not write to you because you do not know the truth. I wrote because you do know it, and because no lie comes from the truth.
Who is the liar? It is the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ. This person is the antichrist. He denies the Father and the Son.
No one who denies the Son has the Father. Anyone who accepts the Son has the Father too.
Let what you heard from the beginning stay in you. If it does, you will stay in the Son and in the Father.
This is the promise He made to us: eternal life.
I have written these things to you about those who are trying to lead you astray.
The anointing you received from Him stays in you. You do not need anyone to teach you. His anointing teaches you about all things. It is true and not a lie. Stay in Him, just as it taught you.
And now, dear children, stay in Him. Then when He appears, we can be confident and not be ashamed before Him when He comes.
If you know that He is right with God, you also know that everyone who does what is right has been born of Him.
See how much love the Father has given us, so that we can be called children of God. And that is what we are. That is why the world does not know us, because it did not know Him.
Dear friends, we are already God's children. We do not yet know what we will be, but we know that when He appears, we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He really is.
Everyone who has this hope in Him keeps himself pure, just as He is pure.
Everyone who keeps on sinning breaks God's law, because sin is lawlessness.
And you know that He came to take away our sins, and there is no sin in Him.
No one who stays in Him keeps on sinning. No one who keeps on sinning has seen Him or known Him.
Dear children, do not let anyone fool you. The one who does what is right is righteous, just as He is righteous.
The one who keeps on sinning belongs to the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The Son of God came to destroy the devil's work.
No one born of God keeps on sinning, because God's seed stays in him. He cannot keep on sinning, because he has been born of God.
This is how we can tell God's children from the devil's children: Anyone who does not do what is right is not from God, and neither is anyone who does not love his brother.
This is the message you heard from the beginning: We should love one another.
We should not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. Why did he murder him? Because his own actions were evil, but his brother's actions were right.
Do not be surprised, brothers and sisters, if the world hates you.
We know that we have moved from death to life, because we love our brothers and sisters. Anyone who does not love stays in death.
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life in him.
This is how we know what love is: He gave His life for us, so we should give our lives for our brothers and sisters.
If anyone has enough of this world's goods and sees a brother or sister in need but does not help, how can God's love stay in that person?
Dear children, let us love not just with words or speech, but with actions and in truth.
This is how we know we belong to the truth, and this is how we can set our hearts at rest before Him.
If our hearts make us feel guilty, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows everything.
Dear friends, if our hearts do not make us feel guilty, we can be bold before God.
We receive from Him whatever we ask, because we obey His commands and do what pleases Him.
His command is this: We must believe in the name of His Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, just as He commanded us.
Whoever obeys His commands stays in Him, and He stays in him. We know He stays in us because of the Spirit He gave us.
Dear friends, do not believe every spirit. Instead, test the spirits to see if they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
This is how you can know the Spirit of God: Every spirit that says Jesus Christ came in the flesh is from God.
But every spirit that does not agree that Jesus Christ came in the flesh is not from God. That is the spirit of the antichrist. You have heard it is coming, and it is already in the world.
You are from God, dear children. You have won the victory over them, because the One who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.
They belong to the world, so they speak like the world, and the world listens to them.
We belong to God. Whoever knows God listens to us. Whoever does not belong to God does not listen to us. This is how we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.
Dear friends, let us love one another, because love comes from God. Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
Anyone who does not love does not know God, because God is love.
God showed His love to us by sending His only Son into the world so that we could live through Him.
